film-school.fs-sound-2.q1.e: Distance matters most; a cheap close mic beats an expensive distant one.

film-school.fs-sound-2.q2.t: Thirty to sixty seconds of room tone
film-school.fs-sound-2.q2.p: You finish at a location. Which recording does the lesson insist on?
film-school.fs-sound-2.q2.e: Room tone is needed to bridge cuts and cannot be fabricated afterwards.

film-school.fs-sound-2.q3.p: Why do professionals often record both boom and lavalier?
film-school.fs-sound-2.q3.e: A boom is natural but needs an operator and may dip; a lav is consistent but closed-in and rustly, so each backs up the other.

film-school.fs-sound-3.q1.e: ADR is automated dialogue replacement: re-recording lines in a studio to picture.

film-school.fs-sound-3.q2.t: Add matched reverb and original ambience underneath
film-school.fs-sound-3.q2.p: Your ADR sounds too clean and close. How does the lesson say to fix it?
film-school.fs-sound-3.q2.e: Adding reverb matched to the location plus ambient bed puts ADR back into the space.

film-school.fs-sound-3.q3.t: It makes every later process faster
film-school.fs-sound-3.q3.p: Why keep each character on their own track in dialogue editing?
film-school.fs-sound-3.q3.e: Split tracks cost nothing and speed up noise reduction and the final mix.

film-school.fs-sound-4.q1.t: Performing footsteps, cloth and prop sounds in sync with picture
film-school.fs-sound-4.q1.h: Under the control of the mix.
film-school.fs-sound-4.q1.e: Foley is performed to picture so these sounds can be controlled in the mix.

film-school.fs-sound-4.q2.t: Layer a low thud, a mid crack and a high transient
film-school.fs-sound-4.q2.p: You need an impactful punch sound. What does the lesson suggest?
film-school.fs-sound-4.q2.e: A convincing impact is usually three or four layered sounds covering weight, material and initiation.

film-school.fs-sound-4.q3.p: Why can dropping the ambient bed for two seconds before an event be so powerful?
film-school.fs-sound-4.q3.e: Subtraction breaks continuous expectation, often giving more impact than an added effect.

film-school.fs-sound-5.q1.p: What does the lesson say music should do rather than duplicate?
film-school.fs-sound-5.q1.h: It should not repeat what is already there.
film-school.fs-sound-5.q1.e: Music that merely matches the scene tells the audience nothing new.

film-school.fs-sound-5.q2.p: You are editing a grief scene and cheerful music over it plays against the mood. What is this technique called?
film-school.fs-sound-5.q2.e: Counterpoint pairs music that contrasts with the scene to reveal something deeper.

film-school.fs-sound-5.q3.t: Everyone falls in love with it and the composer is asked to write something like it but legally different
film-school.fs-sound-5.q3.p: Why is the temp track a hazard?
film-school.fs-sound-5.q3.e: A hardened temp track makes a bad brief that produces derivative work.

film-school.fs-sound-6.q1.t: Lowering effects and music beneath dialogue by automation
film-school.fs-sound-6.q1.p: What does ducking mean in the lesson's description of the mix?
film-school.fs-sound-6.q1.e: When dialogue matters, effects and music duck beneath it.

film-school.fs-sound-6.q2.t: Check the mix on the worst speaker you can find, in mono
film-school.fs-sound-6.q2.p: You want to check dialogue survives a phone speaker. What does the lesson recommend?
film-school.fs-sound-6.q2.e: If dialogue survives a phone speaker in mono, it should survive anything.

film-school.fs-sound-6.q3.t: The mix lacks a decision about which layer is the subject
film-school.fs-sound-6.q3.p: A mix has everything equally present and is tiring even at high volume. What is the diagnosis?
film-school.fs-sound-6.q3.h: At any moment one layer is the subject.
film-school.fs-sound-6.q3.e: Mixes fail when everything is equally present, because the mix decides what the audience attends to.

film-school.fs-prod-1.q1.t: The only role present from first idea to last payment
film-school.fs-prod-1.q1.p: What is the producer's distinguishing feature among film roles?
film-school.fs-prod-1.q1.e: The producer is attached from the option on rights to the final distribution payment.

film-school.fs-prod-1.q2.t: Brought money, rights or talent but does not run it
film-school.fs-prod-1.q2.p: A credit reads executive producer. In broad practice what does it typically indicate?
film-school.fs-prod-1.q2.h: Not the person on set daily.
film-school.fs-prod-1.q2.e: Executive producers typically brought money, rights or talent; the line producer manages budget and physical production.

film-school.fs-prod-1.q3.t: Judgement about people and risk is acquired by doing it
film-school.fs-prod-1.q3.p: Why does the lesson recommend producing your own shorts?
film-school.fs-prod-1.q3.h: Most judgement is learned by doing.
film-school.fs-prod-1.q3.e: Producer judgement can mainly be gained by practising it.

film-school.fs-prod-2.q1.t: Exclusive right to buy full rights within a fixed window
film-school.fs-prod-2.q1.p: What does an option give you?
film-school.fs-prod-2.q1.h: Twelve to eighteen months, often renewable.
film-school.fs-prod-2.q1.e: An option pays a small sum for the exclusive right to buy within a window.

film-school.fs-prod-2.q2.t: A gap in chain of title that can block release
film-school.fs-prod-2.q2.p: A friend wrote a scene in week one but never signed anything. What risk does this create?
film-school.fs-prod-2.q2.e: An unsigned contributor creates a gap in the chain of title that financiers and distributors will not accept.

film-school.fs-prod-2.q3.t: Works with lapsed copyright can be adapted freely, which explains frequent remakes
film-school.fs-prod-2.q3.p: Why does the lesson call public domain a strategic tool?
film-school.fs-prod-2.q3.e: Public domain works can be adapted without rights deals, which is why the canon is repeatedly remade.

film-school.fs-prod-3.q1.t: Tagging each scene's elements such as cast, props and locations
film-school.fs-prod-3.q1.e: The breakdown goes scene by scene tagging every element, and each tag has cost and scheduling consequences.

film-school.fs-prod-3.q2.p: Which line item below falls above the line?
film-school.fs-prod-3.q2.e: Above the line covers the creative deals: writer, director, producers and principal cast.

film-school.fs-prod-3.q3.t: It still pays by cutting shooting days, the most expensive way to save
film-school.fs-prod-3.q3.p: Why does the lesson say a production with no contingency does not avoid problems?
film-school.fs-prod-3.q3.e: Without contingency, problems are paid for by cutting shooting days, which is the costliest way to save.

film-school.fs-prod-4.q1.t: Production incentives such as tax credits return a percentage of spend
film-school.fs-prod-4.q1.p: Why are films often shot in places other than where they are set?
film-school.fs-prod-4.q1.e: Incentives move production to cheaper or subsidised places.

film-school.fs-prod-4.q2.t: Scout in person at the time of day you will shoot, check sun path, noise and power
film-school.fs-prod-4.q2.p: You scout a location. What does the lesson say to do?
film-school.fs-prod-4.q2.e: Scout in person at the shooting time and check practicalities and permission authority.

film-school.fs-prod-4.q3.t: It develops no screen identity of its own
film-school.fs-prod-4.q3.p: What critical cost does the lesson identify for a city that always stands in for somewhere else?
film-school.fs-prod-4.q3.e: A stand-in city never builds its own screen identity and its texture is suppressed.

film-school.fs-prod-5.q1.p: How many licences does music generally require in clearance?
film-school.fs-prod-5.q1.e: Music needs both a composition (publishing) licence and a master licence.

film-school.fs-prod-5.q2.t: Clear the artwork or remove it
film-school.fs-prod-5.q2.p: Your film shows a poster on a cafe wall in several shots. What should you do?
film-school.fs-prod-5.q2.e: Artwork on walls and similar items require clearance or removal.

film-school.fs-prod-5.q3.t: The title was changed on the prints and the copyright notice was omitted
film-school.fs-prod-5.q3.p: How did Night of the Living Dead end up in the public domain?
film-school.fs-prod-5.q3.e: The distributor changed the title and omitted the copyright notice, forfeiting copyright under the law of the time.

film-school.fs-prod-6.q1.t: Brings original camera files back in against the locked timeline
film-school.fs-prod-6.q1.e: The conform relinks full-quality camera originals to the locked offline edit.

film-school.fs-prod-6.q2.t: At least two, verified by checksum
film-school.fs-prod-6.q2.p: On set, how many locations should cards be backed up to before wiping?
film-school.fs-prod-6.q2.e: The lesson says every card is backed up to at least two locations and verified by checksum before wiping.

film-school.fs-prod-6.q3.t: Running out of money at 95 percent complete with no funds for sound, grade or deliverables
film-school.fs-prod-6.q3.p: What is the most common independent-film failure described in the lesson?
film-school.fs-prod-6.q3.e: Many films stall at the finish because deliverables and post were underbudgeted.

film-school.fs-prod-7.q1.t: Premiere status can be spent once
film-school.fs-prod-7.q1.p: Why does sequencing of festival submissions matter?
film-school.fs-prod-7.q1.e: Top-tier festivals usually require a genuine premiere, which can be used only once.

film-school.fs-prod-7.q2.t: It is simple and usually the worst outcome for the filmmaker
film-school.fs-prod-7.q2.p: A distributor offers an all-rights worldwide deal in perpetuity. What does the lesson say about this?
film-school.fs-prod-7.q2.h: Rights split by territory, media and duration.
film-school.fs-prod-7.q2.e: It is simple but usually the worst outcome; filmmakers should understand what is taken and for how long.

film-school.fs-prod-7.q3.t: A director with a following at release has leverage that quality alone does not give
film-school.fs-prod-7.q3.p: Why does the lesson say to start telling people about your film while making it?
film-school.fs-prod-7.q3.e: Building an audience early gives leverage at release, especially in self-distribution.

film-school.fs-act-1.q1.t: If I were in these circumstances, what would I do?
film-school.fs-act-1.q1.h: It keeps the actor's truthful impulses in play.
film-school.fs-act-1.q1.e: The magic if asks what you would do in the character's circumstances, rather than becoming someone else.

film-school.fs-act-1.q2.p: You list what the character wants across the whole play to give each scene a spine. What is that called?
film-school.fs-act-1.q2.e: The super-objective is what the character wants across the whole play.

film-school.fs-act-1.q3.t: From emotional recall toward the Method of Physical Actions
film-school.fs-act-1.q3.p: How did Stanislavski's thinking change over his lifetime?
film-school.fs-act-1.q3.e: Late Stanislavski trusted truthful physical actions to produce inner life rather than relying on emotional recall.

film-school.fs-act-2.q1.p: Whose Method centres on affective memory?
film-school.fs-act-2.q1.e: Strasberg's Method centres on recalling real emotional experiences.

film-school.fs-act-2.q2.p: An actor wants to build a role from research and imagination rather than their own trauma. Which approach is that?
film-school.fs-act-2.q2.h: She studied with Stanislavski in Paris.
film-school.fs-act-2.q2.e: Adler held that the actor's material is imagination and the given circumstances.

film-school.fs-act-2.q3.t: They are three answers to one problem and professionals borrow from all
film-school.fs-act-2.q3.p: What does the lesson say about the eighty-year argument between schools?
film-school.fs-act-2.q3.e: Different actors and roles are served by different answers, so the techniques are a toolkit.

film-school.fs-act-3.q1.p: What is the foundation exercise of Meisner training?
film-school.fs-act-3.q1.e: The repetition exercise has partners repeat observations back and forth as impressions shift.

film-school.fs-act-3.q2.t: Misplaced attention on your own performance
film-school.fs-act-3.q2.p: A director says your performance is "in your head". What does repetition address?
film-school.fs-act-3.q2.e: Repetition removes attention from your performance and puts it on the scene partner.

film-school.fs-act-3.q3.t: He argued the words are the least important thing in the scene
film-school.fs-act-3.q3.p: Why does Meisner training introduce text last?
film-school.fs-act-3.q3.e: The words are least important; truthful doing and responding come first.

film-school.fs-act-4.q1.t: David Mamet and William H. Macy
film-school.fs-act-4.q1.e: Practical Aesthetics was developed by David Mamet and William H. Macy.

film-school.fs-act-4.q2.t: To get someone to admit they were wrong
film-school.fs-act-4.q2.p: Which phrasing is a valid essential action?
film-school.fs-act-4.q2.h: Something you could genuinely try to do.
film-school.fs-act-4.q2.e: An essential action is an ordinary-language transaction you could attempt, not a feeling.

film-school.fs-act-4.q3.t: It is repeatable at take forty at 3 a.m.
film-school.fs-act-4.q3.p: Why does the lesson say action-based work suits screen acting?
film-school.fs-act-4.q3.e: An actor with a clear action can repeat take after take, which waiting for a feeling cannot ensure.

film-school.fs-act-5.q1.t: What prevents the objective from being achieved
film-school.fs-act-5.q1.p: What is an obstacle in scene study?
film-school.fs-act-5.q1.h: Without it there is no scene.
film-school.fs-act-5.q1.e: The obstacle prevents the objective and must be as strong as the objective.

film-school.fs-act-5.q2.p: Your tactic fails and your character switches to another. What is that?
film-school.fs-act-5.q2.e: When a tactic fails and another begins, that is a beat change.

film-school.fs-act-5.q3.t: Playing the emotion skips the causal chain and goes to the symptom
film-school.fs-act-5.q3.p: Why does the lesson tell actors to play the action rather than the emotion?
film-school.fs-act-5.q3.h: Pursue an objective against an obstacle.
film-school.fs-act-5.q3.e: Chasing an objective against a real obstacle produces genuine emotion; deciding the scene is sad produces the symptom.

film-school.fs-act-6.q1.t: The camera sits close and records involuntary micro-behaviour
film-school.fs-act-6.q1.p: What is the key scale difference between stage and screen acting?
film-school.fs-act-6.q1.e: The close camera photographs thought, so do it for real and let the lens find it.

film-school.fs-act-6.q2.t: Continuity: actions must match across coverage
film-school.fs-act-6.q2.p: You shot a scene yesterday and today you pick up the cup in the other hand. What is the problem?
film-school.fs-act-6.q2.e: Actors must reproduce physical details so shots cut together.

film-school.fs-act-6.q3.t: They produce feeling reliably across many takes
film-school.fs-act-6.q3.p: Why do action-based approaches dominate screen work?
film-school.fs-act-6.q3.e: Screen work needs reliable life on every take, and action-based approaches deliver it.

film-school.fs-act-7.q1.t: Making no choice, a safe general read
film-school.fs-act-7.q1.p: What is the most common audition failure according to the lesson?
film-school.fs-act-7.q1.e: The most common failure is giving the room nothing to respond to.

film-school.fs-act-7.q2.t: Stay in it and keep going
film-school.fs-act-7.q2.p: You stumble over a line during an audition. What should you do?
film-school.fs-act-7.q2.e: Staying in it through a stumble shows how you behave on a set.

film-school.fs-act-7.q3.t: Just beside the lens so your eyeline is slightly off-camera
film-school.fs-act-7.q3.p: For a self-tape, where should your reader sit?
film-school.fs-act-7.q3.e: The reader sits beside the lens so your eyeline is slightly off-camera unless asked otherwise.

film-school.fs-act-8.q1.t: Remove tensions blocking the voice a person already has
film-school.fs-act-8.q1.p: What is Kristin Linklater's goal in voice work, according to the lesson?
film-school.fs-act-8.q1.e: Linklater frames the goal as removing tensions that block the existing voice.

film-school.fs-act-8.q2.p: You want a practical way to answer "how does this person move?" Which system analyses weight, space, time and flow?
film-school.fs-act-8.q2.h: Heavy and direct versus light and indirect.
film-school.fs-act-8.q2.e: Laban's effort system analyses movement along weight, space, time and flow.

film-school.fs-act-8.q3.t: A large physical shape of the character's inner drive, rehearsed then internalised
film-school.fs-act-8.q3.p: What is Michael Chekhov's Psychological Gesture?
film-school.fs-act-8.q3.e: Chekhov distils the inner drive into a physical shape that is rehearsed, then internalised so it informs the performance invisibly.

photo-art-school.px-1.q1.p: Which three controls govern how much light lands on the recording surface?
photo-art-school.px-1.q1.h: Think hole size, time, and sensitivity.
photo-art-school.px-1.q1.e: The lesson names aperture (size of the hole), shutter speed (how long it stays open) and ISO (how strongly the surface reacts) as the three light controls.

photo-art-school.px-1.q2.t: Aperture, giving up light per moment for depth of field
photo-art-school.px-1.q2.p: You want a landscape sharp from foreground rock to distant mountain. Which of the three controls are you mainly spending?
photo-art-school.px-1.q2.h: Which control buys depth of field?
photo-art-school.px-1.q2.e: Aperture buys depth of field; a small opening gives deep focus but passes less light, so you must compensate elsewhere.

photo-art-school.px-1.q3.p: According to the lesson, a correct exposure is whatever number the camera meter calculates.
photo-art-school.px-1.q3.h: Who decides what the picture should look like?
photo-art-school.px-1.q3.e: The lesson says correct exposure is the brightness that serves the picture you intend, and the meter is only a suggestion from a machine that cannot see your subject.

photo-art-school.px-2.q1.t: Focal length divided by the diameter of the opening
photo-art-school.px-2.q1.p: What is an f-number a ratio of?
photo-art-school.px-2.q1.h: It is why larger numbers mean smaller holes.
photo-art-school.px-2.q1.e: The f-number is focal length divided by aperture diameter, so a bigger number means a smaller opening.

photo-art-school.px-2.q2.p: You are shooting a portrait and want only the eyes sharp with the ears dissolving. Which aperture is the best choice?
photo-art-school.px-2.q2.h: You want a very thin band of sharpness.
photo-art-school.px-2.q2.e: Wide open, such as f/1.4, gives millimetre-thin depth of field; f/11 and f/16 hold much more of the scene sharp.

photo-art-school.px-2.q3.t: Depth of field is a way of saying something, and always using shallow depth repeats one sentence
photo-art-school.px-2.q3.p: Why does the lesson advise against shooting everything wide open?
photo-art-school.px-2.q3.h: The lesson compares depth of field to sentence structure.
photo-art-school.px-2.q3.e: Shallow depth says only this matters; deep depth says everything and its relationships. Using one always repeats one statement.

photo-art-school.px-3.q1.p: By the reciprocal rule, what is the slowest recommended hand-held shutter speed for a 200mm lens?
photo-art-school.px-3.q1.e: The reciprocal rule says hand-hold no slower than one over the focal length, so 200mm wants 1/200s or faster.

photo-art-school.px-3.q2.t: Use a slow shutter speed such as two seconds, ideally on a stable support
photo-art-school.px-3.q2.p: You want a river to look like silk and a crowd to turn into ghosts. What do you do?
photo-art-school.px-3.q2.e: A slow exposure accumulates, so only the stationary parts of the scene register consistently while moving elements smear.

photo-art-school.px-3.q3.t: It stabilises your hands, not a moving subject
photo-art-school.px-3.q3.p: Why does image stabilisation not solve every blur problem?
photo-art-school.px-3.q3.e: Stabilisation compensates for camera shake but cannot freeze a subject that moves during the exposure.

photo-art-school.px-4.q1.t: Amplifies the signal already collected, noise included
photo-art-school.px-4.q1.p: What does raising ISO actually do, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.px-4.q1.e: ISO amplifies the signal off the sensor; it does not collect more light, and noise rises with it.

photo-art-school.px-4.q2.t: Expose brighter, then pull down in editing
photo-art-school.px-4.q2.p: In low light you can either shoot underexposed at low ISO and brighten later, or expose properly at higher ISO. Following expose for the shadows you intend to keep, which is usually cleaner?
photo-art-school.px-4.q2.h: Noise lives in the underexposed parts.
photo-art-school.px-4.q2.e: A brighter capture pulled down is almost always cleaner than a dark one pushed up, since noise lives in underexposed regions.

photo-art-school.px-4.q3.p: The lesson argues a sharp noisy photograph is better than a clean blurred one.
photo-art-school.px-4.q3.h: Grain is a texture; blur from timidity is a mistake.
photo-art-school.px-4.q3.e: The lesson says a sharp noisy photograph beats a clean blurred one every time, so be willing to raise ISO.

photo-art-school.px-5.q1.p: Roughly what reflectance does a reflective meter assume the scene averages to?
photo-art-school.px-5.q1.e: Meters assume middle grey, about 18% reflectance.

photo-art-school.px-5.q2.p: You are photographing a snowy field and the camera renders the snow grey. What correction fixes it?
photo-art-school.px-5.q2.h: The meter wants to make everything average.
photo-art-school.px-5.q2.e: Snow fools the meter into underexposing, so you add +1 to +2 stops of compensation.

photo-art-school.px-5.q3.t: Clipped highlights contain no data and cannot be recovered, whereas shadows can often be lifted at the cost of noise
photo-art-school.px-5.q3.p: Why are blown highlights treated as worse than crushed shadows?
photo-art-school.px-5.q3.h: Think about what remains in the file.
photo-art-school.px-5.q3.e: Pixels clipped at the white wall are gone, while crushed shadows can often be lifted although they become noisier.

photo-art-school.px-6.q1.p: On full-frame, which focal length range does the lesson call classic portraiture?
photo-art-school.px-6.q1.e: The lesson lists 85-135mm as classic portraiture.

photo-art-school.px-6.q2.t: The change in where you stood, which alters perspective
photo-art-school.px-6.q2.p: You shoot a face with a 24mm lens from one metre and a 200mm lens from eight metres, then compare. What explains the different look?
photo-art-school.px-6.q2.e: Perspective is determined by camera position; wide lenses make you step closer, exaggerating near-to-far size differences.

photo-art-school.px-6.q3.p: A 35mm lens on an APS-C camera frames like roughly what on full-frame?
photo-art-school.px-6.q3.e: APS-C multiplies the effective angle, so 35mm frames like about 52mm; the sensor sees a smaller part of the image circle.

photo-art-school.px-7.q1.p: Which autofocus mode should you use for moving subjects?
photo-art-school.px-7.q1.h: One mode locks, the other tracks.
photo-art-school.px-7.q1.e: Continuous AF tracks moving subjects; single AF locks and holds for stationary ones.

photo-art-school.px-7.q2.p: You are shooting through a chain-link fence and the camera keeps focusing on the wire. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.px-7.q2.e: Shooting through obstructions is one of three situations where manual focus still wins, because AF grabs the fence.

photo-art-school.px-7.q3.t: It separates focusing from the shutter release so you can recompose and never refocus accidentally at release
photo-art-school.px-7.q3.p: What is the main advantage of back-button focus?
photo-art-school.px-7.q3.e: Assigning AF to a rear button means the shutter only fires, so you focus when you choose and recompose freely.

photo-art-school.px-8.q1.t: A RAW is the negative, with white balance stored as a note; a JPEG is a finished print
photo-art-school.px-8.q1.p: How does the lesson describe a RAW file compared with a JPEG?
photo-art-school.px-8.q1.e: The lesson says a JPEG is a finished print with settings baked in, while RAW is the unprocessed negative with white balance stored as a note.

photo-art-school.px-8.q2.t: Shoot RAW and change white balance in editing
photo-art-school.px-8.q2.p: You shot a series under tungsten light and the colour looks wrong. Which approach gives the cleanest fix after the fact?
photo-art-school.px-8.q2.h: One format stores white balance as a note.
photo-art-school.px-8.q2.e: RAW lets you change white balance after shooting with no penalty, which JPEG cannot do cleanly.

photo-art-school.px-8.q3.p: An unprocessed RAW file looking flat and dull usually means something is wrong with the camera.
photo-art-school.px-8.q3.e: The lesson says RAW is meant to look flat; that is headroom for editing, not a fault.

photo-art-school.pc-1.q1.t: Photographers cut a rectangle from an infinite world, so the question is what to get rid of
photo-art-school.pc-1.q1.p: Why does the lesson call photographic composition subtractive?
photo-art-school.pc-1.q1.h: Compare to painting on an empty surface.
photo-art-school.pc-1.q1.e: Painters add to an empty surface, whereas photographers begin with the whole world and decide what to leave out.

photo-art-school.pc-1.q2.p: Before pressing the shutter you spot a pole seeming to grow out of your subject head. What does the lesson say is usually the fix?
photo-art-school.pc-1.q2.e: These edge problems are all fixed by moving two feet, which is why you should scan the four borders.

photo-art-school.pc-1.q3.p: Which aspect ratio does the lesson say removes any argument about direction and suits portraits and still life?
photo-art-school.pc-1.q3.e: The square 1:1 frame forces the eye to the centre and removes directional arguments.

photo-art-school.pc-2.q1.p: What two blandest options does the rule of thirds prevent?
photo-art-school.pc-2.q1.e: Placing subjects near the third lines avoids dead centre and dead edge placements.

photo-art-school.pc-2.q2.t: Centre the subject deliberately for symmetry
photo-art-school.pc-2.q2.p: You want a formal, confrontational, monumental portrait. Which composition choice fits?
photo-art-school.pc-2.q2.e: The lesson says symmetry reads as formal, confrontational, monumental and still; a dead-centred portrait stares back at the viewer.

photo-art-school.pc-2.q3.p: What does the lesson say is the real principle underneath both thirds and symmetry?
photo-art-school.pc-2.q3.h: The eye notices when weight pools in one corner.
photo-art-school.pc-2.q3.e: Both are ways of balancing the frame visual weight, which is more important than any grid.

photo-art-school.pc-3.q1.p: In left-to-right reading cultures, where does the eye usually enter a photograph, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.pc-3.q1.h: Think about the corner where reading starts at the bottom.
photo-art-school.pc-3.q1.e: The lesson says the eye usually enters bottom-left in left-to-right reading cultures.

photo-art-school.pc-3.q2.t: One interruption, such as a single figure or broken element
photo-art-school.pc-3.q2.p: You photograph a row of identical arches and want a story rather than mere pattern. What should you add?
photo-art-school.pc-3.q2.e: Pure repetition is decorative and static; repetition with one interruption becomes a story and the interruption becomes the subject.

photo-art-school.pc-3.q3.p: Which shape does the lesson call the most stable arrangement of three subjects?
photo-art-school.pc-3.q3.e: The triangle is the most stable arrangement and underpins most classical group portraits.

photo-art-school.pc-4.q1.p: What are the three layers of a layered photograph?
photo-art-school.pc-4.q1.e: A layered photograph has a foreground, middle ground and background, each carrying information.

photo-art-school.pc-4.q2.t: Frame it and wait for the foreground to arrive
photo-art-school.pc-4.q2.p: You find a background with great light and a gesture. Following the lesson method, what do you do next?
photo-art-school.pc-4.q2.e: The method is to find a worthwhile background, frame it, then wait for a foreground element to converge.

photo-art-school.pc-4.q3.t: The instant when form and content align
photo-art-school.pc-4.q3.p: What did Henri Cartier-Bresson decisive moment actually describe, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pc-4.q3.h: It is not just about action.
photo-art-school.pc-4.q3.e: The lesson says it is when the geometry of the frame and the meaning of the event become right together.

photo-art-school.pc-5.q1.t: The emptiness around a subject, treated as an active material
photo-art-school.pc-5.q1.p: How does the lesson define negative space?
photo-art-school.pc-5.q1.e: Negative space is the emptiness around a subject and acts as a compositional material.

photo-art-school.pc-5.q2.t: Crouch so the subject sits against sky
photo-art-school.pc-5.q2.p: A cluttered background ruins your portrait. Which tactic from the lesson helps?
photo-art-school.pc-5.q2.e: Changing your height lets you place the subject against a simple background such as sky; opening the aperture also dissolves clutter.

photo-art-school.pc-5.q3.t: The space around the subject shapes meaning
photo-art-school.pc-5.q3.p: The same small figure reads as solitude in a vast field of snow but as presence when filling the frame. What does this show?
photo-art-school.pc-5.q3.e: The subject did not change; the space did, showing negative space actively shapes meaning.

photo-art-school.pc-6.q1.p: What happens when you lower the camera, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pc-6.q1.e: Lowering the camera makes you look up at the subject, so it gains stature against sky.

photo-art-school.pc-6.q2.p: You want viewers to identify with a figure, looking with them rather than at them. Which camera position fits?
photo-art-school.pc-6.q2.e: The figure seen from behind creates identification, a staple from Friedrich onward.

photo-art-school.pc-6.q3.t: Adult eye-level is a default viewpoint looking down; their own eye level makes them look like people
photo-art-school.pc-6.q3.p: Why do children and animals photographed from adult height look like specimens?
photo-art-school.pc-6.q3.e: From above they are observed as specimens; at their own eye level they feel like people.

photo-art-school.pc-7.q1.p: What does the lesson say photographers are usually read through?
photo-art-school.pc-7.q1.e: Reputations are built through series: picture stories, essays, books and portfolios.

photo-art-school.pc-7.q2.t: Variety of scale: establishing wides, mid-shots, details and portraits
photo-art-school.pc-7.q2.p: Your twenty-frame set is all shot at the same distance. What does the lesson suggest it needs?
photo-art-school.pc-7.q2.e: A working series needs variety of scale, otherwise it is monotonous however good each frame is.

photo-art-school.pc-7.q3.t: A weak frame drags down the frames beside it, and twelve strong beat forty adequate
photo-art-school.pc-7.q3.p: Why edit ruthlessly in a series?
photo-art-school.pc-7.q3.e: The lesson says twelve strong frames beat forty adequate ones and a weak frame drags down its neighbours.

photo-art-school.pl-1.q1.p: Which four properties can describe any lighting situation?
photo-art-school.pl-1.q1.h: Think soft/hard, where from, how much, what temperature.
photo-art-school.pl-1.q1.e: The lesson lists quality, direction, intensity and colour as the four properties of light.

photo-art-school.pl-1.q2.t: Make the source bigger or bring it closer
photo-art-school.pl-1.q2.p: You have a bare flash and want softer light on a portrait. What works?
photo-art-school.pl-1.q2.h: Quality depends on source size relative to subject.
photo-art-school.pl-1.q2.e: Softness depends on source size relative to the subject, so enlarge the source or bring it closer.

photo-art-school.pl-1.q3.t: It inverts the lifelong assumption that light falls from above
photo-art-school.pl-1.q3.p: Why is bottom light the horror-film convention?
photo-art-school.pl-1.q3.e: Light normally comes from above, so lighting from below feels unnatural and unsettling.

photo-art-school.pl-2.q1.t: The fading sky against artificial lights
photo-art-school.pl-2.q1.p: What does blue hour balance, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.pl-2.q1.e: Blue hour balances the fading sky against artificial lights so both can be exposed correctly together.

photo-art-school.pl-2.q2.t: Put them in open shade and use the sunlit street as background
photo-art-school.pl-2.q2.p: You must photograph a person at noon in hard sun. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pl-2.q2.h: Use hard light for shape and shadow, not faces.
photo-art-school.pl-2.q2.e: The lesson suggests using hard midday light for shape and shadow, or placing the subject in open shade against a sunlit background.

photo-art-school.pl-2.q3.t: It makes almost anything look pleasant, which is not the same as good
photo-art-school.pl-2.q3.p: What is the lesson main caution about golden hour?
photo-art-school.pl-2.q3.e: The lesson warns that golden light is easy and flattering, which risks sentimentality rather than quality.

photo-art-school.pl-3.q1.p: Which window orientation does the lesson say produced most great Western portraiture before electric light?
photo-art-school.pl-3.q1.e: The lesson names the north-facing window as the source of most of the greatest portraiture.

photo-art-school.pl-3.q2.t: Add a reflector on the shadow side
photo-art-school.pl-3.q2.p: The shadow side of a window-lit face is too dark. What quick fix does the lesson give?
photo-art-school.pl-3.q2.e: A white board, sheet or wall bounces light into the shadows; moving it closer reduces contrast.

photo-art-school.pl-3.q3.p: Which pattern is defined by a small triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek?
photo-art-school.pl-3.q3.e: Rembrandt lighting produces a small triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek.

photo-art-school.pl-4.q1.t: The source is tiny and on the lens axis, giving hard, frontal light
photo-art-school.pl-4.q1.p: Why is direct on-camera flash disliked?
photo-art-school.pl-4.q1.e: A tiny source on the lens axis gives flat faces, black shadows behind and red eye.

photo-art-school.pl-4.q2.p: You want fill flash outdoors that nobody can tell is flash. What compensation does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pl-4.q2.h: Just enough to lift the face.
photo-art-school.pl-4.q2.e: The lesson says dial flash to -1 to -2 stops of compensation so it lifts the face subtly.

photo-art-school.pl-4.q3.p: Why does shutter speed control the ambient light but not the flash exposure?
photo-art-school.pl-4.q3.h: Think of how brief the burst is.
photo-art-school.pl-4.q3.e: Because the flash burst is so short, shutter speed mainly affects ambient light while aperture and flash power control the flash.

photo-art-school.pl-5.q1.t: Make the source bigger and softer, or smaller and more controlled
photo-art-school.pl-5.q1.p: What two jobs does every modifier do?
photo-art-school.pl-5.q1.e: Modifiers either enlarge the source for softer light or shrink and control it for harder, directional light.

photo-art-school.pl-5.q2.p: You want a pool of light on a face with the room going black. Which tool fits?
photo-art-school.pl-5.q2.e: Grids and snoots restrict spread so the light lands only where pointed.

photo-art-school.pl-5.q3.p: A 4:1 or 8:1 key-to-fill ratio produces what look?
photo-art-school.pl-5.q3.e: The lesson says 1:1 is flat and commercial, while 4:1 or 8:1 is dramatic and cinematic.

photo-art-school.pl-6.q1.p: What does chiaroscuro mean in Italian?
photo-art-school.pl-6.q1.e: Chiaroscuro means light-dark: the modelling of form through strong contrast.

photo-art-school.pl-6.q2.t: A small hard source high and to one side, no fill, exposing for highlights
photo-art-school.pl-6.q2.p: To recreate Caravaggio-style light with a camera, what setup does the lesson give?
photo-art-school.pl-6.q2.e: Caravaggio used a small hard source high and to one side with no fill; expose for highlights and let shadows go black.

photo-art-school.pl-6.q3.t: Shadow is information that masters lit to place
photo-art-school.pl-6.q3.p: What transferable insight does the lesson draw about shadow?
photo-art-school.pl-6.q3.e: Beginners light to eliminate shadow; the masters lit to place it.

photo-art-school.pl-7.q1.t: Pools of hard small sources with brutal fall-off
photo-art-school.pl-7.q1.p: How does the lesson describe city light at night?
photo-art-school.pl-7.q1.e: Cities at night are lit by pools, each a hard small source with brutal fall-off.

photo-art-school.pl-7.q2.t: Focus on a light-dark edge or pre-focus manually and wait for the subject
photo-art-school.pl-7.q2.p: Autofocus hunts in the dark. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pl-7.q2.e: Focus on an edge where light meets dark, or pre-focus at a set distance and wait for the subject.

photo-art-school.pl-7.q3.p: The lesson treats black in a night photograph as a failure of exposure.
photo-art-school.pl-7.q3.e: The lesson says black is the majority of the frame and can carry a picture entirely; it is not a failure.

photo-art-school.pk-1.q1.p: Which three dimensions of colour does the lesson name?
photo-art-school.pk-1.q1.e: Colour has hue, saturation and luminance.

photo-art-school.pk-1.q2.t: Acting as structure that directs the eye
photo-art-school.pk-1.q2.p: A frame has a red coat as the only warm object in a cold scene. According to the lesson, colour here is doing what?
photo-art-school.pk-1.q2.h: It is where you want the eye.
photo-art-school.pk-1.q2.e: The lesson uses this as an example of colour becoming structure rather than default.

photo-art-school.pk-1.q3.t: It marked colour becoming a subject rather than a description
photo-art-school.pk-1.q3.p: What was the significance of William Eggleston 1976 MoMA exhibition?
photo-art-school.pk-1.q3.h: It was widely panned at the time.
photo-art-school.pk-1.q3.e: The lesson says it was reviewed badly but is now understood as when colour became a subject.

photo-art-school.pk-2.q1.e: Blue and orange sit opposite on the wheel and give maximum contrast.

photo-art-school.pk-2.q2.t: Scout for a blue wall and put an orange subject against it
photo-art-school.pk-2.q2.p: You want to use blue-orange harmony in street work. What does the lesson recommend?
photo-art-school.pk-2.q2.e: The lesson says use the colour wheel to scout, since harmony invented in post is usually visible and bad.

photo-art-school.pk-2.q3.t: Neighbouring hues are harmonious but easily boring, so contrast must come from brightness
photo-art-school.pk-2.q3.p: Why do analogous schemes need luminance contrast?
photo-art-school.pk-2.q3.e: Analogous hues are unified and calm but flat, so luminance contrast keeps them interesting.

photo-art-school.pk-3.q1.p: Which is bluer in colour temperature, 3000K or 8000K?
photo-art-school.pk-3.q1.e: Higher Kelvin is bluer because it describes the emitting black body temperature; deep shade is around 8000K.

photo-art-school.pk-3.q2.p: You set white balance to tungsten while shooting in daylight. What happens?
photo-art-school.pk-3.q2.h: White balance pushes in the opposite direction.
photo-art-school.pk-3.q2.e: Tungsten setting compensates for orange light, so in daylight everything shifts blue.

photo-art-school.pk-3.q3.t: They add a green spike needing magenta tint correction on a separate axis
photo-art-school.pk-3.q3.p: Why do some fluorescent interiors look sickly regardless of Kelvin?
photo-art-school.pk-3.q3.e: Fluorescent and cheap LED light add a green spike corrected on the tint axis, not by Kelvin.

photo-art-school.pk-4.q1.p: What survives when converting to black and white?
photo-art-school.pk-4.q1.e: In monochrome hue disappears and only luminance survives.

photo-art-school.pk-4.q2.p: You want almost-black skies in a landscape conversion. Which filter effect does the lesson name?
photo-art-school.pk-4.q2.e: A red filter darkens blue sky dramatically, as in Adams skies.

photo-art-school.pk-4.q3.t: Red and green can convert to nearly identical greys
photo-art-school.pk-4.q3.p: Why does a red apple on green grass vanish in conversion?
photo-art-school.pk-4.q3.e: The two hues can have similar luminance, so they turn into nearly identical greys.

photo-art-school.pk-5.q1.p: What does white symbolise in much of East and South Asia, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pk-5.q1.e: The lesson says white is mourning across much of East and South Asia.

photo-art-school.pk-5.q2.t: Do not assume they transfer and ask
photo-art-school.pk-5.q2.p: You are photographing a culture not your own. What does the lesson advise?
photo-art-school.pk-5.q2.e: Do not assume your associations transfer, and do not grade someone else home into a look; ask.

photo-art-school.pk-5.q3.p: Which cinematic convention does the lesson link to institutions and menace?
photo-art-school.pk-5.q3.e: Sickly green is the convention for institutions and menace.

photo-art-school.pk-6.q1.p: What does the lesson say a palette usually is?
photo-art-school.pk-6.q1.e: A palette is built from consistent decisions about light, location, skin treatment and black point.

photo-art-school.pk-6.q2.t: Start from constraints: a few hues, a time of day, a contrast level
photo-art-school.pk-6.q2.p: You are starting a new project and want a consistent look. What does the lesson recommend?
photo-art-school.pk-6.q2.e: Choose two or three hues, a time of day and a contrast level, and apply them throughout.

photo-art-school.pk-6.q3.t: Presets calibrated on light skin can render deeper tones muddy or grey
photo-art-school.pk-6.q3.p: Why should skin tone grading be checked across the full range of subjects?
photo-art-school.pk-6.q3.h: One number does not fit all.
photo-art-school.pk-6.q3.e: The lesson warns a grading approach calibrated only on light skin can muddy deeper skin tones.

photo-art-school.pg-1.q1.p: Which eye should you focus on in a portrait?
photo-art-school.pg-1.q1.e: The lesson says focus on the near eye, always.

photo-art-school.pg-1.q2.t: Give a task such as look out of the window or walk toward me
photo-art-school.pg-1.q2.p: Your subject looks rigid when told to relax. What does the lesson recommend instead?
photo-art-school.pg-1.q2.e: Directions that give a task produce natural bodies, whereas relax produces rigidity.

photo-art-school.pg-1.q3.t: Environmental portraits use context to explain the person; studio portraits strip context to focus on the face
photo-art-school.pg-1.q3.p: What is the difference between environmental and studio portraits?
photo-art-school.pg-1.q3.e: Both are legitimate; they make different claims about the subject.

photo-art-school.pg-2.q1.p: Which lens range does the lesson recommend for street photography?
photo-art-school.pg-2.q1.e: Wide-to-normal lenses of 28-50mm, getting close, are recommended.

photo-art-school.pg-2.q2.t: Work the scene with ten or twenty frames
photo-art-school.pg-2.q2.p: You see a promising scene. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pg-2.q2.e: The lesson advises ten or twenty frames of a promising situation rather than one.

photo-art-school.pg-2.q3.t: Photographing in public is often legal but ethics go beyond the law, such as not exploiting vulnerable people
photo-art-school.pg-2.q3.p: Which statement about law and ethics in street photography matches the lesson?
photo-art-school.pg-2.q3.e: The lesson says law and ethics are different, and vulnerability is not free subject matter.

photo-art-school.pg-3.q1.p: What does the lesson say is the main reason most landscape photographs fail?
photo-art-school.pg-3.q1.e: Most landscape photographs fail because they lack a foreground.

photo-art-school.pg-3.q2.p: Which filter does the lesson say cannot be replicated in software?
photo-art-school.pg-3.q2.e: A polariser cuts reflections off water and foliage and deepens sky in a way software cannot.

photo-art-school.pg-3.q3.t: Beautiful pictures with nothing to say
photo-art-school.pg-3.q3.p: The lesson calls landscape the genre most prone to what?
photo-art-school.pg-3.q3.e: It warns the genre often yields beautiful pictures with nothing to say, and suggests asking about your relationship to place.

photo-art-school.pg-4.q1.p: Which edit is allowed in a news context per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pg-4.q1.e: Global tone, contrast, colour balance and crop are allowed; adding or removing content is not.

photo-art-school.pg-4.q2.p: Where does the lesson say most ethical failures in photojournalism happen?
photo-art-school.pg-4.q2.e: The lesson says most ethical failures are caption failures.

photo-art-school.pg-4.q3.t: It is both a great documentary corpus and a case study in government-funded persuasion
photo-art-school.pg-4.q3.p: What lesson does the FSA archive teach?
photo-art-school.pg-4.q3.e: Both facts are true: it is fine documentary and government-funded persuasion.

photo-art-school.pg-5.q1.t: Everything in the frame is your decision, so every weakness is authorship
photo-art-school.pg-5.q1.p: Why is still life described as merciless?
photo-art-school.pg-5.q1.e: Since nothing moves, every weakness is yours.

photo-art-school.pg-5.q2.t: The reflection, such as with a large white card
photo-art-school.pg-5.q2.p: You photograph a glossy object. What does the lesson say you light?
photo-art-school.pg-5.q2.e: On glossy surfaces you light what is reflected, so a large white card becomes the highlight.

photo-art-school.pg-5.q3.p: Which lighting approach suits bottles, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pg-5.q3.e: Back-lighting through a diffuser makes glass and liquid glow and separates them from the background.

photo-art-school.pg-6.q1.t: Vertical lines converging when a wide lens points up
photo-art-school.pg-6.q1.h: The building appears to fall backwards.
photo-art-school.pg-6.q1.e: Pointing a wide lens upward makes verticals converge, the defining architectural problem.

photo-art-school.pg-6.q2.p: Which lens is the historical solution to keystoning?
photo-art-school.pg-6.q2.e: A tilt-shift lens keeps the sensor parallel to the facade while shifting the image circle.

photo-art-school.pg-6.q3.p: When would you include people in architectural photography?
photo-art-school.pg-6.q3.e: People suit architecture-as-life; architecture-as-form excludes them.

photo-art-school.pg-7.q1.t: It happens once and cannot be reshot
photo-art-school.pg-7.q1.p: What single constraint defines event photography, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.pg-7.q1.e: Event photography is defined by the fact that it happens once, so every other skill is subordinated to reliability.

photo-art-school.pg-7.q2.t: Shoot to dual slots and back up twice before sleeping
photo-art-school.pg-7.q2.p: Your camera has two card slots. What does the lesson advise?
photo-art-school.pg-7.q2.e: The lesson says cards fail, so record to both slots and back up twice.

photo-art-school.pg-7.q3.t: Reactions are frequently better than the event itself
photo-art-school.pg-7.q3.p: Why does the lesson say to photograph the audience during a speech?
photo-art-school.pg-7.q3.h: Think about what tells the story.
photo-art-school.pg-7.q3.e: The lesson says reactions are frequently better than the event, such as the mother during the vows.

photo-art-school.pg-8.q1.p: What does the lesson call genres?
photo-art-school.pg-8.q1.h: Nobody serious has a body of work called by one.
photo-art-school.pg-8.q1.e: Genres are training wheels; serious bodies of work are specific enquiries that happen to be conducted in a genre.

photo-art-school.pg-8.q2.t: One paragraph stating what it is about
photo-art-school.pg-8.q2.p: You want to start a project. The lesson suggests writing what?
photo-art-school.pg-8.q2.h: If you cannot, it is only a subject.
photo-art-school.pg-8.q2.e: If you cannot write the one-paragraph statement it is a subject, not yet a project.

photo-art-school.pg-8.q3.t: A self-imposed restriction such as one lens, one place, one year makes work coherent
photo-art-school.pg-8.q3.p: Why does constraint generate originality more reliably than freedom?
photo-art-school.pg-8.q3.e: The lesson says the photographers we know mostly worked under self-imposed restriction, which made the work coherent.

photo-art-school.pe-1.q1.p: What did editing historically mean in photography?
photo-art-school.pe-1.q1.e: Editing meant selecting frames; processing meant adjusting them.

photo-art-school.pe-1.q2.t: After leaving them for a week
photo-art-school.pe-1.q2.p: You have just returned from a shoot. When does the lesson suggest judging your best frames?
photo-art-school.pe-1.q2.e: You cannot see your own work the day you shot it, so leave it for a week before the second pass.

photo-art-school.pe-1.q3.t: Processing frames you will not use wastes a weekend and produces nothing
photo-art-school.pe-1.q3.p: Why should you select before processing?
photo-art-school.pe-1.q3.e: The lesson says processing a hundred unused frames is how photographers spend weekends and produce nothing.

photo-art-school.pe-2.q1.p: What does the lesson list as the first step of a good global edit?
photo-art-school.pe-2.q1.e: The first step is setting black and white points using the histogram.

photo-art-school.pe-2.q2.p: You want a matte, faded film look. What do you do on the tone curve?
photo-art-school.pe-2.q2.h: Blacks do not go fully black.
photo-art-school.pe-2.q2.e: Lifting the bottom-left point of the curve creates the matte faded look; dropping it deepens blacks.

photo-art-school.pe-2.q3.t: Over-lifted shadows leaving no dark areas
photo-art-school.pe-2.q3.p: What is described as the most common failure of modern editing?
photo-art-school.pe-2.q3.e: A picture with no dark areas reads as artificial and lifeless.

photo-art-school.pe-3.q1.e: Dodging lightens and burning darkens selected areas.

photo-art-school.pe-3.q2.p: A bright corner distracts from your subject. What local fix does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pe-3.q2.e: Burn down bright corners and distracting patches so the eye goes to the subject.

photo-art-school.pe-3.q3.t: Printing choices such as dodging and burning interpret the raw material
photo-art-school.pe-3.q3.p: What did Ansel Adams mean by the negative being the score and the print the performance?
photo-art-school.pe-3.q3.e: The negative holds the potential and the print is an interpretation made through dodging and burning.

photo-art-school.pe-4.q1.p: On which three axes does professional colour grading work, per band?
photo-art-school.pe-4.q1.e: Grading works on hue, saturation and luminance for each colour band.

photo-art-school.pe-4.q2.p: You want to deepen a sky without touching other colours. Which move does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pe-4.q2.e: Darkening blues deepens sky without affecting other regions.

photo-art-school.pe-4.q3.t: It exaggerates the natural blue-shadow/warm-sun relationship
photo-art-school.pe-4.q3.p: Why is cool shadows with warm highlights the near-universal cinematic default?
photo-art-school.pe-4.q3.e: It amplifies the natural relationship between blue shadows and warm sunlight.

photo-art-school.pe-5.q1.e: Sharpening increases local contrast at edges so detail reads more clearly.

photo-art-school.pe-5.q2.p: You export for web. Which colour space does the lesson recommend?
photo-art-school.pe-5.q2.e: sRGB is recommended for web because other spaces can look desaturated in browsers that ignore profiles.

photo-art-school.pe-5.q3.t: Denoise first, sharpen last at output size
photo-art-school.pe-5.q3.p: What is the recommended processing order for noise and sharpening?
photo-art-school.pe-5.q3.e: Denoise first and sharpen last, for the size the picture will be seen.

photo-art-school.pe-6.q1.t: Originals are never altered; adjustments are stored as instructions
photo-art-school.pe-6.q1.e: The original file is never changed and adjustments are applied on export.

photo-art-school.pe-6.q2.t: Three copies, two media, one off-site
photo-art-school.pe-6.q2.e: Three copies on two different media with one off-site.

photo-art-school.pe-6.q3.p: Why is cloud sync not a backup?
photo-art-school.pe-6.q3.e: Sync mirrors changes, so deleting a file deletes it everywhere.

photo-art-school.pe-7.q1.t: Whether the alteration is consistent with what the image claims
photo-art-school.pe-7.q1.p: What does the lesson say the real question about photographic manipulation is?
photo-art-school.pe-7.q1.e: All photographs are constructed; the test is whether the alteration fits what the image claims.

photo-art-school.pe-7.q2.p: Generative fill is used in a commercial composite. How does the lesson regard it?
photo-art-school.pe-7.q2.e: In a commercial composite it is ordinary craft; presented as documentation it would be fabrication.

photo-art-school.pe-7.q3.p: Why does disclosure matter more now?
photo-art-school.pe-7.q3.e: Generative tools make fabrication easy, so disclosure matters more than before.

photo-art-school.pb-1.q1.p: In most jurisdictions, who owns copyright in a photograph at creation?
photo-art-school.pb-1.q1.e: Copyright arises automatically and belongs to the photographer.

photo-art-school.pb-1.q2.t: It should carry a much higher price
photo-art-school.pb-1.q2.p: A client asks for all rights. What does the lesson say about price?
photo-art-school.pb-1.q2.e: A buyout sells the asset rather than renting it, so it should be priced much higher.

photo-art-school.pb-1.q3.p: When is a model release generally required?
photo-art-school.pb-1.q3.e: Releases are generally required for commercial and advertising use, not editorial, news or fine art.

photo-art-school.pb-2.q1.p: Roughly how many days a year does a full-time photographer bill, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.pb-2.q1.e: The lesson says perhaps 80 to 120 billable days a year.

photo-art-school.pb-2.q2.p: What two components make up a commercial fee?
photo-art-school.pb-2.q2.e: Creative fee covers time and expertise; licence fee covers the value of usage.

photo-art-school.pb-2.q3.t: The same labour can deliver very different value depending on usage
photo-art-school.pb-2.q3.p: Why price the job and not just the day?
photo-art-school.pb-2.q3.e: Identical labour can produce an order of magnitude different value, so usage shapes price.

photo-art-school.pb-3.q1.t: They are not delivered; a separate expensive licence if insisted
photo-art-school.pb-3.q1.p: Which delivery rule does the lesson state about RAW files?
photo-art-school.pb-3.q1.e: RAW files are your negatives; handing them over requires a separate, expensive licence.

photo-art-school.pb-3.q2.t: Have a polite prepared answer offering a reduced-scope paid option
photo-art-school.pb-3.q2.p: A client says they cannot pay but it is great exposure. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.pb-3.q2.e: Prepare a standard polite response that suggests a reduced-scope paid option.

photo-art-school.pb-3.q3.p: When should you chase a late invoice?
photo-art-school.pb-3.q3.e: Chase on day one of lateness rather than day thirty.

photo-art-school.pb-4.q1.t: Clients hire you to do again what they have seen you do
photo-art-school.pb-4.q1.p: What is the iron rule of portfolios in the lesson?
photo-art-school.pb-4.q1.e: Clients hire you to repeat what they have already seen you do.

photo-art-school.pb-4.q2.p: How many images does the lesson suggest in a portfolio?
photo-art-school.pb-4.q2.e: Fifteen to twenty-five images, all excellent.

photo-art-school.pb-4.q3.t: You cannot be hired for a job you have not demonstrated
photo-art-school.pb-4.q3.p: Why are self-directed projects the primary marketing tool in commercial photography?
photo-art-school.pb-4.q3.e: Nobody can hire you for a job you have never demonstrated, so personal work should mirror desired commissions.

photo-art-school.pb-5.q1.p: Which work pays the highest rate per day but is least predictable?
photo-art-school.pb-5.q1.e: Commissioned work is the highest rate per day and least predictable.

photo-art-school.pb-5.q2.p: What share do galleries typically take on print sales, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.pb-5.q2.e: Galleries take 40-50% in return for access and legitimacy.

photo-art-school.pb-5.q3.t: They hold up when commissions dry up
photo-art-school.pb-5.q3.p: Why are teaching and workshops described as counter-cyclical?
photo-art-school.pb-5.q3.e: They convert expertise to income and hold up when commissions dry up.

photo-art-school.pb-6.q1.p: What does the lesson say gets you the second job?
photo-art-school.pb-6.q1.e: Ability gets the first job; behaviour gets the second.

photo-art-school.pb-6.q2.p: During a shoot, what role does the lesson give the photographer?
photo-art-school.pb-6.q2.e: Clients and subjects take emotional cues from the photographer, so be the calmest person.

photo-art-school.pb-6.q3.t: The assistant today may be the photographer recommending you in five years
photo-art-school.pb-6.q3.p: Why pay assistants promptly and properly?
photo-art-school.pb-6.q3.e: The assistant on your set this year could be recommending you later.

photo-art-school.ae-1.q1.t: A moving point, the record of a gesture
photo-art-school.ae-1.q1.p: How does the lesson define line?
photo-art-school.ae-1.q1.e: Line is a moving point, preserving the speed, pressure and confidence of the hand.

photo-art-school.ae-1.q2.p: Which line type builds tone from accumulated marks?
photo-art-school.ae-1.q2.e: Hatching and cross-hatching build tone from accumulated lines.

photo-art-school.ae-1.q3.t: It describes three-dimensional form with a single stroke
photo-art-school.ae-1.q3.p: Why is a varied line thick in some places and thin in others?
photo-art-school.ae-1.q3.e: Thick where a form turns or catches shadow, thin where it recedes, creating three-dimensional form.

photo-art-school.ae-2.q1.t: Shape is two-dimensional, form three-dimensional or its illusion
photo-art-school.ae-2.q1.e: Shape is a two-dimensional enclosed area; form is three-dimensional or its illusion.

photo-art-school.ae-2.q2.t: The eye is less prejudiced about an abstract gap than about a known object
photo-art-school.ae-2.q2.p: Why do trained artists draw negative shapes?
photo-art-school.ae-2.q2.e: The eye holds fewer assumptions about an abstract gap than about a hand.

photo-art-school.ae-2.q3.p: Which depth device does the lesson call the oldest and most reliable?
photo-art-school.ae-2.q3.e: Overlapping is the oldest and most reliable depth device.

photo-art-school.ae-3.q1.e: Value is relative lightness or darkness and creates the illusion of form.

photo-art-school.ae-3.q2.p: You want to test whether a design works at its most basic level. Which Japanese concept reduces it to two values?
photo-art-school.ae-3.q2.e: Notan reduces an image to two values to test the underlying design.

photo-art-school.ae-3.q3.t: Value carries form and legibility and outranks colour
photo-art-school.ae-3.q3.p: Why does a painting with correct values and wrong colour still read, while the reverse turns to mud?
photo-art-school.ae-3.q3.e: Value does the work of form and legibility, so colour errors survive but value collapse does not.

photo-art-school.ae-4.q1.t: The physical surface of the work itself, such as impasto ridges
photo-art-school.ae-4.q1.e: Actual texture is the physical surface: impasto, canvas weave, grain, tooth of paper.

photo-art-school.ae-4.q2.t: Reproductions flatten the physical texture of the paint
photo-art-school.ae-4.q2.p: Why does the lesson argue for standing before the real Van Gogh at least once?
photo-art-school.ae-4.q2.e: Photographs flatten the ropes of paint and thick passages that you can only see in person.

photo-art-school.ae-4.q3.p: What did Picasso and Braque do in 1912 that changed the picture surface, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ae-4.q3.e: Gluing oilcloth to a canvas made the surface an object rather than a window.

photo-art-school.ae-5.q1.p: Which elements outweigh almost anything else in visual weight?
photo-art-school.ae-5.q1.e: The lesson says a face or figure outweighs almost anything because human attention is not neutral.

photo-art-school.ae-5.q2.p: A designer wants a formal, stable, institutional feel. Which balance suits?
photo-art-school.ae-5.q2.e: Symmetrical balance reads formal, stable, sacred and institutional.

photo-art-school.ae-5.q3.t: Competing emphases cancel each other, leaving no hierarchy
photo-art-school.ae-5.q3.p: Why is a composition with three competing focal points described as having none?
photo-art-school.ae-5.q3.e: Without a clear hierarchy of primary, secondary and supporting interest, nothing leads.

photo-art-school.ae-6.q1.p: What does repetition with variation create?
photo-art-school.ae-6.q1.e: Pattern with variation creates rhythm, which gives a sensation of movement.

photo-art-school.ae-6.q2.p: Which rhythm changes an element gradually to create directional movement?
photo-art-school.ae-6.q2.e: Progressive rhythm changes gradually and gives directional movement, like a receding arcade.

photo-art-school.ae-6.q3.t: Baroque uses sweeping diagonals to make the eye travel; Renaissance uses stable triangles to stop it
photo-art-school.ae-6.q3.p: How do Baroque and Renaissance compositions differ in handling the eye?
photo-art-school.ae-6.q3.e: Baroque diagonals send the eye travelling, whereas Renaissance triangles stabilise it.

photo-art-school.ae-7.q1.t: Size relative to a norm, usually the human body
photo-art-school.ae-7.q1.p: What does scale describe, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.ae-7.q1.e: Scale is size relative to a norm, typically the human body; proportion is part-to-whole.

photo-art-school.ae-7.q2.p: In an Egyptian relief the pharaoh is far larger than servants. What is this called?
photo-art-school.ae-7.q2.e: Hierarchical proportion sizes figures by importance rather than optical realism.

photo-art-school.ae-7.q3.t: Deliberate distortion straining upward toward the divine
photo-art-school.ae-7.q3.p: How does the lesson interpret El Greco elongated figures?
photo-art-school.ae-7.q3.e: Distortion is expressive; El Greco figures strain toward the divine.

photo-art-school.ae-8.q1.p: What two qualities must be held in tension, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.ae-8.q1.e: Unity (a work as one thing) and variety (interest) are balanced.

photo-art-school.ae-8.q2.p: Which Gestalt principle lets viewers complete a shape you only implied?
photo-art-school.ae-8.q2.e: Closure lets perception complete implied shapes.

photo-art-school.ae-8.q3.t: The freshness of a decisive mark cannot be recovered once softened repeatedly
photo-art-school.ae-8.q3.p: Why is overworking called the most common way to destroy an artwork?
photo-art-school.ae-8.q3.e: A decisive mark softened four times loses its freshness irrecoverably.

photo-art-school.ad-1.q1.t: The symbol the brain substitutes for the object
photo-art-school.ad-1.q1.p: What does the lesson say is the real obstacle to drawing?
photo-art-school.ad-1.q1.e: The brain supplies stored symbols instead of reporting the shape actually seen.

photo-art-school.ad-1.q2.p: Which exercise defeats naming by drawing without looking at the paper?
photo-art-school.ad-1.q2.h: Follow an edge with the eye only.
photo-art-school.ad-1.q2.e: Blind contour drawing follows an edge by eye while drawing without looking at the paper.

photo-art-school.ad-1.q3.p: Why does the lesson favour fifty quick bad drawings over one laboured good one?
photo-art-school.ad-1.q3.e: Corrections accumulate with volume, so many quick drawings teach more.

photo-art-school.ad-2.q1.p: How long does gesture drawing typically take, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ad-2.q1.e: Gesture drawings capture action in thirty seconds to two minutes.

photo-art-school.ad-2.q2.t: Gesture, construction, then contour and detail
photo-art-school.ad-2.q2.p: In which order does the lesson combine the stages?
photo-art-school.ad-2.q2.e: Gesture first, construction second, contour and detail last.

photo-art-school.ad-2.q3.p: What does the lesson say a hairy multi-line sketching habit reveals?
photo-art-school.ad-2.q3.e: Repeated lines are hesitation made visible, a habit rather than a limitation.

photo-art-school.ad-3.q1.t: The darkest band where the form turns fully away from the light
photo-art-school.ad-3.q1.p: What is the core shadow, or terminator?
photo-art-school.ad-3.q1.h: Darker than the cast shadow interior.
photo-art-school.ad-3.q1.e: The core shadow is the darkest band where form turns away, darker than the cast shadow interior.

photo-art-school.ad-3.q2.t: Reflected light must stay darker than the lightest halftone
photo-art-school.ad-3.q2.p: You make reflected light very bright and the form looks flat. What rule did you break?
photo-art-school.ad-3.q2.e: Reflected light that is too bright breaks the illusion; it must stay darker than the lightest halftone.

photo-art-school.ad-3.q3.t: Real form has no outline, only edges where value changes
photo-art-school.ad-3.q3.p: Why is outlining then filling an error in shading?
photo-art-school.ad-3.q3.e: Form has no outline; edges are places where value changes.

photo-art-school.ad-4.q1.p: Who formalised linear perspective around 1415, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ad-4.q1.e: Brunelleschi formalised it around 1415; Alberti codified it in 1435.

photo-art-school.ad-4.q2.p: You draw a corridor with one face parallel to the picture plane. How many vanishing points do you need?
photo-art-school.ad-4.q2.e: One-point perspective applies when one face is parallel to the picture plane.

photo-art-school.ad-4.q3.t: It is a Renaissance European convention describing a one-eyed, motionless viewer
photo-art-school.ad-4.q3.p: What caveat does the lesson give about linear perspective?
photo-art-school.ad-4.q3.e: Other traditions, like Chinese handscrolls and Cubism, reject it deliberately.

photo-art-school.ad-5.q1.p: Where is the halfway point of the classical figure, according to the lesson?
photo-art-school.ad-5.q1.e: The classical canon places the halfway point at the pubic bone, not the waist.

photo-art-school.ad-5.q2.p: Which two masses does the lesson say produce most gesture?
photo-art-school.ad-5.q2.e: Gesture comes from the tilt, twist and separation of the ribcage and pelvis.

photo-art-school.ad-5.q3.t: They do not change with pose or build
photo-art-school.ad-5.q3.e: Landmarks like clavicle and patella stay constant despite pose and build.

photo-art-school.ad-6.q1.p: What are thumbnails, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ad-6.q1.h: Six to ten, under a minute.
photo-art-school.ad-6.q1.e: Thumbnails are quick small sketches that test compositions before committing.

photo-art-school.ad-6.q2.p: Which format does the lesson call static and formal?
photo-art-school.ad-6.q2.e: Square is static and formal; portrait emphasises height; landscape breadth.

photo-art-school.ad-6.q3.t: It reads as timid; let the subject touch or cross edges when the design calls for it
photo-art-school.ad-6.q3.p: Why do beginners drift drawings toward the page middle, and what does the lesson say about it?
photo-art-school.ad-6.q3.e: Even margins read as timid; subjects can touch or cross the edges.

photo-art-school.ad-7.q1.p: Which medium does the lesson recommend for learning big value masses because it is too crude to fiddle with?
photo-art-school.ad-7.q1.e: Charcoal is best for big masses because its crudeness discourages fiddling.

photo-art-school.ad-7.q2.t: You can work up into white and down into black from a middle value
photo-art-school.ad-7.q2.p: What advantage does toned paper offer?
photo-art-school.ad-7.q2.e: Toned paper lets you establish a middle and work both ways, teaching value relationships.

photo-art-school.ad-7.q3.t: Infinite reversibility makes it easy to avoid committing
photo-art-school.ad-7.q3.p: Why is digital drawing both a strength and a danger?
photo-art-school.ad-7.q3.e: Undo is helpful but allows endless avoidance of commitment.

photo-art-school.ac-1.q1.e: Additive colour, i.e. light, uses red, green and blue.

photo-art-school.ac-1.q2.t: The RYB wheel is an approximation; cyan, magenta and yellow are the accurate subtractive set
photo-art-school.ac-1.q2.p: You mix blue and yellow paint and get dull green, but cyan and yellow give vivid green. What explains this?
photo-art-school.ac-1.q2.e: The RYB wheel is a historical approximation; CMY is the accurate subtractive set.

photo-art-school.ac-1.q3.p: What is a tone in the lesson vocabulary?
photo-art-school.ac-1.q3.e: A tint adds white, a shade adds black, and a tone adds grey.

photo-art-school.ac-2.q1.p: What proportion does the lesson give for dominant, subordinate and accent?

photo-art-school.ac-2.q2.t: Add a touch of its complement, orange
photo-art-school.ac-2.q2.p: You want to neutralise a blue without using black. What does the lesson suggest?
photo-art-school.ac-2.q2.e: Mixing complements neutralises a colour and gives living grey rather than dead grey.

photo-art-school.ac-2.q3.t: It has near the punch of complementary with less tension
photo-art-school.ac-2.q3.p: Why is split-complementary reliable for beginners?
photo-art-school.ac-2.q3.h: Two colours adjacent to the complement.
photo-art-school.ac-2.q3.e: It gives nearly complementary contrast with less tension.

photo-art-school.ac-3.q1.p: Who described simultaneous contrast systematically in 1839?
photo-art-school.ac-3.q1.e: Chevreul described it after dyers complained about black yarns next to blue.

photo-art-school.ac-3.q2.p: A neutral grey surrounded by red appears what?
photo-art-school.ac-3.q2.e: The eye induces the complement, so grey appears greenish.

photo-art-school.ac-3.q3.t: Never choose a colour in isolation; judge it in place
photo-art-school.ac-3.q3.p: What practical conclusion did Albers draw?
photo-art-school.ac-3.q3.e: Colour must be judged against actual neighbours at its actual size.

photo-art-school.ac-4.q1.t: It came from lapis lazuli and cost more than gold
photo-art-school.ac-4.q1.p: Why was ultramarine used for the Virgin robe?
photo-art-school.ac-4.q1.e: Ultramarine was ground from lapis lazuli and was more costly than gold.

photo-art-school.ac-4.q2.t: Synthetic pigments and the collapsible metal paint tube
photo-art-school.ac-4.q2.p: Which inventions did Impressionism depend on, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ac-4.q2.e: The lesson cites synthetic pigments and the paint tube patented in 1841.

photo-art-school.ac-4.q3.p: What is happening to Van Gogh sunflowers?

photo-art-school.ac-5.q1.p: Roughly how many colours do professionals typically use, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ac-5.q1.e: Professionals typically use six to twelve colours.

photo-art-school.ac-5.q2.t: Mixing three or more pigments, especially across the wheel
photo-art-school.ac-5.q2.p: What specific cause of mud does the lesson give?
photo-art-school.ac-5.q2.e: Mixing three or more pigments pulls everything toward neutral.

photo-art-school.ac-5.q3.p: Why does a limited palette guarantee harmony?
photo-art-school.ac-5.q3.e: All mixtures derive from the same few pigments, creating coherence.

photo-art-school.ac-6.q1.p: Which group used colour untethered from description around 1905?
photo-art-school.ac-6.q1.e: The Fauves, including Matisse and Derain, were named wild beasts for their colour.

photo-art-school.ac-6.q2.p: Rothko described his subject as what?
photo-art-school.ac-6.q2.e: Rothko said his subject was tragedy and ecstasy, not decoration.

photo-art-school.ac-6.q3.p: What three jobs can colour do, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ac-6.q3.e: Colour describes, structures or signifies; otherwise it is decoration.

photo-art-school.ah-1.q1.p: Roughly how old are the oldest known figurative paintings mentioned in the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-1.q1.e: The lesson dates the oldest known figurative paintings to around 40,000 years ago.

photo-art-school.ah-1.q2.t: Each part is shown from its most identifiable angle for functional afterlife images
photo-art-school.ah-1.q2.p: Why do Egyptian figures combine a profile head with frontal eye and shoulders?
photo-art-school.ah-1.q2.e: The composite view shows each part at its most identifiable angle because the images were functional equipment for the afterlife.

photo-art-school.ah-1.q3.t: They suggest ritual rather than display
photo-art-school.ah-1.q3.p: What does the lesson take from the Chauvet and Lascaux caves being deep and hard to reach?
photo-art-school.ah-1.q3.e: Their location suggests ritual rather than casual viewing.

photo-art-school.ah-2.q1.p: Which Greek figure first shows contrapposto, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-2.q1.e: The Kritios Boy shows weight shifting to one leg, the Classical breakthrough.

photo-art-school.ah-2.q2.p: A Roman republican bust shows wrinkles and jowls precisely. What is this called?
photo-art-school.ah-2.q2.e: Verism records unflattering detail because age signalled authority in Rome.

photo-art-school.ah-2.q3.t: Greek sculpture was painted; the white look is an accident of lost pigment
photo-art-school.ah-2.q3.p: What does the lesson say about the white marble aesthetic?
photo-art-school.ah-2.q3.e: Greek sculpture was painted and the white look comes from lost pigment.

photo-art-school.ah-3.q1.p: What does gold ground signify in a Byzantine icon?
photo-art-school.ah-3.q1.e: Gold ground is the absence of earthly space.

photo-art-school.ah-3.q2.t: Pointed arch, rib vault and flying buttress
photo-art-school.ah-3.q2.p: Which Gothic features let walls dissolve into stained glass?
photo-art-school.ah-3.q2.e: The pointed arch, rib vault and flying buttress allowed large windows.

photo-art-school.ah-3.q3.t: The European narrative is only one thread among many traditions
photo-art-school.ah-3.q3.p: Why does the lesson say to treat art history as plural?
photo-art-school.ah-3.q3.e: China, Islamic world, West Africa, Mesoamerica and others ran their own arcs.

photo-art-school.ah-4.q1.p: What is the intellectual shift behind the Renaissance?
photo-art-school.ah-4.q1.e: Humanism renewed attention to antiquity, the individual and nature.

photo-art-school.ah-4.q2.p: Which artist is associated with sfumato?
photo-art-school.ah-4.q2.e: Leonardo brings sfumato, scientific observation and psychological subtlety.

photo-art-school.ah-4.q3.t: By empirical observation and oil paint detail
photo-art-school.ah-4.q3.p: How did Netherlandish painters organise space compared with Italians?
photo-art-school.ah-4.q3.e: They used empirical observation and oil to render surface precisely.

photo-art-school.ah-5.q1.p: Roughly when is Baroque dated in the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-5.q1.e: The lesson dates Baroque to roughly 1600-1750.

photo-art-school.ah-5.q2.t: A wealthy merchant class bought pictures for their houses
photo-art-school.ah-5.q2.p: Why did the Dutch Republic produce specialised genres like landscape and still life?
photo-art-school.ah-5.q2.e: Merchants created an art market driven by specialised genres.

photo-art-school.ah-5.q3.t: Vanitas: reminders of mortality amid wealth
photo-art-school.ah-5.q3.p: What do skulls and wilting flowers in a Dutch still life signal?
photo-art-school.ah-5.q3.e: Vanitas still lifes combine displays of wealth with mortality reminders.

photo-art-school.ah-6.q1.p: Which painting by David is described as severe and politically charged?
photo-art-school.ah-6.q1.e: David Oath of the Horatii is the Neoclassical example in the lesson.

photo-art-school.ah-6.q2.t: Ordinary contemporary life is a legitimate subject
photo-art-school.ah-6.q2.p: Courbet painted stone breakers at heroic scale. What claim did Realism make?
photo-art-school.ah-6.q2.e: Realism claimed ordinary life is legitimate and need not be idealised.

photo-art-school.ah-6.q3.t: It made what painting is uniquely for an urgent question
photo-art-school.ah-6.q3.p: How did photography change painting, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-6.q3.e: Once appearance could be recorded cheaply, painting had to ask what it was uniquely for.

photo-art-school.ah-7.q1.p: In what year did the Impressionists hold their first independent exhibition?
photo-art-school.ah-7.q1.e: The first independent exhibition was in 1874.

photo-art-school.ah-7.q2.p: Which inventions enabled painting outdoors and quickly?
photo-art-school.ah-7.q2.e: Paint tubes and synthetic pigments made outdoor painting practical.

photo-art-school.ah-7.q3.p: Which Post-Impressionist laid the foundation for Cubism by building form from planes of colour?
photo-art-school.ah-7.q3.e: Cezanne built form from planes of colour, foundation for Cubism.

photo-art-school.ah-8.q1.p: Which movement began around 1907 with Picasso and Braque?

photo-art-school.ah-8.q2.p: What did Duchamp readymades relocate art from and to?
photo-art-school.ah-8.q2.e: Readymades move art from craft to concept.

photo-art-school.ah-8.q3.t: Formal arguments were never only formal
photo-art-school.ah-8.q3.p: What does the 1937 Degenerate Art exhibition show, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-8.q3.e: The lesson says it makes explicit that these formal arguments were never only formal.

photo-art-school.ah-9.q1.p: Which city became the centre after the war with Abstract Expressionism?
photo-art-school.ah-9.q1.e: Abstract Expressionism made New York the centre.

photo-art-school.ah-9.q2.t: Conceptual art where instructions are the art
photo-art-school.ah-9.q2.p: What do Sol LeWitt wall drawings exemplify?
photo-art-school.ah-9.q2.e: LeWitt wall drawings are instructions, illustrating conceptual art.

photo-art-school.ah-9.q3.t: A single narrative breaking apart into pluralism and challenge to whose history was written
photo-art-school.ah-9.q3.p: What is the actual content of postmodernism, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ah-9.q3.e: It is pluralism, appropriation, irony, institutional critique and challenging the canon.

photo-art-school.ah-10.q1.p: What year did Daguerre announce the daguerreotype?
photo-art-school.ah-10.q1.e: Daguerre and Talbot announced their processes in 1839.

photo-art-school.ah-10.q2.p: Why did Talbot negative-positive process matter for mass media?
photo-art-school.ah-10.q2.e: Negatives allow reproducibility, making photography a mass medium.

photo-art-school.ah-10.q3.p: What does the lesson say of the age of billions of images?
photo-art-school.ah-10.q3.e: Craft is not devalued; intention becomes scarce.

photo-art-school.ak-1.q1.p: About how long does the average museum visitor look at a painting, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ak-1.q1.e: The lesson cites about fifteen to thirty seconds, roughly seventeen on average.

photo-art-school.ak-1.q2.p: When should you read the wall label in the slow looking exercise?
photo-art-school.ak-1.q2.e: Labels shortcut you into someone else reading, so read after your own.

photo-art-school.ak-1.q3.t: You feel you have already seen it
photo-art-school.ak-1.q3.p: Why is the first two minutes of slow looking uncomfortable?
photo-art-school.ak-1.q3.e: You feel you have seen it, but around minute three you notice what you missed.

photo-art-school.ak-2.q1.e: It describes composition, line, value, colour and so on.

photo-art-school.ak-2.q2.t: The palette is earth tones except a single vermilion sleeve at the centre, the lightest value
photo-art-school.ak-2.q2.p: Which statement is precise enough for formal analysis?
photo-art-school.ak-2.q2.e: Precise statements tell what the artist did.

photo-art-school.ak-2.q3.t: A reader who never saw the work could sketch a rough version
photo-art-school.ak-2.q3.p: What is the test of a good formal analysis?
photo-art-school.ak-2.q3.e: The description should be enough to sketch the work.

photo-art-school.ak-3.q1.p: Who gave the three-level model of iconography?
photo-art-school.ak-3.q1.e: Erwin Panofsky gave the standard model.
