photo-art-school.ak-3.q2.p: Seeing a woman in blue, a lily and a kneeling winged figure and concluding Annunciation is which level?
photo-art-school.ak-3.q2.e: Level two identifies conventional meaning, the lily as purity and Gabriel.

photo-art-school.ak-3.q3.t: Assuming symbols mean what they would today
photo-art-school.ak-3.q3.p: What failure does the lesson warn about?
photo-art-school.ak-3.q3.e: Symbols must be read as the original audience did.

photo-art-school.ak-4.q1.p: What does formalism treat as irrelevant?
photo-art-school.ak-4.q1.e: Formalism attends only to visual properties.

photo-art-school.ak-4.q2.p: Which lens explains why Dutch merchants bought still lifes?
photo-art-school.ak-4.q2.e: Social-historical criticism explains patronage and subject.

photo-art-school.ak-4.q3.t: Why great women artists were rare
photo-art-school.ak-4.q3.p: What does Nochlin essay answer by examining institutional exclusion?
photo-art-school.ak-4.q3.e: She argued that exclusion, not talent, explains it.

photo-art-school.ak-5.q1.p: What four steps does Feldman propose?

photo-art-school.ak-5.q2.t: This fails because it has three competing focal points and no narrative centre
photo-art-school.ak-5.q2.p: Which statement is a defensible judgment?
photo-art-school.ak-5.q2.e: It is a claim about the work that can be disputed.

photo-art-school.ak-5.q3.t: It is a set of revisable past judgments by particular people
photo-art-school.ak-5.q3.p: Why is deferring to the canon a failure mode?
photo-art-school.ak-5.q3.e: The canon was made by people with interests and can be revised.

photo-art-school.ak-6.q1.p: About how long should an artist statement be, per the lesson?
photo-art-school.ak-6.q1.e: About 150 to 300 words in plain language.

photo-art-school.ak-6.q2.t: The eye goes to the bright corner instead of the face
photo-art-school.ak-6.q2.p: Which critique comment follows the lesson advice?
photo-art-school.ak-6.q2.e: It names what is physically present and its effect.

photo-art-school.ak-6.q3.t: Take notes, thank people, decide later
photo-art-school.ak-6.q3.e: Do not explain during feedback; sort what to act on later.

chora-history.harm-01.q1.t: A single melodic line with no accompaniment
chora-history.harm-01.q1.e: Monophony is one melodic line, as in Gregorian chant.

chora-history.harm-01.q2.p: A film composer wants a Phrygian colour to signal menace. In which tradition does this vocabulary originate?
chora-history.harm-01.q2.e: These names come from the eight church modes of medieval chant.

chora-history.harm-01.q3.t: Oral transmission failed when distant churches needed to sing the same chant
chora-history.harm-01.q3.p: Why did notation appear in the chant repertory?
chora-history.harm-01.q3.e: Neumes were the fix when oral transmission could not keep churches in sync; Guido of Arezzo later added a staff.

chora-history.harm-02.q1.p: In which treatise is the earliest surviving description of two-part singing?
chora-history.harm-02.q1.e: The lesson names the Musica enchiriadis as the earliest surviving description.

chora-history.harm-02.q2.p: Which ratio describes a perfect fifth?
chora-history.harm-02.q2.e: A fifth is 3:2; an octave is 2:1 and a fourth 4:3.

chora-history.harm-02.q3.t: It held single chant notes for very long durations under florid upper voices
chora-history.harm-02.q3.p: What happened to the lower voice by the Notre-Dame school around 1200?
chora-history.harm-02.q3.e: The chant became a drone-like foundation with melismas above.

chora-history.harm-03.q1.t: One voice states a phrase and others enter with it at staggered intervals
chora-history.harm-03.q1.e: It is the signature gesture of Renaissance counterpoint.

chora-history.harm-03.q2.p: Which theorist formalised Palestrina style in Gradus ad Parnassum (1725)?
chora-history.harm-03.q2.e: Johann Joseph Fux formalised it in 1725.

chora-history.harm-03.q3.t: They were invented by Fux from observing what Palestrina actually did
chora-history.harm-03.q3.p: Why are the famous counterpoint rules described as reverse-engineered?
chora-history.harm-03.q3.e: The rules describe Palestrina practice, codified later by Fux.

chora-history.harm-04.q1.p: Which chord is home in functional harmony?
chora-history.harm-04.q1.e: The tonic is home; the dominant most wants to return to it.

chora-history.harm-04.q2.t: Which intervals to stack above each note
chora-history.harm-04.q2.p: What do the figures under a basso continuo bass line tell the keyboard player?
chora-history.harm-04.q2.e: Numbers specify intervals so chords need not be written out.

chora-history.harm-04.q3.t: A chord keeps its identity through inversion
chora-history.harm-04.q3.p: What did Rameau argue about chord identity?
chora-history.harm-04.q3.e: Rameau said inversions are the same harmonic object and that roots govern structure.

chora-history.harm-05.q1.t: The discrepancy when twelve perfect fifths overshoot seven octaves
chora-history.harm-05.q1.e: Stacking twelve fifths lands slightly above seven octaves.

chora-history.harm-05.q2.p: In equal temperament how large is every semitone?
chora-history.harm-05.q2.e: Every semitone is exactly the twelfth root of two.

chora-history.harm-05.q3.t: Well-tempered almost certainly meant an unequal well temperament
chora-history.harm-05.q3.p: What does the lesson say about the Well-Tempered Clavier?
chora-history.harm-05.q3.e: The title almost certainly referred to unequal temperament where keys had distinct colours.

chora-history.harm-06.q1.p: In which year did Tristan und Isolde premiere per the lesson date?
chora-history.harm-06.q1.e: The lesson dates Tristan und Isolde to 1859.

chora-history.harm-06.q2.t: It can be read several ways at once
chora-history.harm-06.q2.p: Why is the Tristan chord ambiguous?
chora-history.harm-06.q2.e: The ambiguity means no single analysis wins, matching the theme of unsatisfied longing.

chora-history.harm-06.q3.t: If no chord requires resolution, the key has no work left to do
chora-history.harm-06.q3.e: He later built the twelve-tone method by 1921.

chora-history.harm-07.q1.t: It serves as the I chord, i.e. home
chora-history.harm-07.q1.p: In a twelve-bar blues, what role does the dominant seventh often play?
chora-history.harm-07.q1.e: The I chord is often a dominant seventh, so tension becomes texture.

chora-history.harm-07.q2.t: Playing the flat and natural third together
chora-history.harm-07.q2.p: How is a blue note approximated on piano?
chora-history.harm-07.q2.e: Pianos cannot bend, so flat and natural thirds are played together.

chora-history.harm-07.q3.t: Three tonal centres a major third apart move too fast to hear one as home
chora-history.harm-07.q3.p: What happens in Coltrane Giant Steps (1960)?
chora-history.harm-07.q3.e: The harmony moves through three centres a major third apart.

chora-history.harm-08.q1.t: The end of the cycle is also its beginning
chora-history.harm-08.q1.p: Why does a loop have no cadence?
chora-history.harm-08.q1.e: Because the cycle repeats, there is no arrival.

chora-history.harm-08.q2.p: What does Mixolydian remove that makes rock feel grounded?
chora-history.harm-08.q2.e: A flat seventh removes the leading tone and its pull to the tonic.

chora-history.harm-08.q3.t: A reallocation of attention to drums, vocals and low end
chora-history.harm-08.q3.p: How does the lesson explain the single minor pad in trap and drill?
chora-history.harm-08.q3.e: The harmonic content is minimal because the musical argument happens elsewhere.

chora-history.rec-01.q1.e: Edouard-Leon Scott de Martinville built it to make sound legible, not playable.

chora-history.rec-01.q2.t: A disc could be mass-pressed from a master
chora-history.rec-01.q2.p: Why did the flat disc beat the cylinder?
chora-history.rec-01.q2.e: Mass pressing from a master decided the format war.

chora-history.rec-01.q3.t: Its roughly three-minute side defined song length for a century
chora-history.rec-01.q3.p: How did the 78 rpm disc affect popular music?
chora-history.rec-01.q3.e: The three-minute limit shaped song length.

chora-history.rec-02.q1.p: When did the acoustic era end?
chora-history.rec-02.q1.e: Until 1925 there was no electricity in the recording chain.

chora-history.rec-02.q2.t: The tuba fundamental could move the diaphragm
chora-history.rec-02.q2.p: Why were string basses swapped for tubas?
chora-history.rec-02.q2.e: Only loud instruments registered on the horn.

chora-history.rec-02.q3.t: They document the capture system as much as the performance
chora-history.rec-02.q3.p: What does the lesson say about early recordings as evidence?
chora-history.rec-02.q3.e: Every recording documents its capture system as well as the performance.

chora-history.rec-03.q1.t: Western Electric electrical system with microphone, amplifier and electromagnetic cutter
chora-history.rec-03.q1.e: The electrical system replaced acoustic recording in 1925.

chora-history.rec-03.q2.p: Which vocal style is impossible without electronics?
chora-history.rec-03.q2.e: Crooning needs a microphone to carry a quiet voice.

chora-history.rec-03.q3.p: What did radio make a coherent concept for the first time?
chora-history.rec-03.q3.h: Everyone in a country knows it.
chora-history.rec-03.q3.e: Reaching millions at no marginal cost made the hit possible.

chora-history.rec-04.q1.p: Who brought the Magnetophon to the United States?
chora-history.rec-04.q1.e: Jack Mullin brought it after the war.

chora-history.rec-04.q2.p: What new capability did tape give engineers?
chora-history.rec-04.q2.e: You could splice takes so a performance need not be continuous.

chora-history.rec-04.q3.t: They stopped documenting an event and became artefacts assembled from parts
chora-history.rec-04.q3.p: How did multitrack recording change records?
chora-history.rec-04.q3.e: Mix became a creative act; records could exist that could not be performed.

chora-history.rec-05.q1.e: Columbia introduced the LP; RCA answered with the 45.

chora-history.rec-05.q2.t: Twenty-two minutes per side shaped the structure
chora-history.rec-05.q2.p: Why do classic albums often have two distinct halves?
chora-history.rec-05.q2.e: The side length shaped album arcs.

chora-history.rec-05.q3.t: It shortens intros and song lengths
chora-history.rec-05.q3.p: What is streaming royalty threshold effect on songs?
chora-history.rec-05.q3.e: A play counts after about thirty seconds, rewarding earlier hooks.

chora-history.rec-06.q1.p: Who recorded Southern folk music for the Library of Congress from 1933?
chora-history.rec-06.q1.e: The Lomaxes carried a 315-pound machine into the South.

chora-history.rec-06.q2.t: Record everything and never delete anything
chora-history.rec-06.q2.p: What was Moses Asch Folkways commitment?
chora-history.rec-06.q2.e: Folkways kept its catalogue permanently in print.

chora-history.rec-06.q3.t: Preservation and access versus outsiders taking recordings from unequal communities
chora-history.rec-06.q3.p: What ethical tension does field recording carry?
chora-history.rec-06.q3.e: It preserved music but involved unequal power and copyright claims.

chora-history.rec-07.q1.t: A signal can be reconstructed from samples above twice its highest frequency
chora-history.rec-07.q1.p: What does the Nyquist-Shannon theorem state?

chora-history.rec-07.q2.p: Roughly what dynamic range do 16 bits give?
chora-history.rec-07.q2.e: Sixteen bits at 6 dB each gives about 96 dB.

chora-history.rec-07.q3.t: Loud recordings command attention on radio and shuffle
chora-history.rec-07.q3.p: Why did the loudness war happen?
chora-history.rec-07.q3.e: Engineers compressed harder to raise average level.

chora-history.rec-08.q1.t: New incentives, such as per-play royalties
chora-history.rec-08.q1.p: What has replaced physical format constraints in streaming?
chora-history.rec-08.q1.e: Constraints are replaced by a new set of incentives.

chora-history.rec-08.q2.t: It is a licensing arrangement and titles disappear
chora-history.rec-08.q2.p: Why does the lesson say a streaming catalogue is not a library?
chora-history.rec-08.q2.e: Nothing streamed is preserved by the listener.

chora-history.rec-08.q3.t: It divides the pool by total plays platform-wide
chora-history.rec-08.q3.p: Why does pro-rata payout mean your subscription does not primarily pay the artists you listen to?
chora-history.rec-08.q3.e: The pool is shared by total plays across the platform.

chora-history.form-01.q1.t: Two phrases in a question-and-answer relationship
chora-history.form-01.q1.e: A period has an inconclusive first phrase and a closing second.

chora-history.form-01.q2.t: Statement, repetition, then fragmentation to a cadence
chora-history.form-01.q2.p: What is the shape of a sentence?
chora-history.form-01.q2.e: A short idea is repeated then fragments and accelerates.

chora-history.form-01.q3.t: They are where expressive weight usually lives
chora-history.form-01.q3.p: Why do irregular phrase lengths matter?
chora-history.form-01.q3.e: Stretching or compressing a unit marks expressive moments.

chora-history.form-02.q1.e: Binary has two sections, the first moving away from the tonic.

chora-history.form-02.q2.p: Which operatic form built on ternary form with ornamented returns?
chora-history.form-02.q2.e: The da capo aria used ABA with ornamentation of A.

chora-history.form-02.q3.t: Contrast between movements rather than development within one
chora-history.form-02.q3.p: What is the Baroque suite significant for?
chora-history.form-02.q3.e: It is the earliest large form based on contrast between movements.

chora-history.form-03.q1.p: What are the three parts of sonata form?
chora-history.form-03.q1.e: Sonata form has exposition, development and recapitulation.

chora-history.form-03.q2.p: Where does the second theme return in the recapitulation?
chora-history.form-03.q2.e: It is restated in the tonic to resolve the tonal conflict.

chora-history.form-03.q3.t: The drama is a key relationship set up as a problem then solved
chora-history.form-03.q3.p: Why is sonata form described as being about key, not tunes?
chora-history.form-03.q3.e: The tonic return of the second theme is the resolution.

chora-history.form-04.q1.t: A theme with some skeleton persisting
chora-history.form-04.q1.e: Rhythm, harmony, mode, texture and register change while some skeleton remains.

chora-history.form-04.q2.e: A recurring refrain alternates with contrasting episodes.

chora-history.form-04.q3.t: It is a texture and procedure whose shape comes from the subject
chora-history.form-04.q3.p: Why does the lesson say fugue is not a form?
chora-history.form-04.q3.e: The shape is whatever the subject permits.

chora-history.form-05.q1.p: What is the structure of the 32-bar song form?
chora-history.form-05.q1.e: Eight bars of A repeated, bridge, A returns.

chora-history.form-05.q2.p: What lyric form does the twelve-bar blues use?
chora-history.form-05.q2.h: Time to invent the third line.
chora-history.form-05.q2.e: The singer has time to invent while repeating.

chora-history.form-05.q3.t: Strangers can perform together because everyone knows it
chora-history.form-05.q3.p: Why does the lesson call a shared form public infrastructure?
chora-history.form-05.q3.e: Shared forms let musicians who have never met play together.

chora-history.form-06.q1.t: The title and same lyric each time
chora-history.form-06.q1.p: What does the chorus contain in verse-chorus form?
chora-history.form-06.q1.e: The chorus is the destination with the hook.

chora-history.form-06.q2.e: It builds tension before the chorus.

chora-history.form-06.q3.p: In dance music what replaces the chorus?
chora-history.form-06.q3.e: The drop replaces the chorus with a rhythmic and timbral release.

chora-history.form-07.q1.p: What is Terry Riley In C built from?
chora-history.form-07.q1.e: Players move through 53 fragments at their own pace.

chora-history.form-07.q2.t: Two identical loops with one drifting slightly faster
chora-history.form-07.q2.p: What drives Steve Reich phase pieces?
chora-history.form-07.q2.e: The structure is the consequence of one process.

chora-history.form-07.q3.t: Tracks are stacks of loops for mixing; the real form is the DJ set
chora-history.form-07.q3.p: How does the lesson view house and techno forms?
chora-history.form-07.q3.e: The DJ set is the larger form.

chora-history.rhy-01.q1.t: A pattern of strong and weak beats around the pulse
chora-history.rhy-01.q1.e: Metre is something your brain imposes on pulse.

chora-history.rhy-01.q2.t: Two beats divided in three versus three beats divided in two
chora-history.rhy-01.q2.e: The strong points differ though both have six eighth notes.

chora-history.rhy-01.q3.t: Two groups of three reinterpreted as three groups of two

chora-history.rhy-02.q1.t: Placing accents where the metre does not expect them
chora-history.rhy-02.q1.e: Syncopation accents offbeats or weak beats, or ties across a strong beat.

chora-history.rhy-02.q2.p: In a backbeat, where does the snare fall in common time?
chora-history.rhy-02.q2.e: The backbeat accents 2 and 4, the weak beats.

1524.q2.t: The royal castle of Elsinore in Denmark
1524.q2.h: Something is rotten in the state of Denmark.
1524.q2.e: The play takes place at Elsinore Castle in Denmark.

1524.q3.t: Action versus overthinking and the moral weight of revenge
1524.q3.p: Which theme is shown by Hamlet's long delay in taking revenge?
1524.q3.e: His hesitation raises questions about revenge, conscience, and certainty.

1524.q4.p: In "To be, or not to be," Hamlet speaks his thoughts alone on stage. This device is called
1524.q4.h: He is alone with his thoughts.
1524.q4.e: A soliloquy lets the audience hear a character's private reasoning.

1524.q5.t: Whether Claudius reacts with guilt to a murder scene like his own crime
1524.q5.p: Hamlet stages a play to test Claudius. What does he hope to learn?
1524.q5.e: Hamlet watches the king's reaction to prove the ghost's story.

1400.q1.p: Who is the narrator of Great Expectations?
1400.q1.h: He is an orphan raised in the marshes.
1400.q1.e: Pip narrates his own story as an adult looking back.

1400.q2.t: Magwitch, the convict Pip helped as a child
1400.q2.p: Who is secretly the source of Pip's fortune?
1400.q2.h: Pip first meets him on the marshes.
1400.q2.e: Magwitch, grateful to Pip, funds his rise and is the true benefactor.

1400.q3.t: True worth lies in character and loyalty, not status
1400.q3.p: What does Pip learn about wealth and class by the end?
1400.q3.h: Think of how Joe treats him.
1400.q3.e: Pip realizes that Joe's kindness is worth more than snobbery.

1400.q4.t: symbolism for a life frozen in hurt
1400.q4.p: Miss Havisham's stopped clocks and decaying wedding cake are examples of
1400.q4.h: She stopped time on her wedding day.
1400.q4.e: The stopped clocks and rotting cake symbolize her clinging to the past.

1400.q5.p: Estella was raised by Miss Havisham to
1400.q5.e: Miss Havisham trains Estella to be cold, using her to hurt men like Pip.

730.q1.p: What famous request does Oliver make in the workhouse?
730.q1.e: Oliver asks for more gruel and is punished.

730.q2.p: Which gang leader trains boys to pick pockets in London?
730.q2.h: The Artful Dodger works for him.
730.q2.e: Fagin runs a gang of boy pickpockets in a London den.

730.q3.t: how society treated poor children and workhouse policy
730.q3.p: Dickens wrote Oliver Twist partly to criticize
730.q3.e: The novel attacks the harsh Poor Law system and the neglect of poor children.

730.q4.p: Dickens gives officials like Mr. Bumble comically exaggerated manners. This is
730.q4.e: Satire uses humor and exaggeration to criticize.

730.q5.p: Which kind man takes Oliver in and tries to help him?
730.q5.h: He is a gentleman Oliver is accused of robbing by mistake.
730.q5.e: Mr. Brownlow shelters Oliver and becomes his protector.

46.q1.p: Who is Ebenezer Scrooge's dead business partner who appears as a ghost?
46.q1.e: Marley's ghost warns Scrooge that three spirits will visit him.

46.q2.t: A poor family including the sick boy Tiny Tim
46.q2.p: Which family does Scrooge's clerk Bob Cratchit have?
46.q2.h: They celebrate Christmas despite little money.
46.q2.e: Bob Cratchit, underpaid, supports his family including Tiny Tim.

46.q3.t: Generosity and the possibility of redemption
46.q3.p: What is the main theme of the story?
46.q3.e: Scrooge learns to value kindness and community and reforms.

46.q4.t: structure moving the story through time
46.q4.p: The ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come work as a
46.q4.e: The three spirits show Scrooge time periods that change his outlook.

46.q5.p: When Scrooge calls Christmas "humbug," he means it is
46.q5.h: He does not like the holiday.
46.q5.e: Humbug means nonsense or a sham, showing his scorn.

2554.q1.p: Who is the main character of Crime and Punishment?
2554.q1.h: He is a poor former student.
2554.q1.e: Raskolnikov murders a pawnbroker and is tormented by guilt.

2554.q2.p: In which city is the novel mostly set?
2554.q2.e: The story unfolds in the crowded, poor districts of St. Petersburg.

2554.q3.t: The theory collapses under his guilt and conscience
2554.q3.p: Raskolnikov believes extraordinary people may break moral rules. What does the novel show?
2554.q3.h: Consider how he feels after the crime.
2554.q3.e: His fever, paranoia, and guilt show the theory cannot silence conscience.

2554.q4.p: Dostoevsky shows Raskolnikov's fevers, dreams, and racing thoughts. This is an example of
2554.q4.h: The focus is the inner mind.
2554.q4.e: The novel explores the inner life of a guilty mind.

2554.q5.p: Which character encourages Raskolnikov toward confession and redemption?
2554.q5.h: She is a young woman of deep faith.
2554.q5.e: Sonya urges him to confess and follows him to Siberia.

2600.q1.p: Which French leader's invasion of Russia is central to War and Peace?
2600.q1.e: Napoleon's invasion of Russia and the burning of Moscow are major events.

2600.q2.p: Which two characters are among the novel's main young nobles?
2600.q2.h: One is a bastard turned count; the other is a prince.
2600.q2.e: Pierre and Andrei both search for meaning amid war and society.

2600.q3.t: driven by countless small forces, not just great men
2600.q3.p: Tolstoy argues in the novel that history is
2600.q3.e: He argues leaders are carried along by vast forces and individual acts.

2600.q4.t: To contrast private life and public events and question what matters
2600.q4.p: Why does Tolstoy alternate between salons and battlefields?
2600.q4.e: The contrast invites the reader to weigh private and public life.

2600.q5.t: a gathering of aristocrats for conversation
2600.q5.h: It opens the book at Anna Scherer's party.

1399.q1.t: She leaves her husband for Count Vronsky
1399.q1.p: What choice does Anna make that scandalizes St. Petersburg society?
1399.q1.h: It involves love outside of marriage.
1399.q1.e: Anna's affair with Vronsky leads to social ostracism.

1399.q2.p: Who is the landowner whose parallel story explores faith and meaning?
1399.q2.h: He works on his farm and loves Kitty.
1399.q2.e: Levin seeks meaning through work, family, and faith.

1399.q3.t: a study of different troubled marriages and families
1399.q3.p: The novel begins "All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way." This sets up
1399.q3.h: Think of the Oblonskys, Karenins, and Levins.
1399.q3.e: The opening frames the book's many family stories.

1399.q4.t: Their opposite paths comment on each other
1399.q4.p: Why does Tolstoy tell Anna's and Levin's stories in parallel?
1399.q4.e: The contrasting plots illuminate passion versus purpose.

1399.q5.t: They shun her while excusing similar behavior by men
1399.q5.p: How do high society characters generally treat Anna after her affair?
1399.q5.e: Society judges Anna harshly, unlike men like Oblonsky.

996.q1.t: He reads too many chivalric romances and decides to become a knight
996.q1.p: Why does Alonso Quixano become Don Quixote?
996.q1.e: Reading romances drives him to imitate knights.

996.q2.p: Who is Don Quixote's down-to-earth companion?
996.q2.h: He hopes to be rewarded with an island.
996.q2.e: Sancho serves as squire and offers a practical view.

996.q3.t: the clash between illusion and reality
996.q3.p: When Quixote charges at windmills thinking they are giants, this shows
996.q3.e: He sees what he reads in books rather than what is there.

996.q4.p: Cervantes wrote the book largely as
996.q4.e: The novel mocks the exaggerated romances of knights.

996.q5.p: In Part Two, characters have read Part One. This technique is called
996.q5.h: The book comments on being a book.
996.q5.e: Metafiction draws attention to a work as a work of fiction.

1184.q1.t: He is falsely accused of treason by men who envy him
1184.q1.p: Why is Edmond Dantes imprisoned in the Chateau d'If?
1184.q1.h: Think about who benefits from his arrest.
1184.q1.e: Danglars, Fernand, and Caderousse plot against him, and Villefort jails him to protect himself over a letter from Elba.

1184.q2.t: On the island of Monte Cristo
1184.q2.p: Where does Dantes find the treasure that makes him rich?
1184.q2.e: The Abbe Faria tells him of a treasure hidden on the island of Monte Cristo, which he later finds.

1184.q3.t: Whether revenge can ever be fully just
1184.q3.p: Which theme best describes the novel's central question?
1184.q3.h: Consider what Dantes does after escaping.
1184.q3.e: Dantes pursues elaborate revenge, and the novel questions whether a human can act as an instrument of providence without going too far.

1184.q4.p: Dumas hides the Count's identity from other characters, but readers know it. This is an example of what?
1184.q4.h: The audience knows more than the characters.
1184.q4.e: Readers know the Count is Dantes while his enemies do not, which creates dramatic irony.

1184.q5.p: When the text says Dantes shows "fortitude" in prison, what does it mean?
1184.q5.h: Think about how he survives years in a cell.
1184.q5.e: Fortitude means strength of spirit in the face of suffering, which Dantes shows over fourteen years of imprisonment.

135.q1.p: What small crime first sends Jean Valjean to prison?
135.q1.h: He was trying to feed his sister's children.
135.q1.e: Valjean is jailed for stealing a loaf of bread, and his sentence is extended by escape attempts.

135.q2.t: The Battle of Waterloo and later Paris uprising of 1832
135.q2.p: Which major historical event is a setting for part of the novel?
135.q2.h: The story begins after Napoleon's fall.
135.q2.e: The novel includes the Battle of Waterloo and the June 1832 student uprising in Paris.

135.q3.t: A bishop shows him mercy after he steals silver
135.q3.p: What act changes Valjean's life early in the book?
135.q3.e: The Bishop of Digne tells police the silver was a gift and gives Valjean the candlesticks, inspiring him to change.

135.q4.p: Hugo often pauses the plot for long essays on topics like Waterloo or the sewers. What is this technique called?
135.q4.h: It means leaving the main subject for a time.
135.q4.e: These digressions give historical and social background and make Hugo's arguments directly.

135.q5.t: He cannot reconcile his rigid view of law with Valjean's mercy
135.q5.p: Why does Inspector Javert struggle at the end of the story?
135.q5.e: Javert believes in law without mercy; Valjean's act of mercy breaks that worldview, and he cannot go on.

161.q1.p: Which sisters are the central characters of the novel?
161.q1.h: The title refers to their qualities.
161.q1.e: Elinor represents sense and Marianne sensibility.

161.q2.t: Inheritance passes to their half-brother John
161.q2.p: Why must the Dashwood women leave their home at the beginning?
161.q2.h: Think about how property was inherited at the time.
161.q2.e: Norland Park passes to John Dashwood, leaving his stepmother and half-sisters with little money.

161.q3.t: The balance between reason and emotion
161.q3.p: What is a main theme of the book?
161.q3.e: Both sisters learn that neither pure restraint nor pure feeling is enough.

161.q4.p: Austen often uses a narrator who gently mocks selfishness, such as in John and Fanny Dashwood's conversation about helping the family. This is an example of what?
161.q4.h: The narrator says one thing and means another.
161.q4.e: The narrator shows them reasoning their way out of generosity, a clear case of irony.

161.q5.t: It makes her rethink her extreme sensibility
161.q5.p: Why is Marianne's illness a turning point?
161.q5.h: She nearly dies after a long period of grief.
161.q5.e: After nearly dying, Marianne sees that she brought suffering on herself and her family, and she grows wiser.

158.q1.p: What is Emma Woodhouse's favorite hobby?
158.q1.h: She sets Harriet up with various men.
158.q1.e: Emma loves arranging marriages, with comic and painful results.

158.q2.p: Where does the story take place?
158.q2.h: It is a small English village.
158.q2.e: Almost all action takes place in or near Highbury in Surrey.

158.q3.p: Which theme matters most to Emma's growth?
158.q3.h: She has to learn she can be wrong.
158.q3.e: Emma's confidence is shaken when she sees how her meddling hurts others, and she gains self-knowledge.

158.q4.p: Whose view do we mostly see in the narration, causing readers to believe Emma's mistaken ideas at first?
158.q4.h: The narrator slips into her thoughts.
158.q4.e: Austen filters much of the story through Emma's perceptions, so readers share her errors.

158.q5.p: Who gently criticizes Emma and eventually becomes her husband?
158.q5.h: He is a longtime family friend.
158.q5.e: Mr. Knightley tells Emma the truth when others will not, and they marry at the end.

1257.q1.p: Who is the young man who travels to Paris hoping to become a musketeer?
1257.q1.e: D'Artagnan arrives in Paris and soon befriends the three musketeers.

1257.q2.p: In which country and century does the story take place?
1257.q2.h: Louis XIII is on the throne.
1257.q2.e: The story is set under Louis XIII and Cardinal Richelieu.

1257.q3.t: All for one, one for all
1257.q3.p: What is the motto the friends share?
1257.q3.e: The slogan "All for one, one for all" captures their loyalty to each other.

1257.q4.t: The book was first published in newspaper installments
1257.q4.p: Why do many chapters end at a moment of danger?
1257.q4.h: Think about how readers kept buying the next issue.
1257.q4.e: The serial format encouraged cliffhangers to bring readers back.

1257.q5.p: Who is the main female villain, a spy for Cardinal Richelieu?
1257.q5.h: She has a hidden brand on her shoulder.
1257.q5.e: Milady works for Richelieu and plots against d'Artagnan and his friends.

103.q1.t: That he can travel around the world in eighty days
103.q1.e: Fogg wagers 20,000 pounds with fellow Reform Club members.

103.q2.e: Passepartout joins Fogg on the trip and gets into many scrapes.

103.q3.t: Steamships, railways, and the Suez Canal
103.q3.p: Why was a trip like this newly possible in the 1870s?
103.q3.h: Think about transport technology of Verne's time.
103.q3.e: New steamships, rail lines, and the Suez Canal made faster world travel realistic.

103.q4.t: He gains a day by crossing the International Date Line eastward
103.q4.p: How does Fogg win the bet at the very end?
103.q4.h: Time zones and the calendar matter.
103.q4.e: Traveling east, he gained a day without realizing, so he arrives in time.

103.q5.p: Detective Fix follows Fogg because he thinks Fogg is:
103.q5.h: A robbery has just happened in London.
103.q5.e: Fix believes Fogg robbed the Bank of England and tries to arrest him.

164.q1.p: What is the name of Captain Nemo's submarine?
164.q1.h: It is named for a sea creature.
164.q1.e: The Nautilus is Nemo's advanced electric submarine.

164.q2.h: He is a French marine biologist.
164.q2.e: Aronnax narrates in the first person after being captured with his servant and Ned Land.

164.q3.p: The story begins with sailors reporting a mysterious "monster". What is it really?
164.q3.e: The "sea monster" turns out to be Nemo's ship.

164.q4.t: To give an air of scientific realism
164.q4.p: Why does Verne include long lists of fish and sea creatures?
164.q4.h: Think about the book's mix of fact and fiction.
164.q4.e: The catalogs lend authority and make the imaginary voyage seem real.

164.q5.p: What does Ned Land want throughout the book?
164.q5.h: He is a prisoner, in effect.
164.q5.e: Ned, a harpooner, repeatedly seeks to escape captivity.

36.q1.p: Where do the Martian cylinders first land?
36.q1.e: The first cylinder falls on Horsell Common near Woking.

36.q2.p: Which planet do the invaders come from?
36.q2.h: It is in the title of the book's first chapter.

36.q3.p: How are the Martians finally defeated?
36.q3.h: Something tiny does what armies cannot.
36.q3.e: They die because they have no immunity to Earth's germs.

36.q4.t: The invaders treat humans as Europeans treated colonized peoples
36.q4.p: Wells wrote while Britain ruled a great empire. What idea does reversing roles produce?
36.q4.e: Wells invites British readers to feel what it is like to be conquered by a stronger power.

36.q5.p: What are the Martians' walking war machines called?
36.q5.e: The tall three-legged machines are known as tripods.

35.q1.p: What are the two groups the Time Traveller meets in 802,701?
35.q1.h: One lives above ground, one below.
35.q1.e: The gentle Eloi live above ground and the Morlocks below.

35.q2.p: What is the name of the Eloi woman he saves from drowning?
35.q2.e: Weena is the Eloi woman who becomes his companion.

35.q3.t: The gap between rich and poor
35.q3.p: What social problem does Wells use the future to comment on?
35.q3.h: The Eloi and Morlocks represent classes.
35.q3.e: The two species grew out of the division between the leisured rich and the laboring poor.

35.q4.t: It forms a frame story that makes the fantastic tale seem like a report
35.q4.p: Why is the story told as the Traveller's account to dinner guests?
35.q4.h: It is a story within a story.
35.q4.e: The frame lets the narrator present the account as testimony from a friend.

35.q5.p: The Time Traveller's first theory about the Eloi and Morlocks proves entirely correct.
35.q5.h: He revises his ideas more than once.
35.q5.e: He keeps correcting his theories as he learns about the Morlocks.

43.q1.t: He creates a potion that turns him into Mr. Hyde
43.q1.h: Hyde is not a separate person.
43.q1.e: Jekyll's potion transforms him into the brutal Hyde.

43.q2.p: In which city is the story set?
43.q2.e: The story is set in Victorian London.

43.q3.t: The good and evil that exist in one person
43.q3.p: What central idea does the novel explore?
43.q3.e: The book suggests everyone has a hidden darker side.

43.q4.t: It is held back for mystery and told in letters
43.q4.p: Why is the full truth revealed late in the book?
43.q4.e: Stevenson structures the story as a mystery solved by a lawyer, ending in two written confessions.

43.q5.p: Who is the lawyer who investigates the strange case?
43.q5.h: He is a friend of Jekyll.
43.q5.e: Gabriel Utterson, Jekyll's lawyer, tries to understand the connection with Hyde.

215.q1.p: What kind of animal is Buck?
215.q1.h: He is stolen from a California home.
215.q1.e: Buck, a St. Bernard-Scotch shepherd mix, is sold into sled-dog work.

215.q2.p: During which event is the story set?
215.q2.h: Men need dogs to haul sleds.
215.q2.e: Gold seekers in the Yukon create demand for strong sled dogs.

215.q3.p: What is the central conflict in Buck's life?
215.q3.e: Buck's ancestral instincts awaken as he leaves civilized life behind.

215.q4.t: The harsh rule that strength decides survival
215.q4.p: What does "the law of club and fang" refer to?
215.q4.h: Buck learns it from a man in a red sweater and from fights.
215.q4.e: It sums up the brutal world in which only the strong and clever survive.

215.q5.p: Who is the kind man Buck loves?
215.q5.h: He rescues Buck from cruel owners.
215.q5.e: John Thornton saves Buck and earns his deepest loyalty.

236.q1.p: Who raises Mowgli in the jungle?
236.q1.e: A wolf pack, with Father Wolf and Mother Wolf, raises him.

236.q2.p: Which country is the story set in?
236.q2.e: The stories are set in the jungles of India.

236.q3.t: Rules that all animals must obey to keep order
236.q3.p: What is the "Law of the Jungle" mostly about?
236.q3.e: It is the code that guides animals' behavior and keeps peace.

236.q4.p: What technique makes animals talk and obey laws like people?
236.q4.h: Human traits are given to animals.
236.q4.e: Kipling personifies animals in the story.

236.q5.p: Who is the main villain hunting Mowgli?
236.q5.e: Shere Khan wants Mowgli and threatens the wolf pack.

844.q1.p: What fake name does Jack Worthing use in town?
844.q1.e: Jack calls himself Ernest in London, which Gwendolen adores.

844.q2.t: Inventing a fictional person as an excuse to escape duties
844.q2.p: What does "Bunburying" mean in the play?
844.q2.e: Algernon's imaginary friend Bunbury lets him leave town whenever he likes.

844.q3.h: The play is a comedy of manners.
844.q3.e: The play mocks the strict social rules and hypocrisy of upper-class Victorians.

844.q4.p: Lady Bracknell's short, witty, twisted sayings are known as:
844.q4.e: Epigrams are brief clever statements that turn ideas upside down.

844.q5.t: His real name is Ernest after all
844.q5.p: What is the final twist about Jack's name?
844.q5.e: It turns out Jack was born Ernest, so he has been truthful by accident.

5200.q1.t: He has turned into a giant insect
5200.q1.p: What does Gregor Samsa discover when he wakes up?
5200.q1.h: It is the very first line.
5200.q1.e: Gregor wakes to find himself transformed into a monstrous insect.

5200.q2.e: Gregor works as a traveling salesman to pay his parents' debt.

5200.q3.t: They grow more resentful and neglectful
5200.q3.p: What happens to the family's attitude toward Gregor over time?
5200.q3.e: As he can no longer work, the family's care turns to disgust and neglect.

5200.q4.t: It makes the situation more unsettling and absurd
5200.q4.p: The impossible event is told in a calm, matter-of-fact tone. What effect does that have?
5200.q4.h: Gregor worries about being late for work.
5200.q4.e: The contrast between a bizarre event and ordinary worries is central to Kafka's absurdism.

5200.q5.p: Which family member at first cares for Gregor and plays violin?
5200.q5.h: She brings him food at first.
5200.q5.e: Grete feeds Gregor at first and plays the violin, but later turns against him.

74.q1.t: He makes the work seem like a privilege
74.q1.p: How does Tom get other boys to whitewash his fence?
74.q1.h: Aunt Polly punishes him with the chore.
74.q1.e: Tom pretends painting is fun, so the other boys pay him to take a turn.

74.q2.p: What river runs near the setting of the story?
74.q2.e: The fictional St. Petersburg is a Mississippi River town.

74.q3.p: Which event does Tom witness in the graveyard?
74.q3.h: Tom and Huck were there to try a cure for warts.
74.q3.e: They witness Injun Joe kill Dr. Robinson, a secret they struggle to keep.

74.q4.p: Twain uses spelling to imitate how characters speak. This is called:
74.q4.e: Dialect spelling captures regional and social speech.

74.q5.p: Where do Tom and Becky get lost?
74.q5.h: It is on a school picnic.
74.q5.e: They wander through a cave and nearly die before Tom finds a way out.

25344.q1.p: What is Hester Prynne forced to wear?
25344.q1.e: The letter A stands for adultery.

25344.q2.p: Where and when is the story set?
25344.q2.h: It is a strictly religious colony.
25344.q2.e: The story takes place in seventeenth-century Puritan Massachusetts.

25344.q3.p: Who is the father of Hester's daughter Pearl?
25344.q3.e: Dimmesdale keeps his secret while suffering from guilt.

25344.q4.p: The scarlet letter takes on new meanings across the story. What technique is this?
25344.q4.h: One object stands for many ideas.
25344.q4.e: Hawthorne makes the A a shifting symbol from "adulterer" to "able" to "angel".

25344.q5.p: What is Roger Chillingworth's secret relationship to Hester?
25344.q5.h: He hides his identity to take revenge.
25344.q5.e: He is her husband, who arrives in town and torments Dimmesdale.

1727.q1.p: Where is Odysseus trying to return?
1727.q1.h: His wife and son wait there.
1727.q1.e: Odysseus spends ten years trying to return to Ithaca.

1727.q2.p: Who waits for Odysseus and fends off suitors?
1727.q2.h: She weaves and unweaves a shroud.

1727.q3.t: He blinds him and gives his name as "Nobody"
1727.q3.p: How does Odysseus escape the Cyclops Polyphemus?
1727.q3.h: A trick with his name is key.
1727.q3.e: He blinds Polyphemus and tells him his name is Nobody, so the other Cyclopes do not help.

1727.q4.p: Phrases like "rosy-fingered Dawn" repeated through the poem are called:
1727.q4.h: They help oral poets remember lines.
1727.q4.e: Fixed epithets are a hallmark of oral epic.

1727.q5.p: Which value is tested when strangers arrive at a home in the poem?
1727.q5.h: Good hosts are praised; bad hosts are punished.
1727.q5.e: Many episodes judge characters by how they treat guests.

6130.q1.h: The first word of the poem is "wrath".
6130.q1.e: The poem opens with the rage of Achilles.

6130.q2.p: Which war does the poem cover?
6130.q2.h: It is set in the tenth year.
6130.q2.e: The poem is set late in the Greeks' ten-year siege of Troy.

6130.q3.p: What event makes Achilles return to battle?
6130.q3.e: Hector kills Patroclus, and Achilles fights to avenge him.

6130.q4.p: Long comparisons that stretch across many lines, like a warrior compared to a lion, are called:
6130.q4.e: Epic similes add scale and imagery to battle scenes.

6130.q5.t: Priam begs for Hector's body and they share grief
6130.q5.p: What happens when King Priam visits Achilles?
6130.q5.h: It is one of the poem's most moving scenes.
6130.q5.e: Achilles returns Hector's body to Priam, and both mourn their losses.

145.q1.p: Who is the idealistic young woman at the center of the novel?

145.q2.e: Middlemarch is a Midlands town shown around 1830.

145.q3.p: Whom does Dorothea marry first, expecting a life of intellectual purpose?
145.q3.h: He is writing the "Key to All Mythologies".
145.q3.e: She marries Casaubon and finds the marriage disappointing.

145.q4.p: Eliot's narrator often steps in to comment on characters and morality. This is called:
145.q4.e: The narrator knows all and comments on events.

145.q5.t: Many small, unrecorded acts can shape the world
145.q5.p: What does the novel suggest about a good life?
145.q5.h: See the final paragraph on "unhistoric acts".
145.q5.e: The ending says the growing good of the world depends partly on unhistoric acts.

1661.q1.p: Who narrates most of the stories?
1661.q1.h: He is Holmes's friend and housemate.
1661.q1.e: Dr. John Watson narrates, which keeps Holmes's method a mystery.

1661.q2.p: What is the address of Sherlock Holmes?
1661.q2.e: Holmes and Watson live at 221B Baker Street in London.

1661.q3.p: Which method does Holmes emphasize in solving cases?
1661.q3.e: Holmes reads small clues such as mud, hands, and clothing.

1661.q4.p: A false clue that leads away from the truth is called a:
1661.q4.e: A red herring misleads readers and characters.

1661.q5.p: In "A Scandal in Bohemia", who outwits Holmes?
1661.q5.e: Irene Adler outsmarts Holmes and is called "the woman" by him.

17405.q1.p: What does Sun Tzu say is the best way to win?
17405.q1.h: He prefers to avoid costly battles.
17405.q1.e: He says the supreme art is to subdue the enemy without fighting.

17405.q2.p: In which country was the text written?
17405.q2.h: It dates from the Warring States and earlier period.
17405.q2.e: The Art of War comes from ancient China.

17405.q3.t: Knowing both prevents defeat in a hundred battles
17405.q3.p: What does the text say about knowing yourself and your enemy?
17405.q3.e: Sun Tzu says one who knows both will not be in danger in a hundred battles.

17405.q4.p: Short, memorable statements of principle in the book are called:
17405.q4.e: The text is made up of concise aphorisms.

17405.q5.t: A move meant to mislead the opponent
17405.q5.e: A feint misleads the enemy about your true intent.

hs-capitals.q1.t: Berry Gordy started Motown Records in Detroit in 1959.
hs-capitals.q1.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q1.h: Names of people, companies and cities begin with capitals; small words in the middle of the sentence do not.
hs-capitals.q1.e: Capitalize the names of people (Berry Gordy), companies (Motown Records) and cities (Detroit), but not every word. Berry Gordy founded Motown in Detroit in 1959.

hs-capitals.q2.t: Woodstock took place in August 1969 near Bethel, New York.
hs-capitals.q2.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q2.h: Months and the names of towns and states are proper nouns.
hs-capitals.q2.e: Months, towns and states are capitalized. The Woodstock music festival was held in August 1969 on a farm near Bethel, New York.

hs-capitals.q3.t: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg, Austria, in 1756.
hs-capitals.q3.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q3.h: Every part of a person's name and every place name needs a capital.
hs-capitals.q3.e: Each part of a name and each place name is capitalized, but ordinary words like "born" are not. Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756.

hs-capitals.q4.p: Which title is capitalized correctly? Scott Joplin published this ragtime song in 1899.
hs-capitals.q4.h: In a title, capitalize the important words, including the first one.
hs-capitals.q4.e: Titles capitalize the first word and the important words. Scott Joplin published "Maple Leaf Rag" in 1899, and it became ragtime's best-known piece.

hs-capitals.q5.t: The Lumière brothers showed films to a paying audience in Paris in December 1895.
hs-capitals.q5.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q5.h: Capitalize family names, cities and months, but not common nouns like "films" or "brothers" when they are not part of a name.
hs-capitals.q5.e: Lumière, Paris and December are proper nouns; "brothers" and "films" are common nouns here. The Lumière brothers held the first public paid film screening in Paris in December 1895.

hs-capitals.q6.p: Which title is capitalized correctly? This 1939 film made famous use of Technicolor.
hs-capitals.q6.h: Small words like "of" stay lowercase in the middle of a title.
hs-capitals.q6.e: Capitalize the first word and the important words of a title, but keep small words like "of" lowercase. The Wizard of Oz (1939) was filmed in Technicolor.

hs-capitals.q7.t: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, which came out in 1941.
hs-capitals.q7.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q7.h: A person's name and a film title both start with capitals; a verb like "directed" does not.
hs-capitals.q7.e: Names of people and the important words of film titles are capitalized. Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, released in 1941.

hs-capitals.q8.t: Claude Monet painted Impression, Sunrise in the French port of Le Havre.
hs-capitals.q8.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q8.h: Look at the nationality word and the city name too.
hs-capitals.q8.e: Names, titles, nationalities (French) and cities (Le Havre) are capitalized. Monet painted Impression, Sunrise in 1872 in Le Havre, and its title later gave Impressionism its name.

hs-capitals.q9.t: The daguerreotype, named for Louis Daguerre, was announced in France in 1839.
hs-capitals.q9.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q9.h: A thing named after a person is a common noun, but the person's own name is not.
hs-capitals.q9.e: The person (Louis Daguerre) and the country (France) are capitalized, but the object name "daguerreotype" is a common noun. This early photograph process was announced in 1839.

hs-capitals.q10.t: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, sold shares in Amsterdam.
hs-capitals.q10.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.q10.h: A company's full name is capitalized as one name; ordinary nouns like "shares" are not.
hs-capitals.q10.e: The full name of a company and the name of a city are capitalized, while "shares" is a common noun. The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, was one of the first companies to sell shares to the public.

hs-end-marks.q1.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Did Louis Armstrong record with his Hot Five in Chicago in the 1920s____
hs-end-marks.q1.e: A sentence that asks something ends with a question mark. Yes: Louis Armstrong made landmark recordings with his Hot Five in Chicago in the 1920s.

hs-end-marks.q2.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: What a thrill it must have been to see the Beatles on The Ed Sullivan Show in February 1964____
hs-end-marks.q2.h: The sentence shows a strong feeling.
hs-end-marks.q2.e: An exclamation point shows strong feeling, here excitement. The Beatles appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show in February 1964 and drew a huge television audience.

hs-end-marks.q3.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Ask any jazz fan who made the album Kind of Blue____
hs-end-marks.q3.h: The sentence is a command that contains a question inside it.
hs-end-marks.q3.e: The sentence tells someone to ask, so it is a command and takes a period, even though a question is tucked inside it. Miles Davis recorded Kind of Blue in 1959.

hs-end-marks.q4.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: The first video MTV played was "Video Killed the Radio Star" by the Buggles____
hs-end-marks.q4.e: A plain statement of fact ends with a period. MTV launched on August 1, 1981, and began with that Buggles video.

hs-end-marks.q5.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Did Georges Méliès make A Trip to the Moon in 1902____
hs-end-marks.q5.e: It asks something, so it ends with a question mark. Yes: the French magician Georges Méliès made A Trip to the Moon in 1902.

hs-end-marks.q6.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Hooray, Parasite won Best Picture in 2020____
hs-end-marks.q6.e: The interjection "Hooray" signals strong feeling, so an exclamation point fits. Parasite became the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture at the Academy Awards.

hs-end-marks.q7.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Toy Story, released in 1995, was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation____
hs-end-marks.q7.h: This is a calm statement, not a question or a shout.
hs-end-marks.q7.e: A statement of fact ends with a period. Pixar's Toy Story (1995) was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

hs-end-marks.q8.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Who painted The Starry Night in 1889____
hs-end-marks.q8.e: A sentence that begins with "Who" and asks for information takes a question mark. Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.

hs-end-marks.q9.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Dorothea Lange took the photograph Migrant Mother in 1936____
hs-end-marks.q9.h: It tells a fact in a calm voice.
hs-end-marks.q9.e: A statement ends with a period. Dorothea Lange took Migrant Mother in 1936 while documenting the hardships of the Great Depression.

hs-end-marks.q10.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Wow, Henry Ford paid workers five dollars a day in 1914____
hs-end-marks.q10.e: An exclamation point shows surprise or excitement, as "Wow" signals. In 1914 Henry Ford announced a five-dollar day, about double the usual factory wage.

hs-verb-tense.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: In 1877 Thomas Edison ____ the phonograph.
hs-verb-tense.q1.h: When did it happen: before, now, or later?
hs-verb-tense.q1.e: Past tense is needed because it happened in 1877. Edison announced his phonograph in 1877, the first device that could record and play back sound.

hs-verb-tense.q2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: When you visit Detroit next summer, you ____ the Motown Museum, once Berry Gordy's Hitsville U.S.A.
hs-verb-tense.q2.h: The word "next" points toward the future.
hs-verb-tense.q2.e: Future tense is needed because the visit is "next summer." The Motown Museum in Detroit is in the house where Berry Gordy's Hitsville U.S.A. studio operated.

hs-verb-tense.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: By 1982, Sony and Philips ____ the compact disc.
hs-verb-tense.q3.h: The action was finished before the year 1982 arrived.
hs-verb-tense.q3.e: Past perfect shows an action completed before a past time ("By 1982"). Sony and Philips developed the compact disc, which reached stores in 1982.

hs-verb-tense.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Mozart ____ more than 600 works before he died in 1791.
hs-verb-tense.q4.h: He died in 1791, so his writing is over.
hs-verb-tense.q4.e: The past tense "composed" matches "died in 1791." Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart wrote more than 600 works in a life that lasted only 35 years.

hs-verb-tense.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: In 1927 audiences ____ Al Jolson sing and speak in The Jazz Singer.
hs-verb-tense.q5.h: Look for the year in the sentence.
hs-verb-tense.q5.e: The year 1927 signals past tense. The Jazz Singer (1927) was the first feature film with synchronized singing and speech, and it launched the era of "talkies."

hs-verb-tense.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Pixar's Toy Story, released in 1995, ____ the first fully computer-animated feature film.
hs-verb-tense.q6.h: The film came out long ago; match the past.
hs-verb-tense.q6.e: The film was released in 1995, so the past tense "was" fits. Toy Story was the first feature made entirely with computer animation.

hs-verb-tense.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Every year the Academy Awards ____ filmmakers, a tradition that began in 1929.
hs-verb-tense.q7.h: "Every year" describes something that goes on now; "began" is past.
hs-verb-tense.q7.e: A habit that continues today uses present tense ("honor"), while "began in 1929" stays past. The first Academy Awards ceremony was held in 1929.

hs-verb-tense.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: In 1888 George Eastman ____ the Kodak camera with the slogan "You press the button, we do the rest."
hs-verb-tense.q8.e: The past tense "introduced" matches the year 1888. George Eastman's Kodak camera came loaded with film, and customers mailed it back to be developed.

hs-verb-tense.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Michelangelo ____ the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.
hs-verb-tense.q9.h: The dates are in the past.
hs-verb-tense.q9.e: The dates 1508 to 1512 call for past tense. Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Rome over those years.

hs-verb-tense.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: In 1914 Henry Ford ____ a wage of five dollars a day.
hs-verb-tense.q10.e: The year 1914 is in the past, so past tense is needed. Henry Ford announced the five-dollar day, roughly doubling typical factory pay.

hs-sv-agree.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The Beatles ____ from Liverpool, England.
hs-sv-agree.q1.h: Is the subject one band member or a group?
hs-sv-agree.q1.e: The plural subject "Beatles" takes the plural verb "come." The Beatles formed in Liverpool, England, in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

hs-sv-agree.q2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Each of the four concertos in Vivaldi's The Four Seasons ____ a different season.
hs-sv-agree.q2.e: "Each" is singular, so it takes "represents," even though "concertos" comes right before the blank. Antonio Vivaldi of Venice wrote these four violin concertos.

hs-sv-agree.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Neither Beethoven nor Mozart ____ born in Vienna; Beethoven was born in Bonn.
hs-sv-agree.q3.h: With "neither...nor," match the verb to the subject closest to it.
hs-sv-agree.q3.e: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "Mozart," which is singular, so "was." Beethoven was born in Bonn and Mozart in Salzburg; both later worked in Vienna.

hs-sv-agree.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Hip hop, which began at block parties in the Bronx in the 1970s, ____ now a worldwide art form.
hs-sv-agree.q4.h: Ignore the phrase between commas; what is the subject?
hs-sv-agree.q4.e: The subject "Hip hop" is singular, so it takes "is." Hip hop grew out of block parties in the Bronx, New York, in the 1970s.

hs-sv-agree.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Silent films, which dominated until the late 1920s, ____ often accompanied by live pianists or orchestras.
hs-sv-agree.q5.h: The subject is plural and the time is past.
hs-sv-agree.q5.e: The plural subject "films" takes "were." Before recorded sound, theaters hired live musicians to accompany silent films.

hs-sv-agree.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The special effects in Star Wars, which opened in 1977, ____ still admired today.
hs-sv-agree.q6.e: The plural subject "effects" takes "are." Star Wars opened in 1977, and George Lucas founded the effects company Industrial Light & Magic to create its visuals.

hs-sv-agree.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: There ____ many stars of the silent era, including Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton.
hs-sv-agree.q7.h: In "There ___" sentences, the subject comes after the verb.
hs-sv-agree.q7.e: The real subject is the plural "stars," so the verb must be "were." Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton were two of the greatest comedians of silent film.

hs-sv-agree.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Monet's water lily paintings, which he made at his garden in Giverny, ____ in museums around the world.
hs-sv-agree.q8.e: The plural subject "paintings" takes "hang." Claude Monet painted his water lilies at his garden in Giverny, France.

hs-sv-agree.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Ansel Adams, along with Edward Weston and Imogen Cunningham, ____ a member of Group f/64, which formed in 1932.
hs-sv-agree.q9.h: "Along with..." does not make the subject plural.
hs-sv-agree.q9.e: Phrases that begin with "along with" do not change the subject, which is the singular "Ansel Adams," so "was." Group f/64 was a California photography group formed in 1932 to promote sharply focused images.

hs-sv-agree.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The Dutch East India Company, one of the first companies to sell shares to the public, ____ founded in 1602.
hs-sv-agree.q10.h: Find the main subject before the long phrase.
hs-sv-agree.q10.e: The subject is the singular "Company," so "was." The Dutch East India Company (1602) pioneered selling shares to ordinary investors.

hs-homophones.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Chuck Berry recorded "Johnny B. Goode" in 1958, and ____ still a rock classic.
hs-homophones.q1.h: Can you replace the blank with "it is"?
hs-homophones.q1.e: "It's" means "it is," and the sentence needs that meaning. Chuck Berry released "Johnny B. Goode" in 1958.

hs-homophones.q2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Motown artists recorded in a small Detroit house, and ____ sound became famous worldwide.
hs-homophones.q2.h: Whose sound? It belongs to the artists.
hs-homophones.q2.e: "Their" shows ownership. Motown's early records were made at Hitsville U.S.A., a modest house in Detroit.

hs-homophones.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Johann Sebastian Bach traveled ____ Lübeck, Germany, in 1705 to hear the organist Dieterich Buxtehude.
hs-homophones.q3.e: "To" shows direction. Bach traveled to the city of Lübeck to hear Buxtehude play the organ.

hs-homophones.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: ____ welcome to tour Sun Studio in Memphis, where Elvis Presley made his first records in the 1950s.
hs-homophones.q4.e: "You're" means "you are." Sun Studio in Memphis is where Elvis Presley recorded his first singles in the 1950s.

hs-homophones.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Silent films had no recorded dialogue, so ____ stories were told with pictures and title cards.
hs-homophones.q5.e: "Their" shows that the stories belong to the films. Silent films used title cards to show dialogue and explain the action.

hs-homophones.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Auguste and Louis Lumière were ____ brothers who patented the Cinématographe in 1895.
hs-homophones.q6.e: "Two" is the number. The brothers Auguste and Louis Lumière patented the Cinématographe, a camera and projector in one, in 1895.

hs-homophones.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Charlie Chaplin made The Kid in 1921, and ____ still moving today.
hs-homophones.q7.e: "It's" means "it is." The Kid (1921) was Chaplin's first full-length feature as director.

hs-homophones.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: ____ in luck if you visit the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, because Monet's huge Water Lilies panels hang there.
hs-homophones.q8.e: "You're" is the contraction of "you are." The Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris displays Monet's large Water Lilies panels.

hs-homophones.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The first Kodak camera, sold in 1888, came loaded with film, and ____ price was twenty-five dollars.
hs-homophones.q9.h: Is the camera showing ownership of the price, or is "it is" meant?
hs-homophones.q9.e: "Its" shows possession, with no apostrophe. The 1888 Kodak cost $25 and came with film for 100 pictures.

hs-homophones.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Banks in medieval Florence, like the Medici Bank founded in 1397, helped merchants send money ____ other cities.
hs-homophones.q10.h: Which word shows where the money goes?
hs-homophones.q10.e: "To" shows direction. The Medici Bank, founded in Florence in 1397, moved money between cities for merchants.

hs-commas.q1.t: The Beatles' lineup was John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.
hs-commas.q1.h: Items in a list are separated by commas, and you do not put one right after "was."
hs-commas.q1.e: Commas separate the items in a series, with no comma after the verb "was" or after "and." The Beatles were John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr.

hs-commas.q2.t: In 1913, Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring caused an uproar at its Paris premiere.
hs-commas.q2.h: An introductory phrase is followed by a comma, and nothing else needs splitting.
hs-commas.q2.e: A comma follows an introductory phrase such as "In 1913." Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring caused an uproar at its Paris premiere in 1913.

hs-commas.q3.t: Wendy Carlos released Switched-On Bach in 1968, and the album used a Moog synthesizer to play Bach's music.
hs-commas.q3.h: Two complete sentences joined by "and" need a comma before "and."
hs-commas.q3.e: Put a comma before the conjunction when it joins two independent clauses. Wendy Carlos used a Moog synthesizer on Switched-On Bach in 1968.

hs-commas.q4.t: Sun Records, the Memphis label of Sam Phillips, released early records by Elvis Presley.
hs-commas.q4.h: A phrase that renames a noun and could be removed needs a comma on both sides.
hs-commas.q4.e: Commas set off a nonessential appositive on both sides. Sam Phillips's Sun Records in Memphis released Elvis Presley's early records.

hs-commas.q5.t: Early film directors included Alice Guy-Blaché, Georges Méliès, and Edwin S. Porter.
hs-commas.q5.h: Separate three or more items in a series.
hs-commas.q5.e: Commas separate items in a series. Alice Guy-Blaché in France, Georges Méliès in France and Edwin S. Porter in the United States were all early film directors.

hs-commas.q6.t: In 1937, Disney released Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first full-length cel-animated feature.
hs-commas.q6.h: There are two places that need a comma: after the opening phrase and before the renaming phrase.
hs-commas.q6.e: A comma follows the introductory phrase and another sets off the appositive. Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) was the first full-length cel-animated feature.

hs-commas.q7.t: Alfred Hitchcock released Psycho in 1960, and its shower scene became one of the most famous in film history.
hs-commas.q7.h: Avoid a comma splice: a comma alone cannot join two sentences.
hs-commas.q7.e: A comma plus "and" joins two independent clauses; a comma alone creates a comma splice. Hitchcock's Psycho (1960) is remembered for its shower scene.

hs-commas.q8.t: After Impression, Sunrise appeared at an exhibition in Paris in 1874, a critic mocked Monet and his friends as "Impressionists."
hs-commas.q8.h: When a sentence opens with a dependent clause, where should the comma go?
hs-commas.q8.e: A comma separates an introductory dependent clause from the main clause. A critic's mocking review of the 1874 Paris exhibition gave Impressionism its name.

hs-commas.q9.t: Ansel Adams photographed Yosemite, Death Valley, and the Grand Tetons.
hs-commas.q9.h: Use commas between items in a series.
hs-commas.q9.e: Commas separate the places in the series. Ansel Adams photographed Yosemite, Death Valley and the Grand Tetons among many American landscapes.

hs-commas.q10.t: The first modern credit card, the Diners Club card, appeared in 1950.
hs-commas.q10.h: The renaming phrase needs commas on both sides.
hs-commas.q10.e: An appositive that renames a noun is set off by a pair of commas. The Diners Club card, introduced in 1950, is considered the first general-purpose charge card.

hs-apostrophes.q1.p: Choose the correct form: ____ choral finale sets Friedrich Schiller's poem "Ode to Joy."
hs-apostrophes.q1.e: A singular possessive adds apostrophe + s: "Symphony's." Beethoven's Ninth Symphony ends with a choral finale based on Schiller's "Ode to Joy."

hs-apostrophes.q2.p: Choose the correct form: ____ guitar riffs inspired the Beatles and the Rolling Stones.
hs-apostrophes.q2.h: Chuck Berry owns the riffs; he is one person.
hs-apostrophes.q2.e: A singular owner takes apostrophe + s. Chuck Berry's guitar style strongly influenced the Beatles and the Rolling Stones.

hs-apostrophes.q3.p: Choose the correctly punctuated song title. Elvis Presley's first single on Sun Records came out in 1954.
hs-apostrophes.q3.h: The title contains the contraction of "that is."
hs-apostrophes.q3.e: The apostrophe in the contraction stands for the missing letter in "that is" and goes where the letter was left out. Elvis's first Sun single, "That's All Right," was recorded in July 1954.

hs-apostrophes.q4.p: Choose the correct form: ____ playing drove dozens of Motown hits.
hs-apostrophes.q4.h: The group is plural and ends in s.
hs-apostrophes.q4.e: A plural noun ending in -s shows possession with just an apostrophe after the s. The Funk Brothers were Motown's house band.

hs-apostrophes.q5.p: Choose the correct form: ____ Seven Samurai (1954) inspired the Hollywood western The Magnificent Seven.
hs-apostrophes.q5.e: A singular possessive takes apostrophe + s. Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai (1954) inspired the 1960 western The Magnificent Seven.

hs-apostrophes.q6.p: Choose the correct form: ____ deep-focus cinematography, by Gregg Toland, let every part of a scene stay sharp.
hs-apostrophes.q6.e: A singular title takes apostrophe + s to show possession. Gregg Toland's deep-focus photography on Citizen Kane kept foreground and background in sharp focus.

hs-apostrophes.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Chaplin ____ make a fully talking film until The Great Dictator in 1940.
hs-apostrophes.q7.h: Where did the missing letter go in "did not"?
hs-apostrophes.q7.e: In a contraction, the apostrophe replaces the missing letter: did + not = didn't. Chaplin's first fully talking film was The Great Dictator (1940).

hs-apostrophes.q8.p: Choose the correct form: ____ Guernica (1937) shows the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.
hs-apostrophes.q8.e: A singular possessive takes apostrophe + s. Pablo Picasso painted Guernica in 1937 after the bombing of the Basque town.

hs-apostrophes.q9.p: Choose the correct form: American painter ____ pictures of mothers and children were shown with the Impressionists in Paris.
hs-apostrophes.q9.e: A singular possessive takes apostrophe + s. Mary Cassatt, an American in Paris, exhibited with the Impressionists.

hs-apostrophes.q10.p: Choose the correct form: ____ charter dates to 1694.
hs-apostrophes.q10.h: Add the apostrophe to the end of the whole name.
hs-apostrophes.q10.e: The possessive goes on the last word of the name: "England's." The Bank of England was founded by royal charter in 1694.

hs-pronouns.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Sam Phillips, ____ founded Sun Records in 1952, recorded Elvis Presley.
hs-pronouns.q1.h: Is the missing word doing the founding, or receiving something?
hs-pronouns.q1.e: "Who" is the subject of "founded." Sam Phillips founded Sun Records in Memphis in 1952.

hs-pronouns.q2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Bob Dylan won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016, and the committee praised ____ for creating new poetic expressions in the American song tradition.
hs-pronouns.q2.h: The pronoun is the object of "praised."
hs-pronouns.q2.e: Use the object pronoun "him" after the verb "praised." Bob Dylan received the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.

hs-pronouns.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: My friend and ____ learned that Duke Ellington's orchestra began playing at the Cotton Club in Harlem in 1927.
hs-pronouns.q3.h: Drop "My friend and." Would you say "me learned"?
hs-pronouns.q3.e: "I" is the subject of "learned"; test it by removing the other person. Duke Ellington's orchestra began its Cotton Club engagement in Harlem in 1927.

hs-pronouns.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The trumpeter ____ many people call a founder of jazz soloing, Louis Armstrong, grew up in New Orleans.
hs-pronouns.q4.e: "Whom" is the object of "call" (many people call him). Louis Armstrong was born and raised in New Orleans.

hs-pronouns.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Steven Spielberg, ____ directed Jaws in 1975, helped create the summer blockbuster.
hs-pronouns.q5.h: The missing word is the subject of "directed."
hs-pronouns.q5.e: "Who" is the subject of "directed." Steven Spielberg directed Jaws in 1975, often called the first summer blockbuster.

hs-pronouns.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The film club showed Metropolis, Fritz Lang's 1927 silent classic, to my brother and ____.
hs-pronouns.q6.h: Remove "my brother and." Would you say "showed to I"?
hs-pronouns.q6.e: "Me" is correct as the object of the preposition "to." Metropolis is Fritz Lang's 1927 silent science-fiction film.

hs-pronouns.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Georges Méliès was a stage magician before ____ became a filmmaker.
hs-pronouns.q7.h: The pronoun is the subject of "became."
hs-pronouns.q7.e: The subject pronoun "he" is needed. Georges Méliès was a Paris stage magician before he made trick films like A Trip to the Moon.

hs-pronouns.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Vincent van Gogh, ____ brother Theo supported him financially, painted more than 800 works.
hs-pronouns.q8.e: "Whose" shows ownership. Vincent van Gogh's brother Theo, an art dealer, supported him financially throughout his career.

hs-pronouns.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Edgar Degas, ____ Mary Cassatt admired and befriended, invited her to exhibit with the Impressionists.
hs-pronouns.q9.e: "Whom" is the object of "admired." Degas and Mary Cassatt became friends, and he invited her to show her work with the Impressionists.

hs-pronouns.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Henry Ford, ____ introduced the moving assembly line in 1913, cut the time to build a Model T dramatically.
hs-pronouns.q10.h: The missing word is the subject of "introduced."
hs-pronouns.q10.e: "Who" is the subject of "introduced." Henry Ford introduced the moving assembly line at his Highland Park plant in 1913.

hs-modifiers.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Johann Sebastian Bach, born in Eisenach in 1685, played the organ ____.
hs-modifiers.q1.h: The word describes how he played.
hs-modifiers.q1.e: An adverb describes a verb: he played "brilliantly." Bach was born in Eisenach, Germany, in 1685 and was renowned as an organist.

hs-modifiers.q2.t: Nearly deaf, Beethoven completed his Ninth Symphony in 1824.
hs-modifiers.q2.p: Which sentence has NO dangling modifier?
hs-modifiers.q2.h: Who is "nearly deaf"? The word right after the comma should be that person.
hs-modifiers.q2.e: The opening phrase must describe the word right after the comma. Beethoven, not the symphony, was nearly deaf; he completed his Ninth Symphony in 1824.

hs-modifiers.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Early Moog synthesizers sounded ____ to listeners in the late 1960s.
hs-modifiers.q3.h: After "sounded," use a word that describes the subject.
hs-modifiers.q3.e: "Sounded" is a linking verb, so it takes an adjective: "strange." Robert Moog's synthesizers became popular in the late 1960s.

hs-modifiers.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Aretha Franklin sang "Respect" ____ in 1967, and it topped the charts.
hs-modifiers.q4.h: The word describes how she sang.
hs-modifiers.q4.e: An adverb describes how an action is done: she sang "powerfully." "Respect" reached number one in 1967.

hs-modifiers.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Buster Keaton did his own stunts ____ and rarely used doubles.
hs-modifiers.q5.h: The word describes how he did the stunts.
hs-modifiers.q5.e: An adverb modifies the verb "did," so use "fearlessly." Buster Keaton was famous for performing his own dangerous stunts in silent comedies.

hs-modifiers.q6.t: Because the mechanical shark kept breaking down, Spielberg showed it sparingly in Jaws.
hs-modifiers.q6.p: Which sentence has NO dangling modifier?
hs-modifiers.q6.e: The first phrase must clearly name what broke down: the shark. The mechanical shark in Jaws (1975) malfunctioned so often that Spielberg showed it only briefly.

hs-modifiers.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Technicolor films of the 1930s looked ____ because the process used three strips of film.
hs-modifiers.q7.e: "Looked" is a linking verb, so it takes the adjective "vivid." The three-strip Technicolor process of the 1930s produced rich, saturated color.

hs-modifiers.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Monet painted ____ outdoors to catch changing light.
hs-modifiers.q8.h: The word describes how he painted.
hs-modifiers.q8.e: An adverb modifies the verb "painted." Claude Monet painted series of haystacks and of Rouen Cathedral to capture changing light.

hs-modifiers.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The daguerreotype produced ____ detailed images on silver-coated copper plates.
hs-modifiers.q9.e: An adverb can modify an adjective: "remarkably detailed." Daguerreotypes were sharp photographs on silver-coated copper plates.

hs-modifiers.q10.t: Weighed down by heavy strings of copper coins, merchants in Song China welcomed paper money.
hs-modifiers.q10.p: Which sentence has NO dangling modifier?
hs-modifiers.q10.h: Who was weighed down? That person should come right after the comma.
hs-modifiers.q10.e: Merchants, not the money, were weighed down, so "merchants" must follow the comma. Paper money appeared in Song dynasty China partly because copper coins were so heavy to carry.

hs-parallel.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Johann Sebastian Bach served as an organist, a court composer, and a ____ in Leipzig.
hs-parallel.q1.h: Keep the list items in the same form: "a ___" nouns.
hs-parallel.q1.e: Parallel structure keeps all items in the same grammatical form, here "a" + noun. Bach was cantor of the St. Thomas church school in Leipzig from 1723.

hs-parallel.q2.t: for making hit records with Mary Ford
hs-parallel.q2.p: Which choice completes the sentence in parallel form? Les Paul is remembered for building a solid-body electric guitar, for pioneering multitrack recording, and ____.
hs-parallel.q2.h: Start the third item the way the first two start.
hs-parallel.q2.e: Each item should begin "for" + -ing word. Les Paul built early solid-body guitars, pioneered multitrack recording and had hits with Mary Ford.

hs-parallel.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Motown's Artist Development department taught singers stage choreography, grooming, and ____.
hs-parallel.q3.h: The other two items are single nouns.
hs-parallel.q3.e: Choreography, grooming and etiquette are all nouns, so the list is parallel. Motown trained its young stars in presentation and manners.

hs-parallel.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Hip hop grew from four elements: DJing, rapping, breakdancing, and ____.
hs-parallel.q4.e: Parallel items share a form: DJing, rapping, breakdancing and graffiti writing. These are widely listed as the four core elements of hip hop culture.

hs-parallel.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Alice Guy-Blaché wrote, directed, and ____ films in France and the United States.
hs-parallel.q5.h: Match the verb form of "wrote" and "directed."
hs-parallel.q5.e: All three verbs should be in the simple past: wrote, directed, produced. Alice Guy-Blaché founded her own studio, Solax, in the United States in 1910.

hs-parallel.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Early nickelodeons charged a nickel, showed short films, and ____ pianists to accompany them.
hs-parallel.q6.e: Keep every verb in the same form: charged, showed, hired. Nickelodeon theaters of the early 1900s charged a nickel for admission.

hs-parallel.q7.t: for appearing briefly in his own movies
hs-parallel.q7.p: Which choice completes the sentence in parallel form? Alfred Hitchcock became famous for directing suspense films, for hosting a television series, and ____.
hs-parallel.q7.e: The series uses "for" + -ing: directing, hosting, appearing. Hitchcock hosted the television show Alfred Hitchcock Presents and made cameo appearances in his films.

hs-parallel.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Leonardo da Vinci was a painter, an engineer, and ____.
hs-parallel.q8.e: All items are nouns naming kinds of people: a painter, an engineer, an anatomist. Leonardo made detailed drawings of the human body.

hs-parallel.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: During the 1930s Dorothea Lange traveled across the country, photographed migrant workers, and ____ attention to their hardship.
hs-parallel.q9.e: The three verbs must share a form: traveled, photographed, drew. Dorothea Lange's Depression-era photographs drew national attention to migrant workers.

hs-parallel.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Early banks in Florence, such as the Medici Bank, held deposits, exchanged currencies, and ____ loans to merchants and rulers.
hs-parallel.q10.e: Keep all verbs in the simple past: held, exchanged, made. Banks like the Medici Bank helped create modern banking in Renaissance Florence.

hs-semicolons.q1.t: Louis Armstrong recorded with his Hot Five in Chicago; the recordings helped make the solo central to jazz.
hs-semicolons.q1.h: Two closely related complete sentences can be joined with a semicolon.
hs-semicolons.q1.e: A semicolon joins two independent clauses without a conjunction; a comma alone would be a splice. Armstrong's Hot Five recordings from Chicago in the 1920s made the solo central to jazz.

hs-semicolons.q2.t: Bob Dylan won a surprising honor in 2016: the Nobel Prize in Literature.
