hs-semicolons.q2.h: A colon follows a complete sentence and introduces the explanation.
hs-semicolons.q2.e: A colon after a complete sentence introduces a specific explanation or example. The honor was the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.

hs-semicolons.q3.t: Miles Davis's Kind of Blue—recorded in 1959—became one of the best-selling jazz albums ever.
hs-semicolons.q3.h: Dashes that set off an interruption come in a pair, one on each side.
hs-semicolons.q3.e: A pair of dashes sets off a nonessential interruption. Kind of Blue, recorded in 1959, is among the best-selling jazz albums of all time.

hs-semicolons.q4.t: Chuck Berry's sound blended two traditions: country music and rhythm and blues.
hs-semicolons.q4.h: What comes before the colon must be a complete sentence.
hs-semicolons.q4.e: A colon introduces a list after a complete clause. Chuck Berry mixed country music with rhythm and blues to help invent rock and roll.

hs-semicolons.q5.t: Silent films were accompanied by live musicians; however, The Jazz Singer (1927) used recorded sound.
hs-semicolons.q5.h: A conjunctive adverb like "however" between two sentences needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it.
hs-semicolons.q5.e: Use a semicolon before "however" and a comma after it when it joins two independent clauses. The Jazz Singer (1927) brought synchronized sound to a feature film.

hs-semicolons.q6.t: Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai (1954) follows a simple plan: villagers hire samurai to defend them from bandits.
hs-semicolons.q6.h: A colon can introduce a clause that explains the one before it.
hs-semicolons.q6.e: A colon follows a complete clause and introduces an explanation. In Seven Samurai, villagers hire samurai to protect them from bandits.

hs-semicolons.q7.t: Parasite—a South Korean film directed by Bong Joon-ho—became the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture in 2020.
hs-semicolons.q7.h: Both ends of the interrupting phrase need a dash.
hs-semicolons.q7.e: Paired dashes enclose the interrupting phrase. Parasite, directed by Bong Joon-ho, was the first non-English-language Best Picture winner.

hs-semicolons.q8.t: Claude Monet painted the same cathedral many times; he wanted to show how light changes.
hs-semicolons.q8.h: Two complete, related sentences can be joined with a semicolon alone.
hs-semicolons.q8.e: A semicolon links two related independent clauses. Monet painted about thirty views of Rouen Cathedral to show how light changed its look.

hs-semicolons.q9.t: In 1917 Marcel Duchamp submitted an ordinary porcelain urinal—which he titled Fountain—to an art exhibition in New York.
hs-semicolons.q9.h: Mark the start and end of the interrupting clause with matching dashes.
hs-semicolons.q9.e: A pair of dashes sets off the clause "which he titled Fountain." Duchamp's Fountain (1917) challenged ideas about what counts as art.

hs-semicolons.q10.t: Congress created the Federal Reserve in 1913; it serves as the central bank of the United States.
hs-semicolons.q10.h: Join two complete, related sentences with the right mark.
hs-semicolons.q10.e: A semicolon can join two related independent clauses. Congress created the Federal Reserve System in 1913, and it remains the central bank of the United States.

hs-word-choice.q1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Leo Fender's Broadcaster, introduced in 1950, was the first mass-produced solid-body electric guitar, and it had a lasting ____ on rock music.
hs-word-choice.q1.h: "Effect" is usually the noun; "affect" is usually the verb.
hs-word-choice.q1.e: The noun "effect" (a result) is needed after "a lasting." Leo Fender's 1950 Broadcaster, later renamed the Telecaster, shaped rock guitar sound.

hs-word-choice.q2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Napster, launched in 1999 by Shawn Fanning, began to ____ the way people bought music.
hs-word-choice.q2.h: You need a verb meaning "to influence."
hs-word-choice.q2.e: "Affect" is the verb meaning to influence. Napster, launched in 1999, let people share music files online and changed the music business.

hs-word-choice.q3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Fela Kuti, the Nigerian bandleader who created Afrobeat, did not merely ____ that the military rulers were corrupt; he said so openly in his songs.
hs-word-choice.q3.h: Who is sending the hint: the speaker or the listener?
hs-word-choice.q3.e: A speaker or writer implies; a listener or reader infers. Fela Kuti, who created Afrobeat in Nigeria, openly criticized the military government in his lyrics.

hs-word-choice.q4.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The ____ instrument in Vivaldi's The Four Seasons is the violin.
hs-word-choice.q4.h: One spelling means "main," the other means "a rule."
hs-word-choice.q4.e: "Principal" means main or most important; "principle" is a rule or belief. The Four Seasons are four violin concertos by Antonio Vivaldi of Venice.

hs-word-choice.q5.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: From the huge profits of Snow White in 1937, studio executives could ____ that audiences would pay to see feature-length cartoons.
hs-word-choice.q5.h: The executives are drawing a conclusion from evidence.
hs-word-choice.q5.e: A reader or observer infers; a speaker implies. Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) was a hit and led Disney to make more full-length cartoons.

hs-word-choice.q6.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The look of Metropolis, a 1927 silent film, seems to ____ a future ruled by machines.
hs-word-choice.q6.h: The film suggests an idea; it does not draw a conclusion.
hs-word-choice.q6.e: Something that suggests an idea implies it; the audience infers. Fritz Lang's Metropolis (1927) imagines a future city divided between workers and rulers.

hs-word-choice.q7.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The ____ photography for Star Wars began in Tunisia in 1976.
hs-word-choice.q7.e: "Principal photography" is the main filming period of a movie; "principle" would mean a rule. Star Wars filmed its desert scenes in Tunisia in 1976.

hs-word-choice.q8.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Renaissance artists in Florence adopted the ____ of linear perspective, which the architect Brunelleschi demonstrated in the early 1400s.
hs-word-choice.q8.h: This one means a rule or idea, not "main."
hs-word-choice.q8.e: "Principle" is a rule or basic idea; "principal" means main. Filippo Brunelleschi demonstrated linear perspective in Florence in the early 1400s.

hs-word-choice.q9.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The one-dollar Kodak Brownie camera of 1900 had a huge ____ on who could take photographs.
hs-word-choice.q9.h: After "a huge," you need a noun meaning "result."
hs-word-choice.q9.e: The noun "effect" means a result. The one-dollar Brownie, introduced in 1900, put cameras into the hands of ordinary families.

hs-word-choice.q10.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The stock market crash of October 1929 would ____ millions of Americans who lost savings.
hs-word-choice.q10.h: You need a verb meaning "to influence."
hs-word-choice.q10.e: "Affect" is the verb meaning to influence. The October 1929 stock market crash marked the start of the Great Depression.

hs-capitals.s1.t: Jackie Robinson joined the Brooklyn Dodgers in April 1947.
hs-capitals.s1.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.s1.h: Names of people, teams and months begin with capitals; ordinary words like "joined" do not.
hs-capitals.s1.e: Capitalize people (Jackie Robinson), teams (Brooklyn Dodgers) and months (April), but not every word. Robinson made his major-league debut for the Dodgers on April 15, 1947.

hs-capitals.s2.t: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
hs-capitals.s2.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.s2.h: Look at the name of the event and the names of the city and country.
hs-capitals.s2.e: The Olympic Games is a proper name, and Athens and Greece are places, so all are capitalized, while "first modern" is not. The first modern Olympics took place in Athens in 1896.

hs-capitals.s3.t: Pelé led Brazil to the World Cup title in Sweden in 1958.
hs-capitals.s3.p: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
hs-capitals.s3.h: Check the name of the player, the country, the tournament and the host country.
hs-capitals.s3.e: Names of people, countries and events are capitalized, including both words of "World Cup." Seventeen-year-old Pelé helped Brazil win the 1958 World Cup in Sweden.

hs-end-marks.s1.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Did Roger Bannister run a mile in under four minutes in 1954____
hs-end-marks.s1.e: A sentence that asks something ends with a question mark. Yes: on May 6, 1954, Roger Bannister became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes.

hs-end-marks.s2.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: What a speedy sprinter Jesse Owens was in the 1936 Olympic Games____
hs-end-marks.s2.e: An exclamation point shows strong feeling, here admiration. Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin.

hs-end-marks.s3.p: Choose the best ending mark for this sentence: Wilma Rudolph won three gold medals at the 1960 Olympic Games in Rome____
hs-end-marks.s3.e: A plain statement of fact ends with a period. Wilma Rudolph won the 100 meters, the 200 meters and the relay in Rome in 1960.

hs-verb-tense.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: In 1891 James Naismith ____ basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts.
hs-verb-tense.s1.h: When did it happen: before, now, or later?
hs-verb-tense.s1.e: Past tense is needed because it happened in 1891. James Naismith invented basketball, with peach baskets for goals, in Springfield, Massachusetts.

hs-verb-tense.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Next summer our class ____ the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio, where Super Bowl history is on display.
hs-verb-tense.s2.h: The word "next" points toward the future.
hs-verb-tense.s2.e: Future tense is needed because the visit is "next summer." The Pro Football Hall of Fame stands in Canton, Ohio.

hs-verb-tense.s3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Before Roger Bannister ran his famous mile in 1954, no one ____ the distance in under four minutes.
hs-verb-tense.s3.h: The action was finished before 1954 arrived.
hs-verb-tense.s3.e: Past perfect shows something that had or had not happened before a past time ("before ... 1954"). Bannister ran the first sub-four-minute mile at Oxford on May 6, 1954.

hs-sv-agree.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The Green Bay Packers, who won the first Super Bowl in 1967, ____ one of the oldest teams in the NFL.
hs-sv-agree.s1.h: Is the subject one player or a whole team name ending in -s?
hs-sv-agree.s1.e: The plural subject "Packers" takes "are." Green Bay won Super Bowl I over the Kansas City Chiefs, 35 to 10.

hs-sv-agree.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Each of Jesse Owens's four gold medals from the 1936 Berlin Games ____ won in a different event.
hs-sv-agree.s2.e: "Each" is singular, so it takes "was," even though "medals" comes right before the blank. Owens won the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump and the 4x100-meter relay.

hs-sv-agree.s3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Basketball, which James Naismith invented in 1891, ____ now played around the world.
hs-sv-agree.s3.h: Ignore the phrase between commas; what is the subject?
hs-sv-agree.s3.e: The subject "Basketball" is singular, so it takes "is." James Naismith invented the game in Springfield, Massachusetts, with two peach baskets.

hs-homophones.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The Green Bay Packers won ____ first Super Bowl in January 1967.
hs-homophones.s1.h: Whose first Super Bowl? It belongs to the team.
hs-homophones.s1.e: "Their" shows ownership. The Packers beat the Kansas City Chiefs 35 to 10 in the first Super Bowl, played on January 15, 1967.

hs-homophones.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The Dodgers moved to Los Angeles in 1958, and ____ still based there today.
hs-homophones.s2.h: Can you replace the blank with "they are"?
hs-homophones.s2.e: "They're" means "they are." The Dodgers played in Brooklyn until the 1957 season and moved west for 1958.

hs-homophones.s3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Brazil needed only a draw in 1950, but Uruguay scored late and it was ____ late to change the result.
hs-homophones.s3.e: "Too" means "excessively." Uruguay beat Brazil 2 to 1 at the Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro in 1950, in a game still remembered as the "Maracanazo."

hs-commas.s1.t: The 1896 Athens Games included track and field, swimming, cycling, and tennis.
hs-commas.s1.h: Items in a list are separated by commas, with none right after "included."
hs-commas.s1.e: Commas separate the items in a series, with no comma after the verb "included" or after "and." The first modern Olympics in Athens in 1896 featured track and field, swimming, cycling and tennis, among other sports.

hs-commas.s2.t: In 1954, Roger Bannister ran the first mile under four minutes.
hs-commas.s2.h: An introductory phrase is followed by a comma, and nothing else needs splitting.
hs-commas.s2.e: A comma follows an introductory phrase such as "In 1954." Roger Bannister ran his 3:59.4 mile at Oxford on May 6, 1954.

hs-commas.s3.t: Wilma Rudolph, who had worn a leg brace as a child, won three gold medals in 1960.
hs-commas.s3.h: A phrase that adds extra information and could be removed needs a comma on both sides.
hs-commas.s3.e: Commas set off a nonessential clause on both sides. Wilma Rudolph, who wore a leg brace as a child after illness, won three gold medals at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

hs-apostrophes.s1.p: Choose the correct form: ____ 1947 debut changed baseball.
hs-apostrophes.s1.e: A singular possessive adds apostrophe + s. Jackie Robinson's debut with the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947, broke baseball's color barrier in the modern major leagues.

hs-apostrophes.s2.p: Choose the correct form: ____ perfect score in 1976 was the first in Olympic gymnastics.
hs-apostrophes.s2.e: A singular possessive takes apostrophe + s. Fourteen-year-old Nadia Comaneci earned the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, at the 1976 Games in Montreal.

hs-apostrophes.s3.p: Choose the correct form: ____ victory in Super Bowl I came by a score of 35 to 10.
hs-apostrophes.s3.h: The team name is plural and ends in s.
hs-apostrophes.s3.e: A plural noun ending in -s shows possession with just an apostrophe after the s. The Green Bay Packers beat the Kansas City Chiefs in the first Super Bowl in 1967.

hs-pronouns.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Branch Rickey, ____ was the Dodgers' president, signed Jackie Robinson in 1945.
hs-pronouns.s1.h: Is the missing word doing the being, or receiving something?
hs-pronouns.s1.e: "Who" is the subject of "was." Branch Rickey signed Robinson to a contract in 1945, and Robinson reached the major leagues with the Dodgers in 1947.

hs-pronouns.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The crowd in Athens cheered for the marathon winner, Spyridon Louis, and gave ____ a hero's welcome.
hs-pronouns.s2.h: The pronoun is the object of "gave."
hs-pronouns.s2.e: Use the object pronoun "him" after the verb "gave." Spyridon Louis, a Greek runner, won the first modern Olympic marathon in 1896.

hs-pronouns.s3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Pelé, ____ the world met at the 1958 World Cup, was only seventeen years old.
hs-pronouns.s3.e: "Whom" is the object of "met" (the world met him). Pelé helped Brazil win the 1958 World Cup in Sweden at age seventeen.

hs-modifiers.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Wilma Rudolph ran ____ in the 100 meters at the 1960 Rome Olympics.
hs-modifiers.s1.h: The word describes how she ran.
hs-modifiers.s1.e: An adverb describes a verb: she ran "swiftly." Rudolph won the 100 meters, the 200 meters and the relay in Rome in 1960.

hs-modifiers.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The marathon course in 1896 looked ____ to the runners, but Spyridon Louis finished first.
hs-modifiers.s2.e: "Looked" is a linking verb, so it takes an adjective: "difficult." Spyridon Louis, a Greek runner, won the marathon at the first modern Olympics in Athens.

hs-modifiers.s3.t: Running on the cinder track at Oxford, Roger Bannister broke the four-minute barrier on May 6, 1954.
hs-modifiers.s3.p: Which sentence has NO dangling modifier?
hs-modifiers.s3.h: Who was running? That person should come right after the comma.
hs-modifiers.s3.e: The opening phrase must describe the word right after the comma. Roger Bannister, not the barrier, was running when he ran the first mile under four minutes at Oxford in 1954.

hs-parallel.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Jesse Owens won gold in the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump, and ____.
hs-parallel.s1.h: Keep the list items in the same form: "the ___" events.
hs-parallel.s1.e: Parallel structure keeps all items in the same grammatical form, here "the" + an event. Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

hs-parallel.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: James Naismith was a teacher, a coach, and ____.
hs-parallel.s2.h: The other items are "a" + a person.
hs-parallel.s2.e: All items are nouns naming kinds of people: a teacher, a coach, a physician. James Naismith, who invented basketball in 1891, later also earned a medical degree.

hs-parallel.s3.p: Which choice completes the sentence in parallel form? Nadia Comaneci's routines were praised for their precision, for their grace, and ____.
hs-parallel.s3.h: Begin the last item the way the first two begin.
hs-parallel.s3.e: Each item should begin "for their" + a noun. Nadia Comaneci earned the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in Montreal in 1976.

hs-semicolons.s1.t: The Tour de France began in 1903; a newspaper started it to sell more copies.
hs-semicolons.s1.h: Two closely related complete sentences can be joined with a semicolon.
hs-semicolons.s1.e: A semicolon joins two independent clauses without a conjunction; a comma alone would be a splice. A French newspaper launched the first Tour de France in 1903 to boost its sales.

hs-semicolons.s2.t: The 1936 Berlin Olympics gave Jesse Owens four golds: the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump, and the relay.
hs-semicolons.s2.h: A colon follows a complete sentence and introduces a list.
hs-semicolons.s2.e: A colon after a complete clause introduces a list. Jesse Owens won gold in the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump and the 4x100-meter relay at Berlin in 1936.

hs-semicolons.s3.t: The Maracanã—built for the 1950 World Cup—was one of the largest stadiums in the world.
hs-semicolons.s3.h: Dashes that set off an interruption come in a pair, one on each side.
hs-semicolons.s3.e: A pair of dashes sets off a nonessential interruption. The Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro was built for the 1950 World Cup and was among the largest stadiums ever built.

hs-word-choice.s1.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: Jackie Robinson's 1947 debut had a lasting ____ on baseball and on American life.
hs-word-choice.s1.h: "Effect" is usually the noun; "affect" is usually the verb.
hs-word-choice.s1.e: The noun "effect" (a result) is needed after "a lasting." Robinson broke the major-league color barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947.

hs-word-choice.s2.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The ____ idea behind Dr. Ludwig Guttmann's 1948 Stoke Mandeville competition was that sport could help patients recover.
hs-word-choice.s2.h: One spelling means "main," the other means "a rule."
hs-word-choice.s2.e: "Principal" means main or most important; "principle" is a rule or belief. Guttmann's 1948 archery contest for wheelchair users grew into the Paralympic Games, first held in Rome in 1960.

hs-word-choice.s3.p: Choose the word that completes the sentence: When the scoreboard in Montreal showed 1.00 for Nadia Comaneci in 1976, viewers could ____ that it had not been built to show a perfect 10.
hs-word-choice.s3.h: The viewers are drawing a conclusion from evidence.
hs-word-choice.s3.e: A viewer or reader infers; a speaker or writer implies. The scoreboard could not display 10.00, so Comaneci's first perfect score in Olympic gymnastics appeared as 1.00.

art-masters.l01.q1.p: Which technique uses smoke-soft transitions with no visible outline?
art-masters.l01.q1.h: Think of the Mona Lisa's softly blended edges.
art-masters.l01.q1.e: Sfumato is the soft, smoky blending that Leonardo used to avoid hard lines.

art-masters.l01.q2.p: Which of these works is by Leonardo da Vinci?
art-masters.l01.q2.h: It is a mural of a famous dinner.
art-masters.l01.q2.e: Leonardo painted The Last Supper, along with the Mona Lisa and Lady with an Ermine.

art-masters.l01.q3.p: A landscape's distant mountains are paler and bluer than the foreground. Which Leonardo technique is this?
art-masters.l01.q3.h: It uses atmosphere to suggest depth.
art-masters.l01.q3.e: Aerial perspective uses haze and cooler tones to show distance.

art-masters.l01.q4.t: It gave him an understanding of muscle and gesture that made figures convincing
art-masters.l01.q4.p: How did dissecting bodies help Leonardo as a painter?
art-masters.l01.q4.h: Think about what is under the skin.
art-masters.l01.q4.e: Knowing anatomy made his figures' structure and movement more believable.

art-masters.l02.q1.p: Which painting is on the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
art-masters.l02.q1.e: The Creation of Adam is part of Michelangelo's Sistine ceiling.

art-masters.l02.q2.p: Which artist painted The School of Athens?
art-masters.l02.q2.e: Raphael painted The School of Athens in fresco.

art-masters.l02.q3.p: A fresco shows muscular twisting figures that radiate awe and force. Which quality is this?
art-masters.l02.q3.h: It's an Italian word suggesting awe.
art-masters.l02.q3.e: Terribilita describes the awe and force in Michelangelo's figures.

art-masters.l02.q4.t: Michelangelo stresses tension and heroic anatomy; Raphael stresses harmony and idealised beauty
art-masters.l02.q4.p: Which comparison of Michelangelo and Raphael is most accurate?
art-masters.l02.q4.h: Think about the mood each creates.
art-masters.l02.q4.e: Michelangelo conveys force while Raphael conveys calm balance, though both were High Renaissance masters.

art-masters.l03.q1.e: Tenebrism is dramatic contrast of strong light with deep darkness, Caravaggio's signature.

art-masters.l03.q2.h: A tax collector is called by Christ.
art-masters.l03.q2.e: The Calling of St Matthew is a Caravaggio, as are Judith Beheading Holofernes and Bacchus.

art-masters.l03.q3.p: A painting shows a dark room, a beam of light and a figure with dirty feet in a sacred scene. Whose style is this?
art-masters.l03.q3.e: Strong spotlighting plus a gritty realistic treatment of sacred subjects marks Caravaggio.

art-masters.l03.q4.t: It is much more extreme, with huge, near-black shadows
art-masters.l03.q4.p: How does tenebrism differ from general chiaroscuro?
art-masters.l03.q4.h: Consider how much of the picture is dark.
art-masters.l03.q4.e: Chiaroscuro is any light-dark modelling; tenebrism pushes the contrast to a theatrical extreme.

art-masters.l04.q1.p: Who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring?
art-masters.l04.q1.h: He painted quiet rooms with window light.
art-masters.l04.q1.e: Johannes Vermeer painted Girl with a Pearl Earring and The Milkmaid.

art-masters.l04.q2.p: Which technique means thick, sculptural paint?
art-masters.l04.q2.e: Impasto is thickly applied paint that stands out from the canvas.

art-masters.l04.q3.p: A portrait emerges from a dark background with warm light and thick, loose paint, showing deep psychological insight. Which artist?
art-masters.l04.q3.e: Rembrandt used chiaroscuro and impasto for psychological portraiture.

art-masters.l04.q4.p: Vermeer is known for dramatic chiaroscuro and thick impasto, while Rembrandt is known for cool, even light and pointille highlights.
art-masters.l04.q4.h: Check which artist matches which technique.
art-masters.l04.q4.e: It is the reverse: Rembrandt used chiaroscuro and impasto; Vermeer is known for luminous natural light and pointille highlights.

art-masters.l05.q1.p: Which painting by Goya shows an execution during the Napoleonic occupation?
art-masters.l05.q1.h: The date is in the title.
art-masters.l05.q1.e: The Third of May 1808 shows the executions; Saturn Devouring His Son belongs to the Black Paintings.

art-masters.l05.q2.p: Which printmaking technique did Goya use for soft tonal areas?
art-masters.l05.q2.e: Goya used aquatint etching, which produces soft tones.

art-masters.l05.q3.p: A painting with loose, expressive brushwork shows a nightmarish scene of a figure devouring his child. Which work?
art-masters.l05.q3.e: Saturn Devouring His Son is one of Goya's Black Paintings.

art-masters.l05.q4.t: He turned subjects of history and fear into personal, psychological expression
art-masters.l05.q4.p: Why is Goya often seen as a bridge to modern art?
art-masters.l05.q4.e: His expressive handling and psychological darkness anticipated later modern art.

art-masters.l06.q1.e: Hokusai made The Great Wave off Kanagawa as part of Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

art-masters.l06.q2.p: What printing tradition did Hokusai work in?
art-masters.l06.q2.h: It means pictures of the floating world.
art-masters.l06.q2.e: Hokusai worked in ukiyo-e woodblock printing in Edo-period Japan.

art-masters.l06.q3.p: A print shows a giant curling wave in deep blue with a small distant mountain. Which pigment gave the characteristic blue?
art-masters.l06.q3.h: It is a modern synthetic blue.
art-masters.l06.q3.e: Prussian-blue landscapes are a mark of Hokusai's prints.

art-masters.l06.q4.t: The fragility of people against the power of nature
art-masters.l06.q4.p: What contrast does The Great Wave emphasise?
art-masters.l06.q4.h: Compare the wave, the boats and Mount Fuji.
art-masters.l06.q4.e: The towering wave over small boats, with calm Fuji beyond, contrasts human fragility with natural force.

art-masters.l07.q1.p: Which Monet painting gave Impressionism its name?
art-masters.l07.q1.e: Impression, Sunrise gave the movement its name.

art-masters.l07.q2.t: Painting outdoors in front of the subject
art-masters.l07.q2.h: Think of where the artist stands.
art-masters.l07.q2.e: Plein-air painting is done outdoors to capture changing light.

art-masters.l07.q3.p: An artist paints the same cathedral at dawn, noon and dusk to show how light changes. What is this approach?
art-masters.l07.q3.h: Monet did this with haystacks too.
art-masters.l07.q3.e: Monet's series, such as Haystacks and Rouen Cathedral, study changing light on one subject.

art-masters.l07.q4.t: He placed separate touches of broken colour so the eye blends them
art-masters.l07.q4.p: Why do Monet's paintings seem to dissolve up close and cohere from a distance?
art-masters.l07.q4.h: Think of colours placed side by side.
art-masters.l07.q4.e: Broken colour uses distinct strokes that blend optically when viewed from afar.

art-masters.l08.q1.p: Which artist painted The Starry Night?
art-masters.l08.q1.e: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night, Sunflowers and The Bedroom.

art-masters.l08.q2.p: Cezanne reduced nature to which basic shapes?
art-masters.l08.q2.e: Cezanne described nature in terms of the cylinder, sphere and cone.

art-masters.l08.q3.p: A painting of an apple still life shows the table tilted from slightly different viewpoints and built from patches of colour. Who is it?
art-masters.l08.q3.h: Think of The Basket of Apples.
art-masters.l08.q3.e: Constructive strokes and shifting perspective are Cezanne's hallmarks.

art-masters.l08.q4.t: Van Gogh used colour and line for emotion; Cezanne analysed form and structure
art-masters.l08.q4.p: How do Van Gogh and Cezanne differ in aim?
art-masters.l08.q4.e: Van Gogh emphasised expressive feeling, whereas Cezanne built solid structure, pointing toward Expressionism and Cubism.

art-masters.l09.q1.h: Objects are shown from several angles.

art-masters.l09.q2.p: Which technique is Matisse known for in his late years?
art-masters.l09.q2.h: He cut shapes from painted paper.
art-masters.l09.q2.e: Matisse made paper cut-outs, such as those in Jazz.

art-masters.l09.q3.p: A portrait with a green stripe down the face and flat, wild colour. Which movement?
art-masters.l09.q3.e: Fauvism uses wild, non-natural colour; Matisse was its leader.

art-masters.l09.q4.t: Picasso fragments form and viewpoint, while Matisse simplifies shape and lets colour carry feeling
art-masters.l09.q4.h: Think of Guernica and The Dance.
art-masters.l09.q4.e: Picasso broke form apart; Matisse emphasised colour and flat, decorative space.

art-masters.l10.q1.e: The Persistence of Memory is by Dali.

art-masters.l10.q2.p: Frida Kahlo drew on which Mexican folk tradition?
art-masters.l10.q2.e: Kahlo drew on retablo traditions along with symbolic self-portraiture.

art-masters.l10.q3.p: An image that can be read as two different things at once is called what, in Dali's practice?
art-masters.l10.q3.e: Double images were one of his dream-imagery techniques.

art-masters.l10.q4.p: Kahlo's paintings mostly invent dream worlds unrelated to her own life.
art-masters.l10.q4.e: Kahlo painted her own reality, using symbols from her life, pain and identity.

art-masters.l11.q1.p: Which artist is known for drip or action painting?
art-masters.l11.q1.h: He worked on canvases laid on the floor.
art-masters.l11.q1.e: Jackson Pollock used drip and action painting, as in Autumn Rhythm.

art-masters.l11.q2.p: Which artist is known for luminous floating rectangles of colour?
art-masters.l11.q2.e: Mark Rothko painted layered washes of floating rectangles.

art-masters.l11.q3.p: A huge close-up of a flower that becomes almost abstract, in the light of New Mexico. Which artist?
art-masters.l11.q3.e: O'Keeffe magnified natural forms into precise, sensuous abstraction.

art-masters.l11.q4.t: Pollock's is physical and gestural; Rothko's is quiet and meditative
art-masters.l11.q4.p: Which pair correctly contrasts the energy of two artists?
art-masters.l11.q4.e: Pollock emphasised gesture, whereas Rothko's colour fields invite stillness.

art-masters.l12.q1.p: Which sculptor is called the father of modern sculpture?
art-masters.l12.q1.e: Auguste Rodin is known as the father of modern sculpture.

art-masters.l12.q2.p: Which work is by Louise Bourgeois?
art-masters.l12.q2.e: Bourgeois made Maman, the giant spider.

art-masters.l12.q3.p: A large bronze reclining figure with holes through the body. Which sculptor?
art-masters.l12.q3.e: Henry Moore is known for pierced forms in his Reclining Figure series.

art-masters.l12.q4.t: Distilling a subject to its pure, essential form
art-masters.l12.q4.p: Which description best captures Brancusi's goal?
art-masters.l12.q4.e: Brancusi pursued radical abstraction and polished essence rather than detail.

art-masters.l13.q1.e: Dorothea Lange made Migrant Mother as part of her documentary work.

art-masters.l13.q2.p: Which phrase is associated with Henri Cartier-Bresson?
art-masters.l13.q2.e: Cartier-Bresson sought the decisive moment, where form and meaning align.

art-masters.l13.q3.p: A photographer worked as a nanny and shot thousands of street photos with a Rolleiflex, discovered after her death. Who?
art-masters.l13.q3.e: Vivian Maier's lifelong archive was discovered only after her death.

art-masters.l13.q4.t: Adams: making wilderness monumental; Parks: documenting race and poverty
art-masters.l13.q4.p: Which pairing best matches photographer and aim?
art-masters.l13.q4.e: Adams photographed landscapes in large format, while Parks used the photo-essay on social issues.

art-masters.l14.q1.p: Which architect said less is more?
art-masters.l14.q1.e: Mies van der Rohe is associated with less is more.

art-masters.l14.q2.p: Who was the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize?
art-masters.l14.q2.h: She designed the Heydar Aliyev Center.
art-masters.l14.q2.e: Zaha Hadid was the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize.

art-masters.l14.q3.p: A house cantilevered over a waterfall with open flowing interiors. Which architect?

art-masters.l14.q4.t: Both were methods to determine form through a system, one structural, one proportional
art-masters.l14.q4.p: What do Gaudi's catenary models and Le Corbusier's Modulor have in common?
art-masters.l14.q4.h: Each is a system behind the design.
art-masters.l14.q4.e: Gaudi used hanging-chain models to find structural form, and Le Corbusier used the Modulor as a proportional system.

art-movements-classical.l01.q1.p: Scholars agree on exactly why Paleolithic cave paintings were made.
art-movements-classical.l01.q1.h: Think about what is missing from the evidence.
art-movements-classical.l01.q1.e: There are no written records from the makers, so several competing interpretations exist.

art-movements-classical.l01.q2.p: Which of these was a natural pigment commonly used in cave painting?
art-movements-classical.l01.q2.h: Think of materials found in the ground or in fires.
art-movements-classical.l01.q2.e: Ochre (iron-rich earth) and charcoal were among the natural pigments used.

art-movements-classical.l01.q3.p: The Chauvet cave, known for its drawings of lions, rhinoceroses and horses, is in which country?
art-movements-classical.l01.q3.h: It lies in the same country as Lascaux.

art-movements-classical.l01.q4.p: A hand stencil is made by blowing pigment around a hand pressed against a surface.
art-movements-classical.l01.q4.h: The hand acts like a mask.
art-movements-classical.l01.q4.e: Blowing pigment around the hand leaves a negative outline of it on the rock.

art-movements-classical.l01.q5.t: Because the visible evidence is certain while purposes are interpretations
art-movements-classical.l01.q5.p: Why should a student describe what is visible in a cave painting before guessing its purpose?
art-movements-classical.l01.q5.h: One is observation, the other is theory.
art-movements-classical.l01.q5.e: Separating observation from interpretation keeps claims honest when the makers left no records.

art-movements-classical.l02.q1.p: Most surviving ancient Egyptian art comes from tombs and temples.
art-movements-classical.l02.q1.h: Think about where objects were protected.
art-movements-classical.l02.q1.e: Funerary and religious settings produced and preserved most surviving works.

art-movements-classical.l02.q2.p: In a typical Egyptian figure, which parts are shown from the front?
art-movements-classical.l02.q2.e: The conventional view combines a profile head and legs with a frontal eye and shoulders.

art-movements-classical.l02.q3.p: Why might a pharaoh be drawn much larger than the people around him?
art-movements-classical.l02.q3.e: Hierarchical scale used size to show status, not distance.

art-movements-classical.l02.q4.p: The Amarna period under Akhenaten is known for a more naturalistic style than earlier Egyptian art.
art-movements-classical.l02.q4.h: It was a break from tradition.
art-movements-classical.l02.q4.e: Amarna art showed softer, more naturalistic forms before tradition largely returned.

art-movements-classical.l02.q5.t: It served religious and royal purposes more than personal self-expression
art-movements-classical.l02.q5.p: What does the lasting consistency of Egyptian conventions suggest about its art?
art-movements-classical.l02.q5.e: Art made for tombs, temples and kingship stayed close to approved patterns.

art-movements-classical.l03.q1.p: Cuneiform writing was pressed into clay.
art-movements-classical.l03.q1.h: Think about the plentiful local material.
art-movements-classical.l03.q1.e: Cuneiform signs were made by pressing a stylus into wet clay tablets.

art-movements-classical.l03.q2.t: A carved stone roller that leaves an image when rolled over clay
art-movements-classical.l03.q2.e: Rolling it over wet clay produced a repeating picture, often used to mark documents.

art-movements-classical.l03.q3.p: Which Mesopotamian object shows a king standing before a seated god above a law text?
art-movements-classical.l03.q3.h: It is named for a Babylonian king.
art-movements-classical.l03.q3.e: The Hammurabi stele pairs a relief image with an inscribed law code.

art-movements-classical.l03.q4.p: Assyrian palace reliefs often showed royal hunts and military campaigns.
art-movements-classical.l03.q4.h: The palaces were statements of power.
art-movements-classical.l03.q4.e: Reliefs of lion hunts and wars glorified the king.

art-movements-classical.l03.q5.t: Who ordered it, and what did the king want viewers to believe?
art-movements-classical.l03.q5.p: Which question best helps you understand a royal Assyrian relief?
art-movements-classical.l03.q5.e: Royal reliefs were propaganda as well as decoration, so patron and message matter.

art-movements-classical.l04.q1.p: Many Greek marble statues were originally painted.
art-movements-classical.l04.q1.h: The white look of museum marble can mislead.
art-movements-classical.l04.q1.e: Evidence shows that many Greek sculptures and buildings carried colour.

art-movements-classical.l04.q2.t: A pose with weight shifted onto one leg
art-movements-classical.l04.q2.h: Think about how a relaxed person stands.
art-movements-classical.l04.q2.e: Contrapposto gives a lifelike stance by tilting hips and shoulders.

art-movements-classical.l04.q3.p: Which column order has scrolled capitals?
art-movements-classical.l04.q3.e: Ionic capitals have volutes, scroll shapes.

art-movements-classical.l04.q4.p: The Parthenon was built in the Hellenistic period after Alexander the Great.
art-movements-classical.l04.q4.e: The Parthenon dates to the Classical period, in the fifth century BCE.

art-movements-classical.l04.q5.t: Many pieces are Roman copies of lost bronzes, and the colour has worn away
art-movements-classical.l04.q5.p: Why can museum Greek sculpture be misleading about the original?
art-movements-classical.l04.q5.h: Two things changed: who made the surviving piece and its surface.
art-movements-classical.l04.q5.e: Surviving marbles are often copies of lost bronzes and have lost their painted surfaces.

art-movements-classical.l05.q1.p: Pompeii preserved many Roman paintings and mosaics because of a volcanic eruption.
art-movements-classical.l05.q1.e: The eruption of 79 CE buried the city and protected its wall paintings and mosaics.

art-movements-classical.l05.q2.t: Small cut pieces used to make mosaics
art-movements-classical.l05.q2.h: Mosaics are made of many small parts.
art-movements-classical.l05.q2.e: Tesserae are the tiny stones or glass pieces that form a mosaic.

art-movements-classical.l05.q3.p: Which Roman innovation allowed the Pantheon's large dome?
art-movements-classical.l05.q3.e: Roman concrete let builders cast vaults and domes.

art-movements-classical.l05.q4.p: Trajan's Column tells the story of a military campaign in a spiral relief.
art-movements-classical.l05.q4.e: The spiral relief records Trajan's campaigns in Dacia.

art-movements-classical.l05.q5.t: It may have valued experience and seriousness over youthful beauty
art-movements-classical.l05.q5.p: Why would a Republic portrait show an older man with wrinkles?
art-movements-classical.l05.q5.h: Consider what qualities the portrait wanted to show.
art-movements-classical.l05.q5.e: Scholars often read veristic portraits as expressing gravity and civic experience.

art-movements-classical.l06.q1.p: Byzantine mosaics often use gold backgrounds to suggest a heavenly space.
art-movements-classical.l06.q1.h: The gold is not a landscape.
art-movements-classical.l06.q1.e: Gold grounds signal a sacred, timeless setting rather than natural space.

art-movements-classical.l06.q2.p: Which church in Constantinople was completed in 537 under Justinian?

art-movements-classical.l06.q3.t: Curved supports that let a dome sit on a square space
art-movements-classical.l06.q3.h: They solve an engineering problem under a dome.
art-movements-classical.l06.q3.e: Pendentives transfer the dome's weight to the corners of a square base.

art-movements-classical.l06.q4.p: Iconoclasm was a dispute over whether religious images should be used.
art-movements-classical.l06.q4.e: Iconoclast controversies of the eighth and ninth centuries centred on religious images.

art-movements-classical.l06.q5.t: The art aimed to express a spiritual reality rather than ordinary appearances
art-movements-classical.l06.q5.p: Why are Byzantine figures often flat and frontal rather than shown in deep space?
art-movements-classical.l06.q5.h: Consider what the images were for.
art-movements-classical.l06.q5.e: The style supports devotion and the sense of a holy presence.

art-movements-classical.l07.q1.p: Calligraphy is highly honoured in Islamic art because it presents the words of the Qur'an.
art-movements-classical.l07.q1.h: Think about the role of text.
art-movements-classical.l07.q1.e: Writing sacred text beautifully is a central art.

art-movements-classical.l07.q2.p: Which word names interlacing plant-based decoration?
art-movements-classical.l07.q2.e: Arabesque is rhythmic, interlacing vegetal ornament.

art-movements-classical.l07.q3.h: It is a style of writing.
art-movements-classical.l07.q3.e: Naskh is a flowing script still widely used.

art-movements-classical.l07.q4.p: Figural images never appear anywhere in Islamic art.
art-movements-classical.l07.q4.e: Figural images appear in secular and courtly works such as Persian and Mughal manuscripts.

art-movements-classical.l07.q5.t: It covers many regions, centuries and styles
art-movements-classical.l07.q5.p: Why is "Islamic art" a limited label?
art-movements-classical.l07.q5.h: Count the places and centuries named in the lesson.
art-movements-classical.l07.q5.e: The label covers a very wide range of cultures and periods.

art-movements-classical.l08.q1.p: Romanesque churches typically have thick walls and round arches.
art-movements-classical.l08.q1.e: Round arches and heavy walls characterise the style.

art-movements-classical.l08.q2.t: The thick walls had to support heavy stone vaults
art-movements-classical.l08.q2.p: Why do Romanesque churches often have small windows?
art-movements-classical.l08.q2.e: Large openings would weaken walls carrying a heavy vault.

art-movements-classical.l08.q3.p: The Bayeux Tapestry is actually which kind of work?
art-movements-classical.l08.q3.e: It is embroidered with wool thread on linen.

art-movements-classical.l08.q4.p: The tympanum is the carved area above a church doorway.
art-movements-classical.l08.q4.e: The tympanum often held the Last Judgment or another teaching scene.

art-movements-classical.l08.q5.t: To teach and warn a congregation that mostly could not read
art-movements-classical.l08.q5.p: Why might Romanesque doorway sculptures show the Last Judgment?
art-movements-classical.l08.q5.e: Images served as instruction for many who could not read.

art-movements-classical.l09.q1.p: Flying buttresses let Gothic walls be filled with large windows.
art-movements-classical.l09.q1.e: Buttresses take the vault's sideways thrust so walls need not be solid.

art-movements-classical.l09.q2.e: The style is traditionally traced to the abbey church of Saint-Denis in France.

art-movements-classical.l09.q3.t: Later critics used it as an insult, after the Goths
art-movements-classical.l09.q3.p: Where did the word "Gothic" for this style come from?
art-movements-classical.l09.q3.e: Renaissance writers applied it to medieval work they thought barbaric.

art-movements-classical.l09.q4.p: The pointed arch is a feature of Romanesque rather than Gothic buildings.
art-movements-classical.l09.q4.e: Pointed arches are a hallmark of Gothic building.

art-movements-classical.l09.q5.t: It taught stories and symbolised divine light
art-movements-classical.l09.q5.p: Why is stained glass considered more than decoration in a Gothic cathedral?
art-movements-classical.l09.q5.e: Windows carried narrative and spiritual meaning.

art-movements-classical.l10.q1.p: The Chinese word shanshui means "mountain-water" and refers to landscape.
art-movements-classical.l10.q1.e: Shanshui is the traditional term for landscape painting.

art-movements-classical.l10.q2.p: How is a handscroll usually viewed?
art-movements-classical.l10.q2.e: The viewer reveals the scene bit by bit, like a journey.

art-movements-classical.l10.q3.t: Huge mountains with tiny human travellers
art-movements-classical.l10.q3.p: What does Fan Kuan's "Travelers among Mountains and Streams" emphasise?
art-movements-classical.l10.q3.h: Think about the scale of people.
art-movements-classical.l10.q3.e: The vast cliff and small travellers place people within nature.

art-movements-classical.l10.q4.p: Southern Song painters such as Ma Yuan often used large areas of empty space.
art-movements-classical.l10.q4.h: Mist can be an active part of the composition.
art-movements-classical.l10.q4.e: Empty silk suggested mist and distance.

art-movements-classical.l10.q5.t: It was built from observation and memory to show the structure and spirit of nature
art-movements-classical.l10.q5.p: Why is a Song landscape not best described as a copy of one view?
art-movements-classical.l10.q5.e: Artists synthesised experience rather than recording a single viewpoint.

art-movements-classical.l11.q1.p: A single ukiyo-e print was typically the work of one person only.
art-movements-classical.l11.q1.h: Think of the publisher, artist, carver and printer.
art-movements-classical.l11.q1.e: Prints were produced by a team including publisher, artist, carver and printer.

art-movements-classical.l11.q2.e: The phrase refers to the transient pleasures of city life.

art-movements-classical.l11.q3.p: Which artist made "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji"?
art-movements-classical.l11.q3.e: Hokusai made the series in the early 1830s.

art-movements-classical.l11.q4.p: One woodblock was usually used for each colour in a multicolour print.
art-movements-classical.l11.q4.e: Separate blocks were carved and printed for each colour.

art-movements-classical.l11.q5.t: Many impressions could be printed from the same blocks
art-movements-classical.l11.q5.p: Why were prints more widely affordable than paintings?
art-movements-classical.l11.q5.e: The block process allowed many copies, lowering the cost of each.

art-movements-classical.l12.q1.p: The phrase "African art" describes one single style.
art-movements-classical.l12.q1.h: Count the cultures named in the lesson.
art-movements-classical.l12.q1.e: Africa has many cultures and periods, each with its own traditions.

art-movements-classical.l12.q2.p: Which kingdom made cast brass plaques recording court history?
art-movements-classical.l12.q2.e: Benin court artists cast brass plaques and heads.

art-movements-classical.l12.q3.t: Many were made for performance or ritual, so context affects meaning
art-movements-classical.l12.q3.p: Why is it useful to know a mask's original use?
art-movements-classical.l12.q3.e: Understanding the setting prevents mistaking a used object for pure display.

art-movements-classical.l12.q4.p: Debates about returning looted works from the 1897 Benin expedition are called restitution debates.
art-movements-classical.l12.q4.e: Restitution refers to returning cultural property to its places of origin.

art-movements-classical.l12.q5.t: Naming the specific culture, period and purpose of a work
art-movements-classical.l12.q5.h: Specificity is the antidote to stereotype.
art-movements-classical.l12.q5.e: Precise attribution respects the diversity of traditions.

art-movements-classical.l13.q1.p: Inca builders joined stone blocks tightly without mortar at sites such as Machu Picchu.
art-movements-classical.l13.q1.e: Fine stone-cutting held walls together without mortar.

art-movements-classical.l13.q2.t: A system of knotted cords used to record information
art-movements-classical.l13.q2.e: The Inca used khipu for record-keeping.

art-movements-classical.l13.q3.t: Haida, Tlingit and Kwakwaka'wakw, among others
art-movements-classical.l13.q3.p: Which peoples carve cedar poles that record family histories on the Northwest Coast?
art-movements-classical.l13.q3.h: Look at the geography in the lesson.
art-movements-classical.l13.q3.e: Northwest Coast peoples carve such poles.

art-movements-classical.l13.q4.p: Indigenous art traditions in the Americas ended after European arrival.
art-movements-classical.l13.q4.h: Think of Maria Martinez or ledger art.
art-movements-classical.l13.q4.e: Many traditions continued and have been renewed, and Indigenous artists work today.

art-movements-classical.l13.q5.t: Because meanings and uses differ among communities
art-movements-classical.l13.q5.p: Why should museum labels name a community, not just "Native American"?
art-movements-classical.l13.q5.e: Specific attribution reflects real cultural distinctions.

art-movements-classical.l14.q1.h: The word is French for something revived.
art-movements-classical.l14.q1.e: The name refers to the revival of classical antiquity.

art-movements-classical.l14.q2.t: Creates the illusion of depth using lines that meet at a vanishing point
art-movements-classical.l14.q2.e: It uses a mathematical system of converging lines for depth.

art-movements-classical.l14.q3.p: Which Florentine architect is credited with the cathedral dome completed in 1436?
art-movements-classical.l14.q3.h: He is also credited with perspective.
art-movements-classical.l14.q3.e: Brunelleschi designed the dome of Florence Cathedral.

art-movements-classical.l14.q4.p: Historians treat the Renaissance as a sudden complete break from medieval culture.
art-movements-classical.l14.q4.h: The lesson ends with a caution.
art-movements-classical.l14.q4.e: Medieval art and learning continued, and the "break" idea is questioned.

art-movements-classical.l14.q5.t: Using perspective to make a painted chapel seem to open into the wall
art-movements-classical.l14.q5.p: What was Masaccio's Holy Trinity famous for?
art-movements-classical.l14.q5.e: It is an early striking use of linear perspective.

art-movements-classical.l15.q1.p: In fresco, pigment is applied to wet plaster.
art-movements-classical.l15.q1.h: The colour sinks into the wall.
art-movements-classical.l15.q1.e: True fresco uses wet plaster, so artists worked in sections.

art-movements-classical.l15.q2.p: Which artist painted The School of Athens in the Vatican?

art-movements-classical.l15.q3.t: A soft blending of tones without hard outlines
art-movements-classical.l15.q3.e: The word comes from the Italian for smoke.

art-movements-classical.l15.q4.p: High Renaissance compositions often favour balanced, stable arrangements.
art-movements-classical.l15.q4.e: Harmony and balance are central goals.

art-movements-classical.l15.q5.p: Who commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine ceiling?
art-movements-classical.l15.q5.e: Julius II commissioned the ceiling, painted 1508-12.

art-movements-classical.l16.q1.p: Venetian painters often used oil paint on canvas.
art-movements-classical.l16.q1.h: Humid Venice was hard for fresco.
art-movements-classical.l16.q1.e: Canvas and oil suited the damp climate.

art-movements-classical.l16.q2.p: Which word describes the Venetian emphasis on colour?
art-movements-classical.l16.q2.e: Colorito contrasts with the Florentine emphasis on disegno.

art-movements-classical.l16.q3.p: What are glazes in oil painting?
art-movements-classical.l16.q3.h: They let light pass through to lower layers.
art-movements-classical.l16.q3.e: Glazes build depth and luminous colour.

art-movements-classical.l16.q4.p: Titian painted the Assumption of the Virgin for a church in Venice.
art-movements-classical.l16.q4.e: It was painted 1516-18 for the Frari.

art-movements-classical.l16.q5.t: It was light, flexible, and suited to damp conditions
art-movements-classical.l16.q5.p: Why was canvas practical for painters of Venice?
art-movements-classical.l16.q5.h: Think about transport and damp air.
art-movements-classical.l16.q5.e: Canvas could be rolled and shipped and resisted damp better than fresco walls.

art-movements-classical.l17.q1.p: Northern Renaissance painters were famous for detailed observation of textures.
art-movements-classical.l17.q1.e: Oil glazes allowed lifelike surface detail.

art-movements-classical.l17.q2.p: Who painted the Ghent Altarpiece, completed in 1432?

art-movements-classical.l17.q3.p: Which invention helped spread prints across Europe?
art-movements-classical.l17.q3.e: Printing from movable type made images and text cheaper.

art-movements-classical.l17.q5.t: Fewer religious altarpieces were commissioned, so portraits and everyday scenes grew
art-movements-classical.l17.q5.p: How could the Reformation affect artists in Protestant regions?
art-movements-classical.l17.q5.h: Think about what patrons still wanted.
art-movements-classical.l17.q5.e: Demand shifted away from church images in many places.

art-movements-classical.l18.q1.p: The Italian word maniera means "style" or "manner".
art-movements-classical.l18.q1.e: Mannerism takes its name from maniera.

art-movements-classical.l18.q2.p: Which feature is typical of Mannerism?
art-movements-classical.l18.q2.e: Exaggerated, elegant, twisting forms are common.

art-movements-classical.l18.q3.p: Which artist painted the Madonna with the Long Neck?
art-movements-classical.l18.q3.h: The name describes the long neck.

art-movements-classical.l18.q4.p: Scholars unanimously agree that Mannerism was only a reaction against the High Renaissance.
art-movements-classical.l18.q4.h: Debate is mentioned in the lesson.
art-movements-classical.l18.q4.e: Some see a reaction, others a continuation.

art-movements-classical.l18.q5.t: They saw it as mere imitation or affectation of the masters
art-movements-classical.l18.q5.p: Why did earlier critics sometimes dismiss Mannerism?
art-movements-classical.l18.q5.e: The label long carried a negative judgment, now reassessed.

art-movements-classical.l19.q1.p: Baroque art often uses strong contrasts of light and dark.
art-movements-classical.l19.q1.e: Dramatic light is central to the style.

art-movements-classical.l19.q2.p: Which artist painted the Calling of Saint Matthew?

art-movements-classical.l19.q3.t: The Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation
art-movements-classical.l19.q3.e: Church leaders used persuasive art as part of their response.

art-movements-classical.l19.q4.p: Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa is a painted fresco.
art-movements-classical.l19.q4.e: It is a marble sculpture group set within an architectural setting.

art-movements-classical.l19.q5.t: It aimed to involve the viewer emotionally
art-movements-classical.l19.q5.p: Why does Baroque art often show a peak moment of action or feeling?
art-movements-classical.l19.q5.e: Drama and emotional engagement served both church and court.

art-movements-classical.l20.q1.p: Dutch painters of this period sold to a broad market of townspeople.
art-movements-classical.l20.q1.e: A market of burghers, guilds and dealers supported them.

art-movements-classical.l20.q2.e: The Night Watch is Rembrandt's 1642 group portrait.

art-movements-classical.l20.q3.t: A picture reminding viewers that life and wealth are brief
art-movements-classical.l20.q3.p: What is a vanitas still life?
art-movements-classical.l20.q3.e: Vanitas pictures use symbols of transience.

art-movements-classical.l20.q4.p: The wealth behind Dutch art was unconnected to colonial trade.
art-movements-classical.l20.q4.e: Trade empires, including colonial exploitation and slavery, helped fund the economy.

art-movements-classical.l20.q5.t: A market of buyers wanted a variety of subjects for their homes
art-movements-classical.l20.q5.p: Why did Dutch artists specialise in genres such as landscape or still life?
art-movements-classical.l20.q5.e: Market demand favoured specialised, saleable subjects.

art-movements-classical.l21.q1.p: Rococo is generally lighter and more playful than Baroque.
art-movements-classical.l21.q1.e: Rococo favoured intimacy and grace over grandeur.

art-movements-classical.l21.q2.t: An elegant outdoor gathering scene, popularised by Watteau
art-movements-classical.l21.q2.e: Watteau created the type of dreamy leisure scene.

art-movements-classical.l21.q4.p: Diderot admired Rococo as the ideal of seriousness.
art-movements-classical.l21.q4.e: Critics such as Diderot found it frivolous.

art-movements-classical.l21.q5.t: Its delicate scale and ornament suit intimate rooms
art-movements-classical.l21.q5.p: Why does the Rococo style fit private salons better than huge cathedrals?
art-movements-classical.l21.q5.e: Small, graceful decoration matched intimate interiors.

art-movements-classical.l22.q1.p: Neoclassicism took inspiration from ancient Greece and Rome.
art-movements-classical.l22.q1.e: It revived classical forms and subjects.

art-movements-classical.l22.q2.p: Which painter made The Oath of the Horatii?

art-movements-classical.l22.q3.p: Which discoveries encouraged interest in antiquity in the eighteenth century?
art-movements-classical.l22.q3.e: Digs at the buried Roman towns began in 1738 and 1748.

art-movements-classical.l22.q4.p: Neoclassicism was used only by revolutionaries and never by an emperor.
art-movements-classical.l22.q4.e: Napoleon's empire also used classical imagery.

art-movements-classical.l22.q5.t: It shows duty to the state placed above personal feeling
art-movements-classical.l22.q5.p: Why is the Oath of the Horatii often described as a moral statement?
art-movements-classical.l22.q5.e: The scene praises civic duty and sacrifice.

art-movements-classical.l23.q1.p: Romanticism valued emotion, imagination and nature.
art-movements-classical.l23.q1.h: A reply to reason and industry.

art-movements-classical.l23.q2.t: Awe mixed with fear before vast or powerful nature
art-movements-classical.l23.q2.p: What does "the sublime" mean in Romantic thought?
art-movements-classical.l23.q2.h: Think of enormous mountains and storms.
art-movements-classical.l23.q2.e: The sublime is the thrilling terror of overwhelming nature.

art-movements-classical.l23.q3.p: Which painting was based on a real 1816 shipwreck?
art-movements-classical.l23.q3.e: Gericault depicted survivors of the Medusa wreck.

art-movements-classical.l23.q4.p: Romanticism was a single uniform style.
art-movements-classical.l23.q4.e: Artists used many different approaches under the same broad movement.

art-movements-classical.l23.q5.t: They stressed colour and emotion over restrained line and order
art-movements-classical.l23.q5.p: How did Romantic painters differ from Neoclassical painters?
art-movements-classical.l23.q5.e: The contrast of emotion and order was a debate of the time.

art-movements-classical.l24.q1.p: In the Academy hierarchy, history painting ranked above still life.
art-movements-classical.l24.q1.h: Look at the order in the lesson.
art-movements-classical.l24.q1.e: History painting was considered the highest genre, still life the lowest.

art-movements-classical.l24.q2.t: A large official juried exhibition in Paris
art-movements-classical.l24.q2.e: The Salon was the key public art event and career gateway.

art-movements-classical.l24.q3.t: The Salon des Refuses displayed works the jury rejected
art-movements-classical.l24.q3.e: The emperor allowed a separate exhibition for rejected works.

art-movements-classical.l24.q4.p: Academic training began with large original compositions before any drawing practice.
art-movements-classical.l24.q4.e: Students started by copying and drawing from casts and models.

art-movements-classical.l24.q5.t: They find real skill in it and study how the system worked, including its exclusions
art-movements-classical.l24.q5.p: Why have historians reassessed academic art in recent decades?
art-movements-classical.l24.q5.h: Neither all good nor all bad.
art-movements-classical.l24.q5.e: Recent scholarship is more balanced about both quality and institutional limits.

art-movements-classical.l25.q1.p: Realist painters often chose everyday subjects such as workers and peasants.
art-movements-classical.l25.q1.e: Contemporary working life was a central subject.

art-movements-classical.l25.q2.p: Who organised a "Pavilion of Realism" in 1855?
art-movements-classical.l25.q2.h: He was refused at the Exposition.
art-movements-classical.l25.q2.e: Courbet showed his works in his own pavilion.

art-movements-classical.l25.q3.t: It showed ordinary labourers at near life size, like a history painting
art-movements-classical.l25.q3.p: What was unusual about the scale of Courbet's Stone Breakers?
art-movements-classical.l25.q3.e: Large scale was normally reserved for history subjects.

art-movements-classical.l25.q4.p: Realism is simply the same as a photograph.
art-movements-classical.l25.q4.e: Realist works are selected and composed, and often carry social comment.

art-movements-classical.l25.q5.t: It gave visibility to workers and the poor whom official art usually ignored
art-movements-classical.l25.q5.p: Why was Realism seen as political?
art-movements-classical.l25.q5.e: Choosing labourers as monumental subjects challenged hierarchies of status.

art-movements-classical.l26.q1.p: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood was founded in London in 1848.

art-movements-classical.l26.q2.p: What did the Pre-Raphaelites call for?
art-movements-classical.l26.q2.e: They stressed careful observation and sincerity.

art-movements-classical.l26.q3.p: Which painting shows Ophelia in a stream?

art-movements-classical.l26.q4.p: The Pre-Raphaelites based their aims on the style of Raphael himself.
art-movements-classical.l26.q4.e: They wanted to go back to art before Raphael's influence.

art-movements-classical.l26.q5.h: He also wrote on art and architecture.

art-movements-classical.l27.q1.p: The name "Impressionism" began as a mocking remark by a critic.
art-movements-classical.l27.q1.e: Louis Leroy used the word mockingly in 1874; the group adopted it.

art-movements-classical.l27.q2.p: What does en plein air mean?
art-movements-classical.l27.q2.h: The French phrase means open air.

art-movements-classical.l27.q3.p: How many group exhibitions did the Impressionists hold between 1874 and 1886?
art-movements-classical.l27.q3.e: There were eight exhibitions in those years.

art-movements-classical.l27.q4.e: Some, such as Degas, worked mostly in the studio.

art-movements-classical.l27.q5.t: Small visible strokes of broken colour side by side
art-movements-classical.l27.q5.p: Which brush technique is typical of Impressionism?
art-movements-classical.l27.q5.e: Visible strokes and juxtaposed colour suggest changing light.

art-movements-classical.l28.q1.p: Philippe Burty coined the term "Japonisme" in 1872.
art-movements-classical.l28.q1.e: The term named the European fashion for Japanese art.

art-movements-classical.l28.q2.t: Flat colour, strong outlines and bold cropping
art-movements-classical.l28.q2.p: Which feature did European artists borrow from Japanese prints?
art-movements-classical.l28.q2.e: These design ideas contrasted with academic habits.

art-movements-classical.l28.q3.p: Which painter copied Hiroshige prints in oils in 1887?
art-movements-classical.l28.q3.e: Van Gogh made oil copies of Hiroshige prints.

art-movements-classical.l28.q4.p: The artistic exchange between Japan and the West was one-way only.
art-movements-classical.l28.q4.e: Japan also took up Western technology and ideas while sending its crafts abroad.

art-movements-classical.l28.q5.t: They may show an imagined, exotic Japan rather than real Japanese life
art-movements-classical.l28.q5.p: Why should viewers be cautious about some Japonisme works?
art-movements-classical.l28.q5.e: Some European images reflect stereotypes more than reality.

art-movements-modern.l01.q1.p: Which invention, announced in 1839, led many artists to rethink what painting was for?
art-movements-modern.l01.q1.h: It could record a face faster than any painter.
art-movements-modern.l01.q1.e: Photography could record appearances quickly, pushing many painters toward colour, emotion and ideas.

art-movements-modern.l01.q2.p: The labels for art movements, such as Fauvism, were always chosen by the artists themselves.
art-movements-modern.l01.q2.h: Think about where the name Fauves came from.
art-movements-modern.l01.q2.e: Many movement names were given by critics, sometimes as insults.

art-movements-modern.l01.q3.t: They did not want to depend on the official Salon's approval
art-movements-modern.l01.q3.p: Why did the Impressionists organize their own exhibition in 1874?
art-movements-modern.l01.q3.h: Think about who controlled access to audiences.
art-movements-modern.l01.q3.e: Independent shows let artists present work without waiting for official juries.

art-movements-modern.l01.q4.p: A painting that uses flat colour instead of realistic shading is therefore a failed attempt at realism.
art-movements-modern.l01.q4.h: Consider what the artist might be asking instead.
art-movements-modern.l01.q4.e: Modern artists often chose flat colour on purpose to pursue different questions.

art-movements-modern.l01.q5.t: Movements overlap, and many artists changed direction or belonged to none
art-movements-modern.l01.q5.p: Which statement best describes how movements relate to individual artists?
art-movements-modern.l01.q5.h: The lesson gave two cautions about labels.
art-movements-modern.l01.q5.e: Labels are applied later and overlap, so artists often do not fit one box.

art-movements-modern.l02.q1.p: Which Post-Impressionist painted repeated views of Mont Sainte-Victoire?
art-movements-modern.l02.q1.e: Cézanne painted the mountain many times, building form from patches of colour.

art-movements-modern.l02.q2.p: Georges Seurat built images from small dots of colour that blend in the viewer's eye.
art-movements-modern.l02.q2.e: Seurat placed small dots side by side so that the eye mixes them from a distance.

art-movements-modern.l02.q3.t: It presents a colonial, exoticizing view, and his relationships with young girls there were exploitative
art-movements-modern.l02.q3.p: Why is Gauguin's Tahitian work debated today?
art-movements-modern.l02.q3.h: The debate is about perspective and conduct.
art-movements-modern.l02.q3.e: Critics point to the colonial gaze of the work and to his exploitative relationships.

art-movements-modern.l02.q4.t: They shared no single style; each emphasized a different element of painting
art-movements-modern.l02.q4.p: Which statement best describes the Post-Impressionists as a group?
art-movements-modern.l02.q4.h: The label came later, from a critic.
art-movements-modern.l02.q4.e: Roger Fry's label covers painters with different aims, such as structure, feeling, flatness and colour science.

art-movements-modern.l02.q5.p: Cézanne's way of building form from planes of colour influenced the Cubists.
art-movements-modern.l02.q5.h: Think about what Picasso and Braque learned from earlier painters.
art-movements-modern.l02.q5.e: Cubists drew on Cézanne's treatment of a scene as a structure of shapes.

art-movements-modern.l03.q1.p: Symbolist art mainly favours which kind of subject?
art-movements-modern.l03.q1.h: Think of mystery rather than description.
art-movements-modern.l03.q1.e: Symbolists wanted to suggest ideas and emotions rather than describe things plainly.

art-movements-modern.l03.q2.p: The Scream exists only as a single painting.
art-movements-modern.l03.q2.h: Munch returned to the image in several media.
art-movements-modern.l03.q2.e: Munch made paintings, pastels and a lithograph of The Scream.

art-movements-modern.l03.q3.p: Which artist is known for dark charcoal drawings he called his noirs?
art-movements-modern.l03.q3.h: He later turned to luminous pastel and oil.
art-movements-modern.l03.q3.e: Redon first became known for his noirs, then turned to rich colour.

art-movements-modern.l03.q4.p: In 1886, Jean Moréas published a Symbolist manifesto where?
art-movements-modern.l03.q4.h: It began as a literary movement.
art-movements-modern.l03.q4.e: Symbolism began in literature, with a manifesto in Le Figaro.

art-movements-modern.l03.q5.p: Symbolism's belief that pictures can show inner experience was inherited by Expressionism and Surrealism.
art-movements-modern.l03.q5.h: Consider where later movements found their ideas.
art-movements-modern.l03.q5.e: Both later movements continued the Symbolist focus on inner life.

art-movements-modern.l04.q1.p: Where were the Fauves first shown together in 1905?
art-movements-modern.l04.q1.h: It was a Paris exhibition held each year.
art-movements-modern.l04.q1.e: The 1905 Salon d'Automne room gave the group its name.

art-movements-modern.l04.q2.p: In Fauvism, colour did not have to match the real colour of the thing painted.
art-movements-modern.l04.q2.h: Remember the green and orange strokes on a face.
art-movements-modern.l04.q2.e: Fauves used colour to build structure and mood, not to report appearance.

art-movements-modern.l04.q3.p: Which painter led the Fauves and later made paper cut-outs?
art-movements-modern.l04.q3.h: He made Woman with a Hat in 1905.
art-movements-modern.l04.q3.e: Matisse was the leading Fauve and made cut-outs late in life.

art-movements-modern.l04.q4.t: A few years, to about 1907 or 1908
art-movements-modern.l04.q4.p: Roughly how long did Fauvism last as a recognizable movement?
art-movements-modern.l04.q4.h: It was never a formal organization.
art-movements-modern.l04.q4.e: The Fauves scattered after only a few years.

art-movements-modern.l04.q5.t: It treated colour as a subject in itself
art-movements-modern.l04.q5.p: What is the best summary of Fauvism's lasting influence?
art-movements-modern.l04.q5.h: Think about what Fauves freed colour to do.
art-movements-modern.l04.q5.e: Later painters, including Expressionists, inherited the freedom to use colour expressively.

art-movements-modern.l05.q1.p: Die Brücke was founded in which city?
art-movements-modern.l05.q1.e: Four students founded the group in Dresden in 1905.

art-movements-modern.l05.q2.p: The founders of Die Brücke were originally students of architecture.
art-movements-modern.l05.q2.h: Think about their training before art.
art-movements-modern.l05.q2.e: The founding members were architecture students.

art-movements-modern.l05.q3.p: Which medium did Die Brücke artists especially love for its rough, bold look?
art-movements-modern.l05.q3.e: They revived woodcuts for their bold, jagged look.

art-movements-modern.l05.q4.t: A Nazi show mocking modern art, which included many Expressionists
art-movements-modern.l05.q4.h: It was staged by a government, not the artists.
art-movements-modern.l05.q4.e: The Nazi government seized modern works and displayed them to ridicule them.

art-movements-modern.l05.q5.p: Historians note that Die Brücke's interest in African and Oceanic objects often ignored the makers and meanings of those objects.
art-movements-modern.l05.q5.e: The borrowing was selective and often disregarded context, a point scholars raise about many modernists.

art-movements-modern.l06.q1.p: Which two artists were central to Der Blaue Reiter in Munich?
art-movements-modern.l06.q1.e: Wassily Kandinsky and Franz Marc led the circle.

art-movements-modern.l06.q2.p: Kandinsky compared painting to music in Concerning the Spiritual in Art.
art-movements-modern.l06.q2.h: Think of colour and shape moving viewers without depiction.
art-movements-modern.l06.q2.e: He argued colour and form could move people the way music does.

art-movements-modern.l06.q3.t: Hilma af Klint was painting abstract works around 1906 too
art-movements-modern.l06.q3.p: Why is the phrase "first abstract artist" contested?
art-movements-modern.l06.q3.h: Another artist began earlier, in Sweden.
art-movements-modern.l06.q3.e: Af Klint's early abstract paintings show abstraction emerged in several places.

art-movements-modern.l06.q4.t: Macke and Marc were killed, and the group ended
art-movements-modern.l06.q4.p: What happened to the group during the First World War?
art-movements-modern.l06.q4.e: Macke was killed in 1914 and Marc in 1916, and the circle broke up.

art-movements-modern.l06.q5.p: The 1912 almanac mixed modern paintings with children's art, folk art and non-European works.
art-movements-modern.l06.q5.h: Consider the group's claim about inner life across cultures.
art-movements-modern.l06.q5.e: The almanac argued for a shared expressive impulse across cultures and ages.

art-movements-modern.l07.q1.e: Picasso and Braque developed the style together.

art-movements-modern.l07.q2.p: Cubism shows an object from several viewpoints at once.
art-movements-modern.l07.q2.h: Think about the mug drawn from above and the side.
art-movements-modern.l07.q2.e: The core idea is combining multiple views in one image.

art-movements-modern.l07.q3.t: It is brighter and simpler and uses collage
art-movements-modern.l07.q3.p: What distinguishes Synthetic Cubism from Analytic Cubism?
art-movements-modern.l07.q3.h: Think of the oilcloth in Still Life with Chair Caning.
art-movements-modern.l07.q3.e: Synthetic Cubism, from about 1912, introduced collage and brighter colour.

art-movements-modern.l07.q4.t: Oilcloth printed with a chair-caning pattern
art-movements-modern.l07.q4.p: What did Picasso attach in Still Life with Chair Caning (1912)?
art-movements-modern.l07.q4.h: A printed material stood in for a painted one.
art-movements-modern.l07.q4.e: The oilcloth is a real material used in place of painting the pattern.

art-movements-modern.l07.q5.p: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon is criticized by some historians for its use of non-European art.
art-movements-modern.l07.q5.e: Its mask-like faces drew on Iberian and, per many historians, African and Oceanic objects, which raises appropriation questions.

art-movements-modern.l08.q1.p: In which newspaper was the Futurist Manifesto published in 1909?
art-movements-modern.l08.q1.e: Marinetti's manifesto appeared on the front page of Le Figaro on 20 February 1909.

art-movements-modern.l08.q2.p: Futurists wanted to celebrate speed, machines and modern life.
art-movements-modern.l08.q2.h: Think of Balla's dog on a leash.
art-movements-modern.l08.q2.e: They aimed to show movement and energy.

art-movements-modern.l08.q3.t: By repeating the legs and leash many times
art-movements-modern.l08.q3.p: How did Balla suggest motion in Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash?
art-movements-modern.l08.q3.h: Compare it to a multiple exposure.
art-movements-modern.l08.q3.e: Repeated forms show successive positions within a single image.

art-movements-modern.l08.q4.t: Marinetti glorified war and later supported Italian Fascism
art-movements-modern.l08.q4.p: Which statement about Futurism's politics is accurate?
art-movements-modern.l08.q4.h: Think about the troubling side of the movement.
art-movements-modern.l08.q4.e: Marinetti praised war and later backed Mussolini's movement.

art-movements-modern.l08.q5.p: Historians agree that Futurism's art can be fully separated from its politics.
art-movements-modern.l08.q5.h: The lesson says many conclude otherwise.
art-movements-modern.l08.q5.e: Many historians argue the movement's aesthetics and ideology were closely linked, and the matter is debated.

art-movements-modern.l09.q1.h: A neutral country during the war.
art-movements-modern.l09.q1.e: Hugo Ball opened the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich.

art-movements-modern.l09.q2.p: Dada was a protest against the First World War and the values that led to it.
art-movements-modern.l09.q2.e: Dada artists mocked the reasoning and nationalism they blamed for the war.

art-movements-modern.l09.q3.t: An ordinary manufactured object chosen and presented as art
art-movements-modern.l09.q3.e: Duchamp's readymades made the act of selection the art.

art-movements-modern.l09.q4.p: Which artist made photomontages critiquing politics and gender roles?
art-movements-modern.l09.q4.e: Höch and Raoul Hausmann made Dada photomontages in Berlin.

art-movements-modern.l09.q5.p: What basic question did Dada help shift art toward?
art-movements-modern.l09.q5.h: It moved from craft to concept.
art-movements-modern.l09.q5.e: Dada changed the question from whether a work was well made to what makes something art.

art-movements-modern.l10.q1.p: Who published the first Manifesto of Surrealism in 1924?

art-movements-modern.l10.q2.p: Surrealists were influenced by Sigmund Freud's ideas about dreams and the unconscious.
art-movements-modern.l10.q2.h: Think about the source of the movement's subjects.
art-movements-modern.l10.q2.e: Breton and others drew on Freud's work.

art-movements-modern.l10.q3.t: Making marks or writing without conscious control
art-movements-modern.l10.q3.h: It aims to reach hidden material.
art-movements-modern.l10.q3.e: Automatism tries to bypass reasoning to reach the unconscious.

art-movements-modern.l10.q4.t: The Treachery of Images by Magritte
art-movements-modern.l10.q4.p: Which work shows a pipe with the words "This is not a pipe"?
art-movements-modern.l10.q4.h: It reminds viewers a picture is not the thing itself.
art-movements-modern.l10.q4.e: Magritte's 1929 painting plays on the gap between image and object.

art-movements-modern.l10.q5.p: Women Surrealists such as Leonora Carrington and Remedios Varo were significant artists, even though male leaders often cast women as muses.
art-movements-modern.l10.q5.h: Consider the gap between role and achievement.
art-movements-modern.l10.q5.e: Their work is now recognized as central to the movement.

art-movements-modern.l11.q2.p: Tatlin's Monument to the Third International was built at full scale.
art-movements-modern.l11.q2.e: It remained a model and was never built.

art-movements-modern.l11.q3.p: What did Constructivists believe art should be?
art-movements-modern.l11.q3.e: Constructivists argued for art that served practical and social purposes.

art-movements-modern.l11.q4.t: It was suppressed in favour of Socialist Realism
art-movements-modern.l11.q4.p: What happened to the Russian avant-garde under Stalin in the 1930s?
art-movements-modern.l11.q4.h: A heroic, representational style was promoted.
art-movements-modern.l11.q4.e: Socialist Realism replaced avant-garde abstraction as the official style.

art-movements-modern.l11.q5.p: Many Russian avant-garde artists believed abstraction could help build a new society.
art-movements-modern.l11.q5.h: Think about why they supported the revolution.
art-movements-modern.l11.q5.e: They saw abstract form as part of a new social order, not mere decoration.

art-movements-modern.l12.q1.p: Which colours did Mondrian use besides black, white and grey?
art-movements-modern.l12.q1.e: Neoplasticism used primary colours with black lines and white.

art-movements-modern.l12.q2.p: De Stijl began in 1917 in the Netherlands.
art-movements-modern.l12.q2.h: The name means The Style in Dutch.
art-movements-modern.l12.q2.e: Theo van Doesburg and others began it in 1917.

art-movements-modern.l12.q3.p: Which building applied De Stijl principles to architecture?
art-movements-modern.l12.q3.e: The Schröder House is a De Stijl landmark and a UNESCO site.

art-movements-modern.l12.q4.t: Van Doesburg introduced diagonals, which Mondrian rejected
art-movements-modern.l12.q4.p: Why did Mondrian and van Doesburg split around 1925?
art-movements-modern.l12.q4.e: Diagonals broke Mondrian's system of horizontals and verticals.

art-movements-modern.l12.q5.p: Broadway Boogie Woogie uses small coloured squares to suggest the rhythm of the city.
art-movements-modern.l12.q5.e: Mondrian made it in New York in 1942 to 1943, adapting his grid to city rhythm.
