film-history.l02.q4.e: Several narrators and a question without a final answer make Kane a portrait assembled from partial views, with no single truth.

film-history.l03.q1.t: A plot device whose only purpose is to set the story in motion
film-history.l03.q1.p: What is the "MacGuffin" in Hitchcock's films?
film-history.l03.q1.h: It matters to the characters more than to the audience.
film-history.l03.q1.e: The MacGuffin is a plot device that starts the story; what matters is what people do to obtain it.

film-history.l03.q2.p: Which film is linked to the dolly zoom, also called the "Vertigo shot"?
film-history.l03.q2.h: The effect is named for the film.
film-history.l03.q2.e: The dolly zoom is nicknamed the Vertigo shot because it is associated with that film.

film-history.l03.q3.p: A filmmaker lets the audience see a bomb under a table that the characters have not noticed. Which Hitchcock principle is at work?
film-history.l03.q3.h: The audience knows more than the characters.
film-history.l03.q3.e: Hitchcock gave the audience information the characters lacked, creating suspense instead of a quick shock.

film-history.l03.q4.t: Rely on what the audience anticipates rather than sees
film-history.l03.q4.p: Compared with Spielberg's withholding of the shark in Jaws, Hitchcock's suspense is similar because both:
film-history.l03.q4.h: Think about the effect of waiting.
film-history.l03.q4.e: Both directors build tension through anticipation: what is withheld or known but unseen is scarier than constant display.

film-history.l04.q1.p: During which period did Italian Neorealism flourish?
film-history.l04.q1.h: It followed the Second World War.
film-history.l04.q1.e: The museum dates Italian Neorealism to 1943-1952, in post-war Italy.

film-history.l04.q2.p: Which is a hallmark of Neorealism?
film-history.l04.q2.h: Think about who appears on screen.
film-history.l04.q2.e: Neorealism used non-professional actors, location shooting, natural light and social realism.

film-history.l04.q3.p: A film shot on location in a poor neighbourhood with local people and natural light would fit Neorealist methods.
film-history.l04.q3.h: Compare with the list of hallmarks.
film-history.l04.q3.e: Location shooting, non-professional actors and natural light are core Neorealist methods.

film-history.l04.q4.t: It proved serious cinema could be made cheaply on real locations
film-history.l04.q4.p: Why would Neorealism have influenced later movements such as the French New Wave?
film-history.l04.q4.e: Neorealism showed that real places and ordinary people were enough, an idea the New Wave embraced with location shooting.

film-history.l05.q1.p: Which of these is a Kurosawa film?
film-history.l05.q1.e: Seven Samurai is among Kurosawa's best-known works, with Rashomon, Ran, Ikiru and Yojimbo.

film-history.l05.q2.t: The same event told through irreconcilable subjective accounts
film-history.l05.q2.h: It involves several people describing one event.
film-history.l05.q2.e: The Rashomon effect presents one event through accounts that cannot be reconciled.

film-history.l05.q3.p: A director films a battle in rain and mud with several cameras and long lenses to flatten the action. Whose style is this?
film-history.l05.q3.h: Weather was treated as a narrative force.
film-history.l05.q3.e: Kurosawa used multi-camera coverage with long lenses and treated rain, wind and mud as narrative forces.

film-history.l05.q4.p: Which pair names directors who, with Kurosawa, defined the Japanese Golden Age?
film-history.l05.q4.e: The museum names Kurosawa, Ozu and Mizoguchi as carrying Japanese cinema to the world stage.

film-history.l06.q1.t: Film-writing that fuses documentary and fiction as one voice
film-history.l06.q1.p: What is "cinécriture", the term associated with Agnès Varda?
film-history.l06.q1.h: The word suggests writing with film.
film-history.l06.q1.e: Varda invented cinécriture, or film-writing, blending documentary and fiction.

film-history.l06.q2.p: The French New Wave ran from 1958 to 1969.
film-history.l06.q2.e: The museum dates the French New Wave to 1958-1969.

film-history.l06.q3.p: A young critic makes a film using jump cuts, improvised dialogue and location shooting. Which movement does this resemble?
film-history.l06.q3.e: Jump cuts, location shooting and improvised dialogue are New Wave hallmarks.

film-history.l06.q4.p: Which Varda film is noted for following a woman across ninety minutes of real-time storytelling?
film-history.l06.q4.h: The title mentions a time window.
film-history.l06.q4.e: Cléo from 5 to 7 tracks a woman across ninety unbroken minutes in real time.

film-history.l07.q1.p: What years does the museum give for New Hollywood?
film-history.l07.q1.e: New Hollywood is dated 1967-1980 in the United States.

film-history.l07.q2.p: Which is a hallmark of New Hollywood?
film-history.l07.q2.e: Morally ambiguous heroes, the director as author and location realism define New Hollywood.

film-history.l07.q3.p: Which list contains only New Hollywood key films?
film-history.l07.q3.e: The Godfather, Taxi Driver, Chinatown and Apocalypse Now are the key films listed.

film-history.l07.q4.t: Directors, not studios, came to be seen as authors
film-history.l07.q4.p: Why does the lesson say New Hollywood changed "who a film belongs to"?
film-history.l07.q4.e: The movement made the director the author of the film, shifting credit away from the studio.

film-history.l08.q1.p: Which cinematographer is nicknamed the "Prince of Darkness"?
film-history.l08.q1.e: Gordon Willis earned the nickname for radical underexposure that dropped eyes into shadow.

film-history.l08.q2.p: Which editor is credited with the term and practice of "sound design"?
film-history.l08.q2.h: He also coined the Rule of Six.
film-history.l08.q2.e: Walter Murch is associated with sound design as an authored soundscape.

film-history.l08.q3.p: In the Rule of Six, which element ranks FIRST?
film-history.l08.q3.h: It is about how the audience feels.
film-history.l08.q3.e: Murch's Rule of Six puts emotion first, followed by story, rhythm and continuity.

film-history.l08.q4.t: It states a moral theme by cutting a sacred ritual against killing
film-history.l08.q4.p: What does the baptism and murder montage in The Godfather achieve through editing?
film-history.l08.q4.h: Think of the contrast between two events.
film-history.l08.q4.e: Operatic cross-cutting set a sacred ritual beside murder, letting the editing itself act as a moral thesis.

film-history.l09.q1.p: Who is Martin Scorsese's long-time editor?
film-history.l09.q1.e: Thelma Schoonmaker has edited Scorsese's films for half a century.

film-history.l09.q2.p: Which of these is a Scorsese film?
film-history.l09.q2.h: A gangster story with a famous Steadicam shot.
film-history.l09.q2.e: Goodfellas is listed among Scorsese's works, with Taxi Driver, Raging Bull, Casino and The Departed.

film-history.l09.q3.p: A director places a cheerful pop song over a brutal scene to create irony. Which Scorsese technique is this?
film-history.l09.q3.h: The song comes from existing recordings.
film-history.l09.q3.e: Needle-drop pop soundtracks used as ironic counterpoint to violence are a Scorsese signature.

film-history.l09.q4.t: The look is the camera's and the pulse is the editor's
film-history.l09.q4.p: Why is the Scorsese-Schoonmaker partnership a good example of film as collaboration?
film-history.l09.q4.e: Scorsese supplies camera and music choices, while Schoonmaker's percussive cutting gives the films their rhythm.

film-history.l10.q1.p: Which film shows the Spielberg approach of withholding the monster?
film-history.l10.q1.e: In Jaws, suspense builds from what the audience does not see.

film-history.l10.q2.p: Which composer revived the symphonic film score and wrote the two-note Jaws motif?
film-history.l10.q2.e: John Williams revived the late-Romantic symphonic tradition and wrote the Jaws motif.

film-history.l10.q3.p: Which company did Kathleen Kennedy co-found with Spielberg?
film-history.l10.q3.e: Kennedy co-founded Amblin Entertainment and helped shape the blockbuster era with Spielberg.

film-history.l10.q4.t: They both build dread from very little
film-history.l10.q4.p: What do Hitchcock's suspense and Williams's two-note Jaws motif have in common?
film-history.l10.q4.e: Both create dread from minimal means: information held back, or the simplest possible musical cell.

film-history.l11.q1.t: Drops frames to smear motion into dreamlike blur
film-history.l11.q1.e: Step-printing drops frames so that motion smears into a dreamlike blur.

film-history.l11.q2.p: Which cinematographer collaborated with Wong Kar-wai on In the Mood for Love and Chungking Express?
film-history.l11.q2.e: Christopher Doyle shot In the Mood for Love, Chungking Express and Happy Together.

film-history.l11.q3.p: Wong Kar-wai is associated with Hong Kong's Second Wave.
film-history.l11.q3.h: Check the era listed for him.
film-history.l11.q3.e: The museum lists his era as the Hong Kong Second Wave.

film-history.l11.q4.p: How does Wong's improvised, script-less shooting shape the finished films?
film-history.l11.q4.e: Improvised shooting favours mood and feeling over conventional plot.

film-history.l12.q2.e: Dogme required handheld camera, on-location sound, no artificial lighting and no genre.

film-history.l12.q3.t: Shooting handheld with the available light
film-history.l12.q3.p: A director wants to follow Dogme rules. Which choice is allowed?
film-history.l12.q3.e: Handheld camera and available light fit Dogme; artificial lighting and studio-added sound do not.

film-history.l12.q4.t: Italian Neorealism and the French New Wave
film-history.l12.q4.p: What earlier movements share the Dogme preference for simple means and real places?
film-history.l12.q4.e: Neorealism and the New Wave also chose real places and modest means over studio gloss.

film-producing.l01.q1.p: A producer is mainly responsible for making a film possible and keeping it on track, while the director is mainly responsible for the creative vision on screen.
film-producing.l01.q1.e: This is a rough but widely used division: producers handle the project as a whole, directors the creative vision.

film-producing.l01.q2.p: Which stage comes first in the usual order of a film project?
film-producing.l01.q2.h: Think of what must exist before anything is shot.
film-producing.l01.q2.e: Development turns an idea into a script and plan before planning, shooting, editing and release follow.

film-producing.l01.q3.t: Small productions often combine jobs that are split among many people on larger films
film-producing.l01.q3.p: On a tiny student film, the producer is also doing the scheduling, budget and location finding. What does this show?
film-producing.l01.q3.e: On small projects one person often covers several roles, while larger films divide them.

film-producing.l01.q4.t: Can we afford and finish it?
film-producing.l01.q4.p: Which question is closest to the producer's three basic concerns?
film-producing.l01.q4.e: Producers focus on what is being made, whether it can be afforded and finished, and who will see it.

film-producing.l01.q5.t: They must recognise a story worth telling and also say what it costs and who pays
film-producing.l01.q5.p: Why do good producers need both creative and practical skills?
film-producing.l01.q5.h: Consider both halves of the job.
film-producing.l01.q5.e: The role joins story judgement with money, schedule and people management.

film-producing.l02.q1.p: A producer credit means exactly the same set of duties on every film.
film-producing.l02.q1.e: Titles are used differently from one production to another, so duties and credits vary.

film-producing.l02.q2.p: Which role typically manages the budget and day-to-day logistics of a shoot?
film-producing.l02.q2.e: The line producer turns the plan into a schedule and controls daily spending.

film-producing.l02.q3.p: Ben arranged the main investment for a small film. Which credit might he reasonably receive?
film-producing.l02.q3.h: The title is often tied to money or the deal.
film-producing.l02.q3.e: Executive producer often reflects a role connected to financing, rights or oversight.

film-producing.l02.q4.t: Focuses on the story, script and artists
film-producing.l02.q4.p: Which description best fits a creative producer?
film-producing.l02.q4.e: A creative producer concentrates on the material and the people shaping it.

film-producing.l02.q5.p: Because credits can be negotiated and carry prestige, producer titles are sometimes a matter of real contractual discussion.
film-producing.l02.q5.e: Titles can carry weight and are often negotiated, which is why they are discussed in deals.

film-producing.l03.q1.t: The stage where an idea becomes a script and plan strong enough to attract funding and talent
film-producing.l03.q1.e: Development is the period before a film is approved to be made.

film-producing.l03.q2.p: Many projects that enter development never get made.
film-producing.l03.q2.h: Consider how often projects fail to find funding.
film-producing.l03.q2.e: Most developed projects do not reach production, which is why development costs are a real risk.

film-producing.l03.q3.t: A licence or other permission from the rights holder
film-producing.l03.q3.p: A producer wants to adapt a novel by a living author. What does she generally need?
film-producing.l03.q3.h: Think about who owns the book.
film-producing.l03.q3.e: Adapting protected material requires permission from whoever holds the rights.

film-producing.l03.q4.t: To judge whether it can find an audience and be made at a workable price
film-producing.l03.q4.p: Why might a producer test a story against questions about audience and cost during development?
film-producing.l03.q4.e: Early checks on audience, comparable films and cost help decide whether to commit more money.

film-producing.l03.q5.t: Because most developed projects will not be made
film-producing.l03.q5.p: Why do producers often spread development risk across several projects?
film-producing.l03.q5.e: Since many projects stall, producers diversify and seek outside development funding.

film-producing.l04.q1.t: The exclusive right, for a set period, to buy the rights at an agreed price
film-producing.l04.q1.p: What does an option agreement give a producer?
film-producing.l04.q1.h: It reserves something for a period.
film-producing.l04.q1.e: An option lets a producer reserve the material while trying to raise money.

film-producing.l04.q2.p: If a producer does not exercise an option before it expires, the rights usually return to the owner.
film-producing.l04.q2.e: Unless the option is extended or exercised, the rights generally revert.

film-producing.l04.q3.t: The documented trail showing rights passed properly from the creator to the production company
film-producing.l04.q3.p: What is the chain of title?
film-producing.l04.q3.e: It shows each transfer of rights, and financiers and insurers want it clean.

film-producing.l04.q4.t: A gap in the chain of title that could delay a deal
film-producing.l04.q4.p: A writer never signed an agreement for a script the production is using. What is the likely problem?
film-producing.l04.q4.e: Missing signed agreements create gaps that distributors and insurers may not accept.

film-producing.l04.q5.t: It reserves the material without paying the full price before financing is found
film-producing.l04.q5.p: Why can an option be more attractive to a producer than buying the rights outright at the start?
film-producing.l04.q5.e: A smaller option fee lets the producer hold the project while raising money.

film-producing.l05.q1.t: A script combined with key creative elements such as a director or lead actors
film-producing.l05.q1.e: Packaging attaches key people to a script to make it more attractive to backers.

film-producing.l05.q2.p: A letter of interest from an actor is as binding as a signed contract.
film-producing.l05.q2.e: A letter of interest is not a binding contract, though it can still help in a pitch.

film-producing.l05.q3.p: What do comparable films (comps) help a buyer judge?
film-producing.l05.q3.e: Comps give a sense of potential audience and revenue, if chosen honestly.

film-producing.l05.q4.t: A short, clear presentation to persuade someone to read, fund or buy a project
film-producing.l05.q4.p: Which is the best way to describe a pitch?
film-producing.l05.q4.e: A pitch states the idea, audience, comparables and what the producer needs.

film-producing.l05.q5.t: It damages trust and can create legal problems
film-producing.l05.q5.p: Why is overstating who is attached to a project harmful?
film-producing.l05.q5.e: Misleading backers can destroy relationships and may cause legal trouble.

film-producing.l06.q1.t: A short summary of the major budget categories and the total
film-producing.l06.q1.p: What does a top sheet show?
film-producing.l06.q1.e: The top sheet summarises the whole budget on one or two pages.

film-producing.l06.q2.t: Story and rights, producer, director and principal cast
film-producing.l06.q2.p: Which costs are typically listed above the line?
film-producing.l06.q2.h: Think of the elements negotiated first.
film-producing.l06.q2.e: Above-the-line costs cover key creative elements, while below-the-line covers physical production.

film-producing.l06.q3.p: Fringes are payroll taxes, benefits and similar charges added on top of salaries.
film-producing.l06.q3.h: They sit on top of pay.
film-producing.l06.q3.e: Fringes can be a significant percentage of labour costs.

film-producing.l06.q4.t: Line items are built from a rate and a quantity
film-producing.l06.q4.p: A camera department line multiplies a daily rental rate by the number of shooting days. What does this show?
film-producing.l06.q4.e: Each line item typically has a rate, a quantity and a total.

film-producing.l06.q5.t: A scene such as a night exterior with a crowd has real costs that must be shown
film-producing.l06.q5.p: Why must a budget be tied closely to the script?
film-producing.l06.q5.e: Every demanding scene should appear in the budget or the plan will be unrealistic.

film-producing.l07.q1.t: An amount set aside for unexpected costs
film-producing.l07.q1.e: A contingency is a reserve for genuine surprises.

film-producing.l07.q2.p: A contingency is meant to cover a budget that was too low from the start.
film-producing.l07.q2.e: It is for unexpected events, not for correcting a poor budget.

film-producing.l07.q3.t: Budgeted, spent or committed so far, and the forecast final cost
film-producing.l07.q3.p: A cost report typically compares which three things?
film-producing.l07.q3.e: The comparison shows whether a production is over or under budget.

film-producing.l07.q4.t: When money comes in and goes out
film-producing.l07.q4.p: What does a cash flow schedule show?
film-producing.l07.q4.h: It is about timing of money.
film-producing.l07.q4.e: Productions need money available at each point to pay people and deposits.

film-producing.l07.q5.t: Use contingency if appropriate, record the change and check the remaining plan
film-producing.l07.q5.p: A storm forces a reshoot costing $25,000 (illustrative). What should the producer do?
film-producing.l07.q5.e: Recording changes early keeps the forecast accurate and decisions timely.

film-producing.l08.q1.t: A list of the elements each scene needs
film-producing.l08.q1.h: It splits the script into needs.
film-producing.l08.q1.e: The breakdown identifies cast, props, locations and other elements for every scene.

film-producing.l08.q2.p: Scenes are commonly measured in eighths of a page.
film-producing.l08.q2.h: A page is split into parts.
film-producing.l08.q2.e: Eighths of a page are a standard way to measure scene length.

film-producing.l08.q3.t: They affect lighting, crew and scheduling
film-producing.l08.q3.p: Why do breakdowns note interior or exterior and day or night?
film-producing.l08.q3.e: These details influence how and when a scene can be shot.

film-producing.l08.q4.p: A scene reads, "A bus stops in the rain and Lena runs to catch it." Which element would the breakdown note?
film-producing.l08.q4.e: Rain, a vehicle and likely extras and permits turn a short line into costs.

film-producing.l08.q5.t: Exposing costs a quick read might miss
film-producing.l08.q5.p: What is the second main use of a breakdown besides scheduling?
film-producing.l08.q5.e: A careful breakdown reveals hidden items such as animals, children or special effects.

film-producing.l09.q1.t: A tool arranging scenes into shooting days
film-producing.l09.q1.e: Strips representing scenes are moved to test shooting orders.

film-producing.l09.q2.p: Films are almost always shot in story order.
film-producing.l09.q2.e: Scenes are grouped by location, cast and other factors instead.

film-producing.l09.q3.t: To avoid moving the crew back and forth
film-producing.l09.q3.p: Why are scenes in one location usually grouped together?
film-producing.l09.q3.h: Think about moving trucks and gear.
film-producing.l09.q3.e: Grouping saves set-up and travel time.

film-producing.l09.q4.t: An interior scene ready to shoot if bad weather ruins an exterior plan
film-producing.l09.q4.e: Having an alternative scene prevents a lost day.

film-producing.l09.q5.p: What is a likely effect of adding more shooting days?
film-producing.l09.q5.e: Each additional day adds crew, gear and location costs.

film-producing.l10.q1.t: Minimum pay, hours, rest periods, safety rules and benefit contributions
film-producing.l10.q1.p: What do union agreements typically set?
film-producing.l10.q1.e: Collective agreements set minimum terms that apply when a production signs on.

film-producing.l10.q2.p: Every film must use union crew.
film-producing.l10.q2.e: Many independent productions work non-union or use special agreements.

film-producing.l10.q3.p: Which union represents many directors in the United States?
film-producing.l10.q3.e: The DGA represents directors and certain other roles, while the other groups represent different workers.

film-producing.l10.q4.t: Pay, credit, dates and ownership of work
film-producing.l10.q4.p: What does a deal memo set out?
film-producing.l10.q4.e: Deal memos are signed before work begins.

film-producing.l10.q5.t: It may require meal breaks and minimum turnaround time between workdays
film-producing.l10.q5.p: How might using a union agreement affect the schedule?
film-producing.l10.q5.e: Agreements typically include rest and meal rules that shape the day.

film-producing.l11.q1.t: Claims of injury or property damage to others
film-producing.l11.q1.p: What does general liability insurance typically respond to?
film-producing.l11.q1.e: It covers third-party injury or damage claims.

film-producing.l11.q2.p: Distributors commonly require errors and omissions insurance for a finished film.
film-producing.l11.q2.h: Think about legal claims in the film itself.
film-producing.l11.q2.e: E&O protects against claims such as infringement or defamation and is commonly requested.

film-producing.l11.q3.t: To confirm coverage and name parties as additional insured where needed
film-producing.l11.q3.p: Why does a producer ask a location owner for a certificate of insurance?
film-producing.l11.q3.e: Certificates document coverage and are a standard request.

film-producing.l11.q4.t: Planning and rehearsing a stunt with specialists
film-producing.l11.q4.p: Which is an example of reducing a risk rather than insuring it?
film-producing.l11.q4.e: Risk management aims to prevent losses as well as transfer the cost.

film-producing.l11.q5.p: Why should entertainment insurance be discussed with a specialist broker?
film-producing.l11.q5.e: Exact terms vary, so expert advice helps avoid gaps.

film-producing.l12.q1.t: A document showing who is needed, where and when for the next shooting day
film-producing.l12.q1.h: It is sent the evening before.
film-producing.l12.q1.e: It also lists scenes, weather and safety notes.

film-producing.l12.q2.p: Wrap includes returning rentals, closing accounts and collecting paperwork.
film-producing.l12.q2.e: Wrap tasks are part of the job and delays can cause disputes.

film-producing.l12.q3.t: What was shot, hours worked and any delays or incidents
film-producing.l12.q3.p: What does the production report at the end of a day record?
film-producing.l12.q3.e: It helps track progress and problems.

film-producing.l12.q4.p: Who typically runs the set to keep to the schedule?
film-producing.l12.q4.e: The assistant director manages the day.

film-producing.l12.q5.t: Meet the director to decide how to catch up
film-producing.l12.q5.p: The crew shot six of seven planned scenes. What should the producer do?
film-producing.l12.q5.e: Dealing with a shortfall early keeps changes cheap.

film-producing.l13.q1.p: Which concern is typical of a producer rather than a director?
film-producing.l13.q1.e: Producers tend to guard budget, schedule and financiers' interests.

film-producing.l13.q2.p: Tension between producer and director is natural and not necessarily a sign of failure.
film-producing.l13.q2.e: Different priorities create tension, and open communication keeps it healthy.

film-producing.l13.q3.t: The right to determine the finished version of the film
film-producing.l13.q3.e: Many directors do not hold it, and on studio films the studio often does.

film-producing.l13.q4.t: Check costs and offer a cheaper alternative that achieves a similar effect
film-producing.l13.q4.p: A director wants a costly crane shot mid-shoot. What is a constructive response?
film-producing.l13.q4.e: Collaboration on options respects both creative and budget limits.

film-producing.l13.q5.t: Later decisions then have a shared reference point
film-producing.l13.q5.p: Why should the producer and director agree creative aims and limits early?
film-producing.l13.q5.e: Early agreement on budget, schedule and tone gives a basis for later choices.

film-producing.l14.q1.p: Safety and fair treatment are part of a producer's responsibility.
film-producing.l14.q1.e: Producers carry ethical and legal responsibility for those on the production.

film-producing.l14.q2.p: Which person is typically hired to help plan and supervise dangerous action?
film-producing.l14.q2.e: Stunt coordinators plan and supervise stunts.

film-producing.l14.q3.t: The death of cinematographer Halyna Hutchins during filming of Rust
film-producing.l14.q3.p: What event in October 2021 drew attention to weapons safety on set?
film-producing.l14.q3.e: The incident prompted scrutiny of on-set weapons practices.

film-producing.l14.q4.p: Why do union agreements set rest periods?
film-producing.l14.q4.e: Long hours cause accidents, so rest rules are a safety measure.

film-producing.l14.q5.t: Respect their dignity and avoid misleading portrayals
film-producing.l14.q5.p: What is a sound ethical approach to depicting a real person?
film-producing.l14.q5.e: Producers should respect real people and take legal advice where appropriate.

film-producing.l15.q1.t: No further changes to picture length are expected
film-producing.l15.q1.e: Sound, music and effects depend on a stable picture.

film-producing.l15.q2.p: Post-production often takes longer than the shoot itself.
film-producing.l15.q2.e: Editing, sound, music and effects usually take considerable time.

film-producing.l15.q3.p: Who adjusts the look of the image in grading?

film-producing.l15.q4.t: They can affect many departments and facilities that keep charging
film-producing.l15.q4.p: Why are late changes after lock expensive?
film-producing.l15.q4.e: Late changes ripple through sound, effects and delivery.

film-producing.l15.q5.t: The impact on sound and other departments
film-producing.l15.q5.p: A producer receives a note to trim a scene after sound work began. What should she check first?
film-producing.l15.q5.e: Checking knock-on effects avoids costly surprises.

film-producing.l16.q1.t: The finished film and the supporting materials a buyer requires
film-producing.l16.q1.e: Delivery schedules list required materials, often tied to payment.

film-producing.l16.q2.p: A music and effects track lets a film be dubbed into other languages.
film-producing.l16.q2.e: Having sound apart from dialogue makes dubbing possible.

film-producing.l16.q3.t: Chain of title and music cue sheets
film-producing.l16.q3.p: Which is a legal or administrative deliverable?
film-producing.l16.q3.e: Legal documents prove rights and list music use.

film-producing.l16.q4.t: To budget and plan for every required item
film-producing.l16.q4.p: Why should a producer read the delivery schedule early?
film-producing.l16.q4.e: Delivery costs and deadlines are easy to overlook.

film-producing.l16.q5.t: Build a checklist with owners and dates
film-producing.l16.q5.p: A contract lists 40 deliverables. What is a sensible method?
film-producing.l16.q5.e: Assigning each item prevents last-minute gaps such as missing music licences.

film-producing.l17.q1.t: Being the first public screening in a given country or region

film-producing.l17.q2.p: A festival screening guarantees a film will be sold.
film-producing.l17.q2.e: Festivals can help but guarantee nothing.

film-producing.l17.q3.t: Honest questions about audience and what success looks like
film-producing.l17.q3.p: What should a festival strategy begin with?
film-producing.l17.q3.e: Strategy follows from audience and goals.

film-producing.l17.q4.t: It may match a specific community, genre or region
film-producing.l17.q4.p: Why might a smaller regional festival suit a film better than a major one?
film-producing.l17.q4.e: Smaller festivals can suit particular audiences.

film-producing.l17.q5.t: An early screening elsewhere may rule a film out of a festival that wants premieres
film-producing.l17.q5.p: Why plan the order of festival submissions?
film-producing.l17.q5.e: Premiere requirements can make sequencing important.

film-producing.l18.q1.t: Takes a film to buyers on behalf of the producer for a commission
film-producing.l18.q1.p: What does a sales agent typically do?
film-producing.l18.q1.e: Sales agents sell territory by territory and earn a commission.

film-producing.l18.q2.p: A distributor typically recoups its expenses before paying the producer.
film-producing.l18.q2.e: Deals vary, but recoupment of costs is common.

film-producing.l18.q3.t: An advance a distributor pays against future earnings
film-producing.l18.q3.e: It is an advance against earnings.

film-producing.l18.q4.t: A single payment after which the buyer keeps what the film earns
film-producing.l18.q4.p: What is a flat fee or buyout?
film-producing.l18.q4.e: The producer does not share in later earnings.

film-producing.l18.q5.t: Deductible fees, length of the licence and rights included
film-producing.l18.q5.p: What should a producer check before accepting an advance?
film-producing.l18.q5.e: These details determine how much money ever returns.

film-producing.l19.q1.p: Which is typical of an independent producer?
film-producing.l19.q1.e: Independents often raise money separately for each film.

film-producing.l19.q2.p: Studios typically hold strong control over creative and business decisions on films they finance.
film-producing.l19.q2.e: Budget, casting approvals and final cut are often studio decisions.

film-producing.l19.q3.t: A deal giving a studio first chance at a producer's projects
film-producing.l19.q3.h: It concerns who sees projects first.
film-producing.l19.q3.e: It commonly comes with funding for the producer's office.

film-producing.l19.q4.t: More freedom but more uncertainty and personal risk
film-producing.l19.q4.p: What is a trade-off of independent producing?
film-producing.l19.q4.e: Independents gain freedom but carry more risk.

film-producing.l19.q5.t: An independent producer may bring a project to a studio or streamer as partner
film-producing.l19.q5.p: Why do many films mix both models?

film-producing.l20.q1.t: They are more flexible because the story may be found while filming
film-producing.l20.q1.p: How do documentary schedules typically differ from fiction?
film-producing.l20.q1.e: Shooting may stretch over months or years.

film-producing.l20.q2.p: Producers typically secure signed releases from documentary participants.
film-producing.l20.q2.e: Releases document permission, though ethics go beyond paperwork.

film-producing.l20.q3.t: Licences for photographs, footage and music can be a large cost
film-producing.l20.q3.p: Why must archive material often be budgeted for?
film-producing.l20.q3.e: Archival licensing is a major documentary cost.

film-producing.l20.q4.t: It is a fact-based judgement, not a guarantee
film-producing.l20.q4.p: What is true of fair use in the United States?
film-producing.l20.q4.e: Distributors and insurers often ask for legal review.

film-producing.l20.q5.t: Conditions about reporting and editorial independence
film-producing.l20.q5.p: What should a producer understand before accepting grant money?

film-producing.l21.q1.t: The service may pay costs plus a fee and take broad rights
film-producing.l21.q1.p: How may a streaming commission differ from a traditional licence?
film-producing.l21.q1.e: Commissions often trade ownership for certainty.

film-producing.l21.q2.p: Streaming practices are identical across all services and never change.
film-producing.l21.q2.e: Terms differ by service and change quickly.

film-producing.l21.q3.t: Less financing risk but fewer later earnings
film-producing.l21.q3.p: A fixed fee deal usually means which for the producer?
film-producing.l21.q3.e: Earnings may be fixed rather than tied to viewing.

film-producing.l21.q4.t: Rights granted, duration, bonuses and ownership of sequels
film-producing.l21.q4.p: What should a producer compare when weighing two offers?
film-producing.l21.q4.e: These details define the real value of a deal.

film-producing.l21.q5.t: It affects how success is judged and negotiated
film-producing.l21.q5.p: Why might viewing data held by a service matter to producers?
film-producing.l21.q5.e: Limited data can make it harder to prove audience.

film-producing.l22.q1.p: What is the core skill the course ends on?

film-producing.l22.q2.p: A producer's most important asset includes trust built through honest dealings.
film-producing.l22.q2.h: Many people rely on one another.
film-producing.l22.q2.e: Clear agreements and honest communication sustain collaboration.

film-producing.l22.q3.t: Identify, estimate, decide how to treat, then monitor
film-producing.l22.q3.p: Which is the correct sequence for handling a risk?
film-producing.l22.q3.e: A simple cycle of identifying, estimating, treating and monitoring works.

film-producing.l22.q4.t: List options such as delay, recast, rewrite or cancel and check contracts and insurance
film-producing.l22.q4.p: A lead actor drops out three weeks before the shoot. What is a sensible first step?
film-producing.l22.q4.e: Weighing options against obligations protects people and money.

film-producing.l22.q5.t: Further spending on something that cannot work wastes money and effort
film-producing.l22.q5.p: Why might stopping a project sometimes be right?
film-producing.l22.q5.e: Good judgement includes knowing when to restructure or stop.

founding-documents.l01.q1.p: In what year was Magna Carta issued?
founding-documents.l01.q1.e: Magna Carta was issued in 1215 between King John and his barons.

founding-documents.l01.q2.t: The lawful judgement of his equals or the law of the land
founding-documents.l01.q2.p: According to clause 39, a free man may not be seized or imprisoned except by what?
founding-documents.l01.q2.h: Think of a trial by peers.
founding-documents.l01.q2.e: Clause 39 requires lawful judgement of equals or the law of the land.

founding-documents.l01.q3.t: It spoke of free men, so it was not a charter of universal rights
founding-documents.l01.q3.p: What limit did Magna Carta have as originally written?
founding-documents.l01.q3.h: Look at the phrase no free man.
founding-documents.l01.q3.e: It was a bargain among the powerful, and its later power came from broader readings.

founding-documents.l01.q4.t: He read it as a guarantee of due process of law
founding-documents.l01.q4.p: How did Sir Edward Coke help give clause 39 lasting influence?
founding-documents.l01.q4.h: He lived in the seventeenth century.
founding-documents.l01.q4.e: Coke's reading of clause 39 as due process helped carry it into colonial charters and the Fifth Amendment.

founding-documents.l02.q1.p: Who wrote the Second Treatise of Government?
founding-documents.l02.q1.e: John Locke wrote the Second Treatise, published in 1689.

founding-documents.l02.q2.p: In Locke's argument, what must a government have to be legitimate?
founding-documents.l02.q2.h: It is a key phrase in the Declaration too.
founding-documents.l02.q2.e: Locke argued that no one can be subjected to political power without his own consent.

founding-documents.l02.q3.t: A hypothetical condition of freedom and equality before government
founding-documents.l02.q3.p: What does Locke mean by the state of nature?
founding-documents.l02.q3.e: It is an imagined starting point from which he builds his argument.

founding-documents.l02.q4.t: He gave both a founding justification and a justification for replacing a failed government
founding-documents.l02.q4.p: Why could both revolutionaries and constitution-builders cite Locke?
founding-documents.l02.q4.e: His writings cover how governments begin and when they may be dissolved.

founding-documents.l03.q1.t: It ought not to be required
founding-documents.l03.q1.p: What did the English Bill of Rights say about excessive bail?
founding-documents.l03.q1.h: The Eighth Amendment has similar words.
founding-documents.l03.q1.e: The text said excessive bail ought not to be required, nor excessive fines imposed.

founding-documents.l03.q2.p: In what year was the English Bill of Rights adopted?

founding-documents.l03.q3.p: Which American provision has wording almost identical to the English ban on cruel and unusual punishments?
founding-documents.l03.q3.h: It was written about a century later.
founding-documents.l03.q3.e: The Eighth Amendment borrowed the English phrasing closely.

founding-documents.l03.q4.t: It placed sovereignty in the King-in-Parliament, while the Americans moved to popular sovereignty
founding-documents.l03.q4.p: How does the English settlement of 1689 differ from the American approach to who rules?
founding-documents.l03.q4.h: Compare Parliament with We the People.
founding-documents.l03.q4.e: The 1689 settlement favoured the King-in-Parliament, not the people.

founding-documents.l04.q1.p: Who was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence?
founding-documents.l04.q1.e: Thomas Jefferson was its principal author.

founding-documents.l04.q2.p: In what year was the Declaration adopted?
founding-documents.l04.q2.h: It is the year of independence.

founding-documents.l04.q3.t: It is instituted to secure rights and gets its power from consent
founding-documents.l04.q3.p: What does the second step of the Declaration's argument say about government?
founding-documents.l04.q3.h: Look at the phrase consent of the governed.
founding-documents.l04.q3.e: Governments are instituted to secure rights, deriving their just powers from consent.

founding-documents.l04.q4.t: It states a premise and then lists specific charges against the King
founding-documents.l04.q4.p: Why is the Declaration described as like a legal brief?
founding-documents.l04.q4.e: It sets out a principle and then charges the King with particular acts.

founding-documents.l05.q1.h: Not even a king can do it.
founding-documents.l05.q1.e: An unalienable right cannot be taken away or given up.

founding-documents.l05.q2.t: Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness
founding-documents.l05.q2.p: Which three rights does the Declaration name, using the words among these?
founding-documents.l05.q2.h: They are in the famous second sentence.
founding-documents.l05.q2.e: The text names Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness.

founding-documents.l05.q3.p: What does the phrase among these signal about the list of rights?
founding-documents.l05.q3.e: Among these suggests that other rights exist too.

founding-documents.l05.q4.t: The people may change a government that turns against its purposes
founding-documents.l05.q4.p: What remedy does the phrase alter or abolish describe?
founding-documents.l05.q4.h: Think about the right of the people.
founding-documents.l05.q4.e: It states the people's right to change a destructive government and form a new one.

founding-documents.l06.q1.t: Slavery existed in the new states, and its author enslaved people
founding-documents.l06.q1.p: What tension do historians note about the Declaration's claim of equality?
founding-documents.l06.q1.e: The ideal of equality sat beside the reality of slavery.

founding-documents.l06.q2.p: Whose 1852 speech used the Declaration as an indictment?
founding-documents.l06.q2.e: Douglass pressed the nation to live up to its own founding words.

founding-documents.l06.q3.t: A founding text becomes a standard for criticizing the nation
founding-documents.l06.q3.p: What pattern does the lesson describe?
founding-documents.l06.q3.e: Reformers cited the Declaration to say the country had not yet lived up to it.

founding-documents.l06.q4.t: Good history notices what was written and what was done
founding-documents.l06.q4.p: Why should a student keep both the ideal and the reality in view?
founding-documents.l06.q4.e: Seeing both lets us understand the document's importance and its limits.

founding-documents.l07.q1.p: What are the first three words of the Preamble?
founding-documents.l07.q1.e: The Preamble begins We the People of the United States.

founding-documents.l07.q2.p: How many purposes does the Preamble list?
founding-documents.l07.q2.h: Count the goals in the sentence.
founding-documents.l07.q2.e: It lists union, justice, tranquility, defence, welfare and liberty.

founding-documents.l07.q3.p: What does the Preamble NOT do?
founding-documents.l07.q3.e: It states purposes; powers are in the articles that follow.

founding-documents.l07.q4.t: It was an argument that the Constitution rests on the people
founding-documents.l07.q4.p: Why did We the People replace a list of states, as in the Articles of Confederation?
founding-documents.l07.q4.e: The substitution signalled that authority came from the people, and critics noticed.

founding-documents.l08.q1.h: He is often called the Father of the Constitution.
founding-documents.l08.q1.e: James Madison wrote No. 51, published in 1788.

founding-documents.l08.q2.p: Complete the quotation: If men were angels...
founding-documents.l08.q2.h: Think of what governments are for.
founding-documents.l08.q2.e: Madison wrote that if men were angels, no government would be necessary.

founding-documents.l08.q3.t: Officials' self-interest is arranged to restrain other officials
founding-documents.l08.q3.p: What does Ambition must be made to counteract ambition mean?
founding-documents.l08.q3.e: The structure makes each officeholder defend the powers of the office against others.

founding-documents.l08.q4.t: It must control the governed and oblige itself to control itself
founding-documents.l08.q4.p: What two-part challenge does Madison describe for a government?
founding-documents.l08.q4.h: One part is about the governed, one about government.
founding-documents.l08.q4.e: It must first be able to govern and then be restrained.

founding-documents.l09.q1.p: In what year was the First Amendment added?
founding-documents.l09.q1.h: It is part of the Bill of Rights.
founding-documents.l09.q1.e: The Bill of Rights, including the First Amendment, was added in 1791.

founding-documents.l09.q2.p: Which of these is one of the five freedoms in the First Amendment?
founding-documents.l09.q2.h: Petition the government for a redress of grievances.
founding-documents.l09.q2.e: Religion, speech, press, assembly and petition are protected.

founding-documents.l09.q3.p: Whom does the text of the First Amendment restrain?
founding-documents.l09.q3.e: It says Congress shall make no law, and later applied to states through incorporation.

founding-documents.l09.q4.t: Applying limits on Congress to state governments through the Fourteenth Amendment
founding-documents.l09.q4.h: The text stayed the same but its reach grew.
founding-documents.l09.q4.e: Courts extended the First Amendment's limits to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment.

founding-documents.l10.q1.p: Who delivered What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?

founding-documents.l10.q2.p: In what year was the oration given?
founding-documents.l10.q2.h: It is between the Constitution and the Civil War.

founding-documents.l10.q3.p: What was the occasion for the speech?
founding-documents.l10.q3.e: Douglass was invited to speak at an Independence Day celebration.

founding-documents.l10.q4.t: He holds the country to it rather than rejecting it
founding-documents.l10.q4.p: How does Douglass treat the Declaration of Independence?
founding-documents.l10.q4.h: Think of demanding that a promise be kept.
founding-documents.l10.q4.e: He uses the nation's own principles as the standard against which to judge it.

founding-documents.l11.q1.p: How many words long is the Gettysburg Address, according to the course data?

founding-documents.l11.q2.p: What does four score and seven years mean?
founding-documents.l11.q2.e: Four score and seven is 4 times 20 plus 7, or 87 years.

founding-documents.l11.q3.p: To what year does Lincoln count back from 1863?
founding-documents.l11.q3.h: It is the year of the Declaration.

founding-documents.l11.q4.t: It treats equality in the Declaration as the nation's founding premise
founding-documents.l11.q4.p: Why does it matter that Lincoln dated the nation from 1776?
founding-documents.l11.q4.h: Compare the Declaration with the Constitution.
founding-documents.l11.q4.e: Starting from 1776 puts the Declaration's principle of equality at the centre.

founding-documents.l12.q1.e: Magna Carta dates from 1215, long before the others.

founding-documents.l12.q2.p: Which phrase moved from Locke into the Declaration?
founding-documents.l12.q2.h: It concerns where power comes from.
founding-documents.l12.q2.e: Locke's idea of consent became Jefferson's phrase.

founding-documents.l12.q3.p: Which later provision echoes the English Bill of Rights on cruel and unusual punishments?
founding-documents.l12.q3.h: It is in the Bill of Rights.
founding-documents.l12.q3.e: The Eighth Amendment is nearly identical in wording.

founding-documents.l12.q4.t: They are old or federal works, so they belong to everyone
founding-documents.l12.q4.p: Why are these documents in the public domain?
founding-documents.l12.q4.e: Their age and federal origin mean no one owns them, so everyone may read and share them.

graphic-design.l01.q1.p: Graphic design is mainly about making things look decorative, whether or not the message gets through.
graphic-design.l01.q1.e: Design is about making a message work for an audience; decoration alone does not do that.

graphic-design.l01.q2.t: Who is this for and what must they understand or do?
graphic-design.l01.q2.p: Which question should a designer ask before opening any software?
graphic-design.l01.q2.e: Audience and message come before any tool or style choice.

graphic-design.l01.q3.t: A designer typically works within a brief and is judged on whether the message gets through
graphic-design.l01.q3.p: How does a designer's job usually differ from a painter's private vision?
graphic-design.l01.q3.e: Design usually serves a client and audience, and success is measured by communication.

graphic-design.l01.q4.p: Constraints such as budget and deadline can push designers toward clever solutions.
graphic-design.l01.q4.h: Consider whether limits are only a problem.
graphic-design.l01.q4.e: Constraints make inventive solutions necessary and are a normal part of design.

graphic-design.l01.q5.p: A medicine label must make the dose hard to misread. This shows that design is mainly about what?
graphic-design.l01.q5.h: What does the label need to achieve?
graphic-design.l01.q5.e: The label's design succeeds by communicating clearly, not by decoration.

graphic-design.l02.q1.t: Orders elements by importance so the eye follows a sequence
graphic-design.l02.q1.h: Think about where to begin reading.
graphic-design.l02.q1.e: Hierarchy ranks information so viewers know where to start and what comes next.

graphic-design.l02.q2.p: Making everything bold and large is a reliable way to build hierarchy.
graphic-design.l02.q2.h: If everything stands out, what stands out?
graphic-design.l02.q2.e: Emphasizing everything removes the differences hierarchy depends on.

graphic-design.l02.q3.t: Which elements remain visible once details blur
graphic-design.l02.q3.p: In the squint test, what is the designer looking for?
graphic-design.l02.q3.e: What remains visible when blurred is what the design truly emphasizes.

graphic-design.l02.q4.p: Which is typically the strongest tool for building hierarchy?
graphic-design.l02.q4.h: Think about what you notice first from afar.
graphic-design.l02.q4.e: Larger elements are noticed first, making size the strongest cue.

graphic-design.l02.q5.p: Three levels of hierarchy, such as title, details and small print, are often enough for a simple flyer.
graphic-design.l02.q5.h: Simple pieces rarely need many levels.
graphic-design.l02.q5.e: A few clear levels usually organize a simple piece well.

graphic-design.l03.q1.p: If two elements are different, what does the contrast principle advise?
graphic-design.l03.q1.e: Contrast works when differences are decisive.

graphic-design.l03.q2.p: Repetition means consistently treating similar elements in the same way.
graphic-design.l03.q2.e: Repeating fonts, colors and styles unifies a design.

graphic-design.l03.q3.t: A timid contrast that looks like a mistake
graphic-design.l03.q3.p: A headline set at 18 points above 16-point text is an example of what?
graphic-design.l03.q3.e: The size difference is too small to read as intentional.

graphic-design.l03.q4.t: It records repeated choices so they stay consistent
graphic-design.l03.q4.p: Why does a style guide help a design?
graphic-design.l03.q4.e: Style guides capture repeated decisions that keep a piece unified.

graphic-design.l03.q5.p: Breaking an established pattern is a way to draw attention to one element.
graphic-design.l03.q5.e: A pattern broken against consistent surroundings stands out.

graphic-design.l04.q1.p: What does proximity mean in design?
graphic-design.l04.q1.e: Nearness signals that items belong together.

graphic-design.l04.q2.p: Almost-aligned elements look more intentional than clearly misaligned ones.
graphic-design.l04.q2.e: Near-alignment looks like an error, so choose clear alignments.

graphic-design.l04.q3.t: Every line starts in the same place
graphic-design.l04.q3.p: Why is flush-left, ragged-right text common for reading?
graphic-design.l04.q3.h: Think about finding the next line.
graphic-design.l04.q3.e: A consistent left edge helps the eye return to each line start.

graphic-design.l04.q4.t: Place them close together with a larger gap before other details
graphic-design.l04.q4.p: On a business card, how can spacing alone group the name with the job title?
graphic-design.l04.q4.e: Small gaps inside groups and larger gaps between groups reveal structure.

graphic-design.l04.q5.p: Spacing everything evenly makes the page structure clearer.
graphic-design.l04.q5.e: Even spacing fails to show which items are related.

graphic-design.l05.q1.t: A typeface is the design family; a font is one specific version of it
graphic-design.l05.q1.p: What is the difference between a typeface and a font?
graphic-design.l05.q1.e: Helvetica is a typeface; Helvetica Bold at a size is a font.

graphic-design.l05.q2.h: Think of a line on lined paper.
graphic-design.l05.q2.e: The baseline is the imaginary line on which most letters rest.

graphic-design.l05.q3.p: A descender is the part of a letter that drops below the baseline, as in g or y.

graphic-design.l05.q4.t: The enclosed or partly enclosed space within a letter
graphic-design.l05.q4.e: Counters are the open spaces inside letterforms.

graphic-design.l05.q5.p: Two fonts at the same point size can look different in size because of what?
graphic-design.l05.q5.h: Most lowercase letters are the body height.
graphic-design.l05.q5.e: A larger x-height makes lowercase text appear bigger at the same point size.

graphic-design.l06.q1.p: Which typeface group has no small finishing strokes?

graphic-design.l06.q2.p: Script typefaces are usually a good choice for long passages of body text.
graphic-design.l06.q2.e: Script faces are hard to read in long text.

graphic-design.l06.q3.t: Extreme contrast between thick and thin strokes
graphic-design.l06.q3.p: Which description fits Didone or modern serifs such as Bodoni?
graphic-design.l06.q3.e: Didones have hairline serifs and heavy verticals.

graphic-design.l06.q4.p: Which type group gives every character the same width?

graphic-design.l06.q5.p: Choosing a typeface class mainly sets a tone through its associations.
graphic-design.l06.q5.e: Classifications carry associations that shape the tone of a design.

graphic-design.l07.q1.t: A serif headline with a sans serif body
graphic-design.l07.q1.p: Which pairing reads as clearly intentional?
graphic-design.l07.q1.e: Clear contrast between styles reads as deliberate.

graphic-design.l07.q2.p: Using a single family in several weights can guarantee harmony.
graphic-design.l07.q2.h: The weights are designed to match.
graphic-design.l07.q2.e: One family's weights and styles are built to work together.

graphic-design.l07.q3.t: The difference looks like an accident
graphic-design.l07.q3.p: Why is pairing two similar-but-different typefaces risky?
graphic-design.l07.q3.e: Near-matches look like mistakes rather than choices.

graphic-design.l07.q4.p: A sensible limit for most projects is how many typefaces?
graphic-design.l07.q4.e: Few typefaces with clear jobs create consistency.

graphic-design.l07.q5.p: Similar x-heights and proportions can help fonts from different classes sit together comfortably.
graphic-design.l07.q5.e: Shared structure makes pairings look cohesive.

graphic-design.l08.q1.t: The vertical distance from one baseline to the next

graphic-design.l08.q2.t: Between a specific pair of letters
graphic-design.l08.q2.e: Kerning fine-tunes the gap between particular letter pairs.

graphic-design.l08.q3.p: A very long line length makes it harder to find the start of the next line.
graphic-design.l08.q3.h: Imagine reading across a wide page.
graphic-design.l08.q3.e: Overly long measures tire readers and cause lost places.

graphic-design.l08.q4.p: A commonly cited comfortable measure for body text is about how many characters per line?
graphic-design.l08.q4.h: Not too short, not too long.
graphic-design.l08.q4.e: Roughly 45 to 75 characters is a widely cited range, depending on context.

graphic-design.l08.q5.t: Space across a whole word or block of text
graphic-design.l08.q5.h: It affects a group of letters.
graphic-design.l08.q5.e: Tracking, or letter-spacing, adjusts spacing across multiple letters.

graphic-design.l09.q1.t: A limited set of defined text styles, each with a job
graphic-design.l09.q1.e: A type system defines styles for specific roles.

graphic-design.l09.q2.p: Defining paragraph styles lets you change a heading's look everywhere at once.
graphic-design.l09.q2.e: Styles centralize formatting so changes propagate.

graphic-design.l09.q3.p: Which text alignment is usually unsuitable for long paragraphs?
graphic-design.l09.q3.e: Centered text suits short formal lines but is tiring in long passages.

graphic-design.l09.q4.t: A stray line or word left alone at the start or end of a column or page
graphic-design.l09.q4.p: What is a widow or orphan in typesetting?

graphic-design.l09.q5.p: Combining bold, italic, underline and capitals on one heading is the recommended way to show emphasis.

graphic-design.l10.q1.e: Whitespace, or negative space, is empty area that gives content room.

graphic-design.l10.q2.p: Whitespace is wasted space that should be filled.
graphic-design.l10.q2.e: Space is an active tool for grouping, focus and tone.

graphic-design.l10.q3.t: Unlike elements balance each other, such as a small dark shape against a large pale area
graphic-design.l10.q3.h: Weight need not be equal in size.
graphic-design.l10.q3.e: Visual weight can be balanced by different kinds of elements.

graphic-design.l10.q4.p: Which is an example of micro whitespace?
graphic-design.l10.q4.e: Micro whitespace is the small space inside and between small elements.

graphic-design.l10.q5.p: Symmetrical balance typically feels more formal and calm.
graphic-design.l10.q5.e: Mirroring weight around an axis gives stability and formality.

graphic-design.l11.q1.p: What is a gutter in a column grid?
graphic-design.l11.q1.e: Gutters are the spaces between columns.

graphic-design.l11.q2.p: A grid helps elements look related and creates alignment automatically.
graphic-design.l11.q2.h: Elements snap to the same lines.
graphic-design.l11.q2.e: Shared lines produce alignment and repetition.

graphic-design.l11.q3.t: Lets lines of text in neighboring columns line up
graphic-design.l11.q3.p: What does a baseline grid do?
graphic-design.l11.q3.h: It is made of horizontal lines.
graphic-design.l11.q3.e: Text sits on evenly spaced baselines across columns.

graphic-design.l11.q4.t: Twelve divides evenly into twos, threes, fours and sixes
graphic-design.l11.q4.p: Why is a twelve-column grid popular?
graphic-design.l11.q4.e: Its many divisors support flexible column combinations.

graphic-design.l11.q5.p: Breaking the grid on purpose can attract attention because the rest of the layout is regular.

graphic-design.l12.q1.p: Which property of color most affects legibility?
graphic-design.l12.q1.e: Contrast in value is what makes content readable.

graphic-design.l12.q2.p: Complementary colors are located where on the color wheel?
graphic-design.l12.q2.e: Complements sit opposite and look vivid together.

graphic-design.l12.q3.p: The meaning of a color is identical in every culture.
graphic-design.l12.q3.e: Color meanings vary with culture and context.

graphic-design.l12.q4.p: Screens typically form color using which model?
graphic-design.l12.q4.e: Screens mix red, green and blue light.

graphic-design.l12.q5.t: CMYK inks cannot reproduce some colors RGB screens can
graphic-design.l12.q5.p: Why might a vivid screen color look duller in print?
graphic-design.l12.q5.e: Print and screen have different color ranges.

graphic-design.l13.q1.t: It should be scaled evenly, not stretched out of proportion
graphic-design.l13.q1.p: What should happen to an image that is resized?
graphic-design.l13.q1.e: Distorting proportions looks wrong; scale uniformly.

graphic-design.l13.q2.p: If a photo can be found online, you may use it freely in your design.
graphic-design.l13.q2.e: Images are usually protected, so you need a license, permission or public-domain status.

graphic-design.l13.q3.t: A soft overlay or a solid panel behind the text
graphic-design.l13.q3.p: Which helps text remain readable over a busy photo?
graphic-design.l13.q3.e: Overlays and panels create the needed contrast.

graphic-design.l13.q4.t: Does it communicate something words cannot or add real emotion?
graphic-design.l13.q4.p: What is a good test of whether an image earns its place?
graphic-design.l13.q4.e: Useful images add meaning, not mere filler.

graphic-design.l13.q5.p: A set of images should share similar lighting, color treatment and viewpoint to feel cohesive.
graphic-design.l13.q5.e: Consistent treatment makes images feel like they belong together.

graphic-design.l14.q1.p: Under WCAG level AA, what minimum contrast ratio applies to normal-size text?
graphic-design.l14.q1.h: It is a modest ratio but above 3.
graphic-design.l14.q1.e: WCAG AA requires at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text.

graphic-design.l14.q2.p: A chart should rely on color alone to separate good from bad.
graphic-design.l14.q2.e: Color alone excludes some viewers; add labels, icons or patterns.

graphic-design.l14.q3.t: Visible focus states on interactive elements
graphic-design.l14.q3.p: Which helps users who navigate with a keyboard?
graphic-design.l14.q3.h: They need to see where they are.
graphic-design.l14.q3.e: Focus indicators show the active element.

graphic-design.l14.q4.t: Screen readers can then convey them to users
graphic-design.l14.q4.p: Why do meaningful images need text alternatives on the web?
graphic-design.l14.q4.h: Think who cannot see the image.
graphic-design.l14.q4.e: Alt text lets assistive technology describe images.

graphic-design.l14.q5.p: Accessible design benefits many people beyond those with permanent disabilities.
graphic-design.l14.q5.h: Think of glare on a phone.
graphic-design.l14.q5.e: Clear contrast and sizing help everyone in difficult conditions.

graphic-design.l15.q1.t: The organization's name set in distinctive lettering
graphic-design.l15.q1.e: Wordmarks present the name as the logo.

graphic-design.l15.q2.p: A logo and a brand are the same thing.
graphic-design.l15.q2.e: A brand is the full set of impressions; the logo is one identifying mark.

graphic-design.l15.q3.t: To confirm they stay recognizable when color and detail are lost
graphic-design.l15.q3.p: Why do designers test logos small and in black and white?
graphic-design.l15.q3.e: A strong logo works across sizes and in one color.

graphic-design.l15.q4.t: Clear space, minimum size, colors, fonts and misuse examples
graphic-design.l15.q4.p: What does a brand guidelines document usually specify?
graphic-design.l15.q4.e: Guidelines record how the identity should be applied.

graphic-design.l15.q5.t: A toolkit of logo, color, type, imagery and rules applied consistently
graphic-design.l15.q5.h: It is broader than a logo.
graphic-design.l15.q5.e: An identity system extends the logo into a coordinated toolkit.

graphic-design.l16.q1.p: What should a designer decide first for a poster?
graphic-design.l16.q1.e: A poster that says everything says nothing, so choose a dominant message.

graphic-design.l16.q2.p: A poster usually gets only a glance from viewers.
graphic-design.l16.q2.e: Posters must work quickly at a distance.

graphic-design.l16.q3.t: A strong focal point with contrast of scale
graphic-design.l16.q3.p: Which helps a poster grab attention?
graphic-design.l16.q3.e: A bold focal element creates fast attention.

graphic-design.l16.q4.t: People move from the dominant element to the next strongest

graphic-design.l16.q5.p: A poster also needs a findable call to action, such as a web address.
graphic-design.l16.q5.e: Without a clear next step, interest may be wasted.

graphic-design.l17.q2.t: A line at the top of each page carrying the book or chapter title

graphic-design.l17.q3.p: Printed books are made from sheets folded into signatures, so page counts are planned in multiples.
graphic-design.l17.q3.e: Folded sheets produce groups of pages.

graphic-design.l17.q4.t: Text can be lost in the binding fold
graphic-design.l17.q4.p: Why does the inner margin often need extra room?
graphic-design.l17.q4.h: Look at the center of a spread.
graphic-design.l17.q4.e: Extra gutter space keeps text readable near the binding.

graphic-design.l17.q5.p: In e-books with reflowable text, the designer controls exact page layout as in print.
graphic-design.l17.q5.h: Text adjusts to the reader's screen.
graphic-design.l17.q5.e: Reflowable text puts structure and styles in focus, not fixed pages.

graphic-design.l18.q1.t: A flat template showing a package's cuts, folds and glue areas
graphic-design.l18.q1.e: Dielines guide artwork placement on packaging.

graphic-design.l18.q2.p: Packaging has to protect the product, inform and sell all at once.
graphic-design.l18.q2.e: Packaging serves multiple functions at the same time.

graphic-design.l18.q3.t: Folds and cutting can distort or clip it
graphic-design.l18.q3.p: Why keep important text away from folds and cut edges?
graphic-design.l18.q3.e: Text near folds or cuts risks being damaged or hidden.

graphic-design.l18.q4.p: Using one color per flavor with an identical layout is an example of what?
graphic-design.l18.q4.e: Shared layout repeats while color differentiates.

graphic-design.l18.q5.p: Required packaging information is usually set by rules that vary by product and country.
graphic-design.l18.q5.e: Designers follow specifications rather than assuming.

graphic-design.l19.q1.t: A layout adapts to different screen sizes
graphic-design.l19.q1.e: Responsive layouts reflow for different devices.

graphic-design.l19.q2.p: Interface components like buttons should look consistent throughout a product.

graphic-design.l19.q3.t: A shared library of components, colors and type styles

graphic-design.l19.q4.t: So they know the action worked
graphic-design.l19.q4.p: Why give users feedback after they tap a button?
graphic-design.l19.q4.e: Visible feedback confirms that an action registered.

graphic-design.l19.q5.p: UI design is the visual layer within the wider discipline of UX design.
graphic-design.l19.q5.e: UX covers how a product works for users; UI is its visual layer.

graphic-design.l20.q1.p: Which graphics are made of mathematical descriptions of lines and curves?
graphic-design.l20.q1.e: Vector graphics use formulas, not pixels.

graphic-design.l20.q2.p: Enlarging a raster image beyond its original pixel size makes it look soft or blocky.
graphic-design.l20.q2.e: Raster images are tied to a fixed number of pixels.

graphic-design.l20.q3.p: Which file type is a good fit for a photograph on a web page?

graphic-design.l20.q4.p: Which format supports lossless compression and transparency?
graphic-design.l20.q4.e: PNG is lossless and supports transparency.

graphic-design.l20.q5.p: A logo built as vector artwork can be used from a tiny icon to a billboard without losing sharpness.

graphic-design.l21.q1.t: Artwork extending past the trim line so edges print cleanly
graphic-design.l21.q1.e: Bleed prevents white slivers if the cut shifts.

graphic-design.l21.q2.p: Which color mode do most commercial print jobs use?
graphic-design.l21.q2.e: Commercial printing generally uses cyan, magenta, yellow and black.

graphic-design.l21.q3.p: A typical target resolution for photos in print is about 300 ppi at the printed size.
graphic-design.l21.q3.e: 300 ppi is a typical target, though printers' specifications vary.

graphic-design.l21.q4.t: A slightly shifted cut will not clip it
graphic-design.l21.q4.p: Why keep important text inside a safe margin?
graphic-design.l21.q4.e: Safe margins protect content from trimming variation.

graphic-design.l21.q5.p: You should always ask the printer for their specifications because requirements vary.
graphic-design.l21.q5.e: Printers set their own bleed, color and file requirements.

graphic-design.l22.q1.p: In which country did the Swiss Style develop?
graphic-design.l22.q1.e: It emerged in Switzerland, centered on Zurich and Basel.

graphic-design.l22.q2.p: Swiss Style designers favored mathematical grids and sans serif type.
graphic-design.l22.q2.e: Grids and sans serif typography are hallmarks of the style.

graphic-design.l22.q3.p: Which designer is known for grid-based posters and writing on grid systems?
graphic-design.l22.q3.h: Think of the Zurich poster designer.
graphic-design.l22.q3.e: Müller-Brockmann is closely associated with grid systems.

graphic-design.l22.q4.t: Design could be a neutral, universal means of communication
graphic-design.l22.q4.p: What belief underlay the Swiss Style?
graphic-design.l22.q4.e: Practitioners aimed for objective, orderly information design.

graphic-design.l22.q5.p: Later critics argued that strict neutrality can feel cold and reflect particular cultural assumptions.
graphic-design.l22.q5.e: Critiques of universalism and coldness are part of the discussion.

graphic-design.l23.q1.t: A statement of goals, audience, deliverables, constraints, budget and schedule
graphic-design.l23.q1.e: The brief defines what success looks like.

graphic-design.l23.q2.t: The date is hard to find, and the audience needs it first
graphic-design.l23.q2.p: Which is a more useful critique comment?
graphic-design.l23.q2.e: Useful critique refers to goals and specifics.

graphic-design.l23.q3.p: Designers usually try only one idea because the first is best.
graphic-design.l23.q3.e: Generating many options usually produces better results.

graphic-design.l23.q4.t: It sets expectations and limits endless changes
graphic-design.l23.q4.p: Why agree on the number of revision rounds in advance?
graphic-design.l23.q4.e: Defined rounds keep the project manageable.

graphic-design.l23.q5.p: Projects can loop back to earlier stages as feedback arrives.
graphic-design.l23.q5.e: Iteration is a normal part of design.

graphic-design.l24.q1.t: Hiding a cancel button to discourage canceling
graphic-design.l24.q1.p: Which is an example of a dark pattern?
graphic-design.l24.q1.e: Dark patterns steer users against their interests.

graphic-design.l24.q2.p: A chart with a misleading axis can exaggerate differences.

graphic-design.l24.q3.t: Licensed software with terms that may differ for web, app and print
graphic-design.l24.q3.p: Fonts are best understood as what?
graphic-design.l24.q3.e: Font licenses vary, so use them according to their terms.

graphic-design.l24.q4.t: A few strong projects with the problem, your role, process and result
graphic-design.l24.q4.e: Explained, selective work is more convincing.

graphic-design.l24.q5.p: Designers agree universally that unpaid speculative pitches are acceptable.
graphic-design.l24.q5.e: Some argue against spec work, while others accept it in limited cases.

history-arab-world.l01.q1.p: Which term mainly describes a person who speaks Arabic as a first language and identifies with Arab heritage?
history-arab-world.l01.q1.h: Think language and culture, not religion.
history-arab-world.l01.q1.e: Arab is mainly a linguistic and cultural description.

history-arab-world.l01.q2.e: Many Arabs belong to Christian, Druze, Jewish and other communities.

history-arab-world.l01.q3.t: Most Muslims live outside the Arab world
history-arab-world.l01.q3.p: Which is true about the world's Muslim population?
history-arab-world.l01.q3.h: Think of Indonesia, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
history-arab-world.l01.q3.e: Countries such as Indonesia, Pakistan and Bangladesh have more Muslims than any Arab country.

history-arab-world.l01.q4.p: Which language is mainly spoken in Iran?
history-arab-world.l01.q4.h: It is a different language from the one spoken in Iraq.
history-arab-world.l01.q4.e: Iran is mostly Persian-speaking, though it has many minority languages.

history-arab-world.l01.q5.p: The term Middle East is a modern geographic label that has no single fixed definition.
history-arab-world.l01.q5.h: Think about who invented the term and when.
history-arab-world.l01.q5.e: The label arose in the early twentieth century and is used with varying boundaries.

history-arab-world.l02.q1.p: What does the word Mesopotamia mean in Greek?
history-arab-world.l02.q1.h: Think of the Tigris and Euphrates.
history-arab-world.l02.q1.e: It means the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

history-arab-world.l02.q2.p: Cuneiform was a writing system made by pressing a reed stylus into clay.
history-arab-world.l02.q2.e: Cuneiform marks were pressed into clay tablets and used for accounts, letters and laws.

history-arab-world.l02.q3.p: Which people developed an alphabet that is an ancestor of the Greek and Latin alphabets?
history-arab-world.l02.q3.h: They traded by sea from Tyre and Sidon.
history-arab-world.l02.q3.e: The Phoenician alphabet influenced Greek and, through it, Latin.

history-arab-world.l02.q4.p: Which ruler took Babylon in 539 BCE, bringing it into the Persian Empire?
history-arab-world.l02.q4.e: Cyrus of Persia took Babylon in 539 BCE.

history-arab-world.l02.q5.p: When Muslim armies arrived in the 600s CE they were entering lands with no earlier tradition of states or record keeping.
history-arab-world.l02.q5.h: Recall the long history of taxes and bureaucracy.
history-arab-world.l02.q5.e: The region had ancient traditions of states, taxation and writing, which later rulers often built on.

history-arab-world.l03.q1.t: Herding peoples who moved with camels and flocks
history-arab-world.l03.q1.e: Bedouin were nomadic or semi-nomadic herders organised in tribes and clans.

history-arab-world.l03.q2.p: Which Arab people built the rock city of Petra?
history-arab-world.l03.q2.h: Their kingdom was annexed by Rome in 106 CE.
history-arab-world.l03.q2.e: Petra was the Nabataean capital in present-day Jordan.

history-arab-world.l03.q3.p: Mecca was home to the Kaaba sanctuary and was dominated by the tribe of Quraysh before Islam.
history-arab-world.l03.q3.h: Recall the trading town of the Hijaz.
history-arab-world.l03.q3.e: Quraysh controlled Mecca and its sanctuary.

history-arab-world.l03.q4.t: Much was written down only generations later
history-arab-world.l03.q4.p: Why do historians treat collections of pre-Islamic poetry with care?
history-arab-world.l03.q4.e: Because poems were recited from memory first, later collections may have been changed.

history-arab-world.l03.q5.p: Pre-Islamic Arabia had only one religion.
history-arab-world.l03.q5.h: Think of the different communities named in the lesson.
history-arab-world.l03.q5.e: Arabia had tribal religions, Jewish and Christian communities and some individual seekers of a single God.

history-arab-world.l04.q1.t: Muhammad and his followers moving from Mecca to Medina
history-arab-world.l04.q1.p: What does the Hijra of 622 CE refer to?
history-arab-world.l04.q1.h: It marks year one of a calendar.
history-arab-world.l04.q1.e: The migration to Medina begins the Islamic calendar.

history-arab-world.l04.q2.p: Muslims regard the Quran as the word of God.
history-arab-world.l04.q2.h: Consider how Muslims understand the revelations.
history-arab-world.l04.q2.e: The Quran is understood by Muslims as divine revelation.

history-arab-world.l04.q3.p: Which is NOT one of the Five Pillars of Islam?
history-arab-world.l04.q3.h: Look for the item that is not a duty at all.
history-arab-world.l04.q3.e: The pillars are the declaration of faith, prayer, almsgiving, fasting and pilgrimage.

history-arab-world.l04.q4.t: Reports of the Prophet's words and actions
history-arab-world.l04.q4.p: Hadith are best described as which kind of source?
history-arab-world.l04.q4.h: They were collected after his lifetime.
history-arab-world.l04.q4.e: Hadith are reports written down generations after Muhammad.

history-arab-world.l04.q5.p: The lesson says that believers and academic historians approach early sources in exactly the same way.
history-arab-world.l04.q5.e: They often approach reliability differently, so early events are described as traditionally reported.

history-arab-world.l05.q1.p: Who was the first caliph after Muhammad's death in 632?
history-arab-world.l05.q1.e: Abu Bakr was the first of the Rashidun caliphs.

history-arab-world.l05.q2.p: The word caliph comes from the Arabic for successor.

history-arab-world.l05.q3.t: Byzantium and Persia had been exhausted by a long war
history-arab-world.l05.q3.p: Which factor helped the early expansion, according to historians?
history-arab-world.l05.q3.e: Two exhausted empires were easier to defeat.

history-arab-world.l05.q4.p: What status allowed Christians and Jews to practise their religion under Muslim rule in return for a tax?
history-arab-world.l05.q4.e: Dhimma gave protected non-Muslims religious freedom with a tax.

history-arab-world.l05.q5.p: Most conquered people were forced to convert to Islam immediately.
history-arab-world.l05.q5.h: Consider the lesson on gradual conversion.
history-arab-world.l05.q5.e: Conversion and Arabisation happened gradually over centuries.

history-arab-world.l06.q1.p: What does Shia mean in origin?
history-arab-world.l06.q1.h: It refers to Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law.
history-arab-world.l06.q1.e: Shia comes from shiat Ali, the party of Ali.

history-arab-world.l06.q2.h: It is in Iraq and has a major Shia shrine.
history-arab-world.l06.q2.e: Husayn was killed at Karbala, commemorated on Ashura.

history-arab-world.l06.q3.p: Sunni and Shia Muslims both accept the Quran and the Five Pillars.
history-arab-world.l06.q3.h: Their differences concern leadership and authority.
history-arab-world.l06.q3.e: The two branches share core beliefs and practices.

history-arab-world.l06.q4.p: Which of these is a Sunni law school?
history-arab-world.l06.q4.h: Three of these are Shia groups.
history-arab-world.l06.q4.e: Hanafi is one of four Sunni schools, with Maliki, Shafii and Hanbali.

history-arab-world.l06.q5.p: After Ali was assassinated in 661, Muawiya became ruler.
history-arab-world.l06.q5.h: Recall how the first fitna ended.
history-arab-world.l06.q5.e: The death of Ali in 661 left Muawiya in power, founding the Umayyad dynasty.

history-arab-world.l07.q1.p: Which city was the capital of the Umayyads?

history-arab-world.l07.q2.t: Arabic became the language of administration
history-arab-world.l07.q2.e: Arabic replaced Greek and Persian in administration and appeared on coins.

history-arab-world.l07.q3.p: The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem was completed in 691-692.
history-arab-world.l07.q3.h: It is the oldest surviving major Islamic monument.
history-arab-world.l07.q3.e: It dates from Abd al-Malik's reign.

history-arab-world.l07.q4.e: Mawali were non-Arab converts, who often felt unequal.

history-arab-world.l07.q5.p: An Umayyad prince escaped the 750 revolution and founded a state at Cordoba.
history-arab-world.l07.q5.e: He founded the Umayyad state in al-Andalus in 756.

history-arab-world.l08.q1.h: He was an early Abbasid caliph.
history-arab-world.l08.q1.e: Al-Mansur founded the city on the Tigris.

history-arab-world.l08.q2.p: The Round City was the early design of Baghdad.
history-arab-world.l08.q2.e: The early city was laid out as a circle.

history-arab-world.l08.q3.p: What group took control of Baghdad in 945 while the caliph remained as a symbolic leader?
history-arab-world.l08.q3.h: They were a Shia family from Iran.
history-arab-world.l08.q3.e: The Buyids held real power over the Abbasid caliph.

history-arab-world.l08.q4.p: Which development lowered the cost of books and records in the Abbasid world?
history-arab-world.l08.q4.h: Think of the material that replaced parchment.
history-arab-world.l08.q4.e: Paper manufacturing spread in the eighth and ninth centuries.

history-arab-world.l08.q5.p: The Abbasid caliphate ended in Baghdad because of the Ottomans.

history-arab-world.l09.q1.t: Translating Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic
history-arab-world.l09.q1.p: What was the Abbasid translation movement mainly about?
history-arab-world.l09.q1.h: It involved paid scholars in Baghdad.
history-arab-world.l09.q1.e: Scholars translated works from several languages into Arabic.

history-arab-world.l09.q2.p: Historians agree on exactly what the House of Wisdom was.
history-arab-world.l09.q2.h: The lesson says they debate this.
history-arab-world.l09.q2.e: Some see an academy and others a library or workshop.

history-arab-world.l09.q3.t: A Christian translator of Greek medical works
history-arab-world.l09.q3.e: He was a Christian scholar famous for translations.

history-arab-world.l09.q4.p: Which caliph is associated with the House of Wisdom?
