history-europe.l18.q2.h: His name is attached to a unit of force.
history-europe.l18.q2.e: Newton's Principia explained falling objects and planetary orbits with mathematical laws.

history-europe.l18.q3.p: What did Galileo observe with his telescope that supported Copernicus's view?
history-europe.l18.q3.h: It showed that not everything orbits the Earth.
history-europe.l18.q3.e: Observing moons orbiting Jupiter showed that some bodies circle something other than the Earth.

history-europe.l18.q4.t: Personal rivalries, politics and disputes about interpretation also mattered, so it was not simply science versus religion
history-europe.l18.q4.p: How do historians often qualify the story of Galileo and the Church?
history-europe.l18.q4.h: The lesson says many scientists were devout.
history-europe.l18.q4.e: Historians stress that the conflict was more complex than a simple science versus religion story.

history-europe.l18.q5.p: Historians all agree the Scientific Revolution was a sudden event with no earlier roots.
history-europe.l18.q5.h: The lesson mentions Greek and Islamic scholarship.
history-europe.l18.q5.e: It unfolded over a century and drew on earlier work, so scholars debate the term revolution.

history-europe.l19.q1.p: Louis XIV built the palace of Versailles.
history-europe.l19.q1.h: He is the most famous absolutist monarch.
history-europe.l19.q1.e: Louis XIV built Versailles and kept nobles close at court.

history-europe.l19.q2.p: Which thinker argued in The Spirit of the Laws (1748) for dividing government power into separate branches?
history-europe.l19.q2.h: The title of the book is a clue.
history-europe.l19.q2.e: Montesquieu argued for separation of powers.

history-europe.l19.q3.p: Which city did Peter the Great found in 1703?
history-europe.l19.q3.h: It was a new Russian capital on the Baltic.
history-europe.l19.q3.e: Peter founded St Petersburg and modernised the Russian army.

history-europe.l19.q4.t: A ruler who adopted some Enlightenment reforms while keeping supreme power
history-europe.l19.q4.h: Frederick II and Catherine II are examples.
history-europe.l19.q4.e: Such rulers reformed some practices but kept their authority.

history-europe.l19.q5.t: Many thinkers accepted slavery or prejudice, while others such as Mary Wollstonecraft argued for wider rights
history-europe.l19.q5.p: Which statement best reflects the limits of the Enlightenment discussed in the lesson?
history-europe.l19.q5.h: The lesson says tensions became central in later revolutions.
history-europe.l19.q5.e: The ideas of universal rights clashed with continuing exclusions, which later movements challenged.

history-europe.l20.q1.p: The Bastille was stormed on 14 July 1789.
history-europe.l20.q1.h: It is a French national holiday.
history-europe.l20.q1.e: Crowds attacked the Bastille prison on 14 July 1789.

history-europe.l20.q2.p: Which general seized power in France in 1799 and crowned himself emperor in 1804?
history-europe.l20.q2.h: He was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
history-europe.l20.q2.e: Napoleon took power in 1799 and became emperor in 1804.

history-europe.l20.q3.t: A period of repression under the Committee of Public Safety with many executions
history-europe.l20.q3.p: What was the Terror of 1793 to 1794?
history-europe.l20.q3.h: Robespierre was one of its leaders.
history-europe.l20.q3.e: The government killed or imprisoned many perceived enemies during war and internal revolt.

history-europe.l20.q4.t: Liberty and equality before the law
history-europe.l20.q4.p: What did the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen proclaim?
history-europe.l20.q4.e: It proclaimed liberty and legal equality, though women and enslaved colonial people were not given the same rights.

history-europe.l20.q5.t: It created Haiti, the first state founded by a successful slave revolt
history-europe.l20.q5.p: What was historically significant about the revolution in Saint-Domingue that began in 1791?
history-europe.l20.q5.e: Enslaved people rose and created independent Haiti in 1804.

history-europe.l21.q1.p: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain.
history-europe.l21.q1.h: Think about steam engines and textile mills.
history-europe.l21.q1.e: Britain led industrialisation from the later eighteenth century.

history-europe.l21.q2.p: Which industry was among the first to move from homes to factories?
history-europe.l21.q2.h: Think about spinning and weaving machines.
history-europe.l21.q2.e: Spinning and weaving machines moved production into factories.

history-europe.l21.q3.t: Limited children's working hours in textile mills
history-europe.l21.q3.p: What did the Factory Act of 1833 do?
history-europe.l21.q3.e: It restricted children's hours in textile mills, but enforcement was weak initially.

history-europe.l21.q4.t: Historians cite several factors, with no single cause accepted by everyone
history-europe.l21.q4.p: Which statement about why Britain led industrialisation fits the lesson?
history-europe.l21.q4.h: The lesson lists coal, markets, capital and empire.
history-europe.l21.q4.e: Explanations include coal, markets, capital, commercial culture and colonial resources.

history-europe.l21.q5.p: Economic historians have settled the question of how quickly living standards rose in early industrial Britain.
history-europe.l21.q5.h: The lesson says it is still argued.
history-europe.l21.q5.e: Whether living standards rose quickly or only after decades is still debated.

history-europe.l22.q1.p: Nationalism is the belief that people sharing language or culture should form their own political community.
history-europe.l22.q1.h: Look at the first sentence of the lesson.
history-europe.l22.q1.e: That is the basic definition of nationalism used in the lesson.

history-europe.l22.q2.p: Which year is known for a wave of revolutions across Europe called the Springtime of the Peoples?
history-europe.l22.q2.h: It is also the year of The Communist Manifesto.
history-europe.l22.q2.e: Revolutions swept France, the Habsburg lands, the German states and Italy in 1848.

history-europe.l22.q3.p: What happened to most of the 1848 revolutions within a year or two?
history-europe.l22.q3.h: The lesson calls them largely failed in the short term.
history-europe.l22.q3.e: Most were crushed or fizzled, though some lasting changes remained.

history-europe.l22.q4.p: Which lasting change in the Habsburg lands came out of 1848?
history-europe.l22.q4.e: Serfdom was ended in the Habsburg lands even though the revolutions failed.

history-europe.l22.q5.t: Belgium became independent from the Netherlands in 1830
history-europe.l22.q5.p: Which pairing of country and event in the lesson is correct?
history-europe.l22.q5.h: It was a revolution that created a new kingdom.
history-europe.l22.q5.e: In 1830 Belgium broke from the Netherlands and became independent.

history-europe.l23.q1.p: The German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 at Versailles.
history-europe.l23.q1.e: Wilhelm I was proclaimed emperor on 18 January 1871 in the Hall of Mirrors.

history-europe.l23.q2.p: Who led the volunteer expedition that overthrew the Bourbon kingdom in southern Italy in 1860?
history-europe.l23.q2.h: He sailed to Sicily with about a thousand men.
history-europe.l23.q2.e: Garibaldi's volunteers helped bring the south into the new Italy.

history-europe.l23.q3.t: Politics based on practical power rather than ideals
history-europe.l23.q3.e: The term describes pragmatic politics focused on power.

history-europe.l23.q4.p: Which war excluded Austria from German affairs?
history-europe.l23.q4.h: It occurred before the war with France.

history-europe.l23.q5.t: Both popular nationalism and the decisions of statesmen and armies mattered
history-europe.l23.q5.p: Which statement fits the lesson's account of the debate about unification?
history-europe.l23.q5.h: The lesson says both factors played a role.
history-europe.l23.q5.e: Historians discuss how nationalism and state power combined, and note minorities were marginalised.

history-europe.l24.q1.p: By 1914, European powers governed nearly all of Africa, with Ethiopia and Liberia the main exceptions.
history-europe.l24.q1.e: Africa saw the most dramatic change, from limited control in 1870 to nearly complete control by 1914.

history-europe.l24.q2.p: Who ran the Congo Free State as a personal possession?
history-europe.l24.q2.e: Leopold II controlled the Congo Free State until the Belgian state took it over in 1908.

history-europe.l24.q3.t: Set diplomatic rules for claiming African territory among European powers
history-europe.l24.q3.p: What did the Berlin Conference of 1884 and 1885 do?
history-europe.l24.q3.e: It formalised competition, though it did not itself divide Africa.

history-europe.l24.q4.p: Which African state defeated an Italian army at Adwa in 1896?

history-europe.l24.q5.t: The British Crown took direct control from the East India Company
history-europe.l24.q5.p: What happened in 1858 after the rebellion of 1857 in India?
history-europe.l24.q5.e: After the rebellion, the Crown replaced Company rule.

history-europe.l25.q1.p: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo took place on 28 June 1914.
history-europe.l25.q1.h: It happened in the summer of 1914.
history-europe.l25.q1.e: Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne.

history-europe.l25.q2.p: When did the armistice that ended the fighting on the Western Front take effect?
history-europe.l25.q2.h: It is remembered each year on Armistice Day.
history-europe.l25.q2.e: The armistice took effect on 11 November 1918.

history-europe.l25.q3.t: To accept responsibility for the war
history-europe.l25.q3.p: What did Article 231 of the Treaty of Versailles require of Germany?
history-europe.l25.q3.h: It is often called the war guilt clause.
history-europe.l25.q3.e: Germany had to accept responsibility, which was used to justify reparations.

history-europe.l25.q4.p: Which four empires ended as a result of the war?
history-europe.l25.q4.h: Think of the losers and of Russia.
history-europe.l25.q4.e: All four empires collapsed by the end of the war and its aftermath.

history-europe.l25.q5.t: They debate it, with some stressing Germany's decisions and others the shared failures of all the powers
history-europe.l25.q5.p: How do historians view responsibility for the war?
history-europe.l25.q5.h: The lesson says the debate continues.
history-europe.l25.q5.e: Historians still debate how to apportion responsibility.

history-europe.l26.q1.p: The Bolsheviks seized power in Petrograd in October 1917 under Vladimir Lenin.
history-europe.l26.q1.h: It is dated by the Julian calendar.
history-europe.l26.q1.e: The Bolsheviks took power in the second revolution of 1917.

history-europe.l26.q2.t: A council of workers and soldiers that shared power with the Provisional Government
history-europe.l26.q2.e: It was a council that rivalled the Provisional Government's authority.

history-europe.l26.q3.t: Russia still used the older Julian calendar
history-europe.l26.q3.p: Why do dates for the Russian revolutions differ between sources?
history-europe.l26.q3.h: The calendars differed by about two weeks.
history-europe.l26.q3.e: February and October in the Julian calendar correspond to March and November in the Western calendar.

history-europe.l26.q4.t: A system of labour camps in the Soviet Union
history-europe.l26.q4.h: It was used in the Great Terror era.
history-europe.l26.q4.e: Many people were sent to labour camps called the Gulag.

history-europe.l26.q5.p: All historians and governments use exactly the same classification of the Ukrainian famine of 1932 and 1933.
history-europe.l26.q5.h: The lesson says the genocide classification is debated.
history-europe.l26.q5.e: Many historians and governments call it a genocide, the Holodomor, but the classification is debated.

history-europe.l27.q1.p: Hitler was appointed chancellor by President Hindenburg on 30 January 1933.
history-europe.l27.q1.h: He was appointed rather than elected by a majority.
history-europe.l27.q1.e: The Nazi Party never won a majority in a free election but Hitler was appointed chancellor.

history-europe.l27.q2.t: A show of force by Mussolini's followers, after which he became prime minister
history-europe.l27.q2.p: What was the March on Rome of October 1922?
history-europe.l27.q2.e: Mussolini was appointed prime minister by the king and soon built a one-party dictatorship.

history-europe.l27.q3.p: Which economic event beginning in 1929 helped extremist parties gain support in Weimar Germany?
history-europe.l27.q3.h: It followed a stock market crash.
history-europe.l27.q3.e: Mass unemployment from the Depression helped extremist parties gain support.

history-europe.l27.q4.t: Laws stripping Jews of German citizenship and defining them by ancestry
history-europe.l27.q4.p: What were the Nuremberg Laws of 1935?
history-europe.l27.q4.h: They were passed under the Nazi regime.
history-europe.l27.q4.e: They began a legal definition of Jews by ancestry and removed citizenship.

history-europe.l27.q5.t: Trying to avoid war by granting concessions to Germany
history-europe.l27.q5.p: What was appeasement, as practised by Britain and France?
history-europe.l27.q5.h: The Munich Agreement is an example.
history-europe.l27.q5.e: Appeasement meant making concessions, such as allowing Germany to take the Sudetenland.

history-europe.l28.q1.h: Britain and France declared war two days later.
history-europe.l28.q1.e: The invasion began the Second World War in Europe.

history-europe.l28.q2.p: Roughly how many Jews were murdered in the Holocaust?
history-europe.l28.q2.h: It is the figure used by historians for the whole genocide.
history-europe.l28.q2.e: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murdered about six million Jews.

history-europe.l28.q3.p: Which conference in January 1942 coordinated the plan for the murder of Europe's Jews?
history-europe.l28.q3.e: Officials met at Wannsee to coordinate the plan.

history-europe.l28.q4.e: The Allied landings in Normandy helped turn the war.

history-europe.l28.q5.t: Roma and Sinti, people with disabilities and many Soviet prisoners of war were also murdered
history-europe.l28.q5.p: Which statement about the other victims of Nazi persecution is correct?
history-europe.l28.q5.e: The Nazis murdered or persecuted many other groups alongside the genocide of the Jews.

history-europe.l29.q1.p: The Berlin Wall was built by East Germany in 1961.
history-europe.l29.q1.h: It stopped citizens fleeing to the west.
history-europe.l29.q1.e: East Germany built the wall to stop emigration.

history-europe.l29.q2.p: Which plan of 1948 provided billions of dollars to rebuild Western European economies?
history-europe.l29.q2.h: It was named after a U.S. Secretary of State.
history-europe.l29.q2.e: The Marshall Plan supported recovery in Western Europe.

history-europe.l29.q3.t: Rival military alliances, Western and Soviet-led
history-europe.l29.q3.p: What did NATO and the Warsaw Pact represent?
history-europe.l29.q3.e: NATO formed in 1949 and the Warsaw Pact answered it in 1955.

history-europe.l29.q4.p: What happened to the Hungarian uprising of 1956?
history-europe.l29.q4.h: Moscow did not tolerate challenges to its bloc.
history-europe.l29.q4.e: The Soviet Union crushed the revolt.

history-europe.l29.q5.p: What did the Helsinki Accords of 1975 include that dissidents later invoked?
history-europe.l29.q5.e: Dissidents in the East cited the human rights commitments.

history-europe.l30.q1.p: India and Pakistan became independent in 1947.
history-europe.l30.q1.h: It was the end of British rule in South Asia.
history-europe.l30.q1.e: Partition caused mass migration and communal violence.

history-europe.l30.q2.p: Which colony was the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence from Britain, in 1957?
history-europe.l30.q2.h: It was named after an old African empire.
history-europe.l30.q2.e: Ghana's independence in 1957 inspired other African movements.

history-europe.l30.q3.t: Britain and France, with Israel, attacked Egypt and withdrew under American and Soviet pressure
history-europe.l30.q3.p: What was the Suez Crisis of 1956?
history-europe.l30.q3.e: The failure signalled that Britain and France no longer acted as great powers.

history-europe.l30.q4.p: How did France's war in Algeria end?
history-europe.l30.q4.e: A brutal war ended in Algerian independence.

history-europe.l30.q5.p: Portuguese colonies in Africa gained independence after a revolution in Portugal in 1974.
history-europe.l30.q5.h: The empire lasted longer than Britain's or France's.
history-europe.l30.q5.e: The 1974 revolution led to independence for Portugal's African colonies.

history-europe.l31.q1.p: The Treaty of Rome of 1957 created the European Economic Community.
history-europe.l31.q1.h: It was signed by six countries.
history-europe.l31.q1.e: It created a common market among France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

history-europe.l31.q2.p: Which treaty signed in 1992 created the European Union?
history-europe.l31.q2.h: It is named after a Dutch city.
history-europe.l31.q2.e: Maastricht created the EU and set the path to a common currency.

history-europe.l31.q3.p: What did the Schuman proposal of 9 May 1950 suggest?
history-europe.l31.q3.e: It aimed to make war between France and Germany unthinkable and led to the ECSC in 1951.

history-europe.l31.q4.p: In which year did the UK formally leave the EU?
history-europe.l31.q4.h: A referendum took place four years earlier.
history-europe.l31.q4.e: The UK left on 31 January 2020 after the June 2016 referendum.

history-europe.l31.q5.t: Someone who wants a stronger union
history-europe.l31.q5.p: What is a federalist, as used in the lesson?
history-europe.l31.q5.h: It contrasts with preferring cooperation between states.
history-europe.l31.q5.e: Federalists want deeper integration, while others prefer intergovernmental cooperation.

history-europe.l32.q1.p: The Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989.
history-europe.l32.q1.h: It followed weeks of protests in East Germany.
history-europe.l32.q1.e: The opening of the wall became a symbol of the end of the Cold War division.

history-europe.l32.q2.h: It followed the fall of the Wall.

history-europe.l32.q3.p: What did the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev's policy of glasnost mean?
history-europe.l32.q3.e: Glasnost meant openness and perestroika meant restructuring.

history-europe.l32.q4.t: About 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed, an act ruled to be genocide by international courts
history-europe.l32.q4.p: What happened at Srebrenica in July 1995?
history-europe.l32.q4.h: It was part of the Bosnian war.
history-europe.l32.q4.e: Bosnian Serb forces killed about 8,000 people.

history-europe.l32.q5.t: They debate how much the West, Gorbachev or the peoples of Eastern Europe drove the changes
history-europe.l32.q5.p: Which statement best reflects the historians' debate over 1989 described in the lesson?
history-europe.l32.q5.h: The lesson mentions economic stagnation and popular action.
history-europe.l32.q5.e: Historians weigh popular action, Gorbachev's reforms, Western pressure and long-term economic problems.

history-north-america.l01.q1.t: Hundreds of distinct nations with many languages and ways of life
history-north-america.l01.q1.p: Which description best fits North America in 1400?
history-north-america.l01.q1.e: The continent held many separate societies with different languages, economies and governments.

history-north-america.l01.q2.p: All Native peoples of North America spoke the same language and lived the same way.
history-north-america.l01.q2.h: Compare the Arctic with the Southwest.
history-north-america.l01.q2.e: There were hundreds of languages and very different economies, from Arctic hunting to desert farming.

history-north-america.l01.q3.t: The evidence is limited and scholars interpret it differently
history-north-america.l01.q3.p: Why do population estimates for North America in 1492 vary so widely?
history-north-america.l01.q3.e: Without written censuses, historians rely on archaeology and later records, so estimates differ.

history-north-america.l01.q4.t: The crops support each other and the soil, feeding large communities
history-north-america.l01.q4.p: What is the main benefit of planting maize, beans and squash together?
history-north-america.l01.q4.h: Think of how each plant helps the others.
history-north-america.l01.q4.e: Beans add nitrogen and squash shades the soil, so the combination was productive and sustainable.

history-north-america.l01.q5.t: It ignores the many established societies that shaped and used the land
history-north-america.l01.q5.p: Why is "empty wilderness" a misleading description of pre-1492 North America?
history-north-america.l01.q5.e: Native nations farmed, managed forests with fire, traded and governed across the continent.

history-north-america.l02.q1.t: A very large earthen mound at Cahokia
history-north-america.l02.q1.h: It is found at a Mississippian site.
history-north-america.l02.q1.e: Monks Mound is the largest earthwork in the Americas north of Mexico and stood at the heart of Cahokia.

history-north-america.l02.q2.p: Chaco Canyon is in the Southwest and is associated with Ancestral Puebloan people.
history-north-america.l02.q2.e: Chaco Canyon, in present-day New Mexico, held monumental great houses built by Ancestral Puebloans.

history-north-america.l02.q3.t: Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca
history-north-america.l02.q3.p: Which nations were the original five of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy?
history-north-america.l02.q3.e: The Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca formed the confederacy, joined later by the Tuscarora.

history-north-america.l02.q4.t: It is debated, with estimates from roughly the 1100s to the 1400s
history-north-america.l02.q4.p: What does the text say about the date of the Haudenosaunee founding?
history-north-america.l02.q4.e: Scholars disagree about when the Confederacy formed, so a single date cannot be stated with certainty.

history-north-america.l02.q5.t: They were required to pay tribute to it
history-north-america.l02.q5.p: Why did some peoples near Tenochtitlan resent the Triple Alliance?
history-north-america.l02.q5.h: Think about obligations to a powerful state.
history-north-america.l02.q5.e: Tribute demands created resentment that later shaped alliances against the Mexica.

history-north-america.l03.q1.p: What did Columbus originally hope to reach by sailing west?
history-north-america.l03.q1.e: Columbus expected to reach Asia and mistakenly believed he had, which is why the islands were named the West Indies.

history-north-america.l03.q2.p: Columbus was the first European ever to reach the Americas.
history-north-america.l03.q2.e: Norse voyagers reached Newfoundland around 1000, centuries earlier, though that contact did not last.

history-north-america.l03.q3.p: What was the most devastating part of the Columbian Exchange for Indigenous peoples?
history-north-america.l03.q3.e: Newly introduced diseases killed huge numbers because Indigenous communities had no immunity.

history-north-america.l03.q4.p: Which item moved from the Americas to the Old World?
history-north-america.l03.q4.h: Choose what Europeans did not already have.
history-north-america.l03.q4.e: Potatoes, maize, tomatoes and cacao originated in the Americas; horses, cattle and wheat were brought from the Old World.

history-north-america.l03.q5.t: It shows that contact changed ecology, food and disease across both hemispheres
history-north-america.l03.q5.p: Why is the Columbian Exchange a useful concept for historians?
history-north-america.l03.q5.h: Look at the many kinds of things exchanged.
history-north-america.l03.q5.e: The idea links plants, animals and disease to political and social change on both sides of the ocean.

history-north-america.l04.q1.p: Which city did the Spanish build over the ruins of Tenochtitlan?
history-north-america.l04.q1.e: Mexico City was built on the site of Tenochtitlan after 1521.

history-north-america.l04.q2.p: Cortes defeated the Mexica entirely on his own, without Indigenous allies.
history-north-america.l04.q2.e: Indigenous allies such as the Tlaxcalans were essential to the campaign.

history-north-america.l04.q3.t: A grant of Indigenous labor and tribute to a Spanish colonist
history-north-america.l04.q3.e: The encomienda gave colonists claims on Indigenous labor and often led to severe exploitation.

history-north-america.l04.q4.t: It drove the Spanish out of New Mexico for about twelve years
history-north-america.l04.q4.p: What did the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 achieve?
history-north-america.l04.q4.e: The revolt united Pueblo communities and expelled the Spanish until their return in the 1690s.

history-north-america.l04.q5.t: It shows Indigenous groups acted on their own interests and were not one bloc
history-north-america.l04.q5.p: Why does the Tlaxcalan alliance complicate a "Spaniards versus Aztecs" story?
history-north-america.l04.q5.e: Many Indigenous peoples allied with Cortes to end Mexica domination, so the conflict had many sides.

history-north-america.l05.q1.p: Which colony was the first permanent English settlement in what became the United States?
history-north-america.l05.q1.e: Jamestown, Virginia, founded in 1607, was the first lasting English settlement.

history-north-america.l05.q2.p: New Amsterdam became New York after the English captured it in 1664.
history-north-america.l05.q2.e: The English took New Netherland in 1664 and renamed its main town New York.

history-north-america.l05.q3.t: The fur trade with Native nations
history-north-america.l05.q3.p: What was the main economic basis of New France?
history-north-america.l05.q3.e: New France depended on trading with Native nations for furs.

history-north-america.l05.q4.e: Tobacco brought profit, though it also increased demand for land and labor.

history-north-america.l05.q5.t: They depended on Native partners and had little power to force them
history-north-america.l05.q5.p: Why did the French tend to adopt Native diplomatic customs?
history-north-america.l05.q5.h: Think about relative power and trade.
history-north-america.l05.q5.e: A small French population in a trade-based colony needed alliances, so diplomacy mattered.

history-north-america.l06.q1.p: Most enslaved Africans taken across the Atlantic went to Brazil and the Caribbean.
history-north-america.l06.q1.e: Most captives were taken to Brazil and the Caribbean, and a smaller share to North America.

history-north-america.l06.q2.t: Children would follow the legal status of their mother
history-north-america.l06.q2.h: It changed who was born into slavery.
history-north-america.l06.q2.e: The law made slavery hereditary through the mother.

history-north-america.l06.q3.t: The sea voyage that carried captive Africans across the Atlantic
history-north-america.l06.q3.h: It was a journey across the ocean.
history-north-america.l06.q3.e: The Middle Passage was the Atlantic crossing, during which many captives died.

history-north-america.l06.q4.t: A 1739 uprising of enslaved people in South Carolina
history-north-america.l06.q4.e: In 1739 enslaved people near the Stono River rose and headed for Spanish Florida.

history-north-america.l06.q5.t: Status was hereditary, treated as property and justified by race
history-north-america.l06.q5.p: Why does the text say the Atlantic system was distinctive?
history-north-america.l06.q5.h: Look at the three features named.
history-north-america.l06.q5.e: Hereditary, race-based chattel slavery on a vast scale set the Atlantic system apart.

history-north-america.l07.q1.e: William Penn founded Pennsylvania as a place of religious toleration.

history-north-america.l07.q2.p: Tobacco was the dominant cash crop of the Chesapeake region.
history-north-america.l07.q2.e: Tobacco shaped the economy and labor system of the Chesapeake.

history-north-america.l07.q3.t: A person who worked for a fixed term in exchange for passage or other terms
history-north-america.l07.q3.h: It involved a contract with an end date.
history-north-america.l07.q3.e: Indentured servants agreed to work for years, unlike enslaved people whose bondage was lifelong.

history-north-america.l07.q4.p: Which colony was founded by Roger Williams after he was banished from Massachusetts?
history-north-america.l07.q4.e: Roger Williams founded Rhode Island after Massachusetts expelled him.

history-north-america.l07.q5.t: Geography, religion and labor systems shaped each region's economy and society
history-north-america.l07.q5.p: Why did the colonies develop differently from one another?
history-north-america.l07.q5.e: Climate and crops, along with the aims of settlers, created distinct regional societies.

history-north-america.l08.q1.t: A Wampanoag leader who fought the English in 1675
history-north-america.l08.q1.p: Who was Metacom, known to the English as King Philip?
history-north-america.l08.q1.h: He led a war in New England.
history-north-america.l08.q1.e: Metacom led Wampanoag resistance in King Philip's War.

history-north-america.l08.q2.p: Native nations had their own governments, diplomacy and military strategies.
history-north-america.l08.q2.h: Think of them as political powers.
history-north-america.l08.q2.e: Native nations acted as sovereign powers, negotiating, allying and fighting.

history-north-america.l08.q3.t: A region where neither Natives nor French could dominate and both adapted
history-north-america.l08.q3.e: Richard White used it for Great Lakes relationships built on mutual accommodation.

history-north-america.l08.q4.t: It was destroyed by the English and their allies
history-north-america.l08.q4.p: What happened to Pequot power after 1637?
history-north-america.l08.q4.e: The Pequot War ended with the destruction of Pequot power.

history-north-america.l08.q5.t: The two sides may have understood the transaction differently
history-north-america.l08.q5.p: Why do historians urge caution about colonial land "purchases"?
history-north-america.l08.q5.e: Differences in ideas about land use and ownership, and sometimes pressure, make such deals contested.

history-north-america.l09.q1.t: Canada and French claims east of the Mississippi
history-north-america.l09.q1.p: What did Britain gain in the Treaty of Paris of 1763?
history-north-america.l09.q1.e: France ceded Canada and its lands east of the Mississippi to Britain.

history-north-america.l09.q2.p: The Stamp Act of 1765 taxed printed materials such as paper.
history-north-america.l09.q2.e: The Stamp Act taxed printed documents and provoked widespread colonial protest.

history-north-america.l09.q3.t: Banned colonial settlement west of the Appalachians
history-north-america.l09.q3.p: What did the Proclamation of 1763 do?
history-north-america.l09.q3.e: The proclamation tried to limit settlement and avoid frontier wars, but angered many colonists.

history-north-america.l09.q4.p: What event of December 1773 involved dumping tea into the harbor?
history-north-america.l09.q4.e: Protesters destroyed tea in protest of the Tea Act.

history-north-america.l09.q5.t: They argued only their elected assemblies should tax them
history-north-america.l09.q5.p: Why did colonists object to Parliament taxing them?
history-north-america.l09.q5.e: Colonists claimed taxation without representation violated their rights as British subjects.

history-north-america.l10.q1.p: Which battle in 1777 helped bring France into the war as an American ally?
history-north-america.l10.q1.h: It took place in New York.
history-north-america.l10.q1.e: The American victory at Saratoga helped convince France to ally with the United States.

history-north-america.l10.q2.p: The Treaty of Paris of 1783 recognized American independence.
history-north-america.l10.q2.e: The treaty ended the war and recognized the United States.

history-north-america.l10.q3.t: Freedom to enslaved people of rebels who joined the British
history-north-america.l10.q3.p: What did Lord Dunmore's 1775 proclamation promise?
history-north-america.l10.q3.e: Dunmore offered freedom to enslaved people owned by rebels who joined British forces.

history-north-america.l10.q4.t: They were divided, and many lost land and towns
history-north-america.l10.q4.p: How were Native nations affected by the war?
history-north-america.l10.q4.e: Native nations took different sides, and the peace did not protect their lands.

history-north-america.l10.q5.t: Colonists fought one another as Loyalists and Patriots
history-north-america.l10.q5.p: Why do historians call the Revolution partly a civil war?
history-north-america.l10.q5.e: Americans were divided between Patriots and Loyalists, and fought each other as well as the British.

history-north-america.l11.q1.p: What was a major weakness of the Articles of Confederation?
history-north-america.l11.q1.e: Congress could request money but could not tax directly.

history-north-america.l11.q2.p: The Great Compromise created a House based on population and a Senate with equal representation.
history-north-america.l11.q2.h: Think of large and small states.
history-north-america.l11.q2.e: It balanced the demands of large and small states.

history-north-america.l11.q3.t: Counted each enslaved person as three-fifths for representation and taxes
history-north-america.l11.q3.p: What did the three-fifths clause do?
history-north-america.l11.q3.e: The clause increased the power of slaveholding states in the House.

history-north-america.l11.q4.p: What group argued the Constitution needed added protections for individual rights?
history-north-america.l11.q4.e: Anti-Federalists pushed for a Bill of Rights, which was added in 1791.

history-north-america.l11.q5.t: It convinced many leaders the Articles were too weak
history-north-america.l11.q5.h: It was an uprising of indebted farmers.
history-north-america.l11.q5.e: The rebellion showed the national government could not easily keep order, boosting reform efforts.

history-north-america.l12.q1.p: Which land did the United States buy from France in 1803?
history-north-america.l12.q1.e: The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubled U.S. territory.

history-north-america.l12.q2.p: Marbury v. Madison established judicial review.
history-north-america.l12.q2.h: It was a Supreme Court case.
history-north-america.l12.q2.e: The 1803 case established the Court's power to strike down unconstitutional laws.

history-north-america.l12.q3.p: Which pair disagreed about Hamilton's national bank and economic plan?
history-north-america.l12.q3.e: Hamilton's plan was opposed by Jefferson and Madison, helping start party politics.

history-north-america.l12.q4.t: It weakened France's interest in holding Louisiana
history-north-america.l12.q4.p: How did the Haitian Revolution relate to the Louisiana Purchase?
history-north-america.l12.q4.e: France lost its hope of a New World empire in Haiti and chose to sell Louisiana.

history-north-america.l12.q5.t: Many Native nations lived there and had not agreed to the sale
history-north-america.l12.q5.p: Why is it incomplete to say the Louisiana Purchase gave the U.S. "empty" land?
history-north-america.l12.q5.e: The purchase transferred a European claim, not Native ownership.

history-north-america.l13.q1.p: What law of 1830 authorized negotiating Native land exchanges west of the Mississippi?
history-north-america.l13.q1.e: The Indian Removal Act set the stage for forced relocations.

history-north-america.l13.q2.p: The Supreme Court ruled in Worcester v. Georgia that Georgia could not extend its laws over Cherokee territory.
history-north-america.l13.q2.e: The Court sided with the Cherokee, but the decision was not enforced.

history-north-america.l13.q3.t: It was signed by a minority faction, not the elected Cherokee leadership
history-north-america.l13.q3.p: Why was the Treaty of New Echota controversial?
history-north-america.l13.q3.e: Most Cherokee, led by John Ross, rejected the treaty as illegitimate.

history-north-america.l13.q4.p: What technology boosted the demand for land and enslaved labor in the South?
history-north-america.l13.q4.e: Easier processing of cotton increased its profitability and the demand for more land and labor.

history-north-america.l13.q5.t: A prejudiced European-American label, even though the nations had their own sophisticated governments
history-north-america.l13.q5.p: What does the phrase "five civilized tribes" reveal?
history-north-america.l13.q5.e: The label reflected white standards of "civilization" and ignored longstanding Native institutions.

history-north-america.l14.q1.p: Which treaty ended the Mexican-American War?
history-north-america.l14.q1.h: It is named for a Mexican town.
history-north-america.l14.q1.e: The 1848 treaty transferred a huge territory from Mexico to the United States.

history-north-america.l14.q2.p: Texas became part of the United States through annexation in 1845.
history-north-america.l14.q2.h: It was an independent republic first.
history-north-america.l14.q2.e: Texas was an independent republic from 1836 until it was annexed in 1845.

history-north-america.l14.q3.t: The belief that the nation was meant to spread across the continent
history-north-america.l14.q3.e: The phrase justified expansion, though many Americans opposed it.

history-north-america.l14.q4.t: A proposal to ban slavery in lands won from Mexico
history-north-america.l14.q4.e: It did not pass, but it intensified the debate over slavery in the territories.

history-north-america.l14.q5.t: Polk used troops in the disputed area, and fighting led to war
history-north-america.l14.q5.p: Why was the border dispute significant?
history-north-america.l14.q5.e: Fighting in the disputed zone gave Polk grounds to ask for war.

history-north-america.l15.q1.p: Who published The Liberator, an abolitionist newspaper, beginning in 1831?
history-north-america.l15.q1.e: Garrison's paper was a leading voice for immediate abolition.

history-north-america.l15.q2.p: The Seneca Falls Convention of 1848 focused on women's rights.
history-north-america.l15.q2.e: It was a landmark convention for women's rights, producing the Declaration of Sentiments.

history-north-america.l15.q3.t: A network of people and routes helping enslaved people escape
history-north-america.l15.q3.e: It was a secret network that assisted people fleeing slavery.

history-north-america.l15.q4.p: Roughly how many people were enslaved in the United States by 1860?
history-north-america.l15.q4.e: The 1860 census counted nearly four million enslaved people.

history-north-america.l15.q5.t: They gave firsthand testimony that shifted public opinion
history-north-america.l15.q5.h: Consider the value of eyewitness accounts.
history-north-america.l15.q5.e: Firsthand testimony made slavery's realities harder to dismiss.

history-north-america.l16.q1.p: Which decision held that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories?
history-north-america.l16.q1.e: The Dred Scott decision was a major cause of sectional anger.

history-north-america.l16.q2.p: Abraham Lincoln won the 1860 election without winning any southern states.
history-north-america.l16.q2.e: Lincoln won through the northern states, and southern states then began to secede.

history-north-america.l16.q3.t: Let settlers vote on slavery in the territories, overturning the Missouri line
history-north-america.l16.q3.p: What did the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 do?
history-north-america.l16.q3.h: It is linked to Bleeding Kansas.
history-north-america.l16.q3.e: The act repealed the Missouri Compromise line and led to violence in Kansas.

history-north-america.l16.q4.t: John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry
history-north-america.l16.q4.p: Which event of 1859 involved an attempt to spark a slave uprising?
history-north-america.l16.q4.e: Brown's raid was captured and hanged, and it deepened the divide.

history-north-america.l16.q5.t: Rights to do what, since slavery was central
history-north-america.l16.q5.p: What question does the text raise about the "states' rights" explanation?
history-north-america.l16.q5.e: Several secession declarations named slavery directly as the cause.

history-north-america.l17.q1.p: Where did the Civil War begin in April 1861?
history-north-america.l17.q1.e: Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter on April 12, 1861.

history-north-america.l17.q2.p: The Emancipation Proclamation freed enslaved people in Confederate-held areas.
history-north-america.l17.q2.h: It did not include the border states.
history-north-america.l17.q2.e: It declared freedom in areas in rebellion and made emancipation a war aim.

history-north-america.l17.q3.p: Roughly how many Black men served in the Union army?
history-north-america.l17.q3.e: Around 180,000 Black soldiers served, and their service helped win the war.

history-north-america.l17.q4.p: Which amendment, ratified in December 1865, abolished slavery?
history-north-america.l17.q4.h: It was the first Reconstruction amendment.
history-north-america.l17.q4.e: The Thirteenth Amendment ended slavery, except as punishment for crime.

history-north-america.l17.q5.t: Enslaved people fled to Union lines and emancipation became a war aim
history-north-america.l17.q5.p: Why did the war's purpose broaden after 1861?
history-north-america.l17.q5.h: Think about how enslaved people acted.
history-north-america.l17.q5.e: Large numbers of people escaping slavery helped push the Union toward emancipation.

history-north-america.l18.q1.p: Which amendment promised citizenship and equal protection of the laws?
history-north-america.l18.q1.e: The Fourteenth Amendment defined citizenship and guaranteed equal protection.

history-north-america.l18.q2.p: Hiram Revels became the first Black U.S. senator in 1870.
history-north-america.l18.q2.e: Revels's election was a symbol of Reconstruction's achievements.

history-north-america.l18.q3.p: What did Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) uphold?
history-north-america.l18.q3.e: The Court allowed racial segregation under a "separate but equal" rule.

history-north-america.l18.q4.t: The Compromise of 1877 after a disputed election
history-north-america.l18.q4.p: What ended federal troop presence in the South in 1877?
history-north-america.l18.q4.e: A political deal ended military Reconstruction.

history-north-america.l18.q5.t: He argued it had real achievements and was overthrown by violence and political retreat
history-north-america.l18.q5.p: How did W.E.B. Du Bois challenge the older view of Reconstruction?
history-north-america.l18.q5.e: Du Bois challenged the Dunning school and stressed Black agency and the role of violence.

history-north-america.l19.q1.t: Completion of the first transcontinental railroad
history-north-america.l19.q1.p: What event of 1869 linked the nation by rail?
history-north-america.l19.q1.e: The line was completed at Promontory Summit.

history-north-america.l19.q2.p: The Dawes Act of 1887 divided tribal lands into individual allotments.
history-north-america.l19.q2.e: The act broke up communal lands, and Native nations lost a large share of land.

history-north-america.l19.q3.p: What did the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 aim to limit?
history-north-america.l19.q3.e: It sought to restrain monopolies, though enforcement was uneven.

history-north-america.l19.q4.t: It undermined their food, trade and way of life
history-north-america.l19.q4.p: Why was the destruction of bison herds so damaging to Plains peoples?
history-north-america.l19.q4.h: Bison were central to their economies.
history-north-america.l19.q4.e: Many Plains nations depended on bison, and the herds were nearly wiped out.

history-north-america.l19.q5.t: It suggests a shiny surface covering social problems
history-north-america.l19.q5.p: Why is the term "Gilded Age" a critical label?
history-north-america.l19.q5.e: Twain and Warner suggested glittering wealth masked corruption and inequality.

history-north-america.l20.q1.p: Which station in New York harbor processed many immigrants beginning in 1892?
history-north-america.l20.q1.h: It is near the Statue of Liberty.

history-north-america.l20.q2.p: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 barred immigration by nationality.
history-north-america.l20.q2.h: It was the first of its type.
history-north-america.l20.q2.e: It was the first major federal law to exclude a group by nationality.

history-north-america.l20.q3.t: The movement of millions of Black Americans from the South to northern and western cities
history-north-america.l20.q3.e: Millions of Black southerners left for cities in search of work and safety.

history-north-america.l20.q4.t: Set national origins quotas that sharply limited immigration
history-north-america.l20.q4.p: What did the Immigration Act of 1924 do?
history-north-america.l20.q4.e: The act favored northern and western Europeans and sharply restricted others.

history-north-america.l20.q5.p: What does nativism mean in this context?
history-north-america.l20.q5.e: Nativists opposed immigration and often discriminated against newcomers.

history-north-america.l21.q1.p: Which amendment gave women the right to vote?
history-north-america.l21.q1.e: The Nineteenth Amendment barred denying the vote on account of sex.

history-north-america.l21.q2.p: Muckrakers were journalists who exposed social and business abuses.

history-north-america.l21.q3.p: What did the Sixteenth Amendment allow?
history-north-america.l21.q3.e: The Sixteenth Amendment authorized a federal income tax.

history-north-america.l21.q4.p: Which organization was founded in 1909 to fight racial discrimination?

history-north-america.l21.q5.t: Reformers expanded democracy in some ways while supporting segregation or eugenics
history-north-america.l21.q5.p: Why do historians describe Progressivism as having contradictions?
history-north-america.l21.q5.e: Many reformers held views that excluded or harmed some groups.

history-north-america.l22.q1.p: In which year did the United States enter World War I?
history-north-america.l22.q1.h: Neutral for nearly three years after 1914.

history-north-america.l22.q2.p: The U.S. Senate ratified the Treaty of Versailles and the United States joined the League of Nations.
history-north-america.l22.q2.e: The Senate did not ratify the treaty, and the United States stayed out of the League.

history-north-america.l22.q3.t: A German proposal for an alliance with Mexico against the United States
history-north-america.l22.q3.e: Its publication angered Americans and helped push the nation toward war.

history-north-america.l22.q4.t: Punished speech considered hostile to the war effort
history-north-america.l22.q4.p: What did the Espionage and Sedition Acts do?
history-north-america.l22.q4.e: The laws restricted speech and led to prosecutions such as Eugene Debs's.

history-north-america.l22.q5.t: It illustrates the tension between wartime security and free speech
history-north-america.l22.q5.p: Why is the Debs case a useful example?
history-north-america.l22.q5.e: It shows how governments may limit speech during war, a continuing debate.

history-north-america.l23.q1.p: Which period of 1920 to 1933 banned the sale of alcohol?
history-north-america.l23.q1.h: It was the Eighteenth Amendment era.

history-north-america.l23.q2.p: The Harlem Renaissance was a flowering of Black art and literature.
history-north-america.l23.q2.e: It centered on Harlem and celebrated Black culture.

history-north-america.l23.q3.t: The teaching of evolution in a Tennessee school
history-north-america.l23.q3.p: What was the Scopes trial about?
history-north-america.l23.q3.e: The trial turned into a national debate over science and religion.

history-north-america.l23.q4.t: Many farmers and workers did not share in the boom
history-north-america.l23.q4.p: Why was the 1920s prosperity described as uneven?
history-north-america.l23.q4.e: Gains were concentrated, and farmers and many workers struggled.

history-north-america.l23.q5.t: Racial violence that destroyed a prosperous Black community
history-north-america.l23.q5.p: What does the Tulsa massacre of 1921 illustrate?
history-north-america.l23.q5.e: A white mob destroyed Greenwood, and the death toll remains debated.

history-north-america.l24.q1.e: FDR's New Deal expanded federal action in the Depression.

history-north-america.l24.q2.p: Economists all agree on a single cause of the Great Depression.
history-north-america.l24.q2.e: Several causes are debated, including speculation, bank failures and policy mistakes.

history-north-america.l24.q3.t: The right of workers to organize unions
history-north-america.l24.q3.p: What did the Wagner Act (1935) protect?
history-north-america.l24.q3.e: It protected collective bargaining and union organizing.

history-north-america.l24.q4.t: Steering loans away from certain neighborhoods, often Black ones
history-north-america.l24.q4.e: Federal housing practices marked many Black neighborhoods as risky and limited credit.

history-north-america.l24.q5.t: Many programs excluded groups such as agricultural and domestic workers
history-north-america.l24.q5.p: Why do historians say the New Deal had limits?
history-north-america.l24.q5.e: Exclusions meant many Black workers and others received fewer benefits.

history-north-america.l25.q1.p: Which event brought the United States into World War II?
history-north-america.l25.q1.e: Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor led the United States to declare war.

history-north-america.l25.q2.p: Most of the roughly 120,000 people of Japanese ancestry incarcerated in 1942 were U.S. citizens.
history-north-america.l25.q2.h: Many were born in the U.S.

history-north-america.l25.q3.t: Victory over fascism abroad and discrimination at home
history-north-america.l25.q3.p: What did the "Double V" campaign seek?
history-north-america.l25.q3.h: It was a Black American campaign.
history-north-america.l25.q3.e: It linked the fight against fascism to the fight for civil rights.

history-north-america.l25.q4.t: A law apologizing and providing redress for Japanese American incarceration
history-north-america.l25.q4.p: What was the Civil Liberties Act of 1988?
history-north-america.l25.q4.e: It acknowledged the injustice and offered payments to survivors.

history-north-america.l25.q5.t: They disagree about whether they were necessary to end the war
history-north-america.l25.q5.p: Why does the text say historians debate the atomic bombings?
history-north-america.l25.q5.e: The question of necessity and alternatives remains a major historical argument.

history-north-america.l26.q1.p: What was the policy of containment?
history-north-america.l26.q1.e: Containment aimed to prevent Soviet influence from spreading.

history-north-america.l26.q2.p: The United States and Soviet Union fought each other directly in a declared war during the Cold War.
history-north-america.l26.q2.e: They avoided direct war and competed through other means.

history-north-america.l26.q3.t: Provided aid to rebuild Western Europe
history-north-america.l26.q3.p: What did the Marshall Plan do?
history-north-america.l26.q3.e: It sent billions of dollars to help rebuild Western Europe.

history-north-america.l26.q4.t: A 1962 confrontation over Soviet missiles in Cuba
history-north-america.l26.q4.p: What was the Cuban Missile Crisis?
history-north-america.l26.q4.h: It came close to nuclear war.
history-north-america.l26.q4.e: The crisis ended with a negotiated deal.

history-north-america.l26.q5.t: They give more weight to the role of American policy
history-north-america.l26.q5.p: How do "revisionist" historians differ from "orthodox" ones on the Cold War?
history-north-america.l26.q5.e: Revisionists stressed U.S. actions while orthodox accounts stressed Soviet expansion.

history-north-america.l27.q1.p: Which 1954 Supreme Court case ruled segregated public schools unconstitutional?
history-north-america.l27.q1.h: It overturned "separate but equal" in schools.
history-north-america.l27.q1.e: Brown rejected school segregation, though enforcement was slow.

history-north-america.l27.q2.p: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 followed the Selma marches.
history-north-america.l27.q2.e: The violence at Selma built support for the law.

history-north-america.l27.q3.t: Students began sit-ins at a lunch counter
history-north-america.l27.q3.e: The sit-ins spread across the South and brought a new generation into the movement.

history-north-america.l27.q4.t: Banned discrimination in public places and employment
history-north-america.l27.q4.p: What did the Civil Rights Act of 1964 do?
history-north-america.l27.q4.e: It outlawed discrimination in many areas of public life.

history-north-america.l27.q5.t: Its roots reach back to Reconstruction and earlier
history-north-america.l27.q5.p: Why does the text describe the movement as long?
history-north-america.l27.q5.e: Earlier generations had challenged segregation and discrimination for decades.

history-north-america.l28.q1.e: Nixon resigned on August 9, 1974, facing likely impeachment.

history-north-america.l28.q2.p: Title IX, passed in 1972, barred sex discrimination in education.
history-north-america.l28.q2.e: Title IX prohibited sex discrimination in federally funded education programs.

history-north-america.l28.q3.t: National Guard soldiers killed four student protesters
history-north-america.l28.q3.p: What happened at Kent State in May 1970?
history-north-america.l28.q3.e: The shootings deepened divisions over the war.

history-north-america.l28.q4.p: What did the Great Society create in 1965?
history-north-america.l28.q4.e: Johnson's program included Medicare and Medicaid.

history-north-america.l28.q5.t: They revealed official deception and abuse of power
history-north-america.l28.q5.p: Why did Watergate and Vietnam reduce trust in government?
history-north-america.l28.q5.h: Think of Tet and the cover-up.
history-north-america.l28.q5.e: Public confidence fell when officials misled the public about the war and covered up wrongdoing.

history-north-america.l29.q1.h: It is celebrated as Canada Day.
history-north-america.l29.q1.e: The British North America Act took effect on July 1, 1867.

history-north-america.l29.q2.p: Canada became independent from Britain through a revolution like the American one.
history-north-america.l29.q2.e: Canada gained autonomy gradually, through reform and negotiation.

history-north-america.l29.q3.t: The French-speaking population to keep its language, religion and civil law
history-north-america.l29.q3.p: What did the Quebec Act of 1774 allow?
history-north-america.l29.q3.e: The Act accommodated French Canadians and angered many American colonists.

history-north-america.l29.q4.t: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
history-north-america.l29.q4.p: Which provinces formed the original Dominion of Canada in 1867?
history-north-america.l29.q4.e: Four provinces joined at the start; others joined later.

history-north-america.l29.q5.t: Patriated the constitution and added the Charter of Rights and Freedoms
history-north-america.l29.q5.p: What did the Constitution Act of 1982 accomplish?
history-north-america.l29.q5.e: Canada gained control over amending its own constitution and adopted the Charter.

history-north-america.l30.q1.p: Which three groups are recognized as Indigenous peoples in Canada's constitution?
history-north-america.l30.q1.e: Section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 names First Nations, Metis and Inuit.

history-north-america.l30.q2.p: Nunavut became a territory in 1999 following Inuit land claims.
history-north-america.l30.q2.e: Nunavut was created in 1999 as part of an Inuit land claims agreement.

history-north-america.l30.q3.t: To assimilate Indigenous children into the dominant culture
history-north-america.l30.q3.p: What was the main purpose of the residential school system?
history-north-america.l30.q3.h: The commission called it cultural genocide.
history-north-america.l30.q3.e: The system removed children from families and attempted to erase Indigenous cultures.

history-north-america.l30.q4.p: Who led the Metis resistance at Red River in 1869 and 1870?
history-north-america.l30.q4.e: Riel led the Red River resistance, leading to Manitoba's creation.

history-north-america.l30.q5.t: The parties often understood their terms differently and promises went unkept
history-north-america.l30.q5.p: Why does the text say Numbered Treaties were contested?
history-north-america.l30.q5.e: Differences in understanding and unkept promises remain at the heart of many disputes.

history-north-america.l31.q1.t: Miguel Hidalgo's 1810 call for rebellion against Spain
history-north-america.l31.q1.p: What was the Grito de Dolores?
history-north-america.l31.q1.e: Hidalgo's call on September 16, 1810, is celebrated as the start of the independence struggle.

history-north-america.l31.q2.p: Benito Juarez led the liberal Reform movement in Mexico.
history-north-america.l31.q2.h: He was president in the 1850s and 1860s.
history-north-america.l31.q2.e: Juarez became a symbol of liberal reform and resistance to the French.

history-north-america.l31.q3.p: What happened to Maximilian, installed by France as emperor?
history-north-america.l31.q3.e: After French withdrawal, Maximilian was captured and executed.

history-north-america.l31.q4.e: Zapata championed the return of land to rural communities.

history-north-america.l31.q5.t: Growth was uneven, with land and power concentrated in few hands
history-north-america.l31.q5.p: Why did the Porfiriato end in revolution?
history-north-america.l31.q5.e: Economic development did not reach many peasants and workers, fueling discontent.

history-north-america.l32.q1.e: The United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement replaced NAFTA.

history-north-america.l32.q2.p: The Immigration Act of 1965 ended the national origins quota system.
history-north-america.l32.q2.e: The 1965 act opened immigration more broadly, especially from Asia and Latin America.

history-north-america.l32.q3.t: Voters ended the long hold on the presidency of the Institutional Revolutionary Party
history-north-america.l32.q3.e: Fox's election ended about seven decades of rule by one party.

history-north-america.l32.q4.t: The full consequences and sources are not yet available
history-north-america.l32.q4.p: Why do historians approach very recent events cautiously?
history-north-america.l32.q4.e: Lack of distance and complete evidence makes confident verdicts risky.

history-north-america.l32.q5.t: Effects can differ across groups and regions, so simple verdicts are misleading
history-north-america.l32.q5.p: What does the NAFTA example show about evaluating a policy?
history-north-america.l32.q5.h: Consider who gained and who lost.
history-north-america.l32.q5.e: Trade policy produces winners and losers, so careful analysis is needed.

history-south-america.l01.q1.p: Which mountain chain runs along the western edge of South America?
history-south-america.l01.q1.h: It runs close to the Pacific coast.
history-south-america.l01.q1.e: The Andes are among the longest mountain chains on Earth and run down the western side of the continent.

history-south-america.l01.q2.p: The lesson says historians rely only on written Spanish and Portuguese accounts to learn about pre-contact peoples.
history-south-america.l01.q2.h: Think about archaeology and oral tradition.
history-south-america.l01.q2.e: Historians combine archaeology, scientific studies, colonial writings and Indigenous oral traditions.

history-south-america.l01.q3.t: A set of knotted cords used for record-keeping
history-south-america.l01.q3.h: It was used by the Inca to keep records.
history-south-america.l01.q3.e: Quipus were knotted cords; scholars agree they recorded numbers.

history-south-america.l01.q4.t: They carry memory that written colonial sources may miss
history-south-america.l01.q4.p: Why do spoken traditions, songs and place names matter to historians of the Americas?
history-south-america.l01.q4.h: Consider who wrote the colonial records.
history-south-america.l01.q4.e: Colonial writers had their own aims, so Indigenous traditions add perspectives that written sources omit.

history-south-america.l01.q5.p: Scholars agree that every quipu recorded full stories, not only numbers.
history-south-america.l01.q5.h: The lesson says part of this is debated.
history-south-america.l01.q5.e: Quipus clearly recorded numbers, but whether some encoded narrative is still debated.

history-south-america.l02.q1.t: On the coast of Peru in the Supe valley
history-south-america.l02.q1.p: Where was the early city of Caral located?
history-south-america.l02.q1.h: It is in Peru, near the Pacific.
history-south-america.l02.q1.e: Caral lies in the Supe valley of Peru and dates to roughly 3000 to 1800 BCE.

history-south-america.l02.q2.h: Compare the dates of Caral and the Inca.
history-south-america.l02.q2.e: Caral is thousands of years older than the Inca.

history-south-america.l02.q3.p: Which society is best known for giant lines and figures drawn in a desert?
history-south-america.l02.q3.h: It lived on the dry south coast of Peru.
history-south-america.l02.q3.e: The Nazca Lines were made by the Nazca, whose purpose for them is debated.

history-south-america.l02.q4.t: That their leaders were buried with great wealth in metalwork
history-south-america.l02.q4.p: What did the tomb of the Lord of Sipán reveal about the Moche?
history-south-america.l02.q4.h: Think of what was buried with the lord.
history-south-america.l02.q4.e: The tomb, found in 1987, held gold, silver and copper ornaments that show elite wealth.

history-south-america.l02.q5.p: Because the purpose of the Nazca Lines is debated, scholars should present several explanations instead of claiming one is certain.
history-south-america.l02.q5.h: Consider how to treat uncertain evidence.
history-south-america.l02.q5.e: When evidence supports multiple interpretations, honest history presents them as possibilities.

history-south-america.l03.q1.p: What was the Inca name for their empire, often translated as the four parts together?
history-south-america.l03.q1.h: It begins with Tawa, meaning four in Quechua.
history-south-america.l03.q1.e: Tawantinsuyu is the name usually given for the Inca empire.

history-south-america.l03.q2.p: The Inca had a large network of roads and used runners to carry messages.
history-south-america.l03.q2.e: Roads, way stations and runners helped the Inca control a large territory.

history-south-america.l03.q3.t: A rotating labour obligation to the state
history-south-america.l03.q3.h: It was a duty owed by communities.
history-south-america.l03.q3.e: Under the mit'a, communities sent workers to serve the state for set periods.

history-south-america.l03.q4.p: The Inca used a wheeled cart system and a written alphabet to run their empire.
history-south-america.l03.q4.e: They used roads, runners and quipus, not wheeled carts or an alphabet.

history-south-america.l03.q5.t: They used both force and cooperation, such as keeping some local rulers in place
history-south-america.l03.q5.p: Which statement best matches the lesson's view of how the Inca ruled?
history-south-america.l03.q5.h: Think about the mix of methods.
history-south-america.l03.q5.e: The evidence points to conquest, rebellion, relocation and also accommodation with local elites.

history-south-america.l04.q1.t: Dark, fertile soil in the Amazon created by long human use
history-south-america.l04.q1.h: It is linked to how people shaped the forest.
history-south-america.l04.q1.e: Terra preta soils suggest that Amazonian peoples lastingly changed their environment.

history-south-america.l04.q2.p: When the Portuguese arrived in 1500, the first Indigenous people they met on the Brazilian coast spoke Tupi languages.
history-south-america.l04.q2.h: Think of the coast of Brazil.
history-south-america.l04.q2.e: Tupi-speaking peoples lived along the Atlantic coast.

history-south-america.l04.q3.t: They resisted both, and fought a long war against the Spanish
history-south-america.l04.q3.p: How did the Mapuche relate to the Inca and the Spanish?
history-south-america.l04.q3.e: The Mapuche resisted Inca expansion and fought the Spanish for generations.

history-south-america.l04.q4.p: The lesson claims the size of the Amazonian population before 1500 is settled fact.
history-south-america.l04.q4.e: The population size is debated and estimates differ widely.

history-south-america.l04.q5.t: A society without a centralised state could organise effective defence
history-south-america.l04.q5.p: What does the Mapuche example show?
history-south-america.l04.q5.h: Think about whether they had a king.
history-south-america.l04.q5.e: The Mapuche lacked a single king yet held out long against powerful enemies.

history-south-america.l05.q1.p: Which people founded Tenochtitlan, according to tradition around 1325?
history-south-america.l05.q1.e: The Mexica built Tenochtitlan on an island in a lake in central Mexico.

history-south-america.l05.q2.p: Maya peoples disappeared completely after the classic period.
history-south-america.l05.q2.h: The lesson says millions of descendants live today.
history-south-america.l05.q2.e: Maya cities declined, but Maya peoples and languages continue today.

history-south-america.l05.q3.t: An Arawak-speaking people of the Caribbean islands
history-south-america.l05.q3.e: The Taino lived in the Caribbean and were the first Indigenous people Columbus met.

history-south-america.l05.q4.t: Many subject peoples resented paying tribute, which affected loyalties after 1519
history-south-america.l05.q4.p: Why did the Triple Alliance matter later?
history-south-america.l05.q4.h: Think about why some peoples later joined Cortés.
history-south-america.l05.q4.e: Resentment of tribute helped some peoples ally with the Spanish against Tenochtitlan.

history-south-america.l05.q5.p: The Americas before 1492 were uniform and mostly empty.
history-south-america.l05.q5.e: They held empires, cities, villages and many different cultures.

history-south-america.l06.q1.p: In which year did Columbus first reach the Caribbean?
history-south-america.l06.q1.h: Think of the late fifteenth century.
history-south-america.l06.q1.e: Columbus sailed for Spain and reached the Caribbean in 1492.

history-south-america.l06.q2.p: New diseases were among the main causes of the Taino decline.
history-south-america.l06.q2.h: Along with violence and forced labour.
history-south-america.l06.q2.e: Disease, violence and enslavement together caused a sharp drop in the Taino population.

history-south-america.l06.q3.t: Divided lands for Spain and Portugal to claim along a line
history-south-america.l06.q3.p: What did the Treaty of Tordesillas do?
history-south-america.l06.q3.h: It was an agreement between two Iberian powers.
history-south-america.l06.q3.e: The 1494 treaty divided claims between Spain and Portugal, ignoring local peoples.

history-south-america.l06.q4.p: Who reached Brazil in 1500 for Portugal?

history-south-america.l06.q5.p: The lesson suggests the Tordesillas line helps explain why Brazil speaks Portuguese while most of the rest of Latin America speaks Spanish.
history-south-america.l06.q5.h: Consider who claimed lands east and west of the line.
history-south-america.l06.q5.e: The line, together with later events, helped place Brazil in the Portuguese sphere.

history-south-america.l07.q1.p: In which year did Tenochtitlan fall to Cortés and his allies?
history-south-america.l07.q1.h: It was about two years after he arrived.

history-south-america.l07.q2.p: Cortés succeeded entirely on his own, without Indigenous allies.
history-south-america.l07.q2.e: Many Indigenous allies, such as the Tlaxcalans, were crucial.

history-south-america.l07.q3.p: Which woman served as a key translator for Cortés?
history-south-america.l07.q3.e: Malintzin helped Cortés communicate and negotiate.

history-south-america.l07.q4.p: Which factor helped weaken Tenochtitlan around 1520?
history-south-america.l07.q4.e: Smallpox killed many people and weakened the defenders.

history-south-america.l07.q5.t: A combination of alliance, disease and violence, with Indigenous actors on both sides
history-south-america.l07.q5.p: Which statement best sums up the lesson's explanation of the conquest?
history-south-america.l07.q5.h: The lesson rejects a single-cause story.
history-south-america.l07.q5.e: Several factors worked together, including Indigenous politics.

history-south-america.l08.q1.p: Where did Pizarro's men capture Atahualpa in 1532?
history-south-america.l08.q1.h: It is a highland town in Peru.
history-south-america.l08.q1.e: The capture at Cajamarca in November 1532 was a turning point.

history-south-america.l08.q2.p: Atahualpa and Huáscar fought a civil war for the Inca throne before Pizarro arrived.
history-south-america.l08.q2.h: They were sons of Huayna Capac.
history-south-america.l08.q2.e: The civil war had left the empire divided.

history-south-america.l08.q3.t: A rebel Inca state resisted until 1572
history-south-america.l08.q3.e: The Neo-Inca state lasted until the capture and execution of Túpac Amaru in 1572.

history-south-america.l08.q4.p: Some peoples conquered by the Inca sometimes allied with the Spanish.
history-south-america.l08.q4.h: Consider why they might resent the Inca.
history-south-america.l08.q4.e: Resentment of Inca rule led some groups to join the invaders.

history-south-america.l08.q5.t: The empire was already divided by civil war, so a small force could exploit the crisis
history-south-america.l08.q5.p: Why does the lesson stress timing in the fall of the Inca?
history-south-america.l08.q5.h: Think about what Pizarro faced when he arrived.
history-south-america.l08.q5.e: Inca divisions made a unified response harder.

history-south-america.l09.q1.t: New diseases such as smallpox and measles
history-south-america.l09.q1.p: What was a leading cause of Indigenous population decline after contact?
history-south-america.l09.q1.e: Indigenous peoples had little immunity to Old World diseases.

history-south-america.l09.q2.p: Scholars agree on exactly how many people died.
history-south-america.l09.q2.e: The numbers are heavily debated, from several million to tens of millions for the pre-contact population.

history-south-america.l09.q3.t: War, forced labour, hunger and enslavement also raised the toll
history-south-america.l09.q3.p: Why is it incomplete to blame only disease?
history-south-america.l09.q3.e: Colonial systems worsened the effects of disease.

history-south-america.l09.q4.p: After the collapse, colonisers turned to other labour sources, including enslaved Africans.
history-south-america.l09.q4.e: Fewer Indigenous workers led to greater use of enslaved Africans in many regions.

history-south-america.l09.q5.t: Ask how it was calculated and what range of estimates exists
history-south-america.l09.q5.p: What is a sensible habit when you see a population figure from this period?
history-south-america.l09.q5.h: Consider the uncertainty of the evidence.
history-south-america.l09.q5.e: Estimates rely on indirect evidence, so asking about method and range is good practice.

history-south-america.l10.q1.t: A grant of tribute and labour from an Indigenous community to a settler
history-south-america.l10.q1.h: In theory the grantee owed protection and religious instruction.
history-south-america.l10.q1.e: The encomienda gave settlers rights to tribute and labour.

history-south-america.l10.q2.p: Where were the silver mines at the Cerro Rico worked?
history-south-america.l10.q2.h: It is in what is now Bolivia.
history-south-america.l10.q2.e: Potosí became one of the largest cities of its time because of silver.

history-south-america.l10.q3.p: The mita system under Viceroy Toledo was a perfect continuation of Inca practice with no changes.
history-south-america.l10.q3.e: The Spanish adapted the mita for their own profit.

history-south-america.l10.q4.p: What did the New Laws of 1542 try to do?
history-south-america.l10.q4.h: They were a response to critics such as Las Casas.
history-south-america.l10.q4.e: The New Laws tried to restrict the encomienda but met strong resistance.

history-south-america.l10.q5.t: A large estate worked by tenants and dependent labourers
history-south-america.l10.q5.e: Haciendas grew over time and often absorbed community land.

history-south-america.l11.q1.p: What crop became the main driver of Brazil's colonial economy in the northeast?
history-south-america.l11.q1.e: Sugar plantations in Pernambuco and Bahia powered the colonial economy.

history-south-america.l11.q2.p: Brazil is named after brazilwood, a tree used for red dye.
history-south-america.l11.q2.e: Brazilwood was among the first goods exported.

history-south-america.l11.q3.t: Large land grants given to nobles to settle the coast
history-south-america.l11.q3.e: The Portuguese Crown divided the coast into captaincies.

history-south-america.l11.q4.p: What discovery in the 1690s moved Brazil's economic centre of gravity south?
history-south-america.l11.q4.h: It was in what became Minas Gerais.
history-south-america.l11.q4.e: A gold rush drew migrants and shifted the colony's centre.

history-south-america.l11.q5.p: By 1763 the colonial capital had moved from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro.
history-south-america.l11.q5.h: Consider where gold and trade now flowed.
history-south-america.l11.q5.e: The move reflected the southward shift in economic activity.

history-south-america.l12.q1.p: Which colonial region received the largest number of enslaved Africans according to the lesson's estimates?
history-south-america.l12.q1.e: Close to half of the Africans who survived the crossing arrived in Brazil, by current estimates.

history-south-america.l12.q2.t: A large community of escaped enslaved people in northeastern Brazil
history-south-america.l12.q2.e: Palmares was the largest known quilombo and was destroyed in 1694.

history-south-america.l12.q3.p: Enslaved people resisted in many ways, including flight and keeping their cultural practices.
history-south-america.l12.q3.h: Resistance was not only open rebellion.
history-south-america.l12.q3.e: Resistance ranged from daily acts to rebellion and escape.

history-south-america.l12.q4.p: The figures for the Atlantic slave trade are exact and never revised.
history-south-america.l12.q4.h: Read how the database is described.
history-south-america.l12.q4.e: They are estimates that scholars refine.

history-south-america.l12.q5.t: They also show survival and creativity, such as cultural and religious traditions
history-south-america.l12.q5.p: Why does the lesson say histories of slavery are not only about suffering?
history-south-america.l12.q5.e: African-descended communities shaped music, food, language and belief.

history-south-america.l13.q1.t: A person of Spanish descent born in the Americas
history-south-america.l13.q1.e: Criollos were American-born people of Spanish descent.

history-south-america.l13.q2.t: A person of Spanish and Indigenous ancestry
history-south-america.l13.q2.p: What did the term mestizo describe?
history-south-america.l13.q2.e: Mestizo referred to Spanish and Indigenous mixture.

history-south-america.l13.q3.p: Historians note that real life was messier than casta paintings suggest.
history-south-america.l13.q3.h: People could sometimes change their category.
history-south-america.l13.q3.e: Categories were negotiated and inconsistent in practice.

history-south-america.l13.q4.t: They could shield people from some colonists but also demanded conformity and labour
history-south-america.l13.q4.p: How could Church missions both help and harm Indigenous communities?

history-south-america.l13.q5.p: The inconsistent labelling of one woman across records is evidence that the system was both flexible and constraining.
history-south-america.l13.q5.e: Differing records show categories were fluid, yet they still limited opportunities.

history-south-america.l14.q1.p: Which ruler is most associated with the strongest Bourbon Reforms?
history-south-america.l14.q1.e: The reforms were especially strong under Charles III.

history-south-america.l14.q2.p: The Bourbon Reforms included the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767.
history-south-america.l14.q2.e: The Jesuits were expelled from the empire in 1767.

history-south-america.l14.q3.t: Top posts were increasingly given to officials from Spain
history-south-america.l14.q3.p: Why were many criollos unhappy with the reforms?
history-south-america.l14.q3.e: Criollos lost influence as peninsular officials were favoured.

history-south-america.l14.q4.t: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, known as Túpac Amaru II
history-south-america.l14.q4.p: Who led the large 1780 rebellion in the Andes?
history-south-america.l14.q4.e: Túpac Amaru II led the rebellion and was executed in 1781.

history-south-america.l14.q5.p: The lesson says different groups wanted different things from reform and rebellion, making unity hard later.

history-south-america.l15.q1.p: What event in 1808 started the political crisis in the Spanish empire?
history-south-america.l15.q1.e: The removal of the Spanish king raised questions of legitimate authority.

history-south-america.l15.q2.p: Haiti became independent in 1804 as the first Black-led republic.
history-south-america.l15.q2.e: Haiti ended slavery and declared independence in 1804.

history-south-america.l15.q3.t: Refuge and military help in return for a promise to abolish slavery
history-south-america.l15.q3.p: What did Bolívar receive from Haiti's president Pétion in 1816?
history-south-america.l15.q3.e: Pétion helped Bolívar and asked for abolition.

history-south-america.l15.q4.t: They feared a slave rebellion on their own lands
history-south-america.l15.q4.p: Why did many creole elites fear the Haitian example?
history-south-america.l15.q4.e: Many elites owned or depended on enslaved labour.

history-south-america.l15.q5.p: Historians debate how much Enlightenment ideas drove independence compared with practical politics.
history-south-america.l15.q5.e: The relative weight of ideas and circumstances is debated.

history-south-america.l16.q1.h: It is the capital of Venezuela.
history-south-america.l16.q1.e: Bolívar was born in Caracas in 1783.

history-south-america.l16.q2.p: Which 1819 battle freed the core of New Granada?

history-south-america.l16.q3.p: Ayacucho in 1824 was the last major battle of the war on the continent.

history-south-america.l16.q4.t: It dissolved around 1830 because of regional rivalries and distance

history-south-america.l16.q5.t: Good history asks what choices he faced and weighs praise and criticism
history-south-america.l16.q5.p: Why does the lesson say Bolívar should not be simply worshipped or dismissed?
history-south-america.l16.q5.e: Both hero worship and dismissal oversimplify.

history-south-america.l17.q1.p: Which mountains did San Martín's army cross in 1817?
history-south-america.l17.q1.e: Crossing the high Andes allowed the attack on Chile.

history-south-america.l17.q2.p: Chacabuco was a 1817 victory for San Martín.

history-south-america.l17.q3.t: He thought Peru could best be approached by sea after freeing Chile
history-south-america.l17.q3.p: Why did San Martín attack Chile before Peru?
history-south-america.l17.q3.h: It was part of a plan.
history-south-america.l17.q3.e: Chile became the base for the naval expedition.

history-south-america.l17.q4.p: The full content of the San Martín and Bolívar meeting at Guayaquil is well documented.
history-south-america.l17.q4.e: Historians still debate what was said.

history-south-america.l17.q5.t: They disagreed about future government and leadership
history-south-america.l17.q5.p: What does the Guayaquil meeting show about independence leaders?
