history-south-america.l17.q5.e: The leaders held differing views, and one stepped aside.

history-south-america.l18.q1.p: Where did the Portuguese court move in 1808?
history-south-america.l18.q1.e: The court sailed to Rio de Janeiro.

history-south-america.l18.q2.p: Who declared Brazil independent on 7 September 1822?

history-south-america.l18.q3.p: Brazil ended slavery at independence in 1822.

history-south-america.l18.q4.p: Who called for rebellion in Mexico in 1810 with the Grito de Dolores?
history-south-america.l18.q4.e: Hidalgo's rising drew many poor and Indigenous people.

history-south-america.l18.q5.p: The lesson suggests Brazil's independence preserved existing social hierarchies more than Mexico's early uprising tried to.
history-south-america.l18.q5.e: Mexico's early uprising had a strong popular element, which was crushed.

history-south-america.l19.q1.t: A strongman who ruled through personal loyalty and armed followers
history-south-america.l19.q1.h: The term appears often in this era.
history-south-america.l19.q1.e: Caudillos held power through personal networks.

history-south-america.l19.q2.e: It split into Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador.

history-south-america.l19.q3.t: Free trade and limits on the Church
history-south-america.l19.q3.p: What did liberals tend to favour?
history-south-america.l19.q3.e: Liberals typically sought free trade and a smaller Church role.

history-south-america.l19.q4.p: Who dominated Buenos Aires from 1829 to 1852?

history-south-america.l19.q5.p: Historians agree that caudillos were all simple tyrants.
history-south-america.l19.q5.e: Some see them as providers of order and regional representation.

history-south-america.l20.q2.p: Which country was especially prominent as a source of foreign capital?

history-south-america.l20.q3.p: Railways built for exports mainly linked regions within a country.
history-south-america.l20.q3.h: They linked mines and farms to the coast.
history-south-america.l20.q3.e: They were designed to serve exports.

history-south-america.l20.q4.p: What was a weakness of the export model?

history-south-america.l20.q5.p: The causes of Latin America's economic problems remain debated among economists and historians.
history-south-america.l20.q5.e: Scholars disagree about the relative weight.

history-south-america.l21.q1.p: Which country was the last in the lesson to abolish slavery, in 1888?
history-south-america.l21.q1.e: The Lei Áurea abolished slavery on 13 May 1888.

history-south-america.l21.q3.t: Freed children born to enslaved women but kept their mothers enslaved

history-south-america.l21.q4.p: In which year did organized Japanese migration to Brazil begin?

history-south-america.l21.q5.p: Elites sometimes promoted European immigration partly for racial reasons, according to critics.
history-south-america.l21.q5.e: Critics highlight racial ideas behind policy.

history-south-america.l22.q1.p: Which countries formed the alliance against Paraguay?

history-south-america.l22.q2.p: Paraguay's death toll in the war is agreed to be exactly known.

history-south-america.l22.q3.p: What did Bolivia lose in the War of the Pacific?
history-south-america.l22.q3.e: Bolivia lost access to the sea.

history-south-america.l22.q4.p: What resource was linked to the War of the Pacific?
history-south-america.l22.q4.e: Disputes over nitrate mining were central.

history-south-america.l22.q5.p: The lesson says borders drawn in the 1880s still influence politics.
history-south-america.l22.q5.e: Sea access remains a diplomatic issue.

history-south-america.l23.q2.p: The Cuban Revolution took power in January 1959.

history-south-america.l23.q4.t: Expanded voting rights and nationalised tin mines
history-south-america.l23.q4.e: It was a major social revolution.

history-south-america.l23.q5.p: Both revolutions inspired some movements and alarmed others.

history-south-america.l24.q1.t: Build domestic factories to replace imports
history-south-america.l24.q1.p: What did import substitution industrialisation aim to do?

history-south-america.l24.q3.p: Perón was elected president of Argentina in 1946.

history-south-america.l24.q4.t: Critics and supporters use it differently
history-south-america.l24.q4.p: Why is the term populist contested?
history-south-america.l24.q4.e: It is used with differing judgments.

history-south-america.l24.q5.p: Both support and criticism of Perón are part of the historical record.

history-south-america.l25.q1.p: Who seized power in Chile on 11 September 1973?
history-south-america.l25.q1.h: The president died in the attack.

history-south-america.l25.q3.t: Seized by the state and never seen again
history-south-america.l25.q3.p: What does disappeared mean in this context?

history-south-america.l25.q4.t: Coordination among Southern Cone intelligence services

history-south-america.l25.q5.p: The figure of 30,000 disappeared in Argentina is debated.

history-south-america.l26.q1.t: That it could not service its debt

history-south-america.l26.q2.p: The 1980s are often called the lost decade.

history-south-america.l26.q3.t: Voters rejected Pinochet's bid to stay in power
history-south-america.l26.q3.h: Think about what voters were asked.

history-south-america.l26.q5.p: Economists agree that structural adjustment policies had uniformly good results.

history-south-america.l27.q1.p: What did the EZLN do on 1 January 1994?

history-south-america.l27.q2.p: Who was elected Bolivia's president in 2005?
history-south-america.l27.q2.e: He was the first Indigenous head of state.

history-south-america.l27.q3.p: CONAIE was founded in Ecuador in 1986.

history-south-america.l27.q4.t: Collective land rights for Black communities
history-south-america.l27.q4.p: What did Colombia's 1991 constitution and 1993 law recognise?

history-south-america.l27.q5.p: Some Indigenous groups criticised reforms because extractive projects still ignored them.

history-south-america.l28.q1.t: It is among the most unequal regions
history-south-america.l28.q1.p: What do many studies say about inequality in Latin America?
history-south-america.l28.q1.e: Historians trace it to colonial systems.

history-south-america.l28.q2.p: Careful historians treat Latin America as one single story.

history-south-america.l28.q3.t: It influences climate and faces deforestation and mining
history-south-america.l28.q3.p: Why is the Amazon a central issue?

history-south-america.l28.q4.t: Ask who wrote a source and why
history-south-america.l28.q4.p: Which habit does the lesson recommend for reading history?

history-south-america.l28.q5.p: The past offers context for the present rather than simple answers.
history-south-america.l28.q5.e: History helps understanding without dictating outcomes.

hq-quest.l01.q1.p: Which age spans about 3.3 million years ago to 3000 BCE?
hq-quest.l01.q1.h: It is the earliest age in the atlas.
hq-quest.l01.q1.e: Prehistory runs from roughly 3.3 million years ago to 3000 BCE.

hq-quest.l01.q2.p: How many ages does the World History atlas list?
hq-quest.l01.q2.h: Count from Prehistory to the Contemporary World.
hq-quest.l01.q2.e: The atlas lists nine ages, from Prehistory to the Contemporary World.

hq-quest.l01.q3.h: Compare the start years of the two overlapping ages.
hq-quest.l01.q3.e: Revolutions began about 1750 and Industrial about 1760, so Revolutions began first.

hq-quest.l01.q4.t: The ages overlap, so only start dates give a clear order
hq-quest.l01.q4.p: Why does the quest ask which age BEGAN first rather than which came first?
hq-quest.l01.q4.e: Because ages overlap, comparing start dates is the only unambiguous way to order them.

hq-quest.l02.q1.p: Which turning point belongs to the river-valley age?
hq-quest.l02.q1.h: It was a law code of Babylon.
hq-quest.l02.q1.e: The Code of Hammurabi is a turning point of the river-valley civilisations (about 3500-1200 BCE).

hq-quest.l02.q2.p: In which age was Egypt unified around 3100 BCE?
hq-quest.l02.q2.e: The unification of Egypt around 3100 BCE is a turning point of the river-valley age.

hq-quest.l02.q3.p: Athenian democracy belongs to which age?
hq-quest.l02.q3.e: Athenian democracy is a turning point of the Classical Age, about 800 BCE to 500 CE.

hq-quest.l02.q4.t: Change was gradual and uneven, with some regions urban while others were not
hq-quest.l02.q4.p: Prehistory and the river-valley age overlap about 3500-3000 BCE. What does that show?
hq-quest.l02.q4.e: Overlap reflects that regions changed at different speeds, so ages are tools rather than sharp boundaries.

hq-quest.l03.q1.p: Which turning point belongs to the Postclassical World?
hq-quest.l03.q1.h: It is a plague of the fourteenth century.
hq-quest.l03.q1.e: The Black Death of 1347-1351 is listed as a turning point of the Postclassical World.

hq-quest.l03.q2.p: Luther's Ninety-five Theses belong to which age?
hq-quest.l03.q2.e: Luther's 1517 theses are a turning point of the Early Modern Era (about 1450-1750).

hq-quest.l03.q3.e: Islam arose in the seventh century, long before the early modern events.

hq-quest.l03.q4.t: Technologies developed earlier were later used at larger scale by new states
hq-quest.l03.q4.p: How do Chinese printing and gunpowder connect the two ages?
hq-quest.l03.q4.h: Think about the development lists of both ages.
hq-quest.l03.q4.e: Printing and gunpowder appear in the Postclassical list and underlie the later printing revolution and gunpowder empires.

hq-quest.l04.q1.p: In which age does the Haitian Revolution belong?
hq-quest.l04.q1.e: The Haitian Revolution (1791-1804) is a turning point of the Age of Revolutions.

hq-quest.l04.q2.p: The Berlin Conference of 1884-85 belongs to which age?
hq-quest.l04.q2.h: It is tied to the Scramble for Africa.
hq-quest.l04.q2.e: The Berlin Conference is a turning point of the Industrial and Imperial Age (about 1760-1914).

hq-quest.l04.q3.p: Which pair of ages overlap in time?
hq-quest.l04.q3.e: Revolutions and Industrial both include the years about 1760-1850.

hq-quest.l04.q4.t: Historians group events by theme, so one development can matter to several periods
hq-quest.l04.q4.p: Why can early industrialisation appear in more than one age?
hq-quest.l04.q4.h: Think about how themes cut across periods.
hq-quest.l04.q4.e: Periods are tools for grouping events, and a development like early industrialisation matters to more than one story.

hq-quest.l05.q1.p: When did World War I take place?
hq-quest.l05.q1.e: World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918.

hq-quest.l05.q2.t: The end of World War II
hq-quest.l05.q2.p: The founding of the United Nations belongs to which point in time?
hq-quest.l05.q2.e: The atlas lists the end of WWII and founding of the UN as a turning point of the Contemporary World.

hq-quest.l05.q3.h: It occurred during the First World War.
hq-quest.l05.q3.e: The Russian Revolution came in 1917, before the later events.

hq-quest.l05.q4.t: They lack distance, some records are not yet open, and the story is still unfolding
hq-quest.l05.q4.p: Why do historians treat the most recent decades with extra caution?
hq-quest.l05.q4.h: Think about what time and distance provide.
hq-quest.l05.q4.e: With recent events, perspective and access to records are limited, so judgments may change.

hq-quest.l06.q1.p: Who led formerly enslaved people to found Haiti, the first Black republic?
hq-quest.l06.q1.e: Toussaint Louverture led the movement that created Haiti.

hq-quest.l06.q2.t: A point of view shaped by a person's position, experience and beliefs
hq-quest.l06.q2.h: It is about how someone sees things.
hq-quest.l06.q2.e: A perspective is a point of view, shaped by position, experience and beliefs.

hq-quest.l06.q3.t: Their interests and experiences differed, so they saw it differently
hq-quest.l06.q3.p: Why would an enslaved person and a colonial authority describe the Haitian Revolution differently?
hq-quest.l06.q3.h: Think about what each stood to gain or lose.
hq-quest.l06.q3.e: People in the same period can differ because of position and interest, which is why perspectives are worth explaining.

hq-quest.l06.q4.t: Who wrote this, and from what position?
hq-quest.l06.q4.p: Which question best helps you detect a source's perspective?
hq-quest.l06.q4.h: Focus on the author, not the physical form.
hq-quest.l06.q4.e: Asking who is speaking and from what position reveals the viewpoint behind a source.

hq-quest.l07.q1.p: Who was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt?
hq-quest.l07.q1.e: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt.

hq-quest.l07.q2.p: Who is called the medieval world's greatest traveller?
hq-quest.l07.q2.e: Ibn Battuta, 1304-1368, travelled over 70,000 miles and wrote the Rihla.

hq-quest.l07.q3.e: Mansa Musa reigned in the early fourteenth century, before the others.

hq-quest.l07.q4.t: It reflects the writer's own background as well as the places described
hq-quest.l07.q4.p: What should a reader remember about a traveller's account like the Rihla?
hq-quest.l07.q4.h: Think about who is describing what.
hq-quest.l07.q4.e: Every account is written from a viewpoint, so it tells us about the writer as well as about what he saw.

hq-quest.l08.q1.p: A diary written the same week as an event is what kind of source?
hq-quest.l08.q1.h: It comes from the time being studied.
hq-quest.l08.q1.e: A diary written at the time is a primary source.

hq-quest.l08.q2.p: A history book written today about ancient Rome is what kind of source?
hq-quest.l08.q2.h: It was made long after the events.
hq-quest.l08.q2.e: A modern history of Rome is a secondary source.

hq-quest.l08.q3.p: Which is a primary source for studying ancient Rome?
hq-quest.l08.q3.e: A coin was made in Roman times, so it is a primary source.

hq-quest.l08.q4.t: Compare both and look for more evidence
hq-quest.l08.q4.p: Two sources describe the same battle differently. What should a historian do?
hq-quest.l08.q4.e: Comparing sources and seeking further evidence is better than choosing by length or age.

hq-quest.l09.q1.p: Which archive is the open collection of Greek and Latin classical texts?
hq-quest.l09.q1.e: Perseus is the open collection of Greek and Latin classical texts with translations.

hq-quest.l09.q2.p: Which is described as the largest library in the world?
hq-quest.l09.q2.h: It is a United States institution.
hq-quest.l09.q2.e: The Library of Congress is described as the largest library in the world.

hq-quest.l09.q3.p: You want treaties, speeches and constitutions as free texts. Where do you search?
hq-quest.l09.q3.e: Wikisource is a free library of source texts such as treaties, speeches and constitutions.

hq-quest.l09.q4.p: You want to compare how American newspapers and European collections treated an event of the 1850s. Which pair fits?
hq-quest.l09.q4.h: One is American and one is European.
hq-quest.l09.q4.e: Chronicling America holds US newspapers 1770-1963, and Europeana holds Europe's cultural heritage.

hq-quest.l10.q1.t: Checking a claim against independent sources
hq-quest.l10.q1.h: It involves more than one source.
hq-quest.l10.q1.e: Corroboration tests a claim across independent sources.

hq-quest.l10.q2.p: A memoir written 40 years after events is limited mainly by what?
hq-quest.l10.q2.e: A memoir written decades later is limited by memory and hindsight.

hq-quest.l10.q3.t: It is incomplete, and some voices are missing
hq-quest.l10.q3.p: Most surviving records were written by the powerful. What does this mean for the record?
hq-quest.l10.q3.e: Because the powerful wrote most records, the surviving record is incomplete.

hq-quest.l10.q4.t: Whose voices are missing and how the story might change with them
hq-quest.l10.q4.p: What does "reading against the grain" ask you to notice?
hq-quest.l10.q4.e: Reading against the grain asks what voices are absent from the sources and how they could change the story.

hq-quest.l11.q1.p: Which development came out of the Industrial and Imperial Age?
hq-quest.l11.q1.e: Railways, steamships and telegraphy are developments of the Industrial and Imperial Age.

hq-quest.l11.q2.t: The Islamic Golden Age of science and philosophy
hq-quest.l11.q2.p: Which development came out of the Postclassical World?
hq-quest.l11.q2.e: The Islamic Golden Age is a development of the Postclassical World (about 500-1500 CE).

hq-quest.l11.q3.t: Revolutions in America, France, Haiti and Latin America
hq-quest.l11.q3.p: Which are political effects of the Enlightenment ideas of liberty and rights?
hq-quest.l11.q3.e: Enlightenment ideas inspired political revolutions in the Age of Revolutions.

hq-quest.l11.q4.t: Luther's theses, printing and vernacular scripture all contributed
hq-quest.l11.q4.p: Why is it better to name several causes of the Reformation than a single one?
hq-quest.l11.q4.e: Luther challenged indulgences, printing spread his writing, and translated scripture reached ordinary readers.

hq-quest.l12.q1.p: The Long Count calendar is a hallmark of which civilisation?
hq-quest.l12.q1.e: The Maya are known for hieroglyphs and the Long Count calendar.

hq-quest.l12.q2.p: Which civilisation kept records on knotted cords called quipu?
hq-quest.l12.q2.e: The Inca kept quipu records and built the Qhapaq Nan road network.

hq-quest.l12.q3.p: The decimal system and zero are hallmarks of which empire?
hq-quest.l12.q3.e: The Gupta Empire is linked with the decimal system, zero and classical Sanskrit literature.

hq-quest.l12.q4.t: Societies shaped their landscape to produce food for large cities
hq-quest.l12.q4.p: What do Aztec chinampas and Khmer baray reservoirs both show?
hq-quest.l12.q4.h: Both are about water and farming.
hq-quest.l12.q4.e: Both are food and water systems that supported large urban populations.

hq-quest.l13.q1.t: Three independent sources and where they disagree
hq-quest.l13.q1.p: What does the "Corroborate it" challenge ask you to find?
hq-quest.l13.q1.h: The number is more than one.
hq-quest.l13.q1.e: It asks for three independent sources and a note of exactly where they disagree.

hq-quest.l13.q2.t: Whose voices are missing from the sources
hq-quest.l13.q2.p: What does "Read against the grain" ask?
hq-quest.l13.q2.e: It asks you to notice whose voices are missing and how the story might change.

hq-quest.l13.q3.p: What does the counterfactual challenge require besides what would have followed?
hq-quest.l13.q3.e: It asks for what would plausibly have followed and what would not have changed.

hq-quest.l13.q4.t: A clear claim backed by several sources that admits its limits
hq-quest.l13.q4.p: Which is the strongest historical argument?
hq-quest.l13.q4.e: Strong arguments use multiple sources, state limits and answer objections.

ip-protection.l01.q1.p: Under the U.S. approach, intellectual property rights are granted for limited times to encourage new creative and inventive work.
ip-protection.l01.q1.h: Think about the trade between creators and society.
ip-protection.l01.q1.e: The Constitution lets Congress grant exclusive rights for limited times to promote progress, and the rights eventually end.

ip-protection.l01.q2.p: A founder wants to protect the name of her new app so customers know it is hers. Which tool is designed for that job?
ip-protection.l01.q2.h: Which tool tells customers who made something?
ip-protection.l01.q2.e: Trademarks identify the source of goods or services; the other tools protect expression, inventions or confidential information.

ip-protection.l01.q3.p: A bakery keeps a special dough recipe confidential and never publishes it. Which type of IP is the recipe most likely to be?
ip-protection.l01.q3.h: Registration is not required for this one.
ip-protection.l01.q3.e: Valuable information kept secret with reasonable measures can be a trade secret; a patent would require public disclosure.

ip-protection.l01.q4.t: Title: trademark; mechanism: patent; supplier list: trade secret
ip-protection.l01.q4.p: A board-game maker has art, a game title, a clever dice mechanism and a supplier list. Which pairing of right to item is correct?
ip-protection.l01.q4.h: Match each item to what each right is designed to cover.
ip-protection.l01.q4.e: Names function as trademarks, inventions can be patented, and confidential business data can be trade secrets.

ip-protection.l01.q5.t: Copyright and patents trade a limited monopoly for public benefit, while trademarks and secrets depend on continuing conduct
ip-protection.l01.q5.p: Why does IP law make most rights temporary, with the exception of trademarks and trade secrets that can last as long as they are used or kept secret?
ip-protection.l01.q5.h: Think about what ends each right.
ip-protection.l01.q5.e: Copyrights and patents are limited deals with society; trademark and secrecy rights last only while you keep using the mark or keep the secret.

ip-protection.l02.q1.p: In the U.S., copyright generally exists automatically once an original work is fixed in a tangible form.
ip-protection.l02.q1.h: Does anything have to be filed first?
ip-protection.l02.q1.e: Registration is optional for the right to exist; fixation of an original work is enough.

ip-protection.l02.q2.t: The specific wording of a short story
ip-protection.l02.q2.p: Which of the following is protected by copyright?
ip-protection.l02.q2.h: Copyright protects how something is expressed.
ip-protection.l02.q2.e: Copyright covers original expression; ideas, titles, names and formulas fall outside it.

ip-protection.l02.q3.t: It is not fixed, so U.S. copyright does not yet attach to it
ip-protection.l02.q3.p: A band plays an unplanned jam at a party and nobody records it. What is true about copyright in the jam?
ip-protection.l02.q3.h: Which requirement concerns a tangible medium?
ip-protection.l02.q3.e: Fixation is required; an unrecorded improvisation is not fixed.

ip-protection.l02.q4.t: Probably no infringement, because only expression is protected, not the idea
ip-protection.l02.q4.p: Another author writes a different novel about a girl who builds a robot to find her missing dog. Without copying Maya's words, characters or scenes, what is the likely result?
ip-protection.l02.q4.h: Separate the premise from the way it is written.
ip-protection.l02.q4.e: Ideas are free; infringement requires copying protected expression.

ip-protection.l02.q5.t: Copying the program's actual source code
ip-protection.l02.q5.p: A software company owns copyright in its program. What does that copyright most likely stop a rival from doing?
ip-protection.l02.q5.h: Copyright covers code as writing, not function.
ip-protection.l02.q5.e: Copyright protects the code itself, not the ideas, methods or functions behind it.

ip-protection.l03.q1.p: In the U.S., you generally must have registered (or been refused registration) before filing a copyright infringement lawsuit over a U.S. work.
ip-protection.l03.q1.h: Think of the Fourth Estate decision.
ip-protection.l03.q1.e: The Supreme Court held that registration (or refusal) must occur before suit for U.S. works.

ip-protection.l03.q2.t: Before infringement begins, or within three months of first publication
ip-protection.l03.q2.p: To preserve the chance for statutory damages and attorney's fees, when should a published work generally be registered?
ip-protection.l03.q2.e: U.S. law generally allows statutory damages and fees only if registration preceded the infringement or came within three months of publication.

ip-protection.l03.q3.t: He may be limited to actual damages and profits for infringement that began earlier
ip-protection.l03.q3.p: Dev did not register his photo book until after discovering the poster seller. What is the most likely effect on his remedies?
ip-protection.l03.q3.h: What happens to statutory damages when registration is late?
ip-protection.l03.q3.e: Late registration generally removes statutory damages and fee-shifting for earlier infringement, leaving actual damages and profits.

ip-protection.l03.q4.t: It is not required for copyright to exist, but it unlocks a lawsuit and stronger remedies
ip-protection.l03.q4.p: Which statement about registration is accurate?
ip-protection.l03.q4.h: Separate existence of the right from the ability to enforce it.
ip-protection.l03.q4.e: Copyright exists automatically, but registration brings enforcement advantages.

ip-protection.l03.q5.t: Use the Copyright Office's group options where they fit and register on a regular schedule
ip-protection.l03.q5.p: A photographer shoots hundreds of photos a month. What is a sensible registration approach?
ip-protection.l03.q5.h: Consider cost per work and the timing windows.
ip-protection.l03.q5.e: Group registration options and a regular schedule balance cost with preserving remedies.

ip-protection.l04.q1.p: Copyright in a work initially belongs to the person who actually created it, unless an exception such as work made for hire applies.
ip-protection.l04.q1.e: The author is the default owner; work made for hire is a key exception.

ip-protection.l04.q2.t: The employer, as a work made for hire
ip-protection.l04.q2.p: An employee writes code during their normal job duties. Who is treated as the author?
ip-protection.l04.q2.e: Works created by employees within the scope of their job are works made for hire owned by the employer.

ip-protection.l04.q3.p: A company hires a freelance designer for a logo with no written agreement. Who most likely owns the copyright?
ip-protection.l04.q3.h: Payment alone does not transfer ownership.
ip-protection.l04.q3.e: A freelancer generally keeps copyright unless a signed assignment or qualifying work-for-hire agreement exists.

ip-protection.l04.q4.t: It falls in one of nine statutory categories and both parties sign a written work-for-hire agreement
ip-protection.l04.q4.p: Which requirement must be met for a commissioned work by an independent contractor to be a work made for hire?
ip-protection.l04.q4.e: Both a statutory category and a signed written agreement are required for a contractor's work.

ip-protection.l04.q5.t: Each is a joint author and co-owner who may license non-exclusively but must account to the others
ip-protection.l04.q5.p: Three bandmates co-write a song intending it to be one work. Absent an agreement otherwise, how are rights usually treated?
ip-protection.l04.q5.e: Joint authors co-own the whole work and share profits, which is why split agreements are wise.

ip-protection.l05.q1.p: A transfer of exclusive copyright ownership in the U.S. generally requires a signed writing.
ip-protection.l05.q1.h: The law requires a formal record for ownership changes.
ip-protection.l05.q1.e: Exclusive transfers must be in writing and signed by the owner granting the rights.

ip-protection.l05.q2.p: Cora allows a magazine to print one photo for a year in North America and keeps everything else. This is best described as?
ip-protection.l05.q2.h: She still owns the copyright afterward.
ip-protection.l05.q2.e: A license permits specific uses without transferring ownership.

ip-protection.l05.q3.p: For a work made today by one individual author (not for hire), the copyright term is generally?
ip-protection.l05.q3.h: It is tied to the author's lifetime.
ip-protection.l05.q3.e: The general term for individual authors is life plus 70 years.

ip-protection.l05.q4.t: She may have a statutory right to terminate the transfer after 35 years by following notice rules
ip-protection.l05.q4.p: A musician signed away her copyright to a label in 1990 in a deal that was not work made for hire. Which statement best fits U.S. law?
ip-protection.l05.q4.h: There is a long-wait safety valve for authors.
ip-protection.l05.q4.e: Section 203 gives authors a conditional right to terminate certain grants after 35 years.

ip-protection.l05.q5.t: 95 years from publication or 120 years from creation, whichever ends first
ip-protection.l05.q5.p: A work made for hire by a corporation, published today, has what general term?
ip-protection.l05.q5.h: No human life measures the term.
ip-protection.l05.q5.e: For works made for hire and anonymous works, the term is 95 years from publication or 120 from creation, whichever is shorter.

ip-protection.l06.q1.p: Using fewer than a set number of seconds or words is always safe under fair use.
ip-protection.l06.q1.h: Is there a fixed numeric safe harbor?
ip-protection.l06.q1.e: There is no automatic safe amount; courts weigh the four factors together.

ip-protection.l06.q2.t: The effect of the use on the market for the original
ip-protection.l06.q2.p: Which is one of the four statutory fair use factors?
ip-protection.l06.q2.h: Think about harm to the owner's sales or licensing.
ip-protection.l06.q2.e: Market effect is the fourth factor. Credit, registration and fame are not factors; commercial or nonprofit use is weighed inside factor one, purpose and character of the use.

ip-protection.l06.q3.t: A transformative purpose such as criticism and commentary
ip-protection.l06.q3.p: Sam's review uses short clips to criticize a movie. Which factor most favors him?
ip-protection.l06.q3.h: Which factor asks what new purpose the use serves?
ip-protection.l06.q3.e: Criticism and commentary can be transformative, which supports the first factor.

ip-protection.l06.q4.t: The "heart of the work" can make a small amount substantial, and a commercial substituting use weighs against fair use
ip-protection.l06.q4.p: A creator copies a small but central, most memorable portion of a song for a commercial ad. Why might this still fail?
ip-protection.l06.q4.h: Quality of the taking matters, not only quantity.
ip-protection.l06.q4.e: Courts consider whether the portion is the heart of the work, and commercial substitution hurts the analysis.

ip-protection.l06.q5.t: Not automatically; these points may help but courts weigh all four factors case by case
ip-protection.l06.q5.p: A teacher asks, "If I credit the artist and it is for education, I am safe, right?" The best answer is?
ip-protection.l06.q5.h: Which claims are rules, and which are factors?
ip-protection.l06.q5.e: Credit is not a defense, and educational purpose is only part of one factor.

ip-protection.l07.q1.p: A takedown notice under the DMCA must include a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the sender is the owner or authorized to act for the owner.
ip-protection.l07.q1.h: Think about what makes the notice reliable.
ip-protection.l07.q1.e: Section 512 requires that statement along with a good-faith belief of unauthorized use.

ip-protection.l07.q2.t: The provider may restore the material after about 10 to 14 business days
ip-protection.l07.q2.p: After a poster files a valid counter-notice, what typically happens if the claimant does not file a federal lawsuit within the time allowed?
ip-protection.l07.q2.h: There is a short waiting period.
ip-protection.l07.q2.e: The DMCA allows restoration after 10 to 14 business days if no suit is filed.

ip-protection.l07.q3.t: The Copyright Office's DMCA Designated Agent Directory
ip-protection.l07.q3.p: Where do you find a service provider's designated agent for DMCA notices?
ip-protection.l07.q3.h: The directory is run by the Office that registers copyrights.
ip-protection.l07.q3.e: Providers register their agents in the Copyright Office's online directory.

ip-protection.l07.q4.t: Knowingly false claims can lead to liability, and you must consider fair use before sending
ip-protection.l07.q4.p: Why is it risky to send a DMCA notice for a use that is plainly licensed or clearly fair use?
ip-protection.l07.q4.e: Knowing material misrepresentations in a notice can create liability, and courts expect consideration of fair use.

ip-protection.l07.q5.p: A designer's illustration was copied for sale and her damages are about $8,000. Which forum is built for modest claims like this?
ip-protection.l07.q5.e: The CCB handles lower-value copyright claims up to $30,000, and participation is voluntary.

ip-protection.l08.q1.p: Works created by U.S. federal government employees as part of their jobs are generally not protected by U.S. copyright.
ip-protection.l08.q1.h: Think about who the public pays.
ip-protection.l08.q1.e: Federal government works are not eligible for U.S. copyright, although they may include third-party material.

ip-protection.l08.q2.p: As of 2026, which works first published in the U.S. have entered the public domain by age?
ip-protection.l08.q2.h: It is a rolling 95-year rule for older works.
ip-protection.l08.q2.e: Published works reach 95 years; in 2026, 1930 and earlier have entered the public domain.

ip-protection.l08.q3.t: Using it in a paid commercial advertisement
ip-protection.l08.q3.p: A creator picks a CC BY-NC license for her photo. Which use is NOT allowed without extra permission?
ip-protection.l08.q3.e: NC prohibits commercial uses unless the owner grants more permission.

ip-protection.l08.q4.t: The original 1920s text, but not the new notes or illustrations
ip-protection.l08.q4.p: A 1920s novel is public domain, but a publisher's 2024 edition has new notes and illustrations. What can Lena freely copy?
ip-protection.l08.q4.h: New material gets its own protection.
ip-protection.l08.q4.e: Fresh additions are protected separately, while the underlying public domain text stays free.

ip-protection.l08.q5.t: The creator keeps copyright and grants permission under stated conditions
ip-protection.l08.q5.p: What is true about a Creative Commons license?
ip-protection.l08.q5.e: CC licenses grant permission; the creator remains the copyright owner (except CC0, a dedication).

ip-protection.l09.q1.p: A song involves two separate copyrights: the musical composition and the sound recording.
ip-protection.l09.q1.h: Think of the songwriter and the recording artist.
ip-protection.l09.q1.e: The composition and the sound recording are distinct works with different owners and licenses.

ip-protection.l09.q2.p: Which organization administers blanket mechanical licenses for U.S. streaming and downloads of compositions?
ip-protection.l09.q2.h: It is a collective created for mechanical rights.
ip-protection.l09.q2.e: The Mechanical Licensing Collective administers mechanical licenses for U.S. digital music uses.

ip-protection.l09.q3.t: Permission for the sound recording and for the underlying composition
ip-protection.l09.q3.p: A producer wants to sample two seconds from a commercial recording. What permission is generally needed?
ip-protection.l09.q3.e: A sample uses the recording and the composition, so both owners generally must authorize it.

ip-protection.l09.q4.t: Copyright needs human authorship; human-authored parts, selection and arrangement can be protected, but prompts alone are generally not enough
ip-protection.l09.q4.p: As of the Copyright Office's January 2025 report, how is AI-generated output generally treated?
ip-protection.l09.q4.h: Think about what the Office says about human contribution.
ip-protection.l09.q4.e: The Office's position is that human authorship is required and prompts alone are generally insufficient; check its AI page for updates.

ip-protection.l09.q5.t: Disclose AI-generated material and claim only the human-authored contributions
ip-protection.l09.q5.p: Kit's app was built partly with AI-generated code. What should Kit do about registration?
ip-protection.l09.q5.e: The Office asks applicants to disclose more than minimal AI-generated content and to claim only human authorship.

ip-protection.l10.q1.p: Unlike copyright, a trademark protects a sign that identifies the source of goods or services.
ip-protection.l10.q1.h: What does a customer rely on a brand for?
ip-protection.l10.q1.e: Marks function as source identifiers and prevent consumer confusion.

ip-protection.l10.q2.p: Which name is an example of a fanciful mark?
ip-protection.l10.q2.e: Fanciful marks are coined words and are the strongest category.

ip-protection.l10.q3.t: It is descriptive of the goods, so it is hard to protect without proof of secondary meaning
ip-protection.l10.q3.p: Rae wants to call her bakery "Great Bread." Why is that weak?
ip-protection.l10.q3.h: Does the name just describe quality?
ip-protection.l10.q3.e: Descriptive marks need acquired distinctiveness before they are protectable.

ip-protection.l10.q4.p: Which ordering runs from weakest to strongest protection?
ip-protection.l10.q4.h: Generic names cannot be protected at all.
ip-protection.l10.q4.e: The standard spectrum starts with generic (unprotectable) and ends with fanciful (strongest).

ip-protection.l10.q5.t: Trademark law focuses on likelihood of confusion in related goods or services
ip-protection.l10.q5.p: Why can two companies sometimes use the same word as a mark, such as for faucets and airlines?
ip-protection.l10.q5.e: Rights depend on whether consumers are likely to be confused, which usually requires related goods or services.

ip-protection.l11.q1.p: Registering a domain name automatically gives you trademark rights in that name.
ip-protection.l11.q1.h: Is a web address the same as a brand right?
ip-protection.l11.q1.e: A domain registration is a technical address; trademark rights come from use and registration of a mark.

ip-protection.l11.q2.t: Search the USPTO Trademark Search database
ip-protection.l11.q2.p: What is a good first free step in clearing a trademark name in the U.S.?
ip-protection.l11.q2.h: Search before you file or print.
ip-protection.l11.q2.e: Searching the USPTO database finds registered and pending conflicts early.

ip-protection.l11.q3.t: USPTO fees are charged per class and it defines your coverage
ip-protection.l11.q3.p: Why do you list goods and services by class on a U.S. application?
ip-protection.l11.q3.e: Each class adds a fee, and the goods list defines the scope of protection.

ip-protection.l11.q4.t: The boutique may still have common-law rights in its area, so it is a risk to evaluate
ip-protection.l11.q4.p: Theo finds no registered "Northgate" for clothing but sees a local boutique using it. What does that mean?
ip-protection.l11.q4.h: Registration is not the only source of rights.
ip-protection.l11.q4.e: Unregistered use can create common-law rights, so searches should go beyond the register.

ip-protection.l11.q5.t: The UDRP process or federal anticybersquatting law, if you have trademark rights
ip-protection.l11.q5.p: If someone registers your brand as a domain only to sell it to you, which route can address it?
ip-protection.l11.q5.h: It requires rights in a mark.
ip-protection.l11.q5.e: Mark owners can use UDRP or the Anticybersquatting Consumer Protection Act against bad-faith domain registrations.

ip-protection.l12.q1.p: An intent-to-use application lets you file before you begin selling, but you must later show actual use.
ip-protection.l12.q1.h: The "ITU" route has a later proof step.
ip-protection.l12.q1.e: An ITU filing claims a bona fide intent to use, followed by a statement of use.

ip-protection.l12.q2.t: File, examination, publication for opposition, registration
ip-protection.l12.q2.p: What is the correct order of the main U.S. trademark application steps?
ip-protection.l12.q2.e: The USPTO examines first, publishes for a 30-day opposition period, then registers.

ip-protection.l12.q3.t: An office action with a deadline to respond
ip-protection.l12.q3.p: An examining attorney finds your mark confusingly similar to an earlier registration. What do you usually receive?
ip-protection.l12.q3.h: It is a written request or refusal.
ip-protection.l12.q3.e: An office action explains the issue and gives you limited time to answer.

ip-protection.l12.q4.t: An application filed by someone who is not the owner of the mark can be void
ip-protection.l12.q4.p: Why is an application filed by the wrong owner a serious problem?
ip-protection.l12.q4.e: A U.S. application must be filed by the true owner, or it may be void and not curable by amendment.

ip-protection.l12.q5.t: Check the sender against official USPTO communications; filings and notices come only through uspto.gov accounts and emails
ip-protection.l12.q5.p: You receive a letter that looks official offering to "register your trademark" for a high fee. What is the best step?
ip-protection.l12.q5.e: Many solicitations imitate official notices; verify through your own USPTO account.

ip-protection.l13.q1.p: Anyone claiming rights in a mark may use the TM symbol, but the circled R may be used only after federal registration.
ip-protection.l13.q1.h: One symbol costs nothing; the other needs a registration.
ip-protection.l13.q1.e: TM is a claim; the circled R signals federal registration for the covered goods or services.

ip-protection.l13.q2.p: Ana has only an application pending for "Ember Lane." Which symbol is appropriate?
ip-protection.l13.q2.e: Until registration issues, use TM; the circled R would be misleading.

ip-protection.l13.q3.p: What happens if you stop using a registered mark and miss a maintenance deadline?
ip-protection.l13.q3.e: U.S. registrations require continuing use and timely maintenance filings.

ip-protection.l13.q4.t: Nationwide priority from the filing date, a presumption of validity and access to federal court
ip-protection.l13.q4.p: Compared with relying only on common-law use, what does federal registration add?
ip-protection.l13.q4.e: Registration provides nationwide constructive priority and evidentiary benefits, but only in the U.S.

ip-protection.l13.q5.t: If the home-country basic mark fails within five years, the international registration can fall too
ip-protection.l13.q5.p: What is the "dependency" risk in the Madrid System?
ip-protection.l13.q5.e: An international registration depends on the basic application or registration for five years.

ip-protection.l14.q1.p: A U.S. utility patent protects how an invention works, and a design patent protects its ornamental appearance.
ip-protection.l14.q1.e: Utility patents cover function; design patents cover ornamental design.

ip-protection.l14.q2.t: An abstract idea or a law of nature
ip-protection.l14.q2.p: Which is generally NOT patentable subject matter?
ip-protection.l14.q2.e: Laws of nature, natural phenomena and abstract ideas are excluded from patent eligibility.

ip-protection.l14.q3.t: Mechanism: possible utility patent; shape: possible design patent
ip-protection.l14.q3.p: Lee invents a new phone clip mechanism and also has a distinctive clip shape. Which pairing fits?
ip-protection.l14.q3.h: Function and ornament are covered separately.
ip-protection.l14.q3.e: Functional features may get utility protection, while ornamental appearance may get a design patent.

ip-protection.l14.q4.t: 20 years from the filing date, subject to maintenance fees
ip-protection.l14.q4.p: Roughly how long does a utility patent last in the U.S.?
ip-protection.l14.q4.h: It runs from filing, not grant.
ip-protection.l14.q4.e: The standard term is 20 years from the earliest non-provisional filing date.

ip-protection.l14.q5.t: Claims must define a specific invention, and a broad idea or result alone is not enough
ip-protection.l14.q5.p: A founder says, "I will patent the idea of holding phones on bikes." Why is this a problem?
ip-protection.l14.q5.e: A patent must describe and claim a specific, enabled invention rather than an abstract goal.

ip-protection.l15.q1.p: To be patentable, an invention must be new (novel) and non-obvious.
ip-protection.l15.q1.e: Novelty and non-obviousness are central conditions, along with eligible subject matter and usefulness.

ip-protection.l15.q2.p: In the U.S., an inventor's own public disclosure is generally excused if the patent application is filed within how long?
ip-protection.l15.q2.e: The U.S. grace period for the inventor's own disclosures is one year.

ip-protection.l15.q3.t: Many countries require absolute novelty, so the video may already bar protection there
ip-protection.l15.q3.p: Marcus posted a demo video in March and plans to file in Europe. What is the main risk?
ip-protection.l15.q3.e: Most jurisdictions outside the U.S. lack a general grace period, so public disclosure can defeat novelty.

ip-protection.l15.q4.t: Learn the landscape and spot problems early, while accepting it will not be complete
ip-protection.l15.q4.p: Which is the best use of a self-run patent search?
ip-protection.l15.q4.h: Consider the limits of amateur searching.
ip-protection.l15.q4.e: Self-searching is educational but never definitive; professionals search more thoroughly.

ip-protection.l15.q5.p: Two earlier patents each show half of an invention, and combining them is a routine step for someone skilled in the field. Which test might this fail?
ip-protection.l15.q5.h: No single reference matches, but a combination might be obvious.
ip-protection.l15.q5.e: Even without a single identical reference, an obvious combination can defeat patentability.

ip-protection.l16.q1.p: A provisional patent application is examined and turns into a patent on its own.
ip-protection.l16.q1.h: What must you file within 12 months?
ip-protection.l16.q1.e: A provisional is never examined and expires; you must file a non-provisional to continue.

ip-protection.l16.q2.p: How long do you have after filing a provisional to file a non-provisional that claims its date?
ip-protection.l16.q2.e: The provisional gives a 12-month window to file the non-provisional.

ip-protection.l16.q3.t: Someone who passed the USPTO registration exam and can prosecute patent applications
ip-protection.l16.q3.p: Which professional may be a patent agent rather than a lawyer?
ip-protection.l16.q3.e: Patent agents are registered with the USPTO and can prepare and prosecute applications, but are not lawyers.

ip-protection.l16.q4.t: One international application that delays country-by-country decisions for about 30 months
ip-protection.l16.q4.p: What does the PCT mainly provide?
ip-protection.l16.q4.h: It is a filing system, not a global patent.
ip-protection.l16.q4.e: The PCT is a unified filing process; patents are still granted nationally.

ip-protection.l16.q5.t: Be cautious, check the USPTO's guidance, and consider pro bono or low-cost professional help
ip-protection.l16.q5.p: A solo inventor with little money gets a pitch from an invention-promotion firm demanding large upfront fees. What is the best step?
ip-protection.l16.q5.e: Promotion firms are a known risk; the USPTO offers inventor resources and a Patent Pro Bono Program for eligible inventors.

ip-protection.l17.q1.p: A trade secret needs no registration but only stays protected while it is kept secret.
ip-protection.l17.q1.e: Trade secret rights depend on secrecy and reasonable measures to preserve it.

ip-protection.l17.q2.p: A rival buys your product and takes it apart to learn how it works. What does trade secret law generally say about reverse engineering?
ip-protection.l17.q2.e: Reverse engineering a lawfully acquired product is generally a proper means of discovery.

ip-protection.l17.q3.t: Limiting access to those who need it and requiring confidentiality agreements
ip-protection.l17.q3.p: Which of these is a "reasonable measure" to protect a secret?
ip-protection.l17.q3.e: Access controls and agreements are classic reasonable measures.

ip-protection.l17.q4.t: Information that was already public or independently developed by the recipient
ip-protection.l17.q4.p: Which clause is a typical exclusion in an NDA?
ip-protection.l17.q4.e: Typical exclusions include public, already-known, independently developed and lawfully received information.

ip-protection.l17.q5.t: When the process can be kept hidden and reverse engineering is unlikely
ip-protection.l17.q5.p: When would a startup prefer trade-secret protection over a patent for a process?
ip-protection.l17.q5.e: A secret can last indefinitely, but only if the process is truly hidden and hard to discover independently.

ip-protection.l18.q1.p: A freelancer usually keeps copyright in work they create unless the contract assigns it or a work-made-for-hire category applies.
ip-protection.l18.q1.e: Independent contractors are not employees, so ownership must be settled by contract.

ip-protection.l18.q2.t: To make sure the company owns inventions made for the job
ip-protection.l18.q2.p: What is the main purpose of an invention assignment agreement with employees?
ip-protection.l18.q2.h: Patent rights start with the inventor.
ip-protection.l18.q2.e: Patent rights begin with the inventor, so employers use assignment agreements to secure ownership.

ip-protection.l18.q3.t: She should sign an assignment transferring the prototype IP to the company
ip-protection.l18.q3.p: Sofia wrote the prototype before the LLC existed. What should happen at formation?
ip-protection.l18.q3.h: Pre-formation work is not automatically transferred.
ip-protection.l18.q3.e: Founders should assign pre-incorporation IP to the company in writing.

ip-protection.l18.q4.t: An exclusive license bars others (and sometimes the owner) from the licensed use; a non-exclusive one lets the owner license others too
ip-protection.l18.q4.p: What is the difference between an exclusive and a non-exclusive license?
ip-protection.l18.q4.h: Think about who else can use it.
ip-protection.l18.q4.e: Exclusivity determines whether the licensee is the only authorized user in the licensed scope.

ip-protection.l18.q5.t: The company may not own the art and may need a signed assignment before the deal
ip-protection.l18.q5.p: An investor's due diligence finds that a freelance artist never signed anything. What is the likely consequence?
ip-protection.l18.q5.h: Gaps in the chain of title are red flags.
ip-protection.l18.q5.e: Without a signed assignment, the artist may still own the copyright, which can derail a financing or sale.

ip-protection.l19.q1.p: A DMCA takedown notice is a relatively quick and low-cost first step against online copyright infringement.
ip-protection.l19.q1.h: It is a platform process, not a lawsuit.
ip-protection.l19.q1.e: Takedown notices are fast and usually free, which is why they often come before litigation.

ip-protection.l19.q2.t: Document it and contact the user or use a platform tool
ip-protection.l19.q2.p: Which is generally the cheapest response when you find a small infringement?
ip-protection.l19.q2.h: Start at the bottom of the ladder.
ip-protection.l19.q2.e: Documentation, polite contact and platform tools are low-cost first steps.

ip-protection.l19.q3.p: Which forum handles bad-faith domain registrations of your trademark?
ip-protection.l19.q3.h: Domains have their own dispute system.
ip-protection.l19.q3.e: UDRP is the standard administrative procedure for cybersquatting disputes.

ip-protection.l19.q4.t: It can provoke a declaratory suit or counterclaims if the claim is weak or overstated
ip-protection.l19.q4.p: Why can a heavy-handed cease-and-desist letter backfire?
ip-protection.l19.q4.e: Overreaching letters can prompt the other side to sue or can create liability for you.

ip-protection.l19.q5.t: A low-cost step such as a platform complaint or letter rather than expensive federal litigation
ip-protection.l19.q5.p: A $400 infringement affects a product that sells $5,000 a year. Which approach is proportionate?
ip-protection.l19.q5.e: Litigation costs commonly dwarf small losses, so match the response to the stakes.

ip-protection.l20.q1.p: A good IP plan starts with an inventory of what the business has created and who owns each piece.
ip-protection.l20.q1.h: You cannot protect what you have not listed.
ip-protection.l20.q1.e: Inventory and ownership checks come first.

ip-protection.l20.q2.t: Decide on patent protection first, because public disclosure can start clocks and harm foreign rights
ip-protection.l20.q2.p: Pawprint Studio launches a new chew design publicly next month and may want a patent. What should it do before the launch?
ip-protection.l20.q2.e: Public disclosure can bar or limit patent rights, especially outside the U.S.

ip-protection.l20.q3.p: Which item should the studio protect with a trademark?
ip-protection.l20.q3.e: Names and logos are classic trademark subject matter; the others fit copyright, patents and trade secrets.

ip-protection.l20.q4.t: Register it promptly, within three months of publication
ip-protection.l20.q4.p: Which action best preserves the strongest copyright remedies for a newly published guide?
ip-protection.l20.q4.e: Prompt registration preserves eligibility for statutory damages and attorney's fees.

ip-protection.l20.q5.t: The 12-month provisional deadline and trademark maintenance dates
ip-protection.l20.q5.p: Which calendar item belongs in a small business IP plan?
ip-protection.l20.q5.e: Missed provisional, maintenance and renewal deadlines can forfeit protection.

lab-archaeology.l01.q1.p: In which year was Winckelmann's History of the Art of Antiquity published?
lab-archaeology.l01.q1.h: It is in the eighteenth century.
lab-archaeology.l01.q1.e: Winckelmann, who lived 1717-1768, published the work in 1764.

lab-archaeology.l01.q2.p: At which site did Schliemann dig in his search for Homer's Troy?
lab-archaeology.l01.q2.e: Schliemann excavated at Hisarlik, which holds nine stratified settlements.

lab-archaeology.l01.q3.t: By comparing its style with a sequence of known pieces
lab-archaeology.l01.q3.p: How can a stylistic chronology date a statue with no inscription?
lab-archaeology.l01.q3.e: Stylistic chronology orders objects by comparing style with sequences of known works.

lab-archaeology.l01.q4.t: Cities were built one on top of another, so deeper layers are older
lab-archaeology.l01.q4.p: What does it mean that Hisarlik has nine stratified settlements?
lab-archaeology.l01.q4.e: Successive cities formed layers on the mound, so digging down reaches older periods, which also means careless trenching can destroy evidence.

lab-archaeology.l02.q1.t: Ordinary finds as well as spectacular ones
lab-archaeology.l02.q1.p: What did Pitt Rivers insist on recording?
lab-archaeology.l02.q1.e: Pitt Rivers practised total recording of ordinary finds with meticulous plans and sections.

lab-archaeology.l02.q2.p: What is Petrie's sequence dating also called?
lab-archaeology.l02.q2.h: It orders groups of finds by style.
lab-archaeology.l02.q2.e: Petrie's sequence dating is known as seriation.

lab-archaeology.l02.q3.t: Their styles change over time, so they can order and date a site
lab-archaeology.l02.q3.e: Common pottery changes in style over time, so it provides a way to date and compare contexts.

lab-archaeology.l02.q4.t: It valued all finds recorded in context rather than just spectacular objects
lab-archaeology.l02.q4.p: How did Pitt Rivers's approach differ from treasure-hunting?
lab-archaeology.l02.q4.h: Think about what counts as evidence.
lab-archaeology.l02.q4.e: Recording all finds with plans and sections turned excavation into evidence-gathering instead of collecting.

lab-archaeology.l03.q1.p: In which year did Howard Carter discover Tutankhamun's tomb?
lab-archaeology.l03.q1.e: Carter discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62) in 1922.

lab-archaeology.l03.q2.p: Which civilisation did Arthur Evans uncover at Knossos?
lab-archaeology.l03.q2.e: Evans uncovered the Minoan civilisation at Knossos on Crete.

lab-archaeology.l03.q3.t: Each object was recorded and conserved in place
lab-archaeology.l03.q3.p: Why was Carter's clearance of the tomb so slow?
lab-archaeology.l03.q3.e: Object-by-object clearance with conservation recording preserved information about each object.

lab-archaeology.l03.q4.t: They mix modern interpretation with ancient remains
lab-archaeology.l03.q4.p: Why are Evans's reconstructions at Knossos controversial?
lab-archaeology.l03.q4.h: Think about the difference between evidence and guesswork.
lab-archaeology.l03.q4.e: Reconstruction can blend conjecture with original fabric, though supporters argue it helps visitors.

lab-archaeology.l04.q1.t: In undisturbed ground, lower deposits are older than those above
lab-archaeology.l04.q1.p: What does the law of superposition say?
lab-archaeology.l04.q1.h: It is about layers in ground.
lab-archaeology.l04.q1.e: Superposition: lower deposits are older than those above them if undisturbed.

lab-archaeology.l04.q2.p: What does a Harris Matrix show?
lab-archaeology.l04.q2.h: It is a diagram about layers.
lab-archaeology.l04.q2.e: The Harris Matrix diagrams how contexts relate to each other in time.

lab-archaeology.l04.q3.p: In undisturbed ground, layers A (top), B (middle) and C (bottom). What is the order of deposition?
lab-archaeology.l04.q3.h: The oldest is at the bottom.
lab-archaeology.l04.q3.e: The lowest layer formed first, so the order is C, B, A.

lab-archaeology.l04.q4.t: It shows sequence but not the number of years
lab-archaeology.l04.q4.p: Why does stratigraphy give only a relative age?
lab-archaeology.l04.q4.e: Stratigraphy says what is older than what, but not how many years ago, which needs another method.

lab-archaeology.l05.q1.p: Who is called the inventor of the modern grid excavation?
lab-archaeology.l05.q1.h: His name is part of a method.
lab-archaeology.l05.q1.e: Mortimer Wheeler is credited with the modern grid method.

lab-archaeology.l05.q2.p: At which site did Kathleen Kenyon refine stratigraphic excavation?
lab-archaeology.l05.q2.e: Kenyon worked at Jericho (Tell es-Sultan) and in Jerusalem.

lab-archaeology.l05.q3.p: What are the walls of unexcavated earth between squares called?
lab-archaeology.l05.q3.e: Baulks preserve vertical sections where layers can be read.

lab-archaeology.l05.q4.t: It controls where finds lie and keeps sections to check layers
lab-archaeology.l05.q4.p: Why is a grid more rigorous than a single large open trench?
lab-archaeology.l05.q4.e: Squares and baulks give precise control and visible sections, so others can check the interpretation.

lab-archaeology.l06.q1.t: Laser pulses that can see through forest canopy
lab-archaeology.l06.q1.p: What does LiDAR use to map the ground?
lab-archaeology.l06.q1.e: LiDAR is a canopy-penetrating laser survey method.

lab-archaeology.l06.q2.t: Walking a landscape to map and record surface finds
lab-archaeology.l06.q2.e: Fieldwalking systematically records surface finds and features to locate sites.

lab-archaeology.l06.q3.p: Which tool detects buried walls without digging?
lab-archaeology.l06.q3.h: It sends signals into the soil.
lab-archaeology.l06.q3.e: GPR records echoes from buried features and is non-invasive.

lab-archaeology.l06.q4.t: Digging destroys evidence, so non-invasive methods help target it
lab-archaeology.l06.q4.p: Why do archaeologists often survey before excavating?
lab-archaeology.l06.q4.h: Think about what digging does to a site.
lab-archaeology.l06.q4.e: Excavation is destructive, so prospection helps limit and focus digging.

lab-archaeology.l07.q1.e: Flotation washes soil in fine mesh so charred plant remains float free.

lab-archaeology.l07.q2.p: What does photogrammetry build from overlapping photographs?
lab-archaeology.l07.q2.e: Photogrammetry produces accurate 3D models and orthophotos.

lab-archaeology.l07.q3.p: Which method studies diet and health from skeletons?
lab-archaeology.l07.q3.e: Osteology reconstructs age, sex, health, diet and mobility from bone.

lab-archaeology.l07.q4.t: Excavation removes the layers, so models preserve a record of them
lab-archaeology.l07.q4.p: Why make a 3D model of each phase of a dig?
lab-archaeology.l07.q4.e: Because digging is destructive, models keep a record of context after it is gone.

lab-archaeology.l08.q1.p: About how long is the half-life of carbon-14?
lab-archaeology.l08.q1.h: It is a few thousand years.
lab-archaeology.l08.q1.e: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years.

lab-archaeology.l08.q2.p: Radiocarbon dating works on which kind of material?
lab-archaeology.l08.q2.h: The sample must once have lived.
lab-archaeology.l08.q2.e: Radiocarbon works on organic material such as charcoal, wood, bone, shell and seeds.

lab-archaeology.l08.q3.p: Which sample could be radiocarbon dated?
lab-archaeology.l08.q3.e: Charred seeds are organic and suitable for radiocarbon dating.

lab-archaeology.l08.q4.t: Each ring is a known calendar year, so radiocarbon ages can be checked against them
lab-archaeology.l08.q4.p: Why are tree-ring dates used to calibrate radiocarbon?
lab-archaeology.l08.q4.e: Tree rings give exact calendar years against which raw radiocarbon results are checked.

lab-archaeology.l09.q1.p: Which method dates fired ceramics by trapped electrons released as light on heating?
lab-archaeology.l09.q1.e: Thermoluminescence dates fired ceramics, burnt flint and heated stones.

lab-archaeology.l09.q2.p: Which method uses volcanic ash to bracket fossils, for instance at Olduvai?
lab-archaeology.l09.q2.h: It involves decay of a potassium isotope.
lab-archaeology.l09.q2.e: Potassium-argon dates volcanic minerals that bracket fossils.

lab-archaeology.l09.q3.p: Which method dates when buried sand last saw sunlight?
lab-archaeology.l09.q3.e: OSL measures time since sediment grains were last exposed to light.

lab-archaeology.l09.q4.t: Each works only for certain materials and ages, and agreement strengthens confidence
lab-archaeology.l09.q4.p: Why do archaeologists use several dating methods?
lab-archaeology.l09.q4.h: Think about limits of each method.
lab-archaeology.l09.q4.e: Methods have different material and time ranges, and independent agreement makes dates more trustworthy.

lab-archaeology.l10.q1.p: Who found the Laetoli hominin footprints in 1978?
lab-archaeology.l10.q1.h: She also found the Zinjanthropus skull.
lab-archaeology.l10.q1.e: Mary Leakey discovered the Laetoli footprints in 1978.

lab-archaeology.l10.q2.p: In which country is Olduvai Gorge?
lab-archaeology.l10.q2.h: It is in the East African Rift.

lab-archaeology.l10.q3.t: They can be dated with potassium-argon, so fossils between them are bracketed
lab-archaeology.l10.q3.p: Why are volcanic ash layers helpful at Olduvai?
lab-archaeology.l10.q3.h: Think about layers above and below.
lab-archaeology.l10.q3.e: Dating the ash above and below a fossil gives upper and lower age limits.

lab-archaeology.l10.q4.t: Toolmaking can be linked to early human ancestors
lab-archaeology.l10.q4.p: What does the association of stone tools with hominin fossils suggest?
lab-archaeology.l10.q4.h: Think about behaviour as well as bones.
lab-archaeology.l10.q4.e: Finding tools with fossils lets archaeologists connect behaviour with particular ancestors.

lab-archaeology.l11.q1.p: Who built the monumental pillars of Gobekli Tepe?
lab-archaeology.l11.q1.h: It was before farming or pottery.
lab-archaeology.l11.q1.e: Gobekli Tepe was raised by hunter-gatherers about 9500 BC.

lab-archaeology.l11.q2.p: How did people enter houses at Catalhoyuk?
lab-archaeology.l11.q2.e: Catalhoyuk houses were densely packed and entered via the roof.

lab-archaeology.l11.q3.e: Gobekli Tepe is older than Catalhoyuk by thousands of years.

lab-archaeology.l11.q4.t: Monumental building appeared before farming, not only after it
lab-archaeology.l11.q4.p: Why did Gobekli Tepe rewrite the timeline of monumental building?
lab-archaeology.l11.q4.e: It showed that groups without farming could organise large monumental projects.

lab-archaeology.l12.q1.p: In which year was Pompeii buried by Vesuvius?
lab-archaeology.l12.q1.h: It is in the first century.
lab-archaeology.l12.q1.e: Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

lab-archaeology.l12.q2.p: Which feature is found at Mohenjo-daro?
lab-archaeology.l12.q2.e: Mohenjo-daro has a grid plan, the Great Bath and sophisticated drainage.

lab-archaeology.l12.q3.e: Giza dates to about 2560 BC, much earlier than the others.

lab-archaeology.l12.q4.t: It was buried quickly, so houses, streets and frescoes were sealed in place
lab-archaeology.l12.q4.p: Why is Pompeii such a rich snapshot of daily life?
lab-archaeology.l12.q4.e: Rapid burial preserved everyday objects and buildings instead of letting them be scavenged or rebuilt.

lab-archaeology.l13.q1.p: Who brought Machu Picchu to world attention through expeditions from 1911?
lab-archaeology.l13.q1.h: He was an American explorer and academic.
lab-archaeology.l13.q1.e: Hiram Bingham led expeditions beginning in 1911 that brought Machu Picchu to world attention.

lab-archaeology.l13.q2.p: How were the walls of Great Zimbabwe built?
lab-archaeology.l13.q2.e: Great Zimbabwe's mortarless granite walls are the largest ancient structures in sub-Saharan Africa.

lab-archaeology.l13.q3.p: Which site is dominated by El Castillo?
lab-archaeology.l13.q3.h: It is in the Maya region.
lab-archaeology.l13.q3.e: El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcan) dominates Chichen Itza.

lab-archaeology.l13.q4.t: Local people already knew the site
lab-archaeology.l13.q4.p: Why is "brought to world attention" more careful than "discovered" for Machu Picchu?
lab-archaeology.l13.q4.e: Locals knew of Machu Picchu; Bingham publicised it internationally.

lab-archaeology.l14.q1.p: Who founded processual, or New, archaeology?
lab-archaeology.l14.q1.h: He used ethnoarchaeology and middle-range theory.

lab-archaeology.l14.q2.p: Which excavation project does Ian Hodder direct?
lab-archaeology.l14.q2.e: Ian Hodder directs the Catalhoyuk research project.

lab-archaeology.l14.q3.p: Which approach stresses reflexive, contextual interpretation?
lab-archaeology.l14.q3.e: Post-processual archaeology emphasises reflexive and contextual interpretation.

lab-archaeology.l14.q4.t: Finds matter to living communities, so who owns and studies them is an ethical question
lab-archaeology.l14.q4.p: Why did Peter Ucko push for ethics and repatriation?
lab-archaeology.l14.q4.e: Ucko argued for ethical practice and consultation, helping found the World Archaeological Congress.

lab-architecture.l01.q1.p: Who is the first architect known by name?
lab-architecture.l01.q1.h: He worked in Old Kingdom Egypt.
lab-architecture.l01.q1.e: Imhotep, active around 2650-2600 BC, is the first architect known by name.

lab-architecture.l01.q2.t: Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara
lab-architecture.l01.q2.p: Which building is associated with Imhotep?
lab-architecture.l01.q2.h: Think of a pyramid built in tiers.
lab-architecture.l01.q2.e: Imhotep is credited with the Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara.

lab-architecture.l01.q3.p: A temple has a hall packed with columns beneath a flat stone roof and a gateway with sloping walls. Which style is this?
lab-architecture.l01.q3.h: Hypostyle halls and battered walls are clues.
lab-architecture.l01.q3.e: Hypostyle halls, pylons and battered walls are hallmarks of ancient Egyptian architecture.

lab-architecture.l01.q4.t: Stone beams span only short distances, so many supports were needed
lab-architecture.l01.q4.p: Why are Egyptian hypostyle halls filled with so many closely spaced columns?
lab-architecture.l01.q4.h: Think about what a long stone beam can carry.
lab-architecture.l01.q4.e: Post-and-lintel stone construction only spans short gaps, so roofs needed dense rows of supports.

lab-architecture.l02.q1.h: Both were active in 5th-century BC Athens.
lab-architecture.l02.q1.e: The Parthenon was designed by Ictinus with Callicrates.

lab-architecture.l02.q2.p: Which of these is a Greek architectural order?
lab-architecture.l02.q2.h: The three orders are Doric, Ionic and Corinthian.
lab-architecture.l02.q2.e: Doric, Ionic and Corinthian are the Greek orders.

lab-architecture.l02.q3.p: A column swells slightly in the middle so it looks straight from a distance. What is this refinement called?
lab-architecture.l02.q3.e: Entasis is the slight swelling of a column, one of the optical corrections of the Parthenon.

lab-architecture.l02.q4.p: The curvature and entasis of the Parthenon were meant to make it appear straight and stable to the eye.
lab-architecture.l02.q4.h: Ask what purpose an optical correction serves.
lab-architecture.l02.q4.e: Greek builders deliberately bent lines slightly so the temple looks perfectly straight, correcting how the eye perceives long horizontals.

lab-architecture.l03.q1.p: What are Vitruvius's three qualities of good architecture?
lab-architecture.l03.q1.e: Vitruvius named firmitas (strength), utilitas (usefulness) and venustas (beauty).

lab-architecture.l03.q2.p: Who was Trajan's master builder, responsible for Trajan's Forum and the Danube bridge?
lab-architecture.l03.q2.h: He was Greek-Syrian and worked in Imperial Rome.
lab-architecture.l03.q2.e: Apollodorus of Damascus (c. 50-130 AD) built Trajan's Forum and Column and the Danube bridge.

lab-architecture.l03.q3.p: You see a tall aqueduct made of stacked semicircular arches crossing a valley. Which civilisation built it?
lab-architecture.l03.q3.h: The Pont du Gard is an example.
lab-architecture.l03.q3.e: Stacked arches carrying water, as in the Pont du Gard, are Roman engineering.

lab-architecture.l03.q4.t: Concrete, arches, vaults and domes could span wide openings
lab-architecture.l03.q4.p: Why could Roman buildings have much larger interior spaces than Greek temples?
lab-architecture.l03.q4.e: Roman concrete, vaults and domes covered wide areas that post-and-lintel construction could not.

lab-architecture.l04.q1.p: Which structural device lets a round dome sit on a square plan?
lab-architecture.l04.q1.h: It is a curved triangular piece in the corners.
lab-architecture.l04.q1.e: Pendentives carry a dome's load down to the four corners of a square base.

lab-architecture.l04.q2.p: Who designed the Hagia Sophia, together with Isidore of Miletus?
lab-architecture.l04.q2.h: He was a Byzantine Greek mathematician.
lab-architecture.l04.q2.e: Anthemius of Tralles, geometer and architect, designed the Hagia Sophia with Isidore of Miletus.

lab-architecture.l04.q3.p: A church has a central plan, brick masonry, gold mosaics and a dome ringed by windows. Which style?
lab-architecture.l04.q3.e: Central plan, pendentive domes and gold mosaics are Byzantine hallmarks.

lab-architecture.l04.q4.t: A great dome supported by semi-domes and buttressing, with windows at its base
lab-architecture.l04.q4.p: What makes the Hagia Sophia's interior feel like one continuous floating space?
lab-architecture.l04.q4.h: Think about how the loads are stepped down.
lab-architecture.l04.q4.e: Semi-domes and buttressing carry the central dome, and a ring of windows at its base makes it seem to hover.

lab-architecture.l05.q1.t: Pointed arch, ribbed vault, flying buttress
lab-architecture.l05.q1.p: Which three devices define Gothic structure?
lab-architecture.l05.q1.h: They redirect loads outward and down.
lab-architecture.l05.q1.e: The pointed arch, ribbed vault and flying buttress are the key Gothic devices.

lab-architecture.l05.q2.t: Rounded arches and thick walls with small windows
lab-architecture.l05.q2.p: Which feature is typical of Romanesque architecture?
lab-architecture.l05.q2.e: Romanesque buildings use rounded arches and thick walls with small openings.

lab-architecture.l05.q3.p: A cathedral has a pointed arch, visible exterior buttress arches and huge windows. Which style is it?
lab-architecture.l05.q3.h: Look for walls dissolving into glass.
lab-architecture.l05.q3.e: Pointed arches, flying buttresses and large glazed areas identify Gothic.

lab-architecture.l05.q4.t: Buttresses and rib vaults carried the roof's thrust, so walls no longer bore the load
lab-architecture.l05.q4.p: Why could Gothic walls hold much larger windows than Romanesque walls?
lab-architecture.l05.q4.h: Where does the load go once ribs and buttresses take it?
lab-architecture.l05.q4.e: Ribbed vaults and flying buttresses channel the loads, freeing the walls to become glass.

lab-architecture.l06.q1.p: Which architect built the dome of Florence Cathedral?
lab-architecture.l06.q1.e: Filippo Brunelleschi built the herringbone brick dome of Florence Cathedral.

lab-architecture.l06.q2.p: Which treatise did Andrea Palladio publish?
lab-architecture.l06.q2.h: Its title means the Four Books.
lab-architecture.l06.q2.e: Palladio wrote I quattro libri dell'architettura; Alberti wrote De re aedificatoria and Vitruvius De architectura.

lab-architecture.l06.q3.p: A symmetrical villa with a temple-front portico and a central domed room on a hill. Whose style is this?
lab-architecture.l06.q3.e: Symmetrical plans with temple-front porticoes are Palladio's signature.

lab-architecture.l06.q4.p: Brunelleschi's dome was built without wooden centering, using a herringbone brick pattern.
lab-architecture.l06.q4.h: Consider why this was an engineering breakthrough.
lab-architecture.l06.q4.e: The herringbone pattern let the brick courses support themselves as the dome rose, avoiding a massive timber framework.

lab-architecture.l07.q1.p: Which architect rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral after the Great Fire of London?
lab-architecture.l07.q1.e: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral, famous for its triple-shell dome.

lab-architecture.l07.q2.t: Dynamic curved forms and dramatic light and shadow
lab-architecture.l07.q2.p: Which is a hallmark of Baroque architecture?
lab-architecture.l07.q2.e: Baroque used curves, rich ornament and dramatic lighting.

lab-architecture.l07.q3.p: A civic building has a calm portico, a dome, strict symmetry and restrained classical detail, built around 1800. Which style?
lab-architecture.l07.q3.e: Restrained classical vocabulary with porticoes and domes is Neoclassical (c. 1750-1850).

lab-architecture.l07.q4.t: It uses sober, restrained classical forms instead of theatrical curves and ornament
lab-architecture.l07.q4.p: How does Neoclassicism differ from Baroque?
lab-architecture.l07.q4.h: One is drama, the other is order.
lab-architecture.l07.q4.e: Neoclassicism reacted against Baroque excess with simpler, restrained Greek and Roman forms.

lab-architecture.l08.q1.p: Who coined form follows function and designed the Wainwright Building?
lab-architecture.l08.q1.e: Louis Sullivan (1856-1924) is linked with form follows function and the Wainwright Building.

lab-architecture.l08.q2.t: Steel frame, safety elevator and reinforced concrete
lab-architecture.l08.q2.p: Which technologies made the first skyscrapers possible?
lab-architecture.l08.q2.e: The steel frame, safety elevator and early reinforced concrete set the stage for the skyscraper.

lab-architecture.l08.q3.p: A huge exhibition hall built of iron and glass in 1851 is an example of which building?
lab-architecture.l08.q3.e: The Crystal Palace is a landmark of iron-and-glass construction.

lab-architecture.l08.q4.t: The frame carries the loads, so walls need not be thick
lab-architecture.l08.q4.p: Why does a steel-frame building let facades have large windows compared with a masonry building?
lab-architecture.l08.q4.e: With a frame carrying the loads, exterior walls become light skins that can be mostly glass.

lab-architecture.l09.q1.p: Which architect designed the Sagrada Familia?
lab-architecture.l09.q1.e: Antoni Gaudi (1852-1926) designed the Sagrada Familia, Casa Batllo, Park Guell and Casa Mila.

lab-architecture.l09.q2.t: A mosaic made from broken ceramic pieces
lab-architecture.l09.q2.h: Gaudi used it on Park Guell.
lab-architecture.l09.q2.e: Trencadis is mosaic made from broken tile pieces, used on Gaudi's surfaces.

lab-architecture.l09.q3.p: A balcony looks like seaweed, with whiplash curves and a nature-inspired pattern in iron. Which style?
lab-architecture.l09.q3.e: Whiplash curves, nature-derived ornament and iron are Art Nouveau traits.

lab-architecture.l09.q4.t: A chain hangs in pure tension, so inverting its shape gives an arch in pure compression
lab-architecture.l09.q4.p: Why did Gaudi use hanging-chain (catenary) models?
lab-architecture.l09.q4.h: Flip the hanging shape upside down.
lab-architecture.l09.q4.e: Inverting a hanging chain's form gives an ideal arch shape that carries load in compression.

lab-architecture.l10.q1.h: He also designed the Fagus Factory.
lab-architecture.l10.q1.e: Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus (c. 1919-1933) in Germany.

lab-architecture.l10.q2.p: Which phrase is associated with Mies van der Rohe?
lab-architecture.l10.q2.e: Mies is known for less is more; Le Corbusier for a machine for living in; Sullivan for form follows function.

lab-architecture.l10.q3.p: A flat-roofed pavilion of steel and glass with open flowing space and no ornament. Which architect fits best?
lab-architecture.l10.q3.e: Steel-and-glass minimalism with universal open space is Mies's hallmark.

lab-architecture.l10.q4.t: A non-structural glass skin hung on a frame
lab-architecture.l10.q4.p: What is a glass curtain wall?
lab-architecture.l10.q4.h: It does not carry the building's weight.
lab-architecture.l10.q4.e: A curtain wall is an outer skin supported by the frame, not a load-bearing wall.

lab-architecture.l11.q1.p: Which is one of Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture?
lab-architecture.l11.q1.e: The five points are pilotis, free plan, free facade, ribbon window and roof garden.

lab-architecture.l11.q2.p: Which house by Frank Lloyd Wright has cantilevered concrete terraces over a waterfall?
lab-architecture.l11.q2.h: Its name hints at the water.
lab-architecture.l11.q2.e: Wright's Fallingwater uses cantilevered reinforced-concrete terraces over a waterfall.

lab-architecture.l11.q3.p: A white box lifted on columns with ribbon windows and a roof garden. Whose house is it?
lab-architecture.l11.q3.e: Villa Savoye is the classic expression of the Five Points.

lab-architecture.l11.q4.t: Wright's organic buildings grow from and anchor to the landscape, while Corbusier often lifts a pure object above it
lab-architecture.l11.q4.p: How does Wright's approach to site differ from Le Corbusier's?
lab-architecture.l11.q4.e: Wright integrates building and site; Le Corbusier often presents a pure object raised on pilotis.

lab-architecture.l12.q1.p: What does the term beton brut mean?
lab-architecture.l12.q1.h: It is French and describes the material.
lab-architecture.l12.q1.e: Beton brut is raw, unfinished concrete, the signature material of Brutalism.

lab-architecture.l12.q2.p: Which building is by Louis Kahn?
lab-architecture.l12.q2.e: The Salk Institute is by Kahn, as are the Kimbell Art Museum and the Bangladesh National Assembly.

lab-architecture.l12.q3.p: A plan separates calm rooms for people from stair towers and utility shafts. Which Kahn idea is this?
lab-architecture.l12.q3.e: Kahn separated served spaces (rooms) from servant spaces (stairs, ducts).

lab-architecture.l12.q4.t: Brutalism flaunts massive raw concrete and structure, while International Style prefers light glass skins
lab-architecture.l12.q4.p: What distinguishes Brutalism's expressive approach from the International Style's?
lab-architecture.l12.q4.e: Brutalism is heavy and sculptural; the International Style favours lightweight glass and steel.

lab-architecture.l13.q1.p: Which building is by Frank Gehry?
lab-architecture.l13.q1.e: Gehry designed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao and Walt Disney Concert Hall.

lab-architecture.l13.q2.p: Zaha Hadid is associated with which approach?
lab-architecture.l13.q2.h: She is called the queen of the curve.
lab-architecture.l13.q2.e: Hadid (1950-2016) is linked with deconstructivism and parametricism.

lab-architecture.l13.q3.p: A building quotes historical columns in bright colours with a wink of irony. Which style?
lab-architecture.l13.q3.e: Historical quotation, colour and irony are postmodern.

lab-architecture.l13.q4.t: It generates form through algorithms and digital fabrication
lab-architecture.l13.q4.p: What most separates parametric design from earlier styles?
lab-architecture.l13.q4.h: Ask how the form is produced.
lab-architecture.l13.q4.e: Parametric design is driven by parameters and computation, then built with CNC or robotic fabrication.

lab-architecture.l14.q1.p: A simply supported beam carries a uniform load w over span L. What is each support reaction?
lab-architecture.l14.q1.h: The two supports share the total equally.
lab-architecture.l14.q1.e: Each end carries half the total load wL, so R = wL/2.
