law-jurisprudence.l14.q3.e: Secrecy and retroactivity violate formal requirements. A thick account adds substantive criteria, so it is at least as demanding.

law-jurisprudence.l14.q4.t: A legal system may conform to the rule of law and still be unjust, as a sharp knife can be used for good or ill
law-jurisprudence.l14.q4.p: Raz called the rule of law a virtue of legal systems "like the sharpness of a knife." What follows from this analogy?
law-jurisprudence.l14.q4.h: It is an instrumental, formal virtue.
law-jurisprudence.l14.q4.e: Raz's point is that the rule of law is a formal virtue compatible with injustice. Thick conceptions would reject that.

law-jurisprudence.l14.q5.t: In rule by law, law is an instrument of rulers who are not bound by it, while in rule of law rulers are constrained by law
law-jurisprudence.l14.q5.p: What is the difference between rule of law and rule by law?
law-jurisprudence.l14.q5.h: Think of authoritarian uses of law.
law-jurisprudence.l14.q5.e: Rule by law treats law as a tool of power, even for regimes that do not submit to it. The rule of law binds officials.

law-jurisprudence.l15.q1.t: the fact that the offender deserves it because of the wrong that he has done
law-jurisprudence.l15.q1.p: A retributivist justifies punishment mainly by
law-jurisprudence.l15.q1.e: Retributivism is backward-looking and grounds punishment in desert. The other options describe deterrence, rehabilitation and restorative justice.

law-jurisprudence.l15.q2.t: the general justifying aim of punishment from the principles governing who may be punished and how much
law-jurisprudence.l15.q2.p: Hart's mixed view in the Prolegomenon distinguishes
law-jurisprudence.l15.q2.e: Hart placed a utilitarian general aim alongside retributive limits on distribution, such as requiring guilt and proportionality.

law-jurisprudence.l15.q3.t: A retributivist objects that it is disproportionate, and a pure deterrence theorist must rely on empirical claims about effects
law-jurisprudence.l15.q3.p: A defendant who stole bread for a hungry child receives a very long sentence meant to deter others. Which statement correctly describes the objections?
law-jurisprudence.l15.q3.e: Retributivism requires proportionality. A consequentialist defense turns on whether the sentence in fact deters more, which is an empirical question.

law-jurisprudence.l15.q4.t: The death penalty is constitutional, but the Supreme Court has barred it for people with intellectual disability and for offenders under eighteen
law-jurisprudence.l15.q4.p: Under current US law, which statement about capital punishment is accurate according to the lesson?
law-jurisprudence.l15.q4.h: State the law apart from the debate.
law-jurisprudence.l15.q4.e: Gregg upheld guided-discretion statutes, while Atkins and Roper barred execution of those groups, and Kennedy barred it for non-fatal child rape.

law-jurisprudence.l15.q5.t: punishment communicates society's condemnation, which distinguishes it from a mere penalty
law-jurisprudence.l15.q5.p: Feinberg's expressive theory of punishment holds that
law-jurisprudence.l15.q5.h: Think about the meaning of punishment.
law-jurisprudence.l15.q5.e: Feinberg argued that condemnation is part of what punishment is. The other options describe consequentialist, fair-play and consent theories.

law-jurisprudence.l16.q1.t: do not know their place in society, their abilities, or their conception of the good
law-jurisprudence.l16.q1.p: In Rawls's original position, the veil of ignorance means that the parties
law-jurisprudence.l16.q1.h: It hides particular facts, not general facts.
law-jurisprudence.l16.q1.e: The parties are ignorant of their particular position and traits, but they know general facts about psychology and economics.

law-jurisprudence.l16.q2.t: Social and economic inequalities are acceptable only if they are to the greatest benefit of the least advantaged
law-jurisprudence.l16.q2.p: Which statement correctly states Rawls's difference principle?
law-jurisprudence.l16.q2.h: It concerns the position of the worst off.
law-jurisprudence.l16.q2.e: The difference principle requires that inequalities benefit the least advantaged. The others describe utilitarian, Nozickian and desert-based views.

law-jurisprudence.l16.q3.t: A utilitarian might support it if total welfare rises, while Rawls would reject it unless it improved the position of the least advantaged
law-jurisprudence.l16.q3.p: A legislature considers a policy that raises average incomes while lowering the income of the poorest tenth. How would Rawls and a utilitarian most likely differ?
law-jurisprudence.l16.q3.h: Compare aggregate welfare with the position of the worst off.
law-jurisprudence.l16.q3.e: Utilitarians aggregate welfare, while the difference principle focuses on the least advantaged. Equal liberties are not the issue.

law-jurisprudence.l16.q4.t: The stakes are high and the probabilities unknown, so parties would avoid risking the worst outcomes
law-jurisprudence.l16.q4.p: Harsanyi argued that parties behind the veil would maximize expected average utility, while Rawls argued for a conservative rule close to maximin. What is Rawls's main reason?
law-jurisprudence.l16.q4.h: Think about choosing under uncertainty with serious stakes.
law-jurisprudence.l16.q4.e: Rawls argued that with high stakes and unknown probabilities, cautious reasoning focused on the worst case is rational.

law-jurisprudence.l16.q5.t: a political conception that could be supported by an overlapping consensus among reasonable comprehensive doctrines
law-jurisprudence.l16.q5.p: In Political Liberalism, Rawls recast justice as fairness as
law-jurisprudence.l16.q5.e: Political Liberalism presents justice as fairness as a freestanding political conception supported by overlapping consensus, not a comprehensive doctrine.

law-jurisprudence.l17.q1.t: just initial acquisition, just transfer, and rectification of past injustices
law-jurisprudence.l17.q1.p: Nozick's entitlement theory says that a distribution is just if it arises from
law-jurisprudence.l17.q1.e: The entitlement theory is historical, with three parts: acquisition, transfer and rectification. The others describe Rawls, utilitarianism and the capability approach.

law-jurisprudence.l17.q2.t: That voluntary exchanges disrupt any pattern of distribution, so maintaining a pattern requires continuous interference
law-jurisprudence.l17.q2.p: What point did Nozick use the Wilt Chamberlain example to make?
law-jurisprudence.l17.q2.e: The example argues that free transfers upset any patterned distribution, so patterns can be maintained only by interfering with liberty.

law-jurisprudence.l17.q3.t: Several reasoned principles may support different claims, yet one can often agree on reducing a clear injustice without a single perfect principle
law-jurisprudence.l17.q3.p: Three children dispute who should get a flute: one can play it, one has no other toys, and one made it. What point does Sen draw from the example?
law-jurisprudence.l17.q3.e: Sen uses the flute example to show that plural reasonable principles can conflict, which supports a comparative approach.

law-jurisprudence.l17.q4.t: Nozick asks about the history of title, and the capability approach asks what people can do and be
law-jurisprudence.l17.q4.p: A city has a parcel claimed by a developer who owns adjoining land, homeless residents, and a community that made the park. Which pairing of theory and question is correct?
law-jurisprudence.l17.q4.h: Match each theory with its core question.
law-jurisprudence.l17.q4.e: Nozick looks to acquisition and transfer. The capability approach looks to what people are able to do and be. The other pairings swap the theories.

law-jurisprudence.l17.q5.t: restoring equality after a wrong, as in tort and contract
law-jurisprudence.l17.q5.p: In Aristotle's account, corrective justice is concerned with
law-jurisprudence.l17.q5.h: It is the justice of rectification.
law-jurisprudence.l17.q5.e: Corrective justice restores equality between parties after a wrong. Distributive justice divides goods by merit.

law-jurisprudence.l18.q1.p: Mill's harm principle holds that power may rightfully be exercised over a member of a civilized community against his will only
law-jurisprudence.l18.q1.e: The harm principle limits coercion to preventing harm to others. Moral improvement and shared morality are the grounds Mill rejected.

law-jurisprudence.l18.q2.t: A society is held together by shared morality, and law may enforce it to protect the society from disintegration
law-jurisprudence.l18.q2.p: What was Devlin's main argument in The Enforcement of Morals?
law-jurisprudence.l18.q2.e: Devlin argued that shared morality is part of social cohesion and may be protected by law. Hart replied with Mill's harm principle.

law-jurisprudence.l18.q3.t: The Hart-Devlin debate about whether law may enforce morality as such
law-jurisprudence.l18.q3.p: In Lawrence v. Texas (2003), the Supreme Court overruled Bowers v. Hardwick and held that moral disapproval of a practice was not a sufficient basis for the statute. Which debate does this echo?
law-jurisprudence.l18.q3.e: The case concerns whether majority morality alone can justify criminalization, the issue in the Hart-Devlin debate.

law-jurisprudence.l18.q4.t: It may qualify, because it is public, nonviolent, conscientious, and the actors accept the legal consequences
law-jurisprudence.l18.q4.p: Activists camp in a park in violation of a city ban, notify police in advance, and accept arrest to draw attention to homelessness. Under Rawls's criteria for civil disobedience, how does this act most likely rank?
law-jurisprudence.l18.q4.h: Review the features of civil disobedience.
law-jurisprudence.l18.q4.e: Rawls describes civil disobedience as public, nonviolent, conscientious and political, accepting penalties. It is not secret and not automatic.

law-jurisprudence.l18.q5.t: upheld contempt convictions of King and others for marching in violation of an injunction they had not first challenged in court
law-jurisprudence.l18.q5.p: In Walker v. City of Birmingham (1967), the Supreme Court
law-jurisprudence.l18.q5.h: The Court avoided the merits of the injunction.
law-jurisprudence.l18.q5.e: The Court upheld the convictions five to four, focusing on the marchers' failure to challenge the injunction first.

law-jurisprudence.l19.q1.p: In Hohfeld's scheme, a claim-right correlates with
law-jurisprudence.l19.q1.e: A claim-right correlates with a duty. Liability correlates with power, and disability with immunity.

law-jurisprudence.l19.q2.t: The ability to change legal relations, such as the power to make a will
law-jurisprudence.l19.q2.p: What does a Hohfeldian "power" refer to?
law-jurisprudence.l19.q2.e: A power is the ability to change legal relations. Freedom from duty is a privilege or liberty, and protection from change is an immunity.

law-jurisprudence.l19.q3.t: The tenant has an immunity and the landlord has a disability
law-jurisprudence.l19.q3.p: A tenant asserts that the landlord cannot terminate the lease without notice. Which Hohfeldian pair describes this?
law-jurisprudence.l19.q3.h: The landlord lacks the ability to change the relation.
law-jurisprudence.l19.q3.e: An immunity is freedom from having one's legal relations changed, correlating with the other's disability to change them.

law-jurisprudence.l19.q4.t: The interest theory, because rights protect interests and do not depend on the holder's power to waive or enforce
law-jurisprudence.l19.q4.p: Children seem to have rights though they cannot waive them. Which theory does this favor, and why?
law-jurisprudence.l19.q4.h: Think about who controls the duty.
law-jurisprudence.l19.q4.e: The interest theory explains rights of those who cannot exercise control. The will theory has trouble with such cases.

law-jurisprudence.l19.q5.t: It is a General Assembly declaration and not a treaty, while the 1966 Covenants are binding on ratifying states
law-jurisprudence.l19.q5.p: Which statement about the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) is accurate?
law-jurisprudence.l19.q5.h: Declarations and treaties differ in legal form.
law-jurisprudence.l19.q5.e: The UDHR is a declaration of the General Assembly. The 1966 Covenants are binding treaties for ratifying states.

law-jurisprudence.l20.q1.t: the positivist separation of what the law is from what it ought to be
law-jurisprudence.l20.q1.p: A judge who says a statute must be applied as written even though the result is harsh, leaving relief to the legislature, is most clearly echoing
law-jurisprudence.l20.q1.h: It separates law from its merits.
law-jurisprudence.l20.q1.e: Applying a harsh statute as written reflects the separation thesis. The other options reject or qualify that view.

law-jurisprudence.l20.q2.t: law and economics, since it compares the burden of precautions with the expected loss
law-jurisprudence.l20.q2.p: Judge Hand's negligence formula in Carroll Towing is best described as an early example of
law-jurisprudence.l20.q2.h: It compares costs and expected harm.
law-jurisprudence.l20.q2.e: The formula is a cost-benefit test. It predates the label law and economics.

law-jurisprudence.l20.q3.t: A Dworkinian sees a principle beside the rules, while a realist sees a policy choice and an economist an argument about incentives
law-jurisprudence.l20.q3.p: A court refuses to enforce a clause that lets a seller keep a deposit even when the seller's own wrong caused the failure, relying on good faith. How might different schools describe this?
law-jurisprudence.l20.q3.h: The same decision can be described in several vocabularies.
law-jurisprudence.l20.q3.e: The decision can be read as principle, policy or incentive reasoning. The other options misassign the schools.

law-jurisprudence.l20.q4.t: The use of both retributive and deterrence theories of punishment in testing a constitutional limit
law-jurisprudence.l20.q4.p: In Atkins v. Virginia, the Court said that the diminished culpability of people with intellectual disability weakens the retributive justification, and their reduced capacity for deliberation weakens deterrence. What does this illustrate?
law-jurisprudence.l20.q4.h: Think about the two theories mentioned.
law-jurisprudence.l20.q4.e: The Court applied both theories to ask whether the punishment serves its purposes for this class. The other options misidentify the reasoning.

law-jurisprudence.l20.q5.t: Judges often combine approaches, so a label should be treated as a question and not a conclusion
law-jurisprudence.l20.q5.p: Why does the lesson caution against over-labelling judicial opinions?
law-jurisprudence.l20.q5.e: The lesson says opinions often mix approaches, so labels should prompt questions. It does not claim theory is irrelevant.

law-legalwriting.l01.q1.t: A published opinion of a state supreme court deciding a dispute
law-legalwriting.l01.q1.p: Which of the following is primary authority?
law-legalwriting.l01.q1.h: Primary authority is the law itself, issued by a body with law-making power.
law-legalwriting.l01.q1.e: A court opinion is itself law. Law review articles, encyclopedias, and Restatements explain law and are secondary, however respected.

law-legalwriting.l01.q2.t: A decision of the Georgia Supreme Court on that contract question
law-legalwriting.l01.q2.p: A supervising attorney asks for mandatory authority in a Georgia trial court on a Georgia contract question. Which source qualifies?
law-legalwriting.l01.q2.h: Think about which courts sit above the trial court in the same system.
law-legalwriting.l01.q2.e: The highest court of the same state binds its lower courts. The California decision and a coordinate trial court decision are at most persuasive, and a treatise is secondary and never binding.

law-legalwriting.l01.q3.t: It supplies vocabulary and leads to primary authority that must then be read
law-legalwriting.l01.q3.p: Why should a researcher usually start with a secondary source in an unfamiliar area?
law-legalwriting.l01.q3.h: A map orients you but you do not cite it as the territory.
law-legalwriting.l01.q3.e: Secondary sources orient the researcher and point to law you must read yourself. They are not binding and may be out of date or wrong.

law-legalwriting.l01.q4.t: The rule is unsettled in the state because no court or legislature there has adopted it
law-legalwriting.l01.q4.p: A client asks whether a state recognizes a particular tort. The only support you find is a Restatement (Second) of Torts section and a law review article urging courts to adopt the rule. No decision in the state has addressed the tort. What is the most accurate assessment?
law-legalwriting.l01.q4.h: Who has the power to make law, and has that body spoken on the question?
law-legalwriting.l01.q4.e: Neither the Restatement nor a journal article is law until a court or legislature adopts the rule. The memo should report the question as open, not settled.

law-legalwriting.l01.q5.t: The footnote is dicta from an unrelated case, so it does not adopt the rule as law in the state
law-legalwriting.l01.q5.p: Fact pattern: Dana, a junior associate, writes that a rule is mandatory because it appears in a Restatement section her state supreme court discussed approvingly in a footnote of an unrelated case. The opposing party argues the rule is not law in the state. Which response is strongest?
law-legalwriting.l01.q5.h: Adoption requires a court to rely on the rule to decide a case.
law-legalwriting.l01.q5.e: A passing approving mention in an unrelated case is dicta and does not adopt the rule. The distractor that treats any statement as a holding confuses holdings with dicta.

law-legalwriting.l02.q1.t: The federal law prevails over the conflicting state law
law-legalwriting.l02.q1.p: Under the Supremacy Clause, what happens when valid federal law conflicts with state law?
law-legalwriting.l02.q1.h: Article VI of the Constitution speaks directly to this.
law-legalwriting.l02.q1.e: Valid federal law is supreme over conflicting state law. Recency and who sued first do not decide it.

law-legalwriting.l02.q2.t: It is vulnerable to being held invalid because it exceeds the agency's statutory authority
law-legalwriting.l02.q2.p: An agency regulation requires a permit that the authorizing statute does not allow the agency to require. How does the hierarchy treat this regulation?
law-legalwriting.l02.q2.h: An agency has only the power the legislature gave it.
law-legalwriting.l02.q2.e: Regulations rank below the statute that authorizes them. A rule beyond the grant of authority can be challenged and set aside.

law-legalwriting.l02.q3.t: The substantive law of the state, as declared by the state's courts
law-legalwriting.l02.q3.p: Under Erie Railroad Co. v. Tompkins, what law does a federal court apply to a state-law tort claim in diversity jurisdiction?
law-legalwriting.l02.q3.h: The case ended the era of a general federal common law for these claims.
law-legalwriting.l02.q3.e: Erie requires substantive state law, including state judicial decisions. A general federal common law was rejected, and Restatements are not binding in themselves.

law-legalwriting.l02.q4.t: It is persuasive evidence of Michigan law but the Michigan Supreme Court is the final authority
law-legalwriting.l02.q4.p: Fact pattern: Priya, a Michigan resident, sues Northline Corp., an Indiana company, in federal court in Michigan for breach of warranty under state law. The Michigan Supreme Court has not decided the precise warranty question, but the Sixth Circuit once predicted Michigan law on it. Which statement best describes the Sixth Circuit prediction?
law-legalwriting.l02.q4.h: Who has the last word on a state's own law?
law-legalwriting.l02.q4.e: A federal prediction of state law does not bind the state's courts, and the state's highest court has the final word on state law. The statement that federal rank controls confuses the federal hierarchy with state-law questions.

law-legalwriting.l02.q5.t: State substantive law supplies the claim, while federal procedure governs how the case is filed and litigated
law-legalwriting.l02.q5.p: Fact pattern: Marcus files a federal diversity suit on a state-law negligence claim. The defense moves to dismiss, arguing a state-court deadline for filing expert affidavits applies. Marcus argues the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure control the filing process. Which analysis is most consistent with the Erie framework as taught in introductory courses?
law-legalwriting.l02.q5.h: Erie sorts rules by function, not by the label on the courthouse.
law-legalwriting.l02.q5.e: The core idea is state substance and federal procedure, with hard cases where a rule is mixed. The first wrong choice overstates Erie and the second ignores it.

law-legalwriting.l03.q1.p: Which federal publication contains agency rules in a subject-organized, codified form?
law-legalwriting.l03.q1.h: Think about where rules are codified by topic, not announced day by day.
law-legalwriting.l03.q1.e: The CFR codifies agency rules by subject. The Federal Register publishes them day by day as they are issued or proposed.

law-legalwriting.l03.q2.t: Confirm the text and citation against the court's official source
law-legalwriting.l03.q2.p: You find a case on a free open-archive website and plan to quote it in a court filing. What is the best practice?
law-legalwriting.l03.q2.h: Official sources are better than aggregators.
law-legalwriting.l03.q2.e: Open archives are excellent for finding cases but may differ in coverage or formatting. Headnotes are editorial and never authoritative.

law-legalwriting.l03.q3.t: The online version is continuously updated and unofficial
law-legalwriting.l03.q3.p: Why does the eCFR carry a notice that the Federal Register and official CFR editions are authoritative?
law-legalwriting.l03.q3.h: Convenience and authority are not the same thing.
law-legalwriting.l03.q3.e: The eCFR is a regularly updated unofficial compilation. It contains final rules but the official published edition controls if they differ.

law-legalwriting.l03.q4.t: Read the statute on the legislature's site, then find cases interpreting its exact words
law-legalwriting.l03.q4.p: Fact pattern: Imani is a legal aid volunteer asked whether a tenant can cure a late rent payment under current state law. She finds a landlord-tenant blog post summarizing the statute, a free case archive containing a decision applying it, and the legislature's own website containing the statute. What is the soundest research order?
law-legalwriting.l03.q4.h: Start from the text of the law, then see how courts read it.
law-legalwriting.l03.q4.e: The statute is primary and official and the cases read it. The blog may lag amendments, and the archive case may predate a statutory change, so each needs checking.

law-legalwriting.l03.q5.t: PACER, the federal courts' electronic access system
law-legalwriting.l03.q5.p: Fact pattern: Tomas needs the actual filings in a federal case to see what motions were made. A free case-law archive gives him the judge's final opinion but not the briefs. Which resource is the authoritative source for the docket and the filings?
law-legalwriting.l03.q5.h: One system holds the dockets of the federal courts.
law-legalwriting.l03.q5.e: PACER is the court system's record of dockets and filings, with fees. The other three publish rules, regulations, or legislation, not court dockets.

law-legalwriting.l04.q1.t: What happened to the same case on appeal or review
law-legalwriting.l04.q1.p: What does subsequent history refer to?
law-legalwriting.l04.q1.h: It follows the very same litigation forward in time.
law-legalwriting.l04.q1.e: Subsequent history tracks the same case through appeals. How other cases treat the principle is called subsequent treatment.

law-legalwriting.l04.q2.t: It remains good law for its holding but you must show your facts match it
law-legalwriting.l04.q2.p: A decision you want to cite has been distinguished on its facts in several later cases. What is the proper conclusion?
law-legalwriting.l04.q2.h: Distinguishing is not the same as overruling.
law-legalwriting.l04.q2.e: To distinguish is to say the facts differ, not to reject the rule. The case may still be good authority where facts are similar.

law-legalwriting.l04.q3.t: The symbol cannot tell you whether the criticized part is the part you rely on
law-legalwriting.l04.q3.p: Why must you read later cases and not rely only on a warning symbol from a citator?
law-legalwriting.l04.q3.h: A case can be partly overruled or criticized on a different point.
law-legalwriting.l04.q3.e: A flag shows something happened but not what. A case can be overruled in part and remain good law for other propositions.

law-legalwriting.l04.q4.t: The Supreme Court overruled Chevron in Loper Bright (2024)
law-legalwriting.l04.q4.p: Fact pattern: An associate's brief for a 2026 case cites Chevron U.S.A. v. NRDC (1984) as controlling authority requiring a court to defer to an agency's reading of an ambiguous statute. What is the most serious problem?
law-legalwriting.l04.q4.h: Think about what the Court did in 2024.
law-legalwriting.l04.q4.e: Loper Bright overruled Chevron and requires courts to use independent judgment on statutory meaning. Chevron was a Supreme Court decision about agency interpretation, so the other claims are false.

law-legalwriting.l04.q5.t: Lena should not cite the vacated opinion as authority
law-legalwriting.l04.q5.p: Fact pattern: Lena relies on a 2008 federal appeals decision. Her check shows that in 2009 the same court granted rehearing en banc and vacated the panel opinion, then in 2010 issued a different en banc decision contradicting it. A coworker says the 2008 opinion is still usable because it was well reasoned. Who is right?
law-legalwriting.l04.q5.h: Vacatur wipes out the opinion's precedential effect.
law-legalwriting.l04.q5.e: A vacated opinion has no precedential force. The en banc decision states the court's law. Good reasoning does not restore binding effect.

law-legalwriting.l05.q1.t: A statement in the opinion that was not necessary to the result
law-legalwriting.l05.q1.p: What is dicta in a judicial opinion?
law-legalwriting.l05.q1.h: Ask whether the statement was needed to reach the result.
law-legalwriting.l05.q1.e: Dicta are remarks not necessary to the decision and are not binding. The holding is the part needed for the result, and the disposition is the final order.

law-legalwriting.l05.q2.t: It determines the standard of review and whether the court treated facts as assumed or as found
law-legalwriting.l05.q2.p: Why does procedural posture matter when reading a case?
law-legalwriting.l05.q2.h: A ruling on a motion to dismiss rests on different assumptions than a ruling after trial.
law-legalwriting.l05.q2.e: Posture tells you what the court was asked to do and how to treat facts, which controls the standard. The appealing party does not automatically win.

law-legalwriting.l05.q3.p: A court of appeals reverses a judgment and sends the case back to the trial court for further proceedings. Which term describes the disposition?
law-legalwriting.l05.q3.h: Reverse means the lower court was wrong; the other word means send back.
law-legalwriting.l05.q3.e: Reversing and remanding corrects the lower court and returns the case for further action. Overruled describes the rejection of a precedent, not a disposition of a case.

law-legalwriting.l05.q4.t: As dicta, which is persuasive from a high court but not binding
law-legalwriting.l05.q4.p: Fact pattern: In Hale v. Orchard Mutual, a state supreme court holds that a homeowner's policy excluded flood damage from a burst pipe because the policy language excluded water damage from outside sources, and the water came from a municipal main. The opinion adds that an inside pipe burst would probably be covered. Later, Nia sues on a policy with identical language after her own pipe burst. How should a lawyer treat the court's statement about inside pipes?
law-legalwriting.l05.q4.h: Was the inside pipe question needed to decide Hale?
law-legalwriting.l05.q4.e: The inside-pipe remark was not needed to decide a case about an outside source, so it is dicta, persuasive but not binding. Treating all supreme court statements as holdings is the common mistake.

law-legalwriting.l05.q5.t: The color of the building was not material to the court's reasoning
law-legalwriting.l05.q5.p: Fact pattern: A court denies a company's claim that a former employee breached a non-compete because the company never gave the employee a copy before he started work, and the court notes the employee's office was in a blue building. Two years later a lawyer cites the case for the idea that blue buildings are relevant to non-competes. Which criticism is strongest?
law-legalwriting.l05.q5.h: Ask which facts the court actually relied on.
law-legalwriting.l05.q5.e: Only facts the court treated as significant shape the rule. Courts often mention background facts that did no work in the reasoning.

law-legalwriting.l06.q1.t: Explanation, which shows how the rule has been applied in authority
law-legalwriting.l06.q1.p: In the CREAC structure, what does the E stand for?
law-legalwriting.l06.q1.h: It is the part that proves the rule means what you say it means.
law-legalwriting.l06.q1.e: Explanation uses cases and other authority to show how the rule has been applied. It is the step most often skipped by new writers.

law-legalwriting.l06.q2.t: Application connecting specific facts to the element
law-legalwriting.l06.q2.p: A writer states that an element is met and simply repeats the rule. What is missing?
law-legalwriting.l06.q2.h: A conclusion needs facts joined to rule language.
law-legalwriting.l06.q2.e: Application ties facts to the rule element by element. A string of citations or a quotation does not do the analytical work.

law-legalwriting.l06.q3.t: Address each element separately, applying the facts to each one in turn
law-legalwriting.l06.q3.p: A rule has three elements. What is the best way to write the analysis?
law-legalwriting.l06.q3.h: Elements must all be met, so each needs its own check.
law-legalwriting.l06.q3.e: Elements are cumulative requirements. Treating them separately lets the reader see which are strong and which are contested.

law-legalwriting.l06.q4.t: Explain what facts made the employee in that decision act within scope
law-legalwriting.l06.q4.p: Fact pattern: A memo reads: "Under the leading state supreme court decision on scope of employment, an employer is vicariously liable when an employee acts within the scope of employment. Driver was a delivery employee, so the company is liable." Which revision most improves the analysis?
law-legalwriting.l06.q4.h: What is missing between rule and conclusion?
law-legalwriting.l06.q4.e: The passage lacks explanation and application. Facts must be tied to how the rule was applied. Deleting the case removes the support, and an encyclopedia is secondary.

law-legalwriting.l06.q5.t: Open with the conclusion on probable cause, then state the rule
law-legalwriting.l06.q5.p: Fact pattern: A supervising attorney tells an associate that her draft section "has the right answer but I had to read three pages to find it." The section analyzes whether a warrant was supported by probable cause, beginning with a history of the Fourth Amendment. Which change best fits the CREAC approach?
law-legalwriting.l06.q5.h: The reader should learn your answer at the start.
law-legalwriting.l06.q5.e: CREAC front-loads the conclusion so the reader knows the destination. History first and block quotes delay the answer, which is what the supervisor complained about.

law-legalwriting.l07.q1.t: The general term is read to cover only things of the same kind as the listed items
law-legalwriting.l07.q1.p: What does ejusdem generis suggest about a general term at the end of a list of specific items?
law-legalwriting.l07.q1.h: Think about reading the catch-all in light of the list before it.
law-legalwriting.l07.q1.e: Ejusdem generis limits a general term to the same category as the specific words. It does not expand the term to everything.

law-legalwriting.l07.q2.t: Because it is not listed, a court might infer it was not meant to be covered
law-legalwriting.l07.q2.p: A statute lists "hammers, saws, and drills." What does expressio unius (the express mention of one excludes others) suggest about a lawn mower?
law-legalwriting.l07.q2.h: This canon reasons from what the legislature chose to list.
law-legalwriting.l07.q2.e: Expressio unius supports an inference of exclusion, but it is a presumption that can be outweighed. The idea that canons are binding rules is wrong.

law-legalwriting.l07.q3.p: Which approach to statutes begins with the ordinary meaning of the enacted words in context?
law-legalwriting.l07.q3.h: One method starts from the words and another from the legislature's aim.
law-legalwriting.l07.q3.e: Textualism focuses on the ordinary meaning of the text. Purposivism focuses on the problem the legislature meant to address.

law-legalwriting.l07.q4.t: Wheelchairs are used to assist mobility and are not like the listed recreational or transport items
law-legalwriting.l07.q4.p: Fact pattern: A town ordinance prohibits "vehicles, bicycles, skateboards, or other conveyances" in a plaza. The town cites Ravi, who was using a motorized wheelchair. The ordinance includes no definitions. Ravi's lawyer wants the strongest textual argument. Which is best?
law-legalwriting.l07.q4.h: Use the list to find the common feature of the specific words.
law-legalwriting.l07.q4.e: A canon-based reading argues the catch-all covers items of the same kind as those listed. The open-ended argument and the exemption argument both overreach the text.

law-legalwriting.l07.q5.t: It pits the ordinary meaning of the words against an argument from the statute's purpose
law-legalwriting.l07.q5.p: Fact pattern: A statute makes it unlawful to "use a firearm during a drug trafficking crime." A defendant bartered a gun as payment in a drug deal rather than carrying it for protection. Prosecutors argue the ordinary meaning of "use" covers it, while the defense argues the statute's purpose is to punish weapons that make drug crimes more dangerous. Which statement best describes the interpretive dispute?
law-legalwriting.l07.q5.h: Identify the two methods each side is using.
law-legalwriting.l07.q5.e: The parties argue text on one side and purpose on the other. Courts begin with text, and legislative history is at most a supporting tool.

law-legalwriting.l08.q1.t: Combining several cases into one statement of the rule that is consistent
law-legalwriting.l08.q1.h: No single case may state the whole rule.
law-legalwriting.l08.q1.e: Synthesis integrates holdings into one rule. Ignoring contrary cases or replacing cases with a Restatement does not synthesize.

law-legalwriting.l08.q2.t: A difference in facts that removes the reason the earlier court reached its result
law-legalwriting.l08.q2.p: Which distinction of a precedent is strongest?
law-legalwriting.l08.q2.h: A good distinction must matter under the court's own logic.
law-legalwriting.l08.q2.e: A meaningful distinction explains why the earlier reasoning does not apply. Names, dates, length, and style do not touch the rationale.

law-legalwriting.l08.q3.t: Address it, usually by distinguishing it on its facts or reasoning
law-legalwriting.l08.q3.p: An opposing party cites a mandatory case that hurts your client. What should an advocate do?
law-legalwriting.l08.q3.h: A mandatory case controls and cannot be ignored.
law-legalwriting.l08.q3.e: A mandatory case must be addressed, and distinguishing is the usual method. Concealing it risks a candor problem and loses credibility.

law-legalwriting.l08.q4.t: Notice is established, as in A, but the short time is like B
law-legalwriting.l08.q4.p: Fact pattern: In Case A a store was liable when it ignored a customer's repeated warnings about a wet floor for hours. In Case B a store was not liable when a spill occurred minutes before a fall. Joel slips on a spill that employees saw ten minutes before but had not yet cleaned because they were serving other customers. What is the best predicted analysis?
law-legalwriting.l08.q4.h: Identify which fact drove each case.
law-legalwriting.l08.q4.e: The cases suggest notice plus a reasonable time to act. Joel's facts share one feature with each, so the question is reasonableness. Exact factual identity is never required for analogy.

law-legalwriting.l08.q5.t: The prior State X decision binds the trial court and must be followed or distinguished
law-legalwriting.l08.q5.p: Fact pattern: A trial court in State X, in a state-law case, finds that a prior decision of the State X court of appeals is adverse. A coworker proposes arguing the prior decision should be ignored because a persuasive case from State Y reaches the opposite result and has better reasoning. Which response is most accurate?
law-legalwriting.l08.q5.h: Only a court with power can change a binding rule.
law-legalwriting.l08.q5.e: A trial court must follow binding state precedent, and the out-of-state case is persuasive only. A party may use it to urge a court with power to change the rule.

law-legalwriting.l09.q1.t: To give a direct short response to the question presented
law-legalwriting.l09.q1.p: What is the purpose of the brief answer in an objective memo?
law-legalwriting.l09.q1.h: A reader who stops here should know what you think.
law-legalwriting.l09.q1.e: The brief answer states the prediction and main reasons. Facts belong in the statement of facts and the research in the discussion.

law-legalwriting.l09.q2.t: State that the fact is unknown, say how each possibility would change the analysis, and recommend finding out
law-legalwriting.l09.q2.p: A key fact is unknown when the memo is written, and it could change the outcome. What is the best way to handle this?
law-legalwriting.l09.q2.h: Candor about gaps lets the supervisor decide what to do.
law-legalwriting.l09.q2.e: An objective memo flags unknown facts and their effects. Silent assumptions mislead the reader and can cause a poor strategy decision.

law-legalwriting.l09.q3.t: The reader needs an accurate prediction to advise the client and plan strategy
law-legalwriting.l09.q3.p: Why should an objective memo include arguments that hurt the client?
law-legalwriting.l09.q3.h: Think about who reads the memo and what they will do with it.
law-legalwriting.l09.q3.e: The audience is the supervising lawyer, who needs accurate risk information. The memo is internal and normally not filed or shared with opposing counsel.

law-legalwriting.l09.q4.t: She breached her duty of thorough, competent work by omitting adverse authority
law-legalwriting.l09.q4.p: Fact pattern: An associate's memo on whether her client's employer can enforce a non-compete says "the covenant is likely unenforceable" but omits a recent appellate decision upholding a similar covenant in the same state, because it hurts the conclusion. The partner relies on the memo and advises the client to take a competing job. What is the most accurate description of the associate's error?
law-legalwriting.l09.q4.h: The audience for a memo needs the whole picture.
law-legalwriting.l09.q4.e: Competence and thoroughness require reporting adverse authority in an objective memo. A memo is not an advocacy piece, and it is not filed with a court.

law-legalwriting.l09.q5.t: The memo is likely work product and may reveal confidential client information
law-legalwriting.l09.q5.p: Fact pattern: A law student posts an unredacted copy of a firm memo about a client's pending lawsuit on a public study forum to ask for feedback. Which concern is the most serious?
law-legalwriting.l09.q5.h: Think about what a client expects when sharing information with a lawyer.
law-legalwriting.l09.q5.e: Internal memos reflect confidential information and may be work product, so disclosure can harm the client. The idea that public posting cancels confidentiality gets the duty backwards.

law-legalwriting.l10.q1.t: It assumes they are true and asks whether they state a plausible claim
law-legalwriting.l10.q1.p: On a Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss, how does the court treat the complaint's well-pleaded facts?
law-legalwriting.l10.q1.h: No evidence is weighed at this stage.
law-legalwriting.l10.q1.e: On a motion to dismiss the facts alleged are taken as true, but conclusions are not. Credibility is for a trier of fact.

law-legalwriting.l10.q2.t: Judgment is proper if there is no genuine dispute of material fact
law-legalwriting.l10.q2.p: Which statement best captures the summary judgment standard under Rule 56?
law-legalwriting.l10.q2.h: The question is whether a trial is necessary.
law-legalwriting.l10.q2.e: Rule 56 asks whether there is a genuine material dispute. Judges do not weigh credibility, and plausibility is the pleading test.

law-legalwriting.l10.q3.t: They are not entitled to the assumption of truth
law-legalwriting.l10.q3.p: What is the effect of Twombly and Iqbal on conclusory allegations in a federal complaint?
law-legalwriting.l10.q3.h: The presumption of truth does not cover bare labels.
law-legalwriting.l10.q3.e: The Court held that labels and conclusions do not receive the presumption of truth. Only well-pleaded facts do.

law-legalwriting.l10.q4.t: The court is likely to dismiss because the allegation is a conclusion
law-legalwriting.l10.q4.p: Fact pattern: Ellis sues a bank in federal court, alleging only that the bank "discriminated against him in lending because of his race." The complaint does not describe the loan application, the bank's decision, or any comparison with other applicants. The bank moves to dismiss. What is the most likely outcome?
law-legalwriting.l10.q4.h: Ask whether the complaint pleads facts or labels.
law-legalwriting.l10.q4.e: A bare statement of discrimination is a conclusion. Summary judgment is a different motion that depends on the record, so it does not apply.

law-legalwriting.l10.q5.t: Deny the motion, because there is a genuine dispute of material fact
law-legalwriting.l10.q5.p: Fact pattern: In a contract case, the defendant moves for summary judgment. The plaintiff submits a sworn declaration that the parties orally agreed to a delivery date, and the defendant's officer swears the opposite. The defendant argues that the officer is more credible because she kept notes. How should the court rule?
law-legalwriting.l10.q5.h: A judge does not weigh credibility at this stage.
law-legalwriting.l10.q5.e: Conflicting sworn accounts on a material fact create a genuine dispute. Summary judgment is available in contract cases when no genuine dispute exists.

law-legalwriting.l11.q1.t: A full-sentence statement of the conclusion the writer wants the court to reach
law-legalwriting.l11.q1.p: What is a point heading in a brief?
law-legalwriting.l11.q1.h: Headings should persuade even if the reader skims only them.
law-legalwriting.l11.q1.e: Point headings are argumentative sentences combining the rule and key facts, so a skim shows the argument.

law-legalwriting.l11.q2.t: Emphasize favorable facts and place unfavorable ones in context
law-legalwriting.l11.q2.p: Which approach to the statement of facts is consistent with both persuasion and honesty?
law-legalwriting.l11.q2.h: Emphasis is allowed; distortion is not.
law-legalwriting.l11.q2.e: A persuasive statement may shape emphasis and order but cannot misstate or hide material facts. A neutral listing wastes the chance to persuade.

law-legalwriting.l11.q3.t: A reasonable inquiry confirming that the legal contentions are warranted
law-legalwriting.l11.q3.p: What does Rule 11 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure require of an attorney who signs a filing?
law-legalwriting.l11.q3.h: The signature is a certification about the filing's basis.
law-legalwriting.l11.q3.e: Rule 11 imposes a certification of reasonable inquiry, which supports sanctions for frivolous filings. It does not guarantee outcomes or require disclosure of privileged communications.

law-legalwriting.l11.q4.t: The court may discount the entire brief and the lawyer may face sanctions
law-legalwriting.l11.q4.p: Fact pattern: A brief for a landlord says the tenant "lied" and calls the trial judge's ruling "absurd and shameful," while citing a case for a rule the case did not hold. Opposing counsel points out the miscitation. What is the likely effect?
law-legalwriting.l11.q4.h: Judges rely on lawyers to describe the law accurately.
law-legalwriting.l11.q4.e: Overstatement and inaccurate citation damage credibility and may violate Rule 11 and professional duties. Courts do not rely on the opposing party to correct a misstatement.

law-legalwriting.l11.q5.t: Heading two, because it joins the rule to the key facts
law-legalwriting.l11.q5.p: Fact pattern: A tenant's attorney writes two possible headings. Heading one: "The Warranty of Habitability." Heading two: "Because the landlord ignored three written repair requests over a month, he breached the warranty of habitability." Which is stronger and why?
law-legalwriting.l11.q5.h: A heading should persuade even when it is read alone.
law-legalwriting.l11.q5.e: Heading two tells the judge what to conclude and why. Heading one is a topic label and gives no argument, and heading two does include the rule.

law-legalwriting.l12.q1.p: Which standard of review applies to a pure question of law, such as statutory interpretation?
law-legalwriting.l12.q1.h: The appellate court gives no deference to the lower court.
law-legalwriting.l12.q1.e: Questions of law are reviewed de novo. Clear error applies to fact findings by a judge, and abuse of discretion to discretionary rulings.

law-legalwriting.l12.q2.t: Clear error, because the trial judge saw and heard the witnesses
law-legalwriting.l12.q2.p: A trial judge, after a bench trial, finds that a witness was credible and that a contract was signed under pressure. On appeal, what is the standard for the finding of fact?
law-legalwriting.l12.q2.h: The reason for deference is the trial judge's vantage point.
law-legalwriting.l12.q2.e: Facts found after a bench trial are reviewed for clear error. Appellate courts do not retry credibility from a transcript.

law-legalwriting.l12.q3.t: Because the appellate court will review it without deference to the lower court
law-legalwriting.l12.q3.p: Why might an appellant try to frame an issue as a question of law?
law-legalwriting.l12.q3.h: Deference helps the party who won below.
law-legalwriting.l12.q3.e: Legal questions get de novo review, which is friendlier to an appellant than clear error. Courts will still examine whether the label is honest.

law-legalwriting.l12.q4.t: The finding is reviewed for clear error, and mere disagreement with the weight of testimony is not enough
law-legalwriting.l12.q4.p: Fact pattern: After a bench trial, Judge Reyes finds that a bakery owner told a supplier that a delivery was cancelled, and rules for the supplier on that basis. The owner appeals, saying the testimony of the supplier's witness was weak and he would have decided differently. Which is the strongest response for the supplier?
law-legalwriting.l12.q4.h: Think about what makes a finding clearly erroneous.
law-legalwriting.l12.q4.e: A finding is not clearly erroneous just because the reviewing court would weigh evidence differently. De novo review would give no deference, so it is the wrong standard.

law-legalwriting.l12.q5.t: Review the ultimate probable cause conclusion de novo
law-legalwriting.l12.q5.p: Fact pattern: In a criminal appeal, the trial judge found that officers saw the defendant hand something to another person in a parking lot known for drug sales, and then ruled that the officers had probable cause to search. On appeal, the defendant challenges the conclusion of probable cause. Under Ornelas v. United States, what is the right approach?
law-legalwriting.l12.q5.h: The mixed question is split into facts and the legal conclusion.
law-legalwriting.l12.q5.e: Ornelas separates historical facts (clear error) from the legal conclusion of probable cause (de novo). The all-de novo approach is wrong because it ignores deference to fact findings.

law-legalwriting.l13.q1.t: Directs the reader to the exact page or paragraph supporting the statement
law-legalwriting.l13.q1.p: What does a pinpoint citation do?
law-legalwriting.l13.q1.h: The name says what the source is; the pinpoint says where in it.
law-legalwriting.l13.q1.e: A pinpoint locates the supporting passage. Subsequent history appears in a separate parenthetical, and a pinpoint does not replace the full citation.

law-legalwriting.l13.q2.p: A case does not directly state your proposition but clearly supports it by implication. Which signal is most appropriate?
law-legalwriting.l13.q2.h: No signal means direct statement; this source is one step removed.
law-legalwriting.l13.q2.e: See is used when the source clearly supports the proposition without stating it directly. Contra and but see indicate opposition, and no signal indicates a direct statement.

law-legalwriting.l13.q3.t: Id. refers only to the immediately preceding authority, so it would point to the inserted source
law-legalwriting.l13.q3.p: Why is it risky to use id. when a new citation has been inserted between the original source and the line using id.?
law-legalwriting.l13.q3.h: The word depends on what comes immediately before it.
law-legalwriting.l13.q3.e: Id. means the immediately preceding authority, so editing can silently change its referent. It is allowed in major systems.

law-legalwriting.l13.q4.t: Use cf. or a parenthetical explaining that the case addressed judgment as a matter of law and reasoned by analogy
law-legalwriting.l13.q4.p: Fact pattern: A brief says a court "may not weigh credibility on a summary judgment motion" and cites a circuit case that actually held that credibility may not be weighed on a motion for judgment as a matter of law, a related but different procedure. The writer wants to be accurate about the source's strength. Which choice is best?
law-legalwriting.l13.q4.h: The signal should tell the truth about how the source relates.
law-legalwriting.l13.q4.e: Cf. flags analogous support. No signal overstates the match, and contra would wrongly signal direct opposition.

law-legalwriting.l13.q5.t: A court's own rules on citation form control over a school's or manual's format
law-legalwriting.l13.q5.p: Fact pattern: A state's trial court rules require citation in a particular format, but a junior lawyer uses the format she learned in school for a brief to be filed there. The supervising attorney asks her to change it. What principle best explains the supervisor's request?
law-legalwriting.l13.q5.h: Who sets the rules of the forum?
law-legalwriting.l13.q5.e: Courts may specify their own citation formats and filings should follow them. No single manual is mandatory everywhere.

law-legalwriting.l14.q1.t: A covenant is a promise to do something, while a condition is an event that must occur first
law-legalwriting.l14.q1.p: What is the difference between a covenant and a condition in a contract?
law-legalwriting.l14.q1.h: One is a promise and the other is a trigger.
law-legalwriting.l14.q1.e: A covenant is a promise and its breach gives a remedy. A condition determines whether a duty arises or must be performed.

law-legalwriting.l14.q2.t: The Seller shall deliver the Goods to the Buyer's warehouse within ten days
law-legalwriting.l14.q2.p: Which revision best fixes the sentence "The Seller shall deliver promptly after payment"?
law-legalwriting.l14.q2.h: Replace vague words with a deadline, place and trigger.
law-legalwriting.l14.q2.e: The best revision supplies a measurable deadline, a place, and a defined trigger. The others keep vague terms such as as soon as possible or best efforts.

law-legalwriting.l14.q3.t: Evidence of prior or contemporaneous agreements is barred if offered to contradict or add to the written terms
law-legalwriting.l14.q3.p: What is the general effect of a fully integrated written contract under the parol evidence rule?
law-legalwriting.l14.q3.h: The writing is treated as the final statement of the deal.
law-legalwriting.l14.q3.e: The rule bars evidence that contradicts or supplements an integrated writing, with exceptions such as fraud, mistake, and interpretation. It does not forbid interpreting ambiguous terms.

law-legalwriting.l14.q4.t: The oral promise is likely barred if the writing is fully integrated
law-legalwriting.l14.q4.p: Fact pattern: A bakery signs a written agreement to buy flour from a mill. The agreement contains an integration clause. The bakery's owner later claims the mill's sales representative orally promised, before signing, that the mill would never raise prices during the first year. The written agreement says nothing on price changes. What is the most likely result on the claim that the oral promise is part of the contract?
law-legalwriting.l14.q4.h: A merger clause signals that the writing is the whole deal.
law-legalwriting.l14.q4.e: A fully integrated writing generally excludes prior terms that add to it, subject to exceptions. Silence in the writing does not by itself open the door.

law-legalwriting.l14.q5.t: The undefined phrase best efforts, which courts interpret inconsistently
law-legalwriting.l14.q5.p: Fact pattern: A vendor's form says the vendor "shall use best efforts to deliver on time" and does not define best efforts. The vendor delivers late because it chose to fill a larger customer's order first. The buyer sues. What drafting weakness most contributes to the dispute?
law-legalwriting.l14.q5.h: Phrases courts read differently invite litigation.
law-legalwriting.l14.q5.e: Courts differ about what best efforts requires, so the term should be defined or replaced with specific obligations. Shall is common in contracts, and delivery terms are normal.

law-legalwriting.l15.q1.t: States that if one provision is held invalid, the remaining provisions stay in effect
law-legalwriting.l15.q1.p: What does a severability clause do?
law-legalwriting.l15.q1.h: Think about what happens when only part of a law fails.
law-legalwriting.l15.q1.e: A severability clause preserves the rest of a law if part is struck. Courts consider it but are not bound by it.

law-legalwriting.l15.q2.t: The Department shall issue a permit within thirty days
law-legalwriting.l15.q2.p: Which sentence is best drafted for a statute?
law-legalwriting.l15.q2.h: Name the actor and use a clear verb and deadline.
law-legalwriting.l15.q2.e: The best draft uses an active voice, names the actor, and sets a deadline. The others use passive voice, vague time, or permissive language.

law-legalwriting.l15.q3.t: Different words in a statute may be read by a court to mean different things
law-legalwriting.l15.q3.p: Why should a statute's drafter define a key term only once and use it consistently?
law-legalwriting.l15.q3.h: Courts presume that different words carry different meanings.
law-legalwriting.l15.q3.e: Inconsistent terms invite arguments that the legislature meant different things. Definitions can appear in different places, and they matter in interpretation.

law-legalwriting.l15.q4.t: Define the covered devices and expressly exclude devices used for mobility
law-legalwriting.l15.q4.p: Fact pattern: A city council passes an ordinance: "No person shall operate a motor vehicle, motorcycle, or other conveyance in Riverside Park." A resident in a motorized wheelchair is cited. The council intended to ban recreational vehicles, not mobility devices. Which drafting change would have best prevented the problem?
law-legalwriting.l15.q4.h: Use definitions and exceptions to match text to purpose.
law-legalwriting.l15.q4.e: A definition plus an express exclusion ties the text to the council's purpose. Open-ended wording would broaden the problem, and may would make the rule permissive.

law-legalwriting.l15.q5.t: The regulation exceeds the authority granted by the statute, so it is invalid
law-legalwriting.l15.q5.p: Fact pattern: A state agency adopts a regulation requiring licensing of tutors. The authorizing statute allows the agency to regulate only schools and does not mention tutors. A tutor challenges the rule. What is the strongest argument?
law-legalwriting.l15.q5.h: An agency has only the power the legislature gave it.
law-legalwriting.l15.q5.e: A regulation must stay within its enabling statute. The claim that regulations outrank statutes reverses the hierarchy.

law-legalwriting.l16.q1.t: A verb turned into a noun, such as make a decision for decide
law-legalwriting.l16.q1.e: Nominalization turns an action into a noun and usually weakens the sentence. Preferring the verb is shorter and clearer.

law-legalwriting.l16.q2.t: It has a precise legal meaning that a substitute everyday word might change
law-legalwriting.l16.q2.p: Why might a lawyer keep a term of art such as consideration, even in plain-language writing?
law-legalwriting.l16.q2.e: Terms of art carry settled meanings, so replacing them risks changing the substance. Use them where needed and explain them for lay readers.

law-legalwriting.l16.q3.t: The defendant argues that the plaintiff cannot recover because she did not give timely notice
law-legalwriting.l16.q3.p: Which is the best plain-language revision of "It is the position of the Defendant that Plaintiff's failure to timely give notice results in a bar to recovery"?
law-legalwriting.l16.q3.h: Active verb, short sentence, same substance.
law-legalwriting.l16.q3.e: The first revision is active and shorter, with the same substance. The others retain legalese, nominalization, or passive structure.

law-legalwriting.l16.q4.t: Clear notices help recipients understand their rights and deadlines
law-legalwriting.l16.q4.p: Fact pattern: A landlord's eviction notice is a dense paragraph of legalese that tells tenants they must "cure the default or surrender possession forthwith pursuant to the aforementioned provisions." Many tenants do not understand it and fail to respond within the deadline, then lose their homes. Which argument best supports a plain-language reform?
law-legalwriting.l16.q4.h: Think about the purpose of a notice.
law-legalwriting.l16.q4.e: A notice aims to inform, and clarity improves comprehension and fairness. The other claims are not accurate.

law-legalwriting.l16.q5.t: Edit in passes, checking substance and structure first, then sentences
law-legalwriting.l16.q5.p: Fact pattern: A junior lawyer edits a brief only by proofreading for typos right after finishing the draft, and the partner finds a missing element and a disorganized argument. Which editing practice would best address the problem?
law-legalwriting.l16.q5.e: Editing in layers catches substance and structure issues before polish. Proofreading alone cannot fix a missing element or poor organization.

law-legalwriting.l17.q1.t: With yes or no, followed by the explanation
law-legalwriting.l17.q1.p: How should an advocate usually begin an answer to a judge's yes-or-no question at oral argument?
law-legalwriting.l17.q1.h: Judges may not give you time to get to the point.
law-legalwriting.l17.q1.e: Answering directly first respects the judge's time and builds credibility. Deferring or restating the brief wastes the opportunity.

law-legalwriting.l17.q2.t: Concede what must be conceded and explain why it does not decide the case
law-legalwriting.l17.q2.p: A judge points to a real weakness in your client's position. What is the most effective response?
law-legalwriting.l17.q2.e: Honest concession with an explanation of why the case still favors you preserves trust. Denial of an obvious weakness costs credibility.

law-legalwriting.l17.q3.t: One or two of the opponent's most important points
law-legalwriting.l17.q3.e: Rebuttal answers the most important points of the opponent. Repeating the argument or adding a new theory wastes limited time.

law-legalwriting.l17.q4.t: The answer is weak because the judge is testing the rule's limits
law-legalwriting.l17.q4.p: Fact pattern: At argument, Judge Alvarez asks appellant's counsel, "If I adopt your rule, would a landlord who made repairs within two days still be liable?" Counsel answers, "That is not our case, Your Honor," and returns to prepared remarks. Which assessment is most accurate?
law-legalwriting.l17.q4.h: Why would a judge ask about a different set of facts?
law-legalwriting.l17.q4.e: Judges use hypotheticals to see how far a rule extends, so avoiding them undermines the argument. Hypotheticals are common and proper.

law-legalwriting.l17.q5.t: Say she is not certain, offer to provide the exact cite promptly if the court permits, and avoid guessing
law-legalwriting.l17.q5.p: Fact pattern: A judge asks counsel where in the record a witness admitted knowing about a defect. Counsel is unsure and says, "I believe it is at page 112," though she has not checked. The page does not contain the admission. What is the best approach she should have taken?
law-legalwriting.l17.q5.e: Accuracy about the record is essential and a guessed cite risks a misstatement to the court. Saying she will supply it preserves credibility.

law-legalwriting.l18.q1.t: Disclose directly adverse authority in the controlling jurisdiction that opposing counsel has not cited
law-legalwriting.l18.q1.p: Under Model Rule 3.3, which duty applies to adverse authority?
law-legalwriting.l18.q1.h: The duty is limited by jurisdiction and directness.
law-legalwriting.l18.q1.e: The model rule requires disclosure of directly adverse controlling authority not disclosed by opposing counsel. It does not require citing every unfavorable case.

law-legalwriting.l18.q2.t: Take reasonable remedial measures, including disclosure to the tribunal if necessary
law-legalwriting.l18.q2.p: A lawyer offers a witness's testimony and later learns, with knowledge, that a material part was false. What does Rule 3.3 require?
law-legalwriting.l18.q2.h: The duty continues until the proceeding ends.
law-legalwriting.l18.q2.e: Rule 3.3 requires remedial measures, including disclosure if needed, and overrides ordinary confidentiality in this setting.

law-legalwriting.l18.q3.t: A defendant has no constitutional right to present perjured testimony
law-legalwriting.l18.q3.p: What did the Supreme Court hold in Nix v. Whiteside (1986)?
law-legalwriting.l18.q3.h: The case involved a defense lawyer who resisted false testimony.
law-legalwriting.l18.q3.e: The Court held there is no right to present perjury and that counsel's response was not ineffective assistance. It did not create a duty to disclose to the prosecutor.

law-legalwriting.l18.q4.t: Lena must disclose the decision to the court even though opposing counsel did not cite it
law-legalwriting.l18.q4.p: Fact pattern: Lena represents a landlord in a state trial court. Her research uncovers a decision of the state's highest court holding that the exact lease clause her client relies on is unenforceable. Opposing counsel did not cite it. Lena's supervisor says to leave it out and hope the judge does not find it. Which analysis is correct under the model rule?
law-legalwriting.l18.q4.h: Is the decision controlling and directly adverse?
law-legalwriting.l18.q4.e: A directly adverse controlling decision must be disclosed even if the opponent missed it. The lawyer may still argue about its reach or ask for change.

law-legalwriting.l18.q5.t: Take reasonable measures to correct the false statement to the court
law-legalwriting.l18.q5.p: Fact pattern: In a deposition summary filed with a court, an attorney, Omar, states that a witness never denied receiving a warning letter. He later realizes the transcript shows the witness did deny it. No one has noticed. What does the duty of candor require?
law-legalwriting.l18.q5.h: The duty to correct applies to the lawyer's own earlier statements.
law-legalwriting.l18.q5.e: Rule 3.3 requires correcting a false statement of material fact the lawyer previously made. Lack of intent at the time does not excuse leaving it uncorrected, and destroying the transcript would be worse.

law-legalwriting.l19.q1.t: The signing lawyer, regardless of who or what produced the draft
law-legalwriting.l19.q1.p: Who is responsible for the accuracy of citations in a filing signed by a lawyer?
law-legalwriting.l19.q1.e: The signing lawyer is responsible for the filing. Tools and staff can assist but responsibility cannot be delegated away.

law-legalwriting.l19.q2.t: Lawyers were sanctioned for filing citations to nonexistent cases generated by an AI tool
law-legalwriting.l19.q2.p: What happened in Mata v. Avianca, Inc. (S.D.N.Y. 2023)?
law-legalwriting.l19.q2.h: The case is a warning about unverified output.
law-legalwriting.l19.q2.e: The court sanctioned lawyers who submitted fabricated citations without verification. It did not ban technology.

law-legalwriting.l19.q3.t: It may disclose confidential information to a third party depending on the tool's terms and settings
law-legalwriting.l19.q3.p: Why is entering confidential client details into an online AI tool potentially a problem?
law-legalwriting.l19.q3.h: Think about Rule 1.6 and where the data goes.
law-legalwriting.l19.q3.e: Confidentiality duties require reasonable efforts to protect client information, and a tool's data practices matter. A blanket waiver or prohibition is not the rule.

law-legalwriting.l19.q4.t: He failed his duty of competence by not verifying the citations
law-legalwriting.l19.q4.p: Fact pattern: A solo practitioner uses a chatbot to draft a motion and receives six case citations with quotations. He checks that each case name looks plausible and files the motion. Three cases do not exist, and two are misdescribed. Which statement best describes his conduct?
law-legalwriting.l19.q4.e: Verification means locating the actual document and confirming content and status. A plausible name proves nothing, and using technology is not itself improper.

law-legalwriting.l19.q5.t: Review the terms, assess confidentiality risks, and limit the client information entered unless adequate protections exist
law-legalwriting.l19.q5.p: Fact pattern: A firm adopts a new AI drafting tool. A partner wants staff to paste whole client files into it to save time. The tool's terms allow the vendor to use inputs to train its models. What is the most defensible course of action?
law-legalwriting.l19.q5.h: Competence and confidentiality require informed choices.
law-legalwriting.l19.q5.e: The lawyer must understand how the tool handles data and take reasonable steps. Unrestricted use ignores confidentiality, and a permanent ban is not required by the rules.

law-legalwriting.l20.q1.t: A basis in law and fact that is not frivolous
law-legalwriting.l20.q1.h: Novel is not the same as frivolous.
law-legalwriting.l20.q1.e: Rule 3.1 requires a non-frivolous basis, which can include good faith arguments to extend or change the law. A lawyer need not personally agree with the client.

law-legalwriting.l20.q2.t: Rule 3.4 bars asserting personal opinion on the justness of a cause
law-legalwriting.l20.q2.p: Why do lawyers generally avoid saying "I believe" or "in my opinion" about the justness of the client's case in court?
law-legalwriting.l20.q2.h: The argument should rest on the record and law.
law-legalwriting.l20.q2.e: Rule 3.4 limits personal opinion in trial advocacy so that arguments rest on evidence and law rather than the lawyer's credibility.

law-legalwriting.l20.q3.t: Telling the other side your client has a signed competing offer when no such offer exists
law-legalwriting.l20.q3.p: Which statement made during negotiation is most clearly a violation of Rule 4.1?
law-legalwriting.l20.q3.e: Inventing a competing offer is a false statement of material fact. Bargaining positions, opinions about a case, and declining to reveal confidences are ordinarily acceptable.

law-legalwriting.l20.q4.t: The lawyer may not assist; destroying evidence is prohibited
law-legalwriting.l20.q4.p: Fact pattern: Dev represents a defendant in a product case. His client, a manufacturer, asks him to quietly delete internal safety emails from the company's server before the plaintiff's discovery requests arrive. A lawsuit is already pending. What is the correct analysis?
law-legalwriting.l20.q4.h: Think about Rule 3.4 and the officer-of-court duty.
law-legalwriting.l20.q4.e: Rule 3.4 bars unlawfully altering or destroying evidence, and a lawyer may not assist client fraud or crime. Ownership and zealous advocacy do not override these limits.

law-legalwriting.l20.q5.t: She may represent the landlord if the position has a non-frivolous basis
law-legalwriting.l20.q5.p: Fact pattern: Priya, an associate, is asked to defend a landlord in an eviction she personally thinks is unfair, though the landlord has a legitimate legal basis under the lease and statute. A colleague says she must refuse because lawyers must believe in their cases. How should the situation be analyzed?
law-legalwriting.l20.q5.h: The rules turn on the legal basis, not the lawyer's feelings.
law-legalwriting.l20.q5.e: Representing a client does not endorse the client's views, and a non-frivolous basis is what matters. Personal disagreement is not itself a conflict, and she must not misstate her beliefs.

law-prek2.l01.q1.t: To help everyone stay safe and have fun together
law-prek2.l01.q1.p: What is the main reason we have rules on a playground?
law-prek2.l01.q1.h: Think about what could happen if everyone pushed on the slide.
law-prek2.l01.q1.e: Playground rules keep children from getting hurt so that everyone can play. The rules are not meant to spoil fun.

law-prek2.l01.q2.t: Grown-ups have rules to follow too, like stopping at a red light
law-prek2.l01.q2.p: Which sentence about rules is true?
law-prek2.l01.q2.h: Think about a bus driver at a red light.
law-prek2.l01.q2.e: Rules are for everybody, including grown-ups. A rule is for a good reason, not just a punishment.

law-prek2.l01.q3.t: Rules give everyone the same plan, so the game can work
law-prek2.l01.q3.p: A game of tag has no agreed rules, and players disagree about who is "it." What does this show?
law-prek2.l01.q3.h: What would happen if each person had a different plan?
law-prek2.l01.q3.e: Shared rules mean everyone knows the plan. Without them, players argue and the game falls apart.

law-prek2.l01.q4.t: Ask a grown-up kindly why we have that rule
law-prek2.l01.q4.p: You do not understand why a rule exists. What is a good thing to do?
law-prek2.l01.q4.h: A kind question is a smart way to learn.
law-prek2.l01.q4.e: Asking kindly is a respectful way to learn the reason. Good rules usually have a reason.

law-prek2.l02.q1.t: Running in a crowded hallway can make children bump or fall
law-prek2.l02.q1.p: Why might a school hallway have a rule that says "walk" while a park does not?
law-prek2.l02.q1.h: Think about how many people share a hallway.
law-prek2.l02.q1.e: Different places have different rules because the risks are different. A narrow hallway is a poor place to run.

law-prek2.l02.q2.t: Do not take things that belong to someone else
law-prek2.l02.q2.p: Which of these is a rule that is almost the same everywhere?
law-prek2.l02.q2.h: Think of a rule that keeps people safe and happy in any place.
law-prek2.l02.q2.e: Not taking what belongs to others is a basic rule for living with other people almost anywhere.

law-prek2.l02.q3.t: Look around and ask a grown-up, "What are the rules here?"
law-prek2.l02.q3.p: You visit a new place and you are not sure what the rules are. What is a good choice?
law-prek2.l02.q3.h: Rules can be different from the ones you know.
law-prek2.l02.q3.e: Looking, listening and asking helps you follow the rules of a new place so that you stay safe and kind.

law-prek2.l02.q4.t: A rule that is written or shown on a sign
law-prek2.l02.q4.p: A stop sign is an example of which kind of rule?
law-prek2.l02.q4.h: Think about how drivers know to stop.
law-prek2.l02.q4.e: A stop sign puts a rule where people can see it, so drivers know what to do.

law-prek2.l03.q1.t: Take turns, so each child gets a chance
law-prek2.l03.q1.p: There is one swing and many children. What is a fair way to share it?
law-prek2.l03.q1.h: Think about how everyone can get a chance.
law-prek2.l03.q1.e: Taking turns gives each child a chance, which makes it fair. A timer can help.

law-prek2.l03.q2.t: Count to ten and watch the person who is going now
law-prek2.l03.q2.p: What can help while you wait for your turn?
law-prek2.l03.q2.h: Waiting is hard, so calm tricks are useful.
law-prek2.l03.q2.e: Counting and watching are calm ways to wait. Grabbing or rushing is not fair to the other child.

law-prek2.l03.q3.t: It is the same for every child, so it feels fair
law-prek2.l03.q3.p: Why is a timer a good tool for taking turns?
law-prek2.l03.q3.h: Think about whether the timer picks favorites.
law-prek2.l03.q3.e: A timer treats each child the same, which is why it helps with fairness.

law-prek2.l03.q4.t: Turns go one at a time; sharing lets someone else use or have some of it
law-prek2.l03.q4.p: What is the difference between taking turns and sharing?
law-prek2.l03.q4.h: One is about order. The other is about letting others have some.
law-prek2.l03.q4.e: Taking turns is going one after another. Sharing is letting others use something or giving part of it. Both are fair and kind.

law-prek2.l04.q1.t: No, because everyone who did the work should get one
law-prek2.l04.q1.p: A teacher gives stickers to some children who did the work, but skips others who did the work, just because she likes them less. Is that fair?
law-prek2.l04.q1.h: Ask if everyone is being treated the same for the same work.
law-prek2.l04.q1.e: It is unfair to treat someone worse for no good reason. All the children who did the work should get a sticker.

law-prek2.l04.q2.t: Give each child shoes that fit them
law-prek2.l04.q2.p: Two children need shoes. One needs a small size and one needs a big size. What is fair?
law-prek2.l04.q2.h: Fair can mean getting what you need.
law-prek2.l04.q2.e: Fair does not always mean exactly the same. Each child gets what they need so that the shoes work.

law-prek2.l04.q3.t: It is unfair, because the others did not agree to the change
law-prek2.l04.q3.p: In a game, one player changes the rules in the middle so only he can win. The others never agreed. What is the problem?
law-prek2.l04.q3.h: Who got to have a say?
law-prek2.l04.q3.e: Changing the rules secretly in your own favor is unfair. Rule changes should be agreed together.

law-prek2.l04.q4.t: "Is everyone getting a chance, and are we being kind?"
law-prek2.l04.q4.p: What can you ask yourself when something might be unfair?
law-prek2.l04.q4.h: The question is about everyone, not just you.
law-prek2.l04.q4.e: Asking whether everyone gets a chance and whether we are kind helps us spot what is unfair.

law-prek2.l05.q1.t: People make rules, so people can change them too
law-prek2.l05.q1.p: Who is it that makes up the rules we follow?
law-prek2.l05.q1.e: Rules are made by people, and people can change a rule when it is not working.

law-prek2.l05.q2.t: Talk about it together and make a better rule
law-prek2.l05.q2.p: A class gets bigger and the art table rule of "two at a time" is too small. What is a good thing to do?
law-prek2.l05.q2.h: Listening to each other helps rules get better.
law-prek2.l05.q2.e: When a rule is not working, people can talk and agree on a better one.

law-prek2.l05.q3.t: Wait for a calm moment and tell a grown-up kindly
law-prek2.l05.q3.p: You think a rule is unfair. What is the best way to handle it?
law-prek2.l05.q3.h: Calm and kind words are most likely to be heard.
law-prek2.l05.q3.e: Speaking up calmly lets a grown-up listen, and it keeps everyone safe while the rule is talked about.

law-prek2.l05.q4.t: Holding a grown-up's hand when you cross a busy road, because it keeps you safe
law-prek2.l05.q4.p: Which rule is least likely to be changed, and why?
law-prek2.l05.q4.e: Some rules, like safety rules, stay for a long time because they protect us. Other rules about small things can change easily.

law-prek2.l06.q1.p: What does it mean to tell the truth?
law-prek2.l06.q1.h: Truth is about what is real.
law-prek2.l06.q1.e: Telling the truth means saying what really happened, even when it is hard.

law-prek2.l06.q2.t: "I bumped it by accident, and I can help clean up."
law-prek2.l06.q2.p: You bumped the table by accident and juice spilled. What is the best thing to say?
law-prek2.l06.q2.e: Telling the truth about an accident usually makes grown-ups glad you were honest. A lie makes the problem bigger.

law-prek2.l06.q3.t: It is hard to trust them, even when they tell the truth
law-prek2.l06.q3.p: Why does it matter if a person tells lies a lot?
law-prek2.l06.q3.e: Trust means you can count on a person. Lies make it harder for others to believe what you say.

law-prek2.l06.q4.p: A friend shows you a picture that you do not love. Which answer is both true and kind?
law-prek2.l06.q4.h: You can be honest without being mean.
law-prek2.l06.q4.e: You can say something that is both true and kind. Being honest does not mean being unkind.

law-prek2.l07.q1.t: Ask, "May I please use your truck?"
law-prek2.l07.q1.p: What should you do before you use a friend's truck?
law-prek2.l07.q1.h: The first step is a polite question.
law-prek2.l07.q1.e: Asking first shows respect. The owner can say yes or no.

law-prek2.l07.q2.t: Using something for a while and then giving it back
law-prek2.l07.q2.e: Borrowing means you use something for a short time, take care of it, and return it.

law-prek2.l07.q3.t: "Okay." Then find something else to play with
law-prek2.l07.q3.p: Your friend says no when you ask to use her toy. What is a good response?
law-prek2.l07.q3.e: The owner can say no. Accepting that is respectful, and you can find something else to do.

law-prek2.l07.q4.t: Give it to a grown-up so the owner can find it
law-prek2.l07.q4.p: You find a mitten on the floor at school. What is the best thing to do?
law-prek2.l07.q4.h: Someone is probably looking for it.
law-prek2.l07.q4.e: Giving a lost item to a grown-up helps the owner get it back. Keeping it would be taking what is not yours.

law-prek2.l08.q1.t: Saying what happened and asking how to fix it
law-prek2.l08.q1.p: Which is a good part of saying sorry?
law-prek2.l08.q1.h: A good sorry tries to make it better.
law-prek2.l08.q1.e: A good sorry says what happened, says you are sorry, and offers to help fix it.

law-prek2.l08.q2.t: "I did that. I am sorry. Can I help build it again?"
law-prek2.l08.q2.p: You knocked over your friend's block tower. What is the most responsible thing to say?
law-prek2.l08.q2.h: Owning it means saying "I did that."
law-prek2.l08.q2.e: Being responsible means owning what you did and helping fix it, rather than blaming something else.

law-prek2.l08.q3.t: Give your friend time and keep being kind
law-prek2.l08.q3.p: You said sorry, but your friend is still upset. What is the best next step?
law-prek2.l08.q3.e: You cannot make someone forgive you. Giving them time and being kind is the right way.

law-prek2.l08.q4.t: It helps put things back the way they should be
law-prek2.l08.q4.p: How does fixing a mistake relate to being fair?
law-prek2.l08.q4.h: Think about the broken tower rebuilt.
law-prek2.l08.q4.e: Fixing a mistake helps set things right for the person who was affected. That is part of fairness.

law-prek2.l09.q1.t: Stop, take a breath, and use words about how they feel
law-prek2.l09.q1.p: Two children want the same red crayon. What should they do first?
