med-clin-fm.l07.q1.p: Which drug class slows kidney disease progression and reduces heart failure hospitalization in people with type 2 diabetes?
med-clin-fm.l07.q1.h: It also causes genital mycotic infections.
med-clin-fm.l07.q1.e: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalization and kidney disease progression in outcome trials. Thiazolidinediones can worsen heart failure.

med-clin-fm.l07.q2.t: Medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2
med-clin-fm.l07.q2.p: A GLP-1 receptor agonist is contraindicated in which condition?
med-clin-fm.l07.q2.h: Boxed warning for C-cell tumors in rodents.
med-clin-fm.l07.q2.e: The boxed warning relates to thyroid C-cell tumors and contraindicates use with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2.

med-clin-fm.l07.q3.t: An SGLT2 inhibitor, while continuing an ACE inhibitor or ARB for albuminuria
med-clin-fm.l07.q3.p: A 60-year-old man with type 2 diabetes on metformin has an eGFR of 48, albuminuria and an A1c of 7.8 percent. Which addition is most appropriate?
med-clin-fm.l07.q3.h: Choose by comorbidity, not only A1c.
med-clin-fm.l07.q3.e: SGLT2 inhibitors offer glycemic, renal and cardiac benefit in diabetic kidney disease. Sulfonylureas add hypoglycemia risk and no renal protection.

med-clin-fm.l07.q4.t: Accept a less stringent target, around 8 percent, to avoid hypoglycemia
med-clin-fm.l07.q4.p: A 70-year-old with type 2 diabetes, advanced heart failure and limited life expectancy has an A1c of 7.9 percent on stable therapy. What is the most reasonable approach?
med-clin-fm.l07.q4.e: Older patients with limited life expectancy and comorbidity warrant relaxed targets (the ADA 2026 Standards give below 8 percent for complex health, and de-emphasize A1c in very poor health). Tight control adds hypoglycemia without enough time to gain benefit.

med-clin-fm.l07.q5.t: Abnormal kidney structure or function lasting longer than three months, staged by eGFR and albuminuria
med-clin-fm.l07.q5.p: Which is a classification feature of chronic kidney disease?
med-clin-fm.l07.q5.e: CKD is defined by persistence beyond three months and staged on two axes, GFR and albuminuria.

med-clin-fm.l08.q1.p: Which description fits the diagnostic finding of COPD on spirometry?
med-clin-fm.l08.q1.e: Persistent airflow obstruction is shown by a post-bronchodilator ratio below 0.70. A large reversible rise suggests asthma.

med-clin-fm.l08.q2.t: It treats bronchospasm but not inflammation, and increases severe event risk
med-clin-fm.l08.q2.p: Why is a long-acting beta agonist never used alone in asthma?
med-clin-fm.l08.q2.e: Monotherapy with a long-acting beta agonist raises the risk of severe exacerbations, so it is combined with an inhaled corticosteroid.

med-clin-fm.l08.q3.t: Step up to an inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol regimen after reviewing technique and triggers
med-clin-fm.l08.q3.p: A 35-year-old woman uses albuterol daily and wakes at night with cough. What is the most appropriate management change?
med-clin-fm.l08.q3.e: Frequent reliever use and nocturnal symptoms show poor control, which needs an anti-inflammatory regimen. Long-acting agonist monotherapy is unsafe.

med-clin-fm.l08.q4.t: An inhaled corticosteroid added to dual long-acting bronchodilators
med-clin-fm.l08.q4.p: A 62-year-old man with COPD has two exacerbations in a year and a blood eosinophil count of 400 cells per microliter. Which addition has the best rationale?
med-clin-fm.l08.q4.e: High eosinophil counts with frequent exacerbations favor adding an inhaled steroid, accepting a small pneumonia risk. Chronic oral steroids cause harm.

med-clin-fm.l08.q5.t: Levothyroxine, adjusted by TSH in six to eight weeks
med-clin-fm.l08.q5.p: A 40-year-old woman has fatigue, weight gain and constipation, with a TSH of 14 mIU/L and low free thyroxine. What is the best treatment?
med-clin-fm.l08.q5.e: The picture is overt primary hypothyroidism, treated with levothyroxine and titrated by TSH. Methimazole treats hyperthyroidism.

med-clin-fm.l09.q1.p: Which body mass index range defines obesity in most adults?
med-clin-fm.l09.q1.e: Obesity is a body mass index of 30 or higher, with overweight at 25 to 29.9.

med-clin-fm.l09.q2.p: Which weight-loss drug is contraindicated in patients with a seizure disorder?
med-clin-fm.l09.q2.h: The bupropion component lowers seizure threshold.
med-clin-fm.l09.q2.e: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold. Orlistat causes steatorrhea, and incretin agents cause gastrointestinal effects.

med-clin-fm.l09.q3.t: Intensive multicomponent behavioral therapy, with discussion of pharmacotherapy
med-clin-fm.l09.q3.p: A 45-year-old woman with a body mass index of 33 and prediabetes asks about weight loss. What is the best approach?
med-clin-fm.l09.q3.e: Intensive behavioral programs are recommended, and pharmacotherapy adds benefit. Surgery is reserved for higher BMI or severe metabolic disease.

med-clin-fm.l09.q4.p: A 50-year-old man who underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass years ago has fatigue, a macrocytic anemia and paresthesias. Which deficiency is most likely?
med-clin-fm.l09.q4.h: Intrinsic factor and acid are reduced.
med-clin-fm.l09.q4.e: Reduced gastric acid and intrinsic factor interaction cause B12 deficiency after gastric bypass, producing macrocytic anemia and neuropathy.

med-clin-fm.l09.q5.t: Mediterranean, low-carbohydrate and low-fat diets produce similar weight loss when adhered to
med-clin-fm.l09.q5.p: Which statement about dietary patterns in weight loss is supported by trials?
med-clin-fm.l09.q5.e: Trials show comparable weight loss across patterns, so the best diet is the one a patient can sustain.

med-clin-fm.l10.q1.t: Varenicline, which reduces craving and the reward from smoking
med-clin-fm.l10.q1.p: Which drug acts as a partial agonist at the alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic receptor and is used for smoking cessation?
med-clin-fm.l10.q1.h: Think of a partial agonist at the nicotinic receptor.
med-clin-fm.l10.q1.e: Varenicline is a partial agonist at that receptor. Bupropion acts on reuptake transporters, and nicotine replacement delivers a full agonist.

med-clin-fm.l10.q2.t: Behavioral interventions plus FDA-approved medication, which work better combined
med-clin-fm.l10.q2.p: What is recommended by the USPSTF for adults who use tobacco and are not pregnant?
med-clin-fm.l10.q2.e: The 2021 USPSTF gives an A grade to combined behavioral and pharmacologic interventions. E-cigarettes lack sufficient evidence as an aid.

med-clin-fm.l10.q3.t: Advise him clearly, explore his motives and offer medication and counseling with follow-up
med-clin-fm.l10.q3.p: A 48-year-old man who smokes a pack daily says he is thinking about quitting someday. What is the best response?
med-clin-fm.l10.q3.h: Brief intervention in a patient who is contemplating change.
med-clin-fm.l10.q3.e: The ask-advise-assess-assist-arrange approach advises quitting, builds motivation and offers help even when readiness is limited. Waiting loses opportunities.

med-clin-fm.l10.q4.t: Bupropion, because it lowers the seizure threshold
med-clin-fm.l10.q4.p: A 35-year-old woman has a seizure disorder and wants help quitting smoking. Which agent should be avoided?
med-clin-fm.l10.q4.h: One of the first-line drugs is an antidepressant.
med-clin-fm.l10.q4.e: Bupropion is contraindicated in seizure disorders. Varenicline does not increase serious neuropsychiatric events, according to the EAGLES trial.

med-clin-fm.l10.q5.t: Medication such as buprenorphine or methadone with counseling
med-clin-fm.l10.q5.p: A man with opioid use disorder asks about treatment. Which approach reduces mortality the most?
med-clin-fm.l10.q5.h: Detoxification alone has high relapse and overdose rates.
med-clin-fm.l10.q5.e: Medications for opioid use disorder lower mortality. Detoxification alone raises the risk of overdose after tolerance is lost.

med-clin-fm.l11.q1.p: Which medication class is contraindicated with nitrates because of profound hypotension?
med-clin-fm.l11.q1.h: It is used for erectile dysfunction.
med-clin-fm.l11.q1.e: PDE-5 inhibitors and nitrates both raise cGMP and dilate vessels, causing severe hypotension. The other classes have no such interaction.

med-clin-fm.l11.q2.t: The PSA is lowered by about half, so values are doubled for interpretation
med-clin-fm.l11.q2.p: A man with benign prostatic hyperplasia takes finasteride. How does this change interpretation of his PSA?
med-clin-fm.l11.q2.e: These drugs lower the PSA by roughly 50 percent after six to twelve months, so clinicians double the measured value.

med-clin-fm.l11.q3.t: Immediate surgical exploration without waiting for imaging if suspicion is high
med-clin-fm.l11.q3.p: A 17-year-old has sudden severe left scrotal pain with nausea. The testis is high-riding and the cremasteric reflex is absent. What is the best next step?
med-clin-fm.l11.q3.e: This is testicular torsion, a surgical emergency in which salvage declines after about six hours. Epididymitis would not cause an absent cremasteric reflex.

med-clin-fm.l11.q4.t: Scrotal ultrasound and tumor markers, followed by radical inguinal orchiectomy if suspicious
med-clin-fm.l11.q4.p: A 24-year-old man has a painless, firm left testicular mass. What is the appropriate approach?
med-clin-fm.l11.q4.e: A solid testicular mass in a young man is cancer until proven otherwise, and inguinal orchiectomy avoids scrotal violation. Transscrotal biopsy can seed tumor.

med-clin-fm.l11.q5.t: Secondary hypogonadism, which needs evaluation for pituitary or systemic causes
med-clin-fm.l11.q5.p: A 58-year-old man has fatigue and low libido and a low morning total testosterone twice, with low luteinizing hormone. What does this indicate?
med-clin-fm.l11.q5.e: Low testosterone with low or normal gonadotropins indicates secondary hypogonadism and prompts evaluation of the pituitary and causes such as obesity, opioids and prolactin excess.

med-clin-fm.l12.q1.p: Which contraceptive method is the most effective emergency contraception?
med-clin-fm.l12.q1.h: It works after unprotected intercourse for up to five days.
med-clin-fm.l12.q1.e: The copper IUD is the most effective emergency method. Levonorgestrel is less effective, especially at higher body mass index.

med-clin-fm.l12.q2.p: Which condition makes combined estrogen-progestin contraception category 4 (unacceptable risk)?
med-clin-fm.l12.q2.e: Migraine with aura carries stroke risk that estrogen raises further. The others are not category 4 conditions.

med-clin-fm.l12.q3.t: Offer a progestin-only method or an intrauterine device instead
med-clin-fm.l12.q3.p: A 33-year-old woman smokes 20 cigarettes per day and has migraine with aura. She requests a combined pill. What is the best response?
med-clin-fm.l12.q3.e: Aura and smoking make estrogen-containing methods inappropriate, but progestin-only methods and IUDs are safe. She still needs effective contraception.

med-clin-fm.l12.q4.t: Estrogen with a progestogen to protect the endometrium
med-clin-fm.l12.q4.p: A 56-year-old woman with a uterus has severe hot flashes and no contraindication, two years after menopause. Which regimen is appropriate if she chooses hormone therapy?
med-clin-fm.l12.q4.e: Women with a uterus need a progestogen with estrogen to prevent endometrial hyperplasia and cancer. Women without a uterus can use estrogen alone.

med-clin-fm.l12.q5.t: An oral bisphosphonate taken upright with water, with calcium and vitamin D
med-clin-fm.l12.q5.p: A 67-year-old woman has a DXA T-score of -2.8 at the femoral neck and no contraindication to oral therapy. What is first-line treatment?
med-clin-fm.l12.q5.e: A T-score of -2.5 or lower defines osteoporosis, and bisphosphonates are first-line. Hormone therapy is not used primarily for osteoporosis in older women.

med-clin-fm.l13.q1.t: Exercise programs, which improve strength and balance
med-clin-fm.l13.q1.p: Which USPSTF-recommended intervention reduces falls in community-dwelling adults aged 65 or older at increased risk?
med-clin-fm.l13.q1.e: The 2024 USPSTF gives exercise interventions a B grade. Vitamin D is no longer covered in the falls statement, and the USPSTF has not recommended it for fall prevention.

med-clin-fm.l13.q2.t: A calcium channel blocker causes edema, which is then treated with a diuretic
med-clin-fm.l13.q2.p: A prescribing cascade is best described by which example?
med-clin-fm.l13.q2.h: An adverse effect is mistaken for a new disease.
med-clin-fm.l13.q2.e: In a prescribing cascade, a drug side effect is treated as a new condition with another drug, adding risk without addressing the cause.

med-clin-fm.l13.q3.t: Exercise program and deprescribing of zolpidem and oxybutynin, with vision and footwear review
med-clin-fm.l13.q3.p: An 80-year-old woman falls twice in a year while taking zolpidem, oxybutynin and amlodipine, and has an orthostatic blood pressure drop. What is the best plan?
med-clin-fm.l13.q3.h: Reduce falls-risk drugs and improve strength.
med-clin-fm.l13.q3.e: Sedatives and anticholinergics are Beers Criteria drugs that increase falls. Exercise reduces risk, while vitamin D alone is not supported.

med-clin-fm.l13.q4.t: A POLST or MOLST form completed with his clinician
med-clin-fm.l13.q4.p: A 78-year-old man has newly diagnosed metastatic cancer and wants to avoid intubation. Which document turns his preferences into portable medical orders?
med-clin-fm.l13.q4.h: It is for patients with serious illness.
med-clin-fm.l13.q4.e: A POLST or MOLST form translates preferences into actionable orders. A living will records wishes but is not an order set.

med-clin-fm.l13.q5.t: Anticholinergic adverse effects of the drug
med-clin-fm.l13.q5.p: A 72-year-old woman has been taking a first-generation antihistamine nightly and now has constipation, confusion and urinary retention. Which explanation fits best?
med-clin-fm.l13.q5.h: Dry, constipated, confused and retaining urine.
med-clin-fm.l13.q5.e: The anticholinergic burden of first-generation antihistamines causes this pattern, which is why Beers Criteria advise avoiding them.

med-clin-fm.l14.q1.p: Which symptom suggests cauda equina syndrome in a patient with back pain?
med-clin-fm.l14.q1.e: Saddle anesthesia and urinary retention suggest cauda equina syndrome, requiring urgent MRI and decompression.

med-clin-fm.l14.q2.p: Which crystal finding on synovial fluid analysis confirms gout?
med-clin-fm.l14.q2.e: Gout shows negatively birefringent needles. Pseudogout shows rhomboid positively birefringent crystals.

med-clin-fm.l14.q3.t: Exercise and weight loss, with topical or oral NSAIDs as needed
med-clin-fm.l14.q3.p: A 60-year-old woman has knee pain with activity, brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement. Which treatment strategy is recommended first?
med-clin-fm.l14.q3.e: The ACR guideline strongly recommends exercise and weight loss, with NSAIDs for symptoms. Glucosamine and hyaluronic acid are not supported, and methotrexate treats rheumatoid arthritis.

med-clin-fm.l14.q4.t: Wrist splinting at night, with steroid injection or surgical release if it fails
med-clin-fm.l14.q4.p: A 35-year-old woman has nocturnal paresthesias of the thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking the hand, and a positive Tinel sign. What is the best initial treatment?
med-clin-fm.l14.q4.e: Carpal tunnel syndrome is treated with night splinting first. Ulnar neuropathy affects the ring and little fingers.

med-clin-fm.l14.q5.t: Arthrocentesis with cell count, Gram stain and culture
med-clin-fm.l14.q5.p: A 45-year-old man has a hot, swollen knee, fever and inability to bear weight. What is the most important next step?
med-clin-fm.l14.q5.h: A septic joint must not be missed.
med-clin-fm.l14.q5.e: A hot swollen joint with fever needs arthrocentesis to exclude infection. Injecting steroids into an infected joint would be harmful.

med-clin-fm.l15.q1.t: Evolution, meaning change in size, shape or color over time
med-clin-fm.l15.q1.p: Which ABCDE feature of a pigmented lesion suggests melanoma?
med-clin-fm.l15.q1.h: E stands for something that changes.
med-clin-fm.l15.q1.e: Evolution, along with asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation and diameter above 6 mm, suggests melanoma.

med-clin-fm.l15.q2.p: Which treatment for severe nodulocystic acne requires a pregnancy prevention program because of teratogenicity?
med-clin-fm.l15.q2.e: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen. The other agents do not require a pregnancy prevention program.

med-clin-fm.l15.q3.t: Systemic acyclovir, treating for eczema herpeticum
med-clin-fm.l15.q3.p: A child with atopic dermatitis develops clustered punched-out vesicles and fever over eczematous skin. What is the best management?
med-clin-fm.l15.q3.e: Eczema herpeticum is a medical emergency needing antiviral therapy. Topical steroids can worsen the infection.

med-clin-fm.l15.q4.t: Full-thickness excisional or punch biopsy including the deepest part of the lesion
med-clin-fm.l15.q4.p: A 58-year-old man has a 9 mm irregular, multicolored, changing pigmented lesion on his back. What is the correct next step?
med-clin-fm.l15.q4.e: Suspected melanoma needs a full-thickness biopsy so depth can be measured. Shave biopsy can transect the lesion and understage it.

med-clin-fm.l15.q5.t: Permethrin applied to the whole body, with treatment of close contacts
med-clin-fm.l15.q5.p: A family presents with intense nocturnal itching and burrows in finger web spaces. Which treatment is appropriate?
med-clin-fm.l15.q5.e: Scabies is treated with permethrin for the patient and close contacts. Steroids alone relieve itch but do not kill mites.

med-clin-fm.l16.q1.p: Which hazard is most strongly associated with malignant mesothelioma?
med-clin-fm.l16.q1.h: Think of insulators and shipyard workers.
med-clin-fm.l16.q1.e: Asbestos causes mesothelioma, and the risk is not strongly dependent on smoking. Silica and coal dust cause pneumoconioses.

med-clin-fm.l16.q2.p: In the hierarchy of controls, which approach is most effective?
med-clin-fm.l16.q2.h: Personal protective equipment is the last line.
med-clin-fm.l16.q2.e: Elimination is the most effective, followed by substitution and engineering controls. Personal protective equipment depends on human behavior and is least effective.

med-clin-fm.l16.q3.t: Tuberculosis, which occurs more often in silicosis
med-clin-fm.l16.q3.p: A 52-year-old sandblaster has upper-lobe nodules and eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes on chest radiography. What additional risk should be monitored?
med-clin-fm.l16.q3.e: Silicosis increases tuberculosis risk, so latent tuberculosis testing is indicated. Mesothelioma relates to asbestos.

med-clin-fm.l16.q4.t: Measure blood lead, remove him from exposure and chelate if levels are high
med-clin-fm.l16.q4.p: A 38-year-old battery plant worker has abdominal pain, anemia with basophilic stippling and wrist drop. What is the best approach?
med-clin-fm.l16.q4.e: The picture suggests lead poisoning, and treatment requires removing exposure and chelation when levels are high. Iron supplementation does not address the cause.

med-clin-fm.l16.q5.p: A factory worker has audiometry showing a notch at 4000 Hz. What is the most likely cause?
med-clin-fm.l16.q5.e: A 4000 Hz notch is characteristic of noise-induced hearing loss. Presbycusis shows a sloping high-frequency loss.

med-clin-fm.l17.q1.p: Which is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States and the leading cause among nonsmokers?
med-clin-fm.l17.q1.e: Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking and the leading cause in nonsmokers.

med-clin-fm.l17.q2.t: Identify and remove the source, with follow-up testing and nutrition review
med-clin-fm.l17.q2.p: What is the most important management for a toddler with a blood lead level of 12 micrograms per deciliter?
med-clin-fm.l17.q2.h: Chelation is for much higher levels.
med-clin-fm.l17.q2.e: This level needs source investigation and follow-up. Chelation is reserved for levels above 45 or encephalopathy.

med-clin-fm.l17.q3.t: Stay indoors with filtered air and use a well-fitted N95 respirator outdoors
med-clin-fm.l17.q3.p: Wildfire smoke blankets a town. Which advice best protects a patient with asthma?
med-clin-fm.l17.q3.h: Fine particles are the main hazard.
med-clin-fm.l17.q3.e: HEPA filtration and fitted N95 respirators reduce exposure to particulate matter. Cloth masks and open windows offer little protection.

med-clin-fm.l17.q4.t: Nitrate in well water causing methemoglobinemia
med-clin-fm.l17.q4.p: A 4-month-old fed formula mixed with well water has cyanosis and chocolate-colored blood with normal PaO2. What exposure is most likely?
med-clin-fm.l17.q4.h: Infants are susceptible to oxidized hemoglobin.
med-clin-fm.l17.q4.e: Nitrate in well water causes infant methemoglobinemia, treated with methylene blue.

med-clin-fm.l17.q5.t: Impaired heat dissipation and volume depletion from her drugs
med-clin-fm.l17.q5.p: During a heat wave an elderly woman taking a diuretic and an anticholinergic becomes confused. Which risk factor most increases her susceptibility?
med-clin-fm.l17.q5.h: Medications blunt sweating and add volume loss.
med-clin-fm.l17.q5.e: Anticholinergics reduce sweating and diuretics deplete volume, raising heat illness risk in older adults.

med-clin-fm.l18.q1.p: At what ages is autism-specific screening recommended by the AAP?
med-clin-fm.l18.q1.e: The AAP recommends autism-specific screening at 18 and 24 months, and general developmental screening at 9, 18 and 30 months.

med-clin-fm.l18.q2.t: Avoid honey until 12 months of age
med-clin-fm.l18.q2.p: Which feeding advice reduces the risk of infant botulism?
med-clin-fm.l18.q2.e: Honey may contain Clostridium botulinum spores, and infants lack protective gut flora. Avoid it before 12 months.

med-clin-fm.l18.q3.t: Audiology referral and developmental and autism screening, with early intervention referral
med-clin-fm.l18.q3.p: A 15-month-old girl has no words, does not point and does not respond to her name. Newborn hearing screening was normal. What is the best next step?
med-clin-fm.l18.q3.h: Red flags in language and social engagement.
med-clin-fm.l18.q3.e: Absent words, pointing and response to name are red flags. Early evaluation and intervention improve outcomes, and hearing should be rechecked.

med-clin-fm.l18.q4.t: Place the infant supine in a separate firm sleep surface without soft bedding
med-clin-fm.l18.q4.p: A 7-month-old has a stuffy nose and a pediatrician hears a family sleeping arrangement with the infant on a sofa with the parent. What is the best advice about sleep?
med-clin-fm.l18.q4.h: Safe sleep reduces sudden infant death syndrome.
med-clin-fm.l18.q4.e: Supine on a firm separate surface lowers SIDS and suffocation risk. Soft bedding and sofas increase it.

med-clin-fm.l18.q5.t: Assess suicide risk, ensure safety and involve parents or others as needed for safety
med-clin-fm.l18.q5.p: A 13-year-old boy has a sad mood, poor sleep and thoughts of self-harm and asks that his parents not be told. Which approach is most appropriate?
med-clin-fm.l18.q5.e: Confidentiality encourages disclosure, but risk of self-harm requires safety planning and involving others. Delay is unsafe.

med-clin-im.l01.q1.t: Elevated serum cardiac troponin indicating necrosis
med-clin-im.l01.q1.p: Which finding most clearly distinguishes NSTEMI from unstable angina?
med-clin-im.l01.q1.h: Think about what the two syndromes share and what only one has.
med-clin-im.l01.q1.e: NSTEMI involves necrosis, detected by troponin; unstable angina has the same ischemic symptoms without a troponin rise. Rest pain and ST depression can occur in both.

med-clin-im.l01.q2.t: Nitroglycerin, since the preload-dependent right ventricle may fail
med-clin-im.l01.q2.p: A man with chest pain has ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF, a blood pressure of 82/50 mmHg, clear lungs and distended neck veins. What should be avoided?
med-clin-im.l01.q2.h: Consider which ventricle is stunned in this pattern.
med-clin-im.l01.q2.e: Inferior STEMI with hypotension and clear lungs suggests right ventricular infarction, where venodilators drop preload and cause collapse. Fluids are the usual help, not harm.

med-clin-im.l01.q3.t: ST elevation in V1 to V4 reflects the left anterior descending
med-clin-im.l01.q3.p: Which ECG territory pairing is correct for a typical culprit vessel in STEMI?
med-clin-im.l01.q3.h: Anterior leads sit over the anterior wall.
med-clin-im.l01.q3.e: V1 to V4 look at the anterior wall supplied by the LAD. Inferior leads usually reflect the RCA, lateral leads the circumflex, and tall R waves with ST depression in V1 to V3 suggest posterior infarction.

med-clin-im.l01.q4.t: Give aspirin and start fibrinolysis at the local hospital
med-clin-im.l01.q4.p: A 58-year-old man has 40 minutes of crushing chest pain, and the ECG shows 3 mm ST elevation in V2 to V5. The nearest hospital has no catheterization laboratory, and transfer to a PCI center would take about three hours. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l01.q4.h: Consider the time limit on first medical contact to device.
med-clin-im.l01.q4.e: When PCI cannot be delivered within roughly 120 minutes, fibrinolysis is appropriate within 30 minutes of arrival if there are no contraindications. Waiting on troponin or echo wastes myocardium in a clear STEMI.

med-clin-im.l01.q5.t: Fibrinolytic and anticoagulant drugs for presumed coronary occlusion
med-clin-im.l01.q5.p: A 62-year-old hypertensive man has sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back, a blood pressure of 190/100 in the right arm and 150/80 in the left, and ST elevation is absent. Which therapy should be avoided before the diagnosis is secured?
med-clin-im.l01.q5.h: What does a torn aortic wall do when clotting is impaired?
med-clin-im.l01.q5.e: The picture suggests aortic dissection, in which thrombolytics or anticoagulants can cause catastrophic bleeding into the false lumen or pericardium. Beta-blockade and CT angiography are the right approach.

med-clin-im.l02.q1.t: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists such as spironolactone
med-clin-im.l02.q1.p: Which heart failure medication class has been shown to improve survival in HFrEF?
med-clin-im.l02.q1.h: Loop diuretics help symptoms, not survival.
med-clin-im.l02.q1.e: Spironolactone and eplerenone reduce mortality in HFrEF. Loop diuretics relieve congestion without a survival benefit, and thiazolidinediones worsen fluid retention.

med-clin-im.l02.q2.t: Stop the ACE inhibitor at least 36 hours beforehand to avoid angioedema
med-clin-im.l02.q2.p: A patient with HFrEF is on a stable ACE inhibitor and the team wants to start sacubitril-valsartan. What is the required precaution?
med-clin-im.l02.q2.e: Neprilysin inhibition plus ACE inhibition increases bradykinin and can cause angioedema, so a 36-hour washout is required. The combination is contraindicated.

med-clin-im.l02.q3.t: Diltiazem, a calcium channel blocker with negative inotropy
med-clin-im.l02.q3.p: Which drug can worsen heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and should generally be avoided?
med-clin-im.l02.q3.h: Consider drugs that reduce contractility directly.
med-clin-im.l02.q3.e: Diltiazem and verapamil depress contractility and are harmful in HFrEF. The other three agents have mortality or hospitalization benefit.

med-clin-im.l02.q4.t: An implantable defibrillator placed for primary prevention of death
med-clin-im.l02.q4.p: A 70-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy and an EF of 28 percent has stable class II symptoms on guideline-directed medicines for six months, and QRS duration is 100 ms. Which intervention addresses his risk of sudden death?
med-clin-im.l02.q4.h: EF at or below 35 percent after at least three months of therapy is the trigger.
med-clin-im.l02.q4.e: A defibrillator is indicated for primary prevention with an EF at or below 35 percent on optimal therapy and reasonable expected survival. Resynchronization needs a wide QRS, and antiarrhythmics do not improve survival.

med-clin-im.l02.q5.t: An SGLT2 inhibitor added to diuretic therapy for congestion
med-clin-im.l02.q5.p: A 66-year-old woman with orthopnea, jugular venous distension and bibasilar crackles has an EF of 60 percent and a markedly enlarged left atrium on echocardiography. She has hypertension and diabetes. Which therapy has been shown to reduce heart failure hospitalization in her condition?
med-clin-im.l02.q5.h: Think about the preserved EF and which class benefits this phenotype.
med-clin-im.l02.q5.e: This is HFpEF, in which SGLT2 inhibitors reduce hospitalization in addition to diuretics. Defibrillators are for low EF, and contractility agents do not help a stiff ventricle with normal ejection.

med-clin-im.l03.q1.t: An irregularly irregular rhythm without discernible P waves
med-clin-im.l03.q1.p: Which feature of the ECG defines atrial fibrillation?
med-clin-im.l03.q1.h: Think about what the atria are doing and what that does to RR spacing.
med-clin-im.l03.q1.e: AF shows chaotic atrial activity with no organized P waves and an irregular ventricular response. Sawtooth waves suggest flutter and AV dissociation suggests ventricular tachycardia.

med-clin-im.l03.q2.t: A direct oral anticoagulant such as apixaban for long-term use
med-clin-im.l03.q2.p: A 68-year-old woman with AF has hypertension, diabetes and a prior TIA. Which approach best prevents stroke?
med-clin-im.l03.q2.h: Anticoagulation depends on stroke risk, not on symptoms or rhythm success.
med-clin-im.l03.q2.e: Her CHA2DS2-VASc score is high, so a DOAC is recommended long term. Cardioversion does not remove stroke risk, and aspirin is inadequate.

med-clin-im.l03.q3.t: Transesophageal echocardiography to exclude atrial thrombus
med-clin-im.l03.q3.p: A patient with AF of unknown duration is stable and scheduled for cardioversion. Which step is needed beforehand?
med-clin-im.l03.q3.h: Think about where clots hide when the atria do not contract.
med-clin-im.l03.q3.e: Cardioversion of AF lasting over 48 hours or unknown duration needs either three weeks of anticoagulation or imaging to exclude thrombus. Adenosine does not convert AF.

med-clin-im.l03.q4.t: Intravenous verapamil that slows AV nodal conduction
med-clin-im.l03.q4.p: A 30-year-old man with known Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome presents with palpitations. His rhythm is irregular and wide-complex at 220 beats per minute, and he is hemodynamically stable. Which drug is most dangerous?
med-clin-im.l03.q4.h: Think about where the impulses are routed when the AV node is blocked.
med-clin-im.l03.q4.e: AV nodal blockers can shunt more atrial impulses down the accessory pathway and precipitate ventricular fibrillation. Procainamide slows the pathway and cardioversion is also safe.

med-clin-im.l03.q5.t: Warfarin with an INR target in the therapeutic range
med-clin-im.l03.q5.p: A 72-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation and moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis needs stroke prevention. Which choice is best?
med-clin-im.l03.q5.h: Valvular AF excluded patients from the DOAC trials.
med-clin-im.l03.q5.e: Moderate to severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves are the exceptions where warfarin is preferred over DOACs. Dual antiplatelet therapy is inferior for stroke prevention.

med-clin-im.l04.q1.t: 130/80 mmHg or higher on repeat measurements
med-clin-im.l04.q1.p: Which blood pressure threshold defines hypertension in the 2025 AHA/ACC guideline?
med-clin-im.l04.q1.h: The 2017 update lowered the previous threshold, and 2025 kept it.
med-clin-im.l04.q1.e: The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline keeps hypertension at 130/80 mmHg, as the 2017 guideline set, while other guidelines have kept 140/90.

med-clin-im.l04.q2.t: Aortic valve replacement, surgical or transcatheter
med-clin-im.l04.q2.p: A 72-year-old has a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids and recent exertional syncope. What is the best definitive treatment?
med-clin-im.l04.q2.h: Symptoms signal a sharp drop in survival without a mechanical fix.
med-clin-im.l04.q2.e: Symptomatic severe aortic stenosis is treated by valve replacement because medical therapy does not change the course. Vasodilators risk hypotension in a fixed outflow lesion.

med-clin-im.l04.q3.t: Standing up quickly or performing a Valsalva maneuver
med-clin-im.l04.q3.p: Which maneuver makes the murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy louder?
med-clin-im.l04.q3.h: Think about which maneuvers reduce preload.
med-clin-im.l04.q3.e: Reduced preload narrows the outflow tract and intensifies the obstruction and murmur. Squatting and handgrip increase afterload or preload and soften it.

med-clin-im.l04.q4.t: Staphylococcus aureus on the tricuspid valve
med-clin-im.l04.q4.p: A 34-year-old man who injects heroin has a fever for five days, a new holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, and multiple pulmonary nodules on chest imaging. What is the most likely organism?
med-clin-im.l04.q4.h: Right-sided disease and injection use point to the skin flora.
med-clin-im.l04.q4.e: Injection drug use classically causes right-sided endocarditis from S. aureus, with septic pulmonary emboli. Viridans streptococci cause subacute disease on damaged left-sided valves.

med-clin-im.l04.q5.t: Measure plasma aldosterone and renin to screen for aldosteronism
med-clin-im.l04.q5.p: A 58-year-old woman with resistant hypertension on three drugs has a potassium of 2.9 mEq/L and mild metabolic alkalosis, and she is not taking a diuretic. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l04.q5.h: Spontaneous hypokalemia with hypertension suggests mineralocorticoid excess.
med-clin-im.l04.q5.e: Hypokalemia and alkalosis in resistant hypertension suggest primary aldosteronism, screened with an aldosterone to renin ratio. A thiazide would worsen potassium loss.

med-clin-im.l05.q1.t: A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio persisting after bronchodilator
med-clin-im.l05.q1.p: Which spirometry result is expected in COPD?
med-clin-im.l05.q1.e: COPD shows airflow obstruction that does not fully reverse. A normal ratio with low capacity is restriction, and reversibility favors asthma.

med-clin-im.l05.q2.t: Long-term oxygen used for more than 15 hours a day
med-clin-im.l05.q2.p: A man with COPD and chronic hypoxemia has a resting saturation of 86 percent on room air despite maximal inhaled therapy. Which intervention improves survival?
med-clin-im.l05.q2.h: Consider the thresholds for domiciliary oxygen.
med-clin-im.l05.q2.e: Long-term oxygen for resting hypoxemia prolongs survival in COPD. Chronic oral steroids cause harm without benefit and do not improve mortality.

med-clin-im.l05.q3.t: An inhaled corticosteroid with formoterol as needed or daily
med-clin-im.l05.q3.p: Which approach to newly diagnosed mild persistent asthma reflects current GINA direction?
med-clin-im.l05.q3.h: Reliever-only treatment leaves airway inflammation untreated.
med-clin-im.l05.q3.e: GINA discourages beta agonist monotherapy, and favors an inhaled corticosteroid together with formoterol. Long-acting beta agonist monotherapy raises the risk of exacerbations.

med-clin-im.l05.q4.t: Noninvasive ventilation along with bronchodilators and steroids
med-clin-im.l05.q4.p: A 64-year-old long-term smoker with COPD arrives with three days of increased dyspnea and purulent sputum. His pH is 7.28, PaCO2 is 68 mmHg and he is drowsy but protecting his airway. Which intervention best reduces his need for intubation?
med-clin-im.l05.q4.h: Acute hypercapnic acidosis responds to ventilatory support.
med-clin-im.l05.q4.e: Noninvasive ventilation in acute hypercapnic COPD exacerbation lowers intubation and mortality. High oxygen can worsen carbon dioxide retention and sedatives depress ventilation further.

med-clin-im.l05.q5.t: Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level to confirm deficiency
med-clin-im.l05.q5.p: A 38-year-old nonsmoker develops progressive dyspnea, and his chest imaging shows hyperlucent lower lobes. His FEV1/FVC is 0.55 and his father died of cirrhosis. Which test is most useful?
med-clin-im.l05.q5.h: Panacinar basal emphysema with liver disease is a pattern.
med-clin-im.l05.q5.e: Early basal emphysema in a nonsmoker with a family history of liver disease suggests alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Methacholine testing is for suspected asthma with normal baseline spirometry.

med-clin-im.l06.q1.t: Exclusion of pulmonary embolism without any imaging study
med-clin-im.l06.q1.p: What does a negative D-dimer allow in a patient with low pretest probability of PE?
med-clin-im.l06.q1.h: D-dimer is a rule-out test, not a rule-in test.
med-clin-im.l06.q1.e: A negative high-sensitivity D-dimer at low or intermediate probability effectively excludes PE. A positive result is nonspecific and needs imaging.

med-clin-im.l06.q2.t: A V/Q scan or CT pulmonary angiography after risk discussion
med-clin-im.l06.q2.p: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks has pleuritic chest pain and a normal chest film. She is hemodynamically stable. Which approach to imaging is acceptable?
med-clin-im.l06.q2.h: Pregnancy does not forbid a diagnosis that threatens two lives.
med-clin-im.l06.q2.e: Both V/Q scanning and CT angiography are accepted in pregnancy. Untreated PE is dangerous to both mother and fetus, so imaging is not avoided.

med-clin-im.l06.q3.t: Hyponatremia with diarrhea after exposure to contaminated water systems
med-clin-im.l06.q3.h: Think about extrapulmonary clues and the urinary antigen.
med-clin-im.l06.q3.e: Legionella causes atypical pneumonia with hyponatremia, diarrhea and neurologic signs. Currant jelly sputum suggests Klebsiella, cold agglutinins Mycoplasma and rust sputum pneumococcus.

med-clin-im.l06.q4.p: A 55-year-old woman is admitted 10 days after hip replacement with sudden dyspnea. Her heart rate is 128 beats per minute, blood pressure is 78/40 mmHg, and her oxygen saturation is 86 percent. Bedside echocardiography shows a dilated right ventricle, and she is too unstable for CT. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l06.q4.h: Shock plus right heart strain defines a high-risk event.
med-clin-im.l06.q4.e: Hemodynamic instability from PE is an indication for systemic thrombolysis. Large fluid boluses can overdistend the failing right ventricle and a filter does not treat existing clot.

med-clin-im.l06.q5.t: Chest tube drainage of the effusion
med-clin-im.l06.q5.p: A 70-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia has no improvement after three days on a beta-lactam and a macrolide. A chest radiograph now shows a large pleural effusion with a pH of 7.05 on sampling. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l06.q5.h: A complicated parapneumonic effusion with low pH is infected fluid.
med-clin-im.l06.q5.e: A pH below 7.2 means complicated effusion or empyema, which needs drainage because antibiotics do not penetrate well. Diuretics do not treat an exudate.

med-clin-im.l07.q1.t: Crohn disease of the terminal ileum
med-clin-im.l07.q1.p: Which condition is most characteristically transmural, with skip lesions and granulomas?
med-clin-im.l07.q1.h: Think about the depth of inflammation.
med-clin-im.l07.q1.e: Crohn disease is transmural and patchy, leading to fistulas and strictures. Ulcerative colitis is limited to the mucosa and is continuous from the rectum.

med-clin-im.l07.q2.t: Octreotide and a prophylactic antibiotic such as ceftriaxone
med-clin-im.l07.q2.p: A 55-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis vomits blood and is hypotensive. Along with resuscitation and endoscopy, which drugs should be given?
med-clin-im.l07.q2.h: Portal pressure and infection both matter in variceal bleeds.
med-clin-im.l07.q2.e: Octreotide reduces splanchnic flow and antibiotic prophylaxis lowers infection and mortality. Beta-blockers are avoided during acute hypotension.

med-clin-im.l07.q3.t: Serum tissue transglutaminase IgA with a total IgA measurement
med-clin-im.l07.q3.p: A 30-year-old woman has iron deficiency anemia that does not respond to oral iron, along with bloating and an itchy blistering rash on the elbows. Which test should be ordered first?
med-clin-im.l07.q3.e: Celiac disease is screened with tissue transglutaminase IgA, with total IgA to detect IgA deficiency. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis while eating gluten.

med-clin-im.l07.q4.t: IV steroids, broad antibiotics and urgent surgical consultation
med-clin-im.l07.q4.p: A 24-year-old man with ulcerative colitis on mesalamine has 12 bloody stools daily, fever, heart rate 120 and diffuse abdominal tenderness. An abdominal film shows a transverse colon of 7 cm. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l07.q4.h: A dilated colon with toxicity is a surgical emergency.
med-clin-im.l07.q4.e: Toxic megacolon needs aggressive medical therapy and early surgical involvement. Colonoscopy and antimotility drugs risk perforation.

med-clin-im.l07.q5.p: A 62-year-old man with long-standing reflux has an esophagogastroduodenoscopy showing salmon-colored mucosa extending above the gastroesophageal junction, and biopsy shows intestinal metaplasia without dysplasia. What is the main cancer risk?
med-clin-im.l07.q5.h: Think about the epithelium that replaces squamous cells.
med-clin-im.l07.q5.e: Barrett esophagus predisposes to adenocarcinoma. Squamous carcinoma is linked with alcohol and smoking, and MALT lymphoma with Helicobacter pylori.

med-clin-im.l08.q1.t: Positive surface antibody with negative core antibody
med-clin-im.l08.q1.p: Which hepatitis B serology indicates immunity from vaccination only?
med-clin-im.l08.q1.e: Vaccination produces antibody to surface antigen without exposure to the core antigen. Natural resolved infection also has core IgG.

med-clin-im.l08.q2.t: A third-generation cephalosporin plus intravenous albumin
med-clin-im.l08.q2.p: A cirrhotic patient with ascites is admitted with fever and abdominal pain, and paracentesis shows 600 neutrophils per microliter. What is the correct treatment?
med-clin-im.l08.q2.h: A count of at least 250 neutrophils is diagnostic.
med-clin-im.l08.q2.e: This is spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, which is treated with antibiotics such as cefotaxime or ceftriaxone, and albumin lowers the risk of renal failure.

med-clin-im.l08.q3.t: Lactulose to acidify the colon and trap ammonia
med-clin-im.l08.q3.p: What is the first-line therapy for acute hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis, after correcting precipitants?
med-clin-im.l08.q3.h: Think about ammonia production by gut bacteria.
med-clin-im.l08.q3.e: Lactulose is the foundation of therapy, with rifaximin added for recurrence. Protein restriction is no longer advised.

med-clin-im.l08.q4.t: Early intravenous fluids, analgesia and oral feeding as tolerated
med-clin-im.l08.q4.p: A 45-year-old woman with gallstones has severe epigastric pain, vomiting and a lipase five times normal. She has no fever, a normal bilirubin and stable vital signs. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l08.q4.h: Mild gallstone pancreatitis without cholangitis does not need ERCP.
med-clin-im.l08.q4.e: Supportive care with fluids, analgesia and early feeding is standard. ERCP is for cholangitis or persistent obstruction and antibiotics do not prevent necrosis.

med-clin-im.l08.q5.t: N-acetylcysteine, even if the ingestion time is uncertain
med-clin-im.l08.q5.p: A 36-year-old woman takes acetaminophen for a headache for several days, then presents after an overdose of unknown timing. Her aminotransferases are in the thousands and her INR is 2.4. What should be given?
med-clin-im.l08.q5.h: The antidote works by replenishing glutathione.
med-clin-im.l08.q5.e: N-acetylcysteine is indicated when timing is unknown or aminotransferases are elevated. Vitamin K does not reverse synthetic failure from acute liver injury.

med-clin-im.l09.q1.t: Fractional excretion of sodium above 2 percent with muddy brown casts
med-clin-im.l09.q1.p: Which urine finding supports acute tubular necrosis rather than prerenal azotemia?
med-clin-im.l09.q1.h: The injured tubule can no longer conserve sodium.
med-clin-im.l09.q1.e: Failed sodium reabsorption and granular casts mark tubular necrosis. A low fractional sodium and concentrated urine mark prerenal disease, and red cell casts mark glomerulonephritis.

med-clin-im.l09.q2.p: A hospitalized patient receiving a penicillin for several days develops fever, a rash, rising creatinine, eosinophilia and urinary white cell casts. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l09.q2.h: Hypersensitivity reaction in the renal interstitium.
med-clin-im.l09.q2.e: Drug-induced allergic interstitial nephritis presents with fever, rash, eosinophilia and white cell casts. Stopping the drug is the main treatment.

med-clin-im.l09.q3.t: ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers
med-clin-im.l09.q3.p: Which drug class slows progression of diabetic kidney disease with albuminuria by lowering intraglomerular pressure?
med-clin-im.l09.q3.h: Dilating the efferent arteriole lowers filtration pressure.
med-clin-im.l09.q3.e: ACE inhibitors and ARBs preferentially dilate the efferent arteriole and reduce proteinuria and progression. NSAIDs constrict the afferent arteriole and harm.

med-clin-im.l09.q4.t: Bladder catheterization with a post-void residual measurement
med-clin-im.l09.q4.p: A 72-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia has 12 hours of anuria after starting an antihistamine and a cold remedy. His creatinine has doubled and a suprapubic mass is palpable. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l09.q4.h: Think about the cheapest relief of the likeliest cause.
med-clin-im.l09.q4.e: Urinary retention from anticholinergic and sympathomimetic drugs with prostatic enlargement causes postrenal injury, relieved by a catheter. Fluids will not fix obstruction.

med-clin-im.l09.q5.t: Reduced renal calcitriol synthesis and phosphate retention
med-clin-im.l09.q5.p: A 55-year-old man with CKD stage 4 has a low calcium, a high phosphate and a high parathyroid hormone. Which mechanism explains the elevated parathyroid hormone?
med-clin-im.l09.q5.h: Consider what the failing kidney stops producing.
med-clin-im.l09.q5.e: In CKD, phosphate retention and low calcitriol lower calcium and drive secondary hyperparathyroidism. Adenomas produce hypercalcemia, not hypocalcemia.

med-clin-im.l10.q1.t: Low serum osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine and euvolemia
med-clin-im.l10.q1.p: What is the urine and serum profile of SIADH?
med-clin-im.l10.q1.h: ADH keeps water despite a dilute plasma.
med-clin-im.l10.q1.e: SIADH retains water so plasma is dilute while urine remains concentrated. Primary polydipsia has maximally dilute urine instead.

med-clin-im.l10.q2.t: Intravenous calcium gluconate to stabilize the cardiac membrane
med-clin-im.l10.q2.p: Which emergency treatment is first for hyperkalemia with peaked T waves and a widening QRS?
med-clin-im.l10.q2.h: Protect the heart before lowering the level.
med-clin-im.l10.q2.e: Calcium antagonizes the membrane effect within minutes without changing the potassium level. Insulin with glucose then shifts potassium into cells.

med-clin-im.l10.q3.t: Ethylene glycol with calcium oxalate crystals in the urine
med-clin-im.l10.q3.p: Which cause of a high anion gap metabolic acidosis is correctly paired with its distinguishing finding?
med-clin-im.l10.q3.h: Only one of these options is truly a high-gap cause.
med-clin-im.l10.q3.e: Ethylene glycol is a high-gap cause and produces oxalate crystals. Diarrhea and renal tubular acidosis give normal gap acidosis, and vomiting gives alkalosis.

med-clin-im.l10.q4.t: Osmotic demyelination from overly rapid sodium correction
med-clin-im.l10.q4.p: A 62-year-old malnourished alcoholic with sodium of 108 mEq/L is treated and over 24 hours his sodium rises to 126 mEq/L. Days later he develops dysarthria and flaccid quadriparesis. What is the most likely mechanism?
med-clin-im.l10.q4.h: The pons is vulnerable to osmotic shifts.
med-clin-im.l10.q4.e: A rise of more than 8 to 10 mEq/L per day in chronic hyponatremia, especially with alcoholism and malnutrition, causes demyelination days later. Cerebral edema occurs when sodium falls, not when corrected.

med-clin-im.l10.q5.t: Intravenous normal saline with potassium replacement
med-clin-im.l10.q5.p: A 25-year-old woman with bulimia has serum potassium 2.8, bicarbonate 36 and urine chloride 8 mEq/L. What is the best therapy for her alkalosis?
med-clin-im.l10.q5.h: A low urine chloride shows the state is saline responsive.
med-clin-im.l10.q5.e: Vomiting causes a chloride-responsive alkalosis with volume contraction, so saline and potassium correct it. Spironolactone is for hyperaldosteronism with high urine chloride.

med-clin-im.l11.q1.p: Which hemoglobin A1c value meets the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus?
med-clin-im.l11.q1.h: The threshold is not the prediabetes cutoff.
med-clin-im.l11.q1.e: The ADA threshold for diabetes is 6.5 percent. A level from 5.7 to 6.4 percent is prediabetes.

med-clin-im.l11.q2.t: A GLP-1 receptor agonist or an SGLT2 inhibitor
med-clin-im.l11.q2.p: A 60-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has established coronary disease and an A1c slightly above goal. Which addition best lowers his cardiovascular risk?
med-clin-im.l11.q2.h: Some classes show outcome benefit independent of glucose lowering.
med-clin-im.l11.q2.e: GLP-1 agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors reduce major cardiovascular events. Sulfonylureas and insulin add hypoglycemia without proven cardiovascular benefit.

med-clin-im.l11.q3.t: Replace potassium and give isotonic fluids first
med-clin-im.l11.q3.p: A young patient with DKA has a glucose of 520, pH 7.1 and serum potassium 2.9 mEq/L. What should be done before insulin?
med-clin-im.l11.q3.e: Insulin with a potassium below 3.5 can cause fatal hypokalemia and arrhythmia, so potassium is replaced first. Bicarbonate is not routinely required.

med-clin-im.l11.q4.t: Respiratory compensation for anion gap metabolic acidosis
med-clin-im.l11.q4.p: A 19-year-old man with type 1 diabetes has two days of vomiting and abdominal pain. His glucose is 460 mg/dL, bicarbonate is 9 mEq/L and he breathes deeply and rapidly. Which finding explains the breathing?
med-clin-im.l11.q4.h: The lungs are blowing off carbon dioxide to rescue pH.
med-clin-im.l11.q4.e: Kussmaul respirations are compensation for ketoacidosis, lowering carbon dioxide. A primary respiratory process would not give a bicarbonate of 9.

med-clin-im.l11.q5.p: A 78-year-old man has glucose 920 mg/dL, calculated osmolality 350 mOsm/kg, a normal pH and negative ketones, and is stuporous. What is the correct first intervention?
med-clin-im.l11.q5.h: Dehydration is the dominant problem in hyperosmolar states.
med-clin-im.l11.q5.e: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state is treated with large fluid deficits first, then insulin. Insulin alone would shift water into cells and worsen shock.

med-clin-im.l12.q1.p: Which antibody is associated with Hashimoto thyroiditis?
med-clin-im.l12.q1.h: This is the common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions.
med-clin-im.l12.q1.e: Anti-TPO antibodies mark Hashimoto disease. Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin causes Graves disease.

med-clin-im.l12.q2.t: Check a complete blood count with differential for agranulocytosis
med-clin-im.l12.q2.p: A woman taking methimazole for Graves disease develops fever and a sore throat. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l12.q2.h: Think about the rare dangerous effect of thionamides.
med-clin-im.l12.q2.e: Agranulocytosis is a rare but serious effect of thionamides and requires stopping the drug if neutrophils are low.

med-clin-im.l12.q3.t: Alpha-blockade first, then a beta-blocker if needed
med-clin-im.l12.q3.p: Which sequence is correct before surgery for a pheochromocytoma?
med-clin-im.l12.q3.h: Beta-blockade alone leaves alpha stimulation unopposed.
med-clin-im.l12.q3.e: Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta-blockade can precipitate a hypertensive crisis, so alpha-blockade comes first.

med-clin-im.l12.q4.t: Secondary adrenal insufficiency from suppression of ACTH
med-clin-im.l12.q4.p: A 45-year-old woman on long-term prednisone for asthma stops it abruptly and a week later has nausea, fatigue and hypotension. Potassium is normal, sodium is 130 mEq/L. What is the most likely cause?
med-clin-im.l12.q4.h: The normal potassium is a clue to the intact renin axis.
med-clin-im.l12.q4.e: Chronic steroids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, so cortisol falls on withdrawal while aldosterone remains intact and potassium stays normal.

med-clin-im.l12.q5.p: A 35-year-old woman has heat intolerance, weight loss, a diffuse goiter, exophthalmos and a low TSH. Radioactive iodine uptake is diffusely increased. Which finding is likely present?
med-clin-im.l12.q5.h: Eye disease and diffuse uptake define one disorder.
med-clin-im.l12.q5.e: Graves disease is caused by stimulating antibodies to the TSH receptor, giving diffuse uptake and orbitopathy. A solitary hot nodule would show focal uptake.

med-clin-im.l13.q1.t: Low ferritin with high total iron-binding capacity
med-clin-im.l13.q1.p: Which laboratory pattern best fits iron deficiency anemia?
med-clin-im.l13.q1.h: The body upregulates its carrier protein when iron is scarce.
med-clin-im.l13.q1.e: Iron deficiency shows depleted stores and a compensatory rise in transferrin capacity. Anemia of chronic disease shows high ferritin with low capacity.

med-clin-im.l13.q2.t: Folic acid given without vitamin B12 replacement
med-clin-im.l13.q2.p: A man with a megaloblastic anemia has numbness in the feet and loss of vibration sense. What should be avoided as monotherapy?
med-clin-im.l13.q2.h: One vitamin can fix the blood but not the nervous system.
med-clin-im.l13.q2.e: Folate corrects the anemia of B12 deficiency but allows neurologic damage to progress, so B12 must be replaced.

med-clin-im.l13.q3.t: Evaluate the gastrointestinal tract for a bleeding source
med-clin-im.l13.q3.p: A 58-year-old man has microcytic anemia with low ferritin. What is the most important next step?
med-clin-im.l13.q3.h: Iron deficiency in an older man is a sign, not just a diagnosis.
med-clin-im.l13.q3.e: Iron deficiency in an adult man implies chronic gastrointestinal blood loss until proven otherwise, with colorectal cancer a key concern.

med-clin-im.l13.q4.p: A 22-year-old man has sudden jaundice and dark urine two days after starting a sulfa antibiotic for infection. His smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies, and Coombs test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l13.q4.h: Oxidant stress, bite cells and negative Coombs point to an enzyme defect.
med-clin-im.l13.q4.e: G6PD deficiency causes oxidative hemolysis, with Heinz bodies and bite cells. A positive Coombs test would indicate autoimmune hemolysis.

med-clin-im.l13.q5.p: A 30-year-old woman of Mediterranean descent has an MCV of 62 fL, a red cell count of 6.1 million per microliter, a normal ferritin and no symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l13.q5.h: A very low MCV with a high red cell count is a clue.
med-clin-im.l13.q5.e: Thalassemia trait gives microcytosis out of proportion to the anemia, with a high red cell count and a normal ferritin.

med-clin-im.l14.q1.t: Hemophilia A due to factor VIII deficiency
med-clin-im.l14.q1.p: Which disorder causes a prolonged aPTT with a normal PT and X-linked inheritance?
med-clin-im.l14.q1.h: The intrinsic pathway and sex linkage point to a factor.
med-clin-im.l14.q1.e: Hemophilia A and B are X-linked and prolong aPTT. Von Willebrand disease is usually autosomal and mucocutaneous.

med-clin-im.l14.q2.p: Which treatment is specific for thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura?
med-clin-im.l14.q2.h: The missing protease must be replaced and antibodies removed.
med-clin-im.l14.q2.e: Plasma exchange replaces ADAMTS13 and removes inhibitors. Platelet transfusion can fuel microthrombi.

med-clin-im.l14.q3.t: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate with vitamin K
med-clin-im.l14.q3.p: A patient bleeds on warfarin with an INR of 9. Which reversal gives the fastest effect for life-threatening bleeding?
med-clin-im.l14.q3.h: Vitamin K alone takes many hours to work.
med-clin-im.l14.q3.e: Prothrombin complex concentrate replaces vitamin K dependent factors immediately, and vitamin K sustains the effect. Protamine reverses heparin.

med-clin-im.l14.q4.t: Stop heparin and begin argatroban or fondaparinux
med-clin-im.l14.q4.p: A 62-year-old woman on heparin after surgery has her platelet count fall from 280,000 to 90,000 on day 7, and she develops a new leg deep venous thrombosis. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l14.q4.h: Think about an antibody-mediated prothrombotic state.
med-clin-im.l14.q4.e: This is heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis, so all heparin stops and a nonheparin anticoagulant starts. Warfarin alone can cause limb gangrene.

med-clin-im.l14.q5.t: Severely deficient ADAMTS13 activity causing platelet-rich microthrombi
med-clin-im.l14.q5.p: A 28-year-old woman has fever, confusion, a platelet count of 18,000, a hemoglobin of 8 g/dL, and schistocytes. Her PT and aPTT are normal and her creatinine is mildly raised. What is the likely mechanism?
med-clin-im.l14.q5.h: Normal clotting studies argue against DIC.
med-clin-im.l14.q5.e: TTP produces microangiopathic hemolysis and thrombocytopenia with normal coagulation studies. DIC would prolong the PT and aPTT.

med-clin-im.l15.q1.p: At what ages does the USPSTF recommend routine colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults (2021)?
med-clin-im.l15.q1.h: The 2021 update moved the starting age earlier.
med-clin-im.l15.q1.e: The 2021 USPSTF recommendation starts at 45, with the strongest evidence from 50 to 75.

med-clin-im.l15.q2.p: A 62-year-old woman has a lung mass, hyponatremia with concentrated urine, and proximal muscle weakness that improves with repeated use. What is the likely tumor?
med-clin-im.l15.q2.h: The syndromes combine SIADH and Lambert-Eaton.
med-clin-im.l15.q2.e: Small cell carcinoma is linked to SIADH, ectopic ACTH and Lambert-Eaton syndrome. Squamous tumors cause hypercalcemia.

med-clin-im.l15.q3.t: Annual low-dose CT of the chest
med-clin-im.l15.q3.p: A 56-year-old man smoked 30 pack-years and quit 5 years ago. Which screening is recommended?
med-clin-im.l15.q3.h: The 2021 USPSTF criteria are age, pack-years and years since quitting.
med-clin-im.l15.q3.e: He meets criteria of age 50 to 80, 20 pack-years and quitting within 15 years. Chest radiographs do not reduce mortality.

med-clin-im.l15.q4.t: Trousseau syndrome from a tumor-related hypercoagulable state
med-clin-im.l15.q4.p: A 66-year-old man with pancreatic adenocarcinoma has recurrent migratory superficial venous thromboses and a new swollen calf. What is the best explanation?
med-clin-im.l15.q4.e: Migratory thrombophlebitis with visceral cancer is Trousseau syndrome. Lambert-Eaton causes weakness, not thrombosis.

med-clin-im.l15.q5.p: A screening test advances the time of diagnosis of a cancer by two years but does not change the date of death. Which bias explains the apparent improvement in survival?
med-clin-im.l15.q5.h: Survival is counted from diagnosis, not from onset.
med-clin-im.l15.q5.e: Earlier diagnosis lengthens measured survival without delaying death, which is lead-time bias. Length bias favors slowly growing tumors.

med-clin-im.l16.q1.p: Which translocation produces BCR-ABL in chronic myeloid leukemia?
med-clin-im.l16.q1.h: The abnormal chromosome is named for a city.
med-clin-im.l16.q1.e: CML carries t(9;22) giving the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase, targeted by imatinib.

med-clin-im.l16.q2.p: A man with a high-grade lymphoma receives chemotherapy and develops potassium 6.4, phosphate 8.5, calcium 6.5 and uric acid 14 within two days. What is the diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l16.q2.h: Think about the release of intracellular contents.
med-clin-im.l16.q2.e: Lysis of rapidly proliferating cells releases potassium, phosphate and nucleic acids, which lowers calcium. Prevention uses hydration and rasburicase or allopurinol.

med-clin-im.l16.q3.t: Empiric antipseudomonal beta-lactam started within an hour
med-clin-im.l16.q3.p: Which feature defines febrile neutropenia management?
med-clin-im.l16.q3.h: Neutropenic patients decline quickly and signs are muted.
med-clin-im.l16.q3.e: Early broad coverage lowers mortality. Delaying for cultures is unsafe.

med-clin-im.l16.q4.t: High-dose dexamethasone and urgent MRI of the entire spine
med-clin-im.l16.q4.p: A 64-year-old man with prostate cancer has two weeks of back pain, and now has leg weakness and urinary retention. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l16.q4.h: Neurologic loss in a cancer patient is time-critical.
med-clin-im.l16.q4.e: Spinal cord compression is an emergency requiring MRI and steroids, followed by radiation or surgery. Delay risks permanent paralysis.

med-clin-im.l16.q5.p: A 35-year-old woman with fever, gingival bleeding and pancytopenia has blasts with Auer rods, a prolonged PT and aPTT, low fibrinogen and a t(15;17). What should be given immediately?
med-clin-im.l16.q5.h: This subtype differentiates in response to a vitamin A derivative.
med-clin-im.l16.q5.e: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is treated with all-trans retinoic acid, started at suspicion because DIC is deadly. Imatinib targets BCR-ABL.

med-clin-im.l17.q1.p: Which vasopressor is recommended first-line for septic shock?
med-clin-im.l17.q1.h: The Surviving Sepsis Campaign names one agent as first choice.
med-clin-im.l17.q1.e: Norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor, with vasopressin added if needed. Dopamine is associated with more arrhythmias.

med-clin-im.l17.q2.t: Vancomycin, ceftriaxone and ampicillin plus dexamethasone
med-clin-im.l17.q2.p: A 68-year-old with meningitis symptoms needs empiric treatment. Which regimen covers the likely organisms?
med-clin-im.l17.q2.h: Age over 50 adds an organism that cephalosporins miss.
med-clin-im.l17.q2.e: Listeria is not covered by cephalosporins, so ampicillin is added in adults over 50, and dexamethasone helps pneumococcal disease.

med-clin-im.l17.q3.p: Cerebrospinal fluid shows 1,200 neutrophils per microliter, glucose 20 mg/dL, and protein 280 mg/dL. What is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l17.q3.h: Low glucose and a neutrophil predominance together are characteristic.
med-clin-im.l17.q3.e: Bacterial meningitis shows neutrophils, low glucose and high protein. Viral meningitis shows lymphocytes and normal glucose.

med-clin-im.l17.q4.t: Blood cultures, then antibiotics and dexamethasone before CT
med-clin-im.l17.q4.p: A 45-year-old woman with fever, confusion and neck stiffness has a papilledema on fundoscopy. What should happen first?
med-clin-im.l17.q4.h: Do not delay antibiotics for imaging.
med-clin-im.l17.q4.e: With features suggesting raised intracranial pressure, imaging comes before lumbar puncture, but antibiotics must not wait.

med-clin-im.l17.q5.t: Oral fidaxomicin and stopping the inciting antibiotic
med-clin-im.l17.q5.p: A 72-year-old woman has profuse watery diarrhea, a white count of 25,000 and fever after treatment for pneumonia with clindamycin. Stool toxin is positive. What is the preferred initial treatment?
med-clin-im.l17.q5.h: The 2021 IDSA update reordered the preferred agents.
med-clin-im.l17.q5.e: Fidaxomicin is preferred for an initial episode, with vancomycin acceptable. Antimotility agents risk toxic megacolon.

med-clin-im.l18.q1.t: A fourth-generation antigen and antibody assay
med-clin-im.l18.q1.p: Which test is recommended first for HIV screening?
med-clin-im.l18.q1.h: The test detects both p24 and antibody.
med-clin-im.l18.q1.e: Fourth-generation assays shorten the window period by detecting p24 antigen as well as antibodies.

med-clin-im.l18.q2.p: A man with HIV has a CD4 count of 90 cells per microliter, and a headache with ring-enhancing brain lesions on MRI and positive Toxoplasma IgG. What is the best therapy?
med-clin-im.l18.q2.h: Toxoplasma reactivates when CD4 falls below 100.
med-clin-im.l18.q2.e: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions with positive serology in advanced HIV are treated empirically for toxoplasmosis, and response confirms it.

med-clin-im.l18.q3.p: Which adverse effect of isoniazid can be prevented with a vitamin supplement?
med-clin-im.l18.q3.h: Isoniazid interferes with vitamin B6 metabolism.
med-clin-im.l18.q3.e: Isoniazid causes B6-deficiency neuropathy, so pyridoxine is given. Optic neuritis is from ethambutol.

med-clin-im.l18.q4.p: A 38-year-old man with HIV and a CD4 count of 120 has three weeks of dry cough and exertional dyspnea. Oxygen saturation drops on walking, LDH is high, and the chest film shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Which is the best treatment?
med-clin-im.l18.q4.h: Think about the organism with a high LDH and ground-glass opacities.
med-clin-im.l18.q4.e: This is Pneumocystis pneumonia, treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and steroids reduce mortality in moderate to severe hypoxemia.

med-clin-im.l18.q5.p: A man receiving rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for active tuberculosis reports that his vision appears blurry, with trouble seeing red and green. Which drug is responsible?
med-clin-im.l18.q5.h: Think about the drug with an optic nerve effect.
med-clin-im.l18.q5.e: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis with loss of color discrimination. Isoniazid causes neuropathy.

med-clin-im.l19.q1.p: What do crystals of monosodium urate look like under polarized light?
med-clin-im.l19.q1.h: Gout is needle-shaped, and the sign is opposite to pseudogout.
med-clin-im.l19.q1.e: Urate crystals are negatively birefringent needles. Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are rhomboid and positively birefringent.

med-clin-im.l19.q2.p: Which antibody is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
med-clin-im.l19.q2.h: ANA is sensitive but not specific.
med-clin-im.l19.q2.e: Anti-Smith and anti-dsDNA are specific for lupus. ANA is positive in most lupus patients but also in many healthy people.

med-clin-im.l19.q3.p: Before starting a biologic for rheumatoid arthritis, which infection should be screened for?
med-clin-im.l19.q3.h: Immune suppression can reactivate dormant infections.
med-clin-im.l19.q3.e: Biologics, especially TNF inhibitors, can reactivate latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B.

med-clin-im.l19.q4.t: High-dose glucocorticoids now, then temporal artery biopsy
med-clin-im.l19.q4.p: A 70-year-old woman has a new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain on chewing and an ESR of 95 mm/hour. She has transient blurred vision in the left eye. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l19.q4.h: Permanent blindness can occur within days.
med-clin-im.l19.q4.e: In suspected giant cell arteritis with visual symptoms, steroids are started immediately, because biopsy remains useful for days after treatment begins.

med-clin-im.l19.q5.t: Intravenous antibiotics and joint drainage after cultures
med-clin-im.l19.q5.p: A 56-year-old man has an acutely hot swollen knee, a temperature of 38.7 C and a synovial white cell count of 85,000 per microliter. Crystals are negative. What is the next best step?
med-clin-im.l19.q5.h: Presume infection until it is excluded.
med-clin-im.l19.q5.e: A very high count without crystals suggests septic arthritis, which needs antibiotics and drainage. Steroid injection into an infected joint is harmful.

med-clin-im.l20.q1.p: Which bone mineral density T-score defines osteoporosis?
med-clin-im.l20.q1.h: The WHO threshold is a standard.
med-clin-im.l20.q1.e: A T-score at or below minus 2.5 defines osteoporosis, and minus 1 to minus 2.5 is osteopenia.

med-clin-im.l20.q2.t: Seek causes and use nonpharmacologic measures first
med-clin-im.l20.q2.p: An 84-year-old woman becomes confused and agitated over two days of hospitalization for pneumonia. Which approach is best?
med-clin-im.l20.q2.h: Acute fluctuating attention changes are not dementia.
med-clin-im.l20.q2.e: Delirium needs treatment of precipitants and supportive measures. Benzodiazepines often worsen it.

med-clin-im.l20.q3.p: Which drug is a typical Beers Criteria example of a potentially inappropriate agent in older adults?
med-clin-im.l20.q3.h: Anticholinergic burden is a major concern.
med-clin-im.l20.q3.e: First-generation antihistamines are anticholinergic and cause confusion, urinary retention and falls in older adults.

med-clin-im.l20.q4.p: A 77-year-old man has progressive memory decline, a broad-based shuffling gait and urinary urgency with incontinence. CT shows enlarged ventricles without prominent sulcal atrophy. What is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-im.l20.q4.h: The triad is wet, wobbly and wacky.
med-clin-im.l20.q4.e: Gait disturbance, incontinence and dementia with ventriculomegaly are classic, and the gait often improves after shunting.

med-clin-im.l20.q5.t: Benefit takes years, so screening is generally not advised
med-clin-im.l20.q5.p: A frail 88-year-old with advanced dementia and a life expectancy under a year is due for repeat colonoscopy. What is the best reasoning?
med-clin-im.l20.q5.h: Time to benefit must be compared with life expectancy.
med-clin-im.l20.q5.e: Screening benefits accrue over years, so in limited life expectancy the harms of the procedure usually outweigh them.

med-clin-obgyn.l01.q1.t: Increased glomerular filtration rate with a lower serum creatinine
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q1.p: Which change in renal physiology is expected in normal pregnancy?
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q1.e: GFR rises about 50 percent in pregnancy, so creatinine falls, and a value near 1.0 mg/dL suggests significant renal impairment.

med-clin-obgyn.l01.q2.t: Anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks and after delivery
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q2.p: A 29-year-old at 27 weeks is Rh-negative with a negative antibody screen and an Rh-positive partner. Which management is correct?
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q2.h: Prevention begins before any sensitising event.
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q2.e: Unsensitised Rh-negative women receive prophylaxis at about 28 weeks and within 72 hours of delivering an Rh-positive infant. Transfusion is for sensitised pregnancies.

med-clin-obgyn.l01.q3.p: A 32-year-old woman at 10 weeks has chronic hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Which intervention reduces her risk of preeclampsia?
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q3.h: A USPSTF recommendation for high-risk women.
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q3.e: Low-dose aspirin is recommended for women with high-risk factors such as chronic hypertension and diabetes. Bed rest does not prevent preeclampsia.

med-clin-obgyn.l01.q4.t: Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks in every pregnancy
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q4.p: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks has not received Tdap. Which statement is most accurate?
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q4.e: Tdap is recommended in each pregnancy at 27 to 36 weeks, to maximise transplacental antibody to the newborn.

med-clin-obgyn.l01.q5.p: A woman with hypertension has just discovered she is 7 weeks pregnant while taking lisinopril. Which fetal effect is the greatest concern if exposure continues into the second and third trimesters?
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q5.h: Angiotensin is needed for fetal kidney development.
med-clin-obgyn.l01.q5.e: ACE inhibitors cause fetal renal injury and oligohydramnios in later pregnancy. Ebstein anomaly relates to lithium and phocomelia to thalidomide.

med-clin-obgyn.l02.q1.t: A sensitive screen whose positives need confirmation
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q1.p: Which statement describes cell-free DNA screening?
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q1.e: Cell-free DNA is the most sensitive screening test for common aneuploidies but is not diagnostic, so a positive result is confirmed by CVS or amniocentesis.

med-clin-obgyn.l02.q2.p: A quadruple screen at 17 weeks shows low AFP, low oestriol, high hCG and high inhibin A. Which condition does this pattern suggest?
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q2.h: Only the hCG and inhibin A rise.
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q2.e: Down syndrome shows low AFP and oestriol with high hCG and inhibin A. Trisomy 18 gives low levels of all markers and neural tube defects raise AFP.

med-clin-obgyn.l02.q3.t: Genetic counselling and diagnostic CVS or amniocentesis
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q3.p: A 25-year-old at 12 weeks receives a positive cell-free DNA screen for trisomy 18, with no ultrasound abnormalities. Which statement best describes the next step?
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q3.h: Positive predictive value depends on prevalence.
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q3.e: In younger women, positive predictive value is lower, so diagnostic testing is needed to confirm. Management decisions follow a diagnostic result and the patient's values.

med-clin-obgyn.l02.q4.p: An Rh-negative woman at 20 weeks has a positive indirect Coombs test with high titre anti-D. What is the best method for assessing fetal anaemia?
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q4.h: Anaemic fetuses have increased cerebral blood flow velocity.
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q4.e: In an alloimmunised pregnancy, middle cerebral artery Doppler non-invasively detects fetal anaemia. Immune globulin does not help once sensitisation has occurred.

med-clin-obgyn.l02.q5.t: Dating error from inaccurate menstrual dates
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q5.p: A pregnant woman at 18 weeks has an elevated maternal serum AFP. Ultrasound shows normal anatomy and a gestational age by crown-rump length 3 weeks less than by menstrual dates. What is the most likely explanation?
med-clin-obgyn.l02.q5.e: AFP varies by gestational age; wrong dates are a common cause of an abnormal value. Early dating by ultrasound resolves the discrepancy, and normal detailed anatomy argues against structural defects.

med-clin-obgyn.l03.q1.p: According to ACOG and SMFM (2014), at what cervical dilation does the active phase of labour generally begin?
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q1.h: The older standard of 4 cm was revised.
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q1.e: Active labour is considered to begin at about 6 cm, which reduces overdiagnosis of dystocia and primary cesarean delivery.

med-clin-obgyn.l03.q2.p: A fetal heart tracing shows decelerations that begin after the peak of each contraction and return to baseline after it ends, with moderate variability. What is the most likely mechanism?
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q2.e: Late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency. Early decelerations arise from head compression and variable decelerations from cord compression.

med-clin-obgyn.l03.q3.t: Expedited delivery, by cesarean if not imminent
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q3.p: A woman at 8 cm dilation has a tracing with absent variability and recurrent late decelerations. Intrauterine resuscitation measures are tried for 20 minutes without change. What is the most appropriate next step?
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q3.h: This is a Category III tracing.
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q3.e: A Category III tracing that does not respond to resuscitation needs prompt delivery. Amnioinfusion treats variable decelerations from cord compression.

med-clin-obgyn.l03.q4.p: Which fetal heart rate feature best reflects an intact, well-oxygenated fetal central nervous system?
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q4.e: Moderate variability is the single most reassuring sign of fetal acid-base status. Early decelerations are benign but are not a marker of oxygenation.

med-clin-obgyn.l03.q5.t: Cervical ripening with prostaglandin or a balloon
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q5.p: A primigravid woman at 39 weeks has a Bishop score of 3 and requires labour induction for a medical indication. Which option is the best initial step?
med-clin-obgyn.l03.q5.e: A low Bishop score predicts failed induction, so cervical ripening is advised before oxytocin. Cesarean is not indicated solely by an unfavourable cervix.

med-clin-obgyn.l04.q1.t: The McRoberts manoeuvre with suprapubic pressure
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q1.p: What is the first manoeuvre in the management of shoulder dystocia after calling for help?
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q1.h: Thigh hyperflexion enlarges the pelvic outlet.
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q1.e: McRoberts positioning with suprapubic pressure is first-line. Fundal pressure and heavy traction on the head increase impaction and plexus injury.

med-clin-obgyn.l04.q2.t: Active-phase arrest, for which cesarean delivery is indicated
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q2.p: A primigravid woman at 40 weeks is 7 cm dilated with ruptured membranes. After 4 hours with adequate contractions, there is no cervical change. What is the best interpretation and plan?
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q2.h: Consider both dilation and the duration of observation.
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q2.e: Dilation of 6 cm or more with ruptured membranes and no change for 4 hours despite adequate contractions defines active-phase arrest. Forceps require full dilation.

med-clin-obgyn.l04.q3.t: She is a candidate for TOLAC, with a uterine rupture risk of roughly 0.5 to 1 percent
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q3.p: A 28-year-old woman with a prior single low-transverse cesarean at 39 weeks wishes to labour. Her previous cesarean was for breech presentation. Which statement is most accurate?
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q3.e: One prior low-transverse incision makes her a candidate for TOLAC with a small risk of rupture. Prostaglandins are generally avoided with a scarred uterus.

med-clin-obgyn.l04.q4.t: It succeeds in about half of attempts and is contraindicated in placenta previa
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q4.p: A 37-week primigravida has a frank breech fetus. Which statement about external cephalic version is correct?
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q4.h: Consider when and for whom it is done.
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q4.e: ECV is offered at 36 to 37 weeks and succeeds about half the time; placenta previa and ruptured membranes are contraindications.

med-clin-obgyn.l04.q5.t: Induction did not raise cesarean rates and is reasonable to offer
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q5.p: A nulliparous woman at 39 weeks with a healthy pregnancy asks whether induction without a medical reason is safe. Her cervix is favourable. What can be said based on the ARRIVE trial?
med-clin-obgyn.l04.q5.e: ARRIVE found that elective induction at 39 weeks in low-risk nulliparas did not raise, and slightly lowered, cesarean delivery. It is reasonable to offer after counselling.

med-clin-obgyn.l05.q1.p: Which drug is given to women at risk of delivery before 32 weeks to reduce the risk of cerebral palsy in the infant?
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q1.e: Magnesium sulfate before anticipated early preterm delivery reduces cerebral palsy. Tocolytics buy time but are not neuroprotective.

med-clin-obgyn.l05.q2.t: Admit, give steroids and latency antibiotics, deliver near 34 weeks
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q2.p: A woman at 31 weeks has leakage of fluid. A sterile speculum examination shows pooling, and the fluid is alkaline and ferns. There is no fever and the tracing is reactive. What is the best management?
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q2.h: PPROM remote from term and no infection.
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q2.e: Preterm PROM without infection or fetal compromise is managed expectantly with steroids and antibiotics to prolong pregnancy, then delivery at about 34 weeks. Digital examinations are avoided.

med-clin-obgyn.l05.q3.t: Broad antibiotics and delivery, cesarean only if indicated
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q3.p: A woman at 30 weeks has fever of 38.6 C, a heart rate of 120, fetal tachycardia, a tender uterus and ruptured membranes. Which is the best management?
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q3.h: Infection of the uterine contents is not compatible with continuing pregnancy.
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q3.e: Chorioamnionitis requires antibiotics and delivery, usually vaginal if no other indication. Tocolysis is contraindicated.

med-clin-obgyn.l05.q4.t: To delay delivery about 48 hours for steroids
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q4.p: A woman at 28 weeks is given nifedipine for preterm contractions with cervical change. What is its purpose?
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q4.h: Tocolytics do not improve neonatal outcomes by themselves.
med-clin-obgyn.l05.q4.e: Tocolytics buy a short window for steroids and maternal transfer. Magnesium and steroids provide neuroprotection and lung maturation.
