med-clin-psych.l03.q4.e: Beta-blockers blunt adrenergic signs in performance-only anxiety. Buspirone and clomipramine require weeks to work, and daily benzodiazepines create unnecessary dependence risk.

med-clin-psych.l03.q5.t: Exposure and response prevention, with or without an SSRI
med-clin-psych.l03.q5.p: Which treatment has the strongest evidence for compulsions in OCD?
med-clin-psych.l03.q5.h: The therapy involves facing triggers while resisting rituals.
med-clin-psych.l03.q5.e: Exposure and response prevention is the specific CBT with the best evidence. Reassurance often reinforces the cycle, and benzodiazepines do not address compulsions.

med-clin-psych.l04.q1.t: Symptom duration of three days to one month after the trauma
med-clin-psych.l04.q1.p: How is acute stress disorder distinguished from PTSD?
med-clin-psych.l04.q1.e: Acute stress disorder lasts three days to one month; PTSD requires more than one month. Both involve intrusion and avoidance and both require a qualifying trauma.

med-clin-psych.l04.q2.t: A trauma-focused psychotherapy such as prolonged exposure or cognitive processing therapy
med-clin-psych.l04.q2.p: Which treatment is preferred first-line for PTSD by the 2023 VA/DoD guideline?
med-clin-psych.l04.q2.h: Think of therapies that directly process the memory.
med-clin-psych.l04.q2.e: Trauma-focused psychotherapies have the strongest evidence. Benzodiazepines do not treat core symptoms and may worsen outcomes, and routine early debriefing has not prevented PTSD.

med-clin-psych.l04.q3.p: A 41-year-old man develops low mood, tearfulness and trouble concentrating six weeks after being laid off. He enjoys time with his children, sleeps adequately, and has no suicidal thoughts. He does not meet criteria for major depression. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-psych.l04.q3.h: Identifiable stressor, subthreshold symptoms, within three months.
med-clin-psych.l04.q3.e: A recognizable stressor with symptoms that do not meet another disorder defines adjustment disorder. Acute stress disorder requires an extreme trauma, and persistent depression requires two years.

med-clin-psych.l04.q4.t: Cognitive processing therapy, with an SSRI as a reasonable alternative or add-on
med-clin-psych.l04.q4.p: A 29-year-old woman was sexually assaulted eight months ago. She has nightmares, avoids the neighborhood, startles easily and feels detached. Which regimen is most appropriate to offer?
med-clin-psych.l04.q4.h: Symptoms exceed one month and cluster across four domains.
med-clin-psych.l04.q4.e: This is PTSD, for which trauma-focused therapy is first-line and SSRIs are acceptable alternatives. Scheduled benzodiazepines are discouraged because they risk dependence and worsened outcomes.

med-clin-psych.l04.q5.p: Which drug is often used for trauma-related nightmares, though guideline support varies?
med-clin-psych.l04.q5.h: It is an alpha-1 blocker also used for blood pressure.
med-clin-psych.l04.q5.e: Prazosin reduces noradrenergic activity and is used for PTSD nightmares. Clonazepam is not recommended for PTSD and stimulants and bupropion could worsen arousal.

med-clin-psych.l05.q1.p: Which Cluster B personality disorder is characterized by instability of relationships, self-image and affect with recurrent self-harm?
med-clin-psych.l05.q1.h: Think of fear of abandonment and splitting.
med-clin-psych.l05.q1.e: Borderline personality disorder features unstable relationships and self-harm. Narcissistic and histrionic involve grandiosity and attention-seeking, and antisocial involves violation of others' rights.

med-clin-psych.l05.q2.p: A man avoids parties because he fears criticism but wants close friends. Which disorder best fits, as opposed to schizoid personality disorder?
med-clin-psych.l05.q2.h: Social inhibition together with a desire for connection.
med-clin-psych.l05.q2.e: Avoidant patients desire closeness but fear rejection, while schizoid patients do not want relationships. Dependent and paranoid disorders have different core features.

med-clin-psych.l05.q3.p: A 30-year-old woman alternately describes one clinician as perfect and then as incompetent and cruel after a missed appointment. Which defense mechanism is most evident?
med-clin-psych.l05.q3.h: People are viewed as all good or all bad.
med-clin-psych.l05.q3.e: Splitting is the failure to integrate good and bad qualities in the same person, typical of borderline personality disorder. Sublimation channels impulses into acceptable activity and is a mature defense.

med-clin-psych.l05.q4.t: Dialectical behavior therapy with skills training
med-clin-psych.l05.q4.p: A 24-year-old woman has chronic emptiness, unstable relationships, impulsive spending and repeated superficial self-cutting after interpersonal stress. Which intervention has the strongest evidence?
med-clin-psych.l05.q4.h: The therapy includes mindfulness and distress tolerance.
med-clin-psych.l05.q4.e: DBT is the best-studied treatment for borderline personality disorder and chronic self-harm. No drug is approved, and benzodiazepines can disinhibit and add overdose risk.

med-clin-psych.l05.q5.p: A 40-year-old accountant is preoccupied with rules and lists, insists others do tasks his way, and views his behavior as simply correct. He has no intrusive thoughts or rituals. What is the diagnosis?
med-clin-psych.l05.q5.h: Look for ego-syntonic traits without obsessions or compulsions.
med-clin-psych.l05.q5.e: OCPD involves ego-syntonic perfectionism and control. OCD involves ego-dystonic obsessions and ritualized compulsions, which are absent here.

med-clin-psych.l06.q1.p: Which laboratory pattern is classic for repeated self-induced vomiting?
med-clin-psych.l06.q1.h: Gastric acid and potassium are lost.
med-clin-psych.l06.q1.e: Vomiting loses hydrochloric acid and potassium, causing hypokalemic hypochloremic alkalosis. Laxative abuse instead tends to cause a non-gap acidosis.

med-clin-psych.l06.q2.p: Which medication is FDA approved for bulimia nervosa and is paired with cognitive behavioral therapy?
med-clin-psych.l06.q2.h: It is an SSRI, and one alternative is contraindicated.
med-clin-psych.l06.q2.e: Fluoxetine is the approved drug for bulimia nervosa. Bupropion is contraindicated because of seizure risk in purging patients.

med-clin-psych.l06.q3.t: Hypophosphatemia from refeeding with intracellular shift of phosphate
med-clin-psych.l06.q3.p: A severely underweight 17-year-old with anorexia nervosa begins aggressive nutritional rehabilitation as an inpatient. On day four she has weakness, edema and dysrhythmia. Which abnormality is most likely?
med-clin-psych.l06.q3.e: Refeeding causes insulin-driven intracellular movement of phosphate, potassium and magnesium, and hypophosphatemia can cause heart failure and arrhythmia. The other options do not explain the typical picture.

med-clin-psych.l06.q4.t: Family-based treatment in which parents take charge of refeeding
med-clin-psych.l06.q4.p: A 15-year-old with anorexia nervosa is medically stable and lives with supportive parents. Which treatment has the best evidence for her?
med-clin-psych.l06.q4.e: Family-based treatment is best supported in adolescent anorexia. Medications have little evidence for weight restoration, and bupropion is contraindicated.

med-clin-psych.l06.q5.p: A woman of normal weight reports weekly episodes of eating a large amount with loss of control, followed by self-induced vomiting, and says her self-worth depends on her shape. What is the diagnosis?
med-clin-psych.l06.q5.h: Consider compensatory behavior and body weight.
med-clin-psych.l06.q5.e: Binges with compensatory vomiting at normal weight is bulimia nervosa. Binge-eating disorder lacks compensation, and anorexia requires significantly low weight.

med-clin-psych.l07.q1.t: Six months, including at least one month of active symptoms
med-clin-psych.l07.q1.p: What is the minimum total duration of illness signs for a diagnosis of schizophrenia?
med-clin-psych.l07.q1.e: Schizophrenia needs six months of disturbance with at least one month of active phase symptoms. Shorter courses are classified as schizophreniform or brief psychotic disorder.

med-clin-psych.l07.q2.p: A man has hallucinations and delusions for three months with no mood episodes and a clear decline in functioning. What is the diagnosis?
med-clin-psych.l07.q2.e: Active symptoms lasting one to six months define schizophreniform disorder. Brief psychotic disorder lasts under a month, and schizoaffective disorder requires a major mood episode.

med-clin-psych.l07.q3.t: Clozapine, with absolute neutrophil count monitoring
med-clin-psych.l07.q3.p: A 27-year-old woman with schizophrenia has had inadequate responses to trials of two different antipsychotics at adequate doses and durations. Which agent is most appropriate next, and what monitoring is essential?
med-clin-psych.l07.q3.e: Clozapine is the drug for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and requires neutrophil monitoring for agranulocytosis. The other agents lack that indication.

med-clin-psych.l07.q4.t: Urine toxicology and a medical workup before diagnosing a primary psychosis
med-clin-psych.l07.q4.p: A 19-year-old man has had six weeks of auditory hallucinations and paranoia after beginning heavy daily cannabis use, with no similar illness before. Which step best improves diagnostic accuracy?
med-clin-psych.l07.q4.e: Substance and medical causes must be excluded before schizophrenia is diagnosed, and the course after abstinence is informative. A diagnosis at six weeks would not satisfy duration criteria.

med-clin-psych.l07.q5.t: Excess dopamine activity in the mesolimbic pathway
med-clin-psych.l07.q5.p: Which dopamine pathway abnormality is linked to positive symptoms of schizophrenia?
med-clin-psych.l07.q5.h: Positive symptoms reflect too much signaling.
med-clin-psych.l07.q5.e: Mesolimbic hyperactivity underlies positive symptoms, while mesocortical hypoactivity relates to negative symptoms. Tuberoinfundibular blockade causes hyperprolactinemia.

med-clin-psych.l08.q1.t: Fluctuating attention and disorientation of acute onset
med-clin-psych.l08.q1.p: Which feature most strongly suggests delirium rather than primary psychosis?
med-clin-psych.l08.q1.e: Delirium disturbs attention and awareness with fluctuation and often disorientation. The other features describe schizophrenia-spectrum illness.

med-clin-psych.l08.q2.t: Improvement after a benzodiazepine such as lorazepam
med-clin-psych.l08.q2.p: Which first-line test response is characteristic and therapeutic in catatonia?
med-clin-psych.l08.q2.h: GABA-A agonism often relaxes the syndrome.
med-clin-psych.l08.q2.e: A lorazepam challenge often produces rapid improvement in catatonia. Antipsychotics can worsen catatonia and risk neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

med-clin-psych.l08.q3.t: Lumbar puncture with antibody testing and a search for ovarian teratoma
med-clin-psych.l08.q3.p: A 22-year-old woman has two weeks of paranoia and insomnia and then a generalized seizure, orofacial dyskinesias and fluctuating blood pressure. Which workup is most appropriate?
med-clin-psych.l08.q3.h: Psychiatric onset followed by seizures and autonomic signs.
med-clin-psych.l08.q3.e: This course suggests anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, diagnosed by antibodies and associated with ovarian teratoma. Diagnosing schizophrenia would miss a treatable immune cause.

med-clin-psych.l08.q4.p: A 70-year-old man with recent hospitalization is agitated, sees insects on the walls, and is disoriented, with symptoms worse at night. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-psych.l08.q4.h: Visual hallucinations and fluctuating orientation in an older inpatient.
med-clin-psych.l08.q4.e: Acute fluctuation, disorientation, visual hallucinations and nocturnal worsening indicate delirium from a medical cause. Late-onset schizophrenia has clear sensorium.

med-clin-psych.l08.q5.t: Emergency psychiatric evaluation, likely admission, with infant safety considered
med-clin-psych.l08.q5.p: A 28-year-old woman 10 days after delivery is confused, paranoid and talks of the baby being a threat. Which action is appropriate?
med-clin-psych.l08.q5.e: Postpartum psychosis is an emergency with risk of infanticide and suicide and needs urgent evaluation. Blues do not include psychosis and resolve within two weeks.

med-clin-psych.l09.q1.t: An external incentive such as money or avoiding work
med-clin-psych.l09.q1.p: What motivates a person with malingering?
med-clin-psych.l09.q1.e: Malingering is intentional symptom production for external gain. Factitious disorder involves the sick role without an external reward, and conversion is not feigned.

med-clin-psych.l09.q2.p: A man reports sudden blindness after a bitter argument, yet his pupils react normally and he avoids obstacles. He is distressed, has no pending lawsuit or disability claim, and no organic cause is found. Which diagnosis fits?
med-clin-psych.l09.q2.h: Examination findings are inconsistent with neurologic disease.
med-clin-psych.l09.q2.e: A deficit incompatible with neurologic disease, a preceding stressor and no identifiable external incentive point to functional neurological symptom disorder. Normal findings alone cannot separate it from malingering; the absence of an incentive and of deliberate feigning does.

med-clin-psych.l09.q3.t: Regularly scheduled visits with one primary clinician and avoidance of unnecessary testing
med-clin-psych.l09.q3.p: A 34-year-old woman has had six months of fatigue, abdominal pain and headaches with repeated normal workups. She spends hours daily worrying about the symptoms and sees many clinicians. What is the best management approach?
med-clin-psych.l09.q3.e: Somatic symptom disorder benefits from a continuous relationship with one clinician and scheduled visits. Repeated testing reinforces illness behavior, and the symptoms are not feigned.

med-clin-psych.l09.q4.t: Ensure the child's safety and file a protective services report
med-clin-psych.l09.q4.p: A mother repeatedly brings her toddler for unexplained vomiting, which resolves when the child is hospitalized away from her. Which action takes priority?
med-clin-psych.l09.q4.h: Think of abuse and mandated reporting.
med-clin-psych.l09.q4.e: This pattern suggests factitious disorder imposed on another, a form of child abuse that requires protection and reporting. Continuing medical testing prolongs the harm.

med-clin-psych.l09.q5.t: Feeling detached from oneself or the surroundings with intact reality testing
med-clin-psych.l09.q5.p: Which symptom is characteristic of depersonalization/derealization disorder?
med-clin-psych.l09.q5.e: Depersonalization and derealization involve detachment with intact reality testing. Memory loss describes dissociative amnesia and distinct states describe identity disorder.

med-clin-psych.l10.q1.t: Symptoms in at least two settings with clear functional interference
med-clin-psych.l10.q1.p: Which finding is required for an ADHD diagnosis in a school-aged child?
med-clin-psych.l10.q1.e: DSM-5 requires symptoms in two or more settings with impairment. Inattentive presentations do not need hyperactivity, and IQ is not part of criteria.

med-clin-psych.l10.q2.p: Which medication for ADHD is a non-stimulant norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor with a boxed warning for suicidal ideation?
med-clin-psych.l10.q2.e: Atomoxetine inhibits norepinephrine reuptake and carries the boxed warning. Guanfacine is an alpha-2 agonist, and the others are stimulants.

med-clin-psych.l10.q3.t: Early intensive developmental and behavioral intervention with speech therapy
med-clin-psych.l10.q3.p: A 2-year-old has no pointing or joint attention, few words, and repetitively lines up toys, with distress at changes in routine. Hearing is normal. What is the best next step?
med-clin-psych.l10.q3.h: Early intervention is key and no drug treats core features.
med-clin-psych.l10.q3.e: The picture suggests autism spectrum disorder, where early behavioral intervention improves outcomes. Risperidone treats irritability, not social deficits, and vaccines do not cause autism.

med-clin-psych.l10.q4.p: A 7-year-old has multiple motor tics and a vocal tic for 14 months, which impair him socially. Which is the best first-line approach?
med-clin-psych.l10.q4.e: Behavioral therapy is first-line, with alpha-2 agonists or antipsychotics when tics are impairing. Stimulants may worsen tics in some children.

med-clin-psych.l10.q5.p: What is the best-supported initial treatment for a preschooler aged four with ADHD, per the 2019 AAP guideline?
med-clin-psych.l10.q5.h: The youngest children start with behavior approaches.
med-clin-psych.l10.q5.e: For four- to five-year-olds, parent training in behavior management is first, with methylphenidate considered if needed. Antipsychotics are not recommended for ADHD.

med-clin-psych.l11.q1.t: Acute onset with fluctuating attention and awareness
med-clin-psych.l11.q1.p: Which feature distinguishes delirium from dementia?
med-clin-psych.l11.q1.e: Delirium is acute with disturbed attention and fluctuation. Dementia is gradual with preserved consciousness until late.

med-clin-psych.l11.q2.t: Extracellular beta-amyloid plaques and intracellular tau tangles
med-clin-psych.l11.q2.p: Which pathologic finding is characteristic of Alzheimer disease?
med-clin-psych.l11.q2.e: Alzheimer disease shows amyloid plaques and tau tangles. Alpha-synuclein suggests Lewy body disease, and Pick bodies suggest frontotemporal dementia.

med-clin-psych.l11.q3.t: Lewy body dementia, with severe sensitivity to antipsychotic drugs
med-clin-psych.l11.q3.p: A 74-year-old man has fluctuating confusion, well-formed visual hallucinations of children, mild parkinsonism, and acts out dreams. Given a haloperidol dose for agitation, he becomes rigid and unresponsive. What is the diagnosis and the concern?
med-clin-psych.l11.q3.h: Fluctuation, visual hallucinations, parkinsonism and REM sleep behavior disorder.
med-clin-psych.l11.q3.e: This is Lewy body dementia, in which antipsychotics can cause severe rigidity and neuroleptic sensitivity. The other dementias lack this core combination.

med-clin-psych.l11.q4.t: Large-volume lumbar puncture or ventriculoperitoneal shunting
med-clin-psych.l11.q4.p: A 78-year-old woman has gait disturbance with a magnetic quality, urinary urgency and incontinence, and progressive forgetfulness. CT shows ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy. What is the most appropriate intervention?
med-clin-psych.l11.q4.h: This is a potentially reversible dementia.
med-clin-psych.l11.q4.e: The triad indicates normal pressure hydrocephalus, treated with CSF removal or shunt. Anticholinergics could worsen cognition.

med-clin-psych.l11.q5.t: Treat the infection, review medications and apply non-drug orientation measures
med-clin-psych.l11.q5.p: A 69-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia is disoriented, inattentive and pulling at his IV, with symptoms that wax and wane. Which is the best initial management?
med-clin-psych.l11.q5.h: Treat the cause and use environmental support.
med-clin-psych.l11.q5.e: Delirium management targets underlying causes and uses non-drug measures. Restraints and benzodiazepines usually worsen delirium unless it is alcohol withdrawal.

med-clin-psych.l12.q1.p: Which drug is given first to a malnourished patient with alcohol use disorder who is about to receive glucose?
med-clin-psych.l12.q1.e: Thiamine precedes glucose to prevent precipitating Wernicke encephalopathy. The other agents do not address this risk.

med-clin-psych.l12.q2.p: Which medication for opioid use disorder is a partial mu agonist with a ceiling effect on respiratory depression?
med-clin-psych.l12.q2.h: It can precipitate withdrawal if started too early.
med-clin-psych.l12.q2.e: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist with a ceiling effect. Methadone is a full agonist, and naltrexone and naloxone are antagonists.

med-clin-psych.l12.q3.t: Benzodiazepines with thiamine and supportive monitoring
med-clin-psych.l12.q3.p: A man arrives 60 hours after his last drink with confusion, visual hallucinations, fever of 38.8 C, heart rate 128 and diaphoresis. What is the most appropriate treatment?
med-clin-psych.l12.q3.e: Delirium tremens is treated with benzodiazepines plus thiamine. Antipsychotics alone lower the seizure threshold and do not treat the underlying withdrawal.

med-clin-psych.l12.q4.t: Precipitated withdrawal from displacement of the full agonist
med-clin-psych.l12.q4.p: A 32-year-old with opioid use disorder asks to start buprenorphine. He last used heroin four hours ago and shows no withdrawal signs. What is the main risk of starting now?
med-clin-psych.l12.q4.h: Partial agonists have high receptor affinity.
med-clin-psych.l12.q4.e: Buprenorphine displaces full agonists and can precipitate withdrawal when started too early. Respiratory depression is limited by its ceiling effect.

med-clin-psych.l12.q5.p: A 27-year-old is brought in agitated and paranoid, with dilated pupils, heart rate 130, temperature 38.5 C and diaphoresis. His friends say he used a stimulant. What is the best initial pharmacologic treatment of agitation?
med-clin-psych.l12.q5.e: Benzodiazepines control agitation, tachycardia and hypertension in stimulant toxicity. Beta-blockers can cause unopposed alpha stimulation, and naloxone and flumazenil target other drugs.

med-clin-psych.l13.q1.p: Which antidepressant lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in bulimia nervosa?
med-clin-psych.l13.q1.e: Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in eating disorders and seizure disorders. The other agents do not carry that contraindication.

med-clin-psych.l13.q2.t: Avoiding tyramine-rich foods such as aged cheese and cured meats
med-clin-psych.l13.q2.p: Which dietary restriction is essential for a patient who takes phenelzine?
med-clin-psych.l13.q2.e: MAO inhibitors prevent tyramine breakdown, risking hypertensive crisis. The other diets relate to warfarin, CYP3A4 drugs or tetracyclines.

med-clin-psych.l13.q3.t: Stop serotonergic drugs and give supportive care, benzodiazepines and cyproheptadine if needed
med-clin-psych.l13.q3.p: A patient taking sertraline is given tramadol for postoperative pain. Hours later she has agitation, diarrhea, temperature 39.2 C, tremor, hyperreflexia and inducible clonus. Which is the best management?
med-clin-psych.l13.q3.h: Clonus and hyperreflexia with rapid onset after a serotonergic combination.
med-clin-psych.l13.q3.e: This is serotonin syndrome, treated by stopping offending drugs, supportive care, benzodiazepines and cyproheptadine. NMS has slow onset with rigidity and bradyreflexia.

med-clin-psych.l13.q4.t: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion from the SSRI
med-clin-psych.l13.q4.p: A 68-year-old woman begins an SSRI and two weeks later has lethargy, confusion and a seizure, with serum sodium of 120 mEq/L and low serum osmolality. Which mechanism is most likely?
med-clin-psych.l13.q4.h: Older age is a risk factor for this electrolyte effect.
med-clin-psych.l13.q4.e: SSRIs can cause SIADH with hypotonic hyponatremia, especially in older adults. Diabetes insipidus would cause hypernatremia, not hyponatremia.

med-clin-psych.l13.q5.p: A teenager overdoses on amitriptyline and has a wide QRS complex and hypotension. Which treatment is most appropriate?
med-clin-psych.l13.q5.h: Sodium channel blockade is the problem.
med-clin-psych.l13.q5.e: Sodium bicarbonate treats tricyclic-induced sodium channel blockade with QRS widening. Physostigmine and flumazenil can worsen toxicity and seizures, and phenytoin is not helpful.

med-clin-psych.l14.q1.p: Which adverse effect of D2-blocking antipsychotics appears within hours to days and is treated with benztropine?
med-clin-psych.l14.q1.h: Sustained muscle spasm of the neck or eyes.
med-clin-psych.l14.q1.e: Acute dystonia occurs early and responds to anticholinergics. Tardive dyskinesia is delayed, and akathisia responds better to beta-blockers.

med-clin-psych.l14.q2.p: Which of these antipsychotics carries the highest risk of metabolic syndrome?
med-clin-psych.l14.q2.h: It causes marked weight gain and dyslipidemia.
med-clin-psych.l14.q2.e: Olanzapine (like clozapine, which is not offered) carries the greatest metabolic risk. Aripiprazole and ziprasidone are metabolically neutral relative to them.

med-clin-psych.l14.q3.t: Stop the antipsychotic and give cooling, fluids and a benzodiazepine, with dantrolene or bromocriptine if severe
med-clin-psych.l14.q3.p: A man started on haloperidol one week ago has fever of 40 C, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion, labile blood pressure and creatine kinase markedly elevated. What is the best next step?
med-clin-psych.l14.q3.e: NMS requires stopping the dopamine antagonist with supportive care. Hyperreflexia and clonus would suggest serotonin syndrome, which is not the picture.

med-clin-psych.l14.q4.t: Blockade of tuberoinfundibular dopamine, which removes inhibition of prolactin
med-clin-psych.l14.q4.p: A 35-year-old woman on risperidone has amenorrhea and galactorrhea. Which mechanism explains this?
med-clin-psych.l14.q4.e: Dopamine from the tuberoinfundibular pathway tonically inhibits prolactin, so D2 blockade raises it. Nigrostriatal blockade produces movement effects.

med-clin-psych.l14.q5.p: A frail 82-year-old with cirrhosis needs short-term treatment for severe anxiety. Which benzodiazepine is most appropriate because it avoids hepatic oxidation and active metabolites?
med-clin-psych.l14.q5.h: Lorazepam, oxazepam and temazepam are cleared by glucuronidation.
med-clin-psych.l14.q5.e: Lorazepam undergoes glucuronidation and lacks active metabolites, so accumulation is less likely. The others are oxidized and have long-acting active metabolites.

med-clin-psych.l15.q1.p: Which therapy is the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia?
med-clin-psych.l15.q1.e: CBT-I is recommended first-line for chronic insomnia. Hypnotics and antihistamines carry adverse effects and do not maintain benefit.

med-clin-psych.l15.q2.p: A patient says, "I know smoking harms my health and I keep going back and forth about whether to quit, but I have no plan yet." Which stage of change is this?
med-clin-psych.l15.q2.h: Aware of the problem, ambivalent about acting.
med-clin-psych.l15.q2.e: Contemplation is awareness of the problem with ambivalence and no commitment to act yet; denial of any problem would be precontemplation. Preparation involves planning to act soon, and action means behavior change is underway.

med-clin-psych.l15.q3.p: A patient with severe depression, refusal of food and active suicidal intent has not responded to several antidepressants. Which treatment offers the most rapid and robust response?
med-clin-psych.l15.q3.e: ECT is the most effective treatment for severe, treatment-resistant or life-threatening depression. TMS is less potent and slower, and switching drugs takes weeks.

med-clin-psych.l15.q4.p: A therapist feels intense irritation toward a patient who reminds her of a critical parent. Which concept describes this?
med-clin-psych.l15.q4.e: Countertransference is the therapist's emotional response to the patient. Transference is the patient's feelings toward the therapist.

med-clin-psych.l15.q5.t: CBT with cognitive restructuring and behavioral activation
med-clin-psych.l15.q5.p: A woman with depression recounts that every setback proves that she is worthless and has stopped seeing friends. Which approach most directly targets this pattern?
med-clin-psych.l15.q5.e: CBT addresses cognitive distortions and withdrawal through restructuring and activation. Aversion therapy and desensitization do not fit this problem.

med-clin-psych.l16.q1.p: Which single factor is the strongest predictor of eventual suicide?
med-clin-psych.l16.q1.e: A previous attempt is the strongest single predictor. Women attempt more often but men die more often, and being married is protective.

med-clin-psych.l16.q2.p: Which evidence-based tool is a written collaborative list of warning signs, coping steps, contacts and means safety?
med-clin-psych.l16.q2.e: Safety planning is supported by evidence and includes steps for making the environment safe. No-suicide contracts lack evidence and do not replace assessment.

med-clin-psych.l16.q3.t: Emergency evaluation with hospitalization and removal of firearm access
med-clin-psych.l16.q3.p: A 60-year-old man recently discharged from a psychiatric unit is intoxicated and says he intends to use the handgun he keeps at home tonight. Which action is most appropriate?
med-clin-psych.l16.q3.h: Plan, intent, means and a recent discharge.
med-clin-psych.l16.q3.e: A plan, intent and means with an acute precipitant mandate protection and hospitalization. Contracts and reassurance do not reduce acute risk.

med-clin-psych.l16.q4.t: Limiting access to firearms and stockpiled medications
med-clin-psych.l16.q4.p: Which lethal-means strategy has the best evidence for reducing suicides?
med-clin-psych.l16.q4.e: Means restriction reduces deaths because suicidal crises are frequently short. Asking directly does not plant the idea, and large prescriptions add overdose risk.

med-clin-psych.l16.q5.t: It does not increase risk and improves detection and rapport
med-clin-psych.l16.q5.p: A clinician asks directly about suicidal thoughts in a depressed patient. What is the effect of this inquiry?
med-clin-psych.l16.q5.h: Evidence does not support the fear of planting ideas.
med-clin-psych.l16.q5.e: Asking about suicide does not provoke it and helps identify risk. Avoiding the topic leaves patients unassessed.

med-clin-psych.l17.q1.p: Which is not one of the four abilities tested in a standard capacity assessment?
med-clin-psych.l17.q1.h: The decision does not have to match the physician's.
med-clin-psych.l17.q1.e: The abilities are understanding, appreciation, reasoning and expressing a choice. Agreement with the clinician is never required.

med-clin-psych.l17.q2.h: Capacity is clinical, competence is legal.
med-clin-psych.l17.q2.e: Competence is a legal status decided by a court, while capacity is a clinical judgment by treating clinicians.

med-clin-psych.l17.q3.t: Respect her refusal, as she has capacity for this decision
med-clin-psych.l17.q3.p: A 45-year-old woman with schizophrenia declines a recommended appendectomy. She explains that she understands the risks of rupture, believes she could die, and would prefer not to have surgery because of fear of anesthesia. Her thinking is organized. What is the most appropriate response?
med-clin-psych.l17.q3.h: A diagnosis does not equal incapacity.
med-clin-psych.l17.q3.e: She shows understanding, appreciation, reasoning and a stable choice, so her refusal is valid despite her diagnosis. Implied consent applies only when capacity is absent in an emergency.

med-clin-psych.l17.q4.t: Proceed under the emergency exception of implied consent
med-clin-psych.l17.q4.p: A patient with severe delirium needs urgent surgery, has no advance directive, and no relatives can be reached. Delay would risk permanent harm. Which is the best approach?
med-clin-psych.l17.q4.h: The emergency doctrine applies when delay endangers life.
med-clin-psych.l17.q4.e: In an emergency with no surrogate available, treatment proceeds under implied consent. Waiting would risk serious harm.

med-clin-psych.l17.q5.t: Substituted judgment based on what she would have chosen
med-clin-psych.l17.q5.p: A patient lacking capacity once told friends she would never want prolonged ventilation. Her husband is the surrogate. Which standard should he apply?
med-clin-psych.l17.q5.h: The decision should reflect her values.
med-clin-psych.l17.q5.e: Surrogates first apply substituted judgment; best interest is used only when wishes are unknown. His own preferences are not the standard.

med-clin-psych.l18.q1.t: A mental illness with danger to self or others or grave disability
med-clin-psych.l18.q1.p: Which are the common requirements for civil commitment?
med-clin-psych.l18.q1.e: Commitment requires mental illness plus dangerousness or grave disability. Refusal of care or a diagnosis alone is not sufficient, as O'Connor v. Donaldson established.

med-clin-psych.l18.q2.t: A therapist has a duty to take reasonable steps to protect an identifiable victim of a patient's serious violent threat
med-clin-psych.l18.q2.p: What did Tarasoff v. Regents of the University of California (1976) hold?
med-clin-psych.l18.q2.h: California Supreme Court, duty to protect.
med-clin-psych.l18.q2.e: Tarasoff established a duty to use reasonable care to protect a foreseeable victim. It does not require reporting all past crimes or abolish confidentiality.

med-clin-psych.l18.q3.t: A finding of incapacity or a court or administrative hearing
med-clin-psych.l18.q3.p: A patient on an involuntary hold refuses antipsychotic medication and is calm and not dangerous. What is typically required to medicate him over objection outside an emergency?
med-clin-psych.l18.q3.h: Commitment and treatment over objection are separate.
med-clin-psych.l18.q3.e: Involuntary admission does not itself authorize medication over objection, which generally requires incapacity or a hearing. Emergencies are an exception.

med-clin-psych.l18.q4.t: Take reasonable protective steps such as notifying the person and police and arranging evaluation
med-clin-psych.l18.q4.p: A man tells his psychiatrist he will shoot his coworker tomorrow and has bought a gun. Which action best fits the duty to protect?
med-clin-psych.l18.q4.h: A specific threat against an identifiable person.
med-clin-psych.l18.q4.e: A specific serious threat triggers protective steps, including warning and police, and HIPAA allows disclosure to prevent serious imminent harm. Inaction risks liability.

med-clin-psych.l18.q5.p: Which standard of proof did the Supreme Court require for civil commitment in Addington v. Texas (1979)?
med-clin-psych.l18.q5.e: Addington held that clear and convincing evidence is the minimum, higher than preponderance but below beyond a reasonable doubt, since commitment deprives liberty.

med-clin-surgery.l01.q1.p: Which of these is one of the six factors in the Revised Cardiac Risk Index?
med-clin-surgery.l01.q1.h: The index counts cardiac and renal markers, not lung disease.
med-clin-surgery.l01.q1.e: Insulin-treated diabetes is one of the six RCRI factors. Age, smoking and lung disease raise other risks but are not in the index.

med-clin-surgery.l01.q2.t: Stop warfarin about five days before, no routine bridging
med-clin-surgery.l01.q2.p: A man with chronic atrial fibrillation takes warfarin and will have elective hernia repair. He has no mechanical valve and no recent stroke. What is the best plan?
med-clin-surgery.l01.q2.h: The BRIDGE trial addressed bridging in atrial fibrillation.
med-clin-surgery.l01.q2.e: Bridging increased bleeding without reducing thromboembolism in most atrial fibrillation patients. Warfarin is held about five days.

med-clin-surgery.l01.q3.t: History and examination without routine testing
med-clin-surgery.l01.q3.p: Which approach to a healthy 40-year-old before knee arthroscopy has the best evidence?
med-clin-surgery.l01.q3.h: Testing should be driven by findings, not by habit.
med-clin-surgery.l01.q3.e: Routine testing in healthy patients for low-risk surgery does not improve outcomes and leads to false positives.

med-clin-surgery.l01.q4.t: IV hydrocortisone for presumed adrenal insufficiency
med-clin-surgery.l01.q4.p: A 70-year-old woman on prednisone for polymyalgia rheumatica for two years undergoes colectomy. After surgery she is hypotensive despite fluids, with normal hemoglobin and no evidence of sepsis. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l01.q4.h: Chronic steroid use suppresses the adrenal axis.
med-clin-surgery.l01.q4.e: Perioperative stress with a suppressed hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis causes adrenal crisis, treated with stress-dose steroid.

med-clin-surgery.l01.q5.p: A 66-year-old man with diabetes treated with an SGLT2 inhibitor has an elective operation. Two days afterward he is nauseated and tachypneic with a glucose of 180 mg/dL and an anion gap acidosis. Which is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l01.q5.h: Ketosis with a near-normal glucose is the clue.
med-clin-surgery.l01.q5.e: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with modest glucose elevation during fasting and surgical stress, which is why they are held beforehand.

med-clin-surgery.l02.q1.p: Which postoperative day range is classically associated with fever from urinary tract infection?
med-clin-surgery.l02.q1.h: Think about a catheter in place for several days.
med-clin-surgery.l02.q1.e: Water, meaning urinary infection, is classically linked to days 3 to 5, wind to the first 48 hours and wound to days 5 to 7.

med-clin-surgery.l02.q2.t: Immediate surgical debridement with broad antibiotics
med-clin-surgery.l02.q2.p: A patient is febrile 36 hours after laparoscopic cholecystectomy, has severe pain out of proportion at a port site, bullae and spreading erythema with crepitus. What is needed?
med-clin-surgery.l02.q2.h: Early postoperative infection with pain disproportion is dangerous.
med-clin-surgery.l02.q2.e: Necrotizing soft tissue infection needs prompt debridement, since antibiotics alone do not reach necrotic tissue.

med-clin-surgery.l02.q3.p: Which finding is most likely when salmon-colored serosanguinous fluid drains from a laparotomy wound on day 7?
med-clin-surgery.l02.q3.h: Think about a deeper layer that has failed.
med-clin-surgery.l02.q3.e: Copious salmon-colored drainage after laparotomy suggests fascial dehiscence, and an abdominal binder or reoperation may be needed.

med-clin-surgery.l02.q4.t: Percutaneous drainage with antibiotics and close monitoring
med-clin-surgery.l02.q4.p: A 60-year-old man had a sigmoid colectomy with primary anastomosis six days ago and now has fever, tachycardia, worsening abdominal pain, and a rising white count. CT shows a localized fluid collection with air near the anastomosis and he has no peritonitis. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l02.q4.h: A contained leak and a stable patient are managed less invasively.
med-clin-surgery.l02.q4.e: A contained anastomotic leak without peritonitis can often be managed by drainage and antibiotics, while diffuse peritonitis needs reoperation.

med-clin-surgery.l02.q5.p: On postoperative day 4 after pelvic surgery a woman develops pleuritic chest pain, a heart rate of 112 and an oxygen saturation of 90 percent. Her chest radiograph is clear. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l02.q5.h: Hypoxemia with a clear film after pelvic surgery is the clue.
med-clin-surgery.l02.q5.e: Pelvic surgery raises thromboembolism risk, and hypoxemia without radiographic findings suggests pulmonary embolism rather than atelectasis.

med-clin-surgery.l03.q1.p: Which type of shock shows low systemic vascular resistance with bradycardia after cervical spinal cord injury?
med-clin-surgery.l03.q1.h: Loss of sympathetic outflow removes vascular tone.
med-clin-surgery.l03.q1.e: Neurogenic shock produces hypotension with bradycardia and warm skin, unlike hemorrhage with tachycardia.

med-clin-surgery.l03.q2.p: Which intervention given early has been shown to reduce death from bleeding in trauma?
med-clin-surgery.l03.q2.e: Tranexamic acid given within three hours reduced bleeding deaths in CRASH-2.

med-clin-surgery.l03.q3.p: A severely malnourished patient begins parenteral feeding and two days later develops weakness and arrhythmia. Which findings are expected?
med-clin-surgery.l03.q3.h: Insulin surge drives electrolytes into cells.
med-clin-surgery.l03.q3.e: Refeeding syndrome shifts phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells, and is avoided by slow feeding with thiamine.

med-clin-surgery.l03.q4.t: Transfuse balanced products and control the bleeding
med-clin-surgery.l03.q4.p: A trauma patient with a pulse of 130, blood pressure 80/50 mmHg and flat neck veins has received 2 liters of crystalloid with minimal improvement. Which next step best addresses the problem?
med-clin-surgery.l03.q4.e: Hemorrhagic shock is treated with balanced transfusion and source control, since crystalloid dilutes clotting factors and worsens coagulopathy.

med-clin-surgery.l03.q5.p: A 55-year-old man after massive transfusion develops muscle cramps, a prolonged QT interval and hypotension. Which abnormality is likely?
med-clin-surgery.l03.q5.h: Citrate preserves blood by binding something.
med-clin-surgery.l03.q5.e: Citrate in stored blood chelates calcium, which prolongs the QT interval and depresses cardiac function.

med-clin-surgery.l04.q1.p: Which drug is the specific treatment for malignant hyperthermia?
med-clin-surgery.l04.q1.h: It acts on the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
med-clin-surgery.l04.q1.e: Dantrolene blocks calcium release through the ryanodine receptor.

med-clin-surgery.l04.q2.p: Which complication is typical of spinal anesthesia?
med-clin-surgery.l04.q2.h: The sympathetic chain is blocked with the sensory fibers.
med-clin-surgery.l04.q2.e: Spinal anesthesia blocks sympathetic fibers, causing vasodilation, hypotension and sometimes bradycardia.

med-clin-surgery.l04.q3.p: Which hemodynamically favorable induction agent suppresses adrenal steroid synthesis?
med-clin-surgery.l04.q3.h: It is chosen for unstable patients despite this effect.
med-clin-surgery.l04.q3.e: Etomidate preserves blood pressure but inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase, which lowers cortisol production.

med-clin-surgery.l04.q4.t: Stop the triggering agents and administer dantrolene
med-clin-surgery.l04.q4.p: A 16-year-old boy has masseter rigidity after succinylcholine and sevoflurane induction, with end-tidal carbon dioxide rising to 80 mmHg, a heart rate of 150 and a temperature of 39.5 C. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l04.q4.h: This is a pharmacogenetic crisis triggered by anesthesia.
med-clin-surgery.l04.q4.e: Malignant hyperthermia requires stopping triggers and giving dantrolene, along with hyperventilation and cooling.

med-clin-surgery.l04.q5.t: Bupivacaine toxicity treated with intravenous lipid emulsion
med-clin-surgery.l04.q5.p: During a nerve block a patient develops perioral numbness and tinnitus, then a seizure and ventricular arrhythmia. Which local anesthetic and treatment are likely involved?
med-clin-surgery.l04.q5.h: This is the most cardiotoxic common amide agent.
med-clin-surgery.l04.q5.e: Systemic toxicity from bupivacaine causes neurologic then cardiac effects and responds to lipid emulsion.

med-clin-surgery.l05.q1.t: Guarding with rebound tenderness and pain on movement
med-clin-surgery.l05.q1.p: Which sign is expected with irritation of the peritoneum?
med-clin-surgery.l05.q1.h: Parietal pain is sharp and localized.
med-clin-surgery.l05.q1.e: Peritonitis produces rigidity, guarding and rebound, and patients lie still. Visceral pain is dull and poorly localized.

med-clin-surgery.l05.q2.t: Transvaginal ultrasound to evaluate for ectopic pregnancy
med-clin-surgery.l05.q2.p: A 24-year-old woman has right lower quadrant pain, a missed period and a positive urine hCG. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l05.q2.h: A pregnancy test changes the whole differential.
med-clin-surgery.l05.q2.e: Ectopic pregnancy is a surgical emergency in a woman with pain and a positive test, and ultrasound is the first test.

med-clin-surgery.l05.q3.t: Ultrasound first, with MRI if it is nondiagnostic
med-clin-surgery.l05.q3.p: Which imaging approach is preferred for suspected appendicitis in a pregnant woman?
med-clin-surgery.l05.q3.e: Ultrasound and MRI avoid ionizing radiation, and are favored in pregnancy and children.

med-clin-surgery.l05.q4.p: A 19-year-old man has 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right lower quadrant, anorexia, a temperature of 38.2 C and a white count of 14,500 with tenderness and guarding at McBurney point. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l05.q4.h: Classic presentation with peritoneal signs needs no further workup.
med-clin-surgery.l05.q4.e: The presentation is classic enough for appendectomy, and imaging is optional in a typical young male. Delay risks perforation.

med-clin-surgery.l05.q5.t: Acute mesenteric ischemia from an arterial embolus
med-clin-surgery.l05.q5.p: A 75-year-old man with atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation has severe diffuse abdominal pain with a soft nontender abdomen, a lactate of 4.8 and a leukocyte count of 18,000. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l05.q5.h: Pain out of proportion is the clue.
med-clin-surgery.l05.q5.e: Atrial fibrillation without anticoagulation predisposes to emboli, and pain out of proportion to examination is classic for mesenteric ischemia.

med-clin-surgery.l06.q1.p: Which is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction in an adult with prior abdominal surgery?
med-clin-surgery.l06.q1.h: Think of scars inside the abdomen.
med-clin-surgery.l06.q1.e: Postoperative adhesions are the most common cause in the Western world, with hernias next.

med-clin-surgery.l06.q2.t: A coffee-bean shaped dilated loop rising from the pelvis
med-clin-surgery.l06.q2.p: Which radiographic sign is typical of sigmoid volvulus?
med-clin-surgery.l06.q2.h: The loop is shaped like a bean.
med-clin-surgery.l06.q2.e: A massively dilated sigmoid loop forms a coffee-bean sign, and the first treatment is endoscopic decompression.

med-clin-surgery.l06.q3.t: Peritonitis, acidosis or CT signs of strangulation
med-clin-surgery.l06.q3.p: Which finding in an adult with small bowel obstruction should prompt urgent operation rather than a trial of nonoperative care?
med-clin-surgery.l06.q3.e: Signs of strangulation or peritonitis demand surgery, while partial obstruction can be observed.

med-clin-surgery.l06.q4.t: Endoscopic detorsion, then sigmoid resection this admission
med-clin-surgery.l06.q4.p: A 78-year-old nursing home resident with chronic constipation has two days of abdominal distension and obstipation. The abdominal film shows a markedly dilated loop in a coffee-bean pattern and there is no peritonitis. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l06.q4.e: Stable sigmoid volvulus is decompressed endoscopically, and resection is advised during the same admission because recurrence is high.

med-clin-surgery.l06.q5.p: A 62-year-old man with severe atherosclerosis has postprandial abdominal pain, food avoidance and 15 kg weight loss over several months. Which diagnosis fits?
med-clin-surgery.l06.q5.h: Pain follows meals because demand outstrips flow.
med-clin-surgery.l06.q5.e: Chronic mesenteric ischemia causes food fear and weight loss, diagnosed by CT angiography and treated with revascularization.

med-clin-surgery.l07.q1.t: Medial to them through Hesselbach triangle
med-clin-surgery.l07.q1.p: Where does a direct inguinal hernia protrude relative to the inferior epigastric vessels?
med-clin-surgery.l07.q1.e: Direct hernias pass through the floor medial to the inferior epigastric vessels, and indirect hernias go lateral through the deep ring.

med-clin-surgery.l07.q2.t: Femoral hernia, which is repaired urgently
med-clin-surgery.l07.q2.p: A 70-year-old woman has a firm tender bulge below the inguinal ligament with vomiting. Which hernia is most likely and how is it managed?
med-clin-surgery.l07.q2.h: A narrow neck makes strangulation likely.
med-clin-surgery.l07.q2.e: Femoral hernias lie below the inguinal ligament, are common in women and strangulate often, so repair is prompt.

med-clin-surgery.l07.q3.t: Only part of the bowel wall is trapped in the defect
med-clin-surgery.l07.q3.e: In a Richter hernia only a portion of the circumference is trapped, so strangulation can occur without obstruction.

med-clin-surgery.l07.q4.t: Urgent surgical exploration with bowel assessment
med-clin-surgery.l07.q4.p: A 55-year-old man has a painful groin bulge for 12 hours, vomiting, and now erythema over the lump with fever and a white count of 16,000. It cannot be reduced. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l07.q4.e: A tender irreducible hernia with systemic signs is strangulated, which requires emergency surgery to prevent bowel gangrene.

med-clin-surgery.l07.q5.t: Prompt repair because infants often incarcerate
med-clin-surgery.l07.q5.p: A 3-month-old boy has an intermittent right groin bulge that is soft and reducible. What is the best management?
med-clin-surgery.l07.q5.h: Pediatric inguinal hernias do not resolve on their own.
med-clin-surgery.l07.q5.e: Indirect inguinal hernias in infants are repaired soon after diagnosis because of the incarceration risk, unlike umbilical hernias.

med-clin-surgery.l08.q1.p: Which procedure is commonly used for perforated diverticulitis with fecal peritonitis?
med-clin-surgery.l08.q1.e: Sigmoid resection with an end colostomy is traditional in unstable patients with generalized peritonitis.

med-clin-surgery.l08.q2.p: A patient with diverticulitis has a 6 cm pericolic abscess on CT and is hemodynamically stable. What is the best approach?
med-clin-surgery.l08.q2.e: Abscesses over about 3 to 4 cm are drained percutaneously to avoid emergency surgery, and colonoscopy is delayed because of perforation risk.

med-clin-surgery.l08.q3.p: Which treatment sequence is standard for locally advanced rectal cancer?
med-clin-surgery.l08.q3.h: Treatment is given before surgery to shrink and downstage.
med-clin-surgery.l08.q3.e: Neoadjuvant chemoradiation reduces local recurrence in locally advanced rectal cancer, and is followed by total mesorectal excision.

med-clin-surgery.l08.q4.p: A 68-year-old man with iron deficiency anemia, fatigue and occult blood positive stool has a mass in the cecum on colonoscopy. Biopsy shows adenocarcinoma, and CT shows no metastases. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l08.q4.h: Resectable colon cancer is treated surgically.
med-clin-surgery.l08.q4.e: Nonmetastatic right-sided colon cancer is treated with segmental resection and lymph node dissection, and node-positive disease gets adjuvant chemotherapy.

med-clin-surgery.l08.q5.p: A 45-year-old woman has recurrent duodenal and jejunal ulcers despite proton pump inhibitors, with diarrhea. What should be measured?
med-clin-surgery.l08.q5.h: Multiple distal ulcers suggest acid hypersecretion.
med-clin-surgery.l08.q5.e: Refractory, multiple or distal ulcers should prompt a gastrin level to evaluate for Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

med-clin-surgery.l09.q1.t: Fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain
med-clin-surgery.l09.q1.p: Which triad defines acute cholangitis (the Charcot triad)?
med-clin-surgery.l09.q1.h: The pentad adds shock and confusion.
med-clin-surgery.l09.q1.e: Charcot triad is fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain, and Reynolds pentad adds hypotension and confusion.

med-clin-surgery.l09.q2.p: A woman has 90 minutes of postprandial right upper quadrant pain that resolved, with normal labs and an ultrasound showing gallstones without wall thickening. What is the best management?
med-clin-surgery.l09.q2.h: This is symptomatic cholelithiasis with biliary colic.
med-clin-surgery.l09.q2.e: Symptomatic stones are treated with elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy because colic recurs and complications can follow.

med-clin-surgery.l09.q3.t: Obtaining the critical view of safety
med-clin-surgery.l09.q3.p: Which technique helps prevent common bile duct injury during cholecystectomy?
med-clin-surgery.l09.q3.e: The critical view of safety demonstrates that only the cystic duct and artery enter the gallbladder before they are divided.

med-clin-surgery.l09.q4.t: Resuscitation, antibiotics and urgent biliary decompression
med-clin-surgery.l09.q4.p: A 72-year-old woman has fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, a blood pressure of 82/50 mmHg and confusion. Ultrasound shows a dilated common bile duct with stones. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l09.q4.h: Severe cholangitis cannot wait for stones to pass.
med-clin-surgery.l09.q4.e: Suppurative cholangitis with shock requires antibiotics and urgent drainage, usually by endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography.

med-clin-surgery.l09.q5.p: A 68-year-old woman has small bowel obstruction, and abdominal imaging shows air in the biliary tree and an ectopic gallstone in the distal ileum. What is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l09.q5.h: A stone erodes into the bowel and obstructs it.
med-clin-surgery.l09.q5.e: Gallstone ileus results from a cholecystoenteric fistula, so pneumobilia plus a stone in the ileum causes obstruction.

med-clin-surgery.l10.q1.t: Malignant obstruction of the distal bile duct
med-clin-surgery.l10.q1.p: What does the Courvoisier sign suggest?
med-clin-surgery.l10.q1.h: A distended gallbladder that is not tender.
med-clin-surgery.l10.q1.e: A painless palpable gallbladder with jaundice suggests malignant distal biliary obstruction, as in pancreatic head cancer.

med-clin-surgery.l10.q2.p: Which operation is used for a resectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma?
med-clin-surgery.l10.q2.h: The head, duodenum and distal bile duct are removed together.
med-clin-surgery.l10.q2.e: Pancreaticoduodenectomy treats head tumors, whereas distal pancreatectomy is for body and tail tumors.

med-clin-surgery.l10.q3.t: Antibiotics with a step-up drainage approach
med-clin-surgery.l10.q3.p: What is the preferred approach for infected pancreatic necrosis in a stable patient?
med-clin-surgery.l10.q3.h: The PANTER trial compared the options.
med-clin-surgery.l10.q3.e: A step-up approach beginning with percutaneous or endoscopic drainage lowered major complications compared with primary open necrosectomy.

med-clin-surgery.l10.q4.p: A 28-year-old woman taking oral contraceptives has sudden right upper quadrant pain and hypotension. CT shows a 9 cm liver mass with intratumoral hemorrhage and free fluid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l10.q4.h: A hormone-related benign tumor can bleed.
med-clin-surgery.l10.q4.e: Hepatic adenomas are associated with oral contraceptives and can rupture, which is why large ones are resected and hormones stopped.

med-clin-surgery.l10.q5.p: A hemodynamically stable man with blunt trauma has a grade III liver laceration on CT without active contrast extravasation. What is the best management?
med-clin-surgery.l10.q5.h: Stability changes the approach to solid organ injury.
med-clin-surgery.l10.q5.e: Stable patients with blunt liver injury are managed without surgery, with angioembolization if bleeding is seen.

med-clin-surgery.l11.q1.p: At what diameter is elective repair of an asymptomatic infrarenal aortic aneurysm typically considered in men?
med-clin-surgery.l11.q1.h: Monitoring continues until a defined threshold.
med-clin-surgery.l11.q1.e: Elective repair is generally recommended at 5.5 cm in men, or with rapid growth or symptoms.

med-clin-surgery.l11.q2.t: Men aged 65 to 75 who have ever smoked
med-clin-surgery.l11.q2.p: Who should receive one-time ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm according to the USPSTF (2019)?
med-clin-surgery.l11.q2.h: The group is defined by sex, age and smoking.
med-clin-surgery.l11.q2.e: The USPSTF recommends one-time screening in men aged 65 to 75 who have ever smoked.

med-clin-surgery.l11.q3.t: Carotid endarterectomy within about two weeks
med-clin-surgery.l11.q3.p: A man had a transient episode of left arm weakness two days ago, and carotid duplex shows 80 percent stenosis of the right internal carotid artery. Which is the best next step?
med-clin-surgery.l11.q3.h: Symptom side matters. Think about the brain hemisphere involved.
med-clin-surgery.l11.q3.e: Left arm weakness localizes to the right hemisphere, matching a symptomatic 70 to 99 percent stenosis, which benefits from early endarterectomy.

med-clin-surgery.l11.q4.t: Immediate transfer to the operating room for repair
med-clin-surgery.l11.q4.p: A 67-year-old smoker has a sudden severe low back pain, a blood pressure of 78/40 mmHg, and a pulsatile abdominal mass. He remains hypotensive despite initial resuscitation, and an operating room is immediately available. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l11.q4.h: An unstable patient with a known pattern should not travel to a scanner.
med-clin-surgery.l11.q4.e: Hypotension, back pain and a pulsatile mass indicate ruptured aneurysm, requiring operative control without delay.

med-clin-surgery.l11.q5.p: A 58-year-old diabetic man with chronic kidney disease has foot ulcers and rest pain. His ankle-brachial index is 1.4 with a very faint dorsalis pedis pulse. What is the best explanation?
med-clin-surgery.l11.q5.e: A falsely high ABI occurs with incompressible calcified vessels, and a toe-brachial index gives a more accurate result.

med-clin-surgery.l12.q1.p: Which finding is among the six Ps of acute limb ischemia?
med-clin-surgery.l12.q1.h: The limb takes the temperature of the room.
med-clin-surgery.l12.q1.e: Poikilothermia, or coldness, is one of the six Ps, along with pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia and paralysis.

med-clin-surgery.l12.q2.p: What is the first drug to give for acute limb ischemia from an embolus?
med-clin-surgery.l12.q2.h: Stop propagation of the clot immediately.
med-clin-surgery.l12.q2.e: Immediate heparin prevents clot extension while revascularization is arranged.

med-clin-surgery.l12.q3.t: Pain out of proportion, worse on passive stretch
med-clin-surgery.l12.q3.p: Which finding is the earliest and most reliable in compartment syndrome?
med-clin-surgery.l12.q3.e: Pain on passive stretch with a tense compartment is early, and pulses are usually preserved until late.

med-clin-surgery.l12.q4.p: A 70-year-old man with atrial fibrillation has an acutely cold, pale, painful left leg for 4 hours, with decreased sensation, mild weakness and no Doppler arterial signal. His right leg pulses are normal. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l12.q4.h: An immediately threatened limb has hours.
med-clin-surgery.l12.q4.e: Sensory and motor loss with no Doppler signal marks a threatened limb, needing heparin and prompt embolectomy.

med-clin-surgery.l12.q5.t: Aggressive fluids and treatment of hyperkalemia
med-clin-surgery.l12.q5.p: After fasciotomy for compartment syndrome following a crush injury, a patient has dark urine that is dipstick positive for blood with almost no red cells, and a potassium of 6.2. What is the next step?
med-clin-surgery.l12.q5.h: Myoglobin is toxic to the tubules.
med-clin-surgery.l12.q5.e: Rhabdomyolysis is treated with brisk fluid resuscitation to protect the kidney, and hyperkalemia is treated at the same time.

med-clin-surgery.l13.q1.p: In the ATLS 11th edition xABCDE primary survey, what is the order of the steps that follow the x step for exsanguinating external bleeding?
med-clin-surgery.l13.q1.e: The ABCDE sequence is airway with cervical spine protection, breathing, circulation, disability and exposure.

med-clin-surgery.l13.q2.t: Needle or finger decompression of the right chest
med-clin-surgery.l13.q2.p: A man with a stab wound to the chest has severe dyspnea, hypotension, distended neck veins and absent breath sounds on the right. What is the immediate step?
med-clin-surgery.l13.q2.h: This diagnosis is clinical and should not be delayed.
med-clin-surgery.l13.q2.e: Tension pneumothorax needs immediate decompression, followed by a chest tube, with no time for radiography.

med-clin-surgery.l13.q3.t: A dressing that lets air out but not in, then a chest tube
med-clin-surgery.l13.q3.p: What is the correct initial management of an open pneumothorax?
med-clin-surgery.l13.q3.h: The dressing must work like a one-way valve.
med-clin-surgery.l13.q3.e: A flutter-valve dressing, classically taped on three sides, or a vented chest seal lets air escape and prevents tension, and a chest tube is placed through intact skin.

med-clin-surgery.l13.q4.t: Emergency surgical exploration and repair in the operating room
med-clin-surgery.l13.q4.p: A 30-year-old man is stabbed in the left chest and has hypotension, muffled heart sounds and distended neck veins. Breath sounds are equal and a FAST scan shows pericardial fluid. What is the best treatment?
med-clin-surgery.l13.q4.e: Penetrating cardiac tamponade requires surgical decompression and repair, and pericardiocentesis is a temporizing step only.

med-clin-surgery.l13.q5.t: CT angiography of the chest with beta-blockade
med-clin-surgery.l13.q5.p: A restrained driver has chest pain after a car crash. Chest radiography shows a widened mediastinum with loss of the aortic knob and a left apical cap. Hemodynamics are stable. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l13.q5.h: Blunt aortic injury needs confirmation and heart rate control.
med-clin-surgery.l13.q5.e: A widened mediastinum suggests blunt aortic injury, confirmed by CT angiography while controlling blood pressure and heart rate.

med-clin-surgery.l14.q1.p: In ATLS classification, which class of hemorrhage involves 30 to 40 percent blood volume loss with hypotension?
med-clin-surgery.l14.q1.h: Hypotension appears after the second class.
med-clin-surgery.l14.q1.e: Class III is 30 to 40 percent loss and typically adds hypotension and confusion.

med-clin-surgery.l14.q2.t: Early balanced blood products and tranexamic acid
med-clin-surgery.l14.q2.p: Which approach to resuscitation is recommended in hemorrhagic shock?
med-clin-surgery.l14.q2.e: Early transfusion of balanced products and tranexamic acid reduces mortality, and crystalloid dilutes clotting factors.

med-clin-surgery.l14.q3.t: Retrograde urethrogram before inserting a catheter
med-clin-surgery.l14.q3.p: What is the correct management of blood at the urethral meatus after pelvic trauma?
med-clin-surgery.l14.q3.h: Blind catheterization can worsen a urethral tear.
med-clin-surgery.l14.q3.e: Suspected urethral injury needs a retrograde urethrogram first because blind catheterization can convert a partial tear to a complete one.

med-clin-surgery.l14.q4.p: A 25-year-old man is thrown from a motorcycle. His blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg with a pulse of 130 after 2 liters of crystalloid, his abdomen is distended and the FAST scan is positive in the left upper quadrant. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l14.q4.h: An unstable patient with a positive FAST should not go to the scanner.
med-clin-surgery.l14.q4.e: Hemodynamic instability with a positive FAST after blunt trauma calls for laparotomy without further imaging.

med-clin-surgery.l14.q5.t: No routine post-splenectomy vaccine series is required
med-clin-surgery.l14.q5.p: A stable 20-year-old has a splenic laceration treated by angioembolization, and the spleen was not removed. Which approach does the 2022 EAST practice management guideline support?
med-clin-surgery.l14.q5.h: The question is whether embolization costs the spleen its immune function.
med-clin-surgery.l14.q5.e: EAST 2022 found splenic immune function in embolized patients similar to controls, and conditionally recommends against routine post-splenectomy vaccines after embolization. Vaccines remain indicated after splenectomy.

med-clin-surgery.l15.q1.p: Which hematoma is lens-shaped and does not cross suture lines?
med-clin-surgery.l15.q1.h: Think of the artery that is torn.
med-clin-surgery.l15.q1.e: Epidural hematomas from middle meningeal artery injury are biconvex, and they are limited by suture lines.

med-clin-surgery.l15.q2.p: What is Cushing triad, a sign of raised intracranial pressure?
med-clin-surgery.l15.q2.h: The body raises pressure to preserve brain perfusion.
med-clin-surgery.l15.q2.e: Hypertension, bradycardia and irregular respiration signal impending herniation.

med-clin-surgery.l15.q3.t: Epidural hematoma with a lucid interval
med-clin-surgery.l15.q3.p: A man falls and strikes his temple, loses consciousness briefly, wakes and is lucid, then deteriorates over several hours. What is the likely lesion?
med-clin-surgery.l15.q3.h: A temporal bone fracture can tear an artery.
med-clin-surgery.l15.q3.e: A lucid interval after temporal trauma is the classic presentation of an epidural hematoma.

med-clin-surgery.l15.q4.p: A 70-year-old man falls and has weakness more marked in the arms than the legs with burning dysesthesias in the hands. Cervical imaging shows spondylosis without fracture. What is the likely syndrome?
med-clin-surgery.l15.q4.e: Central cord syndrome affects the arms more than the legs, typically in older adults with hyperextension injuries.

med-clin-surgery.l15.q5.t: IV antibiotics, tetanus prophylaxis and debridement
med-clin-surgery.l15.q5.p: A 24-year-old man with an open tibial fracture from a motorcycle crash has a wound of 5 cm with moderate contamination. Which measures are part of initial care?
med-clin-surgery.l15.q5.h: Early antibiotics lower infection in open fractures.
med-clin-surgery.l15.q5.e: Open fractures need early antibiotics, tetanus prophylaxis, debridement and stabilization to reduce infection and nonunion.

med-clin-surgery.l16.q1.p: Which burn depth is dry, leathery and painless?
med-clin-surgery.l16.q1.e: Full-thickness burns destroy the dermis including nerve endings, so they are insensate.

med-clin-surgery.l16.q2.t: Lactated Ringer volume in the first 24 hours
med-clin-surgery.l16.q2.p: What does the Parkland formula estimate?
med-clin-surgery.l16.q2.h: It is based on weight and TBSA.
med-clin-surgery.l16.q2.e: The Parkland formula (4 mL per kilogram per percent TBSA) estimates crystalloid for the first 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours from injury. Current American Burn Association guidance starts lower, at 2 mL per kilogram per percent TBSA, and titrates to urine output.

med-clin-surgery.l16.q3.t: Carbon monoxide poisoning, treated with 100 percent oxygen
med-clin-surgery.l16.q3.p: A person rescued from a house fire has headache and confusion, and pulse oximetry reads 99 percent. What is the best explanation and treatment?
med-clin-surgery.l16.q3.h: Standard oximetry cannot tell the two hemoglobins apart.
med-clin-surgery.l16.q3.e: Carboxyhemoglobin reads as oxyhemoglobin, so oximetry is falsely normal, and 100 percent oxygen shortens the half-life.

med-clin-surgery.l16.q4.t: Early endotracheal intubation to secure the airway
med-clin-surgery.l16.q4.p: A 35-year-old man trapped in a fire has facial burns, singed nasal hairs and carbonaceous sputum. His hoarseness is worsening and he now has stridor, although his oxygen saturation is normal. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l16.q4.h: Airway edema can progress in hours.
med-clin-surgery.l16.q4.e: Signs of inhalation injury with hoarseness predict airway swelling, so early intubation is safer than waiting.

med-clin-surgery.l16.q5.t: Increase the fluid rate and titrate to urine output
med-clin-surgery.l16.q5.p: A 70 kg man has 40 percent TBSA partial and full-thickness burns, and an hour after arrival his urine output is 15 mL per hour while on lactated Ringer at the calculated rate. Which is the best next step?
med-clin-surgery.l16.q5.h: Urine output is the guide to resuscitation.
med-clin-surgery.l16.q5.e: Low urine output means under-resuscitation, so the rate is raised and then titrated, avoiding both under and over-resuscitation.

med-clin-surgery.l17.q1.p: Which imaging is first for a palpable breast mass in a 24-year-old woman?
med-clin-surgery.l17.q1.h: Dense tissue makes mammography less useful.
med-clin-surgery.l17.q1.e: Ultrasound is the first test under age 30, and mammography is added for older women.

med-clin-surgery.l17.q2.p: Which adjuvant therapy suits a postmenopausal woman with an estrogen receptor positive early breast cancer?
med-clin-surgery.l17.q2.h: Postmenopausal estrogen comes from peripheral conversion.
med-clin-surgery.l17.q2.e: Aromatase inhibitors block peripheral estrogen synthesis in postmenopausal women, whereas tamoxifen is used before menopause.

med-clin-surgery.l17.q3.p: A woman has a red, swollen, warm breast with skin dimpling like orange peel, for three weeks, without fever or response to antibiotics. What is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l17.q3.e: Inflammatory breast cancer presents with erythema and peau d orange, and it does not respond to antibiotics.

med-clin-surgery.l17.q4.t: Lumpectomy with radiation and sentinel node biopsy
med-clin-surgery.l17.q4.p: A 45-year-old woman has a 1.5 cm invasive ductal carcinoma, estrogen receptor positive and HER2 negative, in a normal-sized breast with no palpable nodes. What is the best surgical approach?
med-clin-surgery.l17.q4.h: Equal survival is achieved with breast conservation.
med-clin-surgery.l17.q4.e: Breast-conserving surgery with radiation has equal survival to mastectomy for early cancer, and sentinel biopsy stages the axilla.

med-clin-surgery.l17.q5.p: A 55-year-old woman has a unilateral bloody discharge from a single duct, and no mass. Imaging is unremarkable. What is the most likely lesion?
med-clin-surgery.l17.q5.h: Single duct and bloody point to a papillary lesion.
med-clin-surgery.l17.q5.e: Intraductal papilloma is the commonest cause of spontaneous bloody single-duct discharge, though cancer must be excluded.

med-clin-surgery.l18.q1.e: Medullary carcinoma arises from C cells and secretes calcitonin, and it is linked to RET mutations.

med-clin-surgery.l18.q2.p: Which histologic finding in the resected specimen distinguishes follicular carcinoma from an adenoma?
med-clin-surgery.l18.q2.e: Follicular carcinoma is diagnosed by invasion in the resected specimen, not by aspiration cytology.

med-clin-surgery.l18.q3.p: A man develops numbness around the mouth and carpopedal spasm 36 hours after total thyroidectomy. What is the treatment?
med-clin-surgery.l18.q3.h: Think about the glands behind the thyroid.
med-clin-surgery.l18.q3.e: Hypocalcemia from parathyroid injury causes perioral numbness and tetany, and calcium is given.

med-clin-surgery.l18.q4.p: A 52-year-old woman has a serum calcium of 11.6 mg/dL, a raised parathyroid hormone, a kidney stone last year and low bone density. What is the best treatment?
med-clin-surgery.l18.q4.h: She has surgical criteria beyond calcium alone.
med-clin-surgery.l18.q4.e: Primary hyperparathyroidism with osteoporosis and nephrolithiasis meets criteria for parathyroidectomy.

med-clin-surgery.l18.q5.p: A patient with a thyroid nodule has a family history of a thyroid cancer and pheochromocytoma in a sibling, and a markedly high calcitonin. What must be done before thyroid surgery?
med-clin-surgery.l18.q5.h: This is MEN2, and anesthetic crises are possible.
med-clin-surgery.l18.q5.e: In MEN2 an unrecognized pheochromocytoma can cause a hypertensive crisis during surgery, so it is excluded first.

med-clin-surgery.l19.q1.p: What is the time-sensitive treatment for testicular torsion?
med-clin-surgery.l19.q1.e: Torsion needs prompt exploration, ideally within 6 hours, with fixation of both testes.

med-clin-surgery.l19.q2.p: Which stone type is radiolucent on plain radiographs?
med-clin-surgery.l19.q2.e: Uric acid stones are radiolucent, though CT shows them. The others are radiopaque.

med-clin-surgery.l19.q3.p: A 24-year-old man has a painless testicular mass. What is the correct procedure for diagnosis and treatment?
med-clin-surgery.l19.q3.e: Inguinal orchiectomy is both diagnostic and therapeutic, and scrotal violation alters lymphatic spread.

med-clin-surgery.l19.q4.t: Antibiotics and urgent stent or nephrostomy
med-clin-surgery.l19.q4.p: A 45-year-old man with an obstructing ureteral stone has a temperature of 39.2 C, a heart rate of 120 and a blood pressure of 90/55 mmHg. Urinalysis shows pyuria. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l19.q4.h: Infected obstructed system is a surgical emergency.
med-clin-surgery.l19.q4.e: An infected obstructed kidney needs urgent drainage because antibiotics cannot sterilize a blocked system.

med-clin-surgery.l19.q5.p: A 13-year-old obese boy has a limp and knee pain, and his hip has limited internal rotation. What is the likely diagnosis?
med-clin-surgery.l19.q5.h: Knee pain may be referred from the hip.
med-clin-surgery.l19.q5.e: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis occurs in obese adolescents, and treatment is surgical pinning.

med-clin-surgery.l20.q1.p: Which collagen type predominates in early granulation tissue?
med-clin-surgery.l20.q1.h: It is later replaced during remodeling.
med-clin-surgery.l20.q1.e: Type III collagen is laid down first and is replaced by type I during remodeling.

med-clin-surgery.l20.q2.p: According to the ASHP, IDSA, SIS and SHEA 2013 guideline, when should a cefazolin prophylactic dose be started?
med-clin-surgery.l20.q2.h: Tissue levels must be present at incision.
med-clin-surgery.l20.q2.e: The ASHP-led 2013 guideline advises starting within 60 minutes before incision and stopping within 24 hours. The WHO allows up to 120 minutes, and the CDC asks only for a bactericidal level at incision.

med-clin-surgery.l20.q3.t: It extends beyond the original wound margins
med-clin-surgery.l20.q3.p: How does a keloid differ from a hypertrophic scar?
med-clin-surgery.l20.q3.e: Keloids overgrow the wound margins and recur after simple excision, unlike hypertrophic scars.

med-clin-surgery.l20.q4.p: A diabetic man has a day of perineal pain, fever and hypotension. His scrotum is red and swollen with crepitus, and a white count is 24,000. What is the next best step?
med-clin-surgery.l20.q4.h: Fournier gangrene is a surgical emergency.
med-clin-surgery.l20.q4.e: Necrotizing perineal infection needs immediate debridement and broad antibiotics, and imaging must not delay it.

med-clin-surgery.l20.q5.p: A 35-year-old man has a farm wound, and 36 hours later has severe pain, bronze skin discoloration, gas in tissue and gram-positive rods on smear. Which is the likely cause?
med-clin-surgery.l20.q5.h: Gas, rapid course and toxin point to a spore-forming anaerobe.
med-clin-surgery.l20.q5.e: Clostridial myonecrosis produces gas and alpha toxin, and treatment is debridement and penicillin with clindamycin.

med-epi-biostats.l01.q1.t: The share of a defined population that has the condition at a given time, including long-standing cases
med-epi-biostats.l01.q1.p: Which description best fits prevalence, as opposed to incidence?
med-epi-biostats.l01.q1.h: One measure includes old cases; the other counts only new ones.
med-epi-biostats.l01.q1.e: Prevalence counts all existing cases at a point or period, regardless of when they began. The second option is the incidence rate and the third is cumulative incidence; the last is the standardized mortality ratio.

med-epi-biostats.l01.q2.t: One percent of the starting group developed it
med-epi-biostats.l01.q2.p: A cohort of 5,000 disease-free adults is followed for exactly one year and 50 develop the condition. What is the one-year cumulative incidence?
med-epi-biostats.l01.q2.h: Divide new cases by the number at risk at the start.
med-epi-biostats.l01.q2.e: 50 / 5,000 = 0.01, or 1%. Five percent would result from dividing by 1,000, and the other values arise from misplacing the decimal.

med-epi-biostats.l01.q3.t: Incidence is unchanged and prevalence rises because patients remain in the population longer
med-epi-biostats.l01.q3.p: A new therapy for a chronic disease prolongs survival without curing patients and does not change how many people get the disease. What happens to its incidence and prevalence?
med-epi-biostats.l01.q3.h: Prevalence is roughly incidence multiplied by duration.
med-epi-biostats.l01.q3.e: Longer duration with unchanged incidence raises prevalence. The therapy does not affect the rate of new cases, so incidence cannot fall or rise from it.

med-epi-biostats.l01.q4.t: Apply age-specific rates to a common standard population and compare the age-adjusted rates
med-epi-biostats.l01.q4.p: Town A has a crude mortality rate of 14 per 1,000 and Town B has 9 per 1,000. Town A has a much older population, and age-specific death rates in the two towns are nearly identical in every age band. What is the best way to compare the two towns?
med-epi-biostats.l01.q4.h: The towns differ in age structure, not in age-specific risk.
med-epi-biostats.l01.q4.e: Standardization removes the effect of different age structures, and here would show nearly equal adjusted rates. The crude comparison is confounded by age, and a chi-square test on crude rates would not fix that.

med-epi-biostats.l01.q5.t: The incidence rate is about 5 per 1,000 person-years, using about 6,000 person-years in the denominator
med-epi-biostats.l01.q5.p: In a cohort of 2,000 adults followed for a mean of 3 years, 30 develop atrial fibrillation. Followed individuals stopped contributing time when they became cases or were lost. Which statement is most appropriate?
med-epi-biostats.l01.q5.h: Multiply the number of people by the mean follow-up to get person-time.
med-epi-biostats.l01.q5.e: 2,000 x 3 = 6,000 person-years, and 30 / 6,000 = 5 per 1,000 person-years. Dividing by persons gives a proportion over the whole period, not a rate, and new cases are incidence, not prevalence.

med-epi-biostats.l02.q1.t: Exposure and outcome are measured together, so temporal sequence is often unclear
med-epi-biostats.l02.q1.p: What is the central limitation of a cross-sectional study for causal inference?
med-epi-biostats.l02.q1.h: Think about which came first, the exposure or the disease.
med-epi-biostats.l02.q1.e: Because both are assessed at the same time, reverse causation cannot be excluded. It estimates prevalence, so the last option is wrong, and it needs no follow-up.

med-epi-biostats.l02.q2.t: Ecological fallacy, because group-level associations may not apply to individuals
med-epi-biostats.l02.q2.p: A survey finds that countries with higher average sugar consumption have higher average diabetes rates. A commentator concludes that each individual who eats more sugar is more likely to have diabetes. Which error is most likely?
med-epi-biostats.l02.q2.h: The unit of analysis is the country, not the person.
med-epi-biostats.l02.q2.e: Inferring individual-level risk from group-level data is the ecological fallacy. Recall bias would need individual self-report, and the other options describe unrelated biases.

med-epi-biostats.l02.q3.t: A prevalence ratio of 2.0 comparing the exposed with the unexposed
med-epi-biostats.l02.q3.p: In a survey, 90 of 300 solvent-exposed workers report chronic cough, and 135 of 900 unexposed workers do. What is the prevalence ratio?
med-epi-biostats.l02.q3.h: Calculate the prevalence in each group first.
med-epi-biostats.l02.q3.e: Exposed prevalence is 90/300 = 30%, unexposed is 135/900 = 15%, so the ratio is 2.0. A value of 3.0 would come from using counts instead of proportions.

med-epi-biostats.l02.q4.t: Prevalence-incidence bias, because patients with rapidly fatal disease die and are missing from the prevalent sample
med-epi-biostats.l02.q4.p: A cross-sectional study in a chronic-disease clinic finds no association between an exposure and a rapidly fatal form of a disease, although a registry shows a strong association. Which explanation best accounts for this discrepancy?
med-epi-biostats.l02.q4.h: Who is still alive to be sampled in a prevalent group?
med-epi-biostats.l02.q4.e: Short-duration, quickly fatal cases are underrepresented in prevalence samples (Neyman bias). The option involving random allocation is internally contradictory, since confounding by indication arises without randomization.

med-epi-biostats.l02.q5.t: The finding is limited because temporality is unknown and depression could have contributed to weight gain
med-epi-biostats.l02.q5.p: A 52-year-old man is part of a survey in which 40% of participants with depression are obese compared with 25% without. The authors write that obesity causes depression. Which statement about the design is most accurate?
