med-skills.l15.q2.e: Troponin signals myocardial injury, which also occurs in myocarditis, sepsis and renal failure. Infarction requires a clinical context of ischemia as well.

med-skills.l15.q3.t: Detecting a disease that would never have caused symptoms or harm
med-skills.l15.q3.h: It is a harm of detection itself.
med-skills.l15.q3.e: Overdiagnosis is detection of disease that would not have caused harm in a lifetime. It differs from a false positive result.

med-skills.l15.q4.t: Interpret in context, consider chance and repeat the test if it is relevant
med-skills.l15.q4.p: A healthy 28-year-old with no symptoms has a 20-test panel as part of a wellness visit, and one result is slightly outside the range. Which action is most appropriate?
med-skills.l15.q4.h: With many tests, an outlier is expected by chance.
med-skills.l15.q4.e: Across many tests a mild outlier is common in healthy people, so context and repeat testing are better than a cascade. Dismissing it as a lab error is also unjustified.

med-skills.l15.q5.t: Explain the usually benign course and defer imaging while no red flags are present
med-skills.l15.q5.p: A 35-year-old man with 10 days of low back pain after lifting, with no fever, trauma history, weight loss or neurological deficit, requests an MRI. Which response is most consistent with high-value care?
med-skills.l15.q5.h: Think about red flags and the expected course.
med-skills.l15.q5.e: Uncomplicated acute low back pain without red flags usually improves, and early imaging offers little benefit while risking incidental findings. A dismissive refusal is not good care.

med-skills.l16.q1.t: Objective, since it is a finding measured by the clinician
med-skills.l16.q1.p: In a SOAP note, where does a measured blood pressure belong?
med-skills.l16.q1.h: Think of what is observed or measured.
med-skills.l16.q1.e: Measured data are Objective. Subjective is for what the patient reports.

med-skills.l16.q2.t: Likely stable angina given exertional pressure and risk factors, with ACS less likely
med-skills.l16.q2.p: Which entry belongs in the Assessment section?
med-skills.l16.q2.h: It is the synthesis with reasoning.
med-skills.l16.q2.e: The Assessment states the working diagnosis with reasoning. The other options are subjective, plan and objective in that order.

med-skills.l16.q3.t: Add a dated and signed addendum that preserves the original entry
med-skills.l16.q3.p: A clinician realizes that a prior note contained a wrong medication dose. What is the correct way to fix it?
med-skills.l16.q3.e: Corrections are made by dated, signed addenda that preserve the original. Deleting or backdating alters the legal record.

med-skills.l16.q4.t: Copy-forward of old text without verification of current data
med-skills.l16.q4.p: A progress note for a 70-year-old with pneumonia on day 3 repeats the admission exam and states the patient is afebrile, but the temperature chart shows 38.4 degrees overnight. This most likely resulted from:
med-skills.l16.q4.e: Carrying old text forward without checking produced the error. Pertinent negatives require that the data be current and accurate.

med-skills.l16.q5.t: The patient has not been taking insulin because of cost, and options will be explored
med-skills.l16.q5.p: A note reads: patient is noncompliant and refuses to take his insulin. On review, the patient says he cannot afford the supplies. Which revision best fits good documentation?
med-skills.l16.q5.h: Describe facts and causes, not labels.
med-skills.l16.q5.e: Neutral language that records the barrier and a plan is more accurate and respectful. The other options keep a label or an unsupported assumption.

med-skills.l17.q1.t: A one-liner giving age, sex, background and reason for the encounter
med-skills.l17.q1.p: What is the usual first element of an oral case presentation?
med-skills.l17.q1.e: The one-liner frames the case. Plan and details come later.

med-skills.l17.q2.t: Focus on interval events, current findings, new data and a plan by problem
med-skills.l17.q2.p: Which is the best approach for a daily inpatient presentation?
med-skills.l17.q2.h: Brief and focused on what changed.
med-skills.l17.q2.e: Daily presentations are focused on change and the plan. Reading the full note aloud is the novice mistake.

med-skills.l17.q3.t: Synthesis by receiver, in which the receiver restates the key points
med-skills.l17.q3.p: In the I-PASS handoff tool, the final S stands for:
med-skills.l17.q3.e: The receiver synthesizes, restating the key points to confirm shared understanding. Illness severity is the I.

med-skills.l17.q4.t: State plainly that rebound and guarding were not assessed
med-skills.l17.q4.p: A student presents a 55-year-old with abdominal pain and says, "the abdomen is soft." The attending asks whether he checked for rebound or guarding. He had not examined for either. What should the student have done?
med-skills.l17.q4.h: Honesty about what was done matters more than completeness.
med-skills.l17.q4.e: A presenter must not report an examination not performed and should state what was not assessed. Inventing findings is dishonest and unsafe.

med-skills.l17.q5.t: A contingency plan with what to do if the hemoglobin drops or bleeding recurs
med-skills.l17.q5.p: A senior resident hands off a patient with a possible bleed overnight, saying only that the patient is stable and will need a repeat hemoglobin. The night resident does not ask questions. Which element would most improve the handoff?
med-skills.l17.q5.h: Think about what could go wrong overnight.
med-skills.l17.q5.e: Situational awareness and contingency planning tell the receiver what to do if the patient worsens. A long history adds length without actionable guidance.

med-skills.l18.q1.t: A guarantee from the clinician that no complications will occur
med-skills.l18.q1.p: Which is NOT a required element of informed consent?
med-skills.l18.q1.h: Honesty about risk is required, guarantees are not.
med-skills.l18.q1.e: Consent requires disclosure, alternatives and voluntariness. No clinician can guarantee that complications will not occur.

med-skills.l18.q2.t: Confirm the patient, procedure and site with the whole team just before starting
med-skills.l18.q2.p: The purpose of the time-out before a procedure is to:
med-skills.l18.q2.h: It is a final team check.
med-skills.l18.q2.e: The time-out is a team-wide verification just before the procedure. It helps prevent wrong-site and wrong-patient errors.

med-skills.l18.q3.t: The neurovascular bundle runs along the lower edge of each rib
med-skills.l18.q3.p: Why is thoracentesis performed just above the upper border of a rib?
med-skills.l18.q3.h: Consider the vein, artery and nerve.
med-skills.l18.q3.e: The intercostal vein, artery and nerve run under the rib, so entering over the upper border avoids them. The other options give anatomical claims that are not the reason.

med-skills.l18.q4.t: Obtain head CT first, and start empiric antibiotics without waiting for the scan
med-skills.l18.q4.p: A 28-year-old man with severe headache, fever and neck stiffness needs a lumbar puncture. He has new confusion and a unilateral dilated pupil. Which step is most appropriate before the procedure?
med-skills.l18.q4.h: Focal signs suggest raised intracranial pressure.
med-skills.l18.q4.e: New confusion and a dilated pupil are signs that call for imaging before lumbar puncture because of herniation risk, and suspected bacterial meningitis calls for empiric antibiotics that are not delayed for the scan. Puncturing first risks herniation, and observing without treatment risks death.

med-skills.l18.q5.t: Implied consent in an emergency where delay would risk life or serious harm
med-skills.l18.q5.p: A 45-year-old man is brought unconscious after a crash with severe hemorrhage and no family reachable. The surgeon proceeds to emergency surgery. Which principle justifies this?
med-skills.l18.q5.h: No one was available to consent and delay would be dangerous.
med-skills.l18.q5.e: Emergency treatment of a patient who cannot consent proceeds under implied consent. Substituted judgment requires a surrogate, and none was reached.

music-business.l01.q1.t: The recording side (sound recording) and the publishing side (composition)
music-business.l01.q1.p: Recorded music generally earns on which two separate sides?
music-business.l01.q1.h: Think about the two copyrights in every song.
music-business.l01.q1.e: Every song has a sound recording and a composition, each owned and collected separately, which is the core of the money map.

music-business.l01.q2.p: A service sets aside $1,000 for one song's plays. Illustrative rules send 60 percent to the recording side and the rest to publishing. How much goes to the publishing side?
music-business.l01.q2.h: Subtract the recording share from 100 percent first.
music-business.l01.q2.e: The publishing side receives 100 minus 60 equals 40 percent, which is $400 of the $1,000.

music-business.l01.q3.p: Using the $600 recording and $400 publishing split of $1,000, an artist owns the publishing and keeps 20 percent of master income (ignore other deductions). What does the artist receive in total?
music-business.l01.q3.h: Compute 20 percent of the recording side, then add publishing.
music-business.l01.q3.e: 20 percent of $600 is $120, plus the $400 publishing side, equals $520.

music-business.l01.q4.t: It ignores the publishing side, which needs its own registrations and collectors
music-business.l01.q4.p: An artist says streaming only pays one party, so registering with a distributor is all they need. What is the main flaw?
music-business.l01.q4.e: The composition earns separately and is collected through channels such as PROs and the MLC, which a distributor does not automatically cover.

music-business.l01.q5.p: Which income is paid for performing rather than for owning a copyright?
music-business.l01.q5.h: Which of these does not depend on a recording or song being used?
music-business.l01.q5.e: Live fees are paid for the performance itself; the other options are paid because a copyrighted work is used.

music-business.l02.q1.p: A sound recording and the song it contains are the same copyright.
music-business.l02.q1.e: They are separate copyrights: the composition and the sound recording, often with different owners.

music-business.l02.q2.t: A mechanical license for the underlying composition
music-business.l02.q2.p: A band records its own version of a song written by someone else. What must it clear for the composition?
music-business.l02.q2.h: The cover is a new recording, so which right still belongs to someone else?
music-business.l02.q2.e: The cover owns its new master but needs a mechanical license for the underlying composition.

music-business.l02.q3.t: Both the master owner and the publisher of the composition
music-business.l02.q3.p: A producer samples five seconds of a commercial record in a new beat. Which clearances are normally needed?
music-business.l02.q3.h: A sample uses the recording and the music inside it.
music-business.l02.q3.e: Sampling a recording typically uses both copyrights, so both owners usually need to clear it. Length alone does not create a safe harbor.

music-business.l02.q4.t: It would transfer the composition copyright as well as the master
music-business.l02.q4.p: A contract says the artist assigns all copyrights in the songs recorded under the deal to the label, when the deal was meant to cover only the recordings. What is the issue?
music-business.l02.q4.h: Compare what the clause says with what was intended.
music-business.l02.q4.e: Wording that covers all copyrights in the songs can sweep in the composition, not just the recording.

music-business.l02.q5.t: Nothing in the compositions unless the contract also transfers them
music-business.l02.q5.p: A label buys a band's master recordings outright. What does that purchase automatically include?
music-business.l02.q5.h: Which copyright is the one being sold?
music-business.l02.q5.e: Selling the master transfers the sound recording copyright only; compositions, names and other rights need separate language.

music-business.l03.q1.t: Each writer's agreed percentage ownership of a song
music-business.l03.q1.p: What does a split sheet record?
music-business.l03.q1.e: A split sheet documents who owns what percent of the composition, ideally at the time of writing.

music-business.l03.q2.p: A song earns $2,000 of publishing income and the writers hold 50, 30 and 20 percent. How much is owed to the 30 percent writer?
music-business.l03.q2.h: Multiply total income by the percentage.

music-business.l03.q3.p: A writer's administrator charges 20 percent on $5,000 collected. What does the writer receive?

music-business.l03.q4.t: No written split sheet was signed when the song was written
music-business.l03.q4.p: Two writers verbally agree to share equally. After release, a producer claims 25 percent of the song. What was the key mistake?
music-business.l03.q4.h: How could the dispute have been prevented?
music-business.l03.q4.e: Without a written agreement signed at the time, ownership disputes are hard to resolve.

music-business.l03.q5.p: Which arrangement most clearly lets the writer keep ownership of the copyright while a publisher collects for a fee?
music-business.l03.q5.h: Look for the structure where the publisher only administers.
music-business.l03.q5.e: In an administration deal the writer keeps ownership and the publisher charges a fee for collecting and administering.

music-business.l04.q1.p: In the US, SESAC and GMR are open to any songwriter who applies.
music-business.l04.q1.e: SESAC and GMR are selective and invitation based, unlike ASCAP and BMI.

music-business.l04.q2.p: A song generates $800 of performance royalties paid half as writer's share and half as publisher's share. How much is the writer's share?
music-business.l04.q2.e: Half of $800 is $400 for the writer, with $400 for the publisher.

music-business.l04.q3.t: Writers generally affiliate with one PRO at a time
music-business.l04.q3.p: A songwriter wants to register the same songs with both ASCAP and BMI. What is the usual problem?
music-business.l04.q3.h: Consider how performances would be allocated.
music-business.l04.q3.e: A songwriter generally belongs to a single PRO at a time, so duplicate affiliation creates conflicts.

music-business.l04.q4.t: PROs cover the composition; SoundExchange covers digital performance of the master
music-business.l04.q4.p: A songwriter says their PRO membership means their recordings are covered on internet radio. What is wrong?
music-business.l04.q4.h: Which copyright does the PRO represent?
music-business.l04.q4.e: PROs collect composition performance royalties, while recording performance royalties for non-interactive digital services go through SoundExchange.

music-business.l04.q5.t: The publisher's share of performance income may go uncollected
music-business.l04.q5.p: A writer has registered with a PRO but never created a publisher entity. What is the likely result?
music-business.l04.q5.e: Performance income has a writer's share and a publisher's share, and without a registered publisher the latter may not be claimed.

music-business.l05.q1.p: Which organization administers the blanket mechanical license for eligible digital music services under the Music Modernization Act?
music-business.l05.q1.h: Its name describes the right it licenses.
music-business.l05.q1.e: The MLC administers the blanket license, receiving reports and payments and distributing mechanical royalties.

music-business.l05.q2.p: Using a hypothetical statutory rate of $0.10 per copy, a band presses 1,000 CDs of a licensed cover. What mechanical royalty is owed?
music-business.l05.q2.e: 1,000 copies times $0.10 equals $100. The real rate is set by regulation and changes.

music-business.l05.q3.t: Register the works and ownership shares with the MLC
music-business.l05.q3.p: A songwriter wants mechanical royalties from interactive streaming services. What should they or their publisher do?
music-business.l05.q3.h: Which collective matches digital usage to works?
music-business.l05.q3.e: The MLC pays based on registered works and shares, so registration with accurate data is how songs get matched.

music-business.l05.q4.t: Part of the royalties cannot be fully matched and paid
music-business.l05.q4.p: A work's registered shares at the MLC total only 90 percent. What is the likely effect?
music-business.l05.q4.h: What must splits add up to?
music-business.l05.q4.e: Incomplete splits cause unmatched or disputed money, so registered shares should total 100 percent.

music-business.l05.q5.p: Under the MMA blanket license the MLC collects performance royalties for radio plays.
music-business.l05.q5.h: Which right does a mechanical license cover?
music-business.l05.q5.e: The MLC handles mechanical rights for digital services; performance royalties go through PROs.

music-business.l06.q1.t: A sync license and a master use license
music-business.l06.q1.p: A typical TV placement of a commercial song needs which two licenses?
music-business.l06.q1.h: One covers the composition, one the recording.
music-business.l06.q1.e: The publisher grants sync for the composition and the master owner grants master use.

music-business.l06.q2.p: A production agrees a $6,000 sync fee with a most favored nations master fee. What is the total paid for both licenses?
music-business.l06.q2.h: MFN means the two sides are equal.
music-business.l06.q2.e: The master fee also equals $6,000, so the total is $12,000.

music-business.l06.q3.t: Additional or expanded rights for the new media and territory
music-business.l06.q3.p: A license covers US broadcast TV for two years. The show is sold to a global streamer in year one. What is needed?
music-business.l06.q3.h: Compare the new use to the original scope.
music-business.l06.q3.e: A license is limited to its scope, so worldwide streaming would require expanded rights.

music-business.l06.q4.t: The broad exclusive scope may block future licensing at a low price
music-business.l06.q4.p: A request offers $500 for a perpetual, all-media, worldwide, exclusive license to a song. What is the main concern?
music-business.l06.q4.h: Compare the breadth of the grant with the price.
music-business.l06.q4.e: A broad, exclusive, perpetual grant should be priced much higher because it limits other income.

music-business.l06.q5.t: It lists each song and its writers so performance royalties can be paid
music-business.l06.q5.p: Why does a production file a cue sheet?
music-business.l06.q5.h: Think about which collectors need usage information.
music-business.l06.q5.e: Cue sheets tell PROs what music was used and who wrote it, supporting performance royalty payments.

music-business.l07.q1.t: A license grants limited permission; an assignment transfers ownership
music-business.l07.q1.p: What is the main difference between a master license and an assignment?
music-business.l07.q1.e: Licenses are scope-limited permissions while assignments transfer title.

music-business.l07.q2.p: A master owner licenses a track non-exclusively to four users at $1,500 each. What is the total, and who still owns the master?
music-business.l07.q2.h: Four payments, and no transfer of ownership.
music-business.l07.q2.e: 4 times $1,500 equals $6,000, and licensing does not transfer ownership.

music-business.l07.q3.p: A new song samples a record. The sample's publisher takes 20 percent of the new song's publishing, which earns $5,000. How much does the sample's publisher receive?
music-business.l07.q3.e: 20 percent of $5,000 is $1,000, leaving $4,000 for the new writers.

music-business.l07.q4.p: Which term most limits the owner's ability to license the master elsewhere?
music-business.l07.q4.h: Think about who else can use it.
music-business.l07.q4.e: An exclusive license prevents the owner from licensing the same use to others within its scope.

music-business.l07.q5.t: It also grants rights in your masters, so scope, term and reversion matter
music-business.l07.q5.p: Why does a distribution agreement raise the same questions as a master license?
music-business.l07.q5.h: What are you actually giving a distributor?
music-business.l07.q5.e: A distribution agreement licenses your recordings, so term, territory, exclusivity and reversion should be checked.

music-business.l08.q1.h: It travels with the recording's metadata.
music-business.l08.q1.e: An ISRC is a unique code for a sound recording, used to track and pay it.

music-business.l08.q2.p: In a month the recording-side pool is $1,000,000 with 500,000,000 total streams. You have 250,000 streams. What do you earn before fees?
music-business.l08.q2.h: Compute your share of total streams first.
music-business.l08.q2.e: 250,000 divided by 500,000,000 is 0.05 percent, and 0.05 percent of $1,000,000 is $500.

music-business.l08.q3.p: The pool stays $1,000,000 but total streams double to 1,000,000,000. What do your same 250,000 streams earn?
music-business.l08.q3.h: Your share of the total halves.

music-business.l08.q4.t: Per-stream amounts are outcomes of pools, mixes and countries, not fixed prices
music-business.l08.q4.p: Someone says Platform B pays $0.004 per stream and Platform A pays $0.003, so B is always better. What is wrong?
music-business.l08.q4.h: Is a per-stream rate promised anywhere?
music-business.l08.q4.e: The effective rate comes from pool revenue divided by streams and varies by period, country and subscriber mix.

music-business.l08.q5.p: Distributor A takes 15 percent of revenue; distributor B charges a flat $30 per year. For $1,000 annual revenue, which costs less and by how much?
music-business.l08.q5.e: A's fee is $150 versus B's $30, so B costs $120 less. The break-even is $200 of revenue.

music-business.l09.q1.t: Digital performance royalties for sound recordings under statutory licenses
music-business.l09.q1.p: What does SoundExchange collect and distribute?
music-business.l09.q1.h: It handles the master, not the composition.
music-business.l09.q1.e: SoundExchange administers the statutory digital performance license for sound recordings on non-interactive services.

music-business.l09.q2.p: A distribution is $10,000 for a recording. What does the featured artist receive under the statutory split?
music-business.l09.q2.e: 45 percent of $10,000 is $4,500, with $5,000 to the owner and $500 to non-featured performers.

music-business.l09.q3.p: A $2,000 distribution is made. How much goes to the non-featured performers fund?

music-business.l09.q4.t: The artist is paid directly by SoundExchange only if registered; otherwise money may sit unclaimed
music-business.l09.q4.p: A label-signed artist assumes the label will pass along the 45 percent featured-artist share. What is the risk?
music-business.l09.q4.h: Who pays the featured artist share?
music-business.l09.q4.e: SoundExchange pays featured artists directly when they are registered, so unregistered artists may miss payment.

music-business.l09.q5.t: Composition performance royalties through PROs, but generally no sound recording performance royalty
music-business.l09.q5.p: A song plays on a terrestrial AM/FM station. What does US law generally require paid?
music-business.l09.q5.h: Terrestrial radio is the exception here.
music-business.l09.q5.e: US terrestrial radio pays composition royalties but generally no sound recording performance royalty, unlike digital transmissions.

music-business.l10.q1.p: Which deal type typically lets the artist keep master ownership while paying a fee for distribution?
music-business.l10.q1.h: Think of the label as a service provider.
music-business.l10.q1.e: In a distribution deal the artist keeps ownership and pays a fee or percentage for distribution.

music-business.l10.q2.p: Under a 360 deal a label takes 15 percent of $20,000 in merch. How much?

music-business.l10.q3.p: A record earns $80,000 with $30,000 in costs under a 50 percent profit split. What is the artist's share?

music-business.l10.q4.t: The license with reversion, because rights return to you
music-business.l10.q4.p: Which is better for long-term ownership: a perpetual label-owned master or a ten-year license with reversion?
music-business.l10.q4.e: Reversion returns rights to the owner after the term, while perpetual ownership by the label does not.

music-business.l10.q5.t: The label shares income without adding matching value for that income stream
music-business.l10.q5.p: A 360 label takes a share of touring income but does no touring support. What is the main issue?
music-business.l10.q5.h: Compare what the label gives to what it takes.
music-business.l10.q5.e: You should compare what services the label provides for each stream it shares in.

music-business.l11.q1.t: The label recovers it from the artist's future royalties
music-business.l11.q1.p: What does it mean for an advance to be recouped?
music-business.l11.q1.h: Where does the recovery come from?
music-business.l11.q1.e: Recoupment means the label recovers the advance out of the artist's royalty share.

music-business.l11.q2.p: A $60,000 recoupable advance and a 15 percent royalty. At what royalty-bearing receipts does the artist recoup?
music-business.l11.q2.h: Divide the advance by the rate.

music-business.l11.q3.p: A $100,000 advance, 20 percent royalty, $700,000 in receipts. How much royalty is payable after recoupment?

music-business.l11.q4.p: A $150,000 recording fund and a $50,000 advance are both recoupable at a 20 percent rate. What receipts are needed before the artist is paid royalties?
music-business.l11.q4.e: The balance is $200,000, and $200,000 divided by 0.20 is $1,000,000.

music-business.l11.q5.p: Album one is $30,000 unrecouped and album two earns $50,000 in royalties. With cross-collateralization, what is paid on album two?
music-business.l11.q5.e: The $30,000 deficit is deducted from $50,000, leaving $20,000.

music-business.l12.q1.t: Finds and negotiates live performance dates
music-business.l12.q1.p: What does a booking agent primarily do?
music-business.l12.q1.e: Agents book live performances and negotiate the performance terms.

music-business.l12.q2.p: On $20,000 of show income an agent takes 10 percent and a manager 15 percent. What does the artist keep before expenses?

music-business.l12.q3.p: A manager takes 15 percent. Gross is $80,000, expenses $50,000. How much more is the commission on gross than on net?
music-business.l12.q3.e: 15 percent of $80,000 is $12,000 and of $30,000 is $4,500, a $7,500 difference.

music-business.l12.q4.t: A conflict of interest in negotiating against their own interests
music-business.l12.q4.p: A manager also owns the label offering you a deal. What is the central concern?
music-business.l12.q4.h: Whose interests is the manager representing?
music-business.l12.q4.e: A manager who benefits on the other side of the deal may not negotiate in the artist's best interest, so independent counsel matters.

music-business.l12.q5.t: To reduce post-term commissions on deals over time
music-business.l12.q5.p: What is the purpose of a sunset clause in a management deal?
music-business.l12.q5.h: It concerns what happens after the contract ends.
music-business.l12.q5.e: Sunset clauses taper or limit commission after the term on deals made during it.

music-business.l13.q1.t: Rights returning to the grantor under stated conditions
music-business.l13.q1.p: What is reversion in a contract?
music-business.l13.q1.e: Reversion clauses specify when and how granted rights return.

music-business.l13.q2.p: A deal has a one-year initial term plus four one-year options held by the label. What is the maximum length?
music-business.l13.q2.h: Count the initial term and all options.
music-business.l13.q2.e: 1 plus 4 equals 5 years if all options are exercised.

music-business.l13.q3.t: It is outside the licensed territory
music-business.l13.q3.p: You license your recording for the United States only. The licensee releases it in Japan. What does that most likely mean?
music-business.l13.q3.e: A license limited to the US does not cover other territories without more rights.

music-business.l13.q4.t: You may end up dealing with an unknown party with your rights
music-business.l13.q4.p: A clause lets the other party assign your contract to any third party without consent. What is the issue?
music-business.l13.q4.h: Who might hold your rights later?
music-business.l13.q4.e: Free assignment can move your contract to someone you never chose.

music-business.l13.q5.t: The window and cost burden make errors hard to catch and recover
music-business.l13.q5.p: Audit rights allow objections only within six months after each statement, with the artist paying all costs. What is the concern?
music-business.l13.q5.e: Short windows and cost burdens weaken the practical value of audit rights.

music-business.l14.q1.t: The greater of a guarantee or a percentage of net
music-business.l14.q1.h: Two numbers, you get the higher one.
music-business.l14.q1.e: Versus deals pay the greater of the guarantee or the percentage of net.

music-business.l14.q2.p: A $2,000 guarantee versus 80 percent of net. Ticket gross is $4,500 and show expenses $1,500. What does the artist receive?
music-business.l14.q2.e: Net is $3,000, 80 percent is $2,400, which beats $2,000.

music-business.l14.q3.p: A tour leaves $5,500 to split among four equal members. What does each take home before taxes?

music-business.l14.q4.p: In the lesson's tour, a 360 label also takes 10 percent of the $30,000 gross, leaving $5,500 before it. What remains?

music-business.l14.q5.p: A $3,000 guarantee versus 85 percent of net after $2,800 expenses. Ticket gross is $9,000. What does the artist receive?
music-business.l14.q5.e: Net is $6,200, 85 percent is $5,270, which beats $3,000.

music-business.l15.q1.p: Margin per item equals price minus what?
music-business.l15.q1.e: Per-item margin subtracts the item cost and fees such as the venue cut.

music-business.l15.q2.p: A shirt costs $8 and sells for $25 with a 20 percent venue cut of gross. What is the profit per shirt?
music-business.l15.q2.e: The cut is $5, so $25 minus $8 minus $5 equals $12.

music-business.l15.q3.p: 100 shirts at $12 profit and 50 hoodies at $22 profit. Total profit?

music-business.l15.q4.t: The venue cut is on gross, so profit is $7 not $9
music-business.l15.q4.p: A $20 shirt costs $8 and the venue takes 25 percent of gross. A band expects to keep 75 percent of the $12 margin. What is the error?
music-business.l15.q4.h: Which amount does the percentage apply to?
music-business.l15.q4.e: 25 percent of $20 is $5, so profit is $20 minus $8 minus $5 equals $7.

music-business.l15.q5.p: Bulk: 300 shirts at $8 cost $2,400. Print-on-demand costs $14. You sell 200 shirts at $25 with a $5 venue cut. Which earns more and by how much?
music-business.l15.q5.e: Bulk nets $4,000 minus $2,400 equals $1,600; print-on-demand nets 200 times $6 equals $1,200, a $400 difference.

music-business.l16.q1.t: Registering compositions and recordings with the proper collectors
music-business.l16.q1.p: Which registration step is recommended before a release?
music-business.l16.q1.h: Think about how money finds you.
music-business.l16.q1.e: Without registrations, usage cannot be matched to the right payee.

music-business.l16.q2.p: A $3,000 budget is 40 percent ads, 30 percent content, 20 percent publicity and 10 percent reserve. How much is for ads?

music-business.l16.q3.p: A distributor needs 28 days before release for editorial pitching. For a June 26 release, what is the latest submission date?

music-business.l16.q4.t: No funds remain to reinforce momentum afterward
music-business.l16.q4.p: A plan spends the entire budget in release week. What is the weakness?
music-business.l16.q4.e: Staging spend allows reinvestment when data shows what works.

music-business.l16.q5.t: Plays occur but collection systems cannot identify who to pay
music-business.l16.q5.p: A team releases tracks but never signs split sheets or registers songs. What is the most likely consequence?
music-business.l16.q5.h: What do collectors need to pay you?
music-business.l16.q5.e: Collection systems rely on accurate registrations and splits to pay correctly.

music-business.l17.q1.t: You can reach fans directly without depending on a platform's algorithm
music-business.l17.q1.p: Why is an email list considered an owned audience?
music-business.l17.q1.e: Direct contact lets you reach fans without a platform's reach rules.

music-business.l17.q2.p: 10,000 monthly listeners, 2 percent join the list, 10 percent of those buy a $25 item. What revenue results?

music-business.l17.q3.p: A $300 campaign yields 150 signups. What is the cost per signup?

music-business.l17.q4.t: CAN-SPAM, which requires an unsubscribe mechanism
music-business.l17.q4.p: Your newsletter has no unsubscribe link. Which US law is most directly implicated?
music-business.l17.q4.e: CAN-SPAM requires commercial email to include a working opt-out.

music-business.l17.q5.t: Reach and rules can change without notice
music-business.l17.q5.p: A band relies only on one social platform's followers. What is the strategic risk?
music-business.l17.q5.e: Rented audiences depend on platform decisions, so pairing them with owned channels reduces risk.

music-business.l18.q1.t: To separate personal and business liability when operated properly
music-business.l18.q1.p: What is a main purpose of forming an LLC?
music-business.l18.q1.e: An LLC can provide liability separation, but only when run properly, and it does not eliminate taxes.

music-business.l18.q2.p: Revenue is $40,000 and expenses are $15,000. What is net profit?

music-business.l18.q3.p: Revenue $18,000; expenses $4,500 gear, $3,000 travel, $1,500 ads. Net profit?

music-business.l18.q4.t: Commingling can weaken the liability protection and muddy records
music-business.l18.q4.p: An LLC owner pays personal bills from the LLC account. What is the risk?
music-business.l18.q4.h: Consider how separate the entity is.
music-business.l18.q4.e: Mixing funds undermines separation and makes bookkeeping unreliable.

music-business.l18.q5.t: A default LLC is generally pass-through, so income is still reported by the owner
music-business.l18.q5.p: A musician believes forming an LLC means the income is tax-free. What is wrong?
music-business.l18.q5.e: An LLC does not make income tax-free; profit generally passes through to the owner's return.

music-business.l19.q1.t: Master and sync clearance for projects
music-business.l19.q1.p: In the lesson, what does the Plajah music licensing store illustrate?
music-business.l19.q1.e: It shows how tracks can be licensed or requested for a project.

music-business.l19.q2.p: Publishing a track on a platform automatically registers your songs with a PRO, the MLC and SoundExchange.
music-business.l19.q2.e: Platform publishing does not by itself register works with collection organizations.

music-business.l19.q3.p: You sign a 60/40 split sheet on a song earning $1,000 in publishing. How much does the 40 percent writer receive?

music-business.l19.q4.t: Chain of title is unclear, so a clean license cannot be promised
music-business.l19.q4.p: A creator offers a track in a licensing marketplace that includes a collaborator's contribution with no agreement. What is the issue?
music-business.l19.q4.h: Can you grant what you do not control?
music-business.l19.q4.e: You can only license what you control, so co-owners need agreements.

music-business.l19.q5.p: Which Plajah tool best fits tracking contracts, invoices and vendors for an artist business?
music-business.l19.q5.e: Artist Manager is the business operations hub for contracts, invoices, payroll and tasks.

music-figures.l01.q1.p: Which opera is described as the first enduring opera?
music-figures.l01.q1.e: Monteverdi composed L'Orfeo, the first enduring opera.

music-figures.l01.q2.t: A practice freeing dissonance to serve the text
music-figures.l01.q2.h: It concerns how words and harmony relate.
music-figures.l01.q2.e: The seconda pratica freed dissonance so music could serve the meaning of the words.

music-figures.l01.q3.p: A composer wants rapid repeated notes to depict anger in a dramatic scene. Which Monteverdi device would they use?
music-figures.l01.q3.h: The name means an agitated style.
music-figures.l01.q3.e: Monteverdi developed the stile concitato for dramatic effect.

music-figures.l01.q4.t: He linked Renaissance polyphony to the opera of the Baroque
music-figures.l01.q4.p: Why is Monteverdi described as a "bridge"?
music-figures.l01.q4.h: Think about which eras surround him.
music-figures.l01.q4.e: He stood between Renaissance polyphony and the Baroque world of opera and dramatic music.

music-figures.l02.q1.p: Which musical form did Bach perfect?
music-figures.l02.q1.h: A theme is imitated by other voices.
music-figures.l02.q1.e: Bach perfected fugue and invertible counterpoint.

music-figures.l02.q2.h: Preludes and fugues in all keys.
music-figures.l02.q2.e: The Well-Tempered Clavier is one of Bach's landmark works.

music-figures.l02.q3.p: Bach's forty-eight preludes and fugues championed an equal-ish temperament.
music-figures.l02.q3.e: The museum notes the 48 preludes and fugues championed an equal-ish temperament.

music-figures.l02.q4.t: It codified functional harmony underpinning Western music
music-figures.l02.q4.p: Why do later composers study Bach's counterpoint and harmony?
music-figures.l02.q4.h: Think about the foundation he provided.
music-figures.l02.q4.e: Bach codified functional harmony, so his works serve as models for how chords and keys work.

music-figures.l03.q1.h: It paints scenes of the year.
music-figures.l03.q1.e: The Four Seasons is Vivaldi's most famous work.

music-figures.l03.q2.p: Which form did Handel elevate to a national form in England?
music-figures.l03.q2.e: Handel elevated the English oratorio to a national form.

music-figures.l03.q3.p: A composer writes a solo concerto in the standard three-movement shape. Whose standard are they following?
music-figures.l03.q3.e: Vivaldi standardised the three-movement solo concerto form.

music-figures.l03.q4.t: Vivaldi shaped the instrumental concerto and picture-painting; Handel shaped public choral works
music-figures.l03.q4.p: How do Vivaldi and Handel mainly differ in their contribution?
music-figures.l03.q4.h: One is instrumental, one is choral.
music-figures.l03.q4.e: Vivaldi's legacy is the concerto and programmatic writing; Handel's is choral grandeur and oratorio.

music-figures.l04.q1.p: Who is called the father of the symphony and the string quartet?
music-figures.l04.q1.e: Haydn established the four-movement symphony and quartet templates.

music-figures.l04.q2.e: The Marriage of Figaro is one of Mozart's major operas.

music-figures.l04.q3.p: A composer grows an entire movement from a small musical idea and adds wit. Whose strength is this?
music-figures.l04.q3.e: Haydn was a master of thematic development and wit.

music-figures.l04.q4.p: What is the relationship between Haydn and Beethoven?
music-figures.l04.q4.e: Haydn mentored Beethoven, who inherited and stretched Haydn's forms.

music-figures.l05.q1.p: Which Beethoven symphony introduced a chorus?
music-figures.l05.q1.e: Beethoven introduced the chorus into the symphony in Symphony No. 9.

music-figures.l05.q2.p: Beethoven was going deaf while writing some of his greatest works.
music-figures.l05.q2.e: The museum notes he bridged Classical order and Romantic expression while going deaf.

music-figures.l05.q3.p: Which work is NOT by Beethoven?
music-figures.l05.q3.h: The Creation is an oratorio by another composer.

music-figures.l05.q4.t: He connected Classical order with Romantic expression
music-figures.l05.q4.p: Why is Beethoven called the "hinge" of music history?
music-figures.l05.q4.e: He bridged Classical forms and Romantic expression, making the composer a hero.

music-figures.l06.q1.e: The Lied is the German art song that Schubert perfected.

music-figures.l06.q2.p: Roughly how many songs did Schubert write?
music-figures.l06.q2.e: The museum notes over 600 songs in a life of 31 years.

music-figures.l06.q3.p: A pianist plays with flexible tempo over a steady pulse. Which composer's technique is this?
music-figures.l06.q3.e: Chopin used rubato as expressive freedom over a steady pulse.

music-figures.l06.q4.t: He elevated national dances to art
music-figures.l06.q4.p: What do the mazurka and polonaise show about Chopin?
music-figures.l06.q4.e: Chopin raised the Polish mazurka and polonaise to the level of concert art.

music-figures.l07.q1.t: A recurring theme tied to a character or idea
music-figures.l07.q1.e: Wagner's leitmotifs are recurring themes tracking character and idea.

music-figures.l07.q2.e: A German Requiem is by Brahms; Tristan is Wagner's and Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's.

music-figures.l07.q3.p: A composer unites music, drama and staging into a single work. Which concept is this?
music-figures.l07.q3.e: The Gesamtkunstwerk is Wagner's unified music, drama and staging.

music-figures.l07.q4.t: Brahms kept Classical forms alive; Wagner pushed chromatic harmony toward modernism
music-figures.l07.q4.p: How do Brahms and Wagner differ?
music-figures.l07.q4.h: One looked back, one looked ahead.
music-figures.l07.q4.e: Brahms kept Classical forms alive against the music of the future; Wagner's chromatic harmony opened the door to modernism.

music-figures.l08.q1.p: Which composer is associated with Impressionism?
music-figures.l08.q1.e: Debussy is the Impressionist composer of Clair de Lune and La Mer.

music-figures.l08.q2.p: Which piece uses ostinato and gradual crescendo as form?
music-figures.l08.q2.e: Ravel's Boléro uses ostinato and gradual crescendo as its form.

music-figures.l08.q3.p: Debussy used whole-tone and modal scales that blurred the sense of key.
music-figures.l08.q3.e: Whole-tone and modal scales were central to Debussy's blurred tonality.

music-figures.l08.q4.t: Ravel stressed exact orchestration; Debussy stressed colour and loosened key
music-figures.l08.q4.p: How does Ravel's approach differ from Debussy's emphasis?
music-figures.l08.q4.e: Ravel is known for dazzling, exact orchestration, while Debussy treated timbre and colour as structure and loosened tonality.

music-figures.l09.q1.p: Which work by Stravinsky provoked a famous riot?
music-figures.l09.q1.h: The museum calls him the riot-starter.
music-figures.l09.q1.e: The Rite of Spring is Stravinsky's explosive, irregular-rhythm work.

music-figures.l09.q3.p: A vocalist delivers music halfway between speech and song. Which technique?
music-figures.l09.q3.e: Sprechstimme is Schoenberg's speech-song vocal delivery.

music-figures.l09.q4.t: Stravinsky changed rhythm; Schoenberg changed the role of the key
music-figures.l09.q4.p: Which contrast best describes Stravinsky and Schoenberg?
music-figures.l09.q4.e: Stravinsky rewrote rhythm, while Schoenberg freed music from the key through atonality and serialism.

music-figures.l10.q1.p: Who made the improvised solo the heart of jazz?
music-figures.l10.q1.e: Armstrong made the improvised solo central to jazz and popularised scat.

music-figures.l10.q2.p: Which work is by Duke Ellington?
music-figures.l10.q2.e: Take the "A" Train is by Ellington; West End Blues is Armstrong's.

music-figures.l10.q3.p: A bandleader writes music that suits each soloist's individual sound. Which jazz figure is known for this?
music-figures.l10.q3.h: He wrote for players, not just instruments.
music-figures.l10.q3.e: Ellington wrote for individual players' voices.

music-figures.l10.q4.t: Armstrong centred the individual voice; Ellington built larger works around many voices
music-figures.l10.q4.p: How do Armstrong and Ellington complement each other?
music-figures.l10.q4.e: Armstrong placed the soloist at the centre, while Ellington extended jazz into suites and concert-length works.

music-figures.l11.q1.p: Whose song gave the Rolling Stones their name?
music-figures.l11.q1.e: Muddy Waters' song Rollin' Stone inspired the band's name.

music-figures.l11.q2.p: Who is called the godmother of rock and roll?
music-figures.l11.q2.e: Sister Rosetta Tharpe brought distorted electric guitar to gospel.

music-figures.l11.q3.p: A musician electrifies the country blues into a full-band sound. Whose achievement is this?
music-figures.l11.q3.e: Muddy Waters electrified country blues into Chicago blues.

music-figures.l11.q4.t: She sang before the I Have a Dream speech
music-figures.l11.q4.p: What was notable about Mahalia Jackson's role at the March on Washington?
music-figures.l11.q4.h: She is the Queen of Gospel.
music-figures.l11.q4.e: Jackson sang at the March on Washington before the I Have a Dream speech.

music-figures.l12.q1.p: Who is known as the Queen of Soul?
music-figures.l12.q1.e: Aretha Franklin is the Queen of Soul.

music-figures.l12.q2.p: Whose emphasis on "the One" helped invent funk?
music-figures.l12.q2.e: James Brown shifted emphasis to the One, the downbeat groove.

music-figures.l12.q3.p: A musician merges gospel intensity with secular R&B. Who is credited?
music-figures.l12.q3.e: Ray Charles fused gospel and blues into soul.

music-figures.l12.q4.t: He is the most-sampled artist in hip-hop history
music-figures.l12.q4.p: Why is James Brown important to hip-hop?
music-figures.l12.q4.e: The museum notes Brown is the most-sampled artist in hip-hop history.

music-figures.l13.q1.p: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016?
music-figures.l13.q1.e: Bob Dylan won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.

music-figures.l13.q2.p: What did the Beatles make a compositional instrument?
music-figures.l13.q2.h: It is not a handheld instrument.
music-figures.l13.q2.e: The museum credits them with making the recording studio a compositional instrument.

music-figures.l13.q3.p: A guitarist uses feedback, wah and distortion as an expressive palette. Who is this?
music-figures.l13.q3.e: Jimi Hendrix used feedback, wah and distortion expressively.

music-figures.l13.q4.t: His riffs and teen-life lyrics became a blueprint for the Beatles and Stones
music-figures.l13.q4.p: How did Chuck Berry's work influence later rock bands?
music-figures.l13.q4.e: Berry defined the rock riff and teen-life lyrics, the blueprint later followed by the Beatles and Stones.

music-figures.l14.q1.p: Who made the DJ an instrumentalist by turning two turntables into one instrument?
music-figures.l14.q1.e: Grandmaster Flash developed the backspin and Quick Mix Theory.

music-figures.l14.q2.p: What did Kendrick Lamar win in 2018?
music-figures.l14.q2.h: He was the first rapper to do so.
music-figures.l14.q2.e: Kendrick Lamar won the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Music.

music-figures.l14.q3.p: An MC introduces complex internal rhyme and enjambment. Who is credited with this?
music-figures.l14.q3.e: Rakim introduced complex internal rhyme and enjambment.

music-figures.l14.q4.t: Dilla used off-grid drum feel; Public Enemy used dense sample collage for protest
music-figures.l14.q4.p: How do J Dilla and Public Enemy differ in approach?
music-figures.l14.q4.e: J Dilla reshaped rhythmic feel with off-grid programming; Public Enemy made layered sample collage a vehicle for protest.

music-genres.l01.q1.p: Genres overlap and their boundaries are often blurry.
music-genres.l01.q1.h: Think about whether music ever fits only one box.
music-genres.l01.q1.e: Genres are groupings made by listeners, performers and sellers, so they overlap and shift.

music-genres.l01.q2.t: What year was the song's composer born?
music-genres.l01.q2.p: Which is NOT one of the five listening questions in the lesson?
music-genres.l01.q2.h: The questions are about what you can hear and sense.
music-genres.l01.q2.e: The five questions cover rhythm, instruments, voice, structure and purpose, not biographical dates.

music-genres.l01.q3.p: In 1949 Billboard began using which term in place of an earlier label for records by Black artists?
music-genres.l01.q3.h: The lesson names the replaced term 'race records'.
music-genres.l01.q3.e: Billboard adopted 'rhythm and blues' in 1949, an example of how labels change while music evolves.

music-genres.l01.q4.t: They shape how music is shelved, advertised and remembered
music-genres.l01.q4.p: Why does the lesson say genre labels are partly a business tool?
music-genres.l01.q4.h: Think about record stores and marketing.
music-genres.l01.q4.e: Labels guide how music is sold and presented, not only how it sounds.

music-genres.l01.q5.t: Using the listening questions to analyze a genre
music-genres.l01.q5.p: A listener taps the pulse, names the lead instrument and decides the music is for dancing. What are they doing?
music-genres.l01.q5.h: Match the actions to the five questions.
music-genres.l01.q5.e: Pulse, instrument and purpose are three of the five listening questions.

music-genres.l02.q1.p: Spirituals have a single known composer who wrote them all.
music-genres.l02.q1.h: Consider how the songs were passed down.
music-genres.l02.q1.e: Spirituals were created and passed on by enslaved African Americans, mostly without known composers.

music-genres.l02.q2.t: A leader sings a line and the group answers
music-genres.l02.q2.h: Think about a conversation in song.
music-genres.l02.q2.e: In call-and-response a leader's line is answered by the group.

music-genres.l02.q3.p: Which group began touring in 1871 to raise money for their university?
music-genres.l02.q3.e: The Fisk Jubilee Singers toured to fund Fisk University and spread spirituals worldwide.

music-genres.l02.q4.p: Who is widely called the father of gospel music?
music-genres.l02.q4.h: He was a former blues pianist who wrote 'Take My Hand, Precious Lord'.
music-genres.l02.q4.e: Dorsey combined blues and jazz influences with church music and is widely called the father of gospel.

music-genres.l02.q5.p: Scholars agree that every spiritual contained a specific secret code about escape routes.
music-genres.l02.q5.h: The lesson advises caution about particular claims.
music-genres.l02.q5.e: Scholars debate how often particular songs were coded messages, so such claims should be treated cautiously.

music-genres.l03.q1.p: The classic blues form is twelve measures long.
music-genres.l03.q1.h: The number is in the lesson title of the form.
music-genres.l03.q1.e: The twelve-bar blues is the classic structure.

music-genres.l03.q2.t: A line is sung, repeated, then answered by a rhyming line
music-genres.l03.q2.p: What does an AAB lyric pattern mean?
music-genres.l03.q2.h: Think about repetition then a response.
music-genres.l03.q2.e: In AAB, the first line repeats and the third line answers it.

music-genres.l03.q3.t: Bent notes, especially the third, fifth and seventh steps of the scale
music-genres.l03.q3.e: Blue notes are expressive pitch bends on certain scale steps.

music-genres.l03.q4.p: Which record is generally cited as the first blues hit record by a Black vocalist?
music-genres.l03.q4.e: Mamie Smith's 'Crazy Blues' of 1920 is generally cited as the first.

music-genres.l03.q5.t: They helped bring electric guitars and amplified bands to the style
music-genres.l03.q5.p: Why did Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf matter to the blues in Chicago?
music-genres.l03.q5.h: Think about technology and the move to cities.
music-genres.l03.q5.e: In Chicago they plugged in and recorded electric blues for Chess Records.

music-genres.l04.q1.p: Improvisation is a defining trait of jazz.
music-genres.l04.q1.h: Players invent melodies on the spot.
music-genres.l04.q1.e: Improvised solos over a chord progression are central to jazz.

music-genres.l04.q2.t: Louis Armstrong's Hot Five and Hot Seven
music-genres.l04.q2.p: Which recordings made the improvised solo the center of jazz in the late 1920s?
music-genres.l04.q2.h: They are named for the size of the band and date from 1925 to 1928.
music-genres.l04.q2.e: Armstrong's Hot Five and Hot Seven records focused on the soloist.

music-genres.l04.q3.p: Which style, developed in the 1940s by Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, was fast and meant for listening?
music-genres.l04.q3.h: It came after the big-band swing era.
music-genres.l04.q3.e: Bebop was a fast, harmonically complex style played more for listening than dancing.

music-genres.l04.q4.t: Improvising over a few scales instead of rapidly changing chords
music-genres.l04.q4.p: What does 'modal' jazz, as on Kind of Blue, emphasize?
music-genres.l04.q4.h: Compare it with bebop's complicated chord changes.
music-genres.l04.q4.e: Modal jazz lets players improvise over a limited set of scales.

music-genres.l04.q5.p: Recordings of the early cornetist Buddy Bolden survive and show exactly how he sounded.
music-genres.l04.q5.h: The lesson says claims about his sound are guesswork.
music-genres.l04.q5.e: No recordings of Bolden survive, so descriptions of his sound are speculation.

music-genres.l05.q1.h: Country music had strong African American contributions.
music-genres.l05.q1.e: The banjo derives from African instruments, one reason the lesson stresses Black contributions.

music-genres.l05.q2.p: Where did producer Ralph Peer hold the 1927 sessions where Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family recorded?
music-genres.l05.q2.h: It is a border town named in the lesson.
music-genres.l05.q2.e: The 1927 Bristol sessions are often called the big bang of commercial country music.

music-genres.l05.q3.p: Who developed bluegrass in the mid-1940s with his band the Blue Grass Boys?
music-genres.l05.q3.e: Bill Monroe is credited with developing bluegrass; Scruggs joined his band.

music-genres.l05.q4.t: Guitar, banjo, mandolin, fiddle and upright bass
music-genres.l05.q4.p: Which instrument set is typical of a bluegrass band?
music-genres.l05.q4.h: Bluegrass is acoustic and has no drums.
music-genres.l05.q4.e: Bluegrass uses acoustic string instruments and no drum kit.

music-genres.l05.q5.p: What did Earl Scruggs contribute to bluegrass?
music-genres.l05.q5.h: It involves how he plucked the banjo.
music-genres.l05.q5.e: Scruggs's three-finger style helped crystallize the bluegrass sound.

music-genres.l06.q1.p: In R&B the backbeat emphasizes beats two and four.
music-genres.l06.q1.h: The lesson describes a punchy, strong backbeat.
music-genres.l06.q1.e: A strong backbeat on beats two and four is central to rhythm and blues.

music-genres.l06.q2.p: Which musician's 1954 recording 'I Got a Woman' brought gospel feeling to secular lyrics?
music-genres.l06.q2.h: He is credited as a soul pioneer.
music-genres.l06.q2.e: Ray Charles blended gospel and R&B, which some church audiences found controversial.

music-genres.l06.q3.p: Who wrote and first recorded 'Respect' before Aretha Franklin's 1967 version?
music-genres.l06.q3.e: Otis Redding wrote and recorded 'Respect' in 1965; Franklin's 1967 version transformed it.

music-genres.l06.q4.p: Which label, founded in Detroit in 1959, was known for polished, pop-friendly arrangements?
music-genres.l06.q4.e: Motown, founded by Berry Gordy, used a house band and a polished sound.

music-genres.l06.q5.t: It favored a rawer, horn-driven sound
music-genres.l06.q5.p: How did Stax in Memphis differ from Motown, as described in the lesson?
music-genres.l06.q5.e: Stax became known for raw, horn-driven soul.

music-genres.l07.q1.p: Historians agree on exactly which record was the first rock and roll song.
music-genres.l07.q1.h: The lesson says historians argue about this.
music-genres.l07.q1.e: Because earlier records used similar sounds and the phrase, there is no agreed first record.

music-genres.l07.q2.p: Which Memphis producer at Sun Records recorded Elvis Presley's 'That's All Right' in 1954?
music-genres.l07.q2.e: Sam Phillips recorded Elvis at Sun Records.

music-genres.l07.q3.t: Electric guitar, bass and drums with a strong backbeat
music-genres.l07.q3.p: What core line-up defines the rock and roll sound?
music-genres.l07.q3.e: A guitar, bass and drums band with a hard backbeat is the core.

music-genres.l07.q4.t: How white artists often overshadowed Black pioneers with softer versions
music-genres.l07.q4.p: What does Pat Boone's 1956 cover of 'Tutti Frutti' illustrate?
music-genres.l07.q4.h: The lesson says the story is also about race and money.
music-genres.l07.q4.e: Cover versions by white artists often earned more than the Black originators.

music-genres.l07.q5.p: The British Invasion bands were inspired by American blues and rock and roll.
music-genres.l07.q5.h: Think of the Beatles and the Rolling Stones.
music-genres.l07.q5.e: British bands drew on American records and returned the music to the U.S. in the 1960s.

music-genres.l08.q1.p: Funk focuses more on rhythmic groove than on chord changes.
music-genres.l08.q1.e: Funk builds from short repeating patterns rather than moving harmony.

music-genres.l08.q2.t: The first beat of the measure, given special weight
music-genres.l08.q2.p: What does 'the one' refer to in funk?
music-genres.l08.q2.e: Funk gives extra emphasis to the first beat of each measure.

music-genres.l08.q3.p: Which James Brown record of 1967 is often cited as a turning point toward funk?
music-genres.l08.q3.h: It is mentioned along with 'Papa's Got a Brand New Bag'.
music-genres.l08.q3.e: 'Cold Sweat' is often cited as a key moment in the birth of funk.

music-genres.l08.q4.p: Whose drum break on 'Funky Drummer' became widely sampled in hip-hop?
music-genres.l08.q4.h: He played in James Brown's band.
music-genres.l08.q4.e: Stubblefield's break from the 1969 recording was sampled countless times.

music-genres.l08.q5.e: George Clinton led Parliament and Funkadelic; the Meters were a separate New Orleans band.

music-genres.l09.q1.p: Punk valued speed, short songs and a do-it-yourself attitude.
music-genres.l09.q1.e: Punk rejected showy rock and encouraged anyone to start a band.

music-genres.l09.q2.p: Which New York club is linked to the Ramones and Patti Smith scene?
music-genres.l09.q2.h: Its initials are in the lesson.
music-genres.l09.q2.e: CBGB was the center of New York's 1970s punk scene.

music-genres.l09.q3.p: Which British band blended punk with reggae on London Calling (1979)?
music-genres.l09.q3.h: The album name is a clue.
music-genres.l09.q3.e: The Clash's London Calling mixed punk with reggae and other styles.

music-genres.l09.q4.t: More polished and experimental, often with synthesizers
music-genres.l09.q4.p: What best describes new wave compared with early punk?
music-genres.l09.q4.h: Think of Talking Heads and the Cars.
music-genres.l09.q4.e: New wave bands used catchy melodies, quirks and increasingly synthesizers.

music-genres.l09.q5.t: Independent labels and underground touring circuits
music-genres.l09.q5.p: Which is a lasting legacy of punk named in the lesson?
music-genres.l09.q5.e: Punk's DIY approach fed independent labels and touring networks.

music-genres.l10.q1.p: Black Sabbath released their debut album in 1970.
music-genres.l10.q1.e: Black Sabbath's debut appeared in 1970 and helped define metal.

music-genres.l10.q2.t: A simple two-note chord played with heavy distortion
music-genres.l10.q2.h: It is the signature guitar sound.
music-genres.l10.q2.e: Power chords with distortion are central to metal.

music-genres.l10.q3.p: Which metal style combined punk speed with metal complexity in the early 1980s United States?
music-genres.l10.q3.h: Metallica and Slayer belong to it.
music-genres.l10.q3.e: Thrash metal fused punk speed with metal heaviness.

music-genres.l10.q4.t: The New Wave of British Heavy Metal
music-genres.l10.q4.p: Which movement of around 1980 featured Iron Maiden and twin guitar harmonies?
music-genres.l10.q4.e: Iron Maiden was part of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal.

music-genres.l10.q5.p: What does doom metal do differently from thrash?
music-genres.l10.q5.e: Doom metal is defined by slow, heavy tempos.

music-genres.l11.q1.p: Ska came before rocksteady and reggae.
music-genres.l11.q1.h: The lesson lists three steps in order.
music-genres.l11.q1.e: The order was ska, rocksteady, then reggae.

music-genres.l11.q2.t: A short chop on the offbeats played by guitar or keyboard
music-genres.l11.q2.e: The skank is the offbeat chop that gives reggae its rhythmic feel.

music-genres.l11.q3.t: On the third beat, leaving the first beat quiet
music-genres.l11.q3.p: In the one drop pattern, where does the drum emphasis fall?
music-genres.l11.q3.h: The first beat is left quiet.
music-genres.l11.q3.e: One drop emphasizes the third beat of the measure.

music-genres.l11.q4.t: 'Do the Reggay' by Toots and the Maytals
music-genres.l11.q4.p: Which song is usually linked to the name 'reggae'?
music-genres.l11.q4.e: 'Do the Reggay' is usually linked to the origin of the word.

music-genres.l11.q5.t: The film The Harder They Come and Island Records' Catch a Fire
music-genres.l11.q5.p: What helped introduce reggae to many listeners abroad around 1972 to 1973?
music-genres.l11.q5.h: One is a film starring Jimmy Cliff.
music-genres.l11.q5.e: The 1972 film and the 1973 Island Records release helped globalize reggae.

music-genres.l12.q1.p: A sound system is a mobile rig of turntables, amplifiers and large speakers.
music-genres.l12.q1.e: Sound systems powered Jamaican dances from the 1950s.

music-genres.l12.q2.t: A DJ talking rhythmically over the music
music-genres.l12.q2.e: Toasting is DJs talking over instrumental records, a forerunner of rapping.

music-genres.l12.q3.t: The B-side without the lead vocal
music-genres.l12.q3.p: What was a 'version' in Jamaican records?
music-genres.l12.q3.h: DJs used it to talk over.
music-genres.l12.q3.e: A version was the instrumental B-side, which engineers then remixed into dub.

music-genres.l12.q4.p: Who are two engineers associated with dub's remixing on the console?
music-genres.l12.q4.e: King Tubby and Lee Perry treated the mixing desk as an instrument.

music-genres.l12.q5.t: DJ Kool Herc, born in Kingston, brought it to the Bronx
music-genres.l12.q5.p: How did Jamaican sound-system culture reach hip-hop?
music-genres.l12.q5.h: Think of who moved from Kingston.
music-genres.l12.q5.e: Kool Herc's Jamaican background shaped Bronx party culture.

music-genres.l13.q1.p: Hip-hop began in the early 1970s in the South Bronx.
music-genres.l13.q1.h: The place is in New York City.
music-genres.l13.q1.e: Hip-hop emerged in the South Bronx in the early 1970s.

music-genres.l13.q2.p: Which is NOT one of the four classic elements of hip-hop?
music-genres.l13.q2.h: Think of DJ, MC, dancer and visual artist.
music-genres.l13.q2.e: The four elements are DJing, MCing, breaking and graffiti writing.

music-genres.l13.q3.t: A short drum-only section of a record that is looped
music-genres.l13.q3.h: Kool Herc used two copies of the same record.
music-genres.l13.q3.e: A break is a short percussion section that DJs extend by looping.

music-genres.l13.q4.p: Which 1979 single was the first rap record to become a widespread commercial hit?
music-genres.l13.q4.h: It is by the Sugarhill Gang.
music-genres.l13.q4.e: 'Rapper's Delight' brought rap to a wide commercial audience.

music-genres.l13.q5.t: It showed rap could describe the hardship of city life
music-genres.l13.q5.e: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five used rap for social observation.

music-genres.l14.q1.p: The Roland TR-808 drum machine was released in 1980.
music-genres.l14.q1.e: The 808 appeared in 1980 and became central to hip-hop and trap.

music-genres.l14.q2.t: Record a snippet of existing sound and loop or rearrange it
music-genres.l14.q2.p: What does a sampler allow a producer to do?
music-genres.l14.q2.e: Samplers capture and rework recorded sound.

music-genres.l14.q3.p: Which Dr. Dre album (1992) is linked to West Coast G-funk?
music-genres.l14.q3.h: The title refers to a plant slang word.

music-genres.l14.q4.t: A shift toward licensing samples and paying original artists
music-genres.l14.q4.p: What did the 1991 court case involving Biz Markie contribute to?
music-genres.l14.q4.e: The ruling pushed the industry toward sample clearance.

music-genres.l14.q5.t: Fast hi-hats, heavy 808 bass and dark synthesizers
music-genres.l14.q5.p: Which sound is typical of trap production from Atlanta?
music-genres.l14.q5.e: Trap relies on rapid hi-hats, 808s and dark synths.

music-genres.l15.q1.p: Disco began in the early 1970s in New York clubs.
music-genres.l15.q1.e: Disco grew in New York clubs frequented by Black, Latino and gay communities.

music-genres.l15.q2.t: A kick drum on every beat
music-genres.l15.q2.e: Four-on-the-floor places the kick on each beat.

music-genres.l15.q3.p: Which 1977 track by Donna Summer used synthesizers for the whole backing?
music-genres.l15.q3.e: 'I Feel Love' pointed toward electronic dance music.

music-genres.l15.q4.t: Long instrumental sections for mixing into the next record
music-genres.l15.q4.p: What advantage did the 12-inch single give DJs?
music-genres.l15.q4.e: Longer versions made blending records easier.

music-genres.l15.q5.t: Disco Demolition Night ended in a riot
music-genres.l15.q5.p: What happened on July 12, 1979 at Comiskey Park?
music-genres.l15.q5.e: The event symbolized the disco backlash.

music-genres.l16.q1.p: The name 'house' is commonly traced to the Warehouse club in Chicago.
music-genres.l16.q1.e: The Warehouse is the commonly cited origin of the name.

music-genres.l16.q2.p: Which instrument is central to acid house?
music-genres.l16.q2.h: It makes a squelchy, twisting sound.
music-genres.l16.q2.e: The TB-303 defines acid house's sound.

music-genres.l16.q3.p: Which typical tempo range fits house music?
music-genres.l16.q3.e: House commonly runs from about 118 to 130 BPM.

music-genres.l16.q4.t: So DJs can blend one record into the next
music-genres.l16.q4.p: Why do house tracks have long intros and outros?

music-genres.l16.q5.t: The arrival of house and acid house
music-genres.l16.q5.p: What fueled the British rave scene's Second Summer of Love in 1988?
music-genres.l16.q5.h: It followed house's move to Britain.
music-genres.l16.q5.e: House and acid house spread to Britain in the late 1980s.

music-genres.l17.q1.p: Techno originated in Detroit in the mid-1980s.
music-genres.l17.q1.e: Atkins, May and Saunderson helped create techno in Detroit.

music-genres.l17.q2.p: Which European group influenced the Detroit pioneers?
music-genres.l17.q2.h: It is a German synthesizer band.

music-genres.l17.q3.t: Techno! The New Dance Sound of Detroit
music-genres.l17.q3.p: Which 1988 compilation introduced techno's name to Britain?
music-genres.l17.q3.e: The 1988 compilation presented Detroit techno to British audiences.

music-genres.l17.q4.t: After the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 the city embraced it, and Tresor opened in 1991
music-genres.l17.q4.p: Why did Berlin become important to techno?
music-genres.l17.q4.e: Berlin's post-Wall scene and the Tresor club made it a hub.

music-genres.l17.q5.t: Small shifts in filter, rhythm or texture
music-genres.l17.q5.p: What excites listeners in techno, according to the lesson?
music-genres.l17.q5.e: Techno develops slowly through subtle changes.

music-genres.l18.q1.p: Brian Eno released Ambient 1: Music for Airports in the late 1970s.

music-genres.l18.q2.t: Slowly shifting textures with little or no rhythm
music-genres.l18.q2.e: Ambient uses long tones and slow change.

music-genres.l18.q3.p: Which style features very fast breakbeats and heavy sub-bass, around 160 to 175 BPM?
music-genres.l18.q3.e: Drum and bass is much faster than house or dubstep.

music-genres.l18.q4.t: It emphasizes deep bass and echo-like space in the mix
music-genres.l18.q4.p: Why is dubstep said to owe much to dub?
music-genres.l18.q4.h: Think about bass and studio effects.
music-genres.l18.q4.e: Dubstep inherited dub's heavy bass and sound-shaping.

music-genres.l18.q5.p: Which tool is a handy way to tell electronic styles apart?
music-genres.l18.q5.e: Different styles cluster in different tempo ranges.

music-genres.l19.q1.p: Pop is defined by a single fixed sound.
music-genres.l19.q1.e: Pop keeps borrowing from other genres, so no single sound defines it.

music-genres.l19.q2.p: What launched on August 1, 1981 and changed pop?
music-genres.l19.q2.h: It was a music video channel.
music-genres.l19.q2.e: MTV's launch elevated the music video.

music-genres.l19.q4.p: Which 1998 song brought wide public attention to Auto-Tune as a vocal effect?
music-genres.l19.q4.e: Cher's 'Believe' is a landmark in audible pitch correction.

music-genres.l19.q5.p: How has streaming changed pop songwriting, according to the lesson?

music-genres.l20.q1.p: Salsa took shape in New York City in the 1960s and 1970s.
music-genres.l20.q1.e: Salsa grew among Puerto Rican and Latin American musicians in New York.

music-genres.l20.q2.t: A two-bar five-note rhythmic pattern that organizes the music
music-genres.l20.q2.e: The clave is the rhythmic backbone.

music-genres.l20.q3.p: Which Cuban form is the foundation of salsa?
music-genres.l20.q3.h: It combined Spanish song and African percussion.

music-genres.l20.q4.p: Which label, founded in 1964 by Johnny Pacheco and Jerry Masucci, is most associated with salsa?
music-genres.l20.q4.e: Fania became the label most linked to the salsa movement.

music-genres.l20.q5.t: Some Cubans say it is a commercial label for what they called son
music-genres.l20.q5.p: Why is the word salsa debated?
music-genres.l20.q5.e: Some argue salsa is a marketing term for son.

music-genres.l21.q1.p: Bossa nova means roughly 'new trend' or 'new wave'.
music-genres.l21.q1.e: The name roughly means new trend.

music-genres.l21.q2.p: Who is considered the key figure of bossa nova guitar and singing?
music-genres.l21.q2.e: João Gilberto's guitar pattern and quiet voice defined the style.

music-genres.l21.q3.p: Which form did bossa nova grow from?
music-genres.l21.q3.h: It is Brazil's central popular music.
music-genres.l21.q3.e: Bossa nova slowed and softened samba.

music-genres.l21.q4.p: Which 1964 album included 'The Girl from Ipanema'?

music-genres.l21.q5.t: Antonio Carlos Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes
music-genres.l21.q5.p: Which pair wrote many bossa nova classics?
music-genres.l21.q5.h: One was a composer and one a poet.
music-genres.l21.q5.e: Jobim and de Moraes wrote many classics.

music-genres.l22.q1.p: Tango developed in the late nineteenth century along the Río de la Plata.
music-genres.l22.q1.h: Think of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.
music-genres.l22.q1.e: Tango grew in these port cities.

music-genres.l22.q2.p: Which instrument is tango's signature sound?
music-genres.l22.q2.h: It is a button accordion from Germany.
music-genres.l22.q2.e: The bandoneón's breathy tone defines tango.

music-genres.l22.q3.p: Who became tango's most famous singer in the 1920s and 1930s?
music-genres.l22.q3.h: He is a singer rather than an instrumentalist.

music-genres.l22.q4.t: Nuevo tango blending tradition with jazz and classical music
music-genres.l22.q4.e: Piazzolla's nuevo tango was controversial but later respected.

music-genres.l22.q5.p: UNESCO inscribed the tango of Argentina and Uruguay on its intangible heritage list in 2009.

music-genres.l23.q1.p: Cumbia originates on the Caribbean coast of Colombia.
music-genres.l23.q1.e: Cumbia's traditional roots are in coastal Colombia.

music-genres.l23.q2.p: Which three heritages are traditionally said to combine in cumbia?
music-genres.l23.q2.e: Cumbia blends Indigenous, African and Spanish elements.

music-genres.l23.q3.e: Chicha blended cumbia with electric guitar sounds.

music-genres.l23.q4.t: The same pulse supports many local versions
music-genres.l23.q4.p: What does the lesson mean by 'a genre can be a family tree'?
music-genres.l23.q4.e: Cumbia branched into many local styles.

music-genres.l23.q5.p: Which Argentine style from the late 1990s is a harsher working-class form?
music-genres.l23.q5.h: It begins with the same word as the genre.

music-genres.l24.q1.p: Reggaeton developed mainly in Puerto Rico in the 1990s with roots in Panama and Jamaica.
music-genres.l24.q1.e: Panamanian Spanish reggae and Jamaican sounds were key influences.

music-genres.l24.q2.t: A 1990 Jamaican track by Shabba Ranks
music-genres.l24.q2.p: What is the dembow rhythm named after?
music-genres.l24.q2.e: Shabba Ranks's track supplied the pattern.

music-genres.l24.q3.p: Which accent grouping is described for the dembow snare pattern?
music-genres.l24.q3.h: Count the beats in a measure.
music-genres.l24.q3.e: The pattern is 3+3+2 within the measure.

music-genres.l24.q4.p: Which 2004 hit by Daddy Yankee was a worldwide breakthrough?

music-genres.l24.q5.p: Which 2017 song became one of the most-streamed ever?
music-genres.l24.q5.h: It features Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee.

music-genres.l25.q1.p: Afrobeat was created chiefly by Fela Kuti and Tony Allen.
music-genres.l25.q1.h: Fela led the band; Allen drummed.
music-genres.l25.q1.e: Fela Kuti and drummer Tony Allen are its key creators.

music-genres.l25.q2.t: Highlife, jazz, funk and Yoruba music
music-genres.l25.q2.p: Which genres did Fela blend into Afrobeat?
music-genres.l25.q2.h: He heard James Brown and Nigerian styles.
music-genres.l25.q2.e: Afrobeat is a blend of West African and African American music.

music-genres.l25.q3.p: What happened in 1977 to Fela's compound, the Kalakuta Republic?
music-genres.l25.q3.e: The 1977 attack was a response to his political stance.

music-genres.l25.q4.t: Afrobeats is a broad modern pop umbrella, while Afrobeat is Fela's style
music-genres.l25.q4.p: How do Afrobeat and Afrobeats differ?
music-genres.l25.q4.e: Afrobeats with an s is a modern pop umbrella.

music-genres.l25.q5.t: Long, building from instrumental grooves before the vocal enters
music-genres.l25.q5.p: How are Afrobeat songs typically structured?
music-genres.l25.q5.h: They often last ten minutes or more.

music-genres.l26.q1.p: 'Afropop' was largely a label created by outsiders for diverse styles.
music-genres.l26.q1.h: Africa is not one musical culture.
music-genres.l26.q1.e: The label covers many distinct regional styles.

music-genres.l26.q2.p: Which style developed in Ghana and Nigeria in the early twentieth century, blending local music with brass and guitar?
music-genres.l26.q2.h: E. T. Mensah is linked to it.
music-genres.l26.q2.e: Highlife blended local and imported instruments.

music-genres.l26.q3.h: It is built around sabar drums.
music-genres.l26.q3.e: Youssou N'Dour is mbalax's most famous figure.

music-genres.l26.q4.t: Cuban records mixed with local music, as in Congolese rumba
music-genres.l26.q4.p: Soukous grew from which earlier influence?
music-genres.l26.q4.h: Cuban records were popular in Central Africa.

music-genres.l26.q5.t: It was made during the cultural boycott of apartheid South Africa
music-genres.l26.q5.p: Why was Paul Simon's Graceland (1986) controversial?
music-genres.l26.q5.e: Critics argued it broke the boycott.

music-genres.l27.q1.p: K-pop is a single musical genre.
music-genres.l27.q1.h: A song may switch among styles.
music-genres.l27.q1.e: K-pop mixes pop, hip-hop, R&B and electronic dance music.

music-genres.l27.q2.p: Which group's 1992 debut is often seen as a turning point?
music-genres.l27.q2.h: They blended rap, rock and dance.
music-genres.l27.q2.e: Seo Taiji and Boys changed Korean pop.

music-genres.l27.q3.t: Trainees train for years before debuting in groups
music-genres.l27.q3.e: Companies train young performers before debut.

music-genres.l27.q4.t: First YouTube video to pass one billion views
music-genres.l27.q4.p: What milestone did 'Gangnam Style' reach in 2012?
music-genres.l27.q4.e: It was the first to pass one billion views.

music-genres.l27.q5.t: The Korean Wave, the global spread of Korean pop culture
music-genres.l27.q5.e: Hallyu is the global spread of Korean pop culture.

music-genres.l28.q1.p: Folk music is typically passed on by memory and practice rather than written scores.
music-genres.l28.q1.e: Folk music is communal and orally transmitted.

music-genres.l28.q2.p: Who collected English and Scottish ballads in the late nineteenth century?
music-genres.l28.q2.e: The Child ballads are named for him.

music-genres.l28.q3.t: Made field recordings of performers in many communities
music-genres.l28.q3.p: What did Alan Lomax do for the Library of Congress from the 1930s?

music-genres.l28.q4.p: Which song did Woody Guthrie write in 1940?
music-genres.l28.q4.h: It is about the American land.
music-genres.l28.q4.e: Guthrie wrote 'This Land Is Your Land' in 1940.

music-genres.l28.q5.t: Bob Dylan performed with an electric band
music-genres.l28.q5.e: Dylan's electric set was a famous controversy.

music-history-eras.l01.q1.p: Because no recordings exist, we know about ancient music only through instruments, pictures, texts and a few notated fragments.
music-history-eras.l01.q1.h: Think about what survives from thousands of years ago.
music-history-eras.l01.q1.e: Sound recording is modern, so the ancient world is known through physical remains, writings and a few notated pieces.

music-history-eras.l01.q2.p: The Seikilos epitaph is a short notated song from which ancient culture?
music-history-eras.l01.q2.h: It was carved on a gravestone.
music-history-eras.l01.q2.e: The Seikilos epitaph is an ancient Greek song with notation, from around the first century AD.

music-history-eras.l01.q3.t: One of the oldest notated pieces of music known
music-history-eras.l01.q3.p: A Hurrian hymn on a clay tablet from Ugarit, dated to around 1400 BC, is notable because it is:
music-history-eras.l01.q3.e: The tablet carries signs read as musical notation, making it among the oldest, though its interpretation is debated.

music-history-eras.l01.q4.p: The 65 bronze bells found in the tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng come from ancient:
music-history-eras.l01.q4.h: Look at the name of the tomb.
music-history-eras.l01.q4.e: The bells of Marquis Yi of Zeng, from around 433 BC, are a famous example of Chinese court music.

music-history-eras.l01.q5.p: Scholars agree on exactly how the Hurrian hymn should sound.
music-history-eras.l01.q5.h: Consider whether the notation is easy to decode.
music-history-eras.l01.q5.e: Interpretation of the Hurrian hymn is debated, so there is no single agreed performance.

music-history-eras.l02.q1.p: Gregorian chant is a single unaccompanied melody sung in Latin.
music-history-eras.l02.q1.e: Chant is monophonic, meaning one melodic line with no harmony or instruments.

music-history-eras.l02.q2.e: Hildegard led a convent in Germany and composed a large body of sacred music.

music-history-eras.l02.q3.t: It is traditionally linked to Pope Gregory I, though the repertory grew over centuries
music-history-eras.l02.q3.h: Consider the traditional link and the actual history.
music-history-eras.l02.q3.e: The name honors Gregory I, but historians agree the repertory developed over many generations.

music-history-eras.l02.q4.p: In her sung drama Ordo Virtutum, what is unusual about the devil's part?
music-history-eras.l02.q4.h: Think about how it sets him apart from the virtues.
music-history-eras.l02.q4.e: In Ordo Virtutum the virtues sing but the devil's role is spoken.

music-history-eras.l02.q5.p: Chant was written in the major and minor scales we know today.
music-history-eras.l02.q5.h: What did chant use instead of those scales?
music-history-eras.l02.q5.e: Chant uses modes, which differ from modern major and minor scales.

music-history-eras.l03.q1.p: Neumes were early marks that showed the shape of a melody going up or down.
music-history-eras.l03.q1.h: They were added above the words.
music-history-eras.l03.q1.e: Neumes indicated melodic direction but not exact pitches.

music-history-eras.l03.q2.t: The staff and the naming of notes with syllables
music-history-eras.l03.q2.p: Guido of Arezzo is remembered as a teacher who advanced:
