music-history-eras.l03.q2.e: Guido is associated with lines for pitch and a syllable method that evolved into solfege.

music-history-eras.l03.q3.t: A Latin hymn to St. John
music-history-eras.l03.q3.p: The syllables ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la were taken from:
music-history-eras.l03.q3.h: Each phrase began one step higher.
music-history-eras.l03.q3.e: The syllables come from the opening of a Latin hymn to St. John whose lines rise stepwise.

music-history-eras.l03.q4.p: Which syllable later replaced ut in the solfege system?
music-history-eras.l03.q4.e: Do replaced ut, giving the do-re-mi familiar today.

music-history-eras.l03.q5.p: Notation helped make it possible to write more than one melodic line at a time.
music-history-eras.l03.q5.h: Consider what writing allows composers to plan.
music-history-eras.l03.q5.e: Notation allowed composers to plan multiple lines together, enabling polyphony and composition at a distance.

music-history-eras.l04.q1.p: Notre Dame cathedral in Paris was a center for early polyphony called organum.
music-history-eras.l04.q1.e: Composers at Notre Dame developed organum in the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries.

music-history-eras.l04.q2.p: Which composer is known for organum in three and four voices?
music-history-eras.l04.q2.h: He is linked with Notre Dame.
music-history-eras.l04.q2.e: Perotin is known for writing three- and four-voice organum.

music-history-eras.l04.q3.p: Troubadours were poet-musicians who sang songs of courtly love in:
music-history-eras.l04.q3.h: Think of the earliest, Guilhem IX of Aquitaine.
music-history-eras.l04.q3.e: Troubadours worked in southern France; their northern counterparts were called trouvères.

music-history-eras.l04.q4.t: Ars Nova, a fourteenth-century style with new rhythmic flexibility
music-history-eras.l04.q4.p: Guillaume de Machaut is best known as a figure of:
music-history-eras.l04.q4.e: Machaut, around 1300 to 1377, was the leading composer of the Ars Nova.

music-history-eras.l04.q5.p: Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame is often described as the earliest complete Mass ordinary attributed to a single composer.
music-history-eras.l04.q5.h: Consider why this work is famous.
music-history-eras.l04.q5.e: It is commonly described this way, which makes it a landmark of the fourteenth century.

music-history-eras.l05.q1.p: Ottaviano Petrucci published an early collection of polyphonic songs printed with movable type in Venice in 1501.
music-history-eras.l05.q1.e: Petrucci's Harmonice Musices Odhecaton of 1501 is a famous early printed music collection.

music-history-eras.l05.q2.p: Josquin des Prez was admired as a leading composer of the:
music-history-eras.l05.q2.e: Josquin was widely regarded as the leading composer of his time in the Renaissance.

music-history-eras.l05.q3.t: A secular piece for a few voices that often paints the meaning of words
music-history-eras.l05.q3.p: A madrigal is best described as:
music-history-eras.l05.q3.h: It was often a poem set to music.
music-history-eras.l05.q3.e: Madrigals set poems for a few voices and often illustrate individual words in the music.

music-history-eras.l05.q4.p: Palestrina's church music became a model of:
music-history-eras.l05.q4.h: It was taught to students for centuries.
music-history-eras.l05.q4.e: His smooth, balanced polyphony became a teaching model for counterpoint.

music-history-eras.l05.q5.p: Printing made music cheaper and helped styles travel faster across Europe.
music-history-eras.l05.q5.h: Compare printed copies to hand copying.
music-history-eras.l05.q5.e: Printed copies cost less than manuscripts, which spread music and let amateurs buy it.

music-history-eras.l06.q1.p: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo, first performed in 1607, is regarded as the first great opera.
music-history-eras.l06.q1.e: L'Orfeo is widely regarded as the first great opera.

music-history-eras.l06.q2.p: Opera began around 1600 in which country?
music-history-eras.l06.q2.h: Think of Florence, Mantua and Venice.
music-history-eras.l06.q2.e: Opera arose in Italian cities around 1600.

music-history-eras.l06.q3.t: The first public opera house opened
music-history-eras.l06.q3.h: It meant ticket buyers could attend.
music-history-eras.l06.q3.e: Opening of the first public opera house made opera available to paying audiences.

music-history-eras.l06.q4.t: The earliest surviving opera by a woman
music-history-eras.l06.q4.p: Francesca Caccini's La liberazione di Ruggiero is usually described as:
music-history-eras.l06.q4.e: Caccini's 1625 work is usually described as the earliest surviving opera by a woman.

music-history-eras.l06.q5.p: Barbara Strozzi published volumes of her own vocal music in Venice.
music-history-eras.l06.q5.h: This was unusual for a woman at the time.
music-history-eras.l06.q5.e: Strozzi published several volumes of cantatas and arias under her own name.

music-history-eras.l07.q1.p: Bach and Handel were both born in 1685 in Germany.
music-history-eras.l07.q1.e: Both were born in 1685 in German towns, Bach in Eisenach and Handel in Halle.

music-history-eras.l07.q2.p: Which composer wrote The Four Seasons?
music-history-eras.l07.q2.e: Vivaldi's Four Seasons violin concertos were published in 1725.

music-history-eras.l07.q3.t: A bass line with chords filled in on keyboard or similar instrument
music-history-eras.l07.q3.e: Continuo pairs a bass instrument with a chord-playing instrument such as harpsichord or organ.

music-history-eras.l07.q4.p: Handel's Messiah, a work for chorus and orchestra in English, premiered in:
music-history-eras.l07.q4.e: Messiah first performed in Dublin in 1742.

music-history-eras.l07.q5.p: Purcell's Dido and Aeneas is a Baroque opera by an English composer.
music-history-eras.l07.q5.e: Dido and Aeneas, from around 1689, is a landmark of English opera.

music-history-eras.l08.q1.p: The church was the main patron of music in the Middle Ages.
music-history-eras.l08.q1.e: Monasteries and cathedrals employed singers and fostered notation and polyphony.

music-history-eras.l08.q2.p: Who built the first piano around 1700?
music-history-eras.l08.q2.e: Cristofori's instrument could play soft and loud, hence pianoforte.

music-history-eras.l08.q3.p: Haydn spent decades in the service of which patron family?
music-history-eras.l08.q3.e: Haydn was employed by the Esterhazy family for much of his career.

music-history-eras.l08.q4.p: Which hall opened in Vienna in 1870?
music-history-eras.l08.q4.h: It is named for a music society.
music-history-eras.l08.q4.e: The Musikverein opened in 1870; Carnegie Hall opened in New York in 1891.

music-history-eras.l08.q5.p: Valves for brass instruments in the early nineteenth century made it easier to play all the notes.
music-history-eras.l08.q5.h: Consider the problem of natural horns and trumpets.
music-history-eras.l08.q5.e: Valves allowed brass players to play full scales, and the modern orchestra grew richer.

music-history-eras.l09.q1.p: A symphony usually has four movements.
music-history-eras.l09.q1.e: The Classical symphony typically has four movements.

music-history-eras.l09.q2.p: The three parts of sonata form are:
music-history-eras.l09.q2.h: The themes are presented, played with, and returned.
music-history-eras.l09.q2.e: Sonata form presents themes, develops them, then brings them back.

music-history-eras.l09.q3.p: Haydn is often called the father of the:
music-history-eras.l09.q3.h: He wrote more than one hundred.
music-history-eras.l09.q3.e: Haydn is often called this, though he did not invent either alone.

music-history-eras.l09.q4.e: Mozart wrote The Marriage of Figaro (1786) and The Magic Flute (1791).

music-history-eras.l09.q5.p: The Classical era grew alongside Enlightenment ideas of reason, order and clarity.
music-history-eras.l09.q5.e: Clarity and balance in Classical music reflected Enlightenment ideals.

music-history-eras.l10.q1.p: Beethoven continued to compose after he lost his hearing.
music-history-eras.l10.q1.e: He kept composing, including his Ninth Symphony and late quartets, although he could not hear them.

music-history-eras.l10.q2.p: Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 includes in its last movement:
music-history-eras.l10.q2.e: The finale adds voices singing words from Schiller's Ode to Joy.

music-history-eras.l10.q3.p: Beethoven was born in which city?
music-history-eras.l10.q3.e: He was born in Bonn and moved to Vienna.

music-history-eras.l10.q4.p: How many piano sonatas did Beethoven write?
music-history-eras.l10.q4.h: The number is also standard in the repertory.

music-history-eras.l10.q5.p: Beethoven's Eroica Symphony, from 1804, was shorter and simpler than symphonies before it.
music-history-eras.l10.q5.e: The Eroica was much longer and more dramatic than earlier symphonies.

music-history-eras.l11.q1.p: Franz Schubert wrote more than 600 songs for voice and piano.
music-history-eras.l11.q1.e: Schubert composed more than 600 Lieder in his short life.

music-history-eras.l11.q2.e: Chopin's music is for piano: nocturnes, etudes, waltzes, mazurkas and polonaises.

music-history-eras.l11.q3.t: A one-movement orchestral work based on a story or idea
music-history-eras.l11.q3.p: Liszt created the symphonic poem, which is:
music-history-eras.l11.q3.e: The symphonic poem is a single-movement orchestral piece tied to a story or image.

music-history-eras.l11.q4.p: Robert Schumann and Clara Wieck married in:
music-history-eras.l11.q4.h: It was early in the Romantic period.

music-history-eras.l11.q5.p: Schubert's Winterreise is a cycle of 24 songs on poems by Wilhelm Muller.
music-history-eras.l11.q5.h: It is a famous song cycle.

music-history-eras.l12.q1.p: Brahms's A German Requiem uses German texts rather than the traditional Latin Mass.
music-history-eras.l12.q1.h: The title hints at the language.
music-history-eras.l12.q1.e: Brahms chose German Biblical texts for his Requiem.

music-history-eras.l12.q2.e: Verdi wrote Rigoletto, La traviata and Aida.

music-history-eras.l12.q3.t: A short musical idea linked to a character, object or idea
music-history-eras.l12.q3.e: Wagner used leitmotifs that return and change through an opera.

music-history-eras.l12.q4.p: Wagner's Ring cycle was first performed complete in 1876 at:
music-history-eras.l12.q4.h: He had a theater built for it.
music-history-eras.l12.q4.e: The Festspielhaus at Bayreuth opened for the first complete Ring in 1876.

music-history-eras.l12.q5.p: Verdi and Wagner were both born in 1813.
music-history-eras.l12.q5.e: Verdi and Wagner were both born in 1813.

music-history-eras.l13.q1.p: Musical nationalism uses folk songs, dances and stories of a composer's homeland.
music-history-eras.l13.q1.h: It is tied to national identity.
music-history-eras.l13.q1.e: Nationalist composers drew on national and folk traditions.

music-history-eras.l13.q2.h: He wrote it while living in New York.
music-history-eras.l13.q2.e: It premiered in 1893 during his stay in the United States.

music-history-eras.l13.q3.p: Grieg composed incidental music for a play by:
music-history-eras.l13.q3.e: Grieg wrote music for Ibsen's Peer Gynt.

music-history-eras.l13.q4.p: Who orchestrated Mussorgsky's piano suite Pictures at an Exhibition in 1922?
music-history-eras.l13.q4.e: Ravel's orchestration is the version most often heard.

music-history-eras.l13.q5.p: Tchaikovsky composed the ballets Swan Lake and The Nutcracker.
music-history-eras.l13.q5.e: Tchaikovsky wrote Swan Lake, The Sleeping Beauty and The Nutcracker.

music-history-eras.l14.q1.p: Hildegard of Bingen is among the earliest composers in Western history whose name and music are firmly documented.
music-history-eras.l14.q1.h: She lived in the twelfth century.
music-history-eras.l14.q1.e: Hildegard's music survives in large quantity with her name attached.

music-history-eras.l14.q2.p: Francesca Caccini worked at the court of which family in Florence?
music-history-eras.l14.q2.h: It was a famous banking family.
music-history-eras.l14.q2.e: She served at the Medici court as a singer, teacher and composer.

music-history-eras.l14.q3.t: Cantatas and arias, published under her own name
music-history-eras.l14.q3.p: Barbara Strozzi is best known for:
music-history-eras.l14.q3.e: She published several volumes of vocal music.

music-history-eras.l14.q4.t: Limited access to training, church posts and public performance
music-history-eras.l14.q4.p: Which was a common barrier faced by women composers in earlier centuries?
music-history-eras.l14.q4.e: Social and institutional limits made it hard to train and publish as professionals.

music-history-eras.l14.q5.p: Hildegard, Caccini and Strozzi all lived in the same century.
music-history-eras.l14.q5.e: Hildegard lived in the twelfth century, while Caccini and Strozzi lived in the seventeenth.

music-history-eras.l15.q1.p: Fanny Mendelssohn Hensel was the older sister of Felix Mendelssohn.
music-history-eras.l15.q1.e: Fanny was born in 1805 and Felix in 1809.

music-history-eras.l15.q2.p: Clara Wieck Schumann was famous as a:
music-history-eras.l15.q2.e: Clara was one of the leading pianists of her century and also composed.

music-history-eras.l15.q3.p: Amy Beach's Gaelic Symphony premiered in:

music-history-eras.l15.q4.p: Florence Price's Symphony No. 1 was played in 1933 by the:
music-history-eras.l15.q4.e: The Chicago Symphony performed it in 1933.

music-history-eras.l15.q5.p: Florence Price blended Romantic style with spirituals and dance rhythms.
music-history-eras.l15.q5.h: Think about her African American heritage.
music-history-eras.l15.q5.e: Her music draws on spirituals and dance rhythms in a Romantic framework.

music-history-eras.l16.q1.p: The term Impressionism first came from painting.
music-history-eras.l16.q1.e: It was borrowed from painting and applied to music by critics.

music-history-eras.l16.q2.p: Debussy's Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun dates from:
music-history-eras.l16.q2.h: It is at the turn of the twentieth century.

music-history-eras.l16.q3.t: Divides the octave into six equal steps
music-history-eras.l16.q3.e: It is a scale of six notes each a whole step apart.

music-history-eras.l16.q4.p: Debussy heard which ensemble at the Paris Exposition of 1889?
music-history-eras.l16.q4.e: Javanese gamelan at the 1889 Exposition influenced his sense of color and texture.

music-history-eras.l16.q5.p: Debussy enthusiastically embraced the label Impressionist for his music.

music-history-eras.l17.q1.p: The Rite of Spring was first performed in Paris in 1913.
music-history-eras.l17.q1.h: It was staged by the Ballets Russes.

music-history-eras.l17.q2.e: Atonal music has no home key.

music-history-eras.l17.q3.p: Schoenberg developed the twelve-tone method in the:
music-history-eras.l17.q3.e: He formulated the method in the early 1920s.

music-history-eras.l17.q4.p: The Second Viennese School consisted of Schoenberg and his students:
music-history-eras.l17.q4.e: Alban Berg and Anton Webern were Schoenberg's students.

music-history-eras.l17.q5.p: Stravinsky wrote The Firebird before The Rite of Spring.
music-history-eras.l17.q5.e: The Firebird is from 1910, The Rite of Spring from 1913.

music-history-eras.l18.q1.p: Spirituals were created by enslaved African Americans.
music-history-eras.l18.q1.e: Spirituals arose among enslaved people in the American South.

music-history-eras.l18.q2.p: The Fisk Jubilee Singers were formed in:
music-history-eras.l18.q2.e: They formed at Fisk University in Nashville in 1871.

music-history-eras.l18.q3.p: Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag was published in:
music-history-eras.l18.q3.h: It was a major sheet music hit.

music-history-eras.l18.q4.p: A typical blues form lasts how many bars?
music-history-eras.l18.q4.e: The standard blues has twelve bars.

music-history-eras.l18.q5.p: Blue notes are bent pitches between the usual piano notes.
music-history-eras.l18.q5.h: They give the blues its sound.
music-history-eras.l18.q5.e: Blue notes are pitches bent between standard scale notes.

music-history-eras.l19.q1.p: Improvisation is a central feature of jazz.
music-history-eras.l19.q1.h: Players invent melodies on the spot.
music-history-eras.l19.q1.e: Jazz values improvised solos over a harmonic framework.

music-history-eras.l19.q2.p: Which city is a famous early center of jazz?
music-history-eras.l19.q2.e: New Orleans was an early center of jazz.

music-history-eras.l19.q3.p: Duke Ellington was known as a:
music-history-eras.l19.q3.h: He led an orchestra for decades.
music-history-eras.l19.q3.e: Ellington composed for his orchestra and treated jazz as composer's art.

music-history-eras.l19.q4.p: Thomas A. Dorsey is widely called the father of:
music-history-eras.l19.q4.h: He wrote Precious Lord, Take My Hand.
music-history-eras.l19.q4.e: Dorsey is widely called the father of gospel music.

music-history-eras.l19.q5.p: Gospel combines spirituals with blues-influenced feeling and rhythm.
music-history-eras.l19.q5.e: Gospel draws on both spirituals and blues-influenced style.

music-history-eras.l20.q1.p: Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue premiered in 1924.
music-history-eras.l20.q1.e: The premiere took place in 1924 with Gershwin at the piano.

music-history-eras.l20.q2.p: Charles Ives earned his living in:
music-history-eras.l20.q2.e: Ives worked in the insurance business.

music-history-eras.l20.q3.p: Copland's Appalachian Spring uses which Shaker tune?
music-history-eras.l20.q3.e: Copland quoted Simple Gifts in Appalachian Spring.

music-history-eras.l20.q4.p: Porgy and Bess is an opera by:
music-history-eras.l20.q4.e: Gershwin wrote Porgy and Bess in 1935.

music-history-eras.l20.q5.p: Ives's music sometimes layers different rhythms or keys at the same time.
music-history-eras.l20.q5.e: Ives layered hymns, marches and folk tunes in simultaneous rhythms and keys.

music-history-eras.l21.q1.p: Cage's 4'33" asks the performer to play no notes for four minutes and thirty-three seconds.
music-history-eras.l21.q1.e: The performer plays nothing so that ambient sound becomes the music.

music-history-eras.l21.q2.e: Cage placed objects between strings to change the sound.

music-history-eras.l21.q3.p: Who gave the first performance of 4'33" in 1952?

music-history-eras.l21.q4.p: Which Chinese text did Cage use for chance procedures?
music-history-eras.l21.q4.h: It is a book of changes.
music-history-eras.l21.q4.e: He used the I Ching to make chance decisions.

music-history-eras.l21.q5.p: Cage and the serialists such as Boulez both favored total control of every detail.
music-history-eras.l21.q5.e: Cage embraced chance, the opposite of serial control.

music-history-eras.l22.q1.p: Minimalism builds music from repeating patterns that change gradually.
music-history-eras.l22.q1.e: Repetition and slow change define minimalism.

music-history-eras.l22.q2.t: Two identical patterns slowly drift out of sync
music-history-eras.l22.q2.p: Phasing is the technique in which:
music-history-eras.l22.q2.h: It appears in It's Gonna Rain.
music-history-eras.l22.q2.e: Phasing makes identical loops shift against each other.

music-history-eras.l22.q3.p: Who wrote the opera Einstein on the Beach with Robert Wilson?
music-history-eras.l22.q3.e: Philip Glass created it with Robert Wilson.

music-history-eras.l22.q4.p: Terry Riley's In C dates from:

music-history-eras.l22.q5.p: Reich traveled to Ghana in 1970 to study drumming.
music-history-eras.l22.q5.e: He studied drumming in Ghana in 1970.

music-history-eras.l23.q1.p: Bartok and Kodaly collected folk songs in villages.
music-history-eras.l23.q1.e: They gathered folk songs in the early twentieth century.

music-history-eras.l23.q2.p: Ravi Shankar is famous as a player of the:
music-history-eras.l23.q2.h: He is an Indian classical musician.

music-history-eras.l23.q3.p: George Harrison used a sitar on the Beatles' song:
music-history-eras.l23.q3.e: Harrison played sitar on Norwegian Wood.

music-history-eras.l23.q4.e: It studies music within its culture.

music-history-eras.l23.q5.p: Cross-cultural borrowing in music never raises questions of credit or payment.
music-history-eras.l23.q5.e: Credit, payment and respect are real, debated questions.

music-history-eras.l24.q1.p: Thomas Edison demonstrated the phonograph in 1877.

music-history-eras.l24.q2.p: Emile Berliner is associated with the:
music-history-eras.l24.q2.e: Berliner developed the disc and gramophone.

music-history-eras.l24.q3.p: Electrical recording with microphones became standard in the:
music-history-eras.l24.q3.e: Microphones became standard in the mid-1920s.

music-history-eras.l24.q4.p: The LP was introduced by Columbia in:
music-history-eras.l24.q4.h: It held about twenty minutes a side.
music-history-eras.l24.q4.e: Columbia introduced the long-playing record in 1948.

music-history-eras.l24.q5.p: Multitrack recording let producers record parts separately and mix them later.
music-history-eras.l24.q5.e: Multitrack tape made layered studio production possible.

music-history-eras.l25.q1.p: Silent films were usually shown with live music.
music-history-eras.l25.q1.e: Pianists, organists or orchestras accompanied silent films.

music-history-eras.l25.q2.p: Which film from 1927 introduced sound to feature films?
music-history-eras.l25.q2.e: The Jazz Singer led the move to sound.

music-history-eras.l25.q4.p: Bernard Herrmann's Psycho score is famous for:
music-history-eras.l25.q4.e: The score uses strings alone for terror.

music-history-eras.l25.q5.p: John Williams used themes for characters in Star Wars in the manner of Wagner's leitmotifs.
music-history-eras.l25.q5.e: Williams linked themes to characters in 1977.

music-history-eras.l26.q1.p: The theremin is played without touching the instrument.
music-history-eras.l26.q1.e: The performer's hands control pitch and volume near two antennas.

music-history-eras.l26.q2.e: It manipulates recorded sounds, for example by tape editing.

music-history-eras.l26.q3.p: Switched-On Bach (1968) was performed on a:

music-history-eras.l26.q4.h: It lets instruments and computers talk.

music-history-eras.l26.q5.p: A digital audio workstation is software for recording and editing music on a computer.
music-history-eras.l26.q5.h: It put a studio into a laptop.
music-history-eras.l26.q5.e: That is the definition of a DAW.

music-history-eras.l27.q1.p: Hip-hop began in the Bronx, New York, in the 1970s.
music-history-eras.l27.q1.e: DJs at Bronx parties began the culture.

music-history-eras.l27.q2.t: Extending instrumental breaks using two copies of a record
music-history-eras.l27.q2.e: Using two copies lets the break repeat for dancers.

music-history-eras.l27.q3.p: Rapper's Delight, released in 1979, was by:
music-history-eras.l27.q3.e: The Sugarhill Gang released it in 1979.

music-history-eras.l27.q4.e: It supplied a deep bass drum and snare.

music-history-eras.l27.q5.p: A sampler records snippets of sound that producers replay in new tracks.
music-history-eras.l27.q5.e: Samplers let producers build tracks from pieces of recordings.

music-history-eras.l28.q1.p: Printing helped spread musical styles across Europe starting with Petrucci in 1501.
music-history-eras.l28.q1.e: Printed music spread widely and quickly.

music-history-eras.l28.q2.p: Which sequence matches changing music patrons in Europe?
music-history-eras.l28.q2.e: Patronage moved from church to court to the paying public.

music-history-eras.l28.q3.p: Which pair shows borrowing across traditions in this course?
music-history-eras.l28.q3.e: Spirituals and blues fed jazz, gospel and later styles.

music-history-eras.l28.q4.t: New tools, audiences and ideas meet
music-history-eras.l28.q4.p: Which is the best summary of how music changes?
music-history-eras.l28.q4.h: Look at the pattern of the course.
music-history-eras.l28.q4.e: The course shows technology, patrons and ideas shaping music together.

music-history-eras.l28.q5.p: Women composers and Black musicians created major work, often with fewer opportunities.
music-history-eras.l28.q5.e: Recovering these stories is still ongoing work.

music-theory-college.l01.q1.p: In first species counterpoint, each note of the counterpoint is set against exactly one note of the cantus firmus.
music-theory-college.l01.q1.h: The name of the species describes the ratio of notes.
music-theory-college.l01.q1.e: First species is note against note, so the ratio is one to one.

music-theory-college.l01.q2.p: In strict two-voice species counterpoint, which interval is treated as a dissonance?
music-theory-college.l01.q2.h: Consider which of these is traditionally avoided between two voices.
music-theory-college.l01.q2.e: Strict two-voice writing treats the perfect fourth as a dissonance, while thirds, sixths, fifths and octaves are consonances.

music-theory-college.l01.q3.p: A cantus firmus in D Dorian ends E to D with the counterpoint above. Which penultimate note is standard?
music-theory-college.l01.q3.h: The penultimate interval above E should be a major sixth.
music-theory-college.l01.q3.e: C-sharp is a major sixth above E and steps up to D, forming an octave at the close.

music-theory-college.l01.q4.p: Parallel perfect fifths between two voices are permitted in strict first species as long as the notes are consonant.
music-theory-college.l01.q4.h: Independence of voices is the aim.
music-theory-college.l01.q4.e: Parallel perfect fifths and octaves are forbidden because they reduce the independence of the voices.

music-theory-college.l01.q5.p: The cantus firmus moves C to D while the counterpoint above moves G to A. What is the error?
music-theory-college.l01.q5.h: Find the interval at each moment.
music-theory-college.l01.q5.e: G over C is a fifth and A over D is also a fifth, so the lines move in parallel perfect fifths.

music-theory-college.l02.q1.p: Which species is built on syncopation and suspensions?
music-theory-college.l02.q1.h: Notes are tied across the barline.
music-theory-college.l02.q1.e: Fourth species ties notes across the barline so that prepared dissonances appear on the strong beat.

music-theory-college.l02.q2.p: In second species, the strong beat may be dissonant as long as the weak beat is consonant.
music-theory-college.l02.q2.e: In second species, the strong beat must be consonant, and dissonance is allowed only on the weak beat as a passing tone.

music-theory-college.l02.q3.p: In fourth species, how should a suspended dissonance resolve?
music-theory-college.l02.q3.e: The suspended dissonance resolves down by step, as in the 7-6 and 4-3 suspensions.

music-theory-college.l02.q4.p: How many counterpoint notes sound against each cantus firmus note in third species?
music-theory-college.l02.q4.h: The species number does not equal the ratio here.
music-theory-college.l02.q4.e: Third species uses four notes against one.

music-theory-college.l02.q5.p: Fifth species combines the techniques of the earlier four species.
music-theory-college.l02.q5.e: Florid counterpoint mixes note values and techniques from species one through four, with decoration added.

music-theory-college.l03.q1.p: Which note is the final of the Phrygian mode on the white keys?
music-theory-college.l03.q1.h: The scale runs E to E.
music-theory-college.l03.q1.e: The white-key Phrygian mode runs from E to E and has the final E.

music-theory-college.l03.q2.p: In Palestrina-style polyphony, the melodic lines move mostly by step.
music-theory-college.l03.q2.e: The style favors stepwise motion with leaps balanced by stepwise motion in the opposite direction.

music-theory-college.l03.q3.p: Which white-key mode has the final F?
music-theory-college.l03.q3.h: Recall the white-key finals D, E, F, G.
music-theory-college.l03.q3.e: Lydian runs from F to F on the white keys.

music-theory-college.l03.q4.p: A plagal mode has the same final as its authentic partner but a range roughly a fourth lower.
music-theory-college.l03.q4.e: Authentic and plagal partners share a final, while the plagal range lies about a fourth lower.

music-theory-college.l03.q5.p: At a Dorian cadence on D, singers customarily raise which note?
music-theory-college.l03.q5.h: The note a step below the final is raised.
music-theory-college.l03.q5.e: Musica ficta raises C to C-sharp, creating a leading tone to the final D.

music-theory-college.l04.q1.p: In a fugue exposition, the answer normally states the subject at which pitch level?
music-theory-college.l04.q1.h: Entries alternate between tonic and one other degree.
music-theory-college.l04.q1.e: The answer is typically at the dominant, a fifth above or a fourth below the subject.

music-theory-college.l04.q2.p: A countersubject typically accompanies the answer as the first voice continues.
music-theory-college.l04.q2.h: The first voice does not stop when the second enters.
music-theory-college.l04.q2.e: The first voice continues with the countersubject while the answer is stated.

music-theory-college.l04.q3.t: Entries of the subject overlapping before it ends
music-theory-college.l04.q3.p: What is stretto in a fugue?
music-theory-college.l04.q3.e: In stretto, a new entry of the subject begins before the previous one has finished.

music-theory-college.l04.q4.p: A tonal answer is always an exact transposition of the subject.
music-theory-college.l04.q4.h: The answer may be adjusted to stay in the home key.
music-theory-college.l04.q4.e: A tonal answer adjusts some intervals, so it is not an exact transposition; an exact one is a real answer.

music-theory-college.l04.q5.t: Two books of prelude and fugue pairs in all 24 keys
music-theory-college.l04.q5.p: What does Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier contain?
music-theory-college.l04.q5.h: Think of a pair in each major and minor key.
music-theory-college.l04.q5.e: Each of the two books has 24 preludes and fugues, one pair in each major and minor key.

music-theory-college.l05.q1.p: Over a bass note G with the figure 6 and no accidentals in the key signature, which pitches form the chord?
music-theory-college.l05.q1.h: A figure 6 means a sixth and a third above the bass.
music-theory-college.l05.q1.e: The sixth above G is E and the third is B, giving a first-inversion E minor triad.

music-theory-college.l05.q2.p: A bass note C is figured 6/4 with no accidentals. Which chord is it?
music-theory-college.l05.q2.h: Find the fourth and sixth above C.
music-theory-college.l05.q2.e: The fourth above C is F and the sixth is A, so the notes C, F, A form an F major triad with C in the bass.

music-theory-college.l05.q3.p: A bass note with no figure normally implies a root-position triad.
music-theory-college.l05.q3.e: An absent figure is read as 5/3, a root-position triad.

music-theory-college.l05.q4.h: Seventh chords add a 5 in the first inversion.
music-theory-college.l05.q4.e: The figure 6/5 stands for a first-inversion seventh chord, with sixth and fifth above the bass.

music-theory-college.l05.q5.p: Basso continuo normally involves a bass-line instrument together with a chord-playing instrument.
music-theory-college.l05.q5.e: The continuo group pairs a bass instrument with a chordal one, such as a keyboard or lute.

music-theory-college.l06.q1.p: In a G7 chord moving to C major, how does the chordal seventh F normally resolve?
music-theory-college.l06.q1.e: The seventh of a dominant seventh resolves down by step, F to E here.

music-theory-college.l06.q2.p: The leading tone is normally not doubled in four-part writing.
music-theory-college.l06.q2.h: Doubling would give parallel octaves on resolution.
music-theory-college.l06.q2.e: A doubled leading tone would rise in parallel octaves, so it is avoided.

music-theory-college.l06.q3.t: Soprano-alto and alto-tenor within an octave
music-theory-college.l06.q3.p: Which spacing guideline applies to the upper three voices in SATB writing?
music-theory-college.l06.q3.e: Adjacent upper voices should be within an octave, while a wider gap between tenor and bass is acceptable.

music-theory-college.l06.q4.t: A voice moving past the previous pitch of a neighboring voice
music-theory-college.l06.q4.h: It is related to, but not the same as, voice crossing.
music-theory-college.l06.q4.e: In overlap, a voice moves beyond the earlier note of an adjacent voice, though the voices have not crossed.

music-theory-college.l06.q5.p: Contrary motion between the outer voices helps avoid parallel perfect intervals.
music-theory-college.l06.q5.e: Contrary motion avoids parallel fifths and octaves and keeps the voices independent.

music-theory-college.l07.q1.p: Which progression is a deceptive cadence?
music-theory-college.l07.q1.h: The submediant substitutes for the tonic.
music-theory-college.l07.q1.e: A deceptive cadence is V moving to vi.

music-theory-college.l07.q2.p: A half cadence ends on the dominant chord.
music-theory-college.l07.q2.e: A half cadence closes a phrase on V.

music-theory-college.l07.q3.t: V to I in root position with tonic in the soprano
music-theory-college.l07.q3.p: Which conditions make a perfect authentic cadence?
music-theory-college.l07.q3.e: A PAC requires both chords in root position and the tonic note on top of the final chord.

music-theory-college.l07.q4.p: In a Phrygian half cadence in C minor, how does the bass move?
music-theory-college.l07.q4.h: The progression is iv6 to V.
music-theory-college.l07.q4.e: iv6 in C minor has A-flat in the bass, which falls by a half step to G, the root of V.

music-theory-college.l07.q5.p: A sentence begins with a presentation in which a basic idea is stated and repeated.
music-theory-college.l07.q5.e: In a sentence, a basic idea and its repetition form the presentation, followed by a continuation.

music-theory-college.l08.q1.p: Which notes form V/V in C major?
music-theory-college.l08.q1.h: It is the dominant of G.
music-theory-college.l08.q1.e: The dominant of G is D major, spelled D, F-sharp, A.

music-theory-college.l08.q2.p: Which notes form V7/vi in C major?
music-theory-college.l08.q2.h: The vi chord is A minor, and its dominant is E.
music-theory-college.l08.q2.e: The dominant seventh of A minor is E7: E, G-sharp, B, D.

music-theory-college.l08.q3.p: The diminished triad vii° is normally not tonicized.
music-theory-college.l08.q3.h: A tonicized chord must be able to sound stable.
music-theory-college.l08.q3.e: Its diminished fifth makes vii° unable to function as a temporary tonic.

music-theory-college.l08.q4.p: Which chord is V7/IV in G major?
music-theory-college.l08.q4.h: The IV chord is C, and its dominant is G.
music-theory-college.l08.q4.e: V7/IV is G7, G, B, D and F natural, where the F natural is the sign of the tonicization of C.

music-theory-college.l08.q5.p: A tonicization is typically briefer than a modulation and does not establish a new key.
music-theory-college.l08.q5.e: Tonicization emphasizes a chord briefly, while a modulation confirms a new key.

music-theory-college.l09.q1.p: In a modulation from C major to G major, what function does the A minor chord have in G?
music-theory-college.l09.q1.h: A is the second note of G major.
music-theory-college.l09.q1.e: A minor is vi in C major and ii in G major, making it a good pivot chord.

music-theory-college.l09.q2.p: Which key is closely related to C major?
music-theory-college.l09.q2.h: Closely related keys differ by at most one accidental.
music-theory-college.l09.q2.e: A minor shares the key signature with C major, so it is closely related.

music-theory-college.l09.q3.p: The fully diminished seventh chord is often used for enharmonic modulation because it can be respelled to resolve to different keys.
music-theory-college.l09.q3.h: Its symmetrical structure is the reason.
music-theory-college.l09.q3.e: Its equal minor-third spacing allows several respellings and resolutions.

music-theory-college.l09.q4.t: One that links chords by a shared pitch
music-theory-college.l09.q4.e: A shared pitch connects the two chords, even when no pivot chord exists.

music-theory-college.l09.q5.p: The C major tonic chord functions as IV in G major and can serve as a pivot chord.
music-theory-college.l09.q5.h: C is the fourth degree of G major.
music-theory-college.l09.q5.e: C major is I in C and IV in G, so it can pivot between the two keys.

music-theory-college.l10.q1.p: Which chord is the lowered submediant, bVI, in C major?
music-theory-college.l10.q1.h: It is built on the lowered sixth degree.
music-theory-college.l10.q1.e: The bVI chord in C is A-flat major: A-flat, C and E-flat.

music-theory-college.l10.q2.p: Which notes form the borrowed iv chord in C major?
music-theory-college.l10.q2.h: It comes from the parallel minor.
music-theory-college.l10.q2.e: The iv chord from C minor is F, A-flat, C.

music-theory-college.l10.q3.p: A Picardy third is a major tonic chord at the end of a minor-key passage.
music-theory-college.l10.q3.h: The third of the final chord is raised.
music-theory-college.l10.q3.e: The Picardy third ends a minor piece on a major tonic.

music-theory-college.l10.q4.p: Mixture chords are borrowed from the relative minor, not the parallel minor.
music-theory-college.l10.q4.e: Mixture chords come from the parallel mode with the same tonic, not the relative one.

music-theory-college.l10.q5.p: Which notes form bIII in C major?
music-theory-college.l10.q5.h: It is built on the lowered mediant.
music-theory-college.l10.q5.e: bIII is E-flat major: E-flat, G and B-flat.

music-theory-college.l11.q1.p: Which notes make up the Neapolitan sixth in C minor, from the bass upward?
music-theory-college.l11.q1.h: It is the first inversion of bII.
music-theory-college.l11.q1.e: N6 in C minor is D-flat major in first inversion, with F in the bass.

music-theory-college.l11.q2.p: The Neapolitan chord normally functions as a predominant.
music-theory-college.l11.q2.e: N6 normally precedes V or a cadential 6/4, acting as a predominant.

music-theory-college.l11.q3.p: Which notes form the Neapolitan chord in A minor?
music-theory-college.l11.q3.h: It is built on the lowered second degree.
music-theory-college.l11.q3.e: The lowered second degree in A minor is B-flat, so the chord is B-flat, D and F.

music-theory-college.l11.q4.t: V or cadential 6/4 leading to V
music-theory-college.l11.q4.p: The Neapolitan sixth most commonly resolves to which chord?
music-theory-college.l11.q4.e: It typically goes to the dominant, either directly or by the cadential 6/4.

music-theory-college.l11.q5.p: The Neapolitan chord is normally used in root position.
music-theory-college.l11.q5.h: The N6 label gives it away.
music-theory-college.l11.q5.e: It is usually in first inversion, so it is labeled N6.

music-theory-college.l12.q1.p: Which notes form the German augmented sixth chord in C minor?
music-theory-college.l12.q1.h: It adds the lowered third degree to the Italian sixth.
music-theory-college.l12.q1.e: The German sixth in C minor is A-flat, C, E-flat and F-sharp.

music-theory-college.l12.q2.p: Which notes form the French augmented sixth chord in C minor?
music-theory-college.l12.q2.h: It adds the second scale degree.
music-theory-college.l12.q2.e: The French sixth in C minor is A-flat, C, D and F-sharp.

music-theory-college.l12.q3.p: The Italian sixth has only three distinct pitch classes.
music-theory-college.l12.q3.e: The Italian sixth contains A-flat, C and F-sharp, with C doubled.

music-theory-college.l12.q4.p: To which pitch do the outer voices of an augmented sixth resolve in C minor?
music-theory-college.l12.q4.h: They move outward to the dominant.
music-theory-college.l12.q4.e: A-flat falls to G and F-sharp rises to G, forming an octave.

music-theory-college.l12.q5.p: A German augmented sixth chord is enharmonically equivalent to a dominant seventh chord.
music-theory-college.l12.q5.e: A-flat, C, E-flat and F-sharp is enharmonic to A-flat, C, E-flat, G-flat, a dominant seventh chord.

music-theory-college.l13.q1.p: Which triads are chromatic mediants of C major?
music-theory-college.l13.q1.h: The roots lie a third apart, with the same quality.
music-theory-college.l13.q1.e: E major and A-flat major are major triads a third away from C major.

music-theory-college.l13.q2.p: Which pitch do C major and E major triads share?
music-theory-college.l13.q2.h: Compare C, E, G with E, G-sharp, B.
music-theory-college.l13.q2.e: C, E, G and E, G-sharp, B share only the note E.

music-theory-college.l13.q3.p: Which notes make up a dominant ninth chord on G?
music-theory-college.l13.q3.h: It is a dominant seventh with a ninth.
music-theory-college.l13.q3.e: The chord is G, B, D, F and A.

music-theory-college.l13.q4.p: A G7 chord with a flat ninth contains A-flat.
music-theory-college.l13.q4.h: The ninth is a step above the octave.
music-theory-college.l13.q4.e: The ninth above G is A, and lowering it gives A-flat.

music-theory-college.l13.q5.p: Which notes form G7 with a raised fifth?
music-theory-college.l13.q5.h: The fifth of G is D.
music-theory-college.l13.q5.e: Raising the fifth D to D-sharp gives G, B, D-sharp and F.

music-theory-college.l14.q1.p: In a major-key Classical sonata exposition, in which key is the secondary theme usually stated?
music-theory-college.l14.q1.h: The exposition moves away from home.
music-theory-college.l14.q1.e: The secondary theme is typically in the dominant in major-key movements.

music-theory-college.l14.q2.p: In a minor-key exposition, the secondary theme is usually in which key?
music-theory-college.l14.q2.h: It is a key sharing the signature.
music-theory-college.l14.q2.e: It is usually in the relative major (III).

music-theory-college.l14.q3.p: The transition in an exposition typically modulates toward the key of the secondary theme.
music-theory-college.l14.q3.e: The transition leads away from the tonic to prepare the new key.

music-theory-college.l14.q4.p: A Classical sonata exposition normally ends in the tonic key.
music-theory-college.l14.q4.e: It ends in the contrasting key, and the recapitulation resolves the conflict.

music-theory-college.l14.q5.t: A break dividing the transition from the secondary theme
music-theory-college.l14.q5.h: It is a pause in the middle of the exposition.
music-theory-college.l14.q5.e: The medial caesura is a break that divides the transition and the secondary theme.

music-theory-college.l15.q1.p: In a typical recapitulation, in which key does the secondary theme appear?
music-theory-college.l15.q1.e: The secondary theme returns in the tonic, achieving tonal resolution.

music-theory-college.l15.q2.p: A development section often fragments and sequences motives from the exposition.
music-theory-college.l15.q2.h: It is the least constrained section.
music-theory-college.l15.q2.e: Fragmentation, sequence and modulation are typical development techniques.

music-theory-college.l15.q3.t: The dominant of the home key
music-theory-college.l15.q3.p: A retransition usually prepares the recapitulation by emphasizing which harmony?
music-theory-college.l15.q3.h: It builds tension before the tonic returns.
music-theory-college.l15.q3.e: The retransition typically lingers on the dominant of the home key.

music-theory-college.l15.q4.p: A coda follows the closing material of the recapitulation.
music-theory-college.l15.q4.e: A coda is an added section after the recapitulation that reinforces the home key.

music-theory-college.l15.q5.p: What is the usual order of the three main sections of sonata form?
music-theory-college.l15.q5.h: The tonal story moves from conflict to resolution.
music-theory-college.l15.q5.e: The exposition comes first, then the development, then the recapitulation.

music-theory-college.l16.q1.t: The Urlinie and the bass arpeggiation
music-theory-college.l16.q1.p: What are the two components of the Ursatz?
music-theory-college.l16.q1.h: One is a melodic line and the other is in the bass.
music-theory-college.l16.q1.e: The Ursatz combines the fundamental line (Urlinie) with a bass arpeggiation, I-V-I.

music-theory-college.l16.q2.e: The Urlinie descends stepwise to the tonic, as in 3-2-1 or 5-4-3-2-1.

music-theory-college.l16.q3.p: A neighbor tone prolongs a note by stepping away and returning.
music-theory-college.l16.q3.e: A neighbor tone steps away from a note and comes back, prolonging it.

music-theory-college.l16.q4.p: Which level of a Schenkerian analysis is the most abstract?
music-theory-college.l16.q4.e: The background shows the fundamental structure, the deepest level.

music-theory-college.l16.q5.p: In an interruption, on which scale degree does the first descent of the Urlinie stop?
music-theory-college.l16.q5.h: The first descent ends on the dominant.
music-theory-college.l16.q5.e: The line stops on 2 over V, then begins again and completes the descent to 1.

music-theory-college.l17.q1.p: How is the Tristan chord spelled in the Prelude to Tristan und Isolde?
music-theory-college.l17.q1.h: It contains an augmented fourth above the bass.
music-theory-college.l17.q1.e: It is spelled F, B, D-sharp and G-sharp.

music-theory-college.l17.q2.p: The pitches of the Tristan chord are enharmonically equivalent to a half-diminished seventh chord.
music-theory-college.l17.q2.h: Respell B as C-flat, D-sharp as E-flat and G-sharp as A-flat.
music-theory-college.l17.q2.e: F, B, D-sharp and G-sharp equal F, A-flat, C-flat and E-flat, a half-diminished seventh.

music-theory-college.l17.q3.p: In which work does the Tristan chord appear?
music-theory-college.l17.q3.h: It is named for a character.
music-theory-college.l17.q3.e: The chord is named after its use in the Prelude to Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

music-theory-college.l17.q4.p: To what chord does the Tristan chord resolve in the Prelude?
music-theory-college.l17.q4.e: It moves to the E dominant seventh chord, E, G-sharp, B and D.

music-theory-college.l17.q5.p: Delaying the resolution of dissonant chords is characteristic of late-Romantic harmony.
music-theory-college.l17.q5.e: Delayed or avoided resolutions weaken tonal clarity and are typical of late-Romantic chromaticism.

music-theory-college.l18.q1.p: How many distinct whole-tone collections exist?
music-theory-college.l18.q1.h: Transposing by a whole step gives the same notes.
music-theory-college.l18.q1.e: Transposition by a whole step maps the collection onto itself, leaving only two distinct collections.

music-theory-college.l18.q2.p: The whole-tone scale contains no half steps.
music-theory-college.l18.q2.e: Every step in the whole-tone scale is a whole step.

music-theory-college.l18.q3.p: Which notes form the C major pentatonic scale?
music-theory-college.l18.q3.h: It has five notes and no half steps.
music-theory-college.l18.q3.e: The major pentatonic from C is C, D, E, G, A.

music-theory-college.l18.q4.p: What kind of triad can be built from notes of the whole-tone scale?
music-theory-college.l18.q4.e: Thirds within the whole-tone scale are major thirds, so triads are augmented.

music-theory-college.l18.q5.p: Planing is the parallel motion of a chord shape as a block.
music-theory-college.l18.q5.e: Planing moves the same chord shape up and down in parallel.

music-theory-college.l19.q1.p: How many distinct octatonic collections exist?
music-theory-college.l19.q1.h: It maps onto itself under transposition by a minor third.
music-theory-college.l19.q1.e: The pattern repeats every three semitones, so there are three collections.

music-theory-college.l19.q2.p: The octatonic scale alternates whole steps and half steps.
music-theory-college.l19.q2.h: The name refers to eight notes.
music-theory-college.l19.q2.e: The scale strictly alternates whole and half steps.

music-theory-college.l19.q3.p: Which chord is contained in the octatonic collection C, D, E-flat, F, G-flat, A-flat, A, B?
music-theory-college.l19.q3.e: C, E-flat, G-flat and A form a fully diminished seventh chord, all drawn from the collection.

music-theory-college.l19.q4.p: How many different pitch classes does an octatonic collection contain?
music-theory-college.l19.q4.e: Octatonic means eight, so the collection has eight pitch classes.

music-theory-college.l19.q5.p: A single octatonic collection can contain both a D major triad and a D minor triad.
music-theory-college.l19.q5.e: The whole-half collection from C includes D, F, A and D, G-flat (F-sharp), A.

music-theory-college.l20.q1.p: What does the P transformation do to C major?
music-theory-college.l20.q1.h: It keeps the root and the fifth.
music-theory-college.l20.q1.e: P changes the quality, so C major becomes C minor.

music-theory-college.l20.q2.p: What does the L transformation do to C major?
music-theory-college.l20.q2.h: C moves down by a half step.
music-theory-college.l20.q2.e: L moves the root down to B, giving E, G, B, an E minor triad.

music-theory-college.l20.q3.p: What does the R transformation do to C major?
music-theory-college.l20.q3.h: G moves up a whole step.
music-theory-college.l20.q3.e: R moves G to A, giving C, E, A, an A minor triad.

music-theory-college.l20.q4.p: Each of P, L and R keeps two common tones between the triads it connects.
music-theory-college.l20.q4.h: The motion is by a single voice.
music-theory-college.l20.q4.e: Only one note moves, so two common tones remain.

music-theory-college.l20.q5.p: Alternating P and L from C major produces a cycle of how many distinct triads?
music-theory-college.l20.q5.h: It is called the hexatonic cycle.
music-theory-college.l20.q5.e: The cycle is C major, C minor, A-flat major, A-flat minor, E major and E minor, six triads.

music-theory-college.l21.q1.p: What is the prime form of the C major triad?
music-theory-college.l21.q1.h: Prime form is the most compact ordering, starting on 0. Major and minor triads share it.
music-theory-college.l21.q1.e: Major and minor triads share the prime form (0, 3, 7), set class 3-11; (0, 4, 7) is the inversion of the same set class.

music-theory-college.l21.q2.p: In pitch-class integer notation with C as 0, what number is A?
music-theory-college.l21.q2.h: Count in semitones up from C.
music-theory-college.l21.q2.e: C is 0, D is 2, E is 4, F is 5, G is 7 and A is 9.

music-theory-college.l21.q3.p: What is the prime form of the pitch classes D, E-flat and G?
music-theory-college.l21.q3.h: Use 2, 3, 7 and compare with the inversion.
music-theory-college.l21.q3.e: {2, 3, 7} transposes to (0, 1, 5), and its inversion gives (0, 4, 5); (0, 1, 5) is more compact.

music-theory-college.l21.q4.p: Sets related by transposition or inversion belong to the same set class.
music-theory-college.l21.q4.h: The prime form is the same.
music-theory-college.l21.q4.e: Set classes group sets that are equivalent under transposition and inversion.

music-theory-college.l21.q5.p: Normal order is the most compact ascending arrangement of a pitch-class set.
music-theory-college.l21.q5.h: It minimizes the span from first to last.
music-theory-college.l21.q5.e: Normal order arranges the set in ascending order with the smallest outer interval.

music-theory-college.l22.q1.p: What is the interval-class vector of a major triad?
music-theory-college.l22.q1.e: The pairs give ic4, ic5 and ic3, so the vector is <001110>.

music-theory-college.l22.q2.p: For a set of n notes, the digits of its interval-class vector add up to n(n-1)/2.
music-theory-college.l22.q2.h: This is the number of pairs.
music-theory-college.l22.q2.e: Each pair of notes contributes one interval class, so the sum equals the number of pairs.

music-theory-college.l22.q3.p: What do the digits of the vector of any tetrachord add up to?
music-theory-college.l22.q3.e: A tetrachord has 4 times 3 divided by 2, which is 6 pairs.

music-theory-college.l22.q4.p: What is the interval-class vector of an augmented triad?
music-theory-college.l22.q4.h: All three intervals are the same.
music-theory-college.l22.q4.e: The augmented triad has three major thirds, ic4, so the vector is <000300>.

music-theory-college.l22.q5.p: Z-related sets share an interval-class vector but are not related by transposition or inversion.
music-theory-college.l22.q5.e: That is the definition of the Z relation.

music-theory-college.l23.q1.p: In a twelve-tone row, each of the twelve pitch classes appears exactly once.
music-theory-college.l23.q1.e: A row is an ordering of all twelve pitch classes with no repeated notes.

music-theory-college.l23.q2.p: How many forms does a twelve-tone row have, counting P, I, R and RI at all transpositions?
music-theory-college.l23.q2.h: Four forms times twelve starting notes.
music-theory-college.l23.q2.e: Four forms at twelve transpositions give 48.

music-theory-college.l23.q3.p: For P0 = 0 2 4 6 8 10 1 3 5 7 9 11, what is the second pitch class of I0?
music-theory-college.l23.q3.e: The first step in P0 is up 2, so in I0 it is down 2, which gives 10.

music-theory-college.l23.q4.p: For P0 = 0 2 4 6 8 10 1 3 5 7 9 11, what are the first four pitch classes of P5?

music-theory-college.l23.q5.t: Right to left along a row
music-theory-college.l23.q5.p: In a standard matrix, how is a retrograde form read?
music-theory-college.l23.q5.h: It runs backward through the prime form.
music-theory-college.l23.q5.e: Reading a prime row from right to left gives its retrograde.

music-theory-college.l24.q1.t: Identical patterns at slightly different speeds drifting apart and back
music-theory-college.l24.q1.e: In phasing, two identical patterns move gradually out of alignment and later back.

music-theory-college.l24.q2.p: Aleatory music leaves some elements to chance or to the performer.
music-theory-college.l24.q2.h: The word comes from a word for dice.
music-theory-college.l24.q2.e: In aleatory music, some elements are not fixed by the composer.

music-theory-college.l24.q3.t: The acoustic spectrum and overtones of sound
music-theory-college.l24.q3.p: On what is spectralism chiefly based?
music-theory-college.l24.q3.h: The name refers to the spectrum.
music-theory-college.l24.q3.e: Spectral composers derive harmony and form from the analysis of the spectrum of sound.

music-theory-college.l24.q4.t: Repetition of short patterns with gradual change
music-theory-college.l24.q4.p: Which feature is typical of minimalism?
music-theory-college.l24.q4.e: Minimalism uses repetition and slow, audible change.

music-theory-college.l24.q5.p: John Cage used chance operations in the composition of some works.
music-theory-college.l24.q5.h: The I Ching was one tool.
music-theory-college.l24.q5.e: Cage used chance procedures such as the I Ching to determine musical parameters.

music-theory-college.l25.q1.p: Which chords form ii-V-I in C major with seventh chords?
music-theory-college.l25.q1.h: The roots are D, G and C.
music-theory-college.l25.q1.e: The progression is D minor seventh, G dominant seventh and C major seventh.

music-theory-college.l25.q2.p: Which chord is the tritone substitution for G7?
music-theory-college.l25.q2.h: The root is a tritone away.
music-theory-college.l25.q2.e: The tritone from G is D-flat, so the substitute is D-flat 7.

music-theory-college.l25.q3.p: G7 and D-flat 7 share the same tritone, the pitches B and F, with the pitch B spelled C-flat in D-flat 7.
music-theory-college.l25.q3.e: The third and seventh of G7 become the seventh and third of D-flat 7.

music-theory-college.l25.q4.p: In C minor, which chord quality is the ii chord of a minor ii-V-i?
music-theory-college.l25.q4.e: In C minor the ii chord is D, F, A-flat and C, a half-diminished seventh.

music-theory-college.l25.q5.p: In ii-V-I, the seventh of ii resolves down by half step to the third of V.
music-theory-college.l25.q5.e: The seventh of Dm7 is C, which falls to B, the third of G7.

music-theory-college.l26.q1.p: Which note is the ninth of a C9 chord?
music-theory-college.l26.q1.h: It is a step above the octave.
music-theory-college.l26.q1.e: The ninth of C is D.

music-theory-college.l26.q2.p: Which note is the thirteenth of a G13 chord?
music-theory-college.l26.q2.h: The thirteenth is a sixth above the root.
music-theory-college.l26.q2.e: The sixth above G is E.

music-theory-college.l26.q3.t: They share E, G and B
music-theory-college.l26.q3.p: Why can E minor seventh substitute for C major seventh?
music-theory-college.l26.q3.e: E minor seventh contains E, G, B and D, and the first three are shared with C major seventh.

music-theory-college.l26.q4.p: The natural eleventh is usually avoided on major chords because it clashes with the major third.
music-theory-college.l26.q4.h: The raised eleventh is common instead.
music-theory-college.l26.q4.e: The natural eleventh sits a half step above the third, so the raised eleventh is usually preferred.

music-theory-college.l26.q5.t: Approaching a target chord with its dominant, then that chord with its dominant, and so on
music-theory-college.l26.q5.h: It follows the circle of fifths.
music-theory-college.l26.q5.e: Backcycling chains dominants backward from a target chord.

music-theory-college.l27.q1.t: D, E, F, G, A, B, C
music-theory-college.l27.q1.e: D Dorian is the white-key scale from D to D.

music-theory-college.l27.q2.p: What is the characteristic note of the Lydian mode?
music-theory-college.l27.q2.e: Lydian is a major scale with a raised fourth.

music-theory-college.l27.q3.p: Modal jazz often stays on a single mode for long stretches.
music-theory-college.l27.q3.e: Modal jazz uses static harmony, with few chord changes.

music-theory-college.l27.q4.p: Which major scale has the same notes as G Mixolydian?
music-theory-college.l27.q4.e: G Mixolydian, G, A, B, C, D, E, F, uses the notes of C major.

music-theory-college.l27.q5.p: Dorian has a natural sixth, while Aeolian has a lowered sixth.
music-theory-college.l27.q5.h: Compare D Dorian with D Aeolian.
music-theory-college.l27.q5.e: This is the difference that distinguishes the two minor-type modes.

music-theory-college.l28.q1.t: A claim supported by specific score evidence
music-theory-college.l28.q1.p: Which feature best marks a strong analytical paragraph?
music-theory-college.l28.q1.e: A good paragraph makes a claim and supports it with specific passages.

music-theory-college.l28.q2.p: Citing measure numbers helps readers locate the evidence for a claim.
music-theory-college.l28.q2.h: Readers need to find the passage.
music-theory-college.l28.q2.e: Measure numbers allow readers to check each example.

music-theory-college.l28.q3.p: What does a lowercase Roman numeral with a small circle denote?
music-theory-college.l28.q3.e: A lowercase numeral with ° denotes a diminished triad.

music-theory-college.l28.q4.p: Good analysis only describes what happens bar by bar, without interpretation.
music-theory-college.l28.q4.e: Strong analysis moves from description to an interpretation that can be argued.

music-theory-college.l28.q5.t: The second theme is in G major.
music-theory-college.l28.q5.p: Which statement is a description rather than an interpretation?
music-theory-college.l28.q5.h: A description states what is there.
music-theory-college.l28.q5.e: The key of the second theme is a fact in the score, while the other statements argue about effect.

music-theory-early.l01.q1.p: The steady beat in music is like a heartbeat that keeps going at an even pace.
music-theory-early.l01.q1.e: The beat is the steady pulse of the music, and it keeps an even pace like a heartbeat.

music-theory-early.l01.q2.t: Patting your knees evenly to the music
music-theory-early.l01.q2.p: Which of these is a good way to show the steady beat?
music-theory-early.l01.q2.h: Pick the one that stays even.
music-theory-early.l01.q2.e: Patting evenly in time with the music shows the steady beat.

music-theory-early.l01.q3.p: The beat changes every time the words of the song change.
music-theory-early.l01.q3.h: Does a clock change its tick when you talk?
music-theory-early.l01.q3.e: The beat keeps going steadily even when the words or the tune change.

music-theory-early.l01.q4.p: In the freeze game, what do you do when the music stops?
music-theory-early.l01.q4.e: In the game you walk on the beat and freeze when the music stops.

music-theory-early.l01.q5.t: All of them: feet, hands or head
music-theory-early.l01.q5.p: Which of these can you use to show the steady beat?
music-theory-early.l01.q5.h: Think about how many ways you can move.
music-theory-early.l01.q5.e: You can show the beat by marching, patting, nodding or tapping, so every one of these works.

music-theory-early.l02.q1.p: How high or low a sound is, is called its pitch.
music-theory-early.l02.q1.e: Pitch is the word for how high or low a sound is.

music-theory-early.l02.q2.p: Which animal sound would most likely be HIGH?
music-theory-early.l02.q2.e: A tiny bird chirps high, while a bear growl and a foghorn are low.

music-theory-early.l02.q3.p: On a piano, the keys on the right side sound...
music-theory-early.l02.q3.h: Think of a ladder going up.
music-theory-early.l02.q3.e: Keys farther to the right on a piano play higher pitches.

music-theory-early.l02.q4.p: A giant growling is a low sound.
music-theory-early.l02.q4.e: Big, deep growls are low sounds.

music-theory-early.l02.q5.p: When you imagine a ladder of sounds, where are the low sounds?
music-theory-early.l02.q5.e: Low sounds are at the bottom of the ladder and high sounds are at the top.

music-theory-early.l03.q1.p: What does the word forte mean in music?

music-theory-early.l03.q2.p: What does the word piano mean when it is used for dynamics?

music-theory-early.l03.q3.p: A kitten purring is a soft sound.
music-theory-early.l03.q3.h: Is a kitten quiet or noisy?
music-theory-early.l03.q3.e: A purr is a soft, quiet sound.

music-theory-early.l03.q4.p: When we sing loud, we should yell as hard as we can.
music-theory-early.l03.q4.e: We can sing loud and strong without yelling, which can hurt your voice.

music-theory-early.l03.q5.t: To help the music tell a story and show feelings
music-theory-early.l03.q5.p: Why do composers use both loud and soft parts?
music-theory-early.l03.q5.e: Soft and loud parts make music feel different, so it can show many feelings.

music-theory-early.l04.q1.p: The speed of the beat is called...
music-theory-early.l04.q1.e: Tempo is the word for how fast or slow the beat is.

music-theory-early.l04.q2.p: A turtle is a good example of a slow tempo.
music-theory-early.l04.q2.e: A turtle moves slowly, so it matches a slow tempo.

music-theory-early.l04.q3.p: Which kind of song might help someone fall asleep?
music-theory-early.l04.q3.e: Slow, calm music like a lullaby can help people relax and sleep.

music-theory-early.l04.q4.p: When the tempo gets faster, the beat stops being steady.
music-theory-early.l04.q4.e: The beat can still be steady at a faster speed; it is just steady at a new tempo.

music-theory-early.l04.q5.t: Listen to the drum and change your walking speed with it
music-theory-early.l04.q5.p: In the game Speed Up, Slow Down, you should...
music-theory-early.l04.q5.e: You follow the leader by listening and matching your steps to the drum speed.

music-theory-early.l05.q1.p: How long a sound lasts is called its...
music-theory-early.l05.q1.e: Duration means how long a sound lasts.

music-theory-early.l05.q2.p: A wood block click is a short sound.
music-theory-early.l05.q2.e: A tap on a wood block makes a quick, short sound.

music-theory-early.l05.q3.h: Which one goes on and on?
music-theory-early.l05.q3.e: A held voice sound can go on for a long time, while the others end quickly.

music-theory-early.l05.q4.p: Rhythm is made by mixing long and short sounds over a steady beat.
music-theory-early.l05.q4.e: Rhythm is a pattern of long and short sounds placed over the steady beat.

music-theory-early.l05.q5.p: A triangle that rings for a while is an example of a...
music-theory-early.l05.q5.e: A ringing triangle keeps sounding for a while, so it makes a long sound.

music-theory-early.l06.q1.p: Your voice is an instrument that you carry with you.
music-theory-early.l06.q1.e: Your voice makes music, so it is an instrument you always have.

music-theory-early.l06.q2.p: When we sing, we hold each sound on a steady...
music-theory-early.l06.q2.e: Singing holds each sound on a steady pitch, which is different from talking.

music-theory-early.l06.q3.t: Sit or stand up tall and breathe calmly
music-theory-early.l06.q3.p: Which is a good tip for a happy singing voice?
music-theory-early.l06.q3.e: Good posture and a calm breath help the voice sing in an easy, healthy way.

music-theory-early.l06.q4.p: Shouting is the best way to sing.
music-theory-early.l06.q4.e: Shouting can hurt the throat; a light, easy sound is better for singing.

music-theory-early.l06.q5.p: In the game Voice Detective, which voice holds notes like a tune?
music-theory-early.l06.q5.e: The singing voice holds notes at steady pitches, like a tune.

music-theory-early.l07.q1.p: In an echo game, what do you do after the leader sings or claps?
music-theory-early.l07.q1.e: In an echo you copy what the leader did.

music-theory-early.l07.q2.p: You need to listen carefully to play an echo game well.
music-theory-early.l07.q2.e: You must hear the pattern first in order to copy it.

music-theory-early.l07.q3.t: One person leads and others answer
music-theory-early.l07.q3.e: In call-and-response a leader makes the call and a group gives the response.

music-theory-early.l07.q4.p: In call-and-response, the answer can be a new reply, not just a copy.
music-theory-early.l07.q4.e: The response can be an exact echo or a different answer to the call.

music-theory-early.l07.q5.p: What makes a group sound like a team in music?
music-theory-early.l07.q5.e: Careful listening helps people play and sing together.

music-theory-early.l08.q1.p: Ta is one sound on how many beats?
music-theory-early.l08.q1.h: It is the easy, steady one.
music-theory-early.l08.q1.e: Ta is a single sound on one beat.

music-theory-early.l08.q2.p: Ti-ti is how many quick, even sounds in one beat?
music-theory-early.l08.q2.e: Ti-ti fits two even sounds into one beat.

music-theory-early.l08.q3.p: A rest is a beat with no sound.
music-theory-early.l08.q3.e: A rest is a beat of silence, though you still feel the beat in your head.

music-theory-early.l08.q4.p: During a rest, you should stop feeling the steady beat.
music-theory-early.l08.q4.e: The beat goes on during a rest; only the sound is missing.

music-theory-early.l08.q5.t: Ti-ti, because it fits two sounds in one beat
music-theory-early.l08.q5.p: Which is faster, ta or ti-ti, when the beat stays the same?
music-theory-early.l08.q5.h: Squeeze two sounds in the box.
music-theory-early.l08.q5.e: Ti-ti puts two sounds in the space where ta has one, so its sounds are quicker.

music-theory-early.l09.q1.p: Which instrument family includes drums, shakers and triangles?
music-theory-early.l09.q1.h: You hit, shake or scrape them.
music-theory-early.l09.q1.e: Percussion instruments are hit, shaken or scraped.

music-theory-early.l09.q2.p: A trumpet belongs to which family?
music-theory-early.l09.q2.h: The player buzzes lips into metal.
music-theory-early.l09.q2.e: The trumpet is a brass instrument.

music-theory-early.l09.q3.p: A violin is a string instrument.
music-theory-early.l09.q3.h: It has strings and a bow.
music-theory-early.l09.q3.e: The violin makes its sound with strings, so it is in the string family.

music-theory-early.l09.q4.h: You blow air into or across it.
music-theory-early.l09.q4.e: The recorder is blown, and it is a woodwind.

music-theory-early.l09.q5.p: A xylophone is a percussion instrument that can play different pitches.
music-theory-early.l09.q5.h: You hit the bars with mallets.
music-theory-early.l09.q5.e: The xylophone is hit with mallets and each bar has its own pitch.

music-theory-early.l10.q1.p: The tune of Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is also used for the Alphabet Song.
music-theory-early.l10.q1.e: The same tune is used for Twinkle, Twinkle and the Alphabet Song.

music-theory-early.l10.q2.p: The Twinkle tune comes from an old song from which country?
music-theory-early.l10.q2.h: It starts with Ah! vous dirai-je.
music-theory-early.l10.q2.e: The tune comes from the French song Ah! vous dirai-je, maman.

music-theory-early.l10.q3.t: A tune changed in new ways
music-theory-early.l10.q3.p: What is a variation in music?
music-theory-early.l10.q3.h: It starts from a tune you know.
music-theory-early.l10.q3.e: A variation takes a tune and changes it, such as making it faster or softer.

music-theory-early.l10.q4.p: Mozart wrote piano variations on the Twinkle tune.
music-theory-early.l10.q4.e: Mozart wrote a set of piano variations on this tune.

music-theory-early.l10.q5.t: Everyone is free to sing and share it
music-theory-early.l10.q5.p: What does it mean for a tune to be in the public domain?
music-theory-early.l10.q5.e: A public domain tune is free for everyone to use.

music-theory-early.l11.q1.p: Who wrote the Ode to Joy tune used in his Ninth Symphony?
music-theory-early.l11.q1.e: Ludwig van Beethoven wrote the Ode to Joy tune in his Ninth Symphony.

music-theory-early.l11.q2.p: The Ode to Joy tune mostly moves by steps, like walking on stairs.
music-theory-early.l11.q2.h: That makes it easy to sing.
music-theory-early.l11.q2.e: The melody moves mostly by steps, which makes it easy to sing along.

music-theory-early.l11.q3.p: Morning was written for a play called...
music-theory-early.l11.q3.h: It has the name of a man.
music-theory-early.l11.q3.e: Grieg wrote Morning as part of his music for the play Peer Gynt.

music-theory-early.l11.q4.p: Which country was Edvard Grieg from?
music-theory-early.l11.q4.h: It is in the cold north of Europe.
music-theory-early.l11.q4.e: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer.

music-theory-early.l11.q5.p: A symphony is a long piece played by an orchestra.
music-theory-early.l11.q5.h: It is for a big group of players.
music-theory-early.l11.q5.e: A symphony is a long piece for orchestra.

music-theory-early.l12.q1.p: Which piece has parts about a lion, an elephant and a swan?
music-theory-early.l12.q1.e: Saint-Saens wrote The Carnival of the Animals, which includes those animals.

music-theory-early.l12.q2.p: In Peter and the Wolf, which instrument plays the bird?
music-theory-early.l12.q2.e: In Peter and the Wolf the bird is played by a flute.

music-theory-early.l12.q3.p: In Peter and the Wolf, the duck is played by an oboe.
music-theory-early.l12.q3.e: The duck is played by the oboe.

music-theory-early.l12.q4.p: In Peter and the Wolf, which instruments play the wolf?
music-theory-early.l12.q4.e: The wolf is played by French horns.

music-theory-early.l12.q5.p: Composer Prokofiev wrote Peter and the Wolf.
music-theory-early.l12.q5.e: Sergei Prokofiev composed Peter and the Wolf.

music-theory-early.l13.q1.p: What are do, re, mi called?
music-theory-early.l13.q1.e: Singing note names such as do, re and mi are called solfege.

music-theory-early.l13.q2.p: What comes right after re when you sing up the scale?
music-theory-early.l13.q2.e: The order going up begins do, re, mi.

music-theory-early.l13.q3.p: In solfege, do is at the bottom and the last do at the top is higher.
music-theory-early.l13.q3.e: The scale starts on do and ends on a higher do.

music-theory-early.l13.q4.t: Do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do
music-theory-early.l13.q4.p: Which is the correct order of solfege going up?
music-theory-early.l13.q4.e: The scale goes do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do.

music-theory-early.l13.q5.p: You must read written notes before you can sing solfege.
music-theory-early.l13.q5.e: Solfege helps you hear and sing tunes even before you read notes on paper.

music-theory-early.l14.q1.p: If you sing do, re, mi, which way does your voice go?
music-theory-early.l14.q1.e: Do, re, mi goes up from low to high.

music-theory-early.l14.q2.p: If you sing mi, re, do, which way does your voice go?

music-theory-early.l14.q3.p: Mi, mi, mi stays on the same note.
music-theory-early.l14.q3.e: Singing mi three times keeps the voice on one pitch.

music-theory-early.l14.q4.p: On the three-step staircase, which note is the top step?
music-theory-early.l14.q4.e: Do is the bottom, re the middle and mi the top step.

music-theory-early.l14.q5.p: You can show a note pattern with your hand moving low, middle and high.
music-theory-early.l14.q5.h: Your hand can be a ladder.
music-theory-early.l14.q5.e: Hand height can show do (low), re (middle) and mi (high).

music-theory-early.l15.q1.p: A person who makes up music is called a...
music-theory-early.l15.q1.e: A composer is someone who makes up music.

music-theory-early.l15.q2.p: What is a good first step when you make up a song?
music-theory-early.l15.q2.e: The lesson starts with a steady beat, then words and notes.

music-theory-early.l15.q3.p: Composers often change things in their songs until they sound right.
music-theory-early.l15.q3.e: Changing and trying again is a regular part of making music.

music-theory-early.l15.q4.p: You must use an instrument to make up a song.
music-theory-early.l15.q4.e: You can make up a song using only your voice.

music-theory-early.l15.q5.p: Which of these can your song be about?
music-theory-early.l15.q5.e: A song can be about anything, such as a pet, lunch or rain.

music-theory-early.l16.q1.p: Which composer wrote music as a child and was born in Salzburg?
music-theory-early.l16.q1.e: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg and began music very young.

music-theory-early.l16.q2.p: Every composer was once a child.
music-theory-early.l16.q2.e: Every person, including famous composers, was once a child.

music-theory-early.l16.q3.p: Beethoven lost his ability to do what as he got older?
music-theory-early.l16.q3.h: It is hard for a musician.
music-theory-early.l16.q3.e: Beethoven lost his hearing as he got older, yet he kept writing music.

music-theory-early.l16.q4.p: Which country was Camille Saint-Saens from?
music-theory-early.l16.q4.h: He wrote The Carnival of the Animals.

music-theory-early.l16.q5.p: Composers learned, practiced and tried again, just like students.
music-theory-early.l16.q5.h: Nobody is perfect on day one.
music-theory-early.l16.q5.e: Learning music takes practice for everyone, including composers.

music-theory-elementary.l01.q1.p: A music staff has five lines.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q1.h: Count the lines in a staff.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q1.e: A staff has five lines and four spaces.

music-theory-elementary.l01.q2.p: Which clef is also called the G clef and is used for higher sounds?
music-theory-elementary.l01.q2.h: Violins and flutes read this clef.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q2.e: The treble clef circles the line where G sits and is used for higher pitches.

music-theory-elementary.l01.q3.p: The higher a note sits on the staff, the lower it sounds.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q3.h: Think of a ladder: higher means higher.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q3.e: Notes placed higher on the staff sound higher in pitch.

music-theory-elementary.l01.q4.p: How many spaces are there between the lines of a staff?
music-theory-elementary.l01.q4.h: There is one fewer space than lines.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q4.e: Five lines leave four spaces between them.

music-theory-elementary.l01.q5.p: Which instrument usually reads the bass clef?
music-theory-elementary.l01.q5.h: It is a low string instrument.
music-theory-elementary.l01.q5.e: The cello plays low notes and reads bass clef; the others normally read treble clef.

music-theory-elementary.l02.q1.p: Which letters name the lines of the treble staff, from bottom to top?
music-theory-elementary.l02.q1.e: The treble-clef lines are E, G, B, D and F from bottom to top.

music-theory-elementary.l02.q2.p: Which word do the treble-clef space notes spell, from bottom to top?
music-theory-elementary.l02.q2.h: It is a word you can see in a mirror.
music-theory-elementary.l02.q2.e: The four spaces are F, A, C and E, spelling FACE.

music-theory-elementary.l02.q3.p: What is the name of the note on the bottom line of the treble staff?
music-theory-elementary.l02.q3.h: It is the first of EGBDF.
music-theory-elementary.l02.q3.e: The bottom line of the treble staff is E.

music-theory-elementary.l02.q4.p: What is the note in the second space from the bottom of the treble staff?
music-theory-elementary.l02.q4.h: The spaces are F, A, C, E.
music-theory-elementary.l02.q4.e: The spaces from bottom to top are F, A, C, E, so the second is A.

music-theory-elementary.l02.q5.p: Middle C is written on a short ledger line just below the treble staff.
music-theory-elementary.l02.q5.e: In treble clef, middle C sits on a ledger line directly under the staff.

music-theory-elementary.l03.q1.p: Which letters name the lines of the bass staff, from bottom to top?
music-theory-elementary.l03.q1.e: The bass-clef lines are G, B, D, F and A from bottom to top.

music-theory-elementary.l03.q2.p: What is the note in the bottom space of the bass staff?
music-theory-elementary.l03.q2.h: The bass spaces are A, C, E, G.
music-theory-elementary.l03.q2.e: The spaces from bottom to top are A, C, E, G, so the bottom space is A.

music-theory-elementary.l03.q3.p: What is the note in the top space of the bass staff?
music-theory-elementary.l03.q3.h: The last of A C E G.
music-theory-elementary.l03.q3.e: The top space of the bass staff is G.

music-theory-elementary.l03.q4.p: Piano music uses a grand staff made of a treble staff and a bass staff joined together.
music-theory-elementary.l03.q4.h: The piano plays both high and low notes.
music-theory-elementary.l03.q4.e: The grand staff joins treble and bass staves, usually for the right and left hands.

music-theory-elementary.l03.q5.t: On a short ledger line between the treble and bass staves
music-theory-elementary.l03.q5.p: Where is middle C written on the grand staff?
music-theory-elementary.l03.q5.h: It sits between the two staves.
music-theory-elementary.l03.q5.e: Middle C sits on its own ledger line between the staves, below the treble and above the bass.

music-theory-elementary.l04.q1.p: How many beats does a whole note get?
music-theory-elementary.l04.q1.h: It is the longest of the basic notes.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q1.e: A whole note lasts four beats.

music-theory-elementary.l04.q2.p: A quarter rest means one beat of silence in 4/4.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q2.h: A rest matches the note of the same name.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q2.e: A quarter rest is silent for the length of a quarter note, one beat.

music-theory-elementary.l04.q3.p: How many eighth notes equal one half note?
music-theory-elementary.l04.q3.h: A half note is two beats; an eighth is half a beat.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q3.e: A half note is two beats, and each eighth is half a beat, so four eighths fit.

music-theory-elementary.l04.q4.t: A half note and a quarter note
music-theory-elementary.l04.q4.p: Which pair of notes together lasts 3 beats?
music-theory-elementary.l04.q4.e: A half note is 2 beats and a quarter is 1 beat, giving 3; the others total 2 or 4.

music-theory-elementary.l04.q5.p: A sixteenth note lasts longer than an eighth note.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q5.h: Each smaller note is half as long.
music-theory-elementary.l04.q5.e: A sixteenth lasts a quarter of a beat, shorter than an eighth at half a beat.

music-theory-elementary.l05.q1.p: How many beats are in each measure of 3/4?
music-theory-elementary.l05.q1.e: The top number 3 means three beats per measure.

music-theory-elementary.l05.q2.t: A quarter note gets one beat
music-theory-elementary.l05.q2.p: In 4/4, what does the bottom number 4 tell you?
music-theory-elementary.l05.q2.h: The bottom number names the beat note.
music-theory-elementary.l05.q2.e: A bottom number of 4 means the quarter note is the beat.

music-theory-elementary.l05.q3.p: In 2/4 there are two quarter-note beats in each measure.
music-theory-elementary.l05.q3.e: The 2 on top means two beats, and the 4 on the bottom means quarter-note beats.

music-theory-elementary.l05.q4.p: Which time signature has the swaying feel of a waltz?
music-theory-elementary.l05.q4.h: ONE two three, ONE two three.
