music-theory-elementary.l05.q4.e: A waltz is in three beats per measure, so 3/4.

music-theory-elementary.l05.q5.p: A 4/4 measure contains a half note and one quarter note. How many beats are still needed to fill it?
music-theory-elementary.l05.q5.h: 2 + 1 = 3, so how many are left of 4?
music-theory-elementary.l05.q5.e: The half and quarter total 3 beats, so one more beat is needed to reach 4.

music-theory-elementary.l06.q1.p: What does a dot after a note do?
music-theory-elementary.l06.q1.h: It adds a bit more length.
music-theory-elementary.l06.q1.e: A dot lengthens a note by half of its original value.

music-theory-elementary.l06.q2.p: How many beats does a dotted half note get in 4/4?
music-theory-elementary.l06.q2.h: Half note is 2, plus half of 2.
music-theory-elementary.l06.q2.e: A half note is 2 beats and the dot adds 1, so 3 beats.

music-theory-elementary.l06.q3.p: How many beats does a dotted quarter note get?
music-theory-elementary.l06.q3.e: A quarter note is 1 beat, and the dot adds half a beat, giving 1 1/2 beats.

music-theory-elementary.l06.q4.p: A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound.
music-theory-elementary.l06.q4.e: A tie connects same-pitch notes so the sound is held for their combined length.

music-theory-elementary.l06.q5.p: A quarter note tied to a half note lasts how many beats?
music-theory-elementary.l06.q5.e: A quarter is 1 beat and a half is 2 beats, so the tied note lasts 3 beats.

music-theory-elementary.l07.q1.p: A measure of 3/4 has a half note. Which note fills the rest of the measure?
music-theory-elementary.l07.q1.e: A half note is 2 beats, so one quarter note makes up the remaining beat of 3.

music-theory-elementary.l07.q2.p: Eighth notes are often counted as "1 and 2 and".
music-theory-elementary.l07.q2.h: The word "and" falls between the numbers.
music-theory-elementary.l07.q2.e: Each number and each "and" is one eighth note.

music-theory-elementary.l07.q3.p: How many eighth notes fit in one measure of 2/4?
music-theory-elementary.l07.q3.h: Two beats, two eighths per beat.
music-theory-elementary.l07.q3.e: Each quarter-note beat holds two eighths, so two beats hold four.

music-theory-elementary.l07.q4.p: A 4/4 measure has a quarter note, a quarter rest, then a half note. On which beats do you start playing a note?
music-theory-elementary.l07.q4.e: You play on beat 1, rest on beat 2, then start the half note on beat 3 and hold it through beat 4.

music-theory-elementary.l07.q5.p: A whole note fits inside one measure of 3/4.
music-theory-elementary.l07.q5.e: A whole note lasts 4 beats, which is more than the 3 beats in a 3/4 measure.

music-theory-elementary.l08.q1.t: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half
music-theory-elementary.l08.q1.p: What is the pattern of steps in a major scale?
music-theory-elementary.l08.q1.h: W W H W W W H.
music-theory-elementary.l08.q1.e: Every major scale follows whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.

music-theory-elementary.l08.q2.t: C D E F G A B C
music-theory-elementary.l08.q2.p: Which notes make up the C major scale?
music-theory-elementary.l08.q2.e: C major uses all the white-key notes from C to C.

music-theory-elementary.l08.q3.p: A major scale has eight notes if you count the starting note again at the top.
music-theory-elementary.l08.q3.h: Count C to the next C.
music-theory-elementary.l08.q3.e: The scale runs from one note up to its octave, giving eight notes counting both ends.

music-theory-elementary.l08.q4.t: E to F and B to C
music-theory-elementary.l08.q4.p: Between which pairs of notes in C major are the half steps?
music-theory-elementary.l08.q4.h: No black key sits between them.
music-theory-elementary.l08.q4.e: There is no black key between E and F or between B and C, so those are half steps.

music-theory-elementary.l08.q5.p: Which note is a whole step above C?
music-theory-elementary.l08.q5.e: C to D is two half steps, or one whole step.

music-theory-elementary.l09.q1.p: Which sharp does the G major scale have?
music-theory-elementary.l09.q1.e: G major has one sharp, F-sharp.

music-theory-elementary.l09.q2.p: Which sharps does D major have?
music-theory-elementary.l09.q2.e: D major has F-sharp and C-sharp.

music-theory-elementary.l09.q3.p: Which flat does the F major scale have?
music-theory-elementary.l09.q3.e: F major has one flat, B-flat.

music-theory-elementary.l09.q4.p: B-flat major has two flats, B-flat and E-flat.
music-theory-elementary.l09.q4.h: Think of the two flats in the scale.
music-theory-elementary.l09.q4.e: The B-flat major scale is B-flat, C, D, E-flat, F, G, A, which uses B-flat and E-flat.

music-theory-elementary.l09.q5.p: What is the third note of the D major scale?
music-theory-elementary.l09.q5.e: D major is D, E, F-sharp, so the third note is F-sharp.

music-theory-elementary.l10.q1.p: A key signature is written at the start of the staff, right after the clef.
music-theory-elementary.l10.q1.e: The key signature appears after the clef at the beginning of each staff.

music-theory-elementary.l10.q2.p: A key signature with one sharp (F-sharp) means which major key?
music-theory-elementary.l10.q2.h: The first key with a sharp.
music-theory-elementary.l10.q2.e: One sharp, F-sharp, is the key signature of G major.

music-theory-elementary.l10.q3.p: A key signature with one flat (B-flat) means which major key?
music-theory-elementary.l10.q3.h: The first key with a flat.
music-theory-elementary.l10.q3.e: One flat, B-flat, is the key signature of F major.

music-theory-elementary.l10.q4.p: A key signature with two flats (B-flat and E-flat) means which major key?
music-theory-elementary.l10.q4.h: The key is named after the first flat.
music-theory-elementary.l10.q4.e: Two flats, B-flat and E-flat, belong to B-flat major.

music-theory-elementary.l10.q5.p: In a key signature, the first sharp is F-sharp and the second is C-sharp.
music-theory-elementary.l10.q5.h: Order of sharps: F, C, G...
music-theory-elementary.l10.q5.e: Sharps always appear in the order F, C, G, D, A, E, B.

music-theory-elementary.l11.q1.p: What interval is C up to E?
music-theory-elementary.l11.q1.e: Counting C, D, E gives three letters, so it is a 3rd.

music-theory-elementary.l11.q2.p: What interval is C up to G?
music-theory-elementary.l11.q2.h: Count C, D, E, F, G.
music-theory-elementary.l11.q2.e: C, D, E, F, G is five letters, so it is a 5th.

music-theory-elementary.l11.q3.p: What is the interval from C up to the next C?
music-theory-elementary.l11.q3.e: The interval from a note to the next note of the same name is an octave, an 8th.

music-theory-elementary.l11.q4.p: C up to D is a 2nd.
music-theory-elementary.l11.q4.e: Counting C and D gives two letter names, so the interval is a 2nd.

music-theory-elementary.l11.q5.p: What interval is D up to A?
music-theory-elementary.l11.q5.h: Count D, E, F, G, A.
music-theory-elementary.l11.q5.e: D, E, F, G, A is five letters, so it is a 5th.

music-theory-elementary.l12.q1.p: Which scale degree is the tonic?
music-theory-elementary.l12.q1.e: The tonic is the first note of the scale.

music-theory-elementary.l12.q2.p: Which scale degree is the dominant?
music-theory-elementary.l12.q2.e: The dominant is the fifth degree of the scale.

music-theory-elementary.l12.q3.p: What is the dominant note in C major?
music-theory-elementary.l12.q3.h: Count C, D, E, F, G.
music-theory-elementary.l12.q3.e: Counting up five notes from C reaches G.

music-theory-elementary.l12.q4.p: What is the dominant note in G major?
music-theory-elementary.l12.q4.h: Count G, A, B, C, D.
music-theory-elementary.l12.q4.e: Counting up five notes from G reaches D.

music-theory-elementary.l12.q5.p: Many tunes in a major key end on the tonic, which gives a feeling of rest.
music-theory-elementary.l12.q5.e: Ending on the tonic gives a sense of arrival, so many tunes finish there.

music-theory-elementary.l13.q1.h: It looks like the letter f.

music-theory-elementary.l13.q2.p: What does piano mean as a dynamic?
music-theory-elementary.l13.q2.h: It looks like the letter p.
music-theory-elementary.l13.q2.e: As a dynamic marking, piano means soft.

music-theory-elementary.l13.q3.p: A crescendo means gradually getting louder.
music-theory-elementary.l13.q3.e: Crescendo means to get gradually louder.

music-theory-elementary.l13.q4.p: Which list is in order from softest to loudest?
music-theory-elementary.l13.q4.e: Pianissimo is softest and fortissimo is loudest, with p and mf in between.

music-theory-elementary.l13.q5.h: It is the opposite of crescendo.
music-theory-elementary.l13.q5.e: Diminuendo, or decrescendo, means gradually getting softer.

music-theory-elementary.l14.q1.h: Think of a lively, quick pace.

music-theory-elementary.l14.q4.e: Ritardando means to gradually slow down.

music-theory-elementary.l14.q5.p: At 60 beats per minute, each beat lasts one second.
music-theory-elementary.l14.q5.h: There are 60 seconds in a minute.
music-theory-elementary.l14.q5.e: Sixty beats in sixty seconds means one beat per second.

music-theory-elementary.l15.q1.p: Which instrument family does the trumpet belong to?
music-theory-elementary.l15.q1.h: Its sound comes from buzzing lips.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q1.e: The trumpet is a brass instrument.

music-theory-elementary.l15.q2.p: Which of these is a woodwind instrument?
music-theory-elementary.l15.q2.e: The oboe is a woodwind; the others are brass, string and percussion.

music-theory-elementary.l15.q3.p: The violin, viola, cello and double bass are all in the string family.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q3.h: They are played with a bow.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q3.e: These four instruments are the main orchestral strings.

music-theory-elementary.l15.q4.p: Which is the largest and lowest of the bowed string instruments?
music-theory-elementary.l15.q4.h: It is taller than the cello.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q4.e: The double bass is the largest and lowest bowed string instrument.

music-theory-elementary.l15.q5.p: The flute is a brass instrument because it is made of metal.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q5.h: Families depend on how sound is made.
music-theory-elementary.l15.q5.e: The flute is a woodwind; instruments are grouped by how they make sound, not by their material.

music-theory-elementary.l16.q1.p: Which family sits nearest the front of the orchestra?
music-theory-elementary.l16.q1.e: The strings sit in front, closest to the conductor.

music-theory-elementary.l16.q2.p: The percussion section usually sits at the back of the orchestra.
music-theory-elementary.l16.q2.e: Percussion instruments are normally placed at the back.

music-theory-elementary.l16.q3.p: Who stands at the front of the orchestra to lead the players?
music-theory-elementary.l16.q3.h: They use a baton or hands.
music-theory-elementary.l16.q3.e: The conductor stands at the front facing the players.

music-theory-elementary.l16.q4.t: In the middle, behind the strings
music-theory-elementary.l16.q4.p: Where do the woodwinds usually sit?
music-theory-elementary.l16.q4.e: Woodwinds sit in the middle of the stage, behind the strings and in front of the brass.

music-theory-elementary.l16.q5.p: Which instrument would you most likely find at the very back of an orchestra?
music-theory-elementary.l16.q5.e: Timpani are percussion instruments and sit at the back.

music-theory-elementary.l17.q1.p: Which letters show the form of a song that begins with a section, changes, and then repeats the first section?
music-theory-elementary.l17.q1.e: ABA means a first section, a contrast, then the first section again.

music-theory-elementary.l17.q2.p: AB form has two different, contrasting sections.
music-theory-elementary.l17.q2.h: A and B are different letters.
music-theory-elementary.l17.q2.e: AB form has one section A followed by a contrasting section B.

music-theory-elementary.l17.q3.p: Which pattern is a simple rondo?
music-theory-elementary.l17.q3.h: The A tune keeps coming back.
music-theory-elementary.l17.q3.e: A rondo returns to A between contrasting sections: ABACA.

music-theory-elementary.l17.q4.t: A tune is repeated, changed each time
music-theory-elementary.l17.q4.p: What happens in theme and variations?
music-theory-elementary.l17.q4.h: The theme comes back in disguise.
music-theory-elementary.l17.q4.e: A theme is played and then repeated with changes such as speed, rhythm or mood.

music-theory-elementary.l17.q5.p: A piece has the form ABA. Counting the first and last, how many times do we hear the A section in all?
music-theory-elementary.l17.q5.h: It appears at the beginning and the end.
music-theory-elementary.l17.q5.e: The pattern A, B, A has two A sections.

music-theory-elementary.l18.q1.p: Which composer was born in Salzburg?
music-theory-elementary.l18.q1.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756.

music-theory-elementary.l18.q2.p: Which composer wrote nine symphonies and gradually lost his hearing?
music-theory-elementary.l18.q2.e: Beethoven wrote nine symphonies and lost his hearing as an adult.

music-theory-elementary.l18.q3.p: Bach was a German composer from the Baroque period.
music-theory-elementary.l18.q3.e: Johann Sebastian Bach was a German Baroque composer.

music-theory-elementary.l18.q4.h: He was also a famous organist.
music-theory-elementary.l18.q4.e: The Brandenburg Concertos were written by Johann Sebastian Bach.

music-theory-elementary.l18.q5.p: Mozart lived to be over 80 years old.
music-theory-elementary.l18.q5.e: Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35.

music-theory-elementary.l19.q1.p: Which composer is famous for ragtime pieces such as Maple Leaf Rag?
music-theory-elementary.l19.q1.e: Scott Joplin wrote Maple Leaf Rag and is known for ragtime.

music-theory-elementary.l19.q2.p: Which Russian composer wrote the ballet The Nutcracker?
music-theory-elementary.l19.q2.e: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky composed The Nutcracker.

music-theory-elementary.l19.q3.p: Clara Schumann was both a pianist and a composer.
music-theory-elementary.l19.q3.e: Clara Schumann was a celebrated pianist who also composed songs and piano music.

music-theory-elementary.l19.q4.p: Which composer was Clara Schumann married to?
music-theory-elementary.l19.q4.e: Clara married the composer Robert Schumann.

music-theory-elementary.l19.q5.p: Which feature is a hallmark of ragtime?
music-theory-elementary.l19.q5.e: Ragtime is known for syncopated rhythms.

music-theory-elementary.l20.q1.t: Choose a key and a time signature
music-theory-elementary.l20.q1.p: What is a good first step when composing a short melody?
music-theory-elementary.l20.q1.e: Choosing a key and time signature gives you the notes and beat grouping to work with.

music-theory-elementary.l20.q2.p: A four-measure melody in 4/4 contains 16 quarter-note beats.
music-theory-elementary.l20.q2.e: Four measures of four beats each make 16 beats.

music-theory-elementary.l20.q3.p: You write 2 measures in 4/4. How many quarter-note beats must you fill?
music-theory-elementary.l20.q3.e: Two measures with four beats each need 8 beats.

music-theory-elementary.l20.q4.p: Which ending note most strongly makes a tune in C major sound finished?
music-theory-elementary.l20.q4.e: Ending on the tonic gives the strongest sense of arrival.

music-theory-elementary.l20.q5.p: A 3/4 measure contains a dotted half note. How many more beats are needed to fill it?
music-theory-elementary.l20.q5.e: A dotted half note lasts 3 beats, which fills the 3/4 measure completely.

music-theory-secondary.l01.q1.p: The key signature of G major has one sharp, F-sharp.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q1.h: Sharps appear in the order F, C, G, D, A, E, B.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q1.e: G major has one sharp, F-sharp, which makes the step from E to the seventh degree a whole step.

music-theory-secondary.l01.q2.p: How many flats are in the key signature of F major?
music-theory-secondary.l01.q2.h: F major is the first flat key.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q2.e: F major has one flat, B-flat.

music-theory-secondary.l01.q3.p: Which major key has three sharps (F-sharp, C-sharp, G-sharp)?
music-theory-secondary.l01.q3.h: The last sharp is the leading tone; the key is a half step above it.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q3.e: The last sharp, G-sharp, is the leading tone of A, so the key is A major.

music-theory-secondary.l01.q4.p: What is the key signature of E-flat major?
music-theory-secondary.l01.q4.h: Flats are added in the order B, E, A, D, G, C, F.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q4.e: E-flat major has three flats, B-flat, E-flat and A-flat; the second-to-last flat names the key.

music-theory-secondary.l01.q5.p: A signature has the sharps F-sharp, C-sharp, G-sharp and D-sharp. Which major key is it?
music-theory-secondary.l01.q5.h: Find the last sharp, then go up a half step.
music-theory-secondary.l01.q5.e: The last sharp, D-sharp, is the leading tone, so the tonic is E.

music-theory-secondary.l02.q1.p: A minor is the relative minor of C major.
music-theory-secondary.l02.q1.h: Relative keys share a key signature.
music-theory-secondary.l02.q1.e: Both keys have no sharps or flats, and A is the sixth degree of C major.

music-theory-secondary.l02.q2.p: Which minor key shares a key signature with E-flat major?
music-theory-secondary.l02.q2.h: Go down a minor third from the major tonic.
music-theory-secondary.l02.q2.e: C minor is the relative minor of E-flat major; both have three flats.

music-theory-secondary.l02.q3.p: Compared with natural minor, which scale degree is raised in the harmonic minor scale?
music-theory-secondary.l02.q3.e: Raising the seventh degree gives the leading tone needed for a dominant chord.

music-theory-secondary.l02.q4.p: In ascending A melodic minor, which notes are raised compared with natural minor?
music-theory-secondary.l02.q4.e: Ascending melodic minor raises the sixth and seventh degrees: F to F-sharp and G to G-sharp.

music-theory-secondary.l02.q5.p: The parallel minor of D major is B minor.
music-theory-secondary.l02.q5.e: The parallel minor is D minor; B minor is the relative minor.

music-theory-secondary.l03.q1.p: Moving clockwise on the circle of fifths from C to G to D adds one sharp at each step.
music-theory-secondary.l03.q1.h: Each step is up a perfect fifth.
music-theory-secondary.l03.q1.e: C has none, G has one sharp, and D has two.

music-theory-secondary.l03.q2.p: Which major key is a perfect fifth above C major on the circle of fifths?
music-theory-secondary.l03.q2.h: Count up five letter names from C.
music-theory-secondary.l03.q2.e: G is a perfect fifth above C, and it has one sharp.

music-theory-secondary.l03.q3.p: Which major key sits one step counterclockwise from F major?
music-theory-secondary.l03.q3.e: B-flat major has two flats, one more than F major.

music-theory-secondary.l03.q4.p: Which pair of major keys is enharmonic?
music-theory-secondary.l03.q4.h: They sound the same but are spelled differently.
music-theory-secondary.l03.q4.e: B major has five sharps and C-flat major has seven flats; they sound identical.

music-theory-secondary.l03.q5.p: Which minor key has a key signature of two flats?
music-theory-secondary.l03.q5.e: G minor is the relative minor of B-flat major, which has two flats.

music-theory-secondary.l04.q1.p: Which mode uses the white keys from D to D?
music-theory-secondary.l04.q1.e: The white-key scale starting on D is D Dorian.

music-theory-secondary.l04.q2.p: Lydian is a major scale with a raised fourth degree.
music-theory-secondary.l04.q2.h: Compare F Lydian with F major.
music-theory-secondary.l04.q2.e: F Lydian has B natural where F major has B-flat; the fourth degree is raised.

music-theory-secondary.l04.q3.p: Which mode differs from the major scale only by a lowered seventh degree?
music-theory-secondary.l04.q3.h: Think of C, D, E, F, G, A, B-flat.
music-theory-secondary.l04.q3.e: Mixolydian is major with a lowered seventh.

music-theory-secondary.l04.q4.p: Which mode uses the white keys from E to E, with the characteristic half step above the tonic?
music-theory-secondary.l04.q4.e: E Phrygian has F natural, a half step above E.

music-theory-secondary.l04.q5.p: In Locrian mode, what is the interval from the tonic to the fifth degree?
music-theory-secondary.l04.q5.e: B Locrian has F natural, a diminished fifth above B, so the tonic triad is diminished.

music-theory-secondary.l05.q1.p: What is the interval from C up to E?
music-theory-secondary.l05.q1.e: C to E is four semitones across three letter names, a major third.

music-theory-secondary.l05.q2.p: How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
music-theory-secondary.l05.q2.e: A perfect fifth contains seven semitones.

music-theory-secondary.l05.q3.p: A minor sixth inverts to a major third.
music-theory-secondary.l05.q3.h: The numbers add to nine, and minor becomes major.
music-theory-secondary.l05.q3.e: Inversion changes minor to major and a sixth to a third.

music-theory-secondary.l05.q4.p: What is the interval from C up to F-sharp?
music-theory-secondary.l05.q4.h: Count letter names first: C, D, E, F.
music-theory-secondary.l05.q4.e: The letters span a fourth, and F-sharp is a semitone larger than a perfect fourth, so it is augmented.

music-theory-secondary.l05.q5.p: What is the interval from E up to B-flat?
music-theory-secondary.l05.q5.h: Letters E to B span a fifth.
music-theory-secondary.l05.q5.e: E to B is a perfect fifth, and B-flat is a semitone smaller, so the interval is a diminished fifth.

music-theory-secondary.l06.q1.p: Which notes make a G major triad?
music-theory-secondary.l06.q1.e: A G major triad is G, B, D.

music-theory-secondary.l06.q2.p: A diminished triad is made of two stacked minor thirds.
music-theory-secondary.l06.q2.e: C to E-flat and E-flat to G-flat are both minor thirds.

music-theory-secondary.l06.q3.p: Which notes make a D minor triad?
music-theory-secondary.l06.q3.e: D minor is D, F, A.

music-theory-secondary.l06.q4.p: The notes C, E, G are played with E in the bass. What is the chord position?
music-theory-secondary.l06.q4.h: The third is in the bass.
music-theory-secondary.l06.q4.e: A triad with its third in the bass is in first inversion.

music-theory-secondary.l06.q5.p: Which triad quality is built on the seventh degree of a major scale?
music-theory-secondary.l06.q5.h: In C major, the chord is B, D, F.
music-theory-secondary.l06.q5.e: B to D is a minor third and D to F is a minor third, so it is diminished.

music-theory-secondary.l07.q1.p: Which notes make a G dominant seventh chord?
music-theory-secondary.l07.q1.e: G7 is G, B, D, F.

music-theory-secondary.l07.q2.p: A dominant seventh chord is a major triad with a minor seventh above the root.
music-theory-secondary.l07.q2.e: This is the definition of a dominant seventh chord.

music-theory-secondary.l07.q3.p: In C major, the chord D, F, A, C has which quality?
music-theory-secondary.l07.q3.h: D, F, A is a minor triad.
music-theory-secondary.l07.q3.e: A minor triad plus a minor seventh (D to C) is a minor seventh chord, the ii7.

music-theory-secondary.l07.q4.p: In C major, what quality is the seventh chord B, D, F, A?
music-theory-secondary.l07.q4.h: B, D, F is diminished; A is a minor seventh above B.
music-theory-secondary.l07.q4.e: A diminished triad plus a minor seventh is half-diminished.

music-theory-secondary.l07.q5.p: Which spells a half-diminished seventh chord on C?
music-theory-secondary.l07.q5.e: C, E-flat, G-flat is diminished, and B-flat is a minor seventh above C.

music-theory-secondary.l08.q1.p: Which Roman numeral labels the chord G-B-D-F in C major?
music-theory-secondary.l08.q1.e: G, B, D, F is a dominant seventh on scale degree five, V7.

music-theory-secondary.l08.q2.p: In Roman numeral analysis, uppercase numerals indicate major triads and lowercase indicate minor triads.

music-theory-secondary.l08.q3.t: A seventh chord in first inversion
music-theory-secondary.l08.q3.p: What does the figured bass 6/5 indicate?
music-theory-secondary.l08.q3.h: It is a seventh chord figure with the third in the bass.
music-theory-secondary.l08.q3.e: The figures 6/5 mean a seventh chord with its third in the bass.

music-theory-secondary.l08.q4.p: In C major, which label fits the chord G-B-D with B in the bass?
music-theory-secondary.l08.q4.e: A dominant triad with its third in the bass is V6.

music-theory-secondary.l08.q5.p: In A minor with a raised leading tone, how is the chord E-G-sharp-B labeled?
music-theory-secondary.l08.q5.h: It is a major triad on the fifth degree.
music-theory-secondary.l08.q5.e: E, G-sharp, B is a major triad on E, the fifth degree, so it is V.

music-theory-secondary.l09.q1.p: Which time signature is a compound meter?
music-theory-secondary.l09.q1.e: 6/8 has a dotted-quarter beat that divides into three eighths.

music-theory-secondary.l09.q2.p: In 6/8 the beat is normally felt as two dotted-quarter pulses per measure.
music-theory-secondary.l09.q2.h: Group the six eighths in threes.
music-theory-secondary.l09.q2.e: The usual grouping is 3 + 3, giving two beats.

music-theory-secondary.l09.q3.e: 12/8 has four beats, each dividing into three, so it is compound quadruple.

music-theory-secondary.l09.q4.p: Which note value usually gets the beat in 6/8?
music-theory-secondary.l09.q4.e: In compound meter the beat is a dotted note, here a dotted quarter.

music-theory-secondary.l09.q5.h: Three beats, each divides into two.
music-theory-secondary.l09.q5.e: It has three beats that each divide into two, so it is simple triple.

music-theory-secondary.l10.q1.t: Emphasis on weak beats or offbeats
music-theory-secondary.l10.q1.h: It goes against the expected accents.
music-theory-secondary.l10.q1.e: Syncopation places accents where the meter does not normally put them.

music-theory-secondary.l10.q2.p: A hemiola superimposes groups of two beats on a meter normally felt in groups of three.
music-theory-secondary.l10.q2.e: Two measures of 3/4 can be felt as three groups of two beats.

music-theory-secondary.l10.q3.p: In simple meter, a triplet fits three notes into the time normally taken by how many notes of the same value?
music-theory-secondary.l10.q3.e: Triplets compress three notes into the space of two.

music-theory-secondary.l10.q4.p: Two measures of 3/4 are accented as if they were three measures of 2/4. What is this called?
music-theory-secondary.l10.q4.h: Baroque composers used it near cadences.

music-theory-secondary.l10.q5.p: Which combination fills exactly one measure of 6/8?
music-theory-secondary.l10.q5.h: Count in eighth notes; six are needed.
music-theory-secondary.l10.q5.e: A dotted quarter is three eighths, so two of them make six.

music-theory-secondary.l11.q1.p: A period consists of which two phrases?
music-theory-secondary.l11.q1.e: A period pairs an antecedent phrase with a consequent phrase.

music-theory-secondary.l11.q2.p: In a period, the antecedent phrase typically ends with a weaker cadence, often a half cadence.
music-theory-secondary.l11.q2.h: The consequent gives the stronger close.
music-theory-secondary.l11.q2.e: The antecedent ends open and the consequent closes more strongly.

music-theory-secondary.l11.q3.t: A continuation that often fragments the material and drives to a cadence
music-theory-secondary.l11.q3.p: What follows the presentation in a sentence?
music-theory-secondary.l11.q3.e: The continuation typically uses fragmentation and leads to a cadence.

music-theory-secondary.l11.q4.p: Melodic motion by step is called what?
music-theory-secondary.l11.q4.e: Stepwise motion is conjunct, and leaping motion is disjunct.

music-theory-secondary.l11.q5.t: Both phrases begin with the same or similar material
music-theory-secondary.l11.q5.h: Compare the openings of the two phrases.
music-theory-secondary.l11.q5.e: In a parallel period the consequent begins like the antecedent.

music-theory-secondary.l12.q1.p: In movable-do solfege, which syllable always names the tonic?
music-theory-secondary.l12.q1.h: It does not change with the key.
music-theory-secondary.l12.q1.e: Movable do assigns do to the tonic of whatever key is in use.

music-theory-secondary.l12.q2.p: The leading tone has a tendency to rise to the tonic.
music-theory-secondary.l12.q2.h: It is a half step below do.
music-theory-secondary.l12.q2.e: The seventh degree resolves upward by half step to the tonic.

music-theory-secondary.l12.q3.p: Which scale degree is called sol in solfege?
music-theory-secondary.l12.q3.e: Sol is the fifth degree, the dominant.

music-theory-secondary.l12.q4.p: A phrase ends on the V chord and sounds unfinished. Which cadence is it?
music-theory-secondary.l12.q4.e: A phrase that ends on V is a half cadence.

music-theory-secondary.l12.q5.p: Two pitches sounded at the same time form which kind of interval?
music-theory-secondary.l12.q5.h: Contrast with notes played in succession.
music-theory-secondary.l12.q5.e: Simultaneous notes form a harmonic interval, successive notes a melodic one.

music-theory-secondary.l13.q1.p: What is the harmonic function of the V chord?
music-theory-secondary.l13.q1.e: V is the main dominant chord and resolves to tonic.

music-theory-secondary.l13.q2.p: The ii chord normally has predominant function.
music-theory-secondary.l13.q2.e: ii is a standard predominant chord.

music-theory-secondary.l13.q3.p: Which progression follows the T-PD-D-T pattern?
music-theory-secondary.l13.q3.e: I is tonic, ii predominant, V dominant, and I tonic again.

music-theory-secondary.l13.q4.p: Which chord can substitute for I as a tonic-function chord?
music-theory-secondary.l13.q4.h: It shares two notes with I.
music-theory-secondary.l13.q4.e: vi shares two notes with I, so it can have tonic function.

music-theory-secondary.l13.q5.p: In a V7 to I resolution in C major, to which notes do the tritone B and F typically resolve?
music-theory-secondary.l13.q5.h: The leading tone rises; the seventh falls.
music-theory-secondary.l13.q5.e: B rises to C and F falls to E.

music-theory-secondary.l14.q1.p: Which cadence moves from V to I, both in root position, with the tonic in the soprano?
music-theory-secondary.l14.q1.e: This is the definition of a perfect authentic cadence.

music-theory-secondary.l14.q2.p: A half cadence ends on the V chord.
music-theory-secondary.l14.q2.e: A half cadence ends on V, whatever chord precedes it.

music-theory-secondary.l14.q3.p: Which cadence moves from V to vi?
music-theory-secondary.l14.q3.e: V to vi is a deceptive cadence.

music-theory-secondary.l14.q4.p: Which cadence moves from IV to I?
music-theory-secondary.l14.q4.e: IV to I is a plagal cadence.

music-theory-secondary.l14.q5.t: A chord is inverted or the soprano does not end on the tonic
music-theory-secondary.l14.q5.p: What distinguishes an imperfect authentic cadence from a perfect one?
music-theory-secondary.l14.q5.e: An IAC loses root-position chords or the tonic in the soprano.

music-theory-secondary.l15.q1.p: Which non-chord tone is defined as moving by step from one chord tone to a different chord tone?
music-theory-secondary.l15.q1.e: A passing tone connects two different chord tones by step.

music-theory-secondary.l15.q2.p: A neighbor tone steps away from a chord tone and returns to the same note.
music-theory-secondary.l15.q2.e: This is the definition of a neighbor tone.

music-theory-secondary.l15.q3.p: How does a suspension typically resolve?
music-theory-secondary.l15.q3.h: It is prepared, held, then resolves.
music-theory-secondary.l15.q3.e: A suspension resolves downward by step; one that resolves upward is a retardation.

music-theory-secondary.l15.q4.p: Which non-chord tone sounds a note of the next chord before the harmony changes?

music-theory-secondary.l15.q5.p: Over a G major chord, a melody moves D, C, B. How is C labeled?
music-theory-secondary.l15.q5.h: It sits between D and B.
music-theory-secondary.l15.q5.e: C connects the chord tones D and B by step, so it is a passing tone.

music-theory-secondary.l16.q1.p: Parallel perfect fifths between two voices are avoided in common-practice voice leading.
music-theory-secondary.l16.q1.e: Parallel fifths and octaves merge two voices into one.

music-theory-secondary.l16.q2.p: Which chord member is usually doubled in a root-position triad?
music-theory-secondary.l16.q2.h: It is the most stable choice.

music-theory-secondary.l16.q3.p: Adjacent upper voices (soprano-alto and alto-tenor) should be no more than how far apart?
music-theory-secondary.l16.q3.h: The tenor and bass can be wider.
music-theory-secondary.l16.q3.e: Close spacing keeps the upper three voices within an octave of each neighbor.

music-theory-secondary.l16.q4.p: How does the seventh of a V7 chord normally resolve?
music-theory-secondary.l16.q4.h: F in G7 goes to E in C.
music-theory-secondary.l16.q4.e: The chordal seventh resolves down by step.

music-theory-secondary.l16.q5.p: Doubling the leading tone is generally avoided.
music-theory-secondary.l16.q5.e: Both doubled leading tones would need to rise to the tonic, producing parallel octaves.

music-theory-secondary.l17.q1.p: In C major, which triad is V/V?
music-theory-secondary.l17.q1.e: The dominant of G is D, and a major triad on D is D, F-sharp, A.

music-theory-secondary.l17.q2.p: A secondary dominant is the dominant of a scale degree other than the tonic.

music-theory-secondary.l17.q3.p: Which spells V7/V in C major?
music-theory-secondary.l17.q3.e: A dominant seventh on D is D, F-sharp, A, C.

music-theory-secondary.l17.q4.p: In C major, which chord is V7/vi?
music-theory-secondary.l17.q4.e: The dominant of A is E, so V7/vi is E, G-sharp, B, D.

music-theory-secondary.l17.q5.p: In G major, which chord is V7/V?
music-theory-secondary.l17.q5.h: The dominant of G is D.
music-theory-secondary.l17.q5.e: The dominant of D is A, so V7/V is A, C-sharp, E, G.

music-theory-secondary.l18.q1.p: Which of the following is a closely related key to C major?
music-theory-secondary.l18.q1.h: Its signature differs by one accidental.
music-theory-secondary.l18.q1.e: G major has one sharp, one more than C major.

music-theory-secondary.l18.q2.p: A pivot chord is diatonic in both the old key and the new key.
music-theory-secondary.l18.q2.e: The pivot is reinterpreted between the keys.

music-theory-secondary.l18.q3.t: vi in C and ii in G
music-theory-secondary.l18.q3.p: In a modulation from C major to G major, A minor is a pivot chord. What is it in each key?
music-theory-secondary.l18.q3.h: Count scale degrees in each key.
music-theory-secondary.l18.q3.e: In G major, A is the second degree, so A minor is ii.

music-theory-secondary.l18.q4.p: A piece in A minor typically modulates to which key?
music-theory-secondary.l18.q4.e: The relative major, here C major, is the most common destination.

music-theory-secondary.l18.q5.p: Which key is NOT closely related to D major?
music-theory-secondary.l18.q5.e: E-flat major has three flats while D major has two sharps, so the signatures differ by five.

music-theory-secondary.l19.q1.p: Which letter pattern describes ternary form?
music-theory-secondary.l19.q1.e: Ternary form returns to A after a contrasting B.

music-theory-secondary.l19.q2.p: A rondo features a refrain that returns between contrasting episodes.
music-theory-secondary.l19.q2.e: This is the defining trait of rondo form.

music-theory-secondary.l19.q3.p: Which letter pattern is a five-part rondo?
music-theory-secondary.l19.q3.e: The refrain A returns between episodes B and C.

music-theory-secondary.l19.q4.t: The opening material returns near the end of the B section
music-theory-secondary.l19.q4.p: What makes a binary form rounded?
music-theory-secondary.l19.q4.e: Rounded binary brings back the opening material within the second section.

music-theory-secondary.l19.q5.p: In a Baroque binary form in a major key, the first section typically ends in which key?
music-theory-secondary.l19.q5.h: It moves away from the home key.
music-theory-secondary.l19.q5.e: The first section usually moves to the dominant key.

music-theory-secondary.l20.q1.p: What is the order of the three main sonata form sections?
music-theory-secondary.l20.q1.e: The three sections are exposition, development and recapitulation.

music-theory-secondary.l20.q2.p: In a major-key sonata exposition, the second theme is usually in the dominant key.
music-theory-secondary.l20.q2.e: The second theme normally appears in the dominant key.

music-theory-secondary.l20.q3.t: Themes are developed through several keys
music-theory-secondary.l20.q3.p: What happens in the development section?
music-theory-secondary.l20.q3.h: It is the middle of the form.
music-theory-secondary.l20.q3.e: The development takes up exposition material and modulates freely.

music-theory-secondary.l20.q4.p: In which key does the second theme usually appear in the recapitulation?
music-theory-secondary.l20.q4.e: The second theme returns in the tonic.

music-theory-secondary.l20.q5.p: In a minor-key sonata exposition, which key is usually the second key area?
music-theory-secondary.l20.q5.e: The relative major is the usual second key.

music-theory-secondary.l21.q1.p: Which notes make a Cmaj7 chord?
music-theory-secondary.l21.q1.e: Cmaj7 is C, E, G, B.

music-theory-secondary.l21.q2.p: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7 is a ii-V-I progression in C major.
music-theory-secondary.l21.q2.h: Dm7 is on the second degree.
music-theory-secondary.l21.q2.e: The roots are D, G and C, scale degrees 2, 5 and 1.

music-theory-secondary.l21.q3.p: Which notes make a C9 chord?
music-theory-secondary.l21.q3.e: C9 is C7 with a D added.

music-theory-secondary.l21.q4.p: Which chord is the usual tritone substitute for G7?
music-theory-secondary.l21.q4.h: A tritone from G is D-flat.
music-theory-secondary.l21.q4.e: D-flat 7 is a tritone away from G7.

music-theory-secondary.l21.q5.t: They share the same tritone, B and F (spelled F and C-flat)
music-theory-secondary.l21.q5.h: Compare the third and seventh of each.
music-theory-secondary.l21.q5.e: Both contain the same tritone, with one chord spelling B as C-flat.

music-theory-secondary.l22.q1.p: In C major, which chords make up I, V, vi, IV?
music-theory-secondary.l22.q1.e: I is C, V is G, vi is Am and IV is F.

music-theory-secondary.l22.q2.p: The standard 12-bar blues uses the I, IV and V chords.
music-theory-secondary.l22.q2.e: The form is built from I, IV and V.

music-theory-secondary.l22.q3.p: In a 12-bar blues in C, which chord is usually played in bar 5?
music-theory-secondary.l22.q3.h: The second line begins with IV.
music-theory-secondary.l22.q3.e: Bars 5 and 6 usually move to IV.

music-theory-secondary.l22.q4.t: C, E-flat, F, G-flat, G, B-flat
music-theory-secondary.l22.q4.p: Which spells the C blues scale?
music-theory-secondary.l22.q4.h: It contains the lowered third, fifth and seventh.
music-theory-secondary.l22.q4.e: The blues scale is 1, flat 3, 4, flat 5, 5, flat 7.

music-theory-secondary.l22.q5.p: Which chords make up vi, IV, I, V in C major?
music-theory-secondary.l22.q5.e: vi is Am, IV is F, I is C and V is G.

music-theory-secondary.l23.q1.p: Which of these appears on a lead sheet?
music-theory-secondary.l23.q1.e: A lead sheet gives the melody, chord symbols and lyrics.

music-theory-secondary.l23.q2.p: The slash chord C/E means a C major chord with E in the bass.
music-theory-secondary.l23.q2.h: The note after the slash is the bass.
music-theory-secondary.l23.q2.e: C/E is a first-inversion C chord.

music-theory-secondary.l23.q3.t: Return to the beginning and play to the word Fine
music-theory-secondary.l23.q3.p: What does D.C. al Fine instruct a player to do?
music-theory-secondary.l23.q3.e: It means go back to the beginning and play to Fine.

music-theory-secondary.l23.q4.p: Which notes make an Am7 chord?
music-theory-secondary.l23.q4.e: Am7 is A, C, E, G.

music-theory-secondary.l23.q5.t: G major with B in the bass
music-theory-secondary.l23.q5.p: What does the symbol G/B mean?
music-theory-secondary.l23.q5.e: G/B is G major in first inversion.

music-theory-secondary.l24.q1.p: Which family includes the oboe, clarinet and bassoon?

music-theory-secondary.l24.q2.p: Concert pitch is the actual sounding pitch.
music-theory-secondary.l24.q2.h: It is not the written pitch.
music-theory-secondary.l24.q2.e: Concert pitch is the real sound produced.

music-theory-secondary.l24.q3.p: An E-flat alto saxophone sounds which interval below its written pitch?
music-theory-secondary.l24.q3.h: A written C sounds as E-flat.
music-theory-secondary.l24.q3.e: A written C sounds as the E-flat a major sixth below.

music-theory-secondary.l24.q4.p: Which instrument sounds an octave lower than written?
music-theory-secondary.l24.q4.e: The double bass sounds an octave below its written pitch.

music-theory-secondary.l24.q5.p: A B-flat trumpet plays a written D. What concert pitch sounds?
music-theory-secondary.l24.q5.h: It sounds a major second lower.
music-theory-secondary.l24.q5.e: A major second below D is C.

music-theory.l01.q1.p: How many natural note names does Western music use?
music-theory.l01.q1.h: They run from A to G.
music-theory.l01.q1.e: The natural notes are A, B, C, D, E, F and G, after which the pattern repeats an octave higher.

music-theory.l01.q2.p: What is the name for the distance between a note and the next note with the same letter name?
music-theory.l01.q2.h: It sounds like the same note, higher or lower.
music-theory.l01.q2.e: The repetition of the seven letter names at a higher pitch is called an octave.

music-theory.l01.q3.p: A singer starts a tune on C4 and then repeats it exactly one octave higher. On which note does the repeated tune start?
music-theory.l01.q3.e: Moving up one octave keeps the letter name and raises the octave number by one, so C4 becomes C5.

music-theory.l01.q4.t: The piano spans a much wider range of pitches
music-theory.l01.q4.p: A full piano covers A0 to C8 on 88 keys. What does this tell you about its range compared with a violin (about G3 to A7)?
music-theory.l01.q4.h: Compare the lowest and highest notes.
music-theory.l01.q4.e: The piano reaches far lower and higher than the violin, and has the widest range of any common acoustic instrument.

music-theory.l02.q1.t: The distance from one key to the very next key on a piano
music-theory.l02.q1.h: It is also called a half step.
music-theory.l02.q1.e: A semitone, or half step, is the smallest step in Western music.

music-theory.l02.q2.p: What does a flat sign do to a note?
music-theory.l02.q2.e: A flat lowers a note by one semitone, and a sharp raises it by one.

music-theory.l02.q3.p: Start on C and go up three semitones. Which note do you reach?
music-theory.l02.q3.h: Count the keys: C-sharp, D, then one more.
music-theory.l02.q3.e: C to C-sharp is 1, to D is 2, and to D-sharp (E-flat) is 3 semitones.

music-theory.l02.q4.t: Those pairs of white keys are already one semitone apart
music-theory.l02.q4.p: Why is there no black key between E and F or between B and C?
music-theory.l02.q4.h: Think about how many semitones are in an octave and how many white keys there are.
music-theory.l02.q4.e: E to F and B to C are already a single semitone, so no extra key fits between them.

music-theory.l03.q1.p: How many lines does a staff have?
music-theory.l03.q1.h: There are four spaces between them.
music-theory.l03.q1.e: A staff is made of five horizontal lines.

music-theory.l03.q2.t: It tells which pitches the lines and spaces stand for
music-theory.l03.q2.h: It sits at the start of the staff.
music-theory.l03.q2.e: A clef fixes the pitch of the lines, so the same staff can be read for high or low instruments.

music-theory.l03.q3.t: Bass clef for the cello and treble clef for the flute
music-theory.l03.q3.p: A cello part and a flute part both appear in a score. Which clefs would you most likely expect?
music-theory.l03.q3.h: The cello is a low instrument.
music-theory.l03.q3.e: Low instruments like the cello usually read bass clef, and high instruments like the flute read treble clef.

music-theory.l03.q4.t: The viola's range is lower, and the alto clef keeps its notes on the staff
music-theory.l03.q4.p: Why does a viola part use a different clef from a violin part?
music-theory.l03.q4.e: The viola is tuned a fifth below the violin and reads alto clef, which fits its middle range.

music-theory.l04.q1.p: How many beats does a half note last?
music-theory.l04.q1.e: A half note is half of a whole note, so it lasts two beats.

music-theory.l04.q2.t: A written silence with a duration
music-theory.l04.q2.e: Each note value has a matching rest that tells the player how long to be silent.

music-theory.l04.q3.p: The tempo is 120 beats per minute. How long does one beat last?
music-theory.l04.q3.e: 60 seconds divided by 120 beats is 0.5 seconds per beat.

music-theory.l04.q4.t: The real duration of every note doubles, but the written note values stay the same
music-theory.l04.q4.p: A piece is played at half the original tempo. What changes and what stays the same?
music-theory.l04.q4.h: Note values are relative to the beat.
music-theory.l04.q4.e: Note values are relative, so a slower tempo lengthens each beat in seconds without changing what is written.

music-theory.l05.q1.t: There are four beats in each measure
music-theory.l05.q1.p: In a 4/4 time signature, what does the top number tell you?
music-theory.l05.q1.e: The top number gives the beats per measure, and the bottom number says a quarter note gets one beat.

music-theory.l05.q2.p: Which time signature gives a waltz feel?
music-theory.l05.q2.e: 3/4 has three beats in each measure, which is the waltz feel.

music-theory.l05.q3.p: A measure of 3/4 contains a half note. Which note completes the measure?
music-theory.l05.q3.e: A half note is two beats, so one more beat, a quarter note, fills the three-beat measure.

music-theory.l05.q4.t: As two groups of three eighth notes, rather than three equal beats
music-theory.l05.q4.p: How is a measure of 6/8 felt, compared with 3/4?
music-theory.l05.q4.h: Remember how the six eighth notes are grouped.
music-theory.l05.q4.e: 6/8 groups its six eighth notes into two sets of three, giving a compound rhythm with two main pulses.

music-theory.l06.q1.p: What is the step pattern of a major scale?
music-theory.l06.q1.h: Two wholes, a half, three wholes, a half.
music-theory.l06.q1.e: The major scale is W-W-H-W-W-W-H, as in C-D-E-F-G-A-B-C.

music-theory.l06.q2.p: How many major keys are there in total?
music-theory.l06.q2.h: One for each of the twelve tones.
music-theory.l06.q2.e: There are twelve major keys, one for each starting pitch in the twelve-tone system.

music-theory.l06.q3.p: The major scale pattern W-W-H-W-W-W-H has how many semitones in total?
music-theory.l06.q3.h: A whole step is 2 semitones and a half step is 1.

music-theory.l06.q4.t: To keep the same step pattern, with a half step from the seventh note up to G
music-theory.l06.q4.p: Why does the G major scale contain F-sharp rather than F?
music-theory.l06.q4.h: Check the steps between E, F and G.
music-theory.l06.q4.e: Going E to F-sharp is a whole step and F-sharp to G is a half step, matching the pattern. F natural would break it.

music-theory.l07.q1.p: Which of these intervals is called perfect?
music-theory.l07.q1.h: Perfect intervals are unison, fourth, fifth and octave.
music-theory.l07.q1.e: The unison, fourth, fifth and octave are the perfect intervals.

music-theory.l07.q2.p: How many semitones are in a major third?
music-theory.l07.q2.e: A major third, such as C to E, spans four semitones.

music-theory.l07.q3.p: What is the interval from C up to E-flat?
music-theory.l07.q3.h: It spans three letter names and three semitones.
music-theory.l07.q3.e: C to E-flat spans three letter names, with three semitones, so it is a minor third.

music-theory.l07.q4.t: The third is one semitone lower in the minor triad
music-theory.l07.q4.p: What single difference separates a major triad from a minor triad built on the same root?
music-theory.l07.q4.e: A major third is four semitones and a minor third is three, and this one semitone changes the chord's character.

music-theory.l08.q1.p: What is the frequency ratio of an octave?
music-theory.l08.q1.h: The upper note vibrates twice as fast.
music-theory.l08.q1.e: An octave is a 2:1 ratio, so the upper note has double the frequency.

music-theory.l08.q2.p: What is the frequency ratio of a perfect fifth?
music-theory.l08.q2.h: Multiply by one and a half.
music-theory.l08.q2.e: A perfect fifth is a 3:2 ratio.

music-theory.l08.q3.p: A string vibrates at 220 Hz. What is the frequency of the note a perfect fifth above it?

music-theory.l08.q4.p: Which pair of frequencies forms a perfect fifth?
music-theory.l08.q4.h: Divide the higher by the lower and look for 1.5.
music-theory.l08.q4.e: 450 / 300 = 1.5, which is 3:2. The pair 300 and 600 is an octave, and 300 and 400 is a 4:3 fourth.

music-theory.l09.q1.p: Which notes make up a C major triad?
music-theory.l09.q1.e: A C major triad is C-E-G: a root, a major third and a perfect fifth.

music-theory.l09.q2.t: The third is lowered by one semitone
music-theory.l09.q2.p: What is the only difference between C major and C minor triads?
music-theory.l09.q2.e: C minor has E-flat instead of E, a minor third in place of a major third.

music-theory.l09.q3.p: Which notes make up a G major triad?
music-theory.l09.q3.h: Count four semitones, then three more.
music-theory.l09.q3.e: From G, four semitones gives B and seven gives D, so the triad is G-B-D.

music-theory.l09.q4.t: Two minor thirds stacked on top of each other
music-theory.l09.q4.p: A diminished triad is described as root, minor third and diminished fifth. How is it built from thirds?
music-theory.l09.q4.h: Think of what the major triad does.
music-theory.l09.q4.e: A diminished triad stacks two minor thirds, while a major triad stacks a major third and then a minor third.

music-theory.l10.q1.p: Which chord in a key is called the tonic?
music-theory.l10.q1.e: The I chord, the tonic, is the home chord of a key.

music-theory.l10.q2.t: To create tension that wants to resolve to I
music-theory.l10.q2.p: What is the usual job of the V chord?
music-theory.l10.q2.e: The dominant creates tension and pulls back toward the tonic.

music-theory.l10.q3.p: In C major, which notes make up the dominant seventh chord G7?
music-theory.l10.q3.h: Stack another third on top of G-B-D.
music-theory.l10.q3.e: A seventh chord adds a fourth note a third above the fifth, so G7 is G-B-D-F.

music-theory.l10.q4.t: The bass notes outline the chord roots and imply the harmony
music-theory.l10.q4.p: Why can a single cello line, such as in Bach's suites, still suggest a full chord progression?
music-theory.l10.q4.h: Think about which notes mark chord changes.
music-theory.l10.q4.e: Following the bass notes reveals the chords the line implies, even though they are never fully played.

music-theory.l11.q1.p: Which mode is the same as the major scale?
music-theory.l11.q1.e: Ionian is the first mode and is identical to the major scale.

music-theory.l11.q2.p: Which mode is the natural minor scale?
music-theory.l11.q2.h: It starts on the sixth degree.
music-theory.l11.q2.e: Aeolian, the sixth mode, is the natural minor.

music-theory.l11.q3.p: You play the white keys on a piano from D up to the next D. Which mode do you hear?
music-theory.l11.q3.h: D is the second note of the C major scale.
music-theory.l11.q3.e: A rotation of C major starting on D, its second degree, is Dorian.

music-theory.l11.q4.t: The focus is on the colour of the mode rather than the pull to a dominant chord
music-theory.l11.q4.p: Why do modal pieces such as Kind of Blue often sound more static than pieces built on I-IV-V-I?
music-theory.l11.q4.h: Think about what drives motion in a I-IV-V-I progression.
music-theory.l11.q4.e: Modal harmony sits on one chord or related chords, so the pull of dominant resolution gives way to the mode's own colour.

music-theory.l12.q1.p: What is the vibrating source in a brass instrument?
music-theory.l12.q1.h: It is not an object in the instrument.
music-theory.l12.q1.e: In brass instruments the player's lips buzz, and the tubing selects which harmonic sounds.

music-theory.l12.q2.h: The player splits an airstream against an edge.
music-theory.l12.q2.e: The flute is the only orchestral woodwind without a reed.

music-theory.l12.q3.t: The pitch is lowered, because a longer tube gives a lower harmonic series
music-theory.l12.q3.p: A trombonist moves the slide out to lengthen the tube. What is the effect?
music-theory.l12.q3.e: Changing the length of tubing selects a different harmonic series. A longer tube gives lower notes.

music-theory.l12.q4.t: The same layout can drive hammers, plectra, pipes, tines or oscillators
music-theory.l12.q4.p: Why is a keyboard described as an interface rather than a sound source?
music-theory.l12.q4.h: Think about the piano, organ and synthesiser.
music-theory.l12.q4.e: Different keyboard instruments use the same keys to trigger very different sound mechanisms.

music-theory.l13.q1.p: Which instrument sounds an octave higher than written?
music-theory.l13.q1.h: It is half the length of a concert flute.
music-theory.l13.q1.e: The piccolo sounds one octave above written, while the double bass and guitar sound an octave below.

music-theory.l13.q2.p: Which instrument do orchestras tune to?
music-theory.l13.q2.e: The oboe's pitch is very stable, so the orchestra tunes to its A.

music-theory.l13.q3.p: A B-flat trumpet player reads a written C. Which note actually sounds?
music-theory.l13.q3.h: It sounds a major second below written.
music-theory.l13.q3.e: A B-flat trumpet sounds a major second below written pitch, so written C sounds B-flat.

music-theory.l13.q4.t: It lets a player move between sizes easily
music-theory.l13.q4.p: Why do saxophones of different sizes share the same fingerings?
music-theory.l13.q4.h: Consider what a performer gains from this.
music-theory.l13.q4.e: Saxophones are a family designed with shared fingerings so players can switch between them.

music-theory.l14.q1.p: What are the three main sections of sonata form?
music-theory.l14.q1.h: The themes are presented, explored and returned.
music-theory.l14.q1.e: Sonata form presents themes in the exposition, explores them in the development and returns to them in the recapitulation.

music-theory.l14.q2.t: One voice states the subject alone
music-theory.l14.q2.h: Voices enter one at a time.
music-theory.l14.q2.e: A fugue opens with a single voice stating the subject, and the others enter in turn.

music-theory.l14.q3.p: Pachelbel's Canon repeats a two-bar ground bass 28 times. How many bars is that in total?
music-theory.l14.q3.h: Multiply the bars by the repeats.

music-theory.l14.q4.t: They make the voices merge into one instead of staying independent
music-theory.l14.q4.p: Why does counterpoint forbid parallel fifths and octaves between voices?
music-theory.l14.q4.e: Parallel fifths and octaves make two voices sound like one, and counterpoint depends on independent lines.

publishing-business.l01.q1.p: A comp (comparable title) is a recent, similar book used to show who the reader is and where your book fits.
publishing-business.l01.q1.h: Think about how agents and booksellers describe a book to others.
publishing-business.l01.q1.e: Comps show the existing audience and market position, which is why agents and editors ask for them.

publishing-business.l01.q2.t: First-time managers who want a simple weekly one-to-one routine
publishing-business.l01.q2.p: An author says her nonfiction book is "for anyone who wants to be happier." Which revision best defines a reader?
publishing-business.l01.q2.h: Look for a person you could picture and find.
publishing-business.l01.q2.e: A specific reader with a specific problem makes the book findable and the promise testable.

publishing-business.l01.q3.t: Her length is far outside the shelf norm, so she should consider cutting or choosing a different audience
publishing-business.l01.q3.p: A novelist's three best comps are all about 70,000 words, but her draft is 150,000 words. What is the most useful conclusion?
publishing-business.l01.q3.h: Compare the draft to what the reader already buys.
publishing-business.l01.q3.e: Large gaps from comparable books signal a possible mismatch with reader expectations.

publishing-business.l01.q4.t: It tests whether the story has a clear engine and can be described to a reader
publishing-business.l01.q4.p: Why is a one-sentence premise (protagonist, want, obstacle) useful BEFORE drafting?
publishing-business.l01.q4.h: What can you check cheaply before spending months?
publishing-business.l01.q4.e: A premise exposes a missing want or obstacle early, when fixing it is cheap.

publishing-business.l01.q5.t: This book covers many topics related to work.
publishing-business.l01.q5.p: Which is the weakest statement of a nonfiction promise?
publishing-business.l01.q5.h: A strong promise names something the reader can do.
publishing-business.l01.q5.e: Vague coverage is not a promise; the others each name a concrete outcome.

publishing-business.l02.q1.p: In a three-act structure, what usually happens in the middle act?
publishing-business.l02.q1.h: The word to think about is confrontation.
publishing-business.l02.q1.e: Act two is where obstacles rise and stakes increase.

publishing-business.l02.q2.p: Using the lesson's rule of thumb, a 60,000-word thriller places its inciting incident at 10 percent. At which word does it occur?

publishing-business.l02.q3.t: The turn arrives late (70 percent), so the middle may sag or the pacing needs rebalancing
publishing-business.l02.q3.p: By the lesson's beat-sheet guideline, a 60,000-word novel has its midpoint at 50 percent. A draft's midpoint falls at word 42,000. What is the best conclusion?
publishing-business.l02.q3.e: 42,000 / 60,000 = 70 percent, well after the midpoint, suggesting a slow first half.

publishing-business.l02.q4.t: It lists what each scene or chapter actually does, exposing sags and repeats
publishing-business.l02.q4.p: Why is a reverse outline helpful during revision?
publishing-business.l02.q4.h: It is made from the finished draft, not the plan.
publishing-business.l02.q4.e: Summarising what is on the page reveals where the structure fails.

publishing-business.l02.q5.t: Each chapter states a problem, teaches a principle, gives an example and ends with an exercise
publishing-business.l02.q5.p: Which chapter plan best fits a prescriptive nonfiction book?
publishing-business.l02.q5.h: Think of a repeatable pattern that serves the reader.
publishing-business.l02.q5.e: A repeated framework gives readers a predictable path to the promised outcome.

publishing-business.l03.q1.t: To exist, so there is a whole manuscript to revise
publishing-business.l03.q1.p: What is the main job of a first draft?
publishing-business.l03.q1.h: Think about what you cannot revise.
publishing-business.l03.q1.e: You can only improve a complete draft; polish comes in revision.

publishing-business.l03.q2.p: An author writes 500 words a day, 5 days a week. How many words is that per week?
publishing-business.l03.q2.h: Multiply daily words by working days.

publishing-business.l03.q3.p: Using that pace (2,500 words a week), how many weeks does an 80,000-word draft take?
publishing-business.l03.q3.h: Divide the target by the weekly output.

publishing-business.l03.q4.t: It protects momentum while keeping a record of the problem
publishing-business.l03.q4.p: Why leave a bracketed note like [fix timeline] instead of fixing it immediately?
publishing-business.l03.q4.h: Consider what constant fixing does to flow.
publishing-business.l03.q4.e: Notes separate generating from judging, so the draft keeps moving and the issue is not lost.

publishing-business.l03.q5.t: A short, fixed daily session with a tracked word count
publishing-business.l03.q5.p: Which routine is most likely to finish a book?
publishing-business.l03.q5.e: Consistent small sessions keep the story active and progress measurable.

publishing-business.l04.q1.p: In a sensible revision order, what comes first?
publishing-business.l04.q1.e: Structural problems must be solved before polishing sentences.

publishing-business.l04.q2.p: An author cuts 10 percent from a 90,000-word draft. What is the new length?
publishing-business.l04.q2.h: Find ten percent first, then subtract.

publishing-business.l04.q3.t: A style sheet recording names, spellings and facts
publishing-business.l04.q3.p: An author discovers that a character's eye colour changes between chapters. Which tool prevents this?
publishing-business.l04.q3.e: A style sheet is a running record that keeps facts consistent across the manuscript.

publishing-business.l04.q4.t: The chapter may be removed, so the polish work is wasted
publishing-business.l04.q4.p: Why is proofreading typos before deciding whether to cut a chapter inefficient?
publishing-business.l04.q4.e: Polishing material you later delete wastes effort; do structural decisions first.

publishing-business.l04.q5.t: Authors tend to see what they meant rather than what is on the page
publishing-business.l04.q5.p: What is the main limitation of self-editing?
publishing-business.l04.q5.h: Think about familiarity with your own text.
publishing-business.l04.q5.e: Familiarity makes errors invisible, which is why outside readers and editors add value.

publishing-business.l05.q1.p: Which stage is the LAST check on typeset pages?
publishing-business.l05.q1.e: Proofreading catches errors left on the typeset proofs and does not restructure.

publishing-business.l05.q2.p: An author wants advice on reordering chapters and fixing a sagging middle. Which service fits?
publishing-business.l05.q2.e: Developmental editors address pacing, structure and organisation.

publishing-business.l05.q3.t: Consider the underlying pacing problem and solve it, perhaps differently
publishing-business.l05.q3.p: An editor's letter says a subplot slows the book and suggests cutting it. The author feels the proposed cut is wrong. A sound response is:
publishing-business.l05.q3.h: Separate the problem from the suggested fix.
publishing-business.l05.q3.e: Authors decide, but they should address the problem the editor identified.

publishing-business.l05.q4.t: Polished sentences may be cut or rewritten when the structure changes
publishing-business.l05.q4.p: Why is hiring a copyeditor before a developmental edit usually wasteful?
publishing-business.l05.q4.e: Large structural changes undo sentence-level work, so finer stages come later.

publishing-business.l05.q5.t: A sample edit of the same few pages and a clear list of what each service includes
publishing-business.l05.q5.p: Which request is the best way to compare two freelance editors?
publishing-business.l05.q5.e: Samples and scoped service lists reveal what you actually get, since terminology overlaps.

publishing-business.l06.q1.t: After your own revisions, before final editing
publishing-business.l06.q1.p: When are beta readers most useful?
publishing-business.l06.q1.h: The book must be readable but still changeable.
publishing-business.l06.q1.e: A complete, revised draft can be read straight through while changes remain cheap.

publishing-business.l06.q2.t: Two thirds; a strong signal to examine that chapter
publishing-business.l06.q2.p: Of 6 beta readers, 4 stall at the same chapter. What fraction is that, and what should you conclude?
publishing-business.l06.q2.e: 4/6 = 2/3, enough agreement to treat the chapter as a likely problem.

publishing-business.l06.q3.t: Note it but do not change it unless more evidence appears
publishing-business.l06.q3.p: One reader of eight dislikes your main character's name; the other seven do not mention it. Best action?
publishing-business.l06.q3.h: One voice among eight is weak evidence.
publishing-business.l06.q3.e: A single reaction is an opinion; patterns across readers are what justify changes.

publishing-business.l06.q4.t: Where did you first feel bored or confused?
publishing-business.l06.q4.p: Which question produces the most useful beta-reader feedback?
publishing-business.l06.q4.e: Specific questions draw out where the experience broke, which can be compared across readers.

publishing-business.l06.q5.t: They hold the genre's expectations and can say whether the book meets them
publishing-business.l06.q5.p: Why choose beta readers who enjoy the book's genre?
publishing-business.l06.q5.e: Feedback is only useful from people who resemble the intended readers.

publishing-business.l07.q1.t: Readers expect certain elements, such as tone or ending, from the genre
publishing-business.l07.q1.p: What does it mean to call a genre a promise to the reader?
publishing-business.l07.q1.e: Readers pick a genre for specific experiences; failing to deliver them feels like a broken promise.

publishing-business.l07.q2.t: Readers of the label may feel cheated because it breaks genre expectations
publishing-business.l07.q2.p: A manuscript labelled as cosy mystery ends with the detective's death and the culprit escaping. What is the risk?
publishing-business.l07.q2.h: Compare the ending to what the label promises.
publishing-business.l07.q2.e: Cosy readers expect a fair, satisfying solution; breaking it without repositioning risks disappointment.

publishing-business.l07.q3.t: Check recent comps and consider trimming or repositioning
publishing-business.l07.q3.p: A debut novel is far longer than the usual range for its genre. Which step is wisest?
publishing-business.l07.q3.e: Typical lengths guide acceptable ranges; adjusting or repositioning can improve the book's chance.

publishing-business.l07.q4.t: A category is the label that decides where a book is shelved or listed for sale
publishing-business.l07.q4.p: How does a retail category differ from a craft genre?
publishing-business.l07.q4.e: Categories help sellers file the book; genre describes the reading experience and conventions.

publishing-business.l07.q5.t: They shape protagonist age, themes, length and where the book is marketed
publishing-business.l07.q5.p: Why do age categories (middle grade, young adult, adult) matter to authors?
publishing-business.l07.q5.e: Age categories set expectations about content, style and length for readers and gatekeepers.

publishing-business.l08.q1.t: A one-page pitch sent to an agent or editor
publishing-business.l08.q1.h: It is short and sent first.
publishing-business.l08.q1.e: Queries are brief professional pitches used to ask an agent to read more.

publishing-business.l08.q2.p: A nonfiction proposal outlines 12 chapters of about 5,000 words each. What total word count should it state?

publishing-business.l08.q3.t: The writer ignored the guidelines, which signals poor professionalism
publishing-business.l08.q3.p: An agent's guidelines request a query plus the first 10 pages pasted in the email body. A writer sends a full attachment of 300 pages. What is the best judgement?
publishing-business.l08.q3.e: Following each agent's submission instructions is a basic professional expectation.

publishing-business.l08.q4.t: Publishers judge whether the author can reach readers, since the book is sold before it is written
publishing-business.l08.q4.p: Why does a nonfiction proposal include a platform and marketing section?
publishing-business.l08.q4.h: Consider the business risk for the publisher.
publishing-business.l08.q4.e: A proposal is a business case; author reach and plans help show the book can sell.

publishing-business.l08.q5.t: When a lighthouse keeper hides a smuggler, the harbour inspector's suspicion threatens both their lives.
publishing-business.l08.q5.p: Which opening line of a query is strongest?
publishing-business.l08.q5.h: Look for protagonist, goal and stakes.
publishing-business.l08.q5.e: A good hook shows who wants what and what is at risk, instead of making claims.

publishing-business.l09.q1.p: A reputable literary agent charges a reading fee before considering your manuscript.
publishing-business.l09.q1.h: Think about how legitimate agents are paid.
publishing-business.l09.q1.e: Reputable agents work on commission, and the AAR canon prohibits reading and evaluation fees.

publishing-business.l09.q2.p: A book sells for a 12,000 dollar advance and the agent commission is 15 percent. How much does the author receive before taxes?

publishing-business.l09.q3.t: Be cautious: this is a recognised warning sign, so verify the agent's sales record
publishing-business.l09.q3.p: An agent offers to represent you if you first pay 500 dollars for a manuscript assessment. The best response is:
publishing-business.l09.q3.e: Upfront fees are a red flag that advocacy groups warn about; reputable agents earn commission on sales.

publishing-business.l09.q4.t: Checking royalty statements and negotiating contract terms
publishing-business.l09.q4.p: Beyond selling the manuscript, which agent task most directly protects an author later?
publishing-business.l09.q4.h: Think of ongoing money and rights.
publishing-business.l09.q4.e: Agents scrutinise contracts and statements, which is where authors can lose money or rights.

publishing-business.l09.q5.t: It governs what happens, and who is paid, if the relationship ends
publishing-business.l09.q5.p: Why should an author read the agency agreement's termination clause?
publishing-business.l09.q5.e: Termination terms decide how long commissions continue and which deals the agent keeps rights to.

publishing-business.l10.q1.t: Money paid up front that the publisher recoups from your royalties
publishing-business.l10.q1.e: An advance is an up-front payment against future royalties; it is generally not repaid if the book fails to earn out.

publishing-business.l10.q2.p: A book earns 2 dollars per copy in royalties and the advance is 10,000 dollars. How many copies must sell to earn out?

publishing-business.l10.q3.p: Using the same terms (2 dollars per copy, 10,000 dollar advance), 8,000 copies sell. What royalty cheque beyond the advance does the author get, before agent commission?

publishing-business.l10.q4.t: Royalties of 6,000 dollars fall short of the advance, and the author normally keeps the full advance
publishing-business.l10.q4.p: Only 3,000 copies sell on those terms. What is true?
publishing-business.l10.q4.h: Compare earned royalties to advance, then recall repayment rules.
publishing-business.l10.q4.e: 3,000 x 2 = 6,000, below 10,000; the book is unearned, but advances are generally non-returnable absent breach.

publishing-business.l10.q5.t: Retailers can return unsold copies, so publishers keep a reserve against returns
publishing-business.l10.q5.p: Why may statements hold back part of earnings for a time?
publishing-business.l10.q5.e: Returns reduce net sales, so contracts often allow a reserve against returns.

publishing-business.l11.q1.t: It earns its money mainly from author fees rather than book sales
publishing-business.l11.q1.p: What is the defining feature of a vanity press?
publishing-business.l11.q1.e: Vanity presses profit from authors, so they have little incentive to sell books.

publishing-business.l11.q2.p: A company charges 4,000 dollars and the author earns only 800 dollars in sales revenue. What is the author's net position, ignoring time?

publishing-business.l11.q3.t: A minimum number of copies the author must buy
publishing-business.l11.q3.p: Which clause is a red flag in a publishing contract?
publishing-business.l11.q3.e: Forcing authors to buy copies is a recognised sign of a vanity or predatory model.

publishing-business.l11.q4.t: The selectivity claim may be false and revenue may depend on author fees
publishing-business.l11.q4.p: A publisher claims to be highly selective, but a writer sees it accepts nearly every submission within a day. What does that suggest?
publishing-business.l11.q4.e: Quick acceptance of almost all manuscripts conflicts with selectivity and is a vanity warning sign.

publishing-business.l11.q5.t: Transparent services and costs, author-friendly rights terms, selectivity and real distribution
publishing-business.l11.q5.p: What makes a hybrid publisher acceptable rather than predatory?
publishing-business.l11.q5.e: Clear terms, rights control and real sales channels separate honest hybrids from disguised vanity services.

publishing-business.l12.q1.t: A 13-digit identifier for a specific edition of a book
publishing-business.l12.q1.h: It identifies editions for the trade.
publishing-business.l12.q1.e: ISBNs help retailers and libraries identify an edition; they do not protect copyright.

publishing-business.l12.q2.p: An author releases a paperback, hardcover, ebook and audiobook, each with its own ISBN. How many ISBNs are needed?
publishing-business.l12.q2.e: Each format is a separate edition and needs its own ISBN.

publishing-business.l12.q3.t: The page count and paper type
publishing-business.l12.q3.p: A print cover needs a spine. What determines the spine width?
publishing-business.l12.q3.h: Think about how thick the book is.
publishing-business.l12.q3.e: Spine width depends on the thickness of the interior pages, so it varies with page count and paper.

publishing-business.l12.q4.t: An ISBN identifies an edition but does not give copyright protection
publishing-business.l12.q4.p: Which statement about ISBNs is correct?
publishing-business.l12.q4.e: Identifiers aid trade tracking; copyright arises from creation and is separate.

publishing-business.l12.q5.t: Readers judge genre and quality in a glance, so the title must be legible and the style on-genre
publishing-business.l12.q5.p: Why does cover design matter so much for thumbnails online?
publishing-business.l12.q5.h: Think of a tiny image in search results.
publishing-business.l12.q5.e: A cover has a second to signal genre and professionalism at small size.

publishing-business.l13.q1.t: Structured information about a book used for display and search
publishing-business.l13.q1.h: It is data about the book.
publishing-business.l13.q1.e: Metadata includes title, description, categories, keywords and more, and drives discoverability.

publishing-business.l13.q2.t: Choose more specific, accurate categories that match comparable books
publishing-business.l13.q2.p: An author lists "Fiction" only, while rivals use "Cozy mystery". What is the best fix?
publishing-business.l13.q2.e: Accurate, narrow categories help readers who want that kind of book find it.

publishing-business.l13.q3.p: Which keyword set is honest and useful for a coastal mystery novel?
publishing-business.l13.q3.h: Describe the book, not someone else's.
publishing-business.l13.q3.e: Keywords should reflect what the book actually is; misusing others' names is often prohibited.

publishing-business.l13.q4.t: They order and catalogue through databases that rely on correct data and codes
publishing-business.l13.q4.p: Why is accurate metadata important for libraries and bookshops, beyond online stores?
publishing-business.l13.q4.e: Trade and library systems rely on standardised metadata to find and order titles.

publishing-business.l13.q5.t: Reach across many stores versus special benefits at one retailer
publishing-business.l13.q5.p: What is a typical trade-off between wide distribution and an exclusivity programme?
publishing-business.l13.q5.h: Think of breadth versus a single partner.
publishing-business.l13.q5.e: Exclusivity trades reach for benefits; compare current terms, which change.

publishing-business.l14.q1.t: No inventory or large upfront printing bill
publishing-business.l14.q1.p: What is a main advantage of print on demand?
publishing-business.l14.q1.e: POD prints per order, avoiding warehouse costs and unsold stock.

publishing-business.l14.q2.p: A paperback lists at 15 dollars with a 40 percent wholesale discount. What revenue does the publisher receive per copy?

publishing-business.l14.q3.p: If the print cost for that book is 4.50 dollars, what is the per-copy margin in the wholesale channel?

publishing-business.l14.q4.p: An author buys 2,000 offset copies at 2.50 dollars each, but only 1,200 sell. What does she have in unsold stock and what did the print run cost?

publishing-business.l14.q5.p: A wholesale discount of 40 percent and a print cost of 4 dollars: what list price gives about 5 dollars of margin?

publishing-business.l15.q1.t: One hour of final, edited audio
publishing-business.l15.q1.p: What is a finished hour in audiobook production?
publishing-business.l15.q1.h: It is about the final product.
publishing-business.l15.q1.e: Narrators are often paid by the length of the final audio, not raw recording time.

publishing-business.l15.q2.p: Using about 9,000 words per finished hour, how long is a 90,000-word audiobook?
publishing-business.l15.q2.h: Divide words by words per hour.

publishing-business.l15.q3.p: With those 10 hours at an illustrative 200 dollars per finished hour, what is the narration fee?

publishing-business.l15.q4.t: No upfront fee, but part of future earnings is shared
publishing-business.l15.q4.p: What is the upfront trade-off of a royalty-share narration deal?
publishing-business.l15.q4.h: Think about cash now versus later.
publishing-business.l15.q4.e: Royalty-share lowers the upfront cost but gives the narrator a percentage of sales.

publishing-business.l15.q5.t: You may have already granted audio rights to a publisher
publishing-business.l15.q5.p: Why check your existing publishing contract before producing audio yourself?
publishing-business.l15.q5.e: If a contract grants audio rights, only that rights holder may produce the audiobook.

publishing-business.l16.q1.t: When the original work is fixed in tangible form
publishing-business.l16.q1.p: When does copyright in your manuscript begin in the US?
publishing-business.l16.q1.e: Copyright arises automatically on fixation; registration is optional but useful.

publishing-business.l16.q2.t: Registration (or a refusal) must occur first
publishing-business.l16.q2.p: A US author wants to sue an infringer in federal court. Which statement is generally correct for US works?
publishing-business.l16.q2.e: For works of US origin, registration is generally a prerequisite to filing suit.

publishing-business.l16.q3.t: Three months after first publication (about 1 June), or before the infringement
publishing-business.l16.q3.p: A book is first published on 1 March. For the strongest remedies against an infringement that begins later, by what date should it be registered at the latest?
publishing-business.l16.q3.e: Statutory damages and fees generally require registration before infringement or within three months of first publication.

publishing-business.l16.q4.t: A case-by-case defence, with no guaranteed safe number of words
publishing-business.l16.q4.p: Which is the most accurate view of fair use?
publishing-business.l16.q4.e: Fair use depends on factors weighed by a court; attribution alone does not cure infringement.

publishing-business.l16.q5.t: Obtain a licence or permission from the rights holder, or use properly licensed or original art
publishing-business.l16.q5.p: An author finds a photograph online and wants it on her cover. What is the safest step?
publishing-business.l16.q5.e: Online availability does not transfer rights; licences define what you may do.

publishing-business.l17.q1.t: Returns rights to the author under stated conditions
publishing-business.l17.q1.p: What does a reversion clause do?
publishing-business.l17.q1.e: Reversion lets an author regain rights, for example when sales fall below a threshold.

publishing-business.l17.q2.t: Ebooks and POD keep a book technically in print forever, so rights may never return
publishing-business.l17.q2.p: A contract grants "world rights, all formats, life of copyright" with reversion only if "out of print." Why is that a problem today?
publishing-business.l17.q2.h: Is any book out of print now?
publishing-business.l17.q2.e: Digital availability means the out-of-print trigger is almost never met unless it is defined by sales or earnings.
