world-mythology.l24.q3.p: The surviving copy is a manuscript made in the early 1700s by the friar Francisco Ximenez.
world-mythology.l24.q3.e: Ximenez transcribed the K'iche' text and added a Spanish translation.

world-mythology.l24.q4.e: They are the Hero Twins who defeat the lords of Xibalba.

world-mythology.l24.q5.t: The surviving text was made in the colonial era and may show Christian influence
world-mythology.l24.q5.p: Why do scholars debate the Popol Vuh's pre-conquest content?
world-mythology.l24.q5.h: Consider when the writing was done.
world-mythology.l24.q5.e: Colonial-era writing raises questions about what reflects older tradition.

world-mythology.l25.q1.p: According to the Aztec sources, which sun is the present age?
world-mythology.l25.q1.e: The present age is called the Fifth Sun.

world-mythology.l25.q2.t: A sixteenth-century work compiled by Sahagun with Nahua informants
world-mythology.l25.q2.h: A Franciscan friar and Nahua helpers.
world-mythology.l25.q2.e: Sahagun compiled it with Nahua elders and students who provided information.

world-mythology.l25.q3.p: Archaeologists found a carved stone disk of Coyolxauhqui at the Templo Mayor in 1978.
world-mythology.l25.q3.h: Recall the war god's birth story.
world-mythology.l25.q3.e: The Coyolxauhqui stone was uncovered at the Templo Mayor in 1978.

world-mythology.l25.q4.p: In the birth story of Huitzilopochtli, who is his mother?
world-mythology.l25.q4.e: Coatlicue is his mother, and he defeats Coyolxauhqui and her brothers.

world-mythology.l25.q5.t: The idea appears mainly in accounts written after the conquest
world-mythology.l25.q5.p: What is one reason many historians doubt that the Aztecs saw Cortes as a returning god?
world-mythology.l25.q5.h: Consider when the story was recorded.
world-mythology.l25.q5.e: Such accounts come from after the conquest, which raises doubts.

world-mythology.l26.q1.p: How did the Inca keep records?
world-mythology.l26.q1.e: Quipu stored numbers and perhaps some narrative information.

world-mythology.l26.q2.t: It records local religion of a highland province in Quechua
world-mythology.l26.q2.p: What makes the Huarochiri Manuscript rare?
world-mythology.l26.q2.e: It is a rare major text written in Quechua, from about 1608.

world-mythology.l26.q3.p: Garcilaso de la Vega published his Royal Commentaries in 1609.
world-mythology.l26.q3.h: He was the son of a Spanish captain and an Inca noblewoman.
world-mythology.l26.q3.e: Garcilaso, called El Inca, published the work in 1609.

world-mythology.l26.q4.t: A creator god who emerged from Lake Titicaca
world-mythology.l26.q4.p: Who is Viracocha in many accounts?
world-mythology.l26.q4.e: In many accounts, Viracocha forms people after emerging from the lake.

world-mythology.l26.q5.t: They were shaped for imperial politics and then reshaped by colonial writers
world-mythology.l26.q5.p: Why is caution needed with Inca stories?
world-mythology.l26.q5.e: Inca narratives passed through imperial and then colonial hands.

world-mythology.l27.q1.t: Hundreds of nations speak many languages and tell different stories
world-mythology.l27.q1.p: Why is the phrase Native American mythology too broad?
world-mythology.l27.q1.e: The diversity of nations means we should name the specific people.

world-mythology.l27.q2.p: Which nation tells of Sky Woman who fell from a world above?
world-mythology.l27.q2.h: They are also called the Six Nations.
world-mythology.l27.q2.e: The Haudenosaunee tell of Sky Woman and the turtle.

world-mythology.l27.q3.p: White Buffalo Calf Woman is a figure in Lakota tradition who brought sacred ceremonies.
world-mythology.l27.q3.h: The story is central to Lakota religious life.
world-mythology.l27.q3.e: The lesson attributes this story to the Lakota.

world-mythology.l27.q4.t: Peoples of the Pacific Northwest such as the Haida
world-mythology.l27.q4.p: Raven, a trickster who in many tellings brings light, is told of by which peoples?
world-mythology.l27.q4.h: The coast of the Pacific Northwest.
world-mythology.l27.q4.e: Raven stories belong to peoples including the Haida.

world-mythology.l27.q5.t: Books and teaching by the nations themselves
world-mythology.l27.q5.p: Which source type deserves priority for these stories?
world-mythology.l27.q5.e: Many nations publish their own accounts, and those should come first.

world-mythology.l28.q1.p: Who completed the Shahnameh around 1010 CE?
world-mythology.l28.q1.e: Ferdowsi completed the Book of Kings in Persian.

world-mythology.l28.q2.p: In the Shahnameh, whom does Rostam unknowingly kill?
world-mythology.l28.q2.e: Rostam fights and kills Sohrab without knowing he is his son.

world-mythology.l28.q3.p: Aladdin and Ali Baba are not found in the earliest Arabic manuscripts of the Nights.
world-mythology.l28.q3.h: They came through a French translation.
world-mythology.l28.q3.e: They entered via Antoine Galland's early eighteenth-century French translation.

world-mythology.l28.q4.t: Scheherazade tells stories to delay her execution
world-mythology.l28.q4.p: What is the frame story of the Arabian Nights?
world-mythology.l28.q4.e: Scheherazade tells tales night after night.

world-mythology.l28.q5.t: It comes mostly from later Islamic-era writers
world-mythology.l28.q5.p: Why is knowledge of pre-Islamic Arabian religion based on indirect evidence?
world-mythology.l28.q5.h: Think about when the writers lived.
world-mythology.l28.q5.e: Later writers, such as the author of the Book of Idols, are the main sources.

world-mythology.l29.q1.t: Sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims, and described respectfully without judging their truth
world-mythology.l29.q1.p: How does the lesson describe these narratives?
world-mythology.l29.q1.e: The lesson describes them without asserting or denying religious claims.

world-mythology.l29.q2.p: What is the Quranic name for Joseph?
world-mythology.l29.q2.e: The Quran tells the story of Yusuf in one chapter.

world-mythology.l29.q3.p: The Quran does not name Adam's wife.
world-mythology.l29.q3.e: Unlike the usual reading of Genesis, the Quran does not name her.

world-mythology.l29.q4.p: Who is Maryam in the Quran?
world-mythology.l29.q4.e: Maryam, the mother of Jesus, is prominent in the Quran.

world-mythology.l29.q5.t: Present the question without taking a side on revelation
world-mythology.l29.q5.p: How should a respectful course treat the parallels between Genesis and Mesopotamian flood stories?
world-mythology.l29.q5.e: They may interpret the parallels differently, so the course stays neutral on revelation.

world-mythology.l30.q1.p: Which Mesopotamian epic from the early second millennium BCE tells of a flood and a human survivor?
world-mythology.l30.q1.e: Atrahasis includes a flood sent by gods and a survivor who builds a boat.

world-mythology.l30.q2.p: In Greek tradition, Deucalion and Pyrrha survive a flood sent by Zeus.
world-mythology.l30.q2.e: They are the Greek flood survivors.

world-mythology.l30.q3.p: Who is warned of a flood by a fish in the Shatapatha Brahmana?
world-mythology.l30.q3.h: The first man in Vedic tradition.
world-mythology.l30.q3.e: Manu is warned by a fish, a story first found in that Vedic text.

world-mythology.l30.q4.p: Which explanation says floods are a common experience, so many cultures tell of them?
world-mythology.l30.q4.e: Independent origin accounts for resemblances by shared human experience.

world-mythology.l30.q5.t: Compare in detail and name the source for each version
world-mythology.l30.q5.p: What is a good habit when comparing flood stories?
world-mythology.l30.q5.e: Cause, survivors and moral vary, so careful sourcing is needed.

world-mythology.l31.q1.t: A character who breaks rules and crosses boundaries
world-mythology.l31.q1.e: Tricksters play tricks and move between categories.

world-mythology.l31.q2.p: In the Eddas, Loki both helps and harms the gods.
world-mythology.l31.q2.e: Loki is ambiguous and eventually joins the gods' enemies at Ragnarok.

world-mythology.l31.q3.t: An orisha who is a messenger and guardian of crossroads
world-mythology.l31.q3.p: Who is Eshu in Yoruba tradition?
world-mythology.l31.q3.e: Equating him with the devil was a missionary misunderstanding.

world-mythology.l31.q4.p: In the Homeric Hymn to Hermes, what does Hermes do?
world-mythology.l31.q4.e: Hermes steals Apollo's cattle in the hymn.

world-mythology.l31.q5.t: Each figure has its own tradition, role and audience
world-mythology.l31.q5.p: Why can general patterns about tricksters mislead?
world-mythology.l31.q5.e: Loki, Anansi and Eshu differ in what they do and how they are seen.

world-mythology.l32.q1.p: Who published The Hero with a Thousand Faces in 1949?

world-mythology.l32.q2.t: A pattern of departure, trials, reward and return
world-mythology.l32.q2.e: The hero leaves home, undergoes trials, and returns transformed.

world-mythology.l32.q3.p: Critics say the monomyth is so general that almost any story fits.
world-mythology.l32.q3.e: Critics also note selective examples and neglect of cultural particulars.

world-mythology.l32.q4.t: Adapted Campbell's pattern into a guide for screenwriters
world-mythology.l32.q4.e: Vogler turned Campbell's ideas into practical advice for film writers.

world-mythology.l32.q5.t: Whose story is it, who was consulted, and what do the sources say
world-mythology.l32.q5.p: Which question should a thoughtful viewer ask about a modern retelling of a myth?
world-mythology.l32.q5.e: These questions connect the retelling back to its sources and communities.

world-religions.l01.q1.t: To understand what traditions teach and practise, without ranking them
world-religions.l01.q1.p: What is the aim of an academic study of religion?
world-religions.l01.q1.e: Academic study describes traditions fairly and aims at understanding rather than ranking.

world-religions.l01.q2.t: Buddhists believe that craving causes suffering
world-religions.l01.q2.p: Which phrasing best fits a neutral study guide?
world-religions.l01.q2.h: Look for the one that attributes the belief to the group.
world-religions.l01.q2.e: Describing a tradition in its own terms attributes beliefs to those who hold them.

world-religions.l01.q3.p: How many galleries does the Sacred Library use as a template for each faith?
world-religions.l01.q3.e: Every faith wing is built from the same ten galleries, from Sacred Texts to Study Tools and Glossary.

world-religions.l01.q4.t: Some traditions are structured differently, such as teachings rather than a creed
world-religions.l01.q4.p: Why does the Sacred Library let some faiths deviate from the template?
world-religions.l01.q4.h: Think about how Buddhism is described.
world-religions.l01.q4.e: Buddhism, for example, is described as non-theistic with schools rather than denominations, so its wing bends the template.

world-religions.l02.q1.p: Which text is part of the Mahabharata and is highly revered by many Hindus?
world-religions.l02.q1.h: It is part of an epic.
world-religions.l02.q1.e: The Bhagavad Gita is found within the Mahabharata epic.

world-religions.l02.q2.p: What does dharma mean in Hindu thought?
world-religions.l02.q2.e: In Hinduism dharma refers to duty and right living in accordance with the order of things.

world-religions.l02.q3.t: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
world-religions.l02.q3.h: It is the goal of the paths.
world-religions.l02.q3.e: Moksha is freedom from samsara, the cycle of birth and rebirth.

world-religions.l02.q4.t: It includes devotion, action, knowledge and meditation as ways toward the goal
world-religions.l02.q4.p: Why is Hinduism often described as a family of paths?
world-religions.l02.q4.e: Hindu tradition describes several paths, so it is not a single creed with one founder.

world-religions.l03.q1.t: Under a tree at Bodh Gaya
world-religions.l03.q1.p: Where do Buddhists say Siddhartha Gautama awakened?
world-religions.l03.q1.h: The tree is called the Bodhi tree.
world-religions.l03.q1.e: Buddhist tradition says he awakened while meditating under a tree at Bodh Gaya.

world-religions.l03.q2.p: What does the title Buddha mean?
world-religions.l03.q2.h: It is a title, not a name.
world-religions.l03.q2.e: Buddha means awakened one; Buddhists honour him as a teacher, not a creator.

world-religions.l03.q3.p: Which Indian emperor supported Buddhism and sent teachers abroad?
world-religions.l03.q3.h: He ruled in the 3rd century BCE.
world-religions.l03.q3.e: Ashoka supported the Buddhist community and helped the faith spread.

world-religions.l03.q4.t: Monks, merchants and pilgrims carried it along trade routes such as the Silk Road
world-religions.l03.q4.p: How did Buddhism spread to China and Central Asia?
world-religions.l03.q4.h: Think about a famous trade route.
world-religions.l03.q4.e: The Silk Road carried Buddhism into Central Asia and China.

world-religions.l04.q1.p: How many Noble Truths are in the Buddha's core teaching?
world-religions.l04.q1.h: The number is in the name.
world-religions.l04.q1.e: The Four Noble Truths are the heart of the Dharma.

world-religions.l04.q2.h: It is one of the three marks.
world-religions.l04.q2.e: Anatta is the absence of a fixed, independent self.

world-religions.l04.q3.p: What does the Buddhist tradition say is the cause of dukkha?
world-religions.l04.q3.e: The second Noble Truth identifies craving as the origin of suffering.

world-religions.l04.q4.t: It avoids both indulgence and harsh self-denial
world-religions.l04.q4.p: Why is the Eightfold Path called the Middle Way?
world-religions.l04.q4.e: The Middle Way is a path of balance between extremes.

world-religions.l05.q1.h: It describes how the Pali Canon is organised.
world-religions.l05.q1.e: Tripitaka means three baskets and names the Pali Canon.

world-religions.l05.q2.p: How many verses does the Dhammapada contain, according to the Sacred Library?
world-religions.l05.q2.e: The Dhammapada has 423 verses in 26 chapters.

world-religions.l05.q3.p: Which teaching is central to the Heart Sutra?
world-religions.l05.q3.h: The word means that things lack inherent existence.
world-religions.l05.q3.e: The Heart Sutra is a short Mahayana text on emptiness.

world-religions.l05.q4.p: Which of these are the three great vehicles of Buddhism?
world-religions.l05.q4.h: The word vehicle is the clue.
world-religions.l05.q4.e: Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana are the three vehicles, with schools such as Zen and Pure Land within them.

world-religions.l06.q1.e: The Tanakh is the Hebrew Bible, made up of Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim.

world-religions.l06.q2.e: Passover remembers the exodus from Egypt.

world-religions.l06.q3.p: Which text records centuries of rabbinic discussion applying the Torah to life?
world-religions.l06.q3.h: It is not part of the Tanakh itself.
world-religions.l06.q3.e: The Talmud records rabbinic discussion of the Torah.

world-religions.l06.q4.t: Jewish scriptures were carefully copied over many centuries
world-religions.l06.q4.p: What does the Great Isaiah Scroll, from about 125 BCE, show?
world-religions.l06.q4.h: Think of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
world-religions.l06.q4.e: The scroll is a complete book of Isaiah far older than earlier known Hebrew copies, showing careful transmission.

world-religions.l07.q1.t: A statement of Christian belief from the councils of 325 and 381
world-religions.l07.q1.h: It is named for a city.
world-religions.l07.q1.e: The Council of Nicaea in 325 produced the creed and Constantinople in 381 completed it.

world-religions.l07.q2.p: In what year did Martin Luther's challenge begin the Reformation?

world-religions.l07.q3.t: The Church divided into Western and Eastern branches
world-religions.l07.q3.e: The split of 1054 separated Catholic and Orthodox Christianity.

world-religions.l07.q4.t: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
world-religions.l07.q4.p: What central conviction does the Nicene Creed state about God?
world-religions.l07.q4.e: Christians affirm one God in three persons, as the creed states.

world-religions.l08.q1.p: Which sacrament, also called communion, remembers the Last Supper?
world-religions.l08.q1.e: The Eucharist remembers the Last Supper of Jesus.

world-religions.l08.q2.p: Which are the three major families of Christianity?
world-religions.l08.q2.h: They are named in the lesson.
world-religions.l08.q2.e: Christians are generally grouped as Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant.

world-religions.l08.q3.p: Which season ends the Christian liturgical year's Easter cycle?
world-religions.l08.q3.e: The liturgical year runs from Advent to Pentecost.

world-religions.l08.q4.p: Which early manuscript from around 330 to 360 CE preserves the oldest complete New Testament?
world-religions.l08.q4.h: It is a codex, or early book.
world-religions.l08.q4.e: Codex Sinaiticus is the oldest complete New Testament, as the Sacred Library notes.

world-religions.l09.q1.p: How many times a day do Muslims perform the ritual prayer, salat?
world-religions.l09.q1.h: It is one of the Five Pillars.
world-religions.l09.q1.e: Muslims pray five times a day.

world-religions.l09.q2.t: The migration from Mecca to Medina in 622
world-religions.l09.q2.e: The Hijra is the 622 migration of Muhammad and his followers to Medina.

world-religions.l09.q3.p: Which pillar is fasting during Ramadan?
world-religions.l09.q3.h: Zakat is giving, hajj is pilgrimage.
world-religions.l09.q3.e: Sawm is the fast during the month of Ramadan.

world-religions.l09.q4.t: The sources from which law is developed
world-religions.l09.q4.p: What do the Qur'an and the Sunnah provide for scholars of fiqh?
world-religions.l09.q4.e: Scholars developed fiqh from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

world-religions.l10.q1.e: Guru Nanak (1469 to 1539) was the first of the ten Gurus.

world-religions.l10.q2.t: A free community kitchen at the gurdwara
world-religions.l10.q2.e: Langar is the free communal meal where all sit as equals.

world-religions.l10.q3.p: Which Guru founded the Khalsa in 1699?
world-religions.l10.q3.e: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa and declared the scripture the eternal Guru.

world-religions.l10.q4.t: Sikhs treat it as the eternal Guru
world-religions.l10.q4.p: Why is the Guru Granth Sahib central to a gurdwara?
world-religions.l10.q4.h: It is treated with deep reverence.
world-religions.l10.q4.e: Sikhs honour the scripture as the eternal Guru and keep it at the centre of worship.

world-religions.l11.q1.p: Which scripture is the Sikh holy book?
world-religions.l11.q1.e: The Guru Granth Sahib is the Sikh scripture.

world-religions.l11.q2.p: How were the Vedas first passed down?
world-religions.l11.q2.e: The Vedas were memorised and recited across generations.

world-religions.l11.q3.p: Which tradition has several canons, such as Pali, Chinese and Tibetan?
world-religions.l11.q3.h: The Sacred Library says it has multiple canons.
world-religions.l11.q3.e: Buddhism preserves multiple canons rather than one closed book.

world-religions.l11.q4.t: To read the source closely and see details that translations can blur
world-religions.l11.q4.p: Why do many readers study scriptures in original languages like Hebrew, Greek or Pali?
world-religions.l11.q4.e: Original languages give direct access to the wording; the Sacred Library offers glosses and parallel translations.

world-religions.l12.q1.p: Which Buddhist festival marks the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing?
world-religions.l12.q1.h: It is mentioned in the Calendar gallery.
world-religions.l12.q1.e: Vesak commemorates all three events in the Buddha's life.

world-religions.l12.q2.p: Which festival ends the month of Ramadan?
world-religions.l12.q2.h: Its name refers to breaking the fast.
world-religions.l12.q2.e: Eid al-Fitr celebrates the end of Ramadan.

world-religions.l12.q3.t: A way of fixing the date of Easter
world-religions.l12.q3.p: What did the Council of Nicaea in 325 help to settle?
world-religions.l12.q3.h: It is mentioned in the Sacred Library.
world-religions.l12.q3.e: Nicaea gave the church a way of fixing the date of Easter.

world-religions.l12.q4.t: The Islamic calendar is lunar and about ten or eleven days shorter than the solar year
world-religions.l12.q4.p: Why does Ramadan move earlier through the seasons each year?
world-religions.l12.q4.e: A purely lunar calendar drifts against the solar year by roughly ten or eleven days.

world-religions.l13.q1.p: Which structure is a famous Sikh shrine in Amritsar?
world-religions.l13.q1.h: Its other name is Harmandir Sahib.
world-religions.l13.q1.e: The Golden Temple is the best known Sikh shrine.

world-religions.l13.q2.h: It is one of the Five Pillars.
world-religions.l13.q2.e: Zakat is the Muslim practice of giving to people in need.

world-religions.l13.q3.p: Which emperor promoted compassion in public edicts in the 3rd century BCE?
world-religions.l13.q3.e: Ashoka promoted principles of compassion in his edicts.

world-religions.l13.q4.t: It protects free exercise and forbids an established religion
world-religions.l13.q4.p: What does the First Amendment say about religion?
